text: Abercrombie. Abercrombie appears to be a feeble, eccentric hermit dwelling in a dilapidated shack in western Duskwood near Raven Hill Cemetery. Claiming to be a harmless recluse plagued by the horrors of the woods, he readily enlists sympathetic travelers to gather peculiar reagents and supplies on his behalf. Tucked away in the rotting shadows near Raven Hill Cemetery, Abercrombie cuts a pathetic figure. He presents himself as an old man merely trying to survive the terrors of Duskwood, asking travelers to run modest errands into Darkshire for supplies, herbs, and thread. To those unfamiliar with the history of the region, he seems like just another unfortunate soul left behind as the province fell into decay.

Aelthalyste. Aelthalyste is a banshee priest trainer and prominent figure among the Forsaken priesthood, stationed in the War Quarter of the Undercity. She oversees the spiritual discipline of Forsaken acolytes, teaching them to wield the dark energies of Shadow. She also coordinates with other Horde faith leaders, directing troll acolytes to their own elders in Orgrimmar. Unlike many priests across Azeroth who revere the Holy Light, Aelthalyste guides Forsaken priests who have turned from the Light toward the power of shadow. Rising as an incorporeal banshee, she embodies the spectral agony and relentless resolve of Sylvanas Windrunner's followers. From her chamber in the Undercity's War Quarter, she calls aspiring priests back from distant outposts to master the darker arts of their discipline, teaching them to harness suffering as a lethal weapon.

Agathelos the Raging. Agathelos the Raging is a colossal armored boar penned within the thorned tunnels of Razorfen Kraul. To the quilboar, whose god and progenitor is the great boar Agamaggan, a beast of his size carries considerable spiritual significance, and he grows even more fearsome when enraged. His sheer mass and strength make him one of the most dangerous beasts lurking under the southern Barrens. The god and progenitor of the quilboar is Agamaggan, a titanic boar. A beast the size of Agathelos—standing roughly twice as tall as a Barrens thunder lizard—therefore carries considerable spiritual significance among the Razorfen tribes.

Aggem Thorncurse. Aggem Thorncurse is a living quilboar shaman in Razorfen Kraul, bearing the title Death's Head Prophet. He calls a boar spirit to his aid when threatened. Aggem guards a part of Razorfen Kraul occupied by the Death's Head tribe. His shamanic powers include summoning a boar spirit, reflecting the quilboar's reverence for Agamaggan.

Ahanu. Ahanu is a tauren merchant operating within Hewa's Armory on the lower rise of Thunder Bluff. He crafts and trades leather armor to travelers and young braves setting out across Mulgore and the wider plains. He also helps newly arrived couriers navigate the bluffs when delivering messages from nearby settlements. Situated amidst the leatherworking stalls and armories of Thunder Bluff's lower rise, Ahanu provides vital equipment to those who make their living across Kalimdor's grasslands. Working hides sent by his friend Jahan Hawkwing at the Crossroads, he represents the everyday tradesfolk who keep the tauren capital supplied with durable cured and tanned hide gear. For travelers fresh off a wind rider from the Crossroads, Ahanu frequently serves as a first point of contact in the grand city, receiving deliveries and directing messengers toward the local flight roosts.

Aku'mai. Aku'mai is a monstrous, three-headed hydra dwelling in the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps along the Zoram Strand. A servant of an Old God, it rose from the waters when that Old God's corruption tainted the temple's sacred Moon Well. The Twilight's Hammer cult has gathered in the Deeps and sacrifices innocents to it for power. Blackfathom Deeps was once a great temple of Elune, until the corruption of an Old God seeped up from beneath the earth and tainted its sacred Moon Well. Aku'mai, a gargantuan hydra and servant of the Old God, rose from the waters. Rather than an ordinary denizen of the tides, Aku'mai is a living blight upon the Zoram Strand that has taken up residence in the submerged ruins of the night elves' fallen temple, poisoning the waters with its malice.

Alamar Grimm. Alamar Grimm is a gnome warlock trainer stationed in Coldridge Valley at Anvilmar. Bitter over the tragic loss of Gnomeregan, he distrusts outsiders and focuses on teaching fledgling warlocks how to harness dark arts and summon their first demonic minions. While most gnomes in Coldridge Valley channel their energies into recovery and tinkering, Alamar Grimm harbors a deep resentment over the fall of Gnomeregan. He holds a cynical view of standard adventurers and even the host dwarves of Ironforge, grumbling that their allies care more about diplomacy with humans than reclaiming the fallen techno-city. Operating from Anvilmar, he seeks kindred spirits who understand that ruthless power may be what his people truly need.

Alanndarian Nightsong. Alanndarian Nightsong is a night elf resident of Auberdine in Darkshore dedicated to tending to the region's beleaguered fauna. She works alongside travelers to remedy the blights plaguing the local wildlife, particularly the region's deer, sickened by poison in Darkshore's waters. Situated in the coastal settlement of Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong watches over the fragile ecological balance of Darkshore. As mysterious taints seep into the soil and waters, the creatures of the ancient woods have begun to succumb to sickness and unnatural aggression. Alanndarian acts as a guardian and naturalist, seeking practical remedies to ease their suffering and restore their natural vigor.

Althea Ebonlocke. Commander Althea Ebonlocke leads the Night Watch, the beleaguered town guard protecting Darkshire from the terrors of Duskwood. A relative of Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, she shoulders the defense of an isolated region abandoned by Stormwind's regular military. She organizes patrols, tasks adventurers with culling local horrors, and coordinates the town's survival against constant monstrous threats. While her relative, Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, handles civil governance within the town hall, Commander Althea directs Darkshire's thin line of physical defense. When Stormwind failed to deploy royal troops to guard Duskwood against creeping horrors, the citizenry formed the Night Watch. Under Althea's steady, unyielding command, these volunteers patrol the fog-shrouded roads, keeping skeletal undead, ferocious wolves, and spiders from overrunning the town perimeter.

Altsoba Ragetotem. Altsoba Ragetotem is a tauren weaponsmith stationed at Bloodvenom Post in Felwood. From this remote Horde outpost, he keeps passing champions armed with reliable maces, staves, and axes to face the blighted horrors of the forest. Bloodvenom Post is a treacherous outpost, situated in the heart of Felwood amidst demonic corruption and tainted wildlife. Maintaining a supply line out here is a grim necessity, and Altsoba Ragetotem does his part by outfitting Horde scouts and travelers. Whether someone requires a sturdy crescent axe or a heavy war maul, Altsoba ensures warriors heading into the corrupted timberlands do not enter the fray unarmed.

Alyissia. Alyissia is a kaldorei warrior trainer stationed inside the hollow boughs of Aldrassil in Shadowglen. She guides newly awakened night elf warriors in the fundamentals of martial combat, helping them harness raw strength and discipline to defend their nascent world tree. Standing within the sheltered sanctuary of Aldrassil, Alyissia instructs young night elves who feel drawn to the path of steel and shield rather than nature magic or the priesthood. While the kaldorei military is traditionally renowned for its Sentinels and stealthy archers, the perilous state of modern Kalimdor requires resolute frontline fighters. Alyissia teaches foundational techniques, ensuring that fresh recruits can direct their battle fury, master their stances, and withstand the aggressive wildlife and corrupted grells encroaching on Shadowglen.

Amber Kearnen. Amber Kearnen is a sharp-eyed operative of SI:7 stationed deep in Westfall. From her concealed vantage point overlooking the plains, she monitors the illicit activities of the Defias Brotherhood on behalf of Master Mathias Shaw. An agent of SI:7, Amber Kearnen serves as one of Stormwind's field scouts. Rather than walking the halls of Stormwind Keep, she operates under the open skies of Westfall, watching over an abandoned watchtower commandeered by the Defias Brotherhood. Under the direct leadership of Master Mathias Shaw, Kearnen provides critical oversight and briefing for covert operatives sent to neutralize Defias threats and gather intelligence across the contested countryside.

Anastasia Hartwell. Anastasia Hartwell is a prominent Forsaken mage trainer residing in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. She guides fledgling and developing spellcasters in mastering the arcane arts and oversees vital magical research and field missions across Lordaeron and beyond. Standing within the dark, echoing chambers of the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Anastasia Hartwell instructs Forsaken and Horde mages in channeling arcane energies. Though the kingdom of Lordaeron fell to ruin, former human practitioners like Anastasia have preserved their scholarly traditions in undeath. She maintains that magic demands strict discipline, warning any traveler she meets that careless incantations will quickly consume the untrained.

Andron Gant. Andron Gant is a reclusive, frequently intoxicated Forsaken residing in the murky depths of the Apothecarium in the Undercity. He handles occasional research commissions for local mages. Lounging amidst the noxious fumes of the Apothecarium, Andron Gant rarely ventures beyond the safety of the Undercity's stone walls. To the casual observer, he appears to be little more than a drunken scholar, occasionally hiring adventurous couriers to retrieve obscure relics like the Tablet of Markri from distant shores on behalf of local mages.

Anduin Wrynn. Anduin Llane Wrynn is the ten-year-old crowned King of Stormwind, reigning in the absence of his missing father, King Varian Wrynn. Due to his young age, the true administration of the kingdom rests in the hands of Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and the royal court. Born in the peaceful interlude following the Second War, Prince Anduin was named in honor of both his grandfather King Llane and the legendary knight Sir Anduin Lothar. Following the mysterious disappearance of his father en route to a diplomatic summit in Theramore, the child was abruptly crowned to maintain stability throughout the kingdom. Though intelligent and empathetic beyond his years, the ten-year-old monarch has little actual say in state affairs, leaving rule of the realm divided between Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and royal councilor Lady Katrana Prestor.

Apothecary Helbrim. Apothecary Helbrim is an emissary of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed in the dusty heart of the Crossroads. Sent all the way to Kalimdor to harvest unfamiliar reagents, he studies the native flora and strange ecology of the Barrens on behalf of the Forsaken. While most of the Royal Apothecary Society remains sequestered in the damp underbelly of the Undercity, Helbrim operates out of the harsh sun and parched red dirt of the Crossroads. Sent far across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, his mission is simple yet crucial: identify and extract useful flora, fungi, and natural specimens from the Barrens. To this end, he relies on passing adventurers to gather samples, such as local fungal spores, and coordinates directly with his colleague, Apothecary Zamah, over in Thunder Bluff. His presence reminds travellers that the reach of Sylvanas's alchemists extends well beyond the ruined borders of Lordaeron.

Apothecary Johaan. Apothecary Johaan is an alchemist and researcher of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed in Brill. Tasked by his order and Lady Sylvanas, he conducts lethal experiments on local flora and fauna to develop the Forsaken's new plague. Working openly out of the Forsaken settlement of Brill in Tirisfal Glades, Apothecary Johaan represents the scientific ambitions of the newly formed Royal Apothecary Society. Like his colleagues across Lordaeron, Johaan operates under direct orders to craft biological and alchemical weapons capable of securing the Forsaken's fragile future against the living and the Scourge alike.

Apothecary Renferrel. Apothecary Renferrel is a prominent member of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Tasked with advancing the Forsaken's alchemical endeavors, he coordinates extensive field research into the region's corrupted wildlife and undead threats. Travelers through Silverpine frequently assist him with gathering volatile reagents and investigating dangerous Scourge remnants. Operating out of the Sepulcher, Renferrel serves as one of the Royal Apothecary Society's chief field researchers in Silverpine Forest. While Undercity houses the grand laboratories and high leadership of the society, Renferrel handles the practical, muddy work of securing native biological specimens, refining potent concoctions, and analyzing the grim ecology of Lordaeron's western border.

Apothecary Zinge. Apothecary Zinge is an alchemist and researcher of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed in the Apothecarium beneath the ruins of Lordaeron. Working in service to the Forsaken, she investigates biological specimens and coordinates research shipments across Horde territories. Apothecary Zinge conducts experiments deep within the murky quarters of the Apothecarium in the Undercity. Like her colleagues under Master Apothecary Faranell, she seeks chemical and biological compounds that can further the goals of the Forsaken. Her research often connects her with field researchers and scouts stationed far beyond the boundaries of Tirisfal Glades, including exchanges with remote outposts in Kalimdor.

Aramis Hammerhand. Aramis Hammerhand is an undead holy warrior situated within the desecrated chapel of Deathknell. As a Forsaken paladin trainer, he instructs newly risen dead who seek to reclaim their bond with the Holy Light. Walking this path in undeath requires immense discipline, as wielding such radiant energy inflicts agonizing pain upon their decayed flesh. Standing within the somber walls of Deathknell's chapel, Aramis Hammerhand represents an anomaly among the recently awakened Forsaken. In life, many citizens of Lordaeron answered the call of the Silver Hand, only to perish when the Scourge swept across the north. Aramis survived the fall only to be raised into undeath, yet he chose not to abandon the martial and spiritual teachings of his former existence. Now, he offers guidance to others who refuse to surrender their devotion.

Arcanist Doan. Arcanist Doan is a master human mage residing within the Athenaeum of the Scarlet Monastery's Library wing. He serves the Scarlet Crusade as one of its most lethal arcane specialists and guardian of key crusade archives. While the fanatical ranks of the Scarlet Crusade lean heavily on martial fury and holy fervor, Doan remained convinced that raw arcane power was essential to purging the Scourge from Lordaeron. Stationed deep inside the Athenaeum of the Monastery's library, he was entrusted as both a lorekeeper and an operational gatekeeper, safeguarding the Scarlet Key that secures crusade sanctuaries across the northern kingdoms.

Archaeologist Flagongut. Archaeologist Flagongut is a dwarven scholar representing the Explorers' League, stationed within the Deepwater Tavern at Menethil Harbor. Though originally en route to the local dig at the Whelgar Excavation Site, he becomes an important contact for field reports traveling across the sea from Darkshore. Archaeologist Flagongut can be found resting with a mug in hand at the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Like many members of Ironforge's Explorers' League, he traveled west across Khaz Modan aiming to assist with discoveries near the Whelgar Excavation Site in the Wetlands. Despite being far from the high halls of the library, he maintains vital ties with field researchers, helping process lost relics and reports ferried across the Great Sea from remote expeditions.

Archaeologist Hollee. Archaeologist Hollee is a dwarven researcher stationed in the coastal settlement of Auberdine. Working on behalf of dwarven excavation interests, she keeps tabs on archaeological findings and surveys throughout the ancient, fog-shrouded wilderness of Darkshore. She frequently coordinates with prospectors scouring the region for relics and geological anomalies. While Darkshore is predominantly guarded and settled by the night elves, the presence of dwarven scholars like Archaeologist Hollee reflects Ironforge's growing curiosity about Kalimdor. The Explorers' League sends representatives far across the seas to uncover traces of ancient history, and Darkshore's ruins offer tempting ground for study. Hollee makes her temporary base out of Auberdine, acting as a regional contact for wandering surveyors and expedition teams.

Archbishop Benedictus. Archbishop Benedictus is the supreme spiritual leader of the Church of the Holy Light, presiding over the faithful from the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City. Once the devoted student of Archbishop Alonsus Faol, he now guides the moral and religious heart of the Alliance during a time of immense uncertainty. Benedictus rose to leadership following the death of his revered mentor, Archbishop Alonsus Faol. Having witnessed the devastation of the First and Second Wars, Benedictus helped oversee the construction of the grand Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City, vowing to preserve the virtues of the faith. With the fall of Lordaeron and the rise of the Scourge during the Third War, the weight of the human kingdoms' spiritual guidance fell squarely on his shoulders. From his altar, he offers counsel to the royal court, trains newly initiated priests, and directs holy crusades against the undead and demonic forces threatening Azeroth.

Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver. Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver is a senior human wizard and a ruling member of Dalaran's Council of Six. Having survived the Scourge's destruction of Dalaran in the Third War, he oversees Kirin Tor operations from the Violet Citadel as Dalaran is rebuilt. Though dedicated to the rebuilding of his city, he also maintains discreet interests abroad—including a willful daughter who ran off to Booty Bay to become a pirate. A veteran mage who helped defend Dalaran across decades, Ansirem Runeweaver sits on the Council of Six, the ruling magocracy of the Kirin Tor. He survived the devastation when Arthas Menethil and the Scourge marched upon the city and Archimonde was summoned. In the wake of Dalaran's fall, Ansirem has aided the efforts to rebuild the arcane city, whose protective shield was lifted early, and now works from the Violet Citadel.

Archmage Malin. Archmage Malin is a senior human wizard stationed just outside the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind City's Mage Quarter. A former pupil of Archmage Trelane, Malin coordinates arcane affairs and field operatives dispatched to recover magical artifacts and rare reagents across the Eastern Kingdoms. Standing sentinel beneath the towering spiral of the Wizard's Sanctum, Archmage Malin serves as a central point of contact for the arcane practitioners of Stormwind. He learned his craft under the tutelage of Archmage Trelane, a storied mage whose scattered legacy Malin now strives to protect. While younger acolytes study theory within the tower's swirling blue portals, Malin keeps his focus trained outward on matters across the realm that demand magical oversight.

Archmage Xylem. Archmage Xylem is an eccentric and reclusive human wizard dwelling in an isolated tower atop the cliffs of northern Azshara. Known for his volatile temperament and dangerous experiments, he has withdrawn from worldly affairs to pursue esoteric arcane research. Reaching him requires magical teleportation, and he only entertains adventurers who can assist in his peculiar studies or aid his personal vendettas. Perched high upon the jagged cliffs of northern Azshara, Archmage Xylem makes his home in a secluded spire overlooking the ruined elven coastline. Rather than building a road or trail, the wizard isolated his sanctuary entirely, relying on his servant Sanath Lim-yo to magically transport approved visitors up the cliff face. Observers across Kalimdor consider him profoundly eccentric and perilous to deal with; even fellow scholars treat him with deep caution, noting that he behaves unlike almost any other human mage.

Argent Guard Manados. Argent Guard Manados is a night elf sentry stationed in Darnassus on behalf of the Argent Dawn. Resting at the Craftsmen's Terrace, he keeps watch over Kalimdor's growing corruption and directs adventurers toward the sinister forces lurking in Blackfathom Deeps. While most of the Argent Dawn focuses its vigilance on the blighted lands of Lordaeron and the Scourge, Argent Guard Manados represents their watchful eyes in the night elf capital of Darnassus. Standing among the artisans and tradefolk of the Craftsmen's Terrace, Manados monitors emerging threats that menace the balance of northern Kalimdor. When rumors reach him of the Twilight's Hammer cult establishing a foul foothold beneath the waves of Ashenvale, Manados enlists capable heroes to strike at Blackfathom Deeps and recover artifacts of their dark devotion.

Argos Nightwhisper. Argos Nightwhisper is a night elf emissary found in the Park district of Stormwind City. He serves as an Alliance contact directing adventurers to Darkshore, where his brother Gershala studies the spreading corruption. Argos Nightwhisper resides among the growing night elf presence in Stormwind, often lingering in the lush, secluded Park district crafted to remind the kaldorei of their ancestral woodlands. Like many of his kin stationed in the human kingdom, Argos acts as a bridge between the newfound allies across the Great Sea. Deeply concerned by reports filtering across the ocean, he urges capable Alliance champions to make the long journey to Auberdine in Darkshore, where his brother Gershala needs help against the spreading corruption.

Arugal. Archmage Arugal is a former wizard of Dalaran who unleashed the feral worgen upon Lordaeron. Overcome by madness and grief, he now rules from the heights of Shadowfang Keep, treating the savage beasts as his beloved children while menacing all of Silverpine Forest. Before the fall of Lordaeron, Arugal was a member of the Kirin Tor, though some peers like Dalar Dawnweaver dismissed him as a charlatan whose weak spellcraft relied heavily on enchanted trinkets. When the Scourge swept across the north during the Third War, Arugal sought a weapon powerful enough to stem the tide. Drawing upon the esoteric research of the late Dalaran mage Ur, Arugal pierced the veil between realms and summoned the worgen into the mortal world. The ravenous beasts tore through the undead legions as intended, but their feral ferocity could not be contained, and their savage hunger swiftly turned against innocent mortals.

Ashlan Stonesmirk. Ashlan Stonesmirk is a dwarven explosives expert assigned to the regiment guarding Dun Modr and the Thandol Span in the northern Wetlands. From there, he keeps a vigilant eye on regional dangers threatening the realm of Ironforge. Positioned at Dun Modr in the northern Wetlands, Ashlan Stonesmirk serves the regiment guarding the Thandol Span. His expertise with explosives makes him a useful contact when suspicious materials threaten dwarven defenses.

Asterion. Asterion is an ancient Highborne spirit bound to the ruins of Bashal'Aran in Darkshore. Once the trusted second to governor Athrikus Narassin ten millennia ago, he was mysteriously imprisoned in a magical moonstone seal that held him through mortal life and into the afterlife. Today, his specter remains shackled to the ruined shrine, surrounded by demonic beasts and dreaming of liberation. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran were sister cities blessed by Queen Azshara herself. Azshara appointed Athrikus Narassin to govern the twin settlements, and Asterion served as his right hand. Respected for both his physical combat prowess and his command of arcane sorcery, Asterion lived among the people of Bashal'Aran while frequently traveling between the sister cities to manage the needs of their citizens.

Athridas Bearmantle. Athridas Bearmantle is a night elf druid residing in Dolanaar within the boughs of Teldrassil. Tasked with safeguarding the local settlement, he directs young adventurers to investigate the encroaching corruption affecting the local wildlife and the nearby Gnarlpine furbolgs. Stationed within Dolanaar, Athridas Bearmantle stands as an early line of defense for the night elves emerging from Shadowglen. As the boughs of the newly grown world tree Teldrassil exhibit unnatural signs of decay and unrest, Athridas works tirelessly to coordinate local scouting efforts and protect the peaceful township from surrounding threats.

"Auntie" Bernice Stonefield. “Auntie” Bernice Stonefield is an elder of the Stonefield family, residing at their homestead in south-central Elwynn Forest. Widowed after her husband fell in battle during the kingdom's military campaigns, she is renowned throughout the valley for her famous pork belly pies. She can be found outside the farmhouse alongside Ma Stonefield, keeping a sharp eye on the neighborhood and harboring a deep suspicion of the rival Maclure family. Like many common folk across the Kingdom of Stormwind, Bernice has borne the steep price of ongoing war. Having lost her husband to military campaigns, she now lives out her days on the family homestead with her kin, helping manage daily farm affairs alongside matriarch Ma Stonefield. Despite personal loss, she keeps the household fed and running, earning local fame for her celebrated pork belly pies.

Austil de Mon. Austil de Mon is a Forsaken warrior trainer stationed in Brill within Tirisfal Glades. Based out of the Gallows' End Tavern, he instructs newly risen warriors looking to hone their martial prowess in service of the Dark Lady. Found inside the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, Austil de Mon serves as one of the earliest instructors for Forsaken warriors venturing out of Deathknell. While the living once populated the inn to drink and rest, Austil now uses the gloomy refuge to teach newly liberated undead how to channel raw martial discipline and ruthless combat techniques against the kingdom's surrounding foes.

Ayanna Everstride. Ayanna Everstride is a kaldorei hunter trainer stationed in Aldrassil within the Shadowglen of Teldrassil. She instructs fledgling night elf rangers in the foundational arts of marksmanship, tracking, and wilderness survival. Young hunters taking their first steps beneath the boughs of the World Tree seek her guidance to hone their woodland discipline. Perched inside Aldrassil at the very heart of the Shadowglen, Ayanna Everstride stands ready to instruct newly awakened kaldorei in the ways of the wild. To the night elves, a hunter is not merely a trapper or sharpshooter, but an indispensable guardian of the sacred forests. Ayanna provides guidance on early martial techniques, helping novices master ranged combat and survive in the perilous woods of Teldrassil.

Ayessa Dawnsinger. Ayessa Dawnsinger is a Skyborne leader found in Valanaar on Zephras Isle. She leads the Windshapers, guiding the Skyborne aligned with the Horde through their trials and politics. Standing within the settlement of Valanaar on Zephras Isle, Ayessa Dawnsinger serves as the paramount guide for the Windshapers—the faction of Skyborne aligned with the Horde. From this vantage, she directs critical efforts across the island, managing external threats, internal fractures, and the overarching survival of her people as they navigate alliances in Kalimdor and beyond.

Azar Stronghammer. Azar Stronghammer is a dwarven paladin stationed at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Having completed his own training in the holy arts, he guides newly awakened dwarven champions of the Holy Light and directs promising recruits toward higher instruction in Ironforge. While paladins are more commonly associated with the great cathedrals of humanity, the dwarves of Khaz Modan have fully embraced the virtues of the Holy Light. Stationed at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Azar Stronghammer watches over newly inducted dwarven paladins finding their footing amidst Dun Morogh's freezing slopes. Having mastered his own martial and spiritual vows, he serves as an approachable mentor. When a novice shows enough dedication and spiritual maturity, Azar directs them up the mountain path to Ironforge to study under veteran champions such as Tiza Battleforge.

Azuregos. Azuregos is an eccentric blue dragon stationed along the coast of Azshara to protect ancient Highborne relics. Entrusted with safeguarding immense magical power by the Spell-Weaver Malygos, he prefers quiet study over violence, but he will readily swat aside any adventurer foolish enough to disturb his vigil. Drawn to the magic-soaked shores of Azshara, Azuregos chose the ancient ruins of Eldarath as his sanctuary. Countless relics survived the Great Sundering along these shattered coasts, and Azuregos considers it his sacred duty as a servant of Malygos to keep such powerful artifacts away from careless mortals. Rather than lurking in a dark cave, he freely roams the crags and beaches, proudly dubbing himself the lord of all magic in the region. Though blessed with a sardonic sense of humor, he fiercely defends Azshara's treasures against the endless stream of adventurers seeking fame or plunder.

Bailiff Conacher. Bailiff Conacher serves in the Lakeshire Town Hall as the chief enforcement officer under Magistrate Solomon. Tasked with maintaining civil order and administering local decrees, he turns to independent champions to enforce the laws of Stormwind across the embattled Redridge Mountains. Within the Lakeshire Town Hall, Bailiff Conacher works closely with Magistrate Solomon to uphold lawful authority in the Redridge Mountains. With the town besieged on all fronts by Blackrock orcs and local gnolls, Conacher cannot rely on standard civic procedures or royal garrisons. Instead, he issues legal decrees that grant passing travelers the authority to administer capital justice on behalf of the realm.

Bailor Stonehand. Bailor Stonehand is a skilled dwarven smith residing in Thelsamar within Loch Modan. Renowned for his metallurgical expertise, he once mentored the human weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell and produces a specialized alloy crucial for masterwork armaments. Currently, his forge work faces setbacks after local Mo'grosh ogres ambushed and stole his ore shipments. Operating in the dwarven settlement of Thelsamar, Bailor Stonehand represents the enduring craft of Loch Modan's blacksmiths. Known for his keen eye for raw minerals and his ability to smelt specialized alloys, Bailor's knowledge extends beyond Khaz Modan. He served as a mentor to the renowned human smith Jordan Stilwell, teaching him the foundational arts of metallurgy and sharing formulas that would later prove essential in forging blessed paladin armaments such as Verigan's Fist.

Baine Bloodhoof. Baine Bloodhoof is the son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof and the acting protector of Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. While his father governs the tribes from the towering heights of Thunder Bluff, Baine directly oversees local defense, investigating encroaching industrial exploitation and defending against feral predators. He serves as an essential bridge between youthful tauren braves and the ancestral wisdom of his clan. Born to Cairne, Baine spent his youth traveling alongside his nomadic people before they claimed the rich grasslands of Mulgore. His early life was marked by the ever-present threat of the centaur clans. Shortly after the Third War, a centaur warband under Khiragg captured young Baine, plunging Cairne into a grief-stricken stupor that nearly shattered the newly founded settlements. It was only through the courage of the champion Rexxar that Baine was liberated from captivity. That rescue restored Cairne's spirit, allowing the tauren to stand with Thrall's Horde against the invading Kul Tirans and secure their foothold on the continent.

Balir Frosthammer. Balir Frosthammer is a dwarven defender stationed in Coldridge Valley within Dun Morogh. Alarmed by the sudden and aggressive incursions of Rockjaw troggs into dwarven lands, he recruits fledgling adventurers to stem the tide before the valley is overrun. Perched in the snowy enclave of Coldridge Valley, Balir Frosthammer watches the perimeter against encroaching dangers. The valley has long served as a safe haven and training ground for dwarven and gnomish novices, but recent disturbances underground have unleashed violent Rockjaw troggs onto the surface. Balir is among the first to sound the alarm, rallying newly arrived recruits to cull the troggs before they breach deeper into Dun Morogh.

Balthule Shadowstrike. Balthule Shadowstrike is a night elf scout stationed in northern Darkshore near the Tower of Althalaxx. Serving as a forward agent for Delgren the Purifier, he keeps watch over the sinister cultists and dark practitioners occupying the ancient elven ruins. Adventurers traveling along the northern coast are often directed to him to assist in unravelling and disrupting the dark rituals underway at the tower. Perched in the wilderness just west of the Tower of Althalaxx, Balthule Shadowstrike maintains a lonely and perilous vigil. Darkshore's northern reaches are thick with restless spirits and shadowed ruins, but the activity around the tower poses a particularly acute threat. Balthule operates under the direction of Delgren the Purifier, observing the movements of dark casters who have crept into the ancient Highborne remnants.

Barithras Moonshade. Barithras Moonshade is a night elf resident of Auberdine in Darkshore. Positioned within the coastal settlement, he seeks the help of adventurers willing to explore the shadowy wilderness and gather rare subterranean flora. Standing watch within the village of Auberdine, Barithras Moonshade contributes to the night elves' efforts to study and manage the unsettled land of Darkshore. He directs travelers to venture into nearby subterranean caverns to harvest specific fungi, such as death cap mushrooms, for study and use.

Barkeep Daniels. Barkeep Daniels tends the counter at the Lakeshire Inn, serving weary town guards, local fishermen, and visiting travelers. With the Blackrock clan raiding across the Redridge Mountains and cutting off supply routes, keeping the tavern fully stocked has become an uphill battle. Behind the counter of the Lakeshire Inn stands Barkeep Daniels, pouring drinks and greeting whoever wanders in from the bridge. Lakeshire has spent months under constant pressure from gnolls and the Blackrock orcs, and the town's defenders rely on the tavern to unwind after grim patrols. Unfortunately for Daniels, the severed roads and relentless attacks have disrupted trade throughout the region. Finding himself dangerously low on liquor during a time when the town needs good cheer most, he is eager for any passing adventurer willing to fetch shipments from safer settlements.

Baron Aquanis. Baron Aquanis is a powerful water elemental of the flooded Moonshrine Ruins in Blackfathom Deeps, where the Twilight's Hammer has made its lair. He rises from the deep water when someone disturbs the ruins' Fathom Stone. The shamans of the Earthen Ring have long thought him a corrupted elemental power, and they suspect the cult is behind it. Submerged beneath the flooded halls of the Moonshrine Ruins, the Fathom Stone lies right under the noses of the Twilight's Hammer cultists who now occupy the ruins. Inside it is a fathom core, a device that, properly read, tells the history of all elemental activity around it. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring sends Horde adventurers to recover the core, and disturbing the stone draws Baron Aquanis up from the depths.

Baron Revilgaz. Baron Revilgaz is the cunning goblin leader of Booty Bay and the Blackwater Raiders, ruling the pirate haven on behalf of the Steamwheedle Cartel. Perched high on the balcony of the Salty Sailor Tavern, he balances fragile trade neutrality with ruthlessly pragmatic opportunism. He hires passing mercenaries to secure his investments, undermine rivals like the Bloodsail Buccaneers, and retrieve ancient relics of the jungle. From his vantage atop the Salty Sailor Tavern, Baron Revilgaz watches the bustling docks of Blackwater Cove through a custom enchanted spyglass. Flanked by his trusted advisor, the tauren Fleet Master Seahorn, Revilgaz exercises firm control over the town's cutpurses, merchants, and privateers. Originally a human settlement overwhelmed by trolls before the First War, the port was claimed and fortified by goblins, eventually evolving into the pirate-leaning commercial nexus of the Blackwater Raiders. Revilgaz ensures the port remains officially open to both Alliance and Horde travelers, strictly enforcing neutrality within harbor limits so that trade continues uninterrupted.

Baron Silverlaine. Baron Silverlaine was the rightful human lord of the fortress once known as Silverlaine Keep, perched high above Pyrewood Village. When Archmage Arugal unleashed the savage worgen upon the region, the baron was mercilessly slaughtered. Now, his tormented spirit lingers in the ruined dining hall, bound in undeath to defend the very lair that became his tomb. Before the shadow of the wolf-beasts blanketed the southern hills of Silverpine, Baron Silverlaine ruled over a proud noble estate. His fortress provided safety and oversight to the surrounding lands. That peace shattered when Archmage Arugal, seeking a weapon against the rampaging Scourge, unleashed summoned worgen into the region. The feral monstrosities could not be controlled; they stormed the stronghold, overran its guards, and butchered the baron.

Baros Alexston. Baros Alexston is the Chief Architect of Stormwind City, stationed within the City Hall overlooking Cathedral Square. A former member of the Stonemasons Guild who helped rebuild the capital after the First War, he chose to accept an official post rather than follow his old friend Edwin VanCleef into open rebellion. Baros grew up on the Alexston Farmstead in the rolling grasslands of Westfall. During his youth, thieves overran and torched his family's homestead, forcing his father to hurriedly stash their most cherished heirlooms across the grounds before fleeing. Baros eventually journeyed to the capital and joined the Stonemasons Guild, dedicating years of grueling labor alongside Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef to raise Stormwind anew from the ashes of the First War.

Bartleby. Bartleby is a bellicose drunkard loitering within the Pig and Whistle Tavern in Stormwind's Old Town. Known for his stubborn grip on his ale, he serves as an early martial test for aspiring warriors looking to prove their mettle in a good old-fashioned tavern brawl. Tucked away in the narrow, cobblestone alleys of Old Town, the Pig and Whistle Tavern draws a rougher, more weathered crowd than the pristine taprooms of the Cathedral Square. Bartleby is one of its most persistent fixtures. Clinging tightly to his favorite mug and fueled by cheap ale, he spends his days nursing grievances and picking fights with anyone unfortunate enough to disturb his drinking.

Bashana Runetotem. Bashana Runetotem is an herbalist and druidic researcher residing on the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. The daughter of Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem, she aids the Cenarion Circle by overseeing agricultural investigations and guiding Horde adventurers against corrupting forces. Standing atop the breezy heights of the Elder Rise, Bashana Runetotem carries on the druidic legacy of her father, Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem. While her father guides the burgeoning tauren druids and advises Cairne Bloodhoof, Bashana focuses on practical research into botanical anomalies and regional threats. She equips travelers with tools like evergreen pouches to cultivate mysterious flora, notably the enigmatic morrowgrain, while also coordinating Horde efforts to cleanse foul corruption spreading from places like Blackfathom Deeps.

Bath'rah the Windwatcher. Bath'rah the Windwatcher is a solitary jungle troll shaman and weaponcrafter dwelling amidst the ruins near Chillwind Point. Far from his tropical homelands, he studies the tempestuous elements of the northern mountains, seeking champions powerful enough to help him craft formidable weapons of wind. While most jungle trolls keep to the warm forests and coasts of the south, Bath'rah has embraced the solitary life of a mountain hermit among the cold ruins of the Alterac Mountains. A seasoned shaman and craftsman, he devotes his days to listening to the howling winds and communing with nature spirits. His obsession is not merely philosophical; he seeks to bind the fury of violent elemental storms into tangible armaments for those who possess the strength to wield them.

Bazil Thredd. Bazil Thredd is Edwin VanCleef's lieutenant and most trusted assistant, locked in the Stormwind Stockade since the Stonemasons' riots. Now the prison has risen in revolt, and Thredd leads the rioting Defias inmates from its eastern cell block. When the Stonemasons Guild was refused payment by the nobility of Stormwind for rebuilding the city, Edwin VanCleef rejected government appeasements and sparked open revolt. Bazil Thredd stood at VanCleef's side as his chief lieutenant and most trusted assistant. During the violent clashes that followed, Thredd was captured by the city guard. While VanCleef and the surviving masons fled into Westfall to form the Defias Brotherhood, Thredd was cast into the depths of the Stormwind Stockade.

Bazzalan. Bazzalan is a sinister satyr rogue lurking within the volcanic depths of Ragefire Chasm. Alongside Jergosh the Invoker, he commands the dark activities of the Searing Blade cult directly beneath the Horde capital of Orgrimmar. While Thrall works to establish the Orcs' new home across Durotar, ancient evils have found a roost beneath his feet. Bazzalan, a cunning satyr rogue, has allied with the Searing Blade cult inside the winding lava caverns of Ragefire Chasm. Swift and lethal with twin blades, he serves as one of the cult's primary field commanders.

Beldin Steelgrill. Beldin Steelgrill is a renowned dwarven engineer and the master technician operating Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. Widely regarded as one of the finest siege engine mechanics in Khaz Modan, he oversees the maintenance of the Ironforge military's heavy armor and treaded warmachines. Keeping those massive contraptions running requires an endless supply of high-grade specialized tools. Situated just down the road from Kharanos, Steelgrill's Depot serves as the primary proving ground and service station for dwarven steam tanks and siege engines. Beldin Steelgrill stands as its chief technician, celebrated far and wide for his unmatched expertise in repairing and tuning armored war wagons. Taming heavy metal and rumbling boilers is unforgiving work, and Beldin burns through gear rapidly. His constant demand for heavy wrenches, cutters, and precision instruments frequently pushes local ironworkers to their limits just to keep his workbench supplied.

Bethor Iceshard. Bethor Iceshard is a powerful Forsaken mage based in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Presiding over the arcane and shadow practitioners within the Temple of the Damned, he commands considerable authority in Sylvanas's realm. Beneath his chilly demeanor lies a past entwined with old friends torn apart by the Scourge. Standing within the Temple of the Damned, Bethor Iceshard oversees the practitioners of the arcane arts and shadow magic in the Undercity. Respected and feared for his intellect and icy resolve, Bethor wields sufficient political and magical weight to give direct instructions to provincial magistrates across Lordaeron. He directs agents of the Forsaken to secure valuable grimoires, investigate arcane anomalies, and stamp out rival powers that threaten the Undercity's dominion.

Billy Maclure. Billy Maclure is a mischievous young human boy living at the Maclure Vineyards in Elwynn Forest. Caught in the midst of a bitter feud between his family and the neighboring Stonefields, Billy's petty antics often cause trouble for both farms. His weakness for fresh pastries makes him easy to bribe when his shenanigans get out of hand. Billy Maclure can usually be found loitering outside the barn at the Maclure Vineyards, not far from the farmer Gerard Tiller. Growing up amidst the endless rows of grapevines, Billy spends much of his time dodging chores and running wild across the rural meadows of southern Elwynn Forest. Like the rest of his kin, he is keenly aware of the long-standing hostility between the Maclures and the Stonefields, though Billy treats the feud more like a game of pranks and petty theft than a serious conflict.

Bingles Blastenheimer. Bingles Blastenheimer is an eccentric gnomish aviator stranded on the southeastern shores of the Loch in Loch Modan. Having crash-landed his experimental flying machine, he finds himself marooned amidst local troggs and beasts, desperate to salvage his precious tools and components. Like many ambitious gnomish engineers, Bingles Blastenheimer took to the skies in a customized flying craft, only to discover that coming down safely is far more difficult than lifting off. After his gyrocopter malfunctioned and crashed into the southeastern shores of the Loch, Bingles survived the impact intact, but his machine shattered into scattered parts. Stranded far from Ironforge, he remains huddled near the wreckage, guarded against hungry crocolisks and hostile troggs while pleading with passing travelers to recover the tools and Blastencapper explosives that troggs from a nearby island stole from him.

Bink. Bink is a gnome mage trainer who resides within the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. Quick-witted and enthusiastic, she guides aspiring spellcasters through the intricacies of the arcane arts and connects them with prominent wizards across the Alliance. Located in the Mystic Ward of Ironforge, Bink stands among the gathered scholars, priests, and arcanists in the Hall of Mysteries. Like many gnomes driven from Gnomeregan, she has adapted to life within the dwarven mountain stronghold, offering her keen intellect and knowledge of arcane craft to those learning the path of the mage. She is well connected to wizards across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, regularly pointing promising apprentices toward greater mentors such as High Sorcerer Andromath in Stormwind or Tabetha in Dustwallow Marsh.

Bishop DeLavey. Bishop DeLavey is a senior representative of the Church of the Holy Light stationed within the Petitioner's Chamber in Stormwind Keep. Acting on matters of state and faith, he quietly oversees sensitive court affairs that the Crown cannot publicly address. While Archbishop Benedictus tends to the Cathedral of Light, Bishop DeLavey resides among the nobility and petitioners of Stormwind Keep. He serves as an ecclesiastical liaison to the court, balancing spiritual counsel with the kingdom's political reality. His position allows him to hear whispered rumors and delicate palace grievances before they ever reach the ears of Highlord Bolvar Fordragon or the young King Anduin.

Blanchy. Old Blanchy is the loyal, hard-working mare belonging to Theodore and Verna Furlbrow, currently resting beside their wagon near the Jansen Stead in Westfall. Renowned for her gentle disposition and hefty appetite, she remains a steady companion to her owners amidst the turmoil gripping the countryside. Long before pulling the Furlbrows' wagon through the dust of Westfall, Blanchy worked the Furlbrows' farm in the breadbasket of Stormwind, where she earned a reputation as an exceptionally sweet-tempered, well-behaved mare. Years of heavy labor have worn her down to 'Old Blanchy,' and the arduous journey fleeing troubled homesteads has left her exhausted. Though visibly weary, her appetite remains hearty, and travelers who bring her nourishing handfuls of oats scattered across the surrounding fields are rewarded by Verna with Blanchy's own treasured blanket and feed pouch.

Blind Hunter. The Blind Hunter is an elusive, albino bat that roosts deep within Razorfen Kraul. Unlike the ordinary bats nesting near the cavern entrances, this rare creature prowls the sunless depths of the quilboar redoubt. Razorfen Kraul is riddled with winding briars and dark subterranean caverns. While common Kraul bats roost nearer to the surface where faint light filters in from the outside world, the Blind Hunter has adapted entirely to the furthest, darkest alcoves of the tangle. Its pale, albino hide and milky gaze are likely the result of generations spent completely isolated from natural sunlight.

Blind Mary. Blind Mary is a tormented banshee haunting an abandoned, ruined farmhouse just southeast of Darkshire in Duskwood. Once a vain and beautiful mortal woman, her violent death and transformation drove her to self-inflicted mutilation in grief over what she had become. Before the shadows fell across Duskwood, Mary was known as a striking mortal woman who took immense pride in her beauty, rarely seen without her treasured looking glass. When the undead swept over the region, Mary was slain along with many of her neighbors. Unlike those who found rest in the earth, her spirit lingered on as an ethereal banshee, condemned to wander the mortal realm in a ghastly, translucent form.

Bloodmage Drazial. Bloodmage Drazial is a blood elf practitioner of arcane and blood magic camped in the northern reaches of the Blasted Lands. Alongside his sister Lynnore, he studies the native beasts of the red wastes to craft potent alchemical concoctions for traveling adventurers. Perched near the northern pass where the Swamp of Sorrows gives way to the Blasted Lands, Bloodmage Drazial pursues a peculiar brand of magic. While many high elves shun the forbidden arts or despair over Quel'Thalas, Drazial and his sister Lynnore harness blood magic to harvest power from the harsh environment. The blighted fauna of the wastes—scorpoks, snickerfangs, and blasted boars—show strange, unnatural vigor, which Drazial and Lynnore believe came from the energy released when the Dark Portal opened. By harvesting specific organs and tissues from these creatures, Drazial brews volatile concoctions that grant immense bursts of physical strength, agility, and endurance.

Bloodmage Lynnore. Bloodmage Lynnore is a blood elf practitioner of forbidden blood magic camped with her brother Drazial near the northern entrance to the Blasted Lands. She assists adventurers by concocting potent alchemical draughts from the organs of local beasts. Camped near the northern entrance to the Blasted Lands alongside her brother Drazial, Bloodmage Lynnore is one of the exceptionally rare elven practitioners of blood magic found in the Eastern Kingdoms. Unperturbed by the harsh and corrupting landscape of the Blasted Lands, she studies the latent arcane and vital energies coursing through native beasts. Travelers who bring her the brains and gizzards of local fauna find that she can distill these gruesome reagents into specialized elixirs granting profound enhancements to intellect and spirit.

Bloodmage Thalnos. Bloodmage Thalnos is a skeletal spellcaster who haunts the Graveyard wing of the Scarlet Monastery. Who he was in life is not recorded, but the plague of undeath claimed him, and he now lingers deep within the Crusade's holy grounds, hungering for vengeance. No record tells who Thalnos was in life. Whatever his past, the plague of undeath claimed him. Rather than being cleansed or permanently destroyed, he rose as a withered skeleton, still clinging to his fiery magic and arcane mastery, and crying out for vengeance and for more souls.

Bluff Runner Windstrider. Bluff Runner Windstrider is a wandering tauren messenger roaming the mesas of Thunder Bluff. He carries urgent dispatches across the city, directing Horde adventurers toward distant frontiers like Ashenvale, Feralas, and the Plaguelands. Thunder Bluff's soaring plateaus require swift feet to keep its leaders and visitors informed, and Bluff Runner Windstrider fills that vital role. Continually jogging the rope bridges and pathways of the tauren capital, he acts as a town crier and dispatch runner. When key outposts across Kalimdor or the Eastern Kingdoms require reinforcements, Windstrider flags down passing champions to carry word and take up the call to arms.

Bolvar Fordragon. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon serves as the Regent of Stormwind and Supreme Commander of its armed forces following the mysterious disappearance of King Varian Wrynn. Standing beside the young boy-king Anduin Wrynn in Stormwind Keep, he strives to hold the kingdom together amid escalating domestic turmoil. Though fiercely honorable, Bolvar often finds his martial decisions influenced and stalled by royal advisor Lady Katrana Prestor. When King Varian vanished en route to a peace summit on Theramore Isle, Stormwind was thrown into political disarray. Ten-year-old Prince Anduin was crowned to maintain continuity, but actual governing power fell to Highlord Bolvar Fordragon as Regent. Bolvar is a venerated paladin devoted to the crown, yet he faces immense strain. Stormwind's military is thinly stretched across Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood. Compounding these crises, Bolvar frequently defers to the counsel of Lady Katrana Prestor, whose dismissive advice consistently blocks him from committing royal troops to peripheral towns.

Braelyn Firehand. Braelyn Firehand is an elusive elf residing quietly among the Horde at Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. While presenting herself as an arcane practitioner seeking to clear mystical obstructions in the highlands, she pursues a deep personal grudge against the grove keepers of Stonetalon Peak. Standing out amidst the tauren lodges and rustic orcish tents of Sun Rock Retreat, Braelyn Firehand is a rare sight: a blood elf dwelling openly within a remote Horde settlement. The shaman and chieftains of the retreat tolerate her presence, seemingly oblivious to her true loyalties. Braelyn presents herself as an observer fascinated by the flow of regional magic, eager to hire passing Horde mercenaries to handle dangerous field assignments across the crags.

Braenna Flintcrag. Braenna Flintcrag is a dwarven priest trainer stationed within the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. She instructs devout followers of the Holy Light, guiding dwarven acolytes as they develop their spiritual disciplines and healing arts. She also passes word to visiting night elf priests when they are called home to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Residing within the quiet alcoves of the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Braenna Flintcrag serves the Alliance as a dedicated priest trainer. While Ironforge is renowned for its roaring forges and martial warriors, devout dwarves like Braenna tend to the spiritual welfare of Khaz Modan. She mentors novices answering the call of the Holy Light, teaching the dual disciplines of restorative mending and defensive warding required to survive in an increasingly dangerous world.

Brainwashed Noble. The Brainwashed Noble is an elusive, captive aristocrat found deep within the subterranean caverns outside the Deadmines in Westfall. Stripped of his autonomy through magical manipulation, he serves the Defias Brotherhood alongside undead minions rather than walking the grand halls of Stormwind. Wandering the murky, bone-littered passages leading into the Deadmines, the Brainwashed Noble presents a jarring contrast to the desperate bandits and rotting corpses that surround him. Clad in remnants of highborn finery, he was almost certainly a sitting member or scion of Stormwind's House of Nobles before falling into Edwin VanCleef's hands. Rather than ransom him for gold, the Defias have bent his mind with enchantments, turning a member of the ruling class into a spellcasting guard for their secret sanctuary. His tragic presence speaks volumes about the lengths the Brotherhood will go to inflict revenge upon the peers who refused to pay them.

Brandur Ironhammer. Brandur Ironhammer is a dwarven paladin trainer residing in the Hall of Mysteries within Ironforge. He guides aspiring champions of the Holy Light through their early rites, testing their devotion and dispatching them across the Alliance. Stationed within the quiet alcoves of the Hall of Mysteries, Brandur Ironhammer serves the Alliance by instructing novice paladins in the ways of the Holy Light. Alongside his peer, Tiza Battleforge, Brandur keeps a watchful eye on young dwarven champions, guiding them through the trials of the Tome of Divinity. While deeply committed to his holy duties, he has acknowledged personal flaws under Tiza's frank counsel, working diligently to temper his envy and maintain the inner purity demanded of a warrior of the Light.

Brann Bronzebeard. Brann Bronzebeard is the youngest brother of King Magni and Muradin, who is believed dead, renowned throughout Azeroth as a peerless explorer, archaeologist, and founding leader of the Explorers' League. Driven by an insatiable curiosity for titan ruins and ancient history, his wanderlust has led him deep into the deadly wastes of Silithus. His field companions in southern Silithus await news of his latest expedition. While his eldest brother Magni rules Ironforge from the throne and Muradin served on battlefield frontlines, Brann took to the open wilds. He was a veteran warrior of the Second War. Yet peacetime turned his formidable constitution toward uncovering the forgotten past. As a leader of the Explorers' League, Brann charted vast swathes of the Eastern Kingdoms—from Elwynn Forest to the untamed jungles of Zul'Gurub—before turning his gaze across the Great Sea to the mysteries of ancient Kalimdor.

Branstock Khalder. Branstock Khalder is the priest trainer stationed at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. Friendly and grounded, he introduces novice dwarven priests to the Holy Light while keeping a watchful eye on the growing trogg threat outside. Inside the bustling hall of Anvilmar, Branstock Khalder serves as a patient mentor to aspiring priests embarking on their spiritual journey. An easy-going dwarf with a deep devotion to the Light, he helps new acolytes master their early prayers and sacred runes. While his primary duty is spiritual instruction, Branstock is acutely aware of the valley's mounting perils—most notably the aggressive trogg infestation menacing the local mountaineers. Once a novice demonstrates sufficient command of the Light, he directs them through Coldridge Pass to seek further guidance from his superior, Maxan Anvol, in Kharanos.

Brave Moonhorn. Brave Moonhorn is a tauren scout stationed at the top of the Great Lift on the southern border of the Barrens. From this precipice, he keeps watch over the entry to Thousand Needles and alerts travelers to the local dangers ahead. Perched above the sheer drops of Thousand Needles, Brave Moonhorn stands guard where the northern plains meet the canyonlands. His primary role is keeping watchful eyes on regional threats moving through the canyon floor below, particularly the hostile centaur clans. Anyone looking to descend into the needles often crosses paths with him first, receiving crucial warnings before they step onto the massive platforms of the Great Lift.

Brewmaster Drohn. Brewmaster Drohn is an orcish brewmaster living just uphill from the bustling port of Ratchet. Having learned the art of exotic fermentation through ties connected to the legendary wandering pandaren Chen Stormstout, Drohn crafts potent beverages on the arid frontier of the Barrens. Adventurers who discover discarded kegs across Kalimdor often find themselves directed straight to his porch. Overlooking the goblin docks of Ratchet sits Brewmaster Drohn, an orc who has devoted his craft to the science of brewing rather than simple combat. Brewing from his hillside home, he operates peacefully within the neutral haven established by Gazlowe's Steamwheedle cartel. While most orcs settle for coarse grog or simple spirits, Drohn's work involves rare ingredients, refined balances of flavor, and techniques rarely practiced among his kin.

Brewmeister Bilger. Brewmeister Bilger is an intoxicated dwarven brewer residing in the cellar of the inn at Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. He whiles away his hours tasting potent spirits and waiting on deliveries from distant lands. Bilger spends his days pacing the cool cellar beneath Southshore's inn, nursing hiccups and seeking out the strongest brews Azeroth can offer.

Brine. Brine is an orc shaman residing in the arid hills of Blackthorn Ridge in the southern Barrens. As an expert on the spirits of water, she guides shaman initiates along the spiritual path to commune with the tides and earn their Water Totem. Perched upon a windswept hill in northern Blackthorn Ridge, Brine lives far from the bustling trading posts of the Barrens. Despite the dry savannas surrounding her, she has dedicated her life to understanding the fluid and fickle element of water. Shaman across the Horde are directed to seek her wisdom once they have mastered earth and fire, for water requires patience and perspective that few understand as deeply as she does.

Brock Stoneseeker. Brock Stoneseeker is a dwarven mining instructor based in the settlement of Thelsamar in Loch Modan. As the proprietor of Brock's School of Mining and Surveying, he instructs novice prospectors in the craft of extracting valuable ores and minerals from the earth. Operating out of Thelsamar, Brock Stoneseeker directs Brock's School of Mining and Surveying. In the mineral-rich hills of Loch Modan, seasoned expertise with a pickaxe and an eye for geological veins are indispensable. Brock guides aspiring miners through the foundational techniques of identifying ore nodes, extracting raw metals, and properly surveying subterranean deposits, ensuring Alliance tradesfolk can fuel Ironforge's legendary smithies.

Bromos Grummner. Bromos Grummner is a dwarven paladin trainer stationed in Anvilmar within Coldridge Valley. He mentors fledgling dwarven holy warriors, preaching steadfast faith in the Holy Light and the vital bond between dwarves and humans in the Knights of the Silver Hand. Standing within the sturdy stone hall of Anvilmar, Bromos Grummner welcomes dwarven novices drawn to the discipline of the Holy Light. Confident and resolute, he instructs young paladins in martial rites and sacred invocations. Beyond the basic tenets of combat, Bromos emphasizes unity, reminding his pupils that the order of the Knights of the Silver Hand bridges the realms of Ironforge and the human kingdoms of the Alliance in righteous purpose.

Brother Joshua. Brother Joshua is a human priest of the Church of the Holy Light stationed within the grand Cathedral of Light in Stormwind. Dedicated to guiding the faithful, he trains novice priests in channeling the Holy Light to mend wounds and bolster their allies. His quiet service anchors the day-to-day spiritual instruction carried out in the heart of the kingdom. Within the serene halls of the Cathedral of Light, Brother Joshua stands near the main altar, ready to instruct newly called servants of the faith. As a priest trainer for the Church of the Holy Light, Joshua provides instruction on the foundational disciplines of healing, protective wards, and the spiritual focus required to commune with the Light. For young human priests starting their service to the Alliance, he represents one of their first guides into deeper communion with the divine.

Brother Kristoff. Brother Kristoff is a human member of the Church of the Holy Light stationed in Stormwind's Cathedral Square. He can be found standing outdoors near the grand statue of Uther the Lightbringer. Preoccupied with theological study, he frequently seeks out practical literature to weave into sermons on spiritual strength. Brother Kristoff serves the Church of the Holy Light from the open courtyard of Cathedral Square, lingering in the shadow of the great monument to Uther the Lightbringer. Unlike some clerics who remain secluded within the marble cloisters of the Cathedral of Light, Kristoff works among the citizens and pilgrims passing through the plaza. In preparing his discourses—such as sermons on the Fortitude of the Spirit—he draws upon grounded, worldly analogies. He famously looks to technical treatises like 'The Stresses of Iron' to explain how the mortal soul endures pressure, comparing the inner resolve granted by the Holy Light to the tempered strength of worked metal.

Brother Neals. Brother Neals is a monk residing in Northshire Abbey within Elwynn Forest. Responsible for managing the abbey's stores of food and drink, he spends much of his time overseeing shipments and sampling the vintage produced by the local vineyard. Tucked away in the upper belfry rooms of Northshire Abbey, Brother Neals looks after the monastery's culinary provisions and beverage stores. He takes a particular, enthusiastic interest in the Northshire vineyards, carefully tracking grape manifests and ensuring the quality of the abbey's renowned wine by tasting it with dedicated frequency. Despite the peaceful duties of inventory and cellar management, he keeps close tabs on the shipments arriving from the valley's surrounding fields.

Brother Sarno. Brother Sarno is an affable human cleric stationed at the entrance of the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City. Serving as the primary greeter for worshipers and visitors, he also helps direct brave Alliance travelers toward engineers in Ironforge who need aid in reclaiming Gnomeregan. Standing just inside the archways of Stormwind's magnificent Cathedral of Light, Brother Sarno is often the very first face pilgrims and travelers encounter. As a dedicated brother of the Church of the Holy Light, his role is simple yet vital: offering a kind greeting to anyone who enters the sacred hall seeking solace, prayer, or guidance. His warmth extends even to the most unexpected visitors, making him a reassuring presence amid the city's busy clerical life.

Brother Wilhelm. Brother Wilhelm is a human paladin trainer stationed in Goldshire within Elwynn Forest. Tucked away behind the village blacksmith, he instructs young defenders of the Holy Light taking their first steps outside Northshire Abbey. While Northshire Valley provides initial shelter for fledgling champions of the Light, those stepping into the broader world of Elwynn Forest often seek out Brother Wilhelm. Stationed just behind the busy smithy in Goldshire, he trains newly minted paladins in their sacred duties, providing guidance and lessons as they transition from abbey novices to sworn protectors of the realm.

Bruegal Ironknuckle. Bruegal Ironknuckle is an infamous dwarven prisoner held within the Stormwind Stockade. Unlike the petty criminals and rioting rabble that fill the holding cells, he is a formidable brawler whose presence deep inside the corridors spells immediate danger to anyone trying to restore order. When the Stormwind Stockade erupted into open revolt, many of the city's most volatile cutthroats took control of the subterranean cellblocks. Among them is Bruegal Ironknuckle, a particularly dangerous dwarf inmate known for brutal brawling strength. Rather than staying confined to a single cell, he prowls the riot-torn hallways, ready to bash anyone attempting to quell the uprising.

Cain Firesong. Cain Firesong is a Forsaken mage trainer located in the settlement of Brill within Tirisfal Glades. He assists fledgling practitioners of the arcane as they grow in power, guiding them before directing them onward to deeper studies in the Undercity. He can be found on the upstairs landing of the Gallows' End Tavern. While many Forsaken spellcasters delve into shadow or necromancy, Cain Firesong maintains mastery over traditional arcane disciplines. Stationed in Brill, he serves as an early mentor to Forsaken mages venturing forth from Deathknell. The local Deathguards direct visitors to the upstairs landing of the Gallows' End Tavern, joking that he arrived too late to get a room.

Cairne Bloodhoof. Cairne Bloodhoof is the venerable High Chieftain of the united tauren tribes and ruler of Thunder Bluff. A towering warrior of immense wisdom, he bound the fate of the tauren to Thrall's Horde after the orcs aided his people in escaping extinction at the hands of the centaur. For generations, the tauren lived as wandering nomads across the Barrens, continually hunted and driven toward extinction by savage centaur marauders. When Thrall and his orcs arrived on the shores of Kalimdor, Cairne recognized a rare nobility in them. Thrall offered military protection, escorting Cairne's desperate caravan across the plains to the safety of Mulgore in exchange for guidance to the Oracle at Stonetalon Peak. Settling upon the towering mesas of Thunder Bluff, Cairne finally established a permanent, unified home for all tauren tribes.

Calor. Calor is a dedicated resident of Darkshire who aids the Carevin family in defending Duskwood. Operating under the direction of Jonathan Carevin, he actively coordinates efforts to hunt down the vicious worgen stalking the gloomy forests. Adventurers looking to push back the ravenous beasts haunting the woods often find their assignments through him. Stationed within the beleaguered settlement of Darkshire, Calor works closely with Jonathan Carevin, one of the town's prominent defenders. Amid the endless gloom and creeping terrors of Duskwood, Calor devotes himself to supporting the Carevin household's mission: eradicating the supernatural horrors encroaching upon the town's perimeter before the remaining townsfolk are slaughtered.

Calvin Montague. Calvin Montague is an opportunistic Forsaken rogue loitering near the exit gate of Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. Preying on newly awakened undead as they leave the graveyard, he attempts to trick passersby into running errands on his behalf. Positioned just outside the gates leading away from Deathknell, Calvin Montague embodies the ruthless pragmatism common among Lordaeron's restless dead. Rather than handling his own correspondence or paying fair courier rates, he attempts to smooth-talk wandering adventurers into delivering letters under false pretenses. While several other prominent undead bearing the Montague family name manage banking interests within the Undercity, Calvin pursues a decidedly less reputable trade, preferring petty schemes and deception.

Canaga Earthcaller. Canaga Earthcaller is a Darkspear troll shaman stationed in the sunbaked Valley of Trials. He instructs novice Horde shamans in communing with the spirits of the land and obtaining their first elemental totems. Perched on the red bluffs of the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller serves as one of the very first spiritual guides for Darkspear trolls and orcs who walk the path of the shaman. While many trainers focus strictly on martial readiness, Canaga teaches newcomers how to quiet their minds and listen to the rumblings of Kalimdor itself, preparing the earth sapta necessary to commune with the spirits.

Captain Danuvin. Captain Danuvin is an officer stationed at Sentinel Hill in Westfall, serving as one of the leaders tasked with holding the frontier together. Working alongside the People's Militia, he directs volunteers and recruits to patrol the roads and push back against encroaching Gnolls and outlaws. His commands are vital to keeping the supply lines and farmlands from falling completely into hostile hands. Perched at the fortified tower of Sentinel Hill, Captain Danuvin coordinates ground patrols across Westfall. The region has spiraled into chaos with the withdrawal of regular Stormwind garrison troops, leaving local defenses severely depleted. Danuvin relies heavily on wandering adventurers, local farmhands, and volunteer fighters to maintain even a semblance of order across the grassy plains.

Captain Grayson. Captain Grayson is the restless spirit of a pirate captain stationed at the Westfall Lighthouse. Having lost his own life when his ship smashed against the dark coastline, he now watches over the beacon to prevent other sailors from suffering his fate. In life, Grayson captained a vessel along the perilous southern seas of the Eastern Kingdoms. His voyage came to a violent end off the jagged shoals of Westfall on a night when the lighthouse fire had gone dark. Cast upon the rocks, Grayson perished alongside his ship, only to awaken as an earthbound phantom trapped upon the coast.

Captain Greenskin. Captain Greenskin is an elite goblin pirate overseeing the construction and crew of Edwin VanCleef's massive ironclad juggernaut. Hidden deep in the subterranean cove of the Deadmines, he commands the pirate forces hired by the Defias Brotherhood. His goal is to bring the warship to readiness to sail against Stormwind. Pacing the main deck of the gigantic juggernaut under construction in the Deadmines cove, Captain Greenskin represents the naval backbone of the Defias conspiracy. A seasoned goblin mariner, Greenskin was brought into Edwin VanCleef's inner circle to turn an underground cavern into a drydock for an engine of war.

Captain Rugelfuss. Captain Rugelfuss is a stern dwarven officer stationed at the southern gate in the Valley of Kings. Tasked with securing the border of Loch Modan, he organizes the defense against a sudden and aggressive trogg uprising. Positioned near the monumental carved arches of the Valley of Kings, Captain Rugelfuss oversees the southern gateway into Loch Modan. With Alliance forces stretched thin across the world, Ironforge relies on veteran officers like him to keep the home territories secure. Rugelfuss dismisses military pomp and formalities, preferring to focus entirely on the grim reality facing the border.

Captain Shatterskull. Captain Shatterskull is a seasoned orc commander stationed at the Mor'shan Base Camp on the northern frontier of the Barrens. Serving as a crucial bulwark for the Horde, he coordinates efforts to repulse night elf forces contesting the border near Warsong Gulch. Positioned at Mor'shan Base Camp along the edge of Ashenvale, Captain Shatterskull serves on the front lines of the Horde's territorial clashes. Beside fellow officers like Kadrak, Shatterskull works to maintain the Horde's foothold against night elf sentinels and Silverwing forces striving to reclaim the borderlands. His post demands relentless vigilance, as the conflict over Ashenvale's timber and ancient lands constantly threatens to spill over into the Barrens.

Captain Stoutfist. Captain Stoutfist is the dwarven officer in charge of military defenses at Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. With the Dragonmaw clan pushing aggressively out of their marshland strongholds, Stoutfist coordinates defensive maneuvers and counter-offensives to ensure the vital Alliance port does not fall. Menethil Harbor serves as the principal deepwater port connecting Ironforge and Stormwind to the marshy lowlands of the Wetlands and the sea beyond. As the town's commanding officer, Captain Stoutfist bears the heavy burden of keeping its docks, civilian populace, and garrison secure against surrounding threats. The marshlands are notoriously hazardous, but the biggest peril to the settlement is an organized surge from renegade orcs.

Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun. Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun is a privateer affiliated with the Steamwheedle Cartel, stationed at the docks of Ratchet. Despite keeping a cordial demeanor toward traveling Alliance members, he harbors intense resentment toward the Theramore forces at Northwatch Hold who dare fire upon his vessels. Operating out of the bustling neutral port of Ratchet, Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun leads the Thalo'dan Privateers under the broad banner of the Steamwheedle Cartel. In theory, Ratchet's merchants welcome all flags so long as their coin is good, but maritime trade along the Barrens coast is fraught with danger. Just south of the port lies Northwatch Hold, an aggressive Alliance fortification whose heavy artillery threatens neutral sea lanes. Brightsun maintains an outward neutrality toward visiting travelers, but he has reached his limit with the belligerent garrison firing on his fleet.

Captured Mountaineer. The Captured Mountaineer is an Ironforge dwarf held prisoner in the basement of the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. Bound and guarded by the Forsaken, he serves as an unwilling subject for the Royal Apothecary Society's grim experiments. Tucked away beneath the floorboards of the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, this Ironforge Mountaineer sits captive far from the safety of Khaz Modan. While patrons drink above, the Royal Apothecary Society puts him to work as an unwitting test subject for their concoctions. Apothecary Johaan and his peers test the lethal potency of their developing plague against living Alliance physiology, using the prisoner to gauge how well their toxins bring a swift and agonizing end to the living.

Captured Scarlet Zealot. The Captured Scarlet Zealot is a crusader prisoner held captive in the basement of Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. Watched over by Forsaken apothecaries and townsfolk, he serves as a living test subject for the Royal Apothecary Society's developing concoctions. Confined beneath Gallows' End Tavern, this member of the Scarlet Crusade embodies the unyielding fanaticism of his order. Even in chains, surrounded by the undead he views as an abomination, he offers no remorse, calling on the Light to protect him from the foul and unholy creatures around him. For the Forsaken, capturing a living zealot is not an act of mercy; it provides valuable human test material to evaluate the lethality of experimental plagues and toxins under development by Apothecary Johaan.

Carendin Halgar. Carendin Halgar is a prominent Forsaken warlock trainer residing in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Sharp-tongued and notoriously short on patience, he oversees the training of fledgling practitioners of the dark arts. He instructs aspiring warlocks on how to subjugate powerful demonic entities from the Twisting Nether, notably teaching the rituals to bind Voidwalkers and Succubi. Within the noxious gloom of the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Carendin Halgar instructs those who delve into the Twisting Nether. He demands focus and obedience, holding little tolerance for failure, hesitation, or weakness. Under his watchful gaze, warlocks are pushed beyond basic incantations into the dangerous mastery of summonings and soul manipulation, cementing the Forsaken's ruthless approach to demonic servitude.

Caretaker Folsom. Caretaker Folsom is a somber human servant found along the Canals of Stormwind City near the Park. Once the trusted overseer of the noble Flintridge family's estate, he now handles the bitter remnants of their tragic downfall.
