Like his father before him, Folsom devoted his life to serving the Flintridge family as their estate caretaker. That quiet life of service came to a bloody end with the massacre of the Flintridge household. With the bloodline wiped out, the manor sat abandoned until its remaining funds completely dried up. Left alone to oversee the remnants of the household, Folsom bears the sorrowful duty of liquidating the family's surviving heirlooms and possessions at auction.

Carolai Anise. Carolai Anise is an eccentric Forsaken alchemist residing in the village of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. She trains novice alchemists, though her hazardous concoctions have drawn nervous murmurs from local guards. Operating out of Brill, Carolai Anise devotes her unlife to the volatile art of alchemy. While many Forsaken researchers operate under the Royal Apothecary Society's grim mandate, Carolai pursues her own strange brews right inside the settlement. Her unpredictable experiments and smoking retorts are notorious enough that the Deathguards keeping watch over Brill openly grumble that she seems bent on blowing up her own house.

Cazul. Cazul is an ancient, blind orc warlock dwelling in the darkened cavern of the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. Despite having lost his physical sight, he possesses profound occult insight and guides rising practitioners of the dark arts seeking to expand their demonic command. Tucked away in the cavernous depths of the Cleft of Shadow, Cazul endures as a relic of old warlock traditions. Though entirely blind, his senses are attuned to the shifting currents of the Twisting Nether and the whispers of demonic entities. Rising warlocks are often directed to him when seeking to expand their mastery and bind more dangerous servitors. His sharp awareness and occult wisdom make it clear that losing his eyes cost him nothing of his arcane power.

Cerellean Whiteclaw. Cerellean Whiteclaw is a night elf resting near the docks and inn of Auberdine in Darkshore. Haunted by the memory of his lost love from the ancient Sundering, he struggles to lay her restless spirit to peace. Ten thousand years ago, prior to the War of the Ancients, Cerellean Whiteclaw shared his life with Anaya Dawnrunner. When the demonic invasion tore ancient Kalimdor apart, Anaya perished in the destruction of her city, Ameth'Aran. Stricken with grief, Cerellean followed Malfurion Stormrage into the long druidic slumber, yet the Emerald Dream offered him little respite from her memory. Upon awakening millennia later, he wandered Darkshore in a grief-stricken haze, only to discover that Anaya's ghost remained bound to the very stones where she fell.

Charlga Razorflank. Charlga Razorflank, widely known as the Crone of the Kraul, is the fierce and cunning geomancer chieftain presiding over Razorfen Kraul. Under her leadership, the Razorfen quilboar drove the tauren out of the southern Barrens through ruthless expansion. Within the tangled, massive brambles of Razorfen Kraul rules Charlga Razorflank. Revered by her people as a master geomancer whose experimental magic remains unmatched among quilboar, Charlga organized her fractious kin into a unified, lethal threat. She harnessed the primal earth and giant thorns sprouting from the demigod Agamaggan's remains, reshaping the labyrinthine Kraul into an impenetrable fortress.

Chef Breanna. Chef Breanna is the head cook at Lakeshire's local dining house in the Redridge Mountains. Tasked with feeding the garrison of Stormwind soldiers stationed to protect the embattled lakeside town, she relies on hearty, local ingredients to keep the defenders on their feet. Operating out of a restaurant house in northwestern Lakeshire alongside her assistants Crystal Boughman and Gretchen Vogel, Chef Breanna bears the heavy responsibility of provisioning the entire local battalion. With Lakeshire besieged by Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and murlocs, maintaining the strength and morale of Stormwind's understaffed garrison is essential. Her signature dish, Redridge Goulash, relies on the wild game and beasts roaming the surrounding ridges, turning dangerous wilderness predators into fuel for the town's weary guard.

Chef Grual. Chef Grual is the resident cook at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. In a secluded town choked by mist and monsters, Grual does his best to keep the Night Watch and weary travelers fed, even if his choice of ingredients raises eyebrows. Running an eatery in Darkshire is a grim task. With supply lines from Westfall and Stormwind constantly harassed by highwaymen, wolves, and undead, fresh provisions are virtually nonexistent. Grual makes do with whatever the wilderness provides. From wolf flank to whatever scavenged meats local adventurers drag through the door, Grual cooks with pragmatism born of necessity.

Chef Jessen. Chef Jessen is Southshore's resident meat vendor and culinarian, working to keep the coastal town fed amidst constant border tensions. He is best remembered for his famous turtle bisque. Operating out of Southshore in the southern Hillsbrad Foothills, Chef Jessen provides provisions and meat to locals and visiting Alliance soldiers alike. He possesses notable culinary expertise. Years past, before plague and war disrupted northern Lordaeron, he regularly ventured north past Dalaran to the shores of Lordamere Lake. There, he harvested meat from native snapjaw turtles to concoct his prized Soothing Turtle Bisque, a hearty recipe he is willing to share with aspiring travelers who assist him in gathering ingredients.

Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker is an emissary of the dwarven Explorers' League stationed in Darnassus outside the Temple of the Moon. Sent from Ironforge across the sea to northern Kalimdor, he seeks to uncover ancient history and coordinates dwarven field research throughout the region. Currently, he is preoccupied with gathering field reports and tracking lost colleagues operating in Darkshore. While it is unusual to find an Ironforge dwarf nestled high in the boughs of Teldrassil, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker represents the far-reaching ambitions of the Explorers' League. Having traded the lecture halls and museum vaults of Ironforge for fieldwork in Kalimdor, he can be found standing outside the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, conferring with local night elf scholars such as Tarelvir. Greywhisker's academic lectures back in the Eastern Kingdoms famously touched upon ancient lore and primordial entities like the Wild God Agamaggan, and he is eager to see what ancient secrets the night elves' ancestral lands might hold.

Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII is a veteran dwarven engineer stationed atop the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan. Tasked with the upkeep and defense of this monumental feat of engineering, he oversees its delicate mechanisms while keeping watch for sabotage. Those who speak with him quickly discover that grave dangers threaten the integrity of the great dam. The Stonewrought Dam is one of the crowning achievements of dwarven stonecraft and engineering, holding back the massive waters of the Loch. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII bears the immense responsibility of maintaining its structure and operational machinery. Perched along the crest of the dam, he monitors the waterways, sluice gates, and structural stress points against the elements and local hazards.

Chief Hawkwind. Chief Hawkwind is the tribal leader of Camp Narache, the proving grounds nestled in the Red Cloud Mesa of Mulgore. Responsible for guiding the youth of the Shu'halo, he mentors new adventurers as they embark on their traditional rites of passage. Under his watchful gaze, young braves learn humility, respect for the land, and the strength needed to protect their people. Standing at the heart of Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind carries the solemn responsibility of preparing the next generation of tauren for the wider world. Red Cloud Mesa serves as a sheltered haven where fledgling hunters, shamans, druids, and warriors undertake the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. Hawkwind oversees these customs, ensuring that every youth learns duty and endurance before venturing beyond the safety of the mesa.

Christoph Jeffcoat. Christoph Jeffcoat is a Forsaken merchant stationed in the settlement of Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills. He supplies local crafters and travelers with essential trade goods, cooking seasonings, and specialty recipes. In an active war zone contested by the Alliance and the Syndicate, his mundane wares keep the northern Horde war effort running. While Tarren Mill stands as the Forsaken's military stronghold in Hillsbrad Foothills, a garrison cannot fight on malice alone. Christoph Jeffcoat handles the quiet, practical side of occupation, vending reagents, tools, threads, and spices to soldiers and traveling artisans. From the soothing spices required for local culinary recipes like turtle bisque to rare schematics and alchemical vials, Jeffcoat ensures that Horde forces passing through southern Lordaeron are fully provisioned for the battles against Southshore and the regional perils.

Chronormu. Chronormu, who goes by the mortal name Chromie, is a bronze dragon disguised as an energetic female gnome. Tasked with safeguarding the flow of time on Azeroth, she often works directly with mortals rather than observing from afar. In the Western Plaguelands, she quietly intervenes in the tragic aftermath of the Third War to right disrupted temporal threads. Though she appears to mortals as an eccentric and cheerful gnome named Chromie, Chronormu is a member of the bronze dragonflight serving under the Timeless One, Nozdormu. Bronze dragons are charged by the titans with guarding history and correcting disruptions in the timeways. In the form of a female gnome, she walks beside mortals as an approachable, optimistic peer.

Clarice Foster. Clarice Foster is a Forsaken woman residing deep beneath the bluffs of Mulgore within the Pools of Vision. Far from the plagued glades of Lordaeron, she spends her days in contemplation among the tauren seers and mystics. While most Forsaken remain in the northern lands of Lordaeron rebuilding their kingdom under the Undercity, Clarice Foster has traveled to the heart of the tauren lands in Kalimdor. Sheltered within the cavernous Pools of Vision beneath the mesa of Thunder Bluff, she dwells alongside Forsaken apothecaries and tauren shamans who study the spiritual and elemental mysteries of the earth.

Clerk Daltry. Clerk Daltry is the civic record keeper stationed in Darkshire Town Hall in Duskwood. Surrounded by ledgers and registry books, he helps investigate the village's past and track down historical records, even if his archives are somewhat neglected and out of date. While Darkshire struggles against encroaching beasts, undead horrors, and supernatural gloom, everyday civic duties fall to Clerk Daltry. Working out of the Darkshire Town Hall alongside Lord Ello Ebonlocke and the local council, Daltry maintains the town's historical ledgers, property rolls, and census data. In a region fractured by disaster, his records are among the few surviving links to the days before Grand Hamlet fell into shadow.

Cliffwatcher Longhorn. Cliffwatcher Longhorn is the stoic tauren leader stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Tasked with safeguarding the isolated Horde outpost, he coordinates defenses against encroaching Galak centaur and monitors the suspicious machinations of the Grimtotem tribe. Perched upon the soaring rock spires of Thousand Needles, Freewind Post relies on sharp eyes and steady leadership to survive. Cliffwatcher Longhorn oversees the day-to-day security of this precarious settlement. With hostile forces gathering on the canyon floor below and along neighboring ridges, Longhorn acts as the settlement's primary coordinator for scouting reports and defensive military efforts.

Coleman Farthing. Coleman Farthing is a bitter Forsaken survivor residing in the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. In life, he worked for the wealthy Agamand dynasty at their extensive flour mills in northern Tirisfal. Convinced to stay and defend the estate against the Scourge, he died alongside his fellow laborers, and now dedicates his undeath to exacting vengeance on his former masters. Before the Third War, Coleman Farthing earned an honest living as a laborer at the Agamand Mills, the largest milling and agricultural operation in Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge poured across Lordaeron, the aristocratic Agamand family refused to flee their valuable lands. Instead, they urged their household and laborers to take up arms alongside them, promising they could hold the farmsteads against the undead horde. Coleman and his fellow workers stayed, believing their masters—a decision that cost every last one of them their lives.

Collin Mauren. Collin Mauren is a human mage residing in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind City. A scholarly researcher and crafter of incantations, he experiments with exotic natural reagents to devise unique utility spells. Among his pursuits is assisting his acquaintance, the gnome engineer and explorer Gaxim Rustfizzle, with specialized arcane scrolls. Situated within Stormwind's bustling Mage Quarter, Collin Mauren spends his days pursuing the quieter, more practical applications of magic. Rather than chasing raw elemental power, he focuses on crafting arcane formulas that solve specific, logistical problems. Collin often turns to natural anomalies and raw components scavenged across Azeroth, weaving their intrinsic properties into functional magic scrolls and reagents for friends and travelers alike.

Colonel Kurzen. Colonel Conrad Kurzen was once a decorated and noble officer of the Stormwind Army, sent to lead an expedition into northern Stranglethorn Vale. After descending into sudden madness and tyranny, he turned his force into a rogue jungle militia operating out of an armed compound. Today, his former subordinates at the nearby Rebel Camp actively seek his death to end his reign of terror. Before his downfall, Colonel Conrad Kurzen was regarded in Stormwind as an exceptionally capable and noble officer. Trusted by the kingdom's leadership, he was granted command of an expeditionary unit dispatched south into the dense jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. However, deep within the humid wilds, Kurzen began to exhibit erratic behavior and extreme megalomania, declaring absolute sovereignty over the surrounding wilderness and abandoning his allegiance to Stormwind.

Commander Mar'alith. Commander Mar'alith is the stalwart night elf military commander directing the Cenarion Circle's vanguard at Cenarion Hold in Silithus. Clad in heavy armor and wielding a grand glaive, he coordinates the martial resistance against the silithid swarms and Twilight's Hammer cultists. Beneath his resolute leadership lies a deep personal sorrow regarding the mysterious fate of his beloved wife, Natalia. Stationed at the heart of Cenarion Hold, Commander Mar'alith bears the tremendous responsibility of safeguarding the Circle's desert bastion. While the druids unravel the ancient ecological and cosmic anomalies of Silithus, Mar'alith handles the grim, practical necessities of war. He oversees tactical strikes against the bustling silithid hives of Hive'Ashi, Hive'Zora, and Hive'Regal, ensuring that the relentless insectoid incursions do not overwhelm the expedition's central foothold.

Commander Springvale. Commander Springvale was once a devoted paladin and a commander at Shadowfang Keep. Slain alongside his men during the feral worgen slaughter orchestrated by Archmage Arugal, his vengeful spirit remains behind to haunt the castle halls. Even in death, his ghost fiercely guards the keep against all who enter. Before the ruin of Shadowfang Keep, Commander Springvale stood as an honorable paladin dedicated to the Holy Light. Leading the garrison in Silverpine Forest, he oversaw the keep's security during the fraught days following the fall of Lordaeron to the Scourge.

Cookie. Cookie is an elite murloc serving as the ship's cook aboard the juggernaut hidden deep within the Deadmines. An unusual recruit among the Defias Brotherhood, he tends the crew's cauldrons beneath the watchful eye of Captain Greenskin and Edwin VanCleef. He is the only entirely optional boss encountered within the underground dry dock. Beneath the decks of the towering juggernaut in the Ironclad Cove, cooking duty falls neither to a human outrider nor a goblin engineer, but to a solitary murloc known simply as Cookie. How he came by the position is anyone's guess. Whatever doubts the rest of the crew might harbor about a murloc presiding over their rations, pirates are rarely in a position to be picky, and in the underworld of Moonbrook, a meal is a meal.

Corithras Moonrage. Corithras Moonrage is a night elf scholar and quest giver stationed in the village of Dolanaar on Teldrassil. He guides newly arrived adventurers in understanding the nature of the great World Tree and tasks them with maintaining its sacred moonwells. Through his lessons, he reveals both the spiritual importance of Teldrassil and the growing burdens carried by the kaldorei. Residing in the shaded settlement of Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage serves as an instructor to travelers leaving the sheltered bounds of Shadowglen. As young kaldorei venture into the wider boughs of Teldrassil, Corithras ensures they understand the history of their new home. He teaches that survival in this changing era requires vigilance and reverence for the natural order.

Councilman Millstipe. Councilman Millstipe is a member of Darkshire's governing council, residing within the town hall of Duskwood. Deeply resentful of royal neglect and judicial meddling from the capital, he actively seeks retribution against criminals who endanger the darkened region. While Darkshire struggles under the shadow of the undead and ferocious beast attacks, its local council fights an uphill battle against the bureaucracy of Stormwind City. Councilman Millstipe represents the town's growing bitterness toward the crown. When the notorious grave robber Dextren Ward was caught selling freshly dug corpses to the necromancer Morbent Fel, Darkshire's leaders sentenced him to death. Instead, Stormwind's House of Nobles intervened, commuting Ward's execution and locking him safely away inside the Stormwind Stockade.

Count Remington Ridgewell. Count Remington Ridgewell is a wealthy human aristocrat found in the Petitioner's Chamber within Stormwind Keep. As a member of the House of Nobles, he prides himself on curating the finest private collection of rare historical artifacts, heirlooms, and fine art in the kingdom. Remington Ridgewell represents the elite tastes of the House of Nobles, taking immense pride in his family's personal museum of jewelry and artifacts. Rather than concerning himself with military campaigns or local uprisings, the Count spends his considerable wealth acquiring relics from fallen civilizations and fallen houses across Azeroth. To expand his prestigious gallery, he finances daring adventurers and employs field agents such as Mayara Brightwing, dispatching them to retrieve priceless oddities from perilous ruins, from the mountain redoubts of Alterac to the volcanic wastes of the Burning Steppes.

Crane Operator Bigglefuzz. Crane Operator Bigglefuzz is a goblin dockhand working the heavy machinery at the port of Ratchet. After an overloaded crane mishap scattered cargo across the docks, he finds himself desperate to recover a valuable stolen bottle before his superiors notice. Like many goblin dockworkers, Crane Operator Bigglefuzz prioritized efficiency and haste over basic safety margins. While attempting to hoist an excessively heavy haul from a merchant vessel, his crane buckled, sending crates crashing down across the Ratchet wharves. In the ensuing chaos, opportunistic scoundrels swept in, leaving Bigglefuzz to scramble to clean up the mess and salvage the most precious goods before Gazlowe or the local port masters dock his pay.

Craven Drok. Craven Drok is a wandering orc found skulking in the dimly lit tunnels of the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. True to his moniker, he keeps to the dark corners of the city, occasionally reaching out to travelers willing to help with a delicate matter: how the Alliance sees the Horde. While most orcs of Orgrimmar proudly walk the sunlit avenues of the Valley of Honor or the Valley of Strength, Craven Drok avoids the daylight entirely. He haunts the winding, subterranean paths of the Cleft of Shadow, an enclave typically reserved for warlocks, rogues, and practitioners of less honorable trades. Drok lives up to his cowardly reputation, preferring to stay out of sight while hiring passersby to carry out his discreet errands, including an errand concerning the Horde's standing with the Alliance.

Cyrus Therepentous. Cyrus Therepentous is a formidable black dragonspawn residing in the cavernous depths of Slither Rock in the Burning Steppes. Rather than immediately striking down intruders, he tests daring mortals to see if they possess the strength to serve the purposes of the Black dragonflight. Secluded inside a cavern at Slither Rock, Cyrus Therepentous oversees the volcanic crags of the Burning Steppes. Like many of his kind, he views mortal travelers with immense condescension, declaring that only fools would disturb his lair. Yet beneath his ferocious exterior lies a cold calculation: rather than consuming every trespasser on sight, he offers them a lethal challenge against his minions, willing to exploit those resilient enough to survive the trials of flame.

Dalar Dawnweaver. Dalar Dawnweaver is a former archmage of Dalaran who now serves the Forsaken at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Slain during the Scourge's destruction of the magi's city and later freed from the Lich King's control, he turns his magical intellect toward dissecting regional threats. From the shadows of the tomb, he directs efforts to understand Dalaran's lingering presence and undo the madness of Archmage Arugal. In life, Dalar Dawnweaver held high rank among the Kirin Tor, walking the halls of the Violet Citadel when Dalaran was a pinnacle of arcane mastery. His mortal life ended when the Scourge sacked the city to pave the way for Archimonde's summoning. Reanimated into the mindless thrall of the Lich King, Dalar broke free alongside Lady Sylvanas Windrunner when the Scourge's grip faltered. Now stationed at the Sepulcher, he retains the piercing intellect of an archmage, turned entirely toward safeguarding the Forsaken realm.

Daphne Stilwell. Daphne Stilwell tends an isolated orchard nestled atop the coastal cliffs of Westfall overlooking the Longshore. Together with her husband Jordan, she fled turmoil in the north and relocated south, quietly aiding the Church of the Holy Light while defending her home from nearby outlaws. Perched on the bluffs to the west of Moonbrook and the exit of the Deadmines, Daphne Stilwell manages a secluded homestead and apple orchard. From below along the Longshore or above on gryphon routes south to Stranglethorn Vale, the small farm looks quiet and unassuming. Yet running a homestead in modern Westfall is anything but safe. Despite the encroaching bandits and roaming scavengers, Daphne diligently works her trees and keeps watch over her isolated patch of land.

Darcy. Darcy is a waitress serving drinks and warm meals at the Lakeshire Inn. Amid the constant threats looming over Redridge, she keeps her spirits up by looking after local defenders—particularly Guard Parker. Behind the busy counter of the Lakeshire Inn, Darcy works day and night to keep the town's weary militia fed and watered. Lakeshire sits under constant pressure from gnolls and Blackrock orcs, making the tavern one of the few places of warmth left in the settlement. Darcy takes a personal interest in the guards posted around town, frequently recruiting traveling adventurers to run hot meals and friendly errands out to those stationed along the borders.

Dark Cleric Beryl. Dark Cleric Beryl is a Forsaken priest trainer stationed in the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. He guides newly awakened undead priests as they learn to wield shadow magic and adapt to their new, unholy existence under the Dark Lady. Residing on the upper floor of the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, Dark Cleric Beryl serves the Forsaken by mentoring nascent priests. Beryl teaches that a Forsaken priest's power comes from darkness and shadow, yet one must also know the light before mastering the dark. He assists newly risen practitioners as they turn their focus toward shadow and the dark arts, guiding them through early trials like crafting their Garments of Darkness and proving their dedication to the new path.

Dark Iron Ambassador. The Dark Iron Ambassador is an emissary of the Dark Iron clan found deep within Gnomeregan. His presence raises questions about the clan's interest in the ruined gnome capital. The Dark Iron Ambassador is found among the dangers of irradiated Gnomeregan. He represents the Dark Iron clan, but the purpose of his mission is not explained.

Darkmaster Gandling. Darkmaster Gandling is the mortal headmaster of Scholomance, overseeing the instruction and training of necromancers for the Cult of the Damned. Operating from the depths of the ruined Keep of Caer Darrow, he serves the Scourge by orchestrating gruesome magical experiments upon the living and dead alike. Within the dark halls beneath Caer Darrow, Darkmaster Gandling governs Scholomance, the premier academy for the Scourge's aspiring necromancers. A living human serving the Cult of the Damned, Gandling worked alongside the lich Ras Frostwhisper to orchestrate atrocities against countless innocent captives taken from the surrounding lands. Students who enter his classrooms are instructed in plague brewing, reanimation, and flesh sculpting.

Darn Talongrip. Darn Talongrip is an orc scout stationed along the frontier of the Stonetalon Mountains near Malaka'jin. He monitors local threats in the crags and helps coordinate Horde communication between forward outposts and regional commanders. Darn Talongrip watches the rugged ascents leading into Stonetalon from the southern Barrens. Stationed in the settlement of Malaka'jin, Darn directs recruits toward the Horde's new fronts in Ashenvale. His post serves as an early line of contact for travelers winding upward into contested peaks.

Darsok Swiftdagger. Darsok Swiftdagger is an orc warrior and scout stationed at the Crossroads in the heart of the Barrens. Known for his fierce hatred of harpies, he directs Horde adventurers north into the Dry Hills to break the avian matriarchy harassing travelers and settlements. He is also an old friend of Witch Doctor Jin'Zil in Malaka'jin. Amid the bustling hub of the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger keeps a sharp eye on the threats creeping out of the northern scrubland. The trade artery connecting Durotar, Mulgore, and the northern reaches is under constant siege, not only from raiders and centaur, but from organized aerial hunters. Darsok focuses his wrath on the Witchwing harpies, whose roosts in the Dry Hills northwest of the Forgotten Pools directly threaten northern caravans.

Daryl the Youngling. Daryl the Youngling is a human hunter residing at Farstrider Lodge in the southeastern hills of Loch Modan. Eager to prove his marksmanship among veteran dwarven trackers, he challenges traveling adventurers to hone their wilderness skills and test their mettle against the local beasts. Farstrider Lodge is primarily a haven for dwarven mountaineers, trackers, and seasoned outdoorsmen who watch over the wilderness of Loch Modan. Daryl stands out as a young human striving to earn his place alongside these veteran stalkers. Rather than relying on mere bravado, he actively seeks to measure his hunting instincts against other travelers, issuing challenges to hunt down the tough wild boars and beasts roaming the crags and lakeshore.

Dashel Stonefist. Dashel Stonefist is a notorious dwarven brawler found loitering among the shaded alleys of Old Town in Stormwind City. Nicknamed "Fist" for his quick temper and heavy hands, he is a familiar fixture of the city's rougher underbelly. Beneath his thuggish exterior, he maintains quietly dangerous connections that draw the eye of covert investigators. Tucked away in the narrow, cobblestone backstreets of Old Town, Dashel Stonefist looks like any other drunken, combative dwarf looking for an excuse to throw a punch. Locals and city guards know him simply as "Fist," a moniker earned through countless street fights and scuffles outside tavern doors. Yet Dashel is far more than a simple tavern brawler; his presence in Old Town puts him right at the nexus of Stormwind's underworld, where smugglers, cutpurses, and political agitators exchange coin and rumors away from the prying eyes of Cathedral Square.

David Trias. David Trias is the Forsaken rogue trainer stationed in Deathknell. He instructs freshly awakened undead in the arts of stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft to aid Queen Sylvanas and the Forsaken. Positioned amidst the tombstones and ruins of Deathknell, David Trias is tasked with identifying and training those newly risen undead who possess a talent for unseen murder. For the fledgling Forsaken, survival requires more than sheer force of arms; it demands precise strikes from the dark. Trias decrypts orders and teaches initiates how to wield daggers, conceal their movements, and turn their reanimated reflexes into lethal precision against the living and the Scourge.

Dawnwatcher Selgorm. Dawnwatcher Selgorm is a human representative of the Argent Dawn stationed upon the Craftsmen's Terrace in Darnassus. Acting as an observer and liaison in the night elven capital, he monitors reports of shadowy cult activity and dark threats stirring across northern Kalimdor. While the Argent Dawn focuses heavily on the undead scourge festering in the Eastern Plaguelands, their vigilance extends anywhere ancient evil takes root. Dawnwatcher Selgorm stands watch in Darnassus, bridging the gap between the insular night elves and the broader crusade against malevolence. From the Craftsmen's Terrace, he gathers intelligence on emerging threats in Kalimdor's wilderness, enlisting capable Alliance travelers to strike at cultists and dark powers before their influence can corrupt the realm.

Dawnwatcher Shaedlass. Dawnwatcher Shaedlass is a night elf affiliated with the Argent Dawn, stationed within the Craftsmen's Terrace of Darnassus. Acting as a quiet eyes-and-ears operative in Kalimdor, he seeks news of his fellow order members sent on perilous reconnaissance into hostile lands. While the Argent Dawn is most famous for its bitter crusade against the Scourge in the Eastern Plaguelands, its vigilance extends far beyond Lordaeron. Dawnwatcher Shaedlass maintains a presence in the night elven capital of Darnassus, watching over the faction's interests in Kalimdor. From his quiet post on the Craftsmen's Terrace, he keeps tabs on covert expeditions against dark cults and corrupting powers that threaten the wider world.

Dazalar. Dazalar is a night elf hunter trainer stationed in Dolanaar within Teldrassil. He guides fledgling sentinels and scouts as they hone their marksmanship and learn the sacred art of bonding with the wild beasts of the great boughs. Standing within the settlement of Dolanaar, Dazalar serves as a primary mentor for young hunters venturing beyond the sheltered glade of Shadowglen. Night elf society relies heavily on its rangers and sentinels to patrol the wilderness, and Dazalar ensures newcomers possess the discipline and patience necessary to protect Teldrassil's fragile ecosystem.

Deathguard Bartholomew. Deathguard Bartholomew is a vigilant Forsaken soldier stationed in the town of Brill. Tasked with maintaining security across Tirisfal Glades, he helps travelers navigate the blighted settlement and assists in enforcing discipline among local defenders. Standing watch in the settlement of Brill, Deathguard Bartholomew represents the stalwart military backbone of the Forsaken. Like his fellow Deathguards throughout Tirisfal Glades, he defends reclaimed territory from lingering Scourge, fanatical Scarlet Crusaders, and any other threats to Lady Sylvanas's domain. In addition to keeping watch, he provides directions to travelers attempting to navigate the town's facilities and participates in maintaining orderly conduct among the newly risen.

Deathguard Burgess. Deathguard Burgess is a Forsaken sentry stationed in the town of Brill within Tirisfal Glades. Standing watch over the settlement, he keeps order and directs travelers to vital services across the hamlet. Positioned in the settlement of Brill just north of the Undercity, Deathguard Burgess serves as one of the town guards maintaining security against the Scourge and Scarlet Crusade. Like other Deathguards throughout Tirisfal Glades, Burgess aids arriving Forsaken by providing directions to local tradesfolk, class trainers, and civic services, keeping the vulnerable outpost running smoothly.

Deathguard Dillinger. Deathguard Dillinger is a Forsaken sentry stationed in Brill within Tirisfal Glades. Standing watch over the town's perimeter, he directs newly arrived undead toward necessary services and tasks recruits with keeping the local Scourge remnants at bay. As a member of the Forsaken Deathguard, Dillinger stands at the entrance of Brill, serving as both a frontline protector and an orienting guide for travelers emerging from Deathknell. He provides directions to town amenities such as the inn, the town hall, and local trainers, helping newly awakened undead navigate their new reality under the Dark Lady's rule.

Deathguard Humbert. Deathguard Humbert is a Forsaken sentry stationed in Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills. Assigned to monitor the encroaching Alliance presence, he finds himself in an embarrassing predicament after losing his military gear to the dwarves of Dun Garok. While tasked with maintaining Tarren Mill's perimeter against regional threats, Deathguard Humbert suffered a humiliating setback. Sent by High Executor Darthalia to watch Dun Garok from a hidden camp, he left one morning to gather firewood, and dwarven scouts from Dun Garok made off with his prized sword and assorted equipment, leaving the undead soldier desperate to salvage his pride and armament before high command takes notice.

Deathguard Linnea. Deathguard Linnea is a Forsaken soldier stationed at a Deathguard waystation in southeastern Tirisfal Glades. She helps secure the roads between Brill and the eastern borders, watching for threats posed by the Scarlet Crusade and lingering Scourge. Adventurers passing along the main thoroughfares often assist her unit with patrol duties. Deathguard Linnea stands sentinel at a small fortified post southeast of Brill. Life—or unlife—on patrol in Tirisfal Glades is treacherous, as the Forsaken must vigilantly defend their fledgling realm against Scarlet Crusade infiltrators and mindless Scourge prowling the wilderness. Stationed alongside her fellow guards, Linnea oversees patrol efforts along the roadway, coordinating reports with local authorities such as Magistrate Sevren in Brill to keep the eastern road toward the Bulwark secure.

Deathguard Samsa. Deathguard Samsa is a Forsaken sentry stationed in Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills. Tasked with maintaining Horde vigilance on a tense frontier, he directs traveling champions to strike at local threats encroaching on the settlement. Standing watch in Tarren Mill, Deathguard Samsa represents the defensive backbone of the Forsaken in the contested Hillsbrad Foothills. Tarren Mill serves as the Horde's primary outpost in the region, facing immediate pressure from Alliance outposts like Southshore as well as savage local wildlife. Samsa's duties involve securing the perimeter and directing capable adventurers to eliminate threats before they endanger the encampment.

Deathguard Simmer. Deathguard Simmer is a Forsaken soldier stationed just outside Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. He sizes up newly risen Forsaken and sends them to raid the human pumpkin farm to the west, patrolled by the Scarlet Crusade, for reagents the apothecaries of Brill need. Posted just outside Deathknell, Deathguard Simmer represents the Forsaken military line holding the border between the safe haven of Deathknell and the wider perils of Tirisfal Glades. The region crawls with living humans—most notably the fanatical Scarlet Crusade—who view all undead as abominations to be purged with fire and blade. Simmer tests fledgling Forsaken by sending them west to the Solliden Farmstead, where the Scarlet Crusade patrols from its nearby tower, to steal ten pumpkins and carry them to Apothecary Johaan in Brill.

Deathstalker Faerleia. Deathstalker Faerleia is an operative of the Forsaken intelligence agency stationed deep within enemy territory inside Pyrewood Village. Operating out of the settlement's town hall, she orchestrates covert strikes against the Pyrewood Council, the village leaders Arugal uses as puppets. As an agent of the Deathstalkers—the covert intelligence and assassin branch of the Undercity—Faerleia is tasked with infiltrating Pyrewood Village in southern Silverpine Forest. The isolated human enclave harbors dark secrets, including a curse that transforms its populace under the night sky. Stationed within the upper levels of the town hall, Faerleia coordinates operations to disrupt the settlement from the inside, calling on Horde operatives to eliminate the influential members of the Pyrewood Council.

Deathstalker Lesh. Deathstalker Lesh is a Forsaken rogue serving as a forward scout at Southpoint Tower in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Operating directly under High Executor Darthalia, she keeps watch over the human farms in the Hillsbrad Fields to gauge when the Forsaken should strike. Perched at Southpoint Tower on the southern road through the Hillsbrad Foothills, Deathstalker Lesh monitors the human farmers and town militia working the nearby Hillsbrad Fields. As an operative of the Deathstalkers—the Forsaken's secretive intelligence and assassination network—Lesh tracks enemy movements and numbers for High Executor Darthalia in Tarren Mill. When the moment is right, Lesh sends word to Darthalia with a coded message, 'The raven's cry from the west doth beckon', signaling that Hillsbrad is ripe for the Forsaken's attack.

Rane Yorick. Deathstalker Rane Yorick is an operative of the Forsaken intelligence guild stationed deep in Silverpine Forest. Together with her brother Quinn, she was sent to scout the farms of northern Silverpine and report to High Executor Hadrec. The Deathstalkers serve as Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's eyes, ears, and blades across Lordaeron. Operating out of shadows and hidden posts, agents like Rane Yorick monitor the wilderness for threats that could disrupt Forsaken dominion. When sent to scout northern Silverpine Forest, Rane and her brother Quinn found themselves hemmed in by surrounding feral dangers, turning an undercover reconnaissance mission into a battle for survival.

Deathstalker Vincent. Deathstalker Vincent was a Forsaken scout sent alongside Deathstalker Adamant to infiltrate Shadowfang Keep. Slain by the mad mage Arugal, his corpse remains inside the stronghold as a grim warning to any who challenge the feral worgen within. Before the Forsaken could launch a full-scale assault against the beasts holding Shadowfang Keep, intelligence on the fortress's interior was desperately needed. Two operatives from the Deathstalkers, the intelligence arm of the Forsaken, slipped past the barricades: Vincent and Adamant. Their mission ended in disaster. While Adamant was captured and locked away in a dungeon cell, Vincent was dragged directly before Shadowfang's master. Refusing to bend the knee or serve Arugal's dark designs, Vincent was executed on the spot, his body discarded on the stone floor to rot as a testament to the mage's fury.

Deathwing. Deathwing the Destroyer, once known as Neltharion the Earth-Warder, is the fallen Dragon Aspect of the black dragonflight. Driven mad by the dark whispers of the Old Gods, he turned against the other Aspects and plunged the world into fire and turmoil. Though defeated near Grim Batol after the Second War and believed slain or hidden away, the terror of his legacy still haunts the deep places of Azeroth. Before he was known as the Destroyer, Neltharion was granted dominion over the earth and the subterranean vaults of Azeroth by the titan pantheon. Yet dwelling so close to the world's deepest chambers exposed him to the insidious whispers of the imprisoned Old Gods. During the ancient War of the Ancients, the madness took complete hold. He deceived the other Dragon Aspects into imbuing a golden disc, the Dragon Soul, with portions of their essence under the guise of halting the Burning Legion, only to turn the terrible weapon against his allies and unleash catastrophic devastation.

Deino. Deino is a Darkspear troll mage trainer dwelling within the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar. Alongside her fellow practitioners, she teaches emerging arcanists how to master the arcane and harness volatile elemental forces. She also directs seasoned spellcasters across Kalimdor to unravel ancient magical anomalies and seek out reclusive tutors. Standing amidst the totems, huts, and tranquil waters of the Valley of Spirits, Deino offers instruction to Horde mages who find themselves in the orcish capital. Troll spellcasters traditionally walk a fine line between spiritual reverence and pure arcane mastery, and Deino represents this unique path within the Darkspear tribe, standing shoulder to shoulder with fellow instructors Enyo and Pephredo.

Delgren the Purifier. Delgren the Purifier is a human paladin stationed at Maestra's Post on the northern edge of Ashenvale. Operating alongside comrades Balthule Shadowstrike and Feero Ironhand, he aids the night elves in cleansing demonic and shadow magic threatening the frontier, with a particular focus on the sinister Cult of the Dark Strand. Human paladins are a rare sight deep within the ancient forests of Kalimdor, but Delgren the Purifier arrived with a mission. Affiliated with the Argent Dawn, Delgren traveled west with a cadre of holy warriors determined to assist the Alliance's new night elf allies against the lingering evils of demons and undead remnants from the Third War. Stationed near the border of Darkshore and Ashenvale, he maintains a watchful vigil over travelers passing south from Auberdine.

Demisette Cloyce. Demisette Cloyce is a human warlock trainer sequestered in the subterranean crypts beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. Operating under cover of the city's underbelly, she instructs practitioners of the fel arts and directs promising acolytes toward deeper, more dangerous arcane mysteries. While Stormwind's authorities maintain an outward veneer of order and holy righteousness, practitioners of fel magic convene in the dank cellars beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in the Mage Quarter. Demisette Cloyce makes her residence down within these catacombs, tutoring warlocks willing to brave the forbidden arts. She holds little patience for the untrained or the uninitiated, advising her students that the dark energies corrupt only those lacking the discipline to master them.

Denalan. Denalan is an accomplished night elf herbalist and botanist who tends a quiet lakeside plot along the eastern shore of Lake Al'Ameth. Working under a simple awning, he devotes his days to studying the island's plant life and seeking botanical remedies for the strange corruption affecting Teldrassil. He frequently enlists young adventurers to gather samples, study violent timberlings, and test enchanted soils. While many kaldorei focus on martial vigilance or high druidic rites, Denalan pursues the patient, meticulous craft of herbalism. Stationed along the tranquil eastern banks of Lake Al'Ameth, he has established a modest research camp consisting of a cloth awning, simple field tools, and tidy rows of cultivated planter boxes. Rather than retreating to the grand barrows of Darnassus, he prefers to remain close to the loam, directly examining the unusual flora that has sprouted since the planting of the new World Tree.

Dendrite Starblaze. Dendrite Starblaze is a night elf druid residing in the sacred village of Nighthaven within Moonglade. Serving the Cenarion Circle, he acts as a vital mentor and guide for budding druids of both night elf and tauren descent. Through him, practitioners are summoned to the holy grove to master essential rites such as cleansing toxins and communing with nature's forms. Perched within Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze represents the nonpartisan, enduring spirit of the Cenarion Circle. When novice druids learn to attune their spirits to Teleport: Moonglade, Dendrite is among the first to welcome them upon arrival. He bridges the gap between ancient Kaldorei tradition and the emerging path of the tauren, treating all who heed the call of the wild as kin beneath the boughs of the sacred haven.

Deputy Feldon. Deputy Feldon is a member of the Redridge town guard stationed just south of the Great Lakeshire Bridge. Tasked with watching the primary road into Lakeshire, he keeps a nervous vigil against the aggressive gnoll packs creeping toward the town perimeter. Standing watch near the southern approach to the Lakeshire bridge, Deputy Feldon represents an overextended town guard fighting to keep basic trade and travel routes open. With the Blackrock orcs pressing from the north and gnoll packs overrunning the southern hills, guardsmen like Feldon are stretched to their limits. Unable to leave his post without compromising the town's perimeter, he relies on passing adventurers to cull the gnolls encroaching on the roadway before they can cut Lakeshire off entirely.

Deputy Rainer. Deputy Rainer is a Stormwind Army officer stationed outside Westbrook Garrison along Elwynn Forest's western boundary. Tasked with holding the line against encroaching gnoll packs and bandits bleeding over from Westfall, he coordinates local defense efforts when official military reinforcements fail to arrive. Westbrook Garrison serves as Elwynn Forest's westernmost bulwark, positioned just along the boundary road leading into Westfall. As political paralysis in Stormwind City keeps the bulk of the army stationed abroad or tied up in bureaucracy, border posts like Westbrook are left severely understaffed. Deputy Rainer stands outside the tower to organize what little defense the garrison can muster. With local roads constantly threatened by aggressive Riverpaw gnolls and wandering thieves, Rainer is forced to rely on passing travelers and mercenary adventurers rather than official crown regiments to keep the forest trails secure.

Devrak. Devrak is an orc wind rider master stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Serving as the primary aerial conduit of central Kalimdor, he oversees the Horde's network of wyverns shuttling supplies and couriers between Durotar, Mulgore, and frontier outposts. He also ensures that crucial logistics, such as game meats and prepared hides, travel smoothly to the Horde's capitals. Positioned at the intersection of Kalimdor's major trade routes, Devrak tends the wyverns that keep the Horde unified across vast distances. The Crossroads sits exposed under the baking sun, vulnerable to quilboar, centaur, and Alliance scouts alike, making rapid aerial transit indispensable. Devrak handles both seasoned wayfarers and untested messengers, pairing riders with trained wind riders capable of crossing the savannah and reaching the mountain heights of Mulgore or the stone canyons of Durotar.

Dextren Ward. Dextren Ward is an infamous criminal and grave robber locked away inside the Stormwind Stockade. Before his capture, he profited by exhuming bodies from Duskwood's Raven Hill Cemetery and delivering them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Now caught in the midst of the prison's bloody uprising, he remains marked for death by the town council of Darkshire. Before ending up in chains beneath the streets of Stormwind, Dextren Ward conducted a grim and lucrative business in the fog-choked woods of Duskwood. Raven Hill Cemetery was already a site of sorrow and growing horror, but Ward treated its burial grounds as a private quarry. Rather than hunting merely for trinkets and heirlooms left with the dead, Ward dealt in flesh, unearthing fresh graves to supply local dark practitioners.

Dirania Silvershine. Dirania Silvershine is a night elf resident of Shadowglen in Teldrassil. Deeply loyal and observant, she watches over the tranquil grove and looks out for her companion Iverron when his reckless ventures land him in peril. Dirania stands among the tranquil boughs of Shadowglen, the secluded vale where young night elves begin their service to Kalimdor and the Alliance. While many in the barrow mounds and sanctuaries look to broad spiritual duties, Dirania stays mindful of those nearest to her, attentive to the quiet dangers that stir even in the heart of Teldrassil.

Dirge Quikcleave. Dirge Quikcleave is a goblin culinary master and vendor holding court inside the inn at Gadgetzan. Renowned across Azeroth for his inventive dishes, he trains seasoned chefs seeking to master artisan-level cooking. Dirge Quikcleave resides in the dusty desert outpost of Gadgetzan, serving drinks and meats to parched travelers passing through the Tanaris sands. Despite operating out of a frontier tavern, he claims the mantle of the greatest living culinary artist in Azeroth. City cooking trainers across the world direct their most promising students to Dirge when they have exhausted ordinary lessons. His kitchen mastery is known for demanding, unusual ingredients—from giant clam meat and eggs for his Clamlette creations to the exotic beasts of distant shores.

Doan Karhan. Doan Karhan is a human scholar and practitioner of the dark arts dwelling isolated in the southern Barrens. He has dedicated his life to researching the demonic artifacts of the Burning Legion, especially the enigmatic Orb of Soran'ruk. Tucked away in a solitary camp in the wild savannah of the southern Barrens, Doan Karhan lives far from the civilized bastions of the Alliance. Rather than seeking ordinary solitude, he retreated to the wilderness to study dangerous demonic relics unmolested. Doan holds deep lore concerning powerful fel vessels, possessing the Orb of Zargain and obsessing over the legendary Orb of Soran'ruk. Practicing warlocks often seek him out when delving into artifact crafting and dark rituals.

Doctor Gregory Victor. Doctor Gregory Victor is a Forsaken surgeon stationed at the Horde outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Renowned as the premier trauma physician within the Horde, he evaluates aspiring medics seeking to master advanced triage and battlefield first aid. His cold, clinical efficiency keeps frontline warriors stitched together amidst bitter regional conflicts. While many view Forsaken apothecaries with suspicion, Doctor Gregory Victor serves the Horde through practical battlefield surgery rather than blighted alchemy. Stationed deep within the contested Arathi Highlands at Hammerfall, he operates on soldiers battered by Syndicate brigands, Boulderfist ogres, and Alliance forces. His station doubles as the primary proving ground for Horde field medics, demanding ruthless efficiency and prioritizing critical patients under intense pressure.

Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen. Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen serves as the trauma surgeon and chief physician of Alliance Trauma in Theramore Isle. Stationed within Foothold Citadel, he trains the island's healers and evaluates medics who wish to master the highest tiers of field triage and bandage work. Located on the ground floor of Foothold Citadel in Theramore Isle, Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen oversees the medical care of Lady Jaina Proudmoore's forces and trains the outpost's frontline healers. Facing harsh conditions in Dustwallow Marsh, VanHowzen insists on rigorous field competence, personally putting experienced medics through an intense triage test to ensure they can prioritize critical wounds under severe pressure.

Donova Snowden. Donova Snowden is an intrepid dwarven researcher encamped alongside the thermal waters near Frostfire Hot Springs in Winterspring. Despite the bitter cold and hostile wildlife, she studies the strange thermal activity of the region and monitors the increasingly corrupted Winterfall furbolgs. While most travelers stick to the safety of Everlook, Donova Snowden has chosen to camp in the freezing wilderness near the Frostfire Hot Springs. She spends her days investigating the curious geothermic anomalies bubbling up through the permafrost, as well as the dark influences encroaching upon Winterspring's native wildlife. Practical and determined, she enlists passing adventurers of both the Alliance and the Horde to gather samples and help curb local threats.

Donyal Tovald. Donyal Tovald is a human steward serving in the Royal Library within Stormwind Keep. Under an initiative begun by the young King Anduin Wrynn, he oversees the care of the kingdom's books and works to distribute copies of historical texts to the broader public. Located in the quiet alcoves of the Royal Library wing within Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald tends to the kingdom's vast collection of historical accounts, scrolls, and scholarly volumes. While the library primarily serves the nobility and royal court, young King Anduin Wrynn has sponsored an initiative to make knowledge more accessible to ordinary citizens. Tovald handles the preservation and copying of these texts, helping ensure that the lessons and triumphs of the Alliance are not forgotten amidst the kingdom's turbulent political climate.

Seer Wiserunner. This respected tauren elder is known as Seer Wiserunner, serving his people faithfully in the rolling hills of Mulgore. From a cave in the hills northwest of Bloodhoof Village, he aids young tauren braves as they undertake the traditional rites of passage that lead toward spiritual adulthood. Seer Wiserunner stands among the gentle bluffs of Mulgore as an elder and mystic of the shu'halo. When young tauren complete their initial trials of strength and vision, they are sent to seek his counsel during their ancestral rites. He interprets visions of the Earth Mother and guides the youth on how to honor their forebears, offering the steady wisdom that binds the scattered nomadic tribes into a unified community.

Doras. Doras is the Horde's chief Wind Rider Master in Orgrimmar, perched high upon the wooden tower overlooking the Valley of Strength. He oversees the capital's wyverns, dispatching couriers, scouts, and travelers across Kalimdor. Perched on the wooden platform above the Valley of Strength, Doras tends the winged predators known as wind riders or wyverns. Since the Horde settled Durotar, these cunning, leathery-winged beasts have become the backbone of Horde communication and transit across Kalimdor. Doras manages their care, pairing resting mounts with riders and ensuring critical messages and reinforcements reach remote outposts like the Crossroads, Thunder Bluff, and settlements deep in Ashenvale or Dustwallow Marsh.

Doren. Lieutenant Doren commands the Rebel Camp nestled in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Once an officer under Colonel Kurzen, Doren led a mutiny after his superior and fellow expeditionaries descended into madness. Now, he directs a guerrilla resistance determined to uncover the source of the affliction and eliminate Kurzen. Lieutenant Doren initially deployed to Stranglethorn Vale under the banner of Stormwind and the command of Colonel Kurzen. The expedition was meant to establish a foothold in the wild southern jungle, but it quickly soured as Kurzen and his inner circle succumbed to an erratic, violent insanity. Refusing to abandon their sanity or their honor, Doren and a cadre of loyalists broke rank. They fled north and carved out the Rebel Camp along the road, choosing defection over servitude to a madman.

Dorn Plainstalker. Dorn Plainstalker is a solitary tauren elder residing in the Weathered Nook overlooking the canyons of Thousand Needles. He serves as an overseer of traditional rite of passage trials, challenging Horde adventurers to prove their character and fortitude. Through trials of faith, endurance, strength, and lore, he tests whether travelers are worthy servants of the Earth Mother and their people. Secluded in a shallow cave high atop the canyon ridges of the Weathered Nook, Dorn Plainstalker lives apart from the bustle of Freewind Post. Reaching his mountain redoubt requires winding along the sheer northern cliffs overlooking the towering mesas below. From this quiet vantage point, Dorn maintains ancient customs and judges those who seek guidance in the harsh southern barrens.

Drum Fel. Drum Fel is an orc commander stationed at the Horde outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Alongside his wife, Korin, he directs military efforts to secure the refuge against encroaching trolls, ogres, and human remnants. His strategic push is vital to carving out a lasting foothold for the Horde in Arathi. Situated within the fortified refuge of Hammerfall, Drum Fel oversees the defense and territorial expansion of the Horde in Arathi. Surrounded by rival factions, he coordinates military strikes against the Witherbark forest trolls and the Boulderfist ogre clan holding Boulder'gor and Boulderfist Hall. Drum recognizes that Hammerfall cannot merely survive through isolation; it must break its neighbors' strength to thrive. To that end, he regularly directs veteran champions into hostile territory to disrupt regional threats before they can mount an assault on the Horde encampment.

Drusilla La Salle. Drusilla La Salle is a human warlock trainer situated in the shadowed graveyard outside Northshire Abbey. Operating on the fringes of the Holy Order of Northshire, she mentors fledgling spellcasters in the dark arts of summoning and shadow. When forbidden knowledge slips beyond the abbey walls, she does not hesitate to use opportunism and dark magic to claim it. While paladins and priests practice beneath the stained glass of Northshire Abbey, Drusilla La Salle remains outdoors among the headstones of the graveyard. Practicing demonology and fel magic is deeply taboo within the kingdom of Stormwind, forcing warlocks to dwell on the periphery of polite society. Drusilla provides early instruction to novice warlocks who have received tainted correspondence, teaching them how to harness shadow power without drawing the immediate wrath of abbey authorities.

Duke Hydraxis. Duke Hydraxis is a noble water elemental commanding the Hydraxian Waterlords from a remote, wave-battered islet off the coast of Azshara. Pledged to Neptulon the Tidehunter, he rallies mortal adventurers to strike against his ancient elemental rivals, particularly Ragnaros the Firelord. Perched on a solitary rock northeast of the Ravencrest Monument in Azshara, Duke Hydraxis serves as the primary emissary of the Hydraxian Waterlords. While most elementals bound to Azeroth are hostile and chaotic, Hydraxis acts with measured purpose. As a devoted vassal of Neptulon the Tidehunter, he considers water the purest and most essential of the primal forces. He watches the rising turmoil across Azeroth with cold scrutiny, seeking champions capable of shifting the balance of elemental warfare.

Durnan Furcutter. Durnan Furcutter is a dwarven clothier and leather merchant operating out of Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. Working inside Anvilmar, he equips freshly trained dwarven and gnomish adventurers with lightweight attire suited to withstand the biting mountain chills. Anvilmar serves as the first proving ground for young dwarves and exiled gnomes, and not every warrior steps forth clad in heavy iron. Durnan Furcutter caters to scouts, rogues, and spellcasters who need light, pliable layers to stay agile without succumbing to the bitter winds of Dun Morogh. Positioned right near the hearth of Anvilmar, he sells everyday tailoring and stitched leather, claiming his stock is the finest to be found in the entire valley.

Duthorian Rall. Duthorian Rall is a respected human knight of the Silver Hand stationed within Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. Renowned as one of the most influential paladins in the Alliance, he oversees the training and spiritual trials of emerging holy warriors. He guides recruits through solemn vows of charity, valor, and devotion to defend Azeroth against the Scourge and lurking domestic threats. Standing within the vaulted transept of the Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall represents the venerable traditions of the Knights of the Silver Hand. With the kingdom unsettled by internal strife and the missing King Varian Wrynn, Duthorian shoulders the vital duty of instilling righteous discipline in fresh initiates. Respected paladins in the field, including Brother Wilhelm in Goldshire and Brandur Ironhammer in Ironforge, direct promising recruits to his guidance to begin their sacred trials.

Ebru. Ebru is a night elf druid sheltering in the crags above the Wailing Caverns. As one of Naralex's few remaining uncorrupted disciples, she watches helplessly as her master's dream of restoring the Barrens curdles into a nightmare. From her perch, she enlists travelers brave enough to enter the subterranean depths to cull the mutated horrors spawned by the Nightmare. While most of Naralex's followers succumbed to the emerald corruption creeping through the caverns, Ebru managed to escape the nightmare's grasp. Camped inside the cavernous skull formation overlooking the entrance to the Wailing Caverns, she keeps vigil over the descent. She knows that Naralex's noble plan—to tap subterranean springs and transform the arid Barrens into lush woodland—has gone horribly awry, and she desperately directs willing adventurers to eliminate the burgeoning deviate beasts threatening to overrun the surrounding plains.

Edwin VanCleef. Edwin VanCleef was the brilliant Guildmaster of the Stonemasons who rebuilt Stormwind City after the Second War. After being cheated of payment by the House of Nobles, he led a violent workers' revolt and formed the outlaw Defias Brotherhood. Operating from deep within the Deadmines of Westfall, he seeks vengeance against the kingdom he helped restore. Following the devastation of the First War, Edwin VanCleef was chosen to lead the Stonemasons Guild in the monumental task of rebuilding Stormwind City. A peerless craftsman and an idealist, VanCleef directed the construction of the capital's grand ramparts and towering cathedrals. Alongside his mastery of architecture, VanCleef was a remarkably deadly operative; he was trained in stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft by his childhood friend, Mathias Shaw.

Einar Stonegrip. Einar Stonegrip is a dwarven trapper stationed along the main crossroads of the Wetlands. Rather than risk an uncomfortable reunion with his estranged wife in Menethil Harbor, he relies on passing adventurers to haul his crocolisk skins to town. Perched at the central intersection connecting Dun Algaz, Dun Modr, and Menethil Harbor, Einar Stonegrip earns his living braving the sodden marshes of the Wetlands. He hunts the local crocolisks for their sturdy hides, supplying leatherworkers and merchants along the coast. Though rugged enough to wrestle reptiles out of the mire, he is thoroughly cowed by domestic strife. Embroiled in a bitter falling-out with his wife, Sida, Einar stays out on the road, hiring travelers to deliver his bundles of skins to his trading partner James Halloran rather than set foot in Menethil Harbor himself.

Eitrigg. Eitrigg is a seasoned veteran of the First and Second Wars who stands beside Warchief Thrall as an esteemed advisor in Orgrimmar. Once a warrior of the Blackrock clan, he became disillusioned with the old demonic Horde and lived in exile until an extraordinary friendship with a human paladin changed his fate. Today, he helps guide the New Horde back to its roots of honor and shamanism. Born on Draenor into the Blackrock clan, Eitrigg fought for the Horde through the First and Second Wars. The horrific battles and the ultimate defeat of the Horde in the Second War forced him to confront how far his people had fallen to bloodlust and demonic corruption. Sickened by what the Horde had become, Eitrigg walked away from the scattered remnants and retreated into self-imposed exile, seeking only solitude in the wilds of Lordaeron.

Elanaria. Elanaria is a night elf warrior mentor and coordinator stationed on the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus. She directs developing fighters across Kalimdor, testing their mettle against dangerous threats such as the satyr Vorlus Vilehoof and spiritual entities like the Shade of Elura. Her guidance serves as a crucial bridge for Alliance soldiers honing their martial prowess in the night elven capital. Standing proudly on the Warrior's Terrace within the boughs of Darnassus, Elanaria serves as an instructor and point of contact for martial champions. In an era where the night elves have formally aligned with the Grand Alliance, her role extends beyond mentoring local Sentinels to preparing warriors of all backgrounds for the harsh challenges facing their lands.

Elder Bloodhoof. Elder Bloodhoof is an ancestral spirit found resting just north of Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Appearing prominently to travelers during the Lunar Festival, he stands as a revered guardian spirit of the Bloodhoof tribe. Elder Bloodhoof represents the deep spiritual bond the tauren share with their lineage. Manifesting near Bloodhoof Village, this ghostly elder watches over his people and rewards respectful travelers who seek wisdom during the Lunar Festival. His presence reinforces the enduring guidance of deceased chieftains and tribal forebears, whose spirits remain intimately tied to the plains of Mulgore.

Elder Bronzebeard. Elder Bronzebeard is an ancient spirit of the earthen who appears in the Mystic Ward of Ironforge during the Lunar Festival. Bearing the name of the clan that rules the city, his spectral presence serves as a bridge between modern dwarves and their stony stone-hewn ancestors. Appearing near the pool in Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Elder Bronzebeard does not wear the flesh of modern dwarves; instead, his ghostly form is that of an earthen, the ancient race forged from living stone by the Titans. Dwarven scholars and explorers are only beginning to uncover their origins through excavations across Khaz Modan and beyond, making this spirit's presence a striking living relic. His very name and visage suggest he is a direct ancestor of the Bronzebeard clan, standing silent witness to how far his stoneborn progeny have evolved.

Elder Darkcore. Elder Darkcore is an ancient spirit who appears during the Lunar Festival within the throne room of the Ruins of Lordaeron above the Undercity. Representing the honored ancestors of the world, he offers his blessing and festive tokens to travelers who seek him out. His presence marks a peaceful, reflective moment amidst the ruins of a fallen human kingdom. During the annual Lunar Festival, the spirits of ancient elders manifest across Azeroth to share their wisdom with adventurers. Elder Darkcore takes his vigil in one of the world's most somber locations: the royal throne room in the Ruins of Lordaeron, directly above the entrance to the Undercity. Surrounded by the blood-stained floor where King Terenas Menethil II fell, this spectral ancestor offers a Coin of Ancestry and his blessing to those brave enough to enter the heart of Forsaken territory to pay their respects.

Elder Goldwell. Elder Goldwell is an ancient earthen spirit lingering near the dwarven settlement of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Appearing during the Lunar Festival, this revered ancestor represents the forgotten origins of modern dwarven civilization. Elder Goldwell manifests as a translucent earthen spirit, watching over the snowy slopes of Kharanos. Unlike modern mortal dwarves of flesh and bone, his stony form echoes the ancient Titan-forged race from which the Bronzebeard clan descended. His presence during ancestor celebrations offers travelers a chance to honor that ancient heritage.

Elder Graveborn. Elder Graveborn is an ancestral spirit who manifests just southeast of Brill during the Lunar Festival. Appearing as a spectral earthen elder, he honors travelers and guides pilgrims searching for other ancient spirits scattered throughout northern Lordaeron. Appearing just beyond the Forsaken town of Brill, Elder Graveborn stands among the haunted woods of Tirisfal Glades as part of the worldwide Lunar Festival. Despite the blighted surroundings and the troubled state of the kingdom, the spectral elder offers peaceful greetings to travelers seeking the festival's traditional blessings. In addition to bestowing his own ancestral wisdom, Graveborn shares news of other elders lingering nearby—pointing pilgrims toward spirits abiding in the Undercity, the Sepulcher, and across the Plaguelands.

Elder Morningdew. Elder Morningdew is an ancient night elf spirit who appears during the Lunar Festival in Thousand Needles. She offers wisdom and ancestral blessings to travelers who seek her out amid the arid canyons and dried salt flats of the Shimmering Flats. Throughout the Lunar Festival, the spirits of revered ancestors manifest across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to celebrate wisdom, legacy, and peace. Elder Morningdew is one such apparition, visiting Thousand Needles to greet honoring pilgrims. Bound by neither faction nor mortal conflict, she bestows her coin of ancestry upon any adventurer respectful enough to seek her counsel and receive her blessing.

Elder Obsidian. Elder Obsidian is an ancestral earthen spirit who manifests at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest during the annual Lunar Festival. Appearing among the graves claimed by the Forsaken, he offers the wisdom and blessings of the ancient world to travelers honoring the festival. Standing amid the somber tombs of the Sepulcher, Elder Obsidian provides a striking contrast to Silverpine Forest's gloomy expanse. As an ethereal earthen elder, his spirit manifests during the Lunar Festival to celebrate the ancient heritage of Azeroth. While the surrounding crypts are held by the Forsaken and menaced by feral worgen, Obsidian greets wayfarers of all allegiances in peace, bestowing Coin of Ancestry and ancient blessings upon those who take the time to seek out his wisdom.

Elder Runetotem. Elder Runetotem is an ancestral tauren spirit appearing outside Razor Hill in Durotar during the Lunar Festival. As one of the revered elders honored during the festival, she offers wisdom and her blessing to travelers who seek her out across the red canyons. Though ancestral tauren spirits are typically tied to the grassy plains and sacred burial grounds of Mulgore, Elder Runetotem lingers far from the pastures of her people. She manifests beside the dusty settlement of Razor Hill in Durotar. To young orcs and wandering adventurers, her ethereal presence serves as a bridge between the ancient traditions of the Shu'halo and the harsh new home the Horde has carved along the Great Sea.

Elder Skyseer. Elder Skyseer is the spirit of an ancestral tauren residing atop the towering bluffs of Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. As an honoured elder returned from the spirit world, he observes the ongoing journeys of the Horde and remains deeply tied to the resting grounds of his people. Perched high above the salt canyons of Thousand Needles, Elder Skyseer lingers at the windswept mesa settlement of Freewind Post. While the tauren of Freewind Post bustle around the outpost's perilous bridges and wooden platforms, Skyseer watches over the realm as an ancestor who has crossed beyond the mortal veil. He serves as an ancestral beacon for travelers seeking the wisdom of past generations, offering his blessings to those who honor old traditions.

Elder Starweave. Elder Starweave is an ancestral night elf spirit honored during the Lunar Festival. Found resting at the port town of Auberdine along the misty coast of Darkshore, she shares the wisdom of ancient ages with passing pilgrims. Appearing as an ethereal shade among the coastal dwellings of Auberdine, Elder Starweave is one of the revered ancestors honored by the Cenarion Circle and the peoples of Kalimdor. While many travelers rush through the port on their way inland or across the sea, those who pause before her receive an ancestral blessing. Starweave speaks of celestial movements, observing that the stars of the modern era trace unfamiliar paths that serve as beacons of hope and fortitude for future generations.

Eleanor Shackleton. Eleanor Shackleton is a Forsaken outdoorswoman found camping southwest of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Rather than lingering within town or the Undercity, she assists wandering travelers in learning wilderness survival and field crafts. She shares her surname with other Forsaken surviving in the region, suggesting lingering ties from life before the plague. While many newly awakened Forsaken head straight to Brill or delve into the Undercity, Eleanor Shackleton makes her camp in the haunted woods to the southwest. Surviving out in Tirisfal requires pragmatic self-reliance, and Eleanor serves as an instructor for fledgling adventurers seeking to live off the blighted land. Through her various field lessons, she guides travelers in establishing campsites, gathering firewood, and maintaining trade crafts while roaming far from civilization's forge fires and kitchens.

Electrocutioner 6000. The Electrocutioner 6000 is a deadly, super-charged spider tank deployed to defend the Launch Bay within the irradiated halls of Gnomeregan. It fights for Mekgineer Thermaplugg and the leper gnomes who follow him, holding the upper platform against anyone pushing deeper into the fallen city. Gnomeregan's fall left its war machines in the hands of Mekgineer Thermaplugg and the irradiated leper gnomes who still follow him. The Electrocutioner 6000, a hulking spider tank crackling with high-voltage current, stands guard on the upper platform of Gnomeregan's Launch Bay and lashes intruders with electricity.

Elling Trias. Elling Trias manages Trias' Cheese, a small storefront nestled in the bustling Trade District of Stormwind City. While he presents himself as a jovial and passionate purveyor of dairy, he quietly operates as one of the kingdom's most connected information brokers. Behind wheels of cheese and cordial banter, Trias maintains an ear to the ground that reaches across continents. To the casual customer strolling the Trade District, Elling Trias is merely an artisan dedicated to fine curds, working his shop alongside his wife Elaine and son Ben. He enthusiastically hawks wheels of cheese and chats amicably with townsfolk. Yet those in the know understand that Trias' Cheese is one of the most reliable fronts in Stormwind. The steady hum of city commerce provides perfect cover for operatives, courtiers, and adventurers who need to trade quiet words without drawing the attention of the city watch.

Elu. Elu is an apprentice wind rider stationed atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Eager to begin his formal training and take to the skies, he tasks Horde travelers with retrieving wild wyvern eggs from nearby roosts. Perched high above the salt flats and canyon floor at Freewind Post, Elu spends his days tending to the settlement's aerial mounts while dreaming of his own flight. As a young tauren apprentice, he longs to join the ranks of the master wind riders who patrol the towering mesas of Kalimdor. Before he can begin true flight training, however, he must prove his capability by supplying the roost with fresh wyvern stock, sending capable adventurers to harvest intact eggs from the fierce wild wyverns nesting at Highperch.

Eva Sarkhoff. Eva Sarkhoff is the spectral remnant of the former head maid of House Barov, lingering alongside her husband Lucien just outside the horrors of Scholomance. Tortured and slain by the Butcher during the fall of Caer Darrow, her spirit seeks brave mortals to avenge their deaths and destroy their cursed remains. Eva served the wealthy Barov family for decades as their head maid, caring for the sprawling keep of Caer Darrow alongside her husband Lucien, the family butler. As the Barovs grew paranoid about their aging mortality and vast wealth, they struck a catastrophic pact with Kel'Thuzad. The manor was gradually handed over to the fledgling Cult of the Damned, warping the grand residence into Scholomance, a secretive academy of necromancy. Eva and Lucien hid in the keep's corridors for six months, scavenging food while watching cultists and monstrosities steadily take over their home.

Executor Arren. Executor Arren is a high-ranking Forsaken officer stationed in Deathknell. He oversees the immediate defense and consolidation of the settlement as newly awakened undead emerge from their graves. Arren coordinates the local campaign against mindless Scourge zombies, feral beasts, and the encroaching zealots of the Scarlet Crusade. Standing resolute just outside the chapel in Deathknell, Executor Arren serves as the primary military voice for the nascent Forsaken within their awakening grounds. While the caretakers in the crypts guide newly raised undead through their disorientation, Arren directs their focus outward toward survival. Under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner's banner, he organizes local operations to sweep away mindless zombies that threaten the village borders, establishing secure territory in the shadow of Lordaeron's fall.

Executor Zygand. Executor Zygand is a senior Forsaken commander stationed at the town hall in Brill, overseeing defensive and military operations across central Tirisfal Glades. Reporting directly to the Undercity's high command, he coordinates the purge of Scarlet Crusade forces pressing into Forsaken territory. Positioned at the administrative heart of Brill, Executor Zygand coordinates regional defense for the Forsaken after their initial awakening in Deathknell. Serving as the direct superior to regional officers like Executor Arren and field sentries such as Deathguard Linnea, Zygand synthesizes scout intelligence and dispatches able recruits to safeguard Lordaeron's borders from encroachment.

Falfindel Waywarder. Falfindel Waywarder is a night elf druid stationed at Thalanaar, the outpost guarding the border between Feralas and the Thousand Needles. From this frontier watchpost, he works to heal corrupted lands and safeguard the southern wilderness of Kalimdor. Travelers wandering down from Stonetalon or the Barrens often find him seeking aid to restore balance to the wild. Thalanaar marks the gateway where the lush forests of Feralas descend into the towering mesas and dry salt plains of Thousand Needles. Falfindel Waywarder stands watch at this remote outpost, greeting weary travelers who have ventured far across the continent. Surrounded by natural grandeur and lurking dangers, he serves as a point of contact for the night elves seeking to monitor both local threats and broader environmental calamities across Kalimdor.

Falla Sagewind. Falla Sagewind is a reclusive tauren mystic perched high upon a rocky peak overlooking the central Barrens.
