Stationed between the Crossroads and the Lushwater Oasis, she studies the natural and mystical anomalies troubling the surrounding land. Adventurers probing the twisted corruption seeping from the nearby Wailing Caverns often seek her guidance. Falla Sagewind makes her camp far above the dust and bustle of the Barrens trails, situated on a secluded summit just southwest of the Crossroads. From this vantage, she keeps a solemn watch over the fragile savannas below, observing the sudden shifts in wildlife behavior and the encroaching corruption rising from the subterranean fissures of the Wailing Caverns. Her solitary vigil separates her from the daily trade of the Crossroads, positioning her as an observant hermit tuned to the spirits and the land's silent wounds.

Fallen Hero of the Horde. The Fallen Hero of the Horde is the lingering spirit of an orc warrior standing watch on the southern road out of the Swamp of Sorrows. Bound by regret and dishonor, he warns passing travelers of the horrors awaiting them in the Blasted Lands and seeks champions willing to deliver his tortured soldiers from demonic bondage. In life, this warrior was a celebrated champion dispatched with a handpicked regiment of soldiers to investigate the Blasted Lands and report back on the presence of the Burning Legion. His dispatch never made it; the courier sent north toward Stonard was ambushed and slain by the Swamp Talker and his murlocs. Stranded without orders or reinforcements, the commander eventually marched his soldiers south into the shattered wastes to confront the growing darkness. It was a fatal misjudgment. Overwhelmed by demonic forces, his army was scattered, captured, and subjected to horrific torment at the hands of the dreadlord Razelikh the Defiler.

Fandral Staghelm. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the druids of the Cenarion Circle from the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. Stepping into power after Malfurion Stormrage vanished into the Emerald Dream, he championed the planting of the new World Tree, Teldrassil. Proud, abrasive, and relentlessly ambitious, Fandral advocates for an aggressive Kaldorei resurgence that frequently pits him against High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Following the Third War and the sacrifice of Nordrassil atop Mount Hyjal, the night elves lost their immortality and their sacred sanctuary. When Malfurion Stormrage vanished, Fandral took up leadership of the druids and convinced the Circle of Ancients that it was time for their people to rebuild and regain their immortality. With the Circle's approval, he led the druids in raising Teldrassil off the coast of Kalimdor. He envisioned the colossal bough as a monument to Kaldorei endurance and a vessel to restore their lost supremacy, even though the Dragon Aspects pointedly withheld their blessings from the unapproved endeavor.

Farmer Furlbrow. Farmer Theodore Furlbrow is an evicted Westfall pumpkin farmer stranded alongside his wife Verna on the road near the Jansen Stead. Driven from their home by the Defias Brotherhood, the couple is trying to repair their broken wagon and flee into Elwynn Forest. Theodore Furlbrow once cultivated a pumpkin patch in northern Westfall, but the rising criminal tide forced him and his wife, Verna, to abandon everything they owned. Gathering whatever they could salvage, they set out toward the safety of Elwynn Forest, urging neighbors like Farmer Saldean to follow suit. Disaster struck along the road near the Jansen Stead when their wagon broke down, leaving them stranded in plain sight of bandits and wild beasts. While Verna tends to their beloved horse Old Blanchy, Theodore watches the road with growing despair, desperate to recover cherished possessions—such as the pocket watch given to him by Verna's father on their wedding day—and hoping to warn Sentinel Hill about the bandits closing in.

Farmer Saldean. Farmer Saldean is a resilient human homesteader residing at Saldean's Farm in central Westfall alongside his wife, Salma. Unlike many neighboring farmers who fled or gave up, Saldean stubbornly tends his troubled fields in the face of rogue harvest golems and mounting banditry. Farmer Saldean remembers better days in Westfall. Those prosperous years have crumbled into dust. Surrounded by overgrown fields, rampaging mechanical harvest watchers, and predatory bandits, Saldean refuses to yield his land. While other homesteaders abandoned their acres or turned to thievery, he and his wife Salma remain determined to harvest what little grain they can. Driven to practical desperation, he recruits wandering adventurers to destroy the rogue Harvest Watchers that have taken over his fields and his neighbors' so he can clear his soil for planting.

Farthing. Bishop Farthing is a human clergyman residing within the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City. Known as a kind and wise servant of the Holy Light, he guides parishioners and directs aid toward beleaguered settlements across the kingdom. Within the serene marble halls of the Cathedral of Light, Bishop Farthing stands as one of the prominent figures attending to the spiritual needs of Stormwind City. Alongside Archbishop Benedictus and the gathered clergy, he offers counsel to travelers, assists those pursuing the holy arts, and attends to the civic and pastoral obligations of the Church of the Holy Light.

Feegly the Exiled. Feegly the Exiled is an outcast dwarf found lurking near the dwarven excavation at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. Once praised as one of the expedition's finest diggers, his obsession with an uncovered relic led General Twinbraid to drive him off.

Feero Ironhand. Feero Ironhand is a human paladin stationed at Maestra's Post in the western reaches of Ashenvale. Standing guard along the border between Darkshore and the forest, he works closely with Delgren the Purifier to combat the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand. Located along the road leading south from Darkshore into Ashenvale, Maestra's Post serves as a critical watchpoint for travelers and Alliance defenders alike. Feero Ironhand operates out of this outpost, maintaining communications and trade lines with Auberdine while keeping a vigilant watch over the surrounding woods. Together with Delgren the Purifier, Feero focuses his efforts against the malevolent Cult of the Dark Strand, ensuring the cultists and forest predators do not sever the path between Darnassus's supply lines and the front lines of Ashenvale.

Fel'zerul. Fel'zerul is an orc warlock stationed at Stonard in the murky depths of the Swamp of Sorrows. Acting under direct orders from Warchief Thrall, he investigates the ominous presence lurking within the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar. While Thrall's Horde generally views dark arts with suspicion, the Warchief recognizes that understanding sinister powers requires those who study them. Fel'zerul was dispatched to Stonard specifically to unravel the corruption surrounding the Pool of Tears and the submerged Temple of Atal'Hakkar. By directing adventurers to recover artifacts and investigate the exiled Atal'ai trolls, the warlock seeks to determine what evil stirs beneath the murky waters before it threatens the Horde's southern outpost.

Felgur Twocuts. Felgur Twocuts is a blunt orc scout stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. He coordinates Horde efforts against the regional centaur clans. Standing watch amid the bleak expanse of Ghost Walker Post in central Desolace, Felgur Twocuts has little patience for pleasantries. As a forward scout for the Horde, he assesses the threats facing travelers and settlers venturing west through the mountains, particularly the local Kolkar centaur.

Felix Whindlebolt. Felix Whindlebolt is a displaced gnome refugee taking shelter at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. In his haste to flee the radiation flooding Gnomeregan, he lost his personal belongings, and hostile Frostmane trolls made off with them. Following the tragic fall of Gnomeregan, thousands of gnomes found themselves wandering the freezing reaches of Dun Morogh in search of safety. Felix Whindlebolt fled the irradiated city in such haste that he lost all his personal belongings and tools. To make matters worse, Frostmane ice trolls carried his chest, his box and his bucket of bolts back to their camps southwest of Anvilmar, leaving him stranded, destitute, and relying on sympathetic wanderers to retrieve his stolen gear.

Fenrus the Devourer. Fenrus the Devourer is an enormous worg that prowls the upper sanctum of Shadowfang Keep. Kept as a personal pet and guardian by Archmage Arugal, the ravenous beast is bloated on unnatural magics. Anyone daring to breach the archmage's personal study must contend with this feral horror and the master who watches over it. Deep within Shadowfang Keep, just outside Archmage Arugal's personal chambers, lurks the monstrous worg known as Fenrus the Devourer. Unlike the lupine worgen roaming the ramparts, Fenrus is an actual worg, swollen to gargantuan proportions. Prowling the shelves, scrolls, and arcane apparatuses of Arugal's private study, the beast serves both as a pet and as a violent perimeter guard against any intruder seeking the mad mage's head.

Field Marshal Snowfall. Field Marshal Snowfall is a dwarven military officer stationed in Ironforge's Military Ward to coordinate the Alliance war effort against the rising silithid threat. Facing an ancient evil stirring in the southern sands of Silithus, he oversees the massive logistical drive required to equip the allied armies. Snowfall tracks donated raw materials and rewards those who aid the realm's preparation for war. Standing watch in Ironforge's Military Ward, Field Marshal Snowfall serves as the central coordinator for the Alliance's mobilization against Ahn'Qiraj. He views the brewing conflict not merely as a border skirmish, but as a critical fight against an ancient enemy hostile to all creations of the Titans. Snowfall oversees staggering stockpiles of supplies—millions of bandages, tons of metal bars, leathers, herbs, and rations gathered by adventurers—ensuring that Alliance forces will be armed, armored, and fed when the march south to Silithus begins.

Field Marshal Stonebridge. Field Marshal Stonebridge is a high-ranking Alliance officer stationed near the entrance of Stormwind City. Posted beside the Gates of Stormwind in the Valley of Heroes, she oversees city defenses alongside General Marcus Jonathan and serves as an authority for major martial triumphs. Positioned just inside the towering entrance of the Valley of Heroes, Field Marshal Stonebridge stands watch beneath the eastern archway near the main gates. Her high rank within the Grand Alliance military places her among the highest echelons of Stormwind's strategic leadership, operating in close coordination with General Marcus Jonathan. From this prominent vantage, she observes the flow of defenders, travelers, and returning champions passing into the capital, standing ready to organize the garrison should threats breach the outer perimeter.

First Mate Fitzsimmons. First Mate Fitzsimmons is a ragged, reeking sailor who spends his days drinking outside the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Once the first mate aboard the Wave Mistress of the Kul Tiras Third Fleet, he is the sole known living survivor of the fleet's destruction during the Second War. Haunted by the tragedy, he seeks willing adventurers to face the restless spirits of his drowned comrades. Lounging outside the Deepwater Tavern amid the damp salt air of Menethil Harbor, First Mate Fitzsimmons is an easy man to overlook—or avoid entirely, given his unwashed stench. To most patrons, he is just another broken old salt drinking his memories away. Yet those willing to sit and listen will hear harrowing tales of a proud fleet brought low by fire and claw.

Fizzle Brassbolts. Fizzle Brassbolts is a prominent gnomish engineer stationed out on the baked salt flats of the Mirage Raceway in Thousand Needles. Alongside his rival, the goblin Pozzik, Fizzle co-founded the raceway to pit gnomish precision engineering against reckless goblin ingenuity in high-speed rocket car races. He constantly seeks parts, fuel, and strange desert reagents to keep his racing team running. Out in the shimmering heat of the Shimmering Flats, political alliances and ancient grudges yield to the roar of motorized engines. Fizzle Brassbolts arrived here with one goal in mind: proving once and for all that gnomish craftsmanship is vastly superior to crude goblin tinkering. Together with his goblin counterpart Pozzik, he helped lay out the Mirage Raceway, bringing race cars, pit crews, and spectators to an otherwise desolate basin.

Fleet Master Seahorn. Fleet Master Seahorn is a seasoned tauren mariner who serves as the naval commander of the Blackwater Raiders in Booty Bay. Stationed on the upper balcony of the Salty Sailor Tavern alongside Baron Revilgaz, he oversees the goblin port's maritime defenses. His primary duty is protecting the harbor from the looming threat posed by their sworn enemies, the Bloodsail Buccaneers. While tauren are renowned across Kalimdor as plains-dwellers, Fleet Master Seahorn chose a vastly different life upon the ocean. Clad in pirate regalia, he commands the fleet of the Blackwater Raiders, the private naval arm of the Steamwheedle Cartel's operation in Stranglethorn Vale. Stationed atop the Salty Sailor Tavern, Seahorn works shoulder-to-shoulder with Baron Revilgaz, coordinating shipping routes, crew deployments, and coastal defenses for the lawless yet strictly managed port of Booty Bay.

Foggy MacKreel. Foggy MacKreel is an intrepid dwarf stranded precariously on the ruined lower masonry of the Thandol Span. Despite the shattered stonework beneath his feet and the dizzying drop below, his only real concern is fulfilling his moonshine delivery north to Southshore. Perched on the broken pylons beneath the shattered Thandol Span, Foggy MacKreel appears utterly unfazed by his perilous predicament. While Dark Iron sabotage and war damage have left the grand bridge between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands fractured, MacKreel treats his precarious footing as a minor inconvenience. His primary thought is not his rescue, but an undelivered batch of potent moonshine destined for the patrons of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. He readily hires passing adventurers nimble enough to reach his ledge to finish the courier run on his behalf.

Foreman Oslow. Foreman Oslow is Lakeshire's beleaguered master builder, tasked with repairing the ruined Everstill Bridge in the heart of Redridge Mountains. Beset by Blackrock orc artillery and gnoll raiders, his reconstruction efforts have stalled due to lost shipments and sunken equipment. He relies heavily on traveling adventurers to retrieve his gear and secure materials so Lakeshire can reconnect its vital trade route. Standing by the fractured masonry of the Everstill Bridge, Foreman Oslow faces an uphill battle. The bridge is the lifeline of Lakeshire, spanning the expanse of Lake Everstill and linking the western roads toward Elwynn to the eastern shores. Blackrock orcs, sweeping down from the crags of Stonewatch, targeted the crossing to cripple the town's logistics and military movement, leaving the settlement splintered and vulnerable.

Foreman Stonebrow. Foreman Stonebrow is a dwarven overseer representing the Miners' League at Gol'Bolar Quarry in eastern Dun Morogh. After aggressive troggs erupted from the rock and overran the excavation site, he was forced to organize a defense and hire adventurers to clear the pits. Foreman Stonebrow was charged with directing operations at Gol'Bolar Quarry, a key dwarven excavation nestled in the mountains east of Kharanos. When deep digging broke into hidden trogg burrows, subterranean beasts swarmed the pits and drove the miners from their equipment. Refusing to abandon the site entirely, Stonebrow remains at the rim of the quarry to enlist any able-bodied travelers willing to push the troggs back.

Foreman Thazz'ril. Foreman Thazz'ril is an orc labor supervisor stationed in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. Tasked with keeping peons on schedule and maintaining basic infrastructure for young warriors, he is perpetually frustrated by lazy laborers and nearby cultist activity. Building a new home in the harsh red rock of Durotar requires unending physical labor. In the Valley of Trials, Foreman Thazz'ril oversees the peons chopping lumber and gathering materials needed to support both the encampment and the wider Horde war effort. Unfortunately for Thazz'ril, peons are notoriously prone to slacking off and taking naps under the desert sun. To keep construction moving, he regularly enlists newly arrived recruits to give the slumbering workers a brisk wallop with his trusty blackjack, instilling obedience through blunt persuasion.

Foreman Thistlenettle. Foreman Thistlenettle was once a dwarven overseer representing both the Miners' League and the Explorers' League within the depths of Westfall. After a catastrophic cave-in trapped his crew in the subterranean tunnels of the Deadmines, he perished alongside his workers and rose again as an undead ghoul. He now wanders the dark, collapsed corridors, unrecognizable to all except by the guild badge he still carries. Before the Defias Brotherhood took total control of the Deadmines, legitimate mining expeditions delved deep into its rich veins. Foreman Thistlenettle oversaw one such venture on behalf of the Miners' League and Explorers' League. Deep in the tunnels beneath Moonbrook, disaster struck when a violent cave-in sealed his party off from the surface. The trapped miners died in the darkness, but their rest did not last; a sinister, necrotic taint raised Thistlenettle and his crew as ravenous ghouls to stalk the shadowed passages.

Frahun Shadewhisper. Frahun Shadewhisper is a night elf rogue trainer stationed at Aldrassil within Shadowglen. He provides newly initiated night elf scouts and rogues with foundational techniques in stealth, agility, and covert strikes. He shares a family name with Erion Shadewhisper, another trainer of his craft in Darnassus. Within the safe haven of Aldrassil in the heart of Teldrassil, Frahun Shadewhisper instructs emerging rogues in the quiet arts of concealment and bladecraft. While night elf society often honors priests, sentinels, and druids, the specialized trade of scouts and infiltrators remains essential for safeguarding the boughs of the World Tree. Frahun welcomes recruits who arrive bearing an encrypted sigil, evaluating their potential and guiding their early development.

Furen Longbeard. Furen Longbeard is a master dwarven armorer stationed within Stormwind City's bustling Dwarven District. Apprenticed under the renowned smith Grimand Elmore, he specializes in crafting heavy protective gear and sturdy mail for seasoned defenders of the Alliance. Warriors across the kingdom seek out his metallurgical expertise to forge specialized, battle-ready armor. Furen Longbeard plies his craft far from the great forges of Ironforge, making his home instead among the cobblestones and soot of Stormwind's Dwarven District. Like many of his kin, Furen brought traditional dwarven metallurgy south to support the rebuilding and defense of the kingdom. Working amidst blazing hearths and clanging anvils, he maintains strong ties with other artisans throughout the city and beyond.

Furl Scornbrow. Furl Scornbrow is an aging orc lookout stationed in the watchtower northwest of Razor Hill. No longer able to fight on the front lines due to his advancing years, he keeps watch over the red canyons of Durotar and crafts sturdy packs for young travelers setting out across the land. Perched high in the wooden watchtower just northwest of Razor Hill, Furl Scornbrow keeps a quiet vigil over the central plains of Durotar. In the tense early days following the founding of Orgrimmar, sentries like Furl were vital for sounding signal horns against hostile quilboar, centaur, and Kul Tiras interlopers. As Durotar has stabilized and Razor Hill has established firmer borders, emergencies have grown rarer, leaving Furl plenty of quiet hours at his post.

Gaerolas Talvethren. Gaerolas Talvethren is a night elf sentinel standing watch over the ruins of Starbreeze Village in Teldrassil. Appointed as the protector of the Sleeping druids, he seeks aid in confronting the aggressive furbolgs and dark corruption unsettling the boughs. Positioned amid the troubled settlement of Starbreeze Village, Gaerolas Talvethren bears the solemn mantle of protecting the Sleeping druids who slumber in communion with the Emerald Dream. His vigilance has grown fraught as unnatural corruption creeps through the forest, unsettling the balance of Teldrassil.

Gakin the Darkbinder. Gakin the Darkbinder is a master warlock operating covertly deep beneath The Slaughtered Lamb tavern in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. He instructs aspiring Alliance practitioners in the dark arts, testing their resolve before initiating rituals to summon and bind otherworldly demons to their service. While Stormwind's mages practice openly in their towering sanctuaries, practitioners of shadow and fel must dwell where prying eyes cannot reach. Hidden below the taproom of The Slaughtered Lamb is a damp crypt-like cellar equipped with summoning circles and grim tomes. Gakin serves as the anchor of this hidden conclave, ensuring that young warlocks learn discipline and restraint before unleashing horrors they cannot control.

Galgar. Galgar is an orc cook stationed in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. He prepares provisions for young recruits taking their first steps in service to the Horde. To teach newcomers the basics of foraging in the harsh desert, he tasks them with gathering wild cactus apples for his signature dish. Situated near the cooking fire of the Den in the Valley of Trials, Galgar provides sustenance for young orcs and trolls undergoing their initial rites of passage. Durotar is a dry, unforgiving red wasteland where every scrap of sustenance must be wrung from the landscape. By putting novice warriors to work gathering ripe cactus fruit, Galgar tests their attention and resilience while keeping his kitchen stocked.

Gan'rul Bloodeye. Gan'rul Bloodeye is a senior orc warlock trainer residing deep within the dark cavern of the Cleft of Shadow in Orgrimmar. Hidden away from the watchful gaze of the city above, he initiates Horde warlocks into darker demonic rites. Under his instruction, initiates learn to bend otherworldly entities like voidwalkers and succubi to their will. While Warchief Thrall tolerates the presence of warlocks in the new Horde, their dark arts are not welcomed in the open sunlight of Durotar. Gan'rul Bloodeye makes his home in the Cleft of Shadow, a subterranean refuge beneath Orgrimmar where shadow weavers, rogues, and fel casters can study unmolested. From this subterranean perch, Gan'rul serves as a primary tutor for rising practitioners of fel magic.

Gann Stonespire. Gann Stonespire is an aggrieved tauren nomad found wandering the roads of the southern Barrens near Bael Modan. Driven from his tribe's ancestral hunting grounds by dwarven excavators, he seeks retaliation against the encroaching dig site. Before the dwarven expedition arrived from Ironforge to carve out the fortress of Bael Modan, the surrounding land served as ancestral territory and hunting grounds for Gann Stonespire's tribe. The dwarven miners drove the indigenous tauren from their soil with pickaxes, firearms, and heavy machinery, refusing peaceful overtures. Now camping along the dusty southern Barrens road, Gann refuses to quietly surrender his heritage, marshaling travelers to strike back at the excavators.

Gar'Thok. Gar'Thok is a veteran orc warrior and outpost commander stationed at Razor Hill in Durotar. Having survived the initial Kul Tiras landings on Durotar's coast, he now coordinates local defense against human encroachers and native threats. He directs young Horde recruits stepping out of the Valley of Trials to secure the red wastes of the new homeland. Following the Third War, Gar'Thok marched to Durotar under Warchief Thrall and served as a lieutenant under Nazgrel during the earliest days of building the new homeland. When the half-ogre wanderer Rexxar first arrived in Durotar, it was Gar'Thok who alerted him to the aggressive quilboar raiding their perimeter, enlisting the beastmaster to safeguard the fragile new settlement.

Gart Mistrunner. Gart Mistrunner is the resident druid trainer stationed at Camp Narache on the Red Cloud Mesa. He welcomes novice tauren called by the Earth Mother and guides them through their first rites of nature magic. Standing watch over Camp Narache, Gart Mistrunner represents the ancient druidic path rekindled among the Shu'halo. New tauren druids are directed straight to Gart upon taking their first steps on the Red Cloud Mesa, often carrying a verdant note commending them into his care. Through his patient guidance, young practitioners learn to commune with the natural world, drawing upon the restorative powers of nature and the lunar radiance of Mu'sha to heal their allies and strike down threats to the land.

Gath'Ilzogg. Gath'Ilzogg is the fearsome Blackrock orc warlord who commands the invasion force occupying Stonewatch Keep in the Redridge Mountains. Under his brutal leadership, the orcs seized the fortress and launched devastating raids against the town of Lakeshire, earning him an urgent bounty from the town's desperate magistrate. Gath'Ilzogg marched north out of the Burning Steppes under orders to secure Redridge for the Blackrock clan. Aided by the foul sorcery of the renegade human warlock Morganth, Gath'Ilzogg's warband battered the defenders of Stonewatch Keep and seized the high ground overlooking the entire region. From this entrenched redoubt, he oversees aggressive raids into the valleys and down toward the bridge of Lakeshire, steadily suffocating the human settlement. He rarely fights alone, keeping elite Blackrock guards and a vicious black dragon whelp named Singe close at hand.

Gaxim Rustfizzle. Gaxim Rustfizzle is an ambitious gnome scholar and tinker stationed at a small Alliance camp along the Webwinder Path in Stonetalon Mountains. A representative of the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, he seeks to prove to skeptical night elves that advanced artifice and alchemy can preserve their woodland realm. His scientific curiosity is matched by a fierce vendetta against the destructive operations of the Venture Company. While night elves traditionally rely on ancient druidism and nature magic, Gaxim Rustfizzle arrived in the craggy passes of Stonetalon to demonstrate a radically different perspective. Representing the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, he genuinely believes that calculated mechanisms and chemical solutions can defend and restore Kalimdor's wilderness just as effectively as prayers to Elune. Camped alongside the sentinel Kaela Shadowspear on the Webwinder Path, he works tirelessly to convince his tall, reclusive allies of engineering's ecological merits.

Gazin Tenorm. Gazin Tenorm is a dwarf stationed near the altar in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. Alongside his comrade Henze Faulk, he undertook a dangerous scouting mission to gather evidence of Defias Brotherhood activity for the king's advisors. While Gazin Tenorm spends his days within the tranquil halls of the Cathedral of Light, his mind remains out in the wilds of Elwynn Forest. Gazin and his close friend Henze Faulk set out into the woods on an urgent errand: gathering hard proof of the Defias Brotherhood's movements to present before the royal court. The expedition went awry when they were ambushed by Defias forces. Gazin barely escaped with his life back to the safety of Stormwind, but Henze was left behind in mortal danger, prompting Gazin to seek a stalwart hero of the Light to come to his companion's aid.

Gazrog. Gazrog is an orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads in the heart of the Barrens. Tasked with maintaining logistics and security along the savannah's perilous roads, he recruits able Horde travelers to deal with regional threats and investigate lost patrols. The Crossroads serves as the vital junction for all Horde transit through Kalimdor, but its isolation leaves supply lines vulnerable to marauders and beasts alike. Gazrog stands watch alongside the settlement's defenders, working to ensure that cargo, coin, and couriers reach their destinations. Maintaining order in a sprawling wilderness requires constant vigilance, and Gazrog relies heavily on passing adventurers to handle crises brewing beyond the outpost's stockades.

Gelbin Mekkatorque. Gelbin Mekkatorque is the High Tinker of the gnomes, currently residing in exile in Tinker Town within Ironforge. Renowned as a visionary engineer whose inventions include the mechanostrider and the Deeprun Tram, he now carries the heavy burden of Gnomeregan's fall and oversees efforts to reclaim his people's ancestral home. Gnomish leadership is earned through intellect and merit rather than bloodlines, and Gelbin Mekkatorque's rise to High Tinker was propelled by pure inventive genius. Mekkatorque revolutionized personal transportation with the creation of the first functioning mechanostrider. He also assisted the Bronzebeard dwarves in developing their formidable siege engines, and he was instrumental in the creation of the subterranean Deeprun Tram linking Ironforge to Stormwind.

Gelihast. Gelihast is a ferocious, twin-blade wielding murloc chieftain residing in the Pool of Ask'ar within Blackfathom Deeps. Surrounded by his Blindlight murlocs, he guards a strange altar in the flooded ruins of the sunken temple. While most murlocs stay near coastal shallows, Gelihast has claimed a lair deep in the sunken temple of Blackfathom Deeps beneath the Zoram Strand. Wielding twin swords with blinding speed, he cuts down intruders before they can react, and casters who stray into his reach rarely survive.

Gelkak Gyromast. Gelkak Gyromast is a gnome who talks like a pirate captain, found stranded along the foggy shoreline of Mist's Edge in northern Darkshore. His ship was sunk offshore by threshadons, and he wants his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, back in working order. Perched on the desolate northern coast of Darkshore just west of the ancient Ruins of Mathystra, Gelkak Gyromast represents a peculiar sight among the gloomy night elven shores. Talking like an old sea dog, the self-styled captain lost his ship to the threshadons just offshore. When he washed up on the misty sands, the key to his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, broke on the rocks, and its pieces were carried off by the crawlers, foreststriders and murlocs rummaging through the wreckage.

General Marcus Jonathan. General Marcus Jonathan is the High Commander of Stormwind Defense, stationed directly at the gates in the Valley of Heroes. A veteran of the Second War, he oversees the garrison protecting the capital and manages military requests from the kingdom's frontier settlements. Mounted atop his steed in the Valley of Heroes, General Marcus Jonathan stands as the first line of defense and the highest-ranking military officer overseeing the city gates. He fought in the Second War alongside renowned soldiers like Reginald Windsor under the command of General Turalyon. In this era of rising tension, Jonathan must balance the immediate security of the capital with the increasingly desperate calls for aid from frontier towns like Lakeshire.

Gerard Tiller. Gerard Tiller is a thirsty human farmhand working outside the barn at the Maclure Vineyards in Elwynn Forest. Tending the vineyards under the warm sun, he is always eager to trade a crisp, shiny red apple to any traveler willing to spare a skin of refreshing spring water. Gerard Tiller spends his days toiling in the fields and tending the grounds outside the barn at the Maclure Vineyards. Located just south of Goldshire, the vineyard produces some of Elwynn's best-known grapes, but keeping the harvest running is hard labor. Tiller is constantly parched from his chores, making him quick to barter with passing adventurers. If someone offers him a fresh skin of cool spring water, he happily repays the courtesy with fresh, shiny red apples gathered straight from the local orchards.

Gerrig Bonegrip. Gerrig Bonegrip is an unassuming dwarven shopkeeper tucked away in the shadowy corridors of Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern. Behind the counter of Bonegrip's Runes and Dooms, he quietly buys and sells esoteric texts concerning dark rituals and forgotten ancient powers.

Gershala Nightwhisper. Gershala Nightwhisper is a night elf researcher residing in the coastal settlement of Auberdine in Darkshore. Driven by grave concern over the path taken by the high elves of Quel'Thalas, he studies specimens of cursed aquatic and demonic creatures to understand how magical corruption warps both mind and body. Stationed peacefully within Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper looks beyond the immediate coastal troubles of Darkshore toward a broader, creeping danger. Watching with dismay as the remaining high elves embrace perilous arcane practices and dub themselves blood elves, Gershala seeks to understand the biological and spiritual descent that follows unchecked magic. To unlock these secrets, he directs seasoned Alliance adventurers into the submerged halls of Blackfathom Deeps to harvest corrupted brain stems from the naga and satyr who dwell within.

Ghamoo-ra. Ghamoo-ra is an ancient, giant sea turtle inhabiting the Pool of Ask'ar within Blackfathom Deeps, the sunken temple of Elune now overrun by the Twilight's Hammer cult. Armored in a massive shell, he savagely tramples any intruders who approach his island. Blackfathom Deeps was once a night elven temple dedicated to Elune, now flooded and claimed by naga, satyr and the nihilistic Twilight's Hammer cult. Ghamoo-ra dwells among its drowned ruins, an enormous turtle whose thick shell turns aside all but the most determined blows.

Gilnid. Gilnid, known as the Smelter, is the goblin master engineer running the forges in the depths of the Deadmines. He oversees the smelting of raw ore into refined metal and munitions for Edwin VanCleef's hidden ironclad juggernaut. Without his fiery operations, the Defias Brotherhood would lack the heavy cannons needed to assault Stormwind. Deep within the Deadmines, the Defias Brotherhood relies on industrial expertise to forge weapons of war. Gilnid serves as VanCleef's head smelter, commanding a small army of goblin laborers, tinkers, and smiths in the central foundry. Towering over most of his kin, he drives his crew relentlessly through smoke and slag, barking orders and refusing breaks to ensure raw iron ore is processed into heavy plating and lethal ordnance.

Gilshalan Windwalker. Gilshalan Windwalker is a night elf researcher resting at the base of the great tree Aldrassil in Shadowglen. Concerned by the sudden corruption taking root within Teldrassil, he studies the local wildlife to understand the unnatural aggression plaguing the boughs. His investigations into the Webwood spiders provide early clues about the rot afflicting the World Tree. Sitting calmly on the stone steps leading into Aldrassil, Gilshalan Windwalker watches over the tranquil canopy of Shadowglen with growing unease. Teldrassil was planted to restore the night elves' lost sanctuary and harmony with nature, but signs of deep spiritual malaise have emerged almost immediately. Gilshalan dedicates himself to examining how this corruption manifests in the local beasts, beginning with the venomous arachnids that weave their webs nearby.

Gilthares Firebough. Gilthares Firebough is an elven deckhand held captive atop a tower inside Northwatch Hold. Formerly employed by the Thalo'dan Privateers aboard a moonshine transport between Ratchet and Booty Bay, he seeks any opportunity to escape his Theramore captors. While hauling illicit cargo between Ratchet and Booty Bay, Gilthares Firebough saw his ship blasted to splinters by naval forces out of Theramore. As the sole survivor of the assault, the privateer was dragged ashore in chains and locked away in a tower within Northwatch Hold. Though dressed in vivid red and bearing little affection for the Alliance zealots who slaughtered his crew, Gilthares is not picky about who aids his breakout—so long as they can fight their way down from the ramparts.

Glorin Steelbrow. Glorin Steelbrow is a dwarven operative found drinking at the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Acting as an associate of Bishop Farthing of Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, he helps adventurers investigate the lost Third Fleet and recover sacred relics and materials scattered across the Wetlands coast. His efforts tie the haunted wilderness of Duskwood directly to the sunken shipwrecks of the north. While Bishop Farthing aids the people of Duskwood against its creeping terrors from Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, he maintains ties far to the north in Menethil Harbor. Stationed inside the bustling Deepwater Tavern, Glorin Steelbrow acts as Farthing's eyes and hands on the coast. He offers aid and direction to travelers sent north in search of sacred metals and forgotten relics, providing a crucial bridge between the troubles of the southern forest and the sunken wreckage of the Wetlands.

Gnoarn. Gnoarn is an exiled gnome residing in Tinker Town within the dwarven mountain city of Ironforge. Displaced following the devastating fall of Gnomeregan, he assists his scattered people by directing adventurers to assist fellow gnomish engineers and survivors. Like the majority of his brethren, Gnoarn was forced to flee the depths of Gnomeregan when troggs invaded and catastrophic radiation rendered the great subterranean metropolis uninhabitable. Taking refuge in Ironforge's Tinker Town under the hospitality of the Bronzebeard dwarves, Gnoarn spends his days keeping track of other survivors. He serves as an informal coordinator among the refugees, pointing capable travelers toward gnomes abroad who urgently require assistance, such as the stranded pilot Bingles Blastenheimer in Loch Modan or the ambitious engineer Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind.

Godrick Farsan. Godrick Farsan is an undead warlock assistant located in the Undercity, serving alongside Carendin Halgar in the Magic Quarter. Despite being entirely blind, he says that he sees in a different way. Situated amidst the summoning circles of the Magic Quarter, Godrick Farsan aids Master Carendin Halgar in guiding aspiring Forsaken warlocks. Though he lacks physical sight, Godrick says he can still see in a different way, without explaining the means. He tests practitioners seeking to bind greater demonic entities, dispatching them to gather pure hearts and essences needed for intricate summoning rituals.

Golnir Bouldertoe. Golnir Bouldertoe is a dwarven mining vendor stationed beside the bustling Great Forge in Ironforge. He provides essential supplies for miners and prospectors while handling dispatches for local couriers and travelers. Standing within the roaring heat of Ironforge's Great Forge, Golnir Bouldertoe outfits prospectors and craftsmen with the necessities of their trade. From sturdy mining picks to fluxes and coal, his wares fuel the tireless smelting fires and smithies that define the dwarven capital. Kin to Geofram Bouldertoe, Golnir is a reliable point of contact for workers arriving in the city, often directing fresh hands or receiving supply missives shuttled in from nearby outposts.

Gorbold Steelhand. Gorbold Steelhand is a dwarven merchant stationed in Auberdine along the misty coast of Darkshore. Operating far from the snowy halls of Khaz Modan, he supplies travelers, crafters, and local night elves with general goods and trade supplies. While most of Kalimdor's northern reaches are populated by the secretive night elves, Alliance outposts like Auberdine rely on merchants from across the Great Sea to keep trade moving. Gorbold Steelhand represents the far-reaching presence of Ironforge commerce in the region. Working alongside the kaldorei, he sells trade goods, reagents, crafting sundries, and tools to adventurers preparing to explore the treacherous shores and forests of Darkshore.

Gordon Wendham. Gordon Wendham is a Forsaken weaponsmith and merchant operating out of the bustling Trade Quarter in the Undercity. He equips newly arrived champions and local defenders of the Dark Lady with reliable steel, blades, and bludgeons. Beyond hawking basic armaments, he frequently serves as a local point of contact for couriers arriving from the surface. Situated amidst the damp stonework and chemical canals of the Undercity's Trade Quarter, Gordon Wendham provides essential weaponry to those taking up arms for the Forsaken. From basic daggers and hand axes to sturdy broadswords and maces, his stock caters to fledgling fighters who need dependable iron before venturing out into the contested reaches of Lordaeron.

Gornek. Gornek is an orc overseer stationed in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. He serves as the primary point of intake for fresh orc and Darkspear troll recruits preparing to prove their worth to the New Horde. Standing directly at the heart of the Valley of Trials, Gornek represents the initial test of discipline for aspiring Horde warriors, scouts, and spellcasters. Under Warchief Thrall's order, every youth and newcomer must earn their place through grit and perseverance rather than entitlement. Gornek assesses those stepping into the valley, reading their introductory orders and directing them to trainers throughout the compound. Whether an initiate carries an encrypted scrawl, a glyphic parchment, or a simple tablet, it is Gornek who receives their credentials and sets them upon their harsh path of survival.

Gramma Stonefield. Gramma Stonefield, whose given name is Mildred, is the elderly matriarch of the Stonefield family residing at their farm in Elwynn Forest. Unlike her bickering kin, she has grown weary of the bitter, generations-long feud with the neighboring Maclures. Quietly working behind her family's back, she does everything she can to help her grandson Tommy Joe pursue his forbidden romance with Maybell Maclure. As the oldest living member of the Stonefield clan, Mildred Stonefield has witnessed decades of petty squabbling between her household and the Maclures across the road. Rather than stoking the bad blood, she views the enduring rivalry as senseless and destructive. When her grandson Tommy Joe Stonefield falls in love with Maybell Maclure, Gramma chooses compassion over clan loyalty. Relying on an old friendship with William Pestle in Goldshire, she quietly plots to help the star-crossed sweethearts meet in secret, subverting the stubborn hostility dividing the two farms.

Grand Mason Marblesten. Grand Mason Marblesten is an esteemed dwarven stonemason stationed in the busy Commons of Ironforge. Deeply devoted to the royal legacy of Khaz Modan, he has been commissioned by King Magni Bronzebeard to build a memorial to Sully Balloo, a dwarven soldier who died in the Thandol Span tragedy. Adventurers often meet him when assisting with the materials needed to complete this solemn tribute. Dwarven stonemasonry is not merely a trade; it is an enduring art form that shapes the very soul of Ironforge. Grand Mason Marblesten stands among the city's foremost masters of the chisel, representing the centuries-old tradition of carving halls, pillars, and great effigies straight from the living mountain. Based in the Commons, he oversees civic projects and commemorative monuments that immortalize Bronzebeard history.

Granis Swiftaxe. Granis Swiftaxe is a dwarf warrior trainer stationed inside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Known for his blunt demeanor and hardy training regimen, he mentors fledgling Alliance fighters emerging from Coldridge Pass before directing seasoned warriors to the city of Ironforge. Found warming himself among the casks of the Thunderbrew Distillery, Granis Swiftaxe serves as the primary combat instructor for young warriors traversing Dun Morogh. He possesses the unyielding pride typical of dwarven fighters, showing open amusement and disdain toward non-warriors who try to catch his ear. Once a student demonstrates sufficient prowess in combat, Granis sends them up the mountain path to seek out master trainer Muren Stormpike in the Military Ward of Ironforge.

Great-father Winter. Great-father Winter is an elderly orc hired by the Smokywood Pastures merchant company to pose as the legendary holiday figure in Orgrimmar. Stationed near Grommash Hold in the Valley of Strength during the Feast of Winter Veil, he listens to children's wishes while visibly growing weary of commercial holiday cheer. In exchange for holiday gifts and seasonal tasks, he routinely asks passersby for gingerbread cookies and ice cold milk. While ancient lore speaks of Greatfather Winter as a majestic, elemental spirit wandering the land bringing snow and seasonal renewal, the figure sitting in the Valley of Strength is rather more mundane. He is an orc performer on the payroll of Smokywood Pastures, hired specifically to drive commerce, promote company wares, and entertain the youth of the Horde. Critics grumble that this commercial mascot cheapens genuine seasonal traditions, but few can deny the festive buzz he brings to the city streets.

Greatfather Winter. Greatfather Winter is the legendary personification of the winter season and the central figure of the Feast of Winter Veil. While ancient legends revere him as a mythical being who blankets Azeroth in snow to allow the land to rest and renew, modern city-dwellers know him primarily through the commercial spectacle managed by the goblins of Smokywood Pastures. According to ancient lore, Greatfather Winter is an ethereal wanderer who walks the world late in the year, casting his billowing snowy cloak across the land so nature may slumber and be reborn. Dwarves view him as an embodiment or herald of the titans, pointing to the frosted crags of Dun Morogh as living proof of his favor. Other traditions, such as those of the tauren, respect his role in the season's turning while attributing the cold and storms to the elemental work of the Sun and Moon, giving the Earth Mother time to rest. Wherever the legend traveled, communities learned to gather and feast together against the cold, celebrating the promise of returning life.

Greatmother Hawkwind. Greatmother Hawkwind is a revered tauren elder resting by the water well on Red Cloud Mesa. As the mother of Camp Narache's leader, Chief Hawkwind, she embodies the enduring spirit and communal responsibility of the tribe despite her advanced age. Greatmother Hawkwind spends her days beside the fresh water well at Camp Narache, serving as the spiritual matriarch for young tauren beginning their rites of passage. Though years have slowed her stride, she refuses to let age sideline her duty to the village. She believes that every member of the tribe, young or old, has an active role to play in sustaining the community, often asking fledgling youths to lend a hand with simple domestic chores like fetching fresh water.

Grelin Whitebeard. Grelin Whitebeard is a dwarven scout stationed in Coldridge Valley by royal decree to assess the Frostmane troll threat. Operating out of an isolated camp, he relies on rising adventurers to keep the trolls contained while Ironforge's attention remains consumed by the trogg crisis. Grelin Whitebeard and his brother Senir were dispatched to Coldridge Valley under direct orders from the Senate of Ironforge and King Magni Bronzebeard himself. Their mission was clear: assess and neutralize the threat posed by the native Frostmane trolls. With Ironforge's official military fully bogged down combating trogg outbreaks across Dun Morogh, the brothers were given very few resources to accomplish their task. Grelin had to establish an outpost in the snowy hills and look toward local recruits and passing initiates to carry out the necessary work.

Greta Mosshoof. Greta Mosshoof is a tauren druid allied with the Emerald Circle at the Emerald Sanctuary in southern Felwood. Alongside night elves and fellow guardians of nature, she investigates the foul taint creeping across the ancient forest and directs scouts into the Shadow Council stronghold of Jaedenar. Stationed at the Emerald Sanctuary on the southern boundary of Felwood, Greta Mosshoof works alongside the Emerald Circle to combat the pervasive corruption consuming the ancient woods. Rather than surrendering the blighted lands to the demonic taint left in the wake of the Third War, she coordinates efforts to understand and push back the spreading rot. Her investigations zero in on the poisoned waters of Felwood and the foul cultists burrowed within Jaedenar.

Grif Wildheart. Grif Wildheart is a seasoned dwarven hunter trainer stationed outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Renowned among the local mountaineers for his deep affinity with wildlife, he instructs budding marksmen in tracking, marksmanship, and the rites of beast taming. For young hunters emerging from Coldridge Valley, Grif provides the vital bridge between firing a rifle and walking alongside a loyal animal companion. While many Ironforge dwarves prefer the fiery warmth of a forge or the steady clink of pickaxes, Grif Wildheart has dedicated his life entirely to the frozen wilderness of Dun Morogh. Local mountaineers half-jokingly say he spends a bit too much time with four-legged beasts, but none dispute his mastery of the wild. Having spent years tracking across snowbound ridges alongside seasoned hunting companions, Grif possesses an intimate understanding of the natural predators that roam the crags.

Grimbooze Thunderbrew. Grimbooze Thunderbrew is an eccentric dwarven brewer of the Thunderbrew clan, camped out in the Dagger Hills of Westfall. He spends his days concocting potent spirits and speaking almost entirely in verse. Hailing from the renowned Thunderbrew brewing family of Kharanos, Grimbooze left the snowy mountain peaks of Dun Morogh for the windswept hills of Westfall. Known for his jovial disposition and an unyielding passion for potent spirits, he has a peculiar habit of speaking strictly in rhymes, and he answers a traveler's questions only once they have completed a simple task for him. Travelers passing through the dangerous Dagger Hills can find him tending to his private casks, always eager to test a thirsty traveler's palate.

Grish Longrunner. Grish Longrunner is a tauren scout and messenger stationed near the Great Lift, the vital mechanical crossing connecting the southern Barrens with the canyons of Thousand Needles. Serving the interests of the Horde along this bustling boundary, he keeps watch over travelers and coordinates military movement across the frontier. Positioned right beside the towering machinery of the Great Lift, Grish Longrunner stands watch over one of central Kalimdor's most precarious border crossings. The platform elevator is a lifeline connecting the arid wastes of the southern Barrens to the windswept mesas of Thousand Needles below. Between roving quilboar packs and competing territorial threats, travel along this vertical boundary is dangerous, making scouts like Grish essential for keeping the Horde informed and summoning reinforcements where they are sorely needed.

Grub. Grub is an enterprising orc living in a roadside hut just east of the Crossroads in the Barrens. Operating a modest frontier eatery alongside a cook and a baker, he is famous—or perhaps notorious—for introducing travelers to the culinary uses of local vermin. Tucked against the crags just east of the Crossroads, Grub oversees a rustic dwelling shared with Duhng, his cook, and Tarban Hearthgrain, a baker. While life on the plains demands a hearty stomach, Grub takes frontier self-sufficiency to an extreme. Rather than letting the abundant dig rats of the Barrens go to waste, he has turned them into a staple ingredient, offering to teach passing wanderers how to simmer the subterranean rodents into a savory, if unglamorous, stew.

Grull Hawkwind. Grull Hawkwind is a young tauren brave stationed at Camp Narache on the Red Cloud Mesa in Mulgore. As the son of Chief Hawkwind, he helps guide novice tauren taking their very first steps into the world. He directs young hunters and warriors through their earliest trials to test their resolve and honor their ancestors. Standing proudly beside the braves and elders of Camp Narache, Grull Hawkwind bears both the proud lineage of Chief Hawkwind and the responsibility of preparing the tribe's youth. He serves as an initial mentor for new arrivals on the Red Cloud Mesa, assessing their readiness to serve the Shu'halo. By assigning trials that test stamina, tracking, and survival against local beasts such as plainstriders and mountain cougars, Grull ensures that young tauren understand that balance and respect for nature are foundational to life in Mulgore.

Grunt Dogran. Grunt Dogran is an orc soldier of the Horde held prisoner deep within the quilboar territory of the southern Barrens. Originally assigned to the Crossroads and later Camp Taurajo, his patrol met with disaster during a raid on Agama'gor. Following his promotion within the Horde military, Grunt Dogran was dispatched from the Crossroads to reinforce Camp Taurajo. While leading a detachment of grunts into the bristled territory of Agama'gor, his unit clashed fiercely with the Bristleback quilboar. Severely injured and crippled during the fray, Dogran could not be carried away by his retreating comrades and was dragged into captivity.

Grunt Logmar. Grunt Logmar is an orc warrior of the Horde stationed in the southern Barrens at Camp Taurajo. Dutiful and vigilant, he monitors threats surrounding the camp and coordinates efforts to locate and aid missing Horde scouts in the region. Stationed among the tauren at Camp Taurajo, Grunt Logmar serves as a watchful orc guard on the southern Barrens frontier. The settlement sits close to hostile quilboar grounds and the mountain passes leading into Stonetalon and Mulgore, requiring constant vigilance. Logmar coordinates scouting reports and reaches out to capable Horde travelers when his comrades find themselves ambushed or captured by local hostiles.

Grunth. Grunth is an energetic young orc orphan living under the care of the Orgrimmar orphanage in the Drag. During Children's Week, he eagerly accompanies Horde champions on grand journeys across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to learn what it means to be a hero. Residing in the Drag of Orgrimmar under the watchful gaze of Orphan Matron Battlewail, Grunth represents the next generation of the newly established Horde. Like many young greenskins raised in Durotar's harsh red wastes, he looks upon armored adventurers with wide-eyed awe and an inexhaustible stream of questions—wondering whether armored warriors are truly terrifying, why lightning on water doesn't kill every fish, and whether he will ever see someone fight an actual dragon.

Gryan Stoutmantle. Gryan Stoutmantle is a paladin of the Silver Hand and the commander of the People's Militia, operating out of Sentinel Hill in Westfall. Born in Westfall, he returned from the devastated northern kingdom of Lordaeron to protect his homeland after Stormwind's crown abandoned the region to banditry. Gryan Stoutmantle began his service far from the quiet fields of southern Azeroth. Traveling north to Lordaeron as a young man, he took vows as a Knight of the Silver Hand and endured the horrors of the Third War. When news reached him that his native province of Westfall was collapsing into lawlessness, overrun by organized brigands and abandoned by the crown, Gryan left the northern fronts behind. He traded imperial battlefields for the defense of honest farmers, swearing that his home would not fall as the north had.

Guard Berton. Guard Berton is a human town guardsman stationed outside the Lakeshire Inn in Redridge Mountains. Frustrated by the bureaucratic delays of Stormwind's legal system, he seeks swift justice against Targorr the Dread, an imprisoned orc leader. While Redridge Mountains buckles under the threat of the Blackrock orc invasion, Guard Berton remains posted outside the Lakeshire Inn. Despite local defenses being pushed to the brink, Berton's attention is fixed on a captive enemy: Targorr the Dread. Targorr was captured and locked away deep within the Stormwind Stockade, sentenced to death for his crimes against the kingdom. Yet with Stormwind's execution postponed indefinitely, Berton refuses to let the brutal raider linger in a cell while Lakeshire bleeds. Taking matters into his own hands, he hires willing adventurers to bypass royal delays and execute the orc directly.

Guard Howe. Guard Howe is a town guardsman stationed near the southern foot of the Lakeshire bridge in the Redridge Mountains. Driven by a personal vendetta against the Blackrock orcs encroaching on the valley, he offers bounties to any adventurer willing to cut down the invaders. Positioned just south of the large stone bridge spanning Lake Everstill, Guard Howe stands watch over the heart of Lakeshire. Like many in the beleaguered town, he sees the encroaching Blackrock orcs as an existential threat to Redridge. Harbouring a bitter desire for revenge against the clan, Howe actively recruits passing mercenaries to hunt orcs in the eastern hills, offering pay in exchange for tangible proof of their defeat.

Guard Thomas. Guard Thomas is a dedicated soldier of the Stormwind Army stationed at the bridge west of the Eastvale Logging Camp. Isolated on the eastern frontier of Elwynn Forest, he oversees the defense of local settlers against predatory wildlife and encroaching murlocs. While much of the realm's attention is focused inward toward the capital or west toward Westfall, Guard Thomas holds one of the quietest yet most precarious posts in Elwynn Forest. Positioned at the stone bridge crossing the river toward Eastvale Logging Camp, Thomas acts as the thin blue line between everyday forestry workers and the aggressive creatures roaming the woods. With the Stormwind military stretched thin, guards like Thomas must rely heavily on passing adventurers to maintain order and carry messages back to central command.

Gubber Blump. Gubber Blump is a dwarf fisherman and trainer stationed along the shores of Auberdine in Darkshore. Positioned on the sands between the docks and the flight master, he is an enthusiastic lover of the angling craft and seafood, particularly fresh crab meat. While most dwarves find comfort beneath stone or beside a roaring forge, Gubber Blump prefers the misty coastline of Darkshore. Stationed along the beach at Auberdine, between the flight master and the ferry pier, Gubber teaches the art of fishing and sells basic angling gear to passing travelers. He holds a deep culinary appreciation for crab meat, though he frequently relies on adventurers to help secure his catches along the dangerous coast, as well as reclaim sentimental family fishing tackle.

Gunther Arcanus. Gunther Arcanus is an exceptionally powerful necromancer dwelling on an isolated island in Brightwater Lake. Slain during the Third War and raised into undeath, he managed to shatter the Lich King's mental grip entirely on his own. Long believing he was the sole undead possessing free will, he defended his retreat against all outsiders until discovered by the Forsaken. Before the fall of Lordaeron, Gunther was a promising apprentice among the Kirin Tor in Dalaran. Alongside close friends Bethor Iceshard and Thule Ravenclaw, he studied the arcane arts, secretly delving into necromancy despite the Kirin Tor's strict prohibitions against dark magic. To commemorate their brotherhood, the trio once bound their apprentice wands together into a single heirloom.

Gurda Ragescar. Gurda Ragescar was an orc stationed at a small Horde outpost southwest of Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. Alongside Feran Strongwind, she fell defending their camp against local perils in the shadowed forest. Resting just southwest of the fortified walls of Splintertree Post, Gurda Ragescar maintained a modest Horde camp under the dense canopy of Ashenvale. Deep within territory contested by night elven defenders and wild beasts, maintaining such isolated positions is perilous work. Gurda, along with Feran Strongwind and their detachment of guards, was ultimately overrun and killed at their post, leaving only the remnants of their final stand for passing allies to discover.

Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde is a night elf residing in the coastal port of Auberdine. Stationed along the misty Darkshore coast, she watches the tides and directs travelers to investigate the strange remains washing ashore. Her concerns center on the mysterious sea creatures and massive turtles whose carcasses have begun littering the northern beaches. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde makes her home in Auberdine, the bustling seaside haven of Darkshore. While many in town concern themselves with the forest or shipping across the Veiled Sea, Gwennyth keeps her gaze firmly on the coastline. The tides have recently turned grim, depositing the remains of colossal marine life onto the surf. To understand what is happening in the waters offshore, she relies on willing adventurers to scour the sands, retrieve skeletal samples, and bring back answers.

Hagar Lightninghoof. Hagar Lightninghoof is a tauren scout stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Driven by rumors of a strange clutch hidden in the canyon depths, he investigates reports of an alien egg guarded fiercely by local wind serpents. While stationed among the towering bluffs of Freewind Post, Hagar Lightninghoof caught wind of rumors regarding an unnatural egg nestled deep inside a cavern below. The local wind serpents guarded the nest with unusual ferocity, keeping curious scouts at bay. Seeking an adventurer bold enough to brave the serpents' den, Hagar hopes to study the specimen firsthand and discern what manner of beast could warrant such defensive instincts from the canyon's natural predators.

Halaan Hawk-Eye. Halaan Hawk-Eye is a Skyborne lookout stationed atop the watchtower of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. Lacking both magical sensitivity and the mystic skysight of his peers, he relies instead on keen mundane vision to monitor the surrounding island. From his perch, he tracks the distant anchor pylons and warns visitors of their faltering arcane stability. Perched high above Thendal Village, Halaan Hawk-Eye serves his people without the gifts common to many Skyborne. He cannot draw upon the arcane power flowing through the ley lines beneath Zephras Isle, nor can he gaze between worlds through the mystical skysight. Instead, Halaan relies entirely on his sharp natural senses. From his vantage point on the watchtower, he scans the horizon to observe the island's anchor pylons, calling attention to their increasingly volatile and inconsistent arcane energies.

Hamhock. Hamhock is a massive two-headed ogre confined within the depths of the Stormwind Stockade. Locked away beneath the capital alongside hardened Defias insurgents and cutthroats, he looms as a particularly brutal and unexpected inmate amidst the prison riot. The Stormwind Stockade was built to hold petty thieves, murderers, and political dissidents, making a towering two-headed ogre an imposing sight among the cells. When the prisoners rose up and took control of the facility, Hamhock remained entrenched in the chaos, crushing anyone foolish enough to intrude on his cellblock.

Hana'zua. Hana'zua is a Darkspear troll scout stationed in the Valley of Trials who fell victim to the poisonous beasts prowling the canyon ridges. Stricken and wounded by the monstrous scorpid Sarkoth, he lies awaiting assistance from young Horde initiates seeking to prove their valor. While traversing the arid heights overlooking the Valley of Trials, Hana'zua encountered Sarkoth, an exceptionally vicious and venomous scorpid that stalks the cliffs. Overwhelmed and stung by the beast, the troll barely survived the confrontation. Unable to move or return to camp on his own, he languishes amid the dust, counting on passing recruits to finish the creature and deliver word of his plight back to the Den.

Hands Springsprocket. Hands Springsprocket is an industrious gnome stationed at the entrance of Coldridge Pass in Dun Morogh. He coordinates shipments between the secluded training grounds of Coldridge Valley and the town of Kharanos, though recent trogg incursions have severely hampered his efforts. Perched at the mouth of Coldridge Pass, Hands Springsprocket finds his regular supply runs thoroughly disrupted. He routinely delivers provisions to the Thunderbrew distillery and the inn in Kharanos, but hostile Rockjaw troggs have overrun the subterranean tunnel leading out of the valley. With trade and foot traffic halted by the beasts, Hands is forced to rely on capable travelers to carry essential crates through the dangerous mountain corridor.

Hansel Heavyhands. Hansel Heavyhands is an unusually massive Dark Iron dwarf stationed with the Thorium Brotherhood atop Thorium Point in the Searing Gorge. Tasked with perilous field work by the outpost's overseers, he consistently delegates dangerous jobs to passing adventurers using a colorful array of petty physical complaints. His hulking frame stands out among his kin, even if his enthusiasm for fieldwork does not match his size. Even by the broad-shouldered standards of the Dark Iron clan, Hansel Heavyhands is an anomaly. Towering over his brethren with a massive frame that borders on orcish in width and height, his sheer physical presence suggests a warrior built for frontline slaughter. Yet despite his imposing build and formidable moniker, Hansel appears utterly uninterested in unnecessary physical exertion, preferring the relative security of the Thorium Brotherhood's camp high above the volcanic ash.

Harb Clawhoof. Harb Clawhoof is a tauren mount breeder stationed just outside Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. He tends to the tribe's sturdy kodos, offering them to worthy tauren riders and trusted champions of Thunder Bluff. Situated near the pens of Bloodhoof Village, Harb Clawhoof spends his days tending the massive kodo beasts that serve as the backbone of tauren travel and labor. Built to carry immense weight across vast distances, these sturdy animals are essential to life on the plains. Harb ensures each beast is well-cared for, disciplined, and matched only with riders who command the respect of the tauren people.

Harken Windtotem. Harken Windtotem is a tauren huntsman residing in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Dedicated to the traditions of his people, he tasks young hunters and travelers with proving their tracking and foraging skills across the golden plains. Situated near the heart of Bloodhoof Village, Harken Windtotem serves as an instructor and guide for those learning the hunting ways of the tauren. Life on the plains of Mulgore demands respect for the natural world alongside the practical skill to sustain one's tribe. Harken evaluates young adventurers by directing them to hunt the native swoops that circle the mesas, collecting their quills to gauge a hunter's patience, aim, and ability to harvest without waste.

Harlan Bagley. Harlan Bagley is a human armorer and merchant operating out of the Lionheart Armory in Stormwind City's bustling Trade District. He tends his shop on the northern side of the district center, looking after arms and equipment for citizens and visiting adventurers alike. Situated along the northern side of the Trade District, the Lionheart Armory serves as a steady commercial fixture within the heart of Stormwind. From behind his counter, Harlan Bagley manages inventory and deals in defensive gear, relying on incoming trade and regional couriers to keep his shelves stocked while the capital contends with distant border conflicts and supply constraints.

Harlo Barnaby. Harlo Barnaby is a wounded dwarven refugee residing in Menethil Harbor. Having barely escaped the slaughter when the Dark Iron clan seized Dun Modr, he now alerts travelers to the tragedy that unfolded in the northern marshes. Harlo Barnaby lived in Dun Modr until the northern stronghold fell to a sudden, savage assault by the Dark Iron dwarves. In the chaos of the ambush, Harlo fled south toward safety, only to catch a stray axe square in the back. Knocked unconscious by the blow, he somehow survived the trek across the marshland and awoke bandaged in Menethil Harbor. Though alive, his wounds and memories of the massacre leave him unable to return, prompting him to urge Alliance adventurers to investigate the smoking ruins of his former home.

Hegnar Rumbleshot. Hegnar Rumbleshot is a dwarven gunsmith stationed along the snowy roadway leading from Coldridge Pass toward Kharanos. He maintains a busy shooting range and equips local hunters and mountaineers with firearms and ammunition. Set up at a small campsite between Coldridge Pass and Kharanos, Hegnar Rumbleshot caters to dwarven marksmen, travelers, and the local militia. His camp features a popular shooting range where mountain folk hone their aim against the wild beasts prowling Dun Morogh. Supplying so many eager shooters means Hegnar burns through munitions at a brisk pace, leaving him perpetually reliant on fresh shipments of ammunition from his supplier, the dwarf engineer Loslor Rudge.

Henze Faulk. Henze Faulk is a dwarven adventurer found lying near death on the stone circle outside Heroes' Vigil in Elwynn Forest. Struck down by the Defias Brotherhood while shielding his companion, he serves as a pivotal test for aspiring paladins learning to wield the gift of resurrection. Near the ancient stone ring east of Stormwind sits Heroes' Vigil, a place often haunted by Defias bandits prowling the Elwynn woods. Henze Faulk and his friend Gazin Tenorm were ambushed here by Defias marauders. Putting himself in harm's way to ensure Gazin's survival, Henze fell to the bandits' blades. While his companion survived to summon aid from the Cathedral of Light, Henze's body remains on the threshold of life and death, awaiting the divine intervention of a paladin carrying a Symbol of Life.

Heralath Fallowbrook. Heralath Fallowbrook is a dying night elf druid imprisoned deep within Razorfen Kraul. Dispatched to investigate the thorny corruption surrounding the remains of the Ancient Agamaggan, he was captured and brutalized by the Razorfen tribe. With his final breaths, he seeks to send word of his fate and a cherished pendant back to his wife in Darnassus. Sent by his people to investigate the ancient boar god Agamaggan and the spreading briars choking the southern Barrens, Heralath Fallowbrook sought the root of Razorfen Kraul's corruption. Instead of unearthing answers, the night elf was taken prisoner by the quilboar. Locked in a squalid pen and relentlessly beaten, Heralath succumbed to severe wounds and raging fever. Before fading entirely, he shared what he knew with a fellow captive, the dwarf Henrig Lonebrow, urging him to warn the sentinel outpost at Thalanaar about the aggression stirred up by the quilboar crone Charlga Razorflank.

Herod. Herod is a renowned champion and berserker of the Scarlet Crusade, commanding the Armory within the Scarlet Monastery. Known for his ferocious martial prowess and unyielding zeal, he trains recruits in the brutal melee combat needed to wage holy war. His death is sought by both Alliance dissidents and the Horde's rulers in Undercity to weaken the Crusade's military core. Within the fortified halls of the Scarlet Monastery's Armory, Herod stands as the embodiment of the Crusade's martial aggression. Unlike the spellcasters and paladins who channel holy magic in the Cathedral, Herod relies on raw, bloodthirsty physical power. Clad in mail and wielding a massive two-handed axe, he personally trains cohorts of Scarlet Trainees, instilling a furious devotion to exterminating anyone not allied with their fanatical cause.

High Executor Darthalia. High Executor Darthalia is a high-ranking Forsaken military commander stationed at Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Acting under the direct authority of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and Varimathras, she directs Forsaken operations against the human stronghold of Southshore and local Syndicate brigands. Her leadership is central to securing the Horde's southern flank in Lordaeron. Operating out of Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia serves as the operational commander for Forsaken forces throughout the Hillsbrad Foothills. Her primary strategic concern is halting the expansion of human resistance, keeping the Alliance forces in Southshore contained, and hunting down the lawless Syndicate rogues infesting the surrounding countryside. Every offensive push into southern Hillsbrad flows directly through her command.

High Executor Derrington. High Executor Derrington commands the Forsaken vanguard stationed at the Bulwark on the eastern border of Tirisfal Glades. A no-nonsense military officer, he oversees the Horde's front-line defense against the Scourge and Scarlet Crusade threats emanating from the Western Plaguelands. From this fortified barricade, he directs seasoned champions toward contested ruins like Andorhal and Scholomance. Standing directly before the fortified barricades of the Bulwark, High Executor Derrington serves as the gatekeeper between the haunted safety of Tirisfal Glades and the rotting horrors of the Western Plaguelands. Derrington holds little patience for political maneuvering in the Undercity, viewing the front lines as a crucible of sheer survival. For Horde soldiers and sellswords seeking to test their mettle, Derrington provides direct military orders, sending scouts and strike teams deep into plagueridden territory to blunt enemy incursions before they breach Tirisfal.

High Executor Hadrec. High Executor Hadrec is the military commander of the Forsaken garrison stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. From this central crypt, he oversees defense against regional threats including the gnolls of the Rot Hide clan and investigates the disappearance of scouts across the zone. He serves as the primary officer directing Horde operations throughout Silverpine. Stationed within the gloom of the Sepulcher, High Executor Hadrec directs Forsaken military operations across Silverpine Forest. While Tirisfal Glades is firmly secured by the Dark Lady's forces, Silverpine remains fraught with peril, bordered by hostile Dalaran mages, feral worgen, and encroaching gnolls. Hadrec bears the grim responsibility of consolidating Forsaken territory and stamping out anything that challenges Undercity authority south of the capital.

High Inquisitor Fairbanks. High Inquisitor Fairbanks was once a revered priest of the Knights of the Silver Hand and the most trusted advisor to Highlord Alexandros Mograine. Betrayed, executed, and hidden away behind a secret door in the Scarlet Monastery Cathedral, his rotting, undead form stands as a grim monument to the Scarlet Crusade's dark descent. Before the fall of Lordaeron, Fairbanks was a respected holy man among the Knights of the Silver Hand and the most trusted advisor of Highlord Alexandros Mograine, the bearer of the legendary Ashbringer. He stood beside the Highlord when Mograine, High General Abbendis and Grand Inquisitor Isillien founded the Scarlet Crusade, at first a noble order sworn to destroy the Scourge.

High Priest Rohan. High Priest Rohan is the preeminent leader of the Church of the Holy Light within Ironforge, found pacing inside the Hall of Mysteries. He oversees the spiritual development of fledgling priests across the Alliance and aids those seeking mastery over the Holy Light. Through his guidance and sacred relics, he maintains spiritual ties between the mountain kingdom, Stormwind, and distant allies. Pacing the quiet flagstones of the Hall of Mysteries in the Mystic Ward, High Priest Rohan acts as the highest-ranking representative of the Church of the Holy Light in Ironforge. While dwarves historically honored the titans, dwarven priests have deeply embraced the Light's virtues of wisdom, compassion, and justice. Rohan serves as a patient teacher to young acolytes, teaching them the discipline necessary to channel holy magic and steel their minds against despair.

High Priestess Laurena. High Priestess Laurena is a respected human priest trainer stationed behind the grand altar within Stormwind City's Cathedral of Light. She instructs budding Alliance priests in spiritual devotion and arcane wards. As a High Priestess of the Church of the Holy Light, Laurena holds one of the senior posts within the towering halls of the Cathedral of Light, the heart of the faith in Stormwind City, where Archbishop Benedictus leads the Church.

Highlord Demitrian. Highlord Demitrian is a solitary human hermit dwelling amidst the strange crystals of northwestern Silithus. Describing himself as a loyal servant of Prince Thunderaan, he possesses the esoteric knowledge required to wake the slumbering elemental lord. Adventurers bearing ancient elemental bindings seek him out to unlock the power of the Windseeker. Found lingering at an abandoned encampment in the Crystal Vale, Demitrian appears out of place in the desolate wastes of Silithus. Though he is tied to the Twilight's Hammer whose ravaged camp he haunts, Demitrian acts above all as a herald for Prince Thunderaan, the Windseeker. He treats visitors with aloof indifference unless they carry proof of the Windseeker's shattered essence.

Hogger. Hogger is the vicious chieftain of the Riverpaw gnolls prowling southwestern Elwynn Forest. Towering over his kin and remarkably aggressive, he has become notorious for raiding local farms and butchering unsuspecting travelers. His violent rampages have earned him an official bounty from the Stormwind Marshals. Prowling atop Hogger Hill in southwestern Elwynn Forest, Hogger commands the local Riverpaw pack with unmatched savagery. In the years following the Third War, gnoll raids across local homesteads grew increasingly bold and coordinated. Behind this rise in violence lies an unsettling alliance: the Riverpaw have begun colluding with the Defias Brotherhood, trading raw ferocity for arms, tactical direction, and magical support. To safeguard Elwynn's borders and protect trade routes from further bloodshed, Marshal Dughan has posted a generous bounty on Hogger's head.

Holt Thunderhorn. Holt Thunderhorn is a tauren hunter trainer stationed upon Hunter Rise in the elevated city of Thunder Bluff. He instructs novice and seasoned track-masters in their craft, offering basic martial guidance and pointing maturing marksmen toward specialized trials across Mulgore and beyond. Perched on Hunter Rise above the sweeping plains of Mulgore, Holt Thunderhorn serves the Horde as a seasoned instructor in ranged combat, tracking, and survival. Like many elders of his craft, he guides young tauren as they make the transition from roaming hunters into disciplined defenders of their new capital.

Houndmaster Loksey. Houndmaster Loksey is the officer charged with breeding and training the fearsome war dogs of the Scarlet Crusade. Stationed in the Scarlet Monastery's Library wing, he directs packs of hounds to hunt down undead, intruders, and perceived heretics.
