His merciless discipline has made the Monastery's beasts infamous throughout Tirisfal Glades. Within the heavily fortified walls of the Scarlet Monastery, Houndmaster Loksey commands the training of vicious tracking and attack dogs. The Scarlet Crusade relies on these trained hounds to sniff out plague-tainted corpses, uncover hidden infiltrators, and run down any survivors fleeing the zealots' wrath. Loksey holds absolute authority over the hounds guarding the Library wing, ensuring his charges are primed to tear intruders apart limb by limb.

Huldar. Huldar is a dwarven teamster stationed along the southern road of Loch Modan, near the shores of the lake. Tasked with hauling vital blast powder to the dig site in the south, his delivery caravan faces relentless harassment from local threats and Dark Iron saboteurs. Hauling explosives through Loch Modan is no simple trade route. Huldar was tasked with driving wagonloads of mining blast powder down toward the southern excavation site, where dwarven archaeologists and prospectors desperately need supplies. However, the wilderness roads have become increasingly hazardous. With local wildlife, troggs, and Dark Iron infiltrators lurking near the lake's southern bend, Huldar finds himself stranded by his damaged wagon, relying on wandering travelers to safeguard the remaining powder kegs and ensure the shipment reaches the dig.

Illiyana. Illiyana is an ancient dryad stationed in southwestern Ashenvale, dedicated to protecting the woodland from ancient corruption. Wandering near the Shrine of Aessina, she rallies champions of the Alliance to push back against the vicious satyrs that plague the ancient groves. Her vigilance represents the enduring bond between the daughters of Cenarius and the night elven wilderness. Like all dryads, Illiyana is one of the daughters of the demigod Cenarius. Peaceful yet fiercely protective of wild lands, she patrols the woods of southwestern Ashenvale. As dark forces stir and the woodlands suffer under creeping corruption, Illiyana keeps watch over sacred relics and groves, acting as a steward for nature's primal sanctity.

Illiyana Moonblaze. Illiyana Moonblaze is a night elf supply officer stationed at Silverwing Grove in Ashenvale. Operating alongside the Silverwing Sentinels, she supplies Alliance champions waging war against the Warsong Outriders. Illiyana Moonblaze serves as the supply officer for the Silverwing Sentinels nestled in Silverwing Grove. From her post near the path into Warsong Gulch, she outfits the defenders who hold the southern woods of Ashenvale against the Warsong clan.

Ilthalaine. Ilthalaine is a night elf guardian standing watch over the sacred glade of Shadowglen in Teldrassil. He serves as the primary greeter and mentor for young night elves taking their very first steps into the world. Vigilant and attuned to the wilderness, he guides novice adventurers toward maintaining the delicate balance of nature across the boughs of the World Tree. Positioned just outside the heart of Shadowglen, Ilthalaine is often the first face a fledgling night elf sees upon beginning their journey. He observes the woodland paths and notices the subtle shifts within the forest that go unseen by ordinary eyes. His duty is to welcome returning kin and ensure that any newly awakened defenders are grounded in the traditions of their people, ready to face the responsibilities that come with tending to Teldrassil.

Innkeeper Allison. Innkeeper Allison manages the Gilded Rose, one of the busiest and most central inns in Stormwind City. Located in the heart of the Trade District right between the bank and auction house, she provides weary travelers and local merchants with hearthstone bindings, refreshing drinks, and shelter. Positioned squarely between the bustling trade auction house and the main city vaults, the Gilded Rose serves as an epicenter for adventurers arriving in Stormwind. Innkeeper Allison stands behind the main counter on the ground floor, keeping order amidst a constant flow of peddlers, mercenaries, and visiting diplomats. Beyond offering lodging and hearthstone services, she frequently participates in local holiday festivities and coordinates small errands for traveling heroes seeking rest within the capital.

Innkeeper Farley. Innkeeper Farley manages the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, providing food, lodging, and hearthstones to travelers passing through Elwynn Forest. Well-liked and observant, he often holds misplaced mail and listens to the troubles of adventurers on the road. Innkeeper Farley runs the Lion's Pride Inn with a welcoming hand and a sharp eye. Travelers bound for Stormwind, Westfall and Duskwood stop at his counter for a warm meal, a mug of ale and a bed, and Farley keeps order in one of the realm's busiest waystations, pouring ale and serving cheese to all who pass through Goldshire.

Innkeeper Firebrew. Innkeeper Firebrew manages the Stonefire Tavern in the bustling Commons of Ironforge. A genial host to weary mountaineers and visiting dignitaries alike, he serves hearty dwarven staples and keeps travelers rested beneath the mountain. Situated in the central ring of the Commons, Innkeeper Firebrew's establishment is often the first sanctuary encountered by travelers entering through the Great Gates of Ironforge. Behind a counter laden with flagons of ale, skins of stout, and roasted joints of meat, Firebrew offers hospitality to adventurers bound for the snowy passes of Dun Morogh or deeper into the mountain kingdom. His tavern remains a lively crossroad where miners, riflemen, and emissaries gather to escape the drafty tunnels and exchange tales around the hearth.

Innkeeper Grosk. Innkeeper Grosk manages the inn at Razor Hill, providing weary travelers with food, drink, and a place to rest in central Durotar. Located on the bustling road between the Valley of Trials and Orgrimmar, his establishment serves as the primary resting point for young Horde adventurers setting out into the wider world. Razor Hill serves as the vital crossroad settlement connecting the southern training grounds of Durotar to the high walls of Orgrimmar. At the center of this waystation stands Innkeeper Grosk, an orc tasked with sheltering warriors, scouts, and peons alike. His inn offers a respite from the harsh desert heat, stocked with basic provisions, hearty meats, and cool water for any traveler passing beneath its sturdy timbers.

Innkeeper Gryshka. Innkeeper Gryshka is an orc host who manages the Broken Tusk inn in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. Serving as the primary hospitality contact for travelers arriving through the city gates, she provides hearthstone bindings, food, and drink to visiting Horde adventurers. She maintains close ties with hunters and scouts across Durotar and the Barrens to keep her tavern stocked with choice cuts of meat. Standing behind the counter of the Broken Tusk, Gryshka manages one of the most heavily trafficked inns in the Horde. Located just beyond the main gates of Orgrimmar in the Valley of Strength, her establishment serves as the first point of rest for warriors, messengers, and newly arrived champions seeking shelter under Thrall's banner.

Innkeeper Keldamyr. Innkeeper Keldamyr manages the hearth and lodgings of the central inn in Dolanaar, Teldrassil. He offers food, drink, and a resting place for young night elves venturing forth from Shadowglen into the wider boughs of the World Tree. Dolanaar is the primary village newcomers reach after departing the sheltered glade of Aldrassil. Innkeeper Keldamyr maintains the community's central haven, providing bread, spring water, and soft beds beneath the canopy of Teldrassil. Travelers, sentinels, and young novices bound for Darnassus frequently pause at his counter to rest their spirits, secure their hearthstones, and stock rations for the journey through the boughs.

Innkeeper Norman. Innkeeper Norman tends the hearth at the primary tavern in the Trade Quarter of the Undercity. A quiet, diligent Forsaken, he offers travelers of the Horde respite, hearthstone bindings, and food suited to the varied tastes of both the living and the dead. Located in the bustling Trade Quarter beneath the ruined Capital City of Lordaeron, Innkeeper Norman provides lodging for emissaries, mercenaries, and adventurers passing through the Forsaken stronghold. Despite the damp chill and alchemical stenches of the Undercity, Norman's tavern remains a bustling hub for travelers looking to anchor their hearthstones, share news from across Azeroth, or prepare for expeditions into the Plaguelands.

Innkeeper Pala. Innkeeper Pala manages the Cat and the Shaman, the bustling tavern situated on the lower tier of Thunder Bluff. She offers visiting adventurers a hearthstone binding, cold drinks, and a place to rest between journeys across Mulgore and beyond. Perched on the lower rise of Thunder Bluff's sweeping mesas, Innkeeper Pala tends the hearth at the Cat and the Shaman. The establishment serves as one of the primary gathering points for travelers stepping off the central lifts or arriving from the sprawling plains of Mulgore. Holding a steady vigil over her common room, Pala ensures that weary warriors, wandering druids, and visiting allies of the Horde find a dependable shelter, a warm drink, and a familiar home away from home.

Interrogator Vishas. Interrogator James Vishas is the Scarlet Crusade's master of torment, stationed deep within the Scarlet Monastery's Graveyard wing. Infamous for his shrill voice and sheer cruelty, he takes twisted pleasure in breaking captives and testing the limits of mortal flesh. Few who enter his torture chambers ever leave with their minds or bodies intact. Within the dark crypts and burial grounds of the Scarlet Monastery, Interrogator Vishas tends to the Crusade's captive enemies. While the zealots outside march in gleaming armor under banners of purity, Vishas represents the grim reality behind their crusade: unbridled sadism cloaked in religious righteous fury. He approaches interrogation not merely as an intelligence duty, but as a prized craft, reveling in the agony of Forsaken captives, captured Scourge, and any living travelers unlucky enough to be branded heretics.

Islen Waterseer. Islen Waterseer is a respected tauren shaman who dwells beside a quiet fishing hut on the Tidus Stair, overlooking the eastern sea of the Barrens. Possessing an intimate communion with the spirits of water, she guides initiates on the trials necessary to attune with the element. Novice shamans across the Horde seek her wisdom to earn their Water Totem. Far from the bustling crossroads and encampments of the Barrens, Islen Waterseer lives along the craggy coastline known as the Tidus Stair. Here, where the arid plains break against the Great Sea, the presence of the water spirits is raw and pervasive. Rather than dwelling in thunderous halls or busy cities, Islen prefers this quiet outpost, dedicating her days to listening to the tides and assisting shamans who seek communion with the fluid element.

Iverron. Iverron is a young night elf found in Shadowglen, the sheltered starting bough of Teldrassil. Stricken by the venom of the woodland's increasingly agitated arachnids, his plight serves as an early warning of the growing corruption within the World Tree. While wandering through the quiet canopies of Shadowglen, Iverron ran afoul of the webwood spiders nesting in the vale. Succumbing quickly to their toxic bite, the young elf was left incapacitated, unable to return to safety on his own. His helpless condition highlights the sudden aggression sweeping through creatures that once shared the glade in peace.

Jahan Hawkwing. Jahan Hawkwing is a tauren armorer stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. He provides essential leather and chainmail gear to travelers braving the harsh, predator-filled plains. Situated at the bustling hub of the Crossroads, Jahan Hawkwing tends to the equipment needs of Horde wanderers and defenders. The Barrens is a brutal expanse where durable protective gear often makes the difference between survival and falling to centaur, quilboar, or wild beasts. Jahan works alongside local leatherworkers, handling deliveries of cured hides to keep his shop stocked with reliable tanned leather and sturdy chainmail.

Jaina Proudmoore. Lady Jaina Proudmoore is the ruler of Theramore Isle and the most powerful human sorceress alive. Formerly a star pupil of Dalaran's Kirin Tor, she led the survivors of Lordaeron across the Great Sea and now strives to maintain a fragile peace between the Alliance and the New Horde. The daughter of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras, Jaina showed remarkable aptitude for the arcane at an early age and studied under Archmage Antonidas in Dalaran. During the Third War, she investigated the mysterious Plague of Undeath alongside Prince Arthas Menethil, witnessing firsthand the tragic downfall of Lordaeron. Guided by the warnings of the Prophet Medivh, she rallied an expedition of human survivors and set sail westward to the forgotten continent of Kalimdor. There, her forces forged an unprecedented alliance with Thrall's Horde and the night elves, standing together atop Mount Hyjal to defeat Archimonde and shatter the Burning Legion's invasion.

James Halloran. James Halloran is a human tanner working out of the Wetlands to supply fine hides across the eastern continents. Based in Menethil Harbor, he makes a living harvesting the tough, prized skins of the region's native crocolisks. He relies on passing travelers and nearby trade channels to gather raw materials and transport his finished leathers to market. From his home in Menethil Harbor, James Halloran makes his living from the marshland just outside town. As an enterprising tanner, Halloran recognized that the perilous bogs offer a lucrative commodity: crocolisk skins. Transforming the rugged hide of marsh reptiles into high-quality leather requires rare craftsmanship, and Halloran's finished goods are shipped out through local trade channels to buyers all across Azeroth.

Jannok Breezesong. Jannok Breezesong is a night elf rogue trainer stationed in the village of Dolanaar on Teldrassil. He offers instruction in stealth, cunning, and bladecraft to young kaldorei rogues venturing out into the boughs of the World Tree. Found lounging beneath the boughs of Dolanaar, Jannok Breezesong serves as the primary instructor for novice night elf rogues. Unlike the formal sentinels or cloistered druids of Teldrassil, Jannok guides those who operate quietly on the fringes of society, teaching them how to stalk the shadows, strike from behind, and survive unseen amidst the boughs. Once a rogue has advanced beyond initial lessons in Dolanaar, Jannok directs them onward to more experienced masters in the capital city of Darnassus.

Jasper Fel. Jasper Fel is a discreet supplier operating out of the SI:7 headquarters in Stormwind's Old Town. Providing daggers and assorted vials to operatives, he keeps a sharp eye on visitors and warns them to watch their tongues. His quiet trade supports the covert arm of the kingdom behind closed doors. Tucked away inside the barracks of SI:7 within Old Town, Jasper Fel caters to a very specific clientele. Rather than hawking standard arms to the city guard, he provides essential implements of tradecraft: simple daggers and the delicate vials required for brewing and applying poisons. Fel operates under the strict discipline of Mathias Shaw's intelligence division, curtly advising any who approach to mind their speech. In a stronghold dedicated to espionage and subtle lethality, casual chatter is an easy way to meet an early end.

Je'neu Sancrea. Je'neu Sancrea is a Darkspear troll and a member of the Earthen Ring stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the Ashenvale coast. Sensing dark disturbances deep beneath the shoreline, he directs Horde adventurers to investigate the corruption infesting the ancient submerged temple of Blackfathom Deeps. While most of the Earthen Ring focuses on elemental harmony across Kalimdor, Je'neu Sancrea keeps watch over the secluded and dangerous Zoram Strand. Perched at Zoram'gar Outpost, he observes the dark tremors and unnatural tides stirring near the ruined temple of Blackfathom Deeps. Though bound by the shamanic duties of his circle, his strong loyalties to the Darkspear tribe and Thrall's Horde keep him working exclusively alongside Horde champions.

Jen'shan. Jen'shan is a Darkspear jungle troll and hunter trainer stationed in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. She guides fledgling orc and troll marksmen as they take their first steps into the wilds of the Horde. Young hunters are directed to her to learn the basics of tracking, ranged combat, and survival. Perched among the weathered encampments of the Valley of Trials, Jen'shan serves as the primary hunter mentor for new recruits proving their worth to the Horde. Together, young orcs and Darkspear trolls arrive clutching inscribed tablets and parchments directing them straight to her side. With keen eyes sharpened by years in the untamed wilderness, she imparts foundational techniques in archery, marksmanship, and wilderness survival, ensuring no novice falls prey to the scorpids and boars prowling the canyon floor.

Jennea Cannon. Jennea Cannon is a respected human mage trainer residing within the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. She oversees the education of novice sorcerers, guiding them through foundational studies and investigating disturbances in the flow of local arcane energies. Through her tasks, she tests whether apprentices have the discipline needed to control magic without being consumed by it. Positioned atop the spiral walkway of the Wizard's Sanctum, Jennea Cannon stands as one of the primary mentors for arcane practitioners entering Stormwind. Rather than merely drilling spells into pupils, she emphasizes caution and self-control. To non-mages passing through the tower, she offers a sharp warning: unchecked magic will burn the untrained, a truth novice spellcasters learn quickly under her tutelage.

Jergosh the Invoker. Jergosh the Invoker is a treacherous orc warlock hiding deep within Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. As a high-ranking leader among the Searing Blade cultists, he practices demonic arts directly under the Warchief's nose and plots against the Horde. While Thrall works tirelessly to lead the orcs along a path of honor and shamanism, Jergosh rejected these ideals in favor of raw demonic power. Concealing himself within the subterranean labyrinth of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, he gathered followers into the Searing Blade, an insidious sect aligned with the remnants of the Shadow Council. Operating in the shadows directly below the Horde capital, Jergosh works to undo everything the new Horde stands for.

Jern Hornhelm. Jern Hornhelm is a dwarven miner affiliated with the Explorers' League, stationed in the town of Thelsamar. He coordinates vital logistics and communication between the settlement, Ironforge, and the archaeological dig site deeper in Loch Modan. Adventurers frequently assist him with shuttling mining supplies and progress reports across the region. Stationed within the rustic town of Thelsamar, Jern Hornhelm plays a key logistical role for dwarven operations throughout Loch Modan. While dwarven scholars and field teams venture out into the wilderness to unearth their ancestral past, maintaining consistent supply chains remains essential. Jern ensures that vital resources, tools, and communications reach the active dig sites safely.

Jitters. Jitters is a terrified, half-starved human hiding among the ruins of Raven Hill in Duskwood. He clings to scraps of food and struggles to speak about the horrors he has witnessed. Found shivering amid the dilapidated houses of Raven Hill, Jitters lives in constant terror of the predators stalking Duskwood's western trails. He relies on passing adventurers for simple sustenance, desperate for food while keeping a frantic eye on the encroaching shadows. His skittish mannerisms and uncanny reflex for leaping clear of sudden danger earned him his moniker long ago, but his frantic paranoia is born from firsthand encounters with horrific horrors.

Jocaste. Jocaste is a night elf hunter trainer residing within the verdant Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. Working alongside the Cenarion Circle, she mentors young night elf marksmen and beastmasters who arrive from the wilds of Teldrassil. Stationed among the tranquil groves of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus, Jocaste serves as an instructor for night elf hunters. When fledgling trackers finish their initial training in Shadowglen and venture into the capital city, Jocaste guides their transition into seasoned survivalists. She teaches the arts of marksmanship, wilderness survival, and the sacred bond between a hunter and the wild beasts of Kalimdor.

John J. Keeshan. Corporal John J. Keeshan is a human soldier of Stormwind's army who fought the Blackrock orcs in the Redridge Mountains. After being captured during the fighting around Stonewatch, he was dragged deep into Render's Rock as a prisoner of war. John J. Keeshan is a corporal in the service of Stormwind, posted to the Redridge Mountains as the Blackrock orcs pressed against Lakeshire and its defenders. When the fighting flared up around Stonewatch Keep, Keeshan was in the thick of it alongside the other soldiers holding the line for the kingdom.

Jonathan Carevin. Jonathan Carevin is a resolute human hunter residing in Darkshire, dedicated to eradicating the darkness plaguing Duskwood. Unlike the defensive Night Watch, he and his family actively hunt down the undead, worgen, and any heretical threats lurking under the darkened canopies. While Darkshire depends upon the Night Watch to patrol the roads and safeguard the township, Jonathan Carevin believes a mere defensive perimeter is insufficient. Alongside his family and allies like Calor, Jonathan takes the offensive. He actively targets the unholy fiends wandering Duskwood, pursuing a personal crusade to purge all demons, undead, and heretics from the region under the grace of the Light.

Jorah Annison. Jorah Annison is a Forsaken cartographer stationed in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Though his profession revolves around maps and geography, his expertise proves invaluable to traveling spellcasters in search of obscure, scattered knowledge across Azeroth. Dwelling amidst the alchemical vapors and arcane echoes of the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Jorah Annison plies the trade of cartography. Yet the maps bore him: Jorah would trade every one in the shop for a single good book, and he knows more of ancient texts than almost anyone, a scholar's taste he shares with the warlocks who seek him out.

Jordan Stilwell. Jordan Stilwell is a skilled human weaponsmith stationed outside the snowy Gates of Ironforge in Dun Morogh. Though originally meant to become a paladin of the Holy Light, he followed his father's craft to become an artisan whose work serves paladins across the Alliance. He is best known for forging Verigan's Fist in honor of his old friend, Bosch Verigan. Though Jordan Stilwell was expected to take holy vows and become a paladin within the Church of the Holy Light, he ultimately chose the way of the forge. He followed in his father's footsteps, taking up his father's enchanted smithing hammer. Jordan refined his craft under the tutelage of the dwarven blacksmith Bailor Stonehand. Despite setting aside the mantle of an anointed holy warrior, Jordan remains deeply faithful to the Light, dedicating his extraordinary craftsmanship to outfitting champions who fight in its name.

Jorgen. Jorgen is a discreet human informant residing in Stormwind City, tucked away by the water just inside the Valley of Heroes. Despite his modest and out-of-the-way perch, he is entangled in sensitive matters involving prominent figures in the capital, including Elling Trias and Bishop DeLavey. Positioned down near the water immediately to the right of Stormwind's monumental entryway, Jorgen maintains a low profile away from the bustling thoroughfares of the city. While the towering statues of heroes overlook the bridge above, Jorgen monitors comings and goings from the shadows below, serving as a quiet contact for those who need information kept off the record.

Josef Gregorian. Josef Gregorian is a Forsaken tailoring trainer found working in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. He guides ambitious Horde tailors seeking to weave enchanted fabrics, providing expertise and directing them toward specialized garments. Amid the dim alchemical lanterns and damp vaults of the Magic Quarter, Josef Gregorian maintains the fine craft of tailoring for the Forsaken and their Horde allies. While life in the subterranean kingdom has turned cold, cloth-working remains vital for warlocks, mages, and priests who channel raw energies through woven fibers. Gregorian serves as a dependable instructor in the capital, ready to teach foundational patterns and to stitch the first robes of young mages who bring him the right materials.

Kaal Soulreaper. Kaal Soulreaper is an orc warlock trainer stationed deep within the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Despite dwelling among the Forsaken, he maintains close ties to fellow practitioners of the dark arts across the Horde, frequently guiding apprentices to mentors in distant lands. While Thrall's Horde strictly regulates and monitors fel magic within Orgrimmar, practitioners like Kaal Soulreaper find ample harbor in the subterranean sanctums of Lordaeron. Residing within the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Kaal shares his mastery over demonic entities and curses with Horde warlocks willing to learn. Beyond basic instruction, he acts as an essential contact for practitioners seeking greater power, directing ambitious students across the sea to mentors like Menara Voidrender in the Barrens.

Kadrak. Kadrak is a seasoned orc commander stationed at the Mor'shan Rampart on the border between the Barrens and Ashenvale. Tasked with safeguarding the northern frontier, he coordinates the flow of dispatches and reinforcements into the contested forest. For Horde adventurers pushing past the arid plains, Kadrak serves as the gateway to the ongoing struggle against the night elves. Standing atop the fortified timber barricades of the Mor'shan Rampart, Kadrak watches over the primary route connecting the Barrens to Ashenvale. The border is a precarious frontier: to the south lie the sun-scorched plains claimed by the Horde, while to the north loom the ancient woods guarded fiercely by the night elves. Kadrak ensures that the defensive perimeter remains unbroken against encroaching Sentinels and hostile woodland creatures.

Kaela Shadowspear. Kaela Shadowspear is a night elf sentinel stationed southwest of Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. From her small outpost, she coordinates with fellow sentinels to monitor escalating tensions and regional disruptions in the wilderness. She relies on brave travelers to scout dangerous territory and learn what has corrupted the land's ancient defenders. Positioned just southwest of the industrial devastation of Windshear Crag, Kaela Shadowspear keeps a watchful vigil over the surrounding passes. The Stonetalon Mountains are fraught with danger as the Horde encroaches and goblin operations exploit the land's natural bounty. Operating alongside the gnome Gaxim Rustfizzle, Kaela acts as an essential forward liaison for the night elves, tracking threats that push deeper into ancestral territory.

Kali Remik. Kali Remik is a Darkspear troll hunter who spends her time lending guidance to travelers across the Horde's heartland. Familiar with the ways of tracking and survival in Durotar, she directs young hunters to Thotar in Razor Hill to learn the taming of beasts. Kali Remik is a seasoned jungle troll tracker well-acquainted with the arid wastes of Durotar and the bustling hubs of the Horde. In coastal settlements like Sen'jin Village, she watches over young scouts taking their first steps outside the Valley of Trials. Knowing when a novice outgrows the local training grounds, she steps in to direct promising marksmen toward Thotar in Razor Hill to begin their path as beastmasters, ensuring the Horde's frontier ranks stay sharp and disciplined.

Kaltunk. Kaltunk is an orc overseer stationed at the heart of the Valley of Trials in Durotar. He serves as the very first point of contact for young orcs taking their opening steps into the world. It is his duty to welcome these aspiring champions and direct them to their initial duties in service to the Horde. Standing under the harsh sun of the Valley of Trials, Kaltunk watches over the newly arrived hopefuls seeking to prove themselves worthy of the Horde. While other trainers and elders assign grueling trials and hunting rites, Kaltunk ensures that no recruit wanders aimlessly through the red dust. He delivers straightforward orders, pointing newcomers directly toward Gornek and the path of discipline.

Kam Deepfury. Kam Deepfury is a notorious Dark Iron saboteur incarcerated within the depths of the Stormwind Stockade. Unlike the majority of the prison's inmates, he has no allegiance to the Defias Brotherhood, having been captured for orchestrating a devastating explosion along the Thandol Span far to the north. While the Stockade is overwhelmingly filled with disgruntled Stonemasons and Defias rebels, Kam Deepfury stands apart. A Dark Iron dwarf of cunning and violence, Deepfury was captured and brought to Stormwind after masterminding an operation that crippled vital northern infrastructure. He is locked deep within the prison's cells, isolated from his kin beneath Blackrock Mountain but just as hostile to the Alliance as any rebel rioter sharing the corridors.

Kanati Greycloud. Kanati Greycloud is a tauren hunter stationed at Whitereach Post within Thousand Needles. Alongside his hunting companions, he musters what defense he can while enduring constant hostility from the local Galak centaur. Kanati Greycloud makes his camp at Whitereach Post, high atop the sandstone spires of western Thousand Needles. While the canyon offers abundant game and open vistas, it is hemmed in by the Galak centaur, whose warbands contest every inch of the arid flats below. Together with other tauren hunters, Kanati keeps watch over the canyon floor, striving to preserve the post against the brutal depredations of the surrounding marauders.

Kaplak. Kaplak is an orc rogue trainer stationed in Razor Hill in central Durotar. He instructs young orcs and trolls in the arts of stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft, preparing them for service to the Horde before dispatching them into Orgrimmar. Tucked away in the settlement of Razor Hill, Kaplak serves as a foundational instructor for fledgling Horde rogues emerging from the Valley of Trials. Where traditional orc culture glorifies open combat and roaring charges, Kaplak teaches the colder, quieter disciplines necessary for survival: stalking unseen, picking locks, and striking lethal blows from behind. Once his students outgrow his tutelage in the dusty red ravines of Durotar, he directs them north to the capital of Orgrimmar to deepen their craft among senior guild operatives.

Karang Amakkar. Karang Amakkar is an orc scout stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the rocky coast of Ashenvale. Operating on the fringe of Horde territory, he focuses on curbing the violent furbolg tribes that threaten the outpost's supply lines and borders. Adventurers travelling through the outpost rely on his local intelligence to navigate the perilous tensions of the forest. Perched at Zoram'gar Outpost on the Zoram Strand, Karang Amakkar serves the Horde at one of its most vulnerable border outposts. The encampment faces constant pressure from the sea, the night elves, and wild beasts inland. Karang keeps a close eye on the hostile native populations that surround the road eastward, ensuring that Horde couriers and scouting parties do not get ambushed by territorial indigenous tribes.

Kargal Battlescar. Kargal Battlescar is a veteran orc warrior stationed at the Far Watch Post along the eastern border of the Barrens. Tasked with guarding the crossing from Durotar, he evaluates incoming recruits and directs capable fighters deeper into the territory to bolster Horde defenses. Standing watch at the Far Watch Post, Kargal Battlescar oversees the strategic threshold separating the harsh red plains of Durotar from the vast savanna of the Barrens. As travelers and fresh adventurers cross the bridge over the Southfury River, Kargal ensures they understand that the peaceful days of training in the Valley of Trials are over. The Barrens is a contested and dangerous expanse, plagued by aggressive wildlife, centaur raiding parties, and quilboar tribes. Kargal inspects those who pass, mustering willing recruits into the service of the Horde and sending them onward to the Crossroads to aid local commanders in securing the frontier.

Karos Razok. Karos Razok is the Forsaken bat handler stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. He oversees the roost of undead fliers that connect this contested frontier outpost directly to the Undercity and other Horde strongholds. Perched on the wooden platform above the crypts of the Sepulcher, Karos Razok tends to the skeletal bats vital for Forsaken communications. With Silverpine Forest infested by Moonrage worgen, rogue Dalaran magi, and the human remnants of Ambermill, overland travel along the northern road is treacherous. Razok ensures that messengers, fresh recruits, and vital supplies can cross above the haunted canopy, keeping the front line linked straight back to the capital in Tirisfal Glades.

Katie Hunter. Katie Hunter is a horse breeder stationed at the stables in the Eastvale Logging Camp within eastern Elwynn Forest. She provides trained riding horses and steeds to citizens of Stormwind and trusted champions of the Alliance. Alongside Randal Hunter, she ensures travelers and soldiers have reliable mounts to navigate the kingdom's roads. Tucked away in the quiet, wooded clearings of the Eastvale Logging Camp, Katie Hunter manages the kingdom's primary horse stock for aspiring riders in Elwynn Forest. While the lumberjacks harvest timber for Stormwind's reconstruction, Katie tends to the stables, raising a variety of dependable breeds including pintos, mares, and swift steeds. Her stock represents the classic equestrian tradition of the kingdom, offering faithful companions capable of braving dangerous roads across southern Azeroth.

Kaymard Copperpinch. Kaymard Copperpinch is a goblin merchant representing Smokywood Pastures in Orgrimmar during the Feast of Winter Veil. Stationed in the Valley of Strength, he hawks festive goods and directs travelers toward holiday cheer and missing holiday supplies. His brisk trade brings seasonal merriment—and Goblin commercial enterprise—to the Horde capital. When the Feast of Winter Veil arrives, Smokywood Pastures sets up shop right in the bustling Valley of Strength in Orgrimmar, fronted by the enterprising Kaymard Copperpinch. While Great-father Winter receives visitors nearby, Kaymard makes sure the season remains profitable. Selling higher-end treats, festive wrapping paper, and holiday necessities, he embodies the goblin view that no grand cultural festival is complete without a lively exchange of coin.

Keeper Albagorm. Keeper Albagorm is a keeper of the grove stationed at the idyllic sanctuary of Stonetalon Peak. Deeply concerned by the devastation corrupting the southern reaches of the mountains, he enlists travelers to help heal the scorched wilderness of the Charred Vale. Perched within the peaceful boughs of Stonetalon Peak, Keeper Albagorm stands vigil over one of Kalimdor's sacred elven refuges. Like many sons of Cenarius, he feels the pain of the natural world acutely. His attention is drawn southward toward the smoldering ruins of the Charred Vale, set afire by a greedy mechanized army of industrialists and now held by Bloodfury harpies who block any regrowth. From his sanctuary, Albagorm works tirelessly to halt the spread of the corruption and restore balance to the wounded forest.

Keeper Bel'dugur. Keeper Bel'dugur is a scholarly Forsaken residing deep within the Apothecarium of the Undercity. While ostensibly serving the interests of his people by commissioning expeditions to recover dark tomes and magical artifacts, subtle clues reveal far more sinister allegiances. Situated among the vats and researchers of the Apothecarium, Keeper Bel'dugur tasks adventurers with retrieving dangerous arcane and occult relics from across Azeroth. Among his most prominent interests is the Book of Ur, a legendary treatise on extra-dimensional beings locked away inside Shadowfang Keep. While many in the Undercity seek magical knowledge to cure or weaponize the condition of the undead, Bel'dugur's curated acquisitions appear tailored toward unearthing ancient, forbidden powers.

Keeper Bel'varil. Keeper Bel'varil is a Forsaken caretaker and researcher stationed at Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Working closely alongside Wordeen Voidglare, he directs Horde adventurers to gather magical relics and binding materials from the surrounding lands to further their occult studies. Amid the besieged village of Tarren Mill, Keeper Bel'varil quietly supports the Forsaken's magical and alchemical research. While royal apothecaries and soldiers occupy themselves with the Alliance garrison down the road at Southshore, Bel'varil focuses on practical sorcery, dispatching travelers to recover stone tokens and binding bracers from nearby elemental and enchanted threats.

Keldran. Keldran is an orc operative stationed just north of the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar. Dedicated to paving the way for eventual diplomacy with the Alliance, he coordinates covert strikes against demonic remnants to prove the modern Horde has truly forsaken the Burning Legion. While Thrall governs from the Valley of Wisdom, Keldran works from the city's red rock terraces to solve a lingering diplomatic disaster. The Alliance still views all orcs as bloodthirsty puppets of demonic masters, a reputation cemented during the first wars. Convinced that even Thrall tires of endless conflict, Keldran believes true peace talks can never occur while demon-worshiping cults endure in Kalimdor. Without formal sanction from the Warchief, he takes the initiative upon himself, directing trusted agents toward distant threats to dismantle the demonic stain once and for all.

Kelm Hargunth. Kelm Hargunth is the primary supply officer and quartermaster for the Warsong Outriders, stationed at Mor'shan Base Camp on the northern border of the Barrens. He equips Horde champions fighting against the night elves in the contested forests of Warsong Gulch. Through his care packages and provisions, he ensures that the frontline war effort remains fully supplied. Perched on the earthen ramparts overlooking Ashenvale, Kelm Hargunth oversees logistical operations for the Warsong Outriders at Mor'shan Base Camp. While scouts and raiders skirmish beyond the stockade, Hargunth manages the flow of weapons, armor, and rations required to sustain a protracted border war. To him, victory against the Silverwing Sentinels depends as much on steady provisions as it does on raw battle fury.

Kerlonian Evershade. Kerlonian Evershade is a night elf Druid of the Claw resting at the Grove of the Ancients in Darkshore. Having recently awakened from the long slumber within the Emerald Dream, he requires aid navigating the corrupted wilds to reach the safety of Maestra's Post. Kerlonian Evershade belongs to the Druids of the Claw, followers of the bear totem who spent centuries sleeping in barrows and communion with the Emerald Dream. The Druids of the Claw were called from their slumber during the Third War. Found resting beneath the ancient trees of the Grove of the Ancients, Kerlonian is still shaking off the supernatural grogginess of his prolonged rest. His immediate concern is traveling safely through the troubled forests of Darkshore toward Maestra's Post on the border of Ashenvale.

Kernobee. Kernobee is a goblin engineer trapped deep within the ruined halls of Gnomeregan. After stumbling upon dangerous secrets involving Dark Iron dwarf sabotage, he was captured, beaten unconscious, and left to die among the troggs in the dormitory quarters. While conducting business or scavenging within the fallen gnome capital, Kernobee uncovered a grave secret: the Dark Iron dwarves were directly involved in the construction and operation of the massive super rig burrowing beneath the city. Realizing the immense value—and lethality—of this intelligence, he attempted to flee immediately to Ratchet to deliver word to his associate, Tinkerwiz. Unfortunately, the Dark Irons caught him before he could make his escape.

Keryn Sylvius. Keryn Sylvius is a human rogue trainer stationed on the second floor of Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn. Tucked away in the inn's reading room, she teaches fledgling scoundrels the basics of stealth and bladecraft while acting as a quiet conduit to Stormwind's intelligence service. While the ground floor of the Lion's Pride Inn bustles with boisterous travelers and weary town guards, Keryn Sylvius keeps to the quiet reading room upstairs. Outwardly unassuming, she observes the constant flow of road gossip and serves as the local mentor for rogues cutting their teeth in Elwynn Forest. When promising operatives outgrow local petty thievery and roadside skulduggery, Sylvius discretely sends them onward to Stormwind City to make contact with SI:7.

Khelden Bremen. Khelden Bremen is a human mage and instructor stationed on the upper floor of Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest. He oversees the earliest instruction of novice spellcasters who take up the arcane arts in service to Stormwind. Situated within the tranquil stone walls of Northshire Abbey, Khelden Bremen acts as the primary instructor for fledgling human mages. While the clergy and defenders handle martial and spiritual pursuits below, Bremen maintains a quiet study upstairs. Here, he introduces novices to the discipline, focus, and fundamental techniques required to weave raw magical energy safely before they venture out into Elwynn Forest and beyond to Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

Kil'hala. Kil'hala is a jungle troll tailoring trainer stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Skilled in working with both everyday cloth and exotic woven materials, he instructs Horde crafters looking to refine their needlework. Beyond common thread, he weaves nether-lace robes for young Horde mages who bring him locks of hair from the laughing sisters of Ashenvale. Positioned at the bustling hub of the Crossroads, Kil'hala offers his tailoring expertise to passing travelers and Horde recruits. While much of his craft involves common spun bolts and garments fit for dry plains life, his knowledge extends into rare magical textiles. As a favor to the mage Deino, he fashions nether-lace robes for young mages who bring him hair taken from the laughing sisters, dryads of Ashenvale's forests.

Kin'weelay. Kin'weelay is a renowned Darkspear witch doctor stationed at Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Dispatched directly from Orgrimmar, he offers mystical aid and counsel to the Horde vanguard in the jungle. His spiritual expertise is vital in unravelling dark mojo and aiding the rescue of young Yenniku. Recognized among the Darkspear as one of their most powerful practitioners of traditional witchcraft, Kin'weelay commands deep knowledge of spirits, hexes, and soul magic. When matters involving ancestral spirits or hostile troll enchantments arise, Horde scouts in Stranglethorn Vale look to him to pierce the magical veil.

Kindal Moonweaver. Kindal Moonweaver is a night elf secluded within a concealed nook in the craggy mountains of Feralas, just north of the Grimtotem Compound. Deeply troubled by the mistreatment of wildlife in the wilderness, she watches the aggressive tauren tribe below while seeking help to free captured beasts. She is kin to Jer'kai Moonweaver, sharing a mission to defend the forest's innocent creatures. Perched upon a narrow, winding mountain path partially hidden behind timber east of Dire Maul, Kindal Moonweaver maintains a secret vigil over the valley below. While much of Feralas is contested between the Horde, the night elves of Feathermoon, and the ancient ruins of Eldre'Thalas, Kindal focuses on a more localized and immediate cruelty. Down in the hollow, the Grimtotem tribe operates a fortified compound, capturing and penning up local fauna for reasons far from benign. From her concealed overlook, Kindal watches for anyone willing to brave the enemy camp and undo the suffering inside.

Kirge Sternhorn. Kirge Sternhorn is a tauren stationed in the rugged frontier of the Barrens. Serving as a steady presence for travelers journeying across central Kalimdor, he directs fledgling Horde adventurers northward toward the vital outpost of the Crossroads. The vast, sun-baked plains of the Barrens are daunting for newly arrived wanderers, and Kirge Sternhorn stands as a helpful guide along their path. Stationed south of the central trails, he watches over travelers moving between the southern camps and the heart of Kalimdor. Understanding the dangers of marauding quilboar and fierce predators roaming the savanna, Kirge ensures that young adventurers find their footing and seek out the greater Horde presence gathering to the north.

Klannoc Macleod. Klannoc Macleod is a rugged human warrior residing on Fray Island, situated off the eastern shores of the Barrens. Renowned as an arbiter of martial prowess, he tests aspiring brawlers from both the Alliance and the Horde who seek to master combat stances. Those who earn his respect are directed further inland toward greater trials of strength. Isolated on Fray Island off the coast of the Merchant Coast in the Barrens, Klannoc Macleod oversees a brutal proving ground for seasoned fighters. Despite being human, Klannoc stands apart from the typical political squabbles of the Alliance and Horde, judging contenders solely by their grit, blade work, and resolve under fire.

Kor'ghan. Kor'ghan is a Darkspear jungle troll who can be found lingering in the murky caverns of the Cleft of Shadow in Orgrimmar. Positioned right outside Rekkul's Poisons, he seeks assistance in concocting remedies against venomous wilderness predators. Standing before Rekkul's Poisons in the cavernous depths of the Cleft of Shadow, Kor'ghan keeps close watch over remedies and toxins alike. From the capital he dispatches adventurers across the red canyons to gather venomous components from Durotar's scorpids in order to prepare vital antidotes.

Korran. Korran is a Darkspear troll researcher stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Serving Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar, he monitors odd happenings across the scrublands and studies the emerging menace of the insectoid silithid. While most at the Crossroads concern themselves with aggressive quilboar and local centaur clans, Korran keeps a watchful eye on subtler, more insidious threats. Stationed on orders from Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar, the troll scout observes the changing land and coordinates the collection of intelligence for the Horde's leadership.

Kravel Koalbeard. Kravel Koalbeard is a scheming dwarven entrepreneur and con artist stationed out at the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats. Rather than cheering purely for the love of the sport, he views the fierce gnome and goblin racing rivalry as a golden opportunity to fill his pockets. From scavenging stray machine parts to fixing race results through blackmail and booze, Kravel is always hunting for his next profitable scheme. While most spectators and crew members at the Mirage Raceway are consumed by mechanical rivalries and the roar of rocket engines, Kravel Koalbeard has his eyes squarely on everyone's coin purses. He is an opportunist who operates in the dusty cracks of the raceway encampment, quick to offer contracts and favors that rarely have clean motives. Kravel sees the high-stakes friction between gnome and goblin engineers not as an inspiring competition, but as a fertile ground for extortion, sabotage, and theft.

Kreldig Ungor. Kreldig Ungor is an enterprising dwarven operative representing Reclaimers Inc., stationed high among the crags of Nijel's Point in Desolace. Tasked with managing field operations in the barren wasteland, he hires Alliance adventurers to recover lost cargo and secure valuable local reagents. His salvage and recovery contracts make him a central contact for travelers navigating the hostile region. Nijel's Point offers the Alliance a rare sanctuary amid the blighted canyons of Desolace, making it an ideal staging ground for commercial opportunists like Kreldig Ungor. Representing Reclaimers Inc., Kreldig has ventured far from the safety of Khaz Modan into a desolate wilderness contested by centaur clans, demons, and the Horde. Where others see ruin and ash, Kreldig sees untapped profit and lost assets ripe for recovery.

Krolg. Krolg is an uncorrupted furbolg living in an isolated hut south of Mystral Lake in Ashenvale. Formerly a member of the Foulweald tribe, he was cast out by his kin, who fell to demonic madness, and will only speak with those who appear to him in furbolg form. While most of the Foulweald furbolgs in Ashenvale have succumbed to the demonic taint left behind by the Burning Legion, Krolg remains lucid and untouched by madness. Residing in a secluded shelter south of Mystral Lake, he keeps a cautious vigil over the forest. Having witnessed the tragic descent of his brethren into senseless violence, he refuses to interact with outsiders at face value, speaking only with beings that appear as kin.

Krom Stoutarm. Krom Stoutarm is a dwarven scholar and warlock found deep within the Library of the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. Unlike most of his kin who delve solely into ancient stone and titan relics, Krom studies darker, arcane texts and demonic rituals. He acts as an indispensable contact for Alliance warlocks seeking esoteric knowledge across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. The Hall of Explorers is typically known for dwarven archaeologists obsessed with picks, shovels, and titan artifacts. Krom Stoutarm cuts an unusual figure among them. Lurking in the Library surrounded by massive tomes, he pursues occult lore and the binding rites of demonic summoners. His presence in Ironforge demonstrates that while warlock arts are widely distrusted, scholar-practitioners who study the forbidden arts still operate within the mountain city's halls.

Krusk. Krusk is an orc scout stationed at Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Dispatched directly under Warchief Thrall's orders to investigate the Syndicate and recover relics from the ruins of Durnholde Keep, he now coordinates reconnaissance and rescue efforts after his initial infiltration was ambushed. When Warchief Thrall turned his attention back to the ruins of Durnholde Keep, he dispatched Krusk and a small strike team to scout Syndicate activity and retrieve relics tied to the fortress's grim past. However, the human outlaws proved more entrenched and coordinated than anticipated. An ambush inside Durnholde's crumbling walls overwhelmed the orcish scout squad. Krusk managed to fight his way out, but his comrades were taken captive: Drull and Tog'thar were locked away within the ruins, while the expedition's leader, Gol'dir, was moved to another Syndicate hold. Regrouping at Tarren Mill, Krusk now directs Horde adventurers to breach Durnholde, recover the lost items, and liberate his trapped comrades.

Kuray'bin. Kuray'bin is a Darkspear jungle troll scout stationed at a guard post outside Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. He watches the surrounding forest trails for night elf scouts sneaking close to the Horde encampment. Positioned just outside Splintertree Post, Kuray'bin keeps watch against Alliance infiltration in the deep woods of Ashenvale. The Silverwing Sentinels constantly patrol the surrounding canopy, sending agile outrunners across the border to gather intelligence on Horde lumber operations and defenses. Knowing that unmonitored scouts quickly become ambushing forces, Kuray'bin directs capable Horde fighters to hunt down the outrunners before they can report back to Silverwing Outpost.

Kzan Thornslash. Kzan Thornslash is an orc weapon merchant stationed in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. He provides essential starter weaponry and supplies to fresh recruits beginning their training under the Horde. Situated within the dusty red canyon of the Valley of Trials, Kzan Thornslash serves as the primary weapon vendor for young orcs and Darkspear trolls taking their first steps as warriors of the Horde. Offering an assortment of basic armaments—ranging from crude hand axes and shortswords to clubs and staves—Kzan ensures that newly awakened aspirants are armed adequately to face the local wildlife and regional hazards.

Lady Anacondra. Lady Anacondra is one of the Fanglords leading the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once one of the night elf druids who followed Naralex in his ambitious effort to heal the Barrens, she was lost when her master's Emerald Dream communion turned into a nightmare. Her mind broke, twisting her devotion into a drive to remake the land to match that twisted dream. Before adopting her serpentine title, Lady Anacondra was one of Naralex's druids. When the elder druid Naralex conceived of tapping into the subterranean springs of the Barrens through the Emerald Dream, she followed him into the caverns. Her loyalty, however, proved her undoing. As Naralex's mind was seized by dark visions, the nightmare seeped out from the dreaming realm and contaminated his disciples, shattering her sanity and reshaping her reverie into a cold, reptilian obsession.

Lady Sarevess. Lady Sarevess is a twisted naga sorceress dwelling within the flooded ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, where she dabbles in dark sorceries. Within the Pool of Ask'ar, Lady Sarevess conducts her rituals in a flooded grotto of the ruined temple. A very twisted spellcaster, she dabbles in dark magic while the Twilight's Hammer cultists who also haunt the sunken temple pursue their own worship deeper in the cavern.

Laird. Laird is a night elf fish vendor found inside the seaside inn of Auberdine. Working along Darkshore's mist-shrouded coast, he provides trade goods and culinary recipes to travelers and fishermen braving the rugged shoreline. Situated inside the bustling inn of Auberdine, Laird sells fresh fish and supplies to sailors, locals, and journeying adventurers. Darkshore's waters are notoriously turbulent and rife with danger compared to the sheltered shores of Teldrassil, but Laird knows well that risk brings reward. For daring anglers willing to cast their lines along the misty beaches, the local catch yields a handsome profit.

Lakota Windsong. Lakota Windsong is a young tauren held captive atop the bluffs of Darkcloud Pinnacle in Thousand Needles. After rejecting an unwanted proposal from Arnak Grimtotem, she was abducted by force and awaits rescue from the Grimtotem tribe's clutches. Not long after the Third War, Lakota Windsong was pursued by Arnak Grimtotem. Unwilling to join his clan or accept his courtship, she turned down his proposal. Arnak refused to take no for an answer; he returned under cover of night, slaughtered Lakota's brother when he tried to intervene, and carried her off into the jagged heights of Thousand Needles. Confined high above the canyon floor at Darkcloud Pinnacle, she remains trapped under heavy guard while Arnak still insists on making her his bride.

Lanka Farshot. Lanka Farshot is a tauren hunter trainer stationed at Camp Narache within the Red Cloud Mesa. He guides novice tauren hunters as they take their first steps in tracking, marksmanship, and surviving the plains of Mulgore. Standing watch over Camp Narache, Lanka Farshot greets new tauren called to the path of the hunter. Fresh recruits arrive carrying an etched note directing them to seek his counsel. Under his steady eye, apprentices learn the fundamentals of ranged combat, tracking prey, and respecting the wild beasts that roam the grassy plains of Mulgore. His teachings ensure that every young hunter serves as a capable scout and provider for the tribe.

Lar Prowltusk. Lar Prowltusk is a Darkspear troll sentinel stationed southwest of Sen'jin Village in Durotar. From his post on the frontier, he keeps watch over encroaching threats to the young troll settlement, directing adventurers to blunt the advances of nearby enemies. Situated southwest of Sen'jin Village along the rugged Durotar coastline, Lar Prowltusk stands as one of the Darkspear tribe's forward sentinels. With the trolls still working to secure a permanent home after fleeing their sunken island chain, Sen'jin Village faces constant harassment from hostile neighbors. Lar coordinates scouts and warriors to monitor coastal movements and curb the aggression of hostile forces—particularly the Kolkar centaur—ensuring the fragile settlement has room to breathe.

Laris Geardawdle. Laris Geardawdle is an eccentric gnomish researcher stationed in the Library of the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. He dedicates his academic life to studying the bizarre nature and origins of oozes across Azeroth. Adventurers willing to collect noxious slime samples find him an eager, if slightly unhinged, patron. Tucked away among the towering bookshelves and ancient relics of the Hall of Explorers, Laris Geardawdle pursues a rather unglamorous niche of natural philosophy: the genesis of oozes. While his dwarven colleagues pore over Titan tablets and ancient stone carvings, Laris is convinced that Azeroth's vile, gelatinous horrors hold fascinating alchemical and biological secrets. He tasks roving explorers with gathering caustic samples from remote corners of the world, eager to test his strange hypotheses on how these mindless puddles of malice come to life.

Lars. Lars is a beleaguered human survivor camping out in the wilderness of Duskwood. Along with his companion Sven Yorgen, he struggles to hold his ground on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank against the terrors that stalk the forest. Perched in a modest camp on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank, Lars ekes out a precarious survival far from the questionable safety of Darkshire. Duskwood is treacherous at the best of times, but the surrounding woods crawl with ferocious beasts, relentless undead, and creeping worgen. Lars stays close by Sven Yorgen, striving simply to stay alive in an increasingly hostile wilderness.

Laurna Morninglight. Laurna Morninglight is a night elf priest trainer residing in the tranquil settlement of Dolanaar within Teldrassil. Devoted to the Sisterhood of Elune, she guides budding acolytes emerging from Shadowglen in the spiritual rites and healing graces of the Moon Goddess. Her teachings prepare young night elf priests for the growing threats encroaching on the boughs of the World Tree. Situated amidst the boughs of Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight serves as one of the primary mentors for young priests who have completed their initial rites in Shadowglen. As new initiates step out into the broader reaches of Teldrassil, she instructs them on expanding their communion with Elune, balancing the light of healing with defensive rites necessary to survive an increasingly hostile wild.

Lelanai. Lelanai is a night elf mount handler residing in the Cenarion Enclave of Darnassus. She provides the fierce saber mounts of the night elves to worthy riders, offering both standard nightsabers and swift war beasts to her kin and trusted allies of Darnassus. Stationed beside riding instructor Jartsam among the towering trees of the Cenarion Enclave, Lelanai attends to some of the finest big cats bred in Kalimdor. Night elves have long formed profound bonds with the fierce predators of northern forests, training nightsabers and frostsabers to carry sentinels and scouts across rugged terrain with predator grace. Lelanai serves as the primary provider of these revered mounts in the capital.

Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle is an officer of the Stormwind army currently stationed at the Southshore inn in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Deeply unhappy with his frontier posting, he spends most of his time drinking while outsourcing his duties to passing travelers. His primary military assignment is dealing with the encroaching murlocs along the coast, a chore he eagerly delegates in hopes of securing a transfer back south. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle did not choose Southshore. Dispatched far from Stormwind City, the lieutenant finds the damp, contested shores of Hillsbrad a miserable step down from the civilized comforts of the capital. Instead of patrolling the fields or coordinating defenses with his commanding officer, Marshal Redpath, Orinelle has practically taken up permanent residence inside Southshore's inn. His days are spent sulking, drinking, and dreaming of an official transfer order that will return him to the south.

Lieutenant Haggerdin. Lieutenant Haggerdin is a dwarven officer stationed upon the Headland in the Alterac Mountains. Standing watch outside the fortified gate to Alterac Valley, he acts as the primary recruitment and liaison officer for the Stormpike Guard. He evaluates aspiring Alliance champions and rewards those who prove their valor against the Frostwolf Clan. Perched in the snowy heights of the Headland above the Hillsbrad Foothills, Lieutenant Haggerdin oversees the muster point for the Alliance's ongoing campaign in Alterac Valley. Dwarven banners flutter beside the massive wooden gate as recruits and veterans assemble under his watchful eye, preparing to plunge into the frigid warzone.

Lieutenant Lisande. Lieutenant Lisande is an emissary of the Argent Dawn stationed upon the high mesas of Thunder Bluff. As a human operating openly in tauren lands, she serves as a liaison against the shared existential threat of the Scourge. While human faces are rare across the windblown heights of Thunder Bluff, the Argent Dawn transcends traditional faction enmities. Lieutenant Lisande serves the holy order by watching for signs of the Lich King's taint even in remote Kalimdor. When undead forces stir on the plains below, she rallies brave Horde champions to ride out and investigate the encroaching menace before it can defile the sacred earth.

Lieutenant Nevell. Lieutenant Nevell is an officer of the Argent Dawn stationed outside the gates of Ironforge in Dun Morogh. Serving as a bulwark against the spreading darkness of the Scourge, he coordinates local defenders and alerts arriving adventurers to undead threats probing the dwarf kingdom's borders. While the Argent Dawn is most renowned for holding the line in the shattered Plaguelands of Lordaeron, its vigilance reaches far into the south. Stationed in the freezing winds outside Ironforge, Lieutenant Nevell represents the order's proactive defense against necromantic incursions. When Scourge activity stirs in the mountain passes of Dun Morogh, Nevell directs recruits and capable adventurers toward the front lines to ensure Ironforge's snowy doorstep remains secure.

Lieutenant Orrin. Lieutenant Orrin is an officer of the Argent Dawn stationed at the gates of Stormwind City. Positioned in the Valley of Heroes, he coordinates local defense against incursions by the Scourge and directs fresh recruits to investigate undead threats outside the capital's walls. While the Argent Dawn is primarily known for holding the front lines in the ruined north, their presence extends south to safeguard vital strongholds like Stormwind City. Lieutenant Orrin stands near the towering statues of the Valley of Heroes, watching the road for signs of corruption. When necromantic magic stirs outside the capital, he is tasked with sounding the alarm and rallying adventurers before foul forces can threaten the populace.

Loganaar. Loganaar is a night elf druidic instructor residing in the haven of Nighthaven in Moonglade. Dedicated to guiding initiates from both the Alliance and the Horde, he instructs young druids as they attune to the wild and prepare for the call of the Emerald Dream. Situated amidst the serene boughs of Nighthaven, Loganaar serves as a primary mentor to newly initiated druids traveling to Moonglade. Regardless of whether an initiate hails from Darnassus or Thunder Bluff, Loganaar provides guidance in balance, shape-shifting, and reverence for nature. He reminds his students that even within cold stone and unfamiliar lands, true tranquility must be found within oneself. He also acts as a welcoming guide for those journeying deeper into the Cenarion Circle's affairs, sending promising students to wanderers like Torwa Pathfinder in Un'Goro Crater or deeper into ancient woodland rites.

Lomac Gearstrip. Lomac Gearstrip is an ambitious gnome inventor based in Tinker Town within Ironforge. Renowned for formulating the devastating NG-5 explosive, he liaises with fellow gnomish researchers operating across Kalimdor. Amid the clanging gears and hissing pipes of Ironforge's Tinker Town, Lomac Gearstrip pursues the finer points of gnomish ordnance. Like many exiled gnomes who fled the tragedy at Gnomeregan, Lomac has integrated his tinkering operations directly into the dwarven capital. His workshop focuses on volatile chemical mixtures and specialized munitions designed to overcome heavily defended enemy strongholds.

Longbraid the Grim. Longbraid the Grim is an Ironforge dwarf commander stationed just outside the fallen fortress of Dun Modr in the northern Wetlands. Mourning the loss of his brother and the overrun of the Thandol Span, he coordinates the surviving dwarf forces against the invading Dark Iron clan. Positioned within sight of the bridge to the Arathi Highlands, Longbraid the Grim rallies what remains of the dwarven garrison after the Dark Iron clan seized Dun Modr. The sudden assault devastated the regional defenders and resulted in the death of Longbraid's own brother during the siege of the Thandol Span. Burdened by grief and hatred, Longbraid refuses to abandon the northern boundary, directing travelers and surviving mountaineers in surgical strikes to curb the Dark Iron advance.

Loramus Thalipedes. Loramus Thalipedes is a reclusive night elf demon hunter secluded on a remote isle off the coast of Azshara. Flanked by loyal felhounds, he dedicates his existence to destroying Razelikh the Defiler, directing seasoned champions through rituals to strike down the dreadlord. Perched on a solitary, storm-tossed island southeast of Hetaera's Clutch, Loramus Thalipedes stands apart from the rest of his kin. He is a demon hunter—an exile who underwent the agonizing ritual of blinding himself to gain spectral sight. Surrounded by three towering felhounds named Raytaf, Shahiar, and Zaman, Loramus watches the unseen currents of demonic corruption across Azeroth while keeping a watchful vigil over the shattered ruins of Azshara.

Lord Arkkoroc. Lord Arkkoroc is an ancient, towering sea giant who dwells within the ruined Temple of Arkkoran along the ragged coast of Azshara. Described by the demon hunter Loramus Thalipedes as a lesser deity, he holds sway over the surrounding waters and commands lesser sea giants who serve as his sons. Reclining amidst the brine-crusted ruins of the Temple of Arkkoran, Lord Arkkoroc is far more than a typical sea giant. To hermits like Loramus Thalipedes, this colossal being is considered a lesser deity whose divine will shapes the surrounding waters. His sons patrol the crags and shallows around the sanctuary, enforcing his quiet dominion over Azshara's tempestuous shores.

Lord Baurles K. Wishock. Lord Baurles K. Wishock is a nobleman residing in Stormwind Keep's Petitioner's Chamber. Known among barkeeps for his unpaid tabs and fondness for strong drink, he stumbled upon darker dealings than mere drunkenness in the city's underbelly. Holding court among the petitioners and dignitaries within Stormwind Keep, Lord Baurles K. Wishock is a member of the influential House of Nobles. Despite his elevated station, Wishock developed a habit of frequenting the dive bars of the Mage Quarter, especially the Slaughtered Lamb, leaving behind substantial unpaid bills. While drinking there, however, he caught wind of the warlock coven practicing dark arts in the cellars beneath the floorboards. Determined to shut the tavern down, Wishock began petitioning fellow nobles for a formal investigation—unaware that uncovering demonic cabals in Stormwind rarely goes unpunished.

Lord Cobrahn. Lord Cobrahn is one of the four leaders of the corrupted Druids of the Fang lurking deep within the Wailing Caverns. Once a night elf druid of Naralex's noble order, which hoped to heal the Barrens, he succumbed to the nightmare infecting the cavern springs. Taking a lethal serpent guise, Cobrahn now commands broods of deviate serpents and defends the twisted labyrinth. Before his fall, Cobrahn was one of the noble druids who followed Naralex. When Naralex ventured into the Wailing Caverns beneath the Barrens hoping to tap their underground springs and restore lush life to the arid wastes, Cobrahn accompanied him. However, when Naralex's Emerald Dream communion decayed into a twisting nightmare, Cobrahn's mind shattered alongside his brothers.

Lord Ello Ebonlocke. Lord Ello Ebonlocke is the mayor of Darkshire and the leader of its governing council, stationed inside the Darkshire Town Hall. Surrounded by darkness and creeping horrors, he struggles daily to maintain order and protect his besieged citizens despite receiving little aid from Stormwind. Seated in the gloom of the Darkshire Town Hall, Lord Ello Ebonlocke bears the heavy burden of governing a settlement on the brink of ruin. Once part of the prosperous rural haven known as Grand Hamlet, Darkshire is now smothered by perpetual shadow and besieged by ravenous ghouls, skeletal abominations, and feral beasts. Ello presides over the Council of Darkshire, striving against impossible odds to keep the remnants of civilization functioning while Stormwind turns a blind eye to their plight.

Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker is a veteran paladin commander of the Knights of the Silver Hand stationed within Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. One of the Alliance's foremost paladins, he trains budding champions of the Light and oversees the sacred, arduous trials required for senior paladins to claim their holy chargers. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker stands among the foremost defenders of the Alliance, anchoring the order's presence in Stormwind City. A veteran of the Silver Hand, Grayson does not merely instruct recruits in martial skill; he tests their spiritual conviction. When promising knights demonstrate their readiness, Grayson dispatches them north toward the contested front lines of the Western Plaguelands to aid Commander Ashlam Valorfist at Chillwind Camp.

Lord Jorach Ravenholdt. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt is the master of Ravenholdt, an elite guild of rogues and assassins operating out of a secluded estate in the Alterac Mountains. He directs the league's clandestine operations, training promising operatives while waging a bitter war against the regional bandits of the Syndicate. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt presides over the Assassin's League from his hidden manor nestled in the crags between Alterac and Hillsbrad. A nobleman of mysterious heritage, he opens his halls to outlaws, cutpurses, and assassins regardless of allegiance, provided they exhibit exceptional skill and respect his authority. Under his command, the league acts as both a fraternity for master thieves and an independent syndicate for wetwork and espionage. Ravenholdt harbors a fierce hatred for the Syndicate—the band of disgraced Alterac nobles turned outlaws—and routinely directs his subordinates and visiting freelancers to sabotage their camps and plunder their assets.

Lord Maxwell Tyrosus. Lord Maxwell Tyrosus is the supreme commander of the Argent Dawn, stationed at their forward redoubt of Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. A veteran paladin of the Silver Hand from the Third War, he guides the coalition's crusade against the Scourge and orchestrates strikes into blighted strongholds like Stratholme. Maxwell Tyrosus rode alongside Uther the Lightbringer during the catastrophic Third War, guarding the exits of Andorhal when the Scourge tore through the kingdom. After the fall of Lordaeron, he cast his lot with the Argent Dawn, an order that welcomes anyone willing to stand against the Scourge, in stark contrast to the human-only zealotry of the Scarlet Crusade.

Lord Pythas. Lord Pythas, once a night elf warrior, is one of the four corrupted leaders of the Druids of the Fang in the Wailing Caverns. Originally one of the personal guards of the druid Naralex, he fell victim to the nightmare tainting the oasis underground. Now he wields both martial might and twisted serpent magic against any who try to reach his slumbering master. Before his corruption, Pythas was a seasoned night elf warrior who served among the druid Naralex's personal guard when the expedition ventured into the dry wastes of the Barrens. Alongside his martial training, he took up the druidic arts in service of Naralex's dream of restoring lush life to the arid realm. However, physical discipline and martial valor offered no shelter against the insidious corruption waiting deep within the subterranean fissures.

Lord Serpentis. Lord Serpentis is a corrupted night elf druid who stands as one of the four leaders of the rogue Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once a druid of great power and prestige in the order of Naralex, he was twisted into madness when Naralex's dream became a nightmare within the subterranean springs. Now, he helps command the serpent-worshipping sect deep in the caverns where the corrupted Naralex lies slumbering. Before darkness overtook the cavern springs, Serpentis was a druid of great power and prestige, one of the noble order led by Naralex that hoped to use the caverns' springs and the Emerald Dream to heal the Barrens. However, when Naralex's vision became a corrupting nightmare, Serpentis was among the druids whose minds fell to the emerging madness.

Lord Shalzaru. Lord Shalzaru is the tyrannical leader of the Hatecrest naga operating out of the Isle of Dread off the coast of Feralas. Ruling his serpentine followers with absolute cruelty, he oversees extensive excavations among the submerged and ruined elven settlements. His recent discovery of a strange, ancient relic has drawn the attention of outside investigators eager to wrest it from his grasp. Lord Shalzaru commands the Hatecrest naga, directing their presence along the southern coast of Feralas. From his subterranean lair within a cavern on the Isle of Dread, he enforces his rule through cruelty and ruthless authority. Under his command, the Hatecrest scour the ancient ruins of ancient Kalimdor, searching for forgotten treasures and powerful relics left behind from the Sundering.

Lorekeeper Raintotem. Lorekeeper Raintotem is a tauren elder stationed in northern Mulgore just south of Red Rocks. He tends to the sacred burial grounds and asks adventurers to drive off the Bristleback quilboar disturbing them. Positioned near the sacred bluffs of Red Rocks in Mulgore, Lorekeeper Raintotem tends to the spiritual obligations of his people. He asks adventurers to drive Bristleback Interlopers from the burial ground, restoring peace to the ancestors' resting place.

Lorgus Jett. Lorgus Jett is a human member of the Twilight's Hammer cult operating within the flooded corridors of Blackfathom Deeps. Wandering the Moonshrine Ruins, he serves as a ruthless commander in the cult's service to the Old Gods. Horde leaders have singled him out as a primary target to disrupt the cult's encroaching presence along the Ashenvale coast. While many members of the Twilight's Hammer working under Blackfathom Deeps hail from orcish or tauren lineages, Lorgus Jett stands out as a human in the deep recesses of ancient night elf ruins. Roaming anywhere between the upper Moonshrine Ruins and the cavernous tunnels beyond the murloc defiler Gelihast, Jett coordinates the cult's dark rituals and violent ambitions.

Loslor Rudge. Loslor Rudge is an enterprising dwarven engineering supplier stationed at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. He provides mechanical parts, tools, and munitions to tinkerers across the snowy mountain ridges, keeping critical connections open with gunsmiths like Hegnar Rumbleshot. Operating out of Steelgrill's Depot just down the road from Kharanos, Loslor Rudge keeps a steady inventory of engineering essentials—ranging from copper modulators and bronze tubing to blasting powder and spanners. Dun Morogh's harsh weather and sprawling tinker operations mean practical parts are constantly in demand, and Loslor prides himself on keeping the local gearheads supplied. However, the wilderness between outposts is treacherous; when a courier taking a shortcut near the Grizzled Den was chased away by wendigos, an essential shipment of ammunition meant for his valued client, gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot, was left behind in the snow.

Lotwil Veriatus. Lotwil Veriatus is an eccentric gnomish scholar conducting dangerous elemental experiments in the dusty wastes of the Badlands. Stationed east of Kargath with his sarcastic apprentice Lucien Tosselwrench and a mechanical attendant named Servo, he is dedicated to blending arcane theory, alchemy, and engineering into a unified discipline. Originally from Kharanos in Dun Morogh, Lotwil envisions a grand University for his Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy, and Engineering Sciences. He believes these three disciplines should not be practiced in isolation, but harmonized. In pursuit of this dream, he chose the harsh Badlands as his laboratory to study native rock elementals and construct binding shackles capable of mastering elemental forces. While an accomplished researcher—having studied elemental machines and defeated dark iron constructs in the past—his single-minded focus often blinds him to the explosive hazards of his fieldwork.

Lucius. Lucius is a dwarf operative found near the docks of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains. Operating as an undercover field contact for Stormwind's SI:7 intelligence service, he assists operatives with specialized reconnaissance and trade skills. While Lucius presents himself casually on the Lakeshire waterfront, he is in fact a clandestine operative tied directly to Stormwind's intelligence apparatus, SI:7. From his post on the docks, he monitors trade, unusual traffic, and regional threats encroaching on Redridge. Operatives dispatched eastward from Stormwind are directed to him to coordinate covert tasks and hone practical fieldwork arts such as lockpicking, ensuring the Crown maintains hidden reach far beyond Elwynn Forest.

Lyria Du Lac. Lyria Du Lac is a human warrior trainer stationed in Goldshire within Elwynn Forest. Tucked away just behind the village smithy, she drills novice combatants and guides young warriors as they begin mastering their stances and arms. While Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn bustles with travellers and its blacksmith hammers away at local trade goods, Lyria Du Lac keeps to the yard behind the forge.
