Experienced in martial discipline, she serves the Alliance by instructing fledgeling warriors fresh from Northshire Abbey. She evaluates their readiness and introduces them to specialized combat techniques, ensuring that those who take up shield and blade for Stormwind can hold their own against the encroaching threats of Elwynn Forest.

Ma Stonefield. Ma Stonefield is a human matriarch residing at the Stonefield Farm in western Elwynn Forest. Standing right outside the family homestead alongside Auntie Bernice, she deals with the daily hardships of rural farm life amidst neighboring rivalries and pest troubles. Standing beside her family cottage in southwestern Elwynn Forest, Ma Stonefield watches over the farmstead alongside "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield. Life between the neighboring Maclure homestead and the nearby pumpkin patches is rarely peaceful. Local wild boars continuously threaten the family crops, and none poses a greater nuisance than Princess, an enormous prize sow notorious for trampling fields and devouring hard-earned harvests.

Magus Tirth. Magus Tirth is an eccentric human wizard dwelling out on the salt flats of the Mirage Raceway in Thousand Needles. Known locally for breeding chickens and tormenting his polymorphed apprentice, he is also a scholar of formidable arcane lore who has squandered valuable tomes on racing bets. While most mages of his caliber study in the libraries of Dalaran or Stormwind, Magus Tirth has taken up residence amid the grease and roar of the Shimmering Flats. Surrounded by speeding rocket cars, Tirth peddles chickens to passersby, drinks, gambles, and has long since cursed his unfortunate apprentice, 'Plucky' Johnson, into poultry form. Despite this eccentric demeanor, Tirth possesses genuine arcane mastery, having authored esoteric texts on magical power before losing them to reckless wagers on the speedway.

Madame Eva. Madame Eva is a revered fortune-teller and matriarch living in Darkshire in the shadowed forest of Duskwood. Practicing older, mystic arts of divination and cartomancy, she often serves as the first townsperson to sense unnatural disturbances across the woods. Travelers frequently seek her out to unravel grim mysteries or procure occult charms against the creeping dark. Dwelling quietly amidst the gloom of Darkshire, Madame Eva practices cartomancy and ancient folk rituals that many in Stormwind's cathedral would view with suspicion. In a forsaken region plagued by feral beasts, the undead, and darker horrors, her eerie insights are tolerated and sought after by desperate townspeople and visiting adventurers alike.

Magatha Grimtotem. Magatha Grimtotem is the matriarch of the Grimtotem tribe and the Elder Crone of Thunder Bluff. A formidable shaman and political schemer, she resides on Elder Rise while continually challenging Cairne Bloodhoof's vision for the tauren nation. Magatha rose to absolute authority over the Grimtotem through an arranged union followed by the sudden, fatal climbing accident of her mate. Operating from Elder Rise with her personal retinue and bodyguards, she stands as the undisputed political and spiritual leader of her reclusive tribe. Unlike Cairne Bloodhoof, Magatha preaches tauren dominance, viewing other mortal races as intruders upon Kalimdor who ought to be eradicated or swept aside.

Magga. Magga is an orc resident living in the Valley of Trials within Durotar. Stationed near the Den, she serves as a welcoming face for newly arrived Horde adventurers beginning their journey in the valley. The Valley of Trials is the first taste of the world for young orcs and darkspear trolls. Positioned near the Den, Magga greets new arrivals to the valley. While she keeps a low profile among the valley's busy trainers and recruits, she helps bind the small camp together.

Maggran Earthbinder. Maggran Earthbinder is a grizzled tauren veteran appointed by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof to lead the Horde encampment at Sun Rock Retreat. Hardened by a lifetime of brutal conflict, he oversees the defense of the craggy valleys of Stonetalon against ravenous beasts and aggressive harpy covens. Though wearied by countless battles, he remains a steadfast guardian of the settlement. Maggran Earthbinder was sent into the Stonetalon Mountains by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof himself. A veteran of countless skirmishes and bloody campaigns, Maggran admits that age and violence have hardened his heart, stripping away the natural gentleness typical of his people. Sun Rock Retreat was meant to be both an outpost under his steady command and a place of respite, where warm winds and mountain sunshine might soothe his battle-worn spirit.

Magis Sparkmantle. Magis Sparkmantle is a gnome mage trainer stationed inside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. He offers guidance and training to fledgling spellcasters who venture out from Coldridge Valley into the heart of Dun Morogh. While dwarves gather in the Thunderbrew Distillery for hearty ales, Magis Sparkmantle provides an arcane presence among the casks and kegs of Kharanos. Gnome mages often integrate closely with their dwarven allies across Dun Morogh, and Sparkmantle serves as a key mentor for novice spellcasters ready to expand their theoretical and practical grasp of the arcane arts.

Magistrate Henry Maleb. Magistrate Henry Maleb oversees civic administration in the port town of Southshore, the Alliance's primary coastal bastion in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Tasked with maintaining order amid constant threats, he focuses much of his authority on hunting down the Syndicate conspirators targeting the town's leadership. Operating from the town hall in Southshore, Magistrate Henry Maleb handles civil governance for one of the last true Alliance settlements in Lordaeron. The town sits under constant siege from the Forsaken to the north and West, while ruthless highwaymen prowl the foothills. Maleb stepped into his current station after the mysterious assassination of the prior magistrate, an act he attributes directly to the Syndicate. Determined not to suffer the same fate, he coordinates active investigations to root out hidden assassins, dismantle Syndicate supply networks, and unmask the rogue nobles pulling the strings from the ruins of Alterac.

Magistrate Sevren. Magistrate Sevren is the chief administrative official presiding over the settlement of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Standing inside the town hall, he organizes early Forsaken defense and directs arriving champions to stabilize the territory around the Undercity. Operating from the town hall in Brill, Magistrate Sevren coordinates civil authority and strategic efforts in the lands just north of the Undercity. As new Forsaken step forth into Tirisfal Glades, Sevren assesses local crises and dispatches adventurers to restore order, secure ruined infrastructure, and suppress persistent threats lingering in the surrounding hills.

Magistrate Solomon. Magistrate Solomon is the chief magistrate of Lakeshire, presiding over local affairs from the town hall. Besieged by Blackrock orcs and relentless gnoll clans, he spends his days frantically pleading for military aid from an indifferent and distracted Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon governs Lakeshire during the darkest hour in its recent history. The tranquil lakeside settlement is surrounded by hostility: Redridge and Shadowhide gnolls prowl the surrounding hills, while Blackrock orcs descend from the north in organized warbands. Solomon works alongside Marshal Marris to maintain civil order and muster a defense, but Lakeshire's local guards and militia are stretched to their absolute breaking point.

Magni Bronzebeard. Magni Bronzebeard is the Lord of Ironforge, Thane of the Bronzebeard clan, and ruler of Khaz Modan. A veteran commander of the Second War, he leads his mountainous kingdom through grief and political tension while championing dwarven archaeology across Azeroth. The eldest of three brothers, Magni grew up keenly aware of the weight awaiting him under the mountain. When the Horde invaded during the Second War, he held Ironforge behind its impenetrable gates, emerging to pledge Khaz Modan to the Alliance of Lordaeron once the siege was broken. In the years of peace that followed, Magni welcomed his gnomish allies into the city after the fall of Gnomeregan, granting High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his refugees sanctuary within the mountain. To unite the fractured southern and northern kingdoms, Magni petitioned Mekkatorque to engineer an unprecedented subterranean marvel: the Deeprun Tram, connecting Ironforge directly to Stormwind.

Magus Rimtori. Magus Rimtori is a rogue blood elf sorceress leading an expedition among the ancient ruins of Azshara. Known for her ruthless deception, she manipulated the Horde into securing her passage across Kalimdor before butchering her orcish escort. Magus Rimtori led an expedition of high-borne blood elves across the sea to the ancient shores of Azshara. To ensure her party survived the perils of Kalimdor, she manipulated the orc Belgrom, charming and playing him until he agreed to supply an armed escort. Once the soldiers had delivered her safely to her destination, Rimtori revealed her true colors, turning on her protectors and massacring the entire garrison. Establishing her forces at the Thalassian Base Camp, she ventured out into the coastal wilds accompanied by elite bodyguards to hunt for forgotten magical artifacts.

Mai'ah. Mai'ah is a jungle troll mage trainer stationed within the sun-scorched basin of the Valley of Trials in Durotar. She mentors fledgling spellcasters among the Darkspear trolls who step into the red canyons to hone their command of the arcane. For young trolls beginning the path of wizardry, she offers early guidance and instruction in the foundational arts of magic. While orcs overwhelmingly favor the primal call of the elements or the physical dominance of the warrior, Darkspear trolls possess a rare affinity for arcane study. Standing within the Valley of Trials, Mai'ah serves as an instructor for young troll mages arriving to undertake their rites of adulthood. She receives candidates carrying glyphic inscriptions and begins shaping their chaotic raw power into disciplined incantations, ensuring they learn the control required to survive Durotar's perils.

Major Mattingly. Major Mattingly is a seasoned officer of the Stormwind Army stationed at the grand gates in the Valley of Heroes. Serving under General Marcus Jonathan, he assists in safeguarding the capital's main entrance and advising capable crafters on protecting heroes against draconic threats. Standing watch in the Valley of Heroes, Major Mattingly is one of the high-ranking officers directly responsible for Stormwind City's primary landward defense. A grizzled veteran soldier whose face bears the lines of hard-won experience, he serves under General Marcus Jonathan alongside the city's standing garrison. Beyond his daily duties overseeing gate patrols and incoming travelers, Mattingly possesses specialized tactical knowledge regarding the lethal nature of dragons. He is recognized by seasoned adventurers as a vital contact when learning to craft protective dragonscale gear necessary for braving the realm's deadliest lairs.

Major Samuelson. Major Samuelson is a high-ranking officer in the Stormwind City Guard stationed within the throne room of Stormwind Keep. As an experienced military commander, he oversees vital personnel matters and previously mentored junior officers such as Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Standing within Stormwind Keep before the royal court, Major Samuelson represents the leadership of the Stormwind City Guard. He oversees officer postings and administrative military orders across the realm. Notably, he mentored Lieutenant Farren Orinelle, an officer stationed far north at Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. When junior commanders find themselves overwhelmed or seeking transfer from distant frontier garrisons, their requests and official reports travel directly across the kingdom to Major Samuelson's desk in the capital.

Makaba Flathoof. Makaba Flathoof is a tauren survivor hailing from Camp Aparaje in the Stonetalon Mountains. Having witnessed the devastation of his home and people at the hands of the Grimtotem clan, he seeks brave champions of the Horde to bring vengeance upon the attackers and ensure his family's safety. Makaba Flathoof represents the tragic toll of internal strife among the tauren. His home, Camp Aparaje in the Stonetalon Mountains, fell victim to a ruthless surprise attack by the Grimtotem clan. While many tauren strive for peace and unity under the leadership of Cairne Bloodhoof, the treacherous Grimtotem continually sow discord and violence, leaving survivors like Makaba displaced and grieving.

Malfurion Stormrage. Malfurion Stormrage is the first mortal druid and the revered leader of the night elves alongside High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Renowned for defeating the Burning Legion in both the War of the Ancients and the Third War, he is venerated as the Shan'do, or honored teacher. Currently, he lies trapped in a comatose slumber within the Emerald Dream, leaving the kaldorei without his waking guidance. Ten thousand years ago, before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, Malfurion studied under the demigod Cenarius. While Queen Azshara and her Highborne caste delved dangerously into the arcane energies of the Well of Eternity, Malfurion turned toward the primal forces of nature, becoming Azeroth's first mortal druid. His suspicions regarding the Highborne proved tragically correct when Azshara's reckless sorcery pierced the veil and summoned Sargeras and the Burning Legion into Azeroth, igniting the catastrophic War of the Ancients.

Mangletooth. Mangletooth is an imprisoned Razormane quilboar held captive by the Horde inside Camp Taurajo. Facing execution, he trades strategic information about his rivals and the ancient lore of Agamaggan to adventurers willing to do his bidding. Held in a cage at Camp Taurajo by tauren hunters and orc sentries, Mangletooth is a captured Razormane quilboar awaiting execution. Rather than resigning to death, he attempts to manipulate his captors and visiting Horde adventurers into striking down the enemies of his tribe, hoping his cunning will prove his worth or secure his rescue.

Mankrik. Mankrik is a grief-stricken orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. After a vicious quilboar ambush separated him from his wife, Olgra, he has dedicated his life to avenging her and cutting down every bristled beast he can find. While traveling through the scrublands of the Barrens, Mankrik and his wife Olgra were overrun by swarms of quilboar during a skirmish at a small tauren settlement. Separated in the chaos and frantic fighting, Mankrik watched Olgra disappear under a tide of tusks and thorn-woven weapons. Overwhelmed by fury, he fought recklessly until he was struck down unconscious. He survived only because a passing tauren druid discovered him bleeding out along the Gold Road and bound his injuries.

Marcus Redpath. Marshal Marcus Redpath is the senior military authority defending the Alliance town of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. He organizes patrols and bounty contracts to hold off surrounding ogres, murlocs, and naga. His leadership is essential to maintaining Lordaeron's last southern bastion on the coast. Marcus Redpath is the marshal of Southshore, the Alliance port on the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Southshore endured the fall of Lordaeron's capital and the devastating Scourge invasion, and Redpath now stands at the head of its defense, guarding the port's beleaguered survivors.

Mardant Strongoak. Mardant Strongoak is a night elf druid trainer residing in Aldrassil in the heart of Teldrassil. He guides fledgling druids in communing with the spirits of nature and introduces them to the mysteries of the Emerald Dream. Within the boughs of Aldrassil, young night elves who feel the call of the wild turn to Mardant Strongoak. His primary task is teaching novitiates how to open their senses to nature spirits, interpret their murmurs, and channel rejuvenating magics. For those taking their initial steps as protectors of the wild, he is often the first master to unveil the vast complexities and ancient perils of the Emerald Dream.

Marek Ironheart. Marek Ironheart is a veteran dwarven hunter stationed at the Farstrider Lodge in south-eastern Loch Modan. Dedicated to the traditions of the wild, he tests wandering travelers and marksmen alike before welcoming them into the ranks of the lodge's honored hunters. Perched on the scenic ridge overlooking the lake, the Farstrider Lodge serves as an outpost for the finest marksmen and trackers in the dwarven lands. Marek Ironheart embodies this frontier spirit. Unimpressed by titles or talk, Marek requires anyone seeking the lodge's respect to demonstrate their practical prowess against the varied beasts roaming Loch Modan, proving they have the patience and nerve demanded of a true stalker of the wild.

Marisa du'Paige. Marisa du'Paige is a rare human rogue spellcaster found lurking within the sprawling cave network outside the entrance to the Deadmines in southwestern Westfall. Aligned with the outlaws operating beneath Moonbrook, she wields arcane magic alongside the laborers and highwaymen guarding the tunnels. Deep inside the winding caverns that lead toward the Deadmines beneath Moonbrook, most defenders are rough-hewn cutpurses, renegade miners, and thugs. Marisa du'Paige stands out among them as a skilled human mage. While most spellcasters of the kingdom train within the sanctioned halls of Stormwind's Mage Quarter or serve the Kirin Tor, du'Paige has cast her lot with the outlaws and brigands hiding in Westfall's subterranean depths.

Marleth Barleybrew. Marleth Barleybrew is an ambitious dwarven brewer stationed out in Brewnall Village. Frustrated by the Thunderbrew clan's dominance over the local beer market, she constantly schemes to prove her family's brew is superior to Kharanos's famous Thunder Ale. In Dun Morogh, alcohol is taken as seriously as steel, and the rivalry between the Barleybrew and Thunderbrew families is legendary. Marleth Barleybrew resents the near-monopoly that Ragnar Thunderbrew and his kin maintain out of the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Convinced her own craft is every bit as robust, she seeks clever ways to slip Barleybrew kegs into the hands of tavern patrons. Rather than engaging in open conflict, she opts for petty subterfuge, recruiting passing travelers to secretly swap out Kharanos's prized ale casks with her own.

Marryk Nurribit. Marryk Nurribit is the resident gnome mage trainer stationed at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. A bit more fond of local brews than disciplined pedagogy, he introduces fledgling gnomish arcanists to their craft while frequently soliciting spare coins for a drink. Tucked away inside the warm hearth of Anvilmar, Marryk Nurribit offers arcane guidance to young gnomes taking their very first steps into magic. Though knowledgeable in the arcane arts, his demeanor is decidedly casual—often seeming far more interested in nursing a flagon of dwarven ale and bumming spare pocket change off his new pupils than drilling them in complex theorems. Despite his vices, Marryk remains acutely aware of the perils outside Coldridge Valley, regularly warning aspiring spellcasters about the lingering radioactive and trogg-infested horrors of fallen Gnomeregan.

Marshal Dughan. Marshal Dughan is the commanding officer of the Stormwind Army detachment stationed in Goldshire. Tasked with protecting the heart of Elwynn Forest, he finds his local garrison stretched thin against growing incursions of kobolds, gnolls, and bandits. To keep the crossroads town and surrounding farmsteads safe, he relies heavily on independent adventurers. Stationed prominently in Goldshire outside the Lion's Pride Inn, Marshal Dughan bears the heavy burden of keeping Elwynn Forest secure while Stormwind's military resources are tied up elsewhere. The surrounding woods are steadily deteriorating: vermin choke the mines, gnolls mass along the riverbanks, and highwaymen harass travelers along the King's Road. With too few footmen under his direct command, Dughan orchestrates local defense by directing fresh recruits to reinforce outposts and scout contested ground.

Marshal Marris. Marshal Marris is the beleaguered military officer commanding the town watch at Lakeshire. Stationed near the town's bridge, he coordinates defense operations against the massive Blackrock orc invasion pressing down from the heights of the Redridge Mountains. With Stormwind's army absent, he relies on visiting adventurers to blunt the horde's advances. Lakeshire stands on the brink of collapse, caught between the gnolls to the west and the terrifying military might of the Blackrock clan to the east. Marshal Marris oversees the guard line at the town's primary bridge, but his resources are depleted and his soldiers are spread impossibly thin. With the kingdom of Stormwind withholding royal reinforcements, Marris carries the heavy burden of keeping the township from being overwhelmed by brute force.

Marshal Maxwell. Marshal Maxwell is a high-ranking officer of the Stormwind army stationed at Morgan's Vigil in the Burning Steppes. Tasked with holding the Alliance's northernmost fortified ridge above the Redridge Mountains against the Blackrock clan and the Dark Iron dwarves, he directs scouting missions into the hostile crags below. He also plays a crucial role in coordinating efforts to discover the fate of his captured comrade, Marshal Reginald Windsor. Morgan's Vigil stands as a precarious outpost on the southern rim of the Burning Steppes, overlooking a wasteland choked with ash, dragonkin, and Blackrock orcs. Marshal Maxwell commands the Stormwind military detachment stationed here, providing a rare friendly sight for travelers braving the fiery crags. From this rocky bastion, he oversees defensive maneuvers to keep the hostile forces of the mountain contained before they can sweep southward into Redridge and Elwynn.

Marshal McBride. Marshal Douglas McBride is the commander of the Stormwind garrison stationed at Northshire Abbey. Tasked with the defense of Northshire Valley, he directs freshly arrived recruits against the rising kobold infestation threatening local farms and mines. He serves as the primary military authority for newcomers beginning their service to the kingdom of Stormwind. Stationed right outside Northshire Abbey, Marshal Douglas McBride represents the direct authority of the Stormwind Army in this quiet valley. While the abbey itself is an enclave of faith and learning, rising turmoil across the kingdom has stretched military garrisons thin. McBride must maintain peace and secure the valley's food and resource supplies with only a handful of sworn guards and an influx of green recruits seeking training under the abbey's masters.

Martie Jainrose. Martie Jainrose is Lakeshire's local herbalist, tending to her garden along the edge of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Beside cultivating remedies and flowers for the beleaguered town, she contends with wild beasts trampling her plots and harbors a quiet affection for Guard Parker. Residing in Lakeshire, Martie Jainrose works diligently as the settlement's resident herbalist. Even as Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and local brigands threaten the region, Martie focuses on keeping the town supplied with fresh herbs and floral arrangements. Her daily labors are often disrupted by local wildlife—most notably the monstrous boar Bellygrub, who frequently ravages her prized garden beds. Beyond her herbal pursuits, Martie seems to hold a fondness for Guard Parker, though Parker is courting Darcy, who calls Martie a jealous rival.

Marukai. Marukai is a Darkspear jungle troll stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the foggy coast of northwest Ashenvale. Dedicated to holding this remote beachhead for the Horde, she coordinates efforts to cull the encroaching Wrathtail naga who threaten the outpost. Zoram'gar Outpost sits isolated on the northern edge of the Zoram Strand, surrounded by ancient ruins, hostile night elf territory, and the restless sea. As the Wrathtail naga emerge in force from the waters and ancient elven ruins to claim the shoreline, Marukai works to keep the encampment from being overwhelmed. She directs Horde champions to push the serpent-folk back into the tide and collect their heads, ensuring the outpost remains a viable coastal stronghold.

Master Apothecary Faranell. Master Apothecary Faranell is the head of the Royal Apothecary Society, stationed within the depths of the Apothecarium in the Undercity. In life a respected Dalaran scholar, in undeath he directs the Forsaken's search for a devastating New Plague to eradicate both the Scourge and the living. Before the Third War, Faranell was an esteemed alchemist who spent decades studying alongside the learned mages of Dalaran. He spent his mortal days seeking cures, remedies, and potions to improve mortal health. When the Scourge plague claimed his life and he arose as a free-willed Forsaken, his former scientific curiosity curdled into cruelty. Retaining his encyclopedic intellect, he traded healing salves for catastrophic reagents, quickly becoming one of Queen Sylvanas Windrunner's most valued researchers in the bowels of Lordaeron's fallen capital.

Apothecary Lydon. Apothecary Lydon is a morbid researcher of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed in Tarren Mill. Chronically depressed and intensely bored, he finds joy only in refining lethal concoctions and watching the living suffer. He spearheads the research into potent new toxins aimed at securing Hillsbrad for the Forsaken and furthering Sylvanas's New Plague. Stationed inside the chapel turned laboratory of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon represents the cold, calculating ethos of the Royal Apothecary Society. He is afflicted by a profound, languid melancholy, disgusted by the blooming flowers and crisp air of Hillsbrad Foothills. The only diversion that lifts his perpetual gloom is the art of deathcraft. When left unattended, he passes the time poisoning, dissecting, and reanimating his unfortunate pet frog, Umpi, repeatedly waiting for new reagents to arrive.

Master Gadrin. Master Gadrin is an elderly jungle troll and a venerable witch doctor of the Darkspear tribe, currently residing in Sen'jin Village. Having once trained the tribe's priests and mages alongside the renegade witch doctor Zalazane, he now coordinates efforts to aid his displaced people and break the dark curse gripping their stolen home on the Echo Isles. Long before the Darkspear arrived on Kalimdor, Master Gadrin served as a witch doctor of his tribe in their ancestral South Seas islands, where he guided the mystical training of generations of Darkspear trolls.

Master Vornal. Master Vornal is an elderly Darkspear jungle troll who resides in Sen'jin Village along the southern coast of Durotar. Despite his advancing years and extensive knowledge of alchemical concoctions, he stubbornly refuses to take on any apprentices. Master Vornal is a fixture of Sen'jin Village, known for brewing potent draughts and spirits for his fellow Darkspear trolls. Though age is visibly catching up with him, Vornal remains intensely independent and stubbornly refuses to train any apprentices, preferring to mix his remedies and volatile mixtures entirely by his own hand.

Mastok Wrilehiss. Mastok Wrilehiss is an orc officer stationed at Splintertree Post in eastern Ashenvale. Serving as a crucial defensive coordinator for the Horde in the contested forest, he directs scouts and warriors to secure nearby borders and handle corrupting elemental threats. His presence is vital for maintaining the precarious foothold the Horde holds amidst constant night elf hostility. Splintertree Post stands deep in the shadow of Ashenvale's towering canopy, completely surrounded by hostile night elven territory. Mastok Wrilehiss serves as one of the post's core defenders, monitoring supply routes and forest activity. The position is perilous; any sign of weakness invites swift strikes from the Sentinels who view the settlement as a despoiling intrusion.

Mathias Shaw. Master Mathias Shaw is the leader of SI:7, the covert intelligence agency of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Operating from the shadows of Old Town, he directs spies and scouts to protect the realm from internal conspiracies and external horrors alike. Mathias Shaw stands as Stormwind's foremost spymaster and assassin. From SI:7's discreet headquarters tucked behind the barracks in Old Town, Shaw coordinates a covert network that spans the Eastern Kingdoms and beyond. Pragmatic, calculating, and fiercely loyal to the House of Wrynn, he operates on the philosophy that Stormwind's safety depends just as much on unseen daggers and stolen missives as it does on gleaming armor and palace garrisons.

Mathredis Firestar. Mathredis Firestar is an eccentric blood elf mage residing at Flame Crest in the Burning Steppes. He crafts powerful enchantments known as Lesser Arcanums, drawing upon the arcane research of his deceased master. In doing so, he feeds on the residual energies unleashed during the binding process to stave off his magic addiction. Mathredis Firestar learned the craft of making arcanums—concentrated gems of arcane empowerment—from his mentor, Telmius Dreamseeker. Telmius met a grim end within the ancient ruins of Dire Maul while trying to wrest magical secrets from the Shen'dralar. While Telmius invented these magical bindings, Mathredis lacks the mastery to produce the greatest of them. Instead, he specializes in Lesser Arcanums. For Mathredis, this work is far more than an academic exercise: like all blood elves following the fall of the Sunwell, he suffers from a gnawing hunger for arcane power. Binding materials to ancient librams releases violent discharges of magical energy, which Mathredis siphons to sustain himself.

Mathrengyl Bearwalker. Mathrengyl Bearwalker is a master druid trainer and respected elder of the Cenarion Circle residing in Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave. Having once served as Archdruid Fandral Staghelm's direct assistant, he guides young Alliance druids through their spiritual trials, shapeshifting rites, and duties across Kalimdor. Perched within the verdant reaches of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker stands as one of the most venerable and balanced druids on Teldrassil. He serves as a primary guide for fledgling Alliance druids, overseeing their communion with Moonglade and testing their readiness to master primal animal forms. Having undergone the intense, bewildering communion with the Great Bear Spirit in his own youth, Mathrengyl understands the weight of these rites, personally charging initiates to prove their spirit against the sacred moonkin Lunaclaw before inducting them into the path of the Druid of the Claw.

Maur Grimtotem. Maur Grimtotem was an emissary sent by Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem into the depths of Ragefire Chasm. Dispatched on an ill-fated diplomatic mission to the troggs infesting the subterranean tunnels beneath Orgrimmar, he met a brutal end at their hands. Today, only his remains and personal satchel linger in the dark as evidence of the foolish errand. While most in the Horde view troggs as mindless, savage brutes beneath negotiation, Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem thought otherwise—or at least claimed to. She dispatched Maur Grimtotem deep into the winding caverns of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar to attempt a peaceful overture with the subterranean beasts. Predictably, diplomacy failed. Maur was swiftly slain, his corpse left in the caverns under the watchful eye of the trogg chieftain Oggleflint.

Maur Raincaller. Maur Raincaller is a tauren resident found residing in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Connected to the natural and spiritual life of the plains, he assists the village elders and watches over local matters affecting the herds and wild beasts. Situated near the heart of Bloodhoof Village on the shores of Lake Stonebull, Maur Raincaller serves his community by attending to regional ecological and beast-related concerns. Like many who bear the mantle of Raincaller, he pays close attention to the balance of the elements and wildlife across the fertile plains of Mulgore. After a bite from the fearsome strider Mazzranache left his wound infected, Maur turns to capable young travelers to gather the animal parts he needs for a remedy.

Maurin Bonesplitter. Maurin Bonesplitter is a Forsaken scholar and spellcaster stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. Appointed by Keldran to monitor demonic cult activity, he leverages his deep understanding of ancient lore to dismantle the Burning Blade. Maurin regards the cultists with sheer contempt, viewing them as fools blind to the dark entities pulling their strings. While Ghost Walker Post primarily serves as a tauren and Horde outpost amidst the arid wastes of Desolace, Maurin Bonesplitter stands apart as one of its few undead occupants. Rather than a brutish soldier, Maurin is a learned spellcaster possessing extensive knowledge of forbidden histories and occult forces. His arcane aptitude and sharp intellect caught the eye of Keldran, who dispatched him to the region to observe the growing demonic presence and coordinate targeted strikes against it.

Maxan Anvol. Maxan Anvol is a dwarven priest trainer stationed within the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Dedicated to the Holy Light, he guides fledgling dwarven priests as they learn to channel divine power amid Dun Morogh's frigid climes. He tests young acolytes to ensure they are worthy of wearing the vestments of the church. While it might seem strange to find an ordained minister of the Holy Light stationed inside Thunderbrew Distillery, it suits dwarven culture well. Kharanos serves as the primary hub between Coldridge Valley and Ironforge, and the local inn is where travelers, mountaineers, and acolytes naturally gather. Maxan tends to the spiritual welfare of the hamlet alongside pints of stout, offering prayers and counsel to any who step through the doors.

Maybell Maclure. Maybell Maclure is a young woman living at the Maclure Vineyards in Elwynn Forest. Despite a bitter, long-standing feud between her family and the neighboring Stonefields, she has secretly fallen in love with Tommy Joe Stonefield. Life on the Maclure Vineyards is defined by endless labor and an enduring grudge against the neighboring Stonefield family. Caught in the middle is Maybell Maclure, who has fallen deeply in love with Tommy Joe Stonefield, the young heir to the rival farmstead. Kept apart by vigilant relatives and ancient family resentment, Maybell is desperate for any chance to communicate with Tommy Joe beyond the prying eyes of her kin.

Mebok Mizzyrix. Mebok Mizzyrix is an enterprising goblin entrepreneur residing in the port town of Ratchet. Ever eager to turn bizarre wilderness reagents into profit, he hires passing adventurers to gather unusual flora and fauna from across the Barrens and beyond. His most notorious project involves concocting a commercial intellect-enhancing beverage out of raptor horns. Operating out of the bustling, neutral port of Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix embodies the classic Steamwheedle spirit of relentless opportunism. While Ratchet caters to sailors, pirates, and merchants of all stripes, Mebok focuses his keen eye on Kalimdor's wilderness. Rather than mining standard ore or trading mundane cloth, he seeks out rare biological curiosities that he believes can be refined into highly lucrative concoctions and commodities.

Melithar Staghelm. Melithar Staghelm is a night elf stationed just outside Aldrassil in Shadowglen, Teldrassil's starting glade. He assists young night elf adventurers as they embark on their early training, sending them to learn what has brought the dryad Tarindrella back to the glade. While he shares the prominent Staghelm surname with Archdruid Fandral Staghelm, his exact connection to the ruling druid remains unconfirmed. Standing directly outside the entrance to the great bough of Aldrassil, Melithar serves as an early point of contact for night elves emerging into the world. A druid who listens to the whisperings of the forest spirits, he has learned that the mysterious woodland protector Tarindrella has returned to Shadowglen after years away. Sensing that something is amiss, Melithar sends newcomers to seek out the dryad southwest of Aldrassil and learn what business brings her to the grove.

Melor Stonehoof. Melor Stonehoof is a veteran tauren huntsman stationed atop Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. As a mentor in the ways of the hunt, he tests the tracking prowess and mettle of Horde hunters by sending them after the most dangerous predatory beasts across the Barrens and Thousand Needles. Perched upon the breezy expanse of Hunter Rise, Melor Stonehoof observes the plains below with a practiced eye. The art of the hunt is sacred to the tauren, entwined with survival, spiritual balance, and respect for nature's greatest predators. Melor ensures that those who carry bow and blade in the name of the Horde understand this balance, directing promising stalkers to master their craft through trials against legendary beasts.

Menara Voidrender. Menara Voidrender is a human warlock residing in the goblin port of Ratchet. She acts as a mentor to ambitious practitioners of the dark arts from both the Alliance and the Horde, sharing her deep knowledge of demon-binding artifacts and arcane craft. Her secluded position in Kalimdor keeps her far from the watchful eyes of orthodox authorities. While most warlocks in the Eastern Kingdoms practice in damp cellars or secluded slaughterhouses beneath their home cities, Menara Voidrender chose the neutral goblin port of Ratchet in the Barrens. Operating far from the scrutiny of the Kirin Tor, Stormwind's guards, or Orgrimmar's overseers, she is free to pursue her occult studies in plain sight. Her willingness to deal with any capable apprentice, regardless of faction, makes her a rare point of commonality among practitioners of the dark arts.

Merissa Stilwell. Merissa Stilwell is a young human townsperson residing at Northshire Abbey within Elwynn Forest. Standing near the abbey, she offers a cheerful greeting and a helping hand to the newcomers training in Northshire Valley. Standing at Northshire Abbey, Merissa Stilwell greets the fresh recruits who arrive in Northshire Valley. For wandering novices, she offers simple hospitality and practical advice on resting up and getting oriented. Sharing a surname with notable craftsmen and homesteaders across the kingdom—such as the blacksmith Jordan Stilwell and the Westfall defender Daphne Stilwell—she remains a peaceful local face amidst the kingdom's rising tensions.

Merrin Rockweaver. Merrin Rockweaver is a dwarven researcher representing the Explorers' League in the Wetlands. Following a violent raptor infestation that overran Whelgar's Excavation Site, she took refuge alongside Prospector Whelgar on a ridge overlooking the site. Merrin Rockweaver traveled to the Wetlands on behalf of the Ironforge Explorers' League to unearth ancient Titan secrets buried beneath the muck. The expedition ended in disaster when the large bones they unearthed drew raptors to the dig. Vicious prehistoric beasts swarmed the trenches, forcing Merrin and the surviving crew to abandon their equipment, notes, and progress. She is now trapped with the few survivors on a bluff overlooking the overrun ruins.

Miles Welsh. Miles Welsh is a Forsaken priest trainer residing deep within the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff. He offers spiritual instruction and shadow discipline to priests traversing the tauren capital. Miles Welsh stands far from the plague-scarred ruins of Lordaeron, making his home in the humid, spirit-laden grotto beneath Thunder Bluff known as the Pools of Vision. As a Forsaken priest, he instructs travelers who channel divine and shadowy energies. His presence in the heart of Mulgore reflects the tenuous diplomatic ties binding the Forsaken to the Horde, sharing sanctuary with tauren mystics and shamans while guiding acolytes in the arts of shadow and faith.

Milli Featherwhistle. Milli Featherwhistle is a master gnomish mechanostrider engineer stationed at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. Following the fall of Gnomeregan, she meticulously handcrafts and maintains the clockwork mounts favored by her kin. She sells her prized mechanical creations to fellow gnomes and trusted allies of the exiled Gnomeregan survivors. Operating outdoors in the biting chill of Steelgrill's Depot just east of Kharanos, Milli Featherwhistle oversees the supply of clockwork steeds for Gnomeregan's displaced populace. Unlike the biological beasts favored by dwarves and night elves, Milli builds her entire inventory herself, personally calibrating gears, pistons, and balancing gyros to ensure each mechanical bird runs at peak efficiency across the snowy crags of Dun Morogh.

Milton Sheaf. Milton Sheaf is the head librarian of the Royal Library inside Stormwind Keep. Dedicated to preserving the kingdom's history, he oversees the realm's collection of ancient tomes and historical chronicles. He frequently enlists Alliance travelers to recover lost volumes, track down scattered records, and restore neglected manuscripts. Tucked away in the quiet halls of the Royal Library in Stormwind Keep, Milton Sheaf tends to the collective memory of the kingdom. While the court upstairs bustles with politics, squabbling nobles, and military concerns, Sheaf focuses on the preservation of the written word. He considers maintaining accurate histories of the Alliance and the Eastern Kingdoms a sacred duty, especially in an era fraught with war, loss, and instability.

Miner Johnson. Miner Johnson is an elusive, seasoned miner affiliated with the Defias Brotherhood deep inside the Deadmines. Tucked away in a side alcove alongside ordinary laborers, this dangerous prospector oversees excavation efforts ahead of the heavy machinery found deeper underground. Because he wanders the subterranean tunnels erratically, adventurers only occasionally cross his path. While hundreds of laborers pick at the subterranean veins of the Deadmines to supply Edwin VanCleef's hidden fortress, Miner Johnson stands out as an unusually formidable figure among them. Lurking in a shadowed alcove to the left before the lumbering shredders of the Mast Room, he is far tougher and more aggressive than the regular workforce. His unpredictable presence makes him a legendary target for explorers traversing the Defias tunnels.

Minor Manifestation of Earth. A Minor Manifestation of Earth is a localized elemental spirit bound to sacred stones in Mulgore and Durotar. Invisible to ordinary sight, it reveals itself only to fledgling shamans who drink the sacred Earth Sapta, providing the rough quartz required to carve their very first earth totem. The spirits of the earth dwell everywhere beneath the dirt and stone, but communicating with them requires deliberate ritual. At sacred landmarks like Kodo Rock in Mulgore and Spirit Rock in Durotar, Minor Manifestations of Earth linger in the unseen realm, surrounded by even smaller elemental presences. Only initiates who have drunk the Earth Sapta—a ritual draught brewed by shamanic mentors—can lift the veil between the physical world and the elements. Once acknowledged, the spirit imparts the earth's blessings along with a piece of rough quartz, granting the novice the spiritual focal point needed to fashion an Earth Totem.

Minor Manifestation of Water. The Minor Manifestation of Water is an elemental spirit found along North Tide's Run on the coast of Silverpine Forest. It serves as a vital trial for Horde shamans seeking to commune with and master the element of water. Before this peaceful spirit can be consulted, initiates must first cleanse its corrupted counterpart. Lurking along the mist-shrouded shores of North Tide's Run, west of the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, the Minor Manifestation of Water represents an essential rite of passage for developing shamans. Water elementals embody life, renewal, and fluidity, but they can easily fall victim to malevolent blight. An initiate must face and defeat a corrupted manifestation of this elemental before the pure Minor Manifestation of Water can reveal itself. Once cleansed, the spirit offers guidance to shamans completing their sacred journey to fashion a Water Totem.

Misha. Misha is the loyal bear companion of Rexxar, the Champion of the Horde. She wanders Kalimdor faithfully at the half-ogre beastmaster's side. Misha is a brown bear who walks at the side of the wandering Rexxar, a solitary spirit who trusts beasts more than people. Together they have forged a fierce, protective partnership that has weathered countless wildernesses and bloody battles.

Misha Tor'kren. Misha Tor'kren is an orc mother dwelling at the Tor'kren Farm in western Durotar, southeast of Thunder Ridge. Plagued by anxiety over her missing son Kron, she appeals to passing travelers for aid in discovering his fate. Tucked away near the edge of Thunder Ridge, Misha Tor'kren works her isolated farmstead while enduring a parent's worst fear. Her son Kron ventured west toward the Southfury River to hunt crocolisks and prove his mettle, but he never returned. With Durotar's frontier dangers stretching orcish watchtowers thin, Misha is left alone to hope for word of his whereabouts, desperate for anyone willing to search the riverbanks for signs of her boy.

Mitsuwa. Mitsuwa is a Darkspear troll stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the misty coast of Ashenvale. Deeply troubled by the ambush of his traveling kin, he enlists Horde champions to avenge the fallen and reclaim stolen spiritual talismans. Situated at the remote Zoram'gar Outpost on the strand of the Zoram Strand, Mitsuwa serves the Horde alongside his companion Marukai. When a group of traveling trolls bound for the encampment was ambushed and slaughtered by the aggressive Thistlefur furbolgs of northern Ashenvale, Mitsuwa took the loss as a grievous offense. Driven by duty and anger, he directs able-bodied warriors toward the Thistlefur dens to reclaim the stolen troll charms, ensuring the spirits of his kin are honored and their sacred possessions recovered from the beasts.

Monte Gazlowe. Gazlowe is the pragmatic goblin engineer and overseer who established and rules the port town of Ratchet. After serving as the Horde's chief engineer during the founding of Durotar and Orgrimmar, he used his substantial earnings to build a bustling, neutral trading hub for the Steamwheedle Cartel. After securing a handsome payday for his engineering work with the new Horde, Gazlowe invested directly into the barren coastline, founding the port of Ratchet. Operating under the Steamwheedle Cartel, he runs the dockside town as a strictly neutral port where Horde, Alliance, and independent traders can barter freely—provided they keep their weapons sheathed and their purses heavy.

Moon Priestess Amara. Moon Priestess Amara is a night elf priestess stationed along the main road west of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Flanked by loyal huntress guards, she keeps watch over the woodland pathways connecting the heart of the bough to the capital city of Darnassus. Stationed at a quiet wayside post west of Dolanaar, Moon Priestess Amara represents both the spiritual authority of the Sisterhood of Elune and the practical vigilance required to keep Teldrassil's roadways secure. She travels and watches with two huntress companions, Nhemai and Yaeliura. To travelers journeying westward, Amara acts as a guiding hand, directing adventurers along the road toward Darnassus and tasking those with burdened spirits to seek out paths of redemption.

Mor'rogal. Mor'rogal is a tauren resident of Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. He serves as an advisor and guide for travelers seeking glory and peril within the rugged subterranean reaches of the crags. Perched within the refuge of Sun Rock Retreat, Mor'rogal takes a keen interest in the deep crevices and caverns that cut through the Stonetalon Mountains. Recognizing that the region's twisting subterranean passes offer both great riches and lethal danger, he directs brave Horde wanderers to investigate troubled areas like the Boulderslide Ravine. For Mor'rogal, delving into these treacherous depths is not merely a matter of survival, but a test of spirit for those who follow their heart and soul in search of glory.

Morgan Pestle. Morgan Pestle is a human alchemist and shopkeeper who runs Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District of Stormwind City. Working closely with his brother William Pestle in Goldshire, he handles supplies and alchemical research for the capital. Operating out of Pestle's Apothecary along the busy thoroughfares of Stormwind's Trade District, Morgan Pestle provides alchemical goods, reagents, and practical remedies to city residents and passing travelers. While his brother William maintains a workshop at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Morgan keeps the family trade rooted in the heart of the kingdom's capital, receiving shipments, such as his brother's candles, from the rural heartlands.

Morgan the Collector. Morgan the Collector is a high-ranking Defias operative overseeing the Brotherhood's extortion and gathering activities across Elwynn Forest. Based in the overrun Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, he coordinates local thievery right under the nose of the Goldshire guard. Morgan earned his epithet by skimming gold from the mines of Elwynn Forest on behalf of the Defias Brotherhood. While common bandits harass wayfarers along the roads, Morgan directs organized shakedowns and collects stolen coin and supplies to funnel deeper into the Brotherhood's network. He has made his headquarters inside the farmhouse at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, surrounded by loyal enforcers including Surena Caledon and Erlan Drudgemoor.

Morin Cloudstalker. Morin Cloudstalker is a tauren scout keeping watch along the road leading east from Bloodhoof Village toward the Barrens in Mulgore. Standing vigil over the plains, he monitors local trade routes and investigates the encroaching threats endangering tauren travelers. Positioned beside the dirt path winding east toward the Barrens, Morin Cloudstalker acts as both a scout and a guardian for travelers through Mulgore. The grassy plains here are usually peaceful, but the opening of trade routes and shifting territories have drawn opportunists and bandits dangerously close to the heart of the tauren homeland.

Motega Firemane. Motega Firemane is a tauren scholar stationed at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Dedicated to cataloging the dangerous wildlife of the canyon, he finds his studies disrupted by a vengeful wind serpent spirit and the reckless misadventures of his young assistant. Four years following the Third War, Motega Firemane journeyed south into Thousand Needles to observe and record the distinct beasts surviving among the towering mesas. Accompanied by his youthful assistant, Pao'ka Swiftmountain—whose protective father was reluctant to let him leave Mulgore—Motega set up camp alongside Kanati Greycloud at Whitereach Post. While his original calling was quiet natural observation, the harsh perils of the canyon floor continually demand a more martial approach to survival.

Mountaineer Barleybrew. Mountaineer Barleybrew is an Ironforge mountaineer stationed at the South Gate Outpost in Dun Morogh. Guarding the pass leading eastward toward Loch Modan, he relies on hearty dwarven brews to keep sentries alert in the biting cold. Perched at the South Gate Outpost guarding the snowy roadway toward Loch Modan, Mountaineer Wellart Barleybrew stands as part of Ironforge's border watch. Like many mountaineers serving in the bitter winds of Dun Morogh, he appreciates the fortifying qualities of fine dwarven drink. Bearing the name of the renowned Barleybrew clan, he helps see to it that shipments of potent Shimmer Stout make their way to fellow watchmen who need warmth and stamina during long shifts along the mountain passes.

Mountaineer Kadrell. Mountaineer Kadrell is a stalwart dwarven sentry stationed across from the Stoutlager Inn in Thelsamar. Serving as a crucial liaison within the Loch Modan Mountaineers, he coordinates reconnaissance, supply deliveries, and border defense across the region. Standing watch in the bustling settlement of Thelsamar, Mountaineer Kadrell acts as an anchor for dwarven defenses throughout Loch Modan. While outposts on the valley's fringes face relentless pressure from troggs, gnolls, and native beasts, Kadrell remains at the center of town to organize reinforcements, relay orders, and assess incoming field reports from wandering scouts.

Mountaineer Stormpike. Mountaineer Stormpike is an Ironforge mountaineer stationed at Algaz Station in northern Loch Modan. Watching over the mountain pass leading toward the Wetlands, he works tirelessly to keep vital supply routes safe from lurking troggs and kobolds. As a proud member of the Stormpike clan, his loyalty lies squarely with Ironforge and the safety of dwarven lands. Perched along the northern border of Loch Modan, Algaz Station serves as a critical checkpoint before the perilous descent into the Wetlands. Mountaineer Stormpike is stationed here amid rocky crags and constant wilderness threats. His primary duty is maintaining the line of communication and keeping the roads open for travelers and supply convoys traversing through Dun Algaz.

Mountaineer Thalos. Mountaineer Thalos is a dwarven sentry stationed at the Coldridge Valley mouth of Coldridge Pass. Tasked with guarding the route, he warns travelers about the sudden trogg infestation choking the tunnel. Adventurers carrying urgent reports from the valley rely on him to point the way safely toward Kharanos. Perched on the snowy border where Coldridge Valley gives way to the deeper crags of Dun Morogh, Mountaineer Thalos serves as the first line of defense for travelers leaving the dwarven training grounds. Coldridge Pass has become a treacherous chokepoint overrun by hostile troggs who have burrowed up from the subterranean depths. Thalos stands vigil in the cold, warning the unready to turn back and assessing whether hardy couriers possess the grit to fight their way through to the wider kingdom.

Mr. Smite. Mr. Smite is the imposing tauren first mate serving aboard the Defias Brotherhood's flagship deep inside the Deadmines. An expert weaponmaster under Captain Greenskin, he commands the dockside approach to the hidden juggernaut with ruthless discipline. Intruders who face him must contend with his shifting arsenal and devastating physical strength. Guarding the docks of Ironclad Cove, Mr. Smite serves as first mate to the goblin Captain Greenskin. While the Defias Brotherhood is predominantly composed of disenfranchised humans and allied goblin tinkerers, Smite stands as a striking anomaly: a massive, battle-hardened tauren far from the plains of Kalimdor. Tasked with maintaining strict order among a rowdy pirate crew, he ensures that the labor fitting out Edwin VanCleef's secret dreadnaught proceeds without disruption.

Mull Thunderhorn. Mull Thunderhorn is a tauren elder residing in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Deeply devoted to the Earth Mother and the balance of the land, he watches over the sacred water wells scattered across the plains. As outside exploiters threaten the region's lifegiving waters, Mull guides young tauren through the rituals required to cleanse the ancestral springs. Standing watch in Bloodhoof Village, Mull Thunderhorn carries the weight of Mulgore's spiritual well-being. The nomadic tribes have gathered under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof to establish a permanent home, yet their lands are already under siege by greed and reckless expansion. Mull serves as a spiritual anchor for the young braves stepping out of Camp Narache, calling upon them to safeguard the vital resources of their ancestors.

Mupsi Shacklefridd. Mupsi Shacklefridd is a goblin resident stationed just outside the port town of Ratchet in the Barrens. She serves as a local contact for travelers looking to smooth over troubled relations with the Steamwheedle Cartel. Mupsi Shacklefridd operates just outside Ratchet along the dusty coastal roads of the Barrens. Life near the port town is always busy, with Steamwheedle guards patrolling the perimeter and merchants coming and going. For those who find themselves in poor standing with the goblins, Mupsi provides a path to reconciliation—provided travelers are willing to offer the supplies and labor the cartel demands.

Mutanus the Devourer. Mutanus the Devourer is a monstrous, pale murloc manifested directly from the Emerald Nightmare. Lurking in the darkest recesses of the sleeping druid Naralex's mind, it emerges to devour anyone attempting to break the Nightmare's hold over the Wailing Caverns. Slaying this twisted aberration is the final step in freeing Naralex from his tormented slumber. When the night elf druid Naralex tapped into the underground springs beneath the Barrens, he aimed to restore life to the arid wastes by connecting them to the Emerald Dream. Instead, an ancient corruption known as the Emerald Nightmare invaded his thoughts. Trapped in an agonizing vision, Naralex's subconscious fears took physical form. The corruption gave that nightmare the shape of an immense, albino murloc.

Mux Manascrambler. Mux Manascrambler is an eccentric goblin engineer dwelling in the desert outpost of Gadgetzan. Unlike many of his peers focused strictly on explosives or mining equipment, Mux harbors a peculiar fascination with the supernatural and occult energies. Tucked away inside a building in central Gadgetzan, behind Driz Plunkbow and his clanking Butcherbots, sits Mux Manascrambler. While the Steamwheedle Cartel trades heavily in oil, guns, and salvage, Mux focuses his ingenuity on more esoteric pursuits: the realm of spirits and supernatural anomalies. He uses his technical acumen to design bizarre devices capable of detecting, distilling, and interacting with spectral remnants, bridging crude goblin craftsmanship with the invisible worlds of the dead.

Mydrannul. Mydrannul is a night elf general goods vendor stationed at the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus. He serves the capital's sentinels, soldiers, and visitors by keeping basic supplies, munitions, and provisions readily available. Located among the military pavilions and training grounds of the Warrior's Terrace, Mydrannul provides essential gear to Darnassus's defenders and traveling adventurers alike. His wares include the practical everyday items needed for life in the field: ammunition for archers and gunners, throwing blades, flint, pouches, and simple rations. By tending his stall in the city's martial district, he ensures that the sentinels and trainees preparing for duty on Teldrassil do not want for basic sundries.

Nalpak. Nalpak is a tauren druid disciple who watches over the troubled Wailing Caverns in the Barrens. Stationed in the high cliff-cave overlooking the cavern entrance, he enlists passing adventurers to help contain the nightmare twisting the subterranean ecosystem. Perched inside a hidden cavern directly above the mouth of the Wailing Caverns, Nalpak remains loyal to the vision of Naralex. While his master lies trapped in a corrupted slumber deep below, Nalpak works to keep the spreading corruption at bay. He asks adventurers to gather deviate hides for use as leather.

Nara Meideros. Nara Meideros is a night elf priestess stationed within the tranquil greenery of the Park in Stormwind City. Serving as a mentor to acolytes, she represents the teachings of Elune amidst the human capital. While most priestesses of Elune remain in Kalimdor under the boughs of Teldrassil, Nara Meideros resides far across the Great Sea in Stormwind City. Found within the Park—a haven nurtured by visiting night elf druids and priests—she guides young spiritual seekers in the ways of divine devotion. Alongside human practitioners of the Holy Light in Cathedral Square, Nara offers night elves visiting or living in the Eastern Kingdoms a familiar connection to the grace of the Moon Goddess.

Narain Soothfancy. Narain Soothfancy is an eccentric gnome dwelling in a secluded beach hut just north of Steamwheedle Port in Tanaris. While he loudly advertises himself as a master soothsayer capable of divining the future, those who know him consider his psychic talents a complete farce compared to his genuine engineering genius. Perched on the eastern coast of Tanaris just north of the goblin docks, Narain Soothfancy lives as a retired engineer turned self-proclaimed master fortune teller. He routinely greets visitors by pressing unopened envelopes against his forehead or making wildly inaccurate guesses about their business, such as wondering if they have arrived seeking the legendary Ashbringer. Despite his theatrical charade, Narain possesses deep technical knowledge. Even ancient beings like the blue dragon Azuregos note that while Narain is a terrible psychic, his engineering aptitude is undeniably brilliant. A handbook titled 'Soothsaying for Dummies' rests nearby.

Naralex. Naralex is a night elf druid who sought to restore the parched Barrens to a lush forest using the powers of the Emerald Dream. Instead, his slumber was overtaken by a dark nightmare, twisting the Wailing Caverns beneath the earth and turning his followers into venomous fiends. Long before the Great Sundering, the sun-scorched plains of the Barrens were once a vibrant forest. Viewing this loss as a tragedy, Naralex journeyed to the Barrens with a cohort of devoted disciples to reverse the drought. Deep beneath the savannah, he discovered an intricate subterranean network of underground springs and rushing geysers, naming them the Wailing Caverns after the howling wind and steam that moaned through the rock. He believed that by entering a deep trance and channeling the pristine energies of the Emerald Dream into these subterranean waters, the life-giving flow would reach the surface and cause the entire wasteland to bloom.

Nat Pagle. Nat Pagle is widely hailed as the most renowned angler in all of Azeroth, despite claiming he only fishes as an excuse to drink heavily. He makes his home on a secluded inlet in Dustwallow Marsh, where he trains elite anglers from both the Alliance and the Horde who manage to prove their patience. Though his name is synonymous with angling mastery across the known world, Nat Pagle is remarkably casual about his craft. Having cast lines for several decades, he often admits he has no great reverence for the sport itself, famously calling it little more than a convenient excuse to sit back and drink heavily. Despite this gruff nonchalance, Nat understands aquatic life and the art of angling better than anyone alive, even licensing fishing gear sought out by professionals.

Natalia Mar'alith. Mistress Natalia Mar'alith is a night elf priestess and Cenarion Circle researcher lost deep within the silithid nests of Hive'Regal. Once part of the expedition investigating Silithus alongside her husband, Commander Mar'alith, she has succumbed completely to the maddening influence of the Old Gods. When the Cenarion Circle established their outpost at Cenarion Hold to monitor the awakening sands, Natalia accompanied her husband, Commander Mar'alith, into the wastes. Eager to unravel the mystery behind the resurgence of the silithid and the ancient Qiraji ruins, she joined an exploratory party led by the famed explorer Brann Bronzebeard, accompanied by the dwarven researchers Rutgar Glyphshaper and Frankal Stonebridge.

Nathanos Blightcaller. Nathanos Blightcaller, once Nathanos Marris, stands at his ruined homestead in the Eastern Plaguelands as the deadly champion of Queen Sylvanas Windrunner. In life he was the first and only human Ranger Lord of Quel'Thalas, and in undeath he trains Forsaken hunters while guarding the eastern frontier with biting contempt for all who approach. Before the Third War, Nathanos Marris was an extraordinary marksman and tactical genius hailing from the rural outskirts of Lordaeron. Trained by the high elves of Quel'Thalas and close to Sylvanas Windrunner, he became the only human to ever attain the prestigious rank of Ranger Lord. His home remained the family estate in Lordaeron, the Marris Stead.

Hilary. Hilary is a young human girl living in the lakeside town of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains. Distraught after dropping a cherished gift from her father into the lake, she spends her time crying along the town's docks. Amid the mounting threats of gnoll invasions and Blackrock orc warbands pressing down on Lakeshire, the children of the town still face everyday childhood troubles. Hilary accidentally dropped a necklace given to her by her father into the murky waters of Lake Everstill. Terrified that her father will be angry with her, the distraught girl waits by the town pier in tears, hoping someone brave enough will plunge into the lake to retrieve it.

Nikova Raskol. Nikova Raskol is an elderly human townsperson who walks the cobblestone streets of Old Town in Stormwind City. Grieving the murder of her grandson at the hands of the Defias Brotherhood, she seeks justice against the rioting criminals locked inside the Stockade. Nikova wanders Old Town carrying the weight of a recent and devastating personal tragedy. Her beloved grandson, Mac, was slain by brigands belonging to the Defias Brotherhood. While the kingdom grapples with treason on a political scale, Nikova represents the intimate human cost inflicted upon everyday citizens by the Brotherhood's lawless rampage.

Nissa Firestone. Nissa Firestone is a dwarven physician stationed above the bustle of the Great Forge in Ironforge. She serves as an instructor in field medicine, teaching travelers and soldiers how to dress wounds and bind trauma. Amid the clanging metal and blistering heat of the Great Forge, Nissa Firestone practices medicine from the upper floor of the Ironforge Physician shop. While dwarven warriors are famed for their endurance, even stone-hard skin splits against blade and claw. Nissa ensures that those heading out into the snows of Dun Morogh or beyond know how to keep themselves and their allies alive with basic bandaging and field dressings.

Nogg. Nogg is a goblin engineer operating out of a workshop in the Valley of Honor in Orgrimmar. He offers tinkering expertise and specialized craftsmanship to the Horde, notably analyzing strange mechanical salvage recovered from deep within Gnomeregan. Tucked away in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Nogg runs an independent engineering workshop catering to adventurers and craftsmen alike. While the surrounding city relies heavily on traditional orcish steel and brute strength, Nogg provides the specialized mechanical finesse that only a goblin can offer. He maintains a keen interest in foreign contraptions and tech, happily examining curious trinkets and mechanical oddities dragged back from Alliance lands or subterranean ruins.

Nori Pridedrift. Nori Pridedrift is an enterprising dwarf peddling his piping-hot Scalding Mornbrew throughout snowy Coldridge Valley. He makes his living braving the cold to supply shivering mountaineers with their morning pick-me-up, often enlisting swift recruits to run deliveries while the drink remains steaming. Life in Coldridge Valley is harsh and bitterly cold, and nothing cuts through the chill quite like a draught of Scalding Mornbrew. Nori Pridedrift has carved out a living by brewing and distributing this hot, coffee-like morning drink across the frozen drifts. Because the brew must be consumed while still scalding to be fully appreciated, delivery is a race against the elements. Nori frequently recruits brisk couriers to sprint fresh draughts out to freezing sentries before the mountain air robs the brew of its heat. Just as important as the brew itself are his limited supplies of sturdy mugs, which he expects his runners to return promptly.

Novice Elreth. Novice Elreth is an undead member of the Forsaken stationed inside the chapel at Deathknell. As newly risen undead awaken into their second life, she directs them to confront the mindless Scourge haunting the nearby graves and tend to the tragic aftermath of the plague. Inside the desecrated chapel at Deathknell, Novice Elreth assists the emerging undead as they struggle to understand their horrific awakening. Rather than succumbing to despair or the mindless hunger of the Scourge, the Forsaken must organize quickly to secure their territory. Elreth provides newly freed souls with early tasks, directing them to gather paws and wings from the wolves and bats to the south and deal with the lingering remnants of Lordaeron's tragic downfall, including the sorrow of her friend Marla Fipps, slain by her own husband Samuel after he joined the mindless Scourge.

Oben Rageclaw. Oben Rageclaw is the restless spirit of a night elf druid haunting the corrupted depths of the Ban'ethil Barrow Den in Teldrassil. While his spirit wanders trapped in the barrow den, his slumbering physical form has fallen under the sway of foul furbolg magic. Like many Druids of the Claw, Oben Rageclaw retreated into the subterranean sanctum of Ban'ethil Barrow Den to commune with nature and wander the Emerald Dream. However, when the native Gnarlpine furbolgs fell to corruption and overran the barrows, Oben was caught entirely defenseless in his trance. Rather than simply slaying him, the corrupted Gnarlpine shaman used dark rituals to seize control of his comatose mortal frame, leaving his displaced spirit lingering as an anguished ghost unable to pass on or wake.

Oggleflint. Oggleflint is the chieftain of the trogg tribe dwelling within the volcanic depths of Ragefire Chasm directly beneath Orgrimmar. His troggs have been creeping up from the lava-filled tunnels toward the surface, and from his place near the cavern's entrance he commands a savage pack that poses an immediate threat to the Horde capital above. Oggleflint and his troggs climbed out of the fiery tunnels deep beneath Orgrimmar and into Ragefire Chasm. Brutal and territorial, they carved out a primitive domain among the molten rock. Though troggs possess little in the way of advanced civilization, Oggleflint maintained absolute authority over the pack through sheer brute strength.

Ogtinc. Ogtinc is an independent furbolg hunter perched on a high ridge overlooking the Ruins of Eldarath in Azshara. Having parted ways with his tribe to serve the balance of nature, he acts as a trusted ally and mentor for the Cenarion Circle. Skilled hunters seeking to test their craft against the fiercest beasts of Kalimdor often seek out his guidance. While most furbolg in Kalimdor remain fiercely bound to their tribes—or have succumbed to corruption following the Third War—Ogtinc chose a distinct path. Departing from his kin, he dedicated his bow and survival lore to aiding the Cenarion Circle. He makes his camp high on a bluff southeast of Timbermaw Hold, vigilantly watching over the ancient, shattered lands of Azshara.

Ogunaro Wolfrunner. Ogunaro Wolfrunner is the Horde's premier wolf breeder and kennel keeper in Orgrimmar, stationed by the Hunter's Hall in the Valley of Honor. He tends the fierce wolves chosen to bear orc champions and their trusted allies into battle. For seasoned riders seeking a bond with Durotar's apex predators, Ogunaro is the master to see. Situated near the Hunter's Hall within the Valley of Honor, Ogunaro Wolfrunner oversees the breeding and conditioning of Orgrimmar's battle wolves. The bond between orc and wolf dates back generations across the plains of Draenor and the rugged wilderness of Durotar, representing a partnership of mutual respect rather than mere domestication. Ogunaro ensures only the hardiest, fiercest beasts—from dire wolves to agile timber prowlers—are entrusted to warriors who have proven their strength and worth to the warchief.

Old Murk-Eye. Old Murk-Eye is an infamous, battle-hardened murloc prowling the southern coastline of Westfall. Revered among his kind and feared by coastal sailors, he serves as a lethal menace to anyone wandering near the Westfall Lighthouse. While murlocs are a common pest along the shores of Westfall, Old Murk-Eye stands apart from the lesser scavengers. Considerably tougher and far more aggressive than his kin, this grizzled beast prowls the surf surrounding the Westfall Lighthouse. His continued presence has caused enough grief to local mariners that the spectral Captain Grayson seeks his death, offering a bounty for the creature's pristine scales to break his grip on the shallows.

Old Serra'kis. Old Serra'kis is an ancient, massive threshadon dwelling in the submerged subterranean waters of Blackfathom Deeps. Hidden in a flooded cave beneath the ruins, the enormous beast is lethal to any who seek it out. The Twilight's Hammer has made its home in the sunken Moonshrine Ruins, but the dark waters beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum hide older, wilder things. Old Serra'kis, the largest threshadon in the sunken temple, lurks in the Forgotten Pool, a flooded cave beneath the ruins where few would think to look.

Onyxia. Onyxia is the broodmother of the black dragonflight and the devious daughter of Deathwing. From her lair in Dustwallow Marsh, she schemes to restore the black dragonflight's dominion over the mortal kingdoms.

Orendil Broadleaf. Orendil Broadleaf is a skilled night elf herbalist and healer stationed at Maestra's Post in western Ashenvale. Known for his deep knowledge of forest flora, he concocts vital remedies to save young lives across the troubled woodlands. Positioned at Maestra's Post along the western threshold of Ashenvale, Orendil Broadleaf tends to the sick as a skilled healer. Recognized for his masterful knowledge of local herbs and restorative craft, Orendil relies on passing travelers to gather rare natural reagents. Even as tension and conflict encroach upon the forest, his tireless focus remains on safeguarding his kin and soothing their ailments.

Orenthil Whisperwind. Orenthil Whisperwind is a night elf resident of Teldrassil, encountered beneath the boughs of Shadowglen. Orenthil Whisperwind resides among the night elves of Shadowglen, beneath the canopy of Teldrassil. Little is recorded about his personal history.

Orgnil Soulscar. Orgnil Soulscar is an orc investigator stationed at Razor Hill in central Durotar. He serves as an informal officer of the peace, coordinating defense and intelligence against internal threats to the fledgling nation. His primary concern is the shadow cast by the Burning Blade cult within Durotar's canyons. Positioned at Razor Hill, Orgnil Soulscar takes on the grim responsibility of tracking subversion and insidious threats across Durotar. While grunt patrols look outward toward Alliance footholds and centaur raiding parties, Orgnil focuses on rot brewing from within. He collects reports from scouts across the region, piecing together evidence of ritual corruption and illicit gatherings.

Orgrim Doomhammer. Orgrim Doomhammer was the supreme Warchief of the Old Horde throughout the Second War, remembered as one of the greatest orc warriors in history. Though he died liberating the internment camps in the Arathi Highlands, his legacy endures in the capital of Orgrimmar and through Thrall, who inherited his mighty warhammer and black plate armor. Originally second-in-command to Blackhand of the Blackrock clan, Orgrim refused the demonic blood offered by Gul'dan, though he concealed his doubts beneath fierce loyalty. Near the close of the First War, disgusted by the Shadow Council's treachery and the murder of his childhood friend Durotan, Orgrim slew Blackhand in honorable combat. Assuming the mantle of Warchief, he ruthlessly purged Gul'dan's warlocks and led the Horde across the Eastern Kingdoms during the Second War. Though a devastating strategist who pushed human kingdoms to the brink of ruin, he was ultimately defeated and captured outside Blackrock Spire after the betrayal of Gul'dan split his forces.

Ormak Grimshot. Ormak Grimshot is an experienced orc hunter trainer residing in the Hunter's Hall within Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. Accompanied by his loyal wolf, Grimfang, he instructs young hunters of the Horde in tracking, marksmanship, and bonding with wild beasts. Stationed within the Hunter's Hall in the Valley of Honor, Ormak Grimshot serves as a cornerstone of martial instruction for the Horde's trackers and marksmen. Alongside his companion wolf, Grimfang, Ormak imparts the foundational discipline needed to survive Kalimdor's harsh wilderness. For orc and troll hunters arriving from their trials in Durotar, he provides vital guidance on the sacred art of taming and commanding wild beasts, ensuring every hunter forms an enduring bond with their animal partner.

Ormer Ironbraid. Ormer Ironbraid is a dwarven archaeologist stationed at Whelgar's Excavation Site in the southern Wetlands. His team's historical research has been violently interrupted by ravenous raptors that overran the dig. Ormer seeks adventurous allies to clear out the beasts and avenge the miners driven from the site. Ormer Ironbraid arrived in the Wetlands as part of the dwarven effort to uncover Titan relics and ancient history at Whelgar's Excavation Site. Unfortunately, uncovering ancient stones also unearthed—or at least provoked—packs of fierce Wetlands raptors. Rather than cataloging ancient earthenware and tablets, Ormer spends his days watching the beasts prowl among the ruins, nursing a fierce hatred for the creatures that disrupted their work.

Orokk Omosh. Orokk Omosh is an aging orc blacksmith stationed in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. As the last heir to a storied lineage of smiths, he seeks worthy apprentices across the Horde to preserve his family's armoring secrets before they are lost to time. Standing beside the roaring forges in the Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh carries a heavy burden: he is the final smith of the venerable Omosh line. Having fathered no children to inherit his craft, Orokk refuses to let his family's hard-won techniques die with him. Instead, he invites capable Horde blacksmiths to undertake demanding trials of metalwork, promising to impart the revered secrets of Omosh armorcraft to those who prove their dedication.

Orphan Matron Battlewail. Orphan Matron Battlewail manages the Horde orphanage in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. Together with her fellow caretaker Tosamina, she shelters and raises young orc children who have lost their families to continuous warfare. War takes a constant toll across Azeroth, and the young capital of Orgrimmar bears witness to those costs. Orphan Matron Battlewail tends to the youngsters who lost their kin to violence, ensuring that the next generation of the Horde is protected, sheltered, and nurtured. Working alongside Tosamina in the Valley of Honor, Battlewail opens the orphanage doors to passing adventurers, especially during festive traditions like Children's Week when travelers are called upon to mentor these youths.

Orphan Matron Nightingale. Orphan Matron Nightingale oversees the Stormwind Orphanage located in Cathedral Square.
