Sputtervalve. Sputtervalve is a stressed goblin engineer stationed in the port town of Ratchet. Serving the Tinkers' Union under Director Riddlevox, he oversees regional shredder research and development under crushing corporate deadlines. To keep his standing, he frequently hires adventurers to engage in industrial espionage against the rival Venture Company. Operating out of Ratchet, Sputtervalve answers to Director Riddlevox of the Tinkers' Union. Put in charge of shredder development, he quickly discovered that keeping pace with modern mechanization is brutal work. Facing fierce competition and an unforgiving deadline, Sputtervalve found himself with few working prototypes of his own. Rather than admit failure to the Union, he turned toward the classic goblin solution: stealing better designs from whoever built them first.

Sten Stoutarm. Sten Stoutarm is a practical dwarven outfitter and courier stationed outside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. Responsible for keeping new recruits equipped and managing local dispatches, he helps ensure that novice mountaineers stay warm, fed, and informed despite the harsh mountain conditions. Positioned near the heart of Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm is one of the first friendly faces new dwarven and gnomish recruits encounter outside Anvilmar's tavern. With the valley isolated by winter blizzards and encroaching dangers, Sten takes it upon himself to outfit green apprentices with sturdy gear before they freeze or wander unprepared into the drifts.

Stitches. Stitches is a colossal, stitched-together undead abomination stalking Duskwood's main thoroughfare. His march threatens travelers, the Night Watch, and the town of Darkshire. Stitches is an undead abomination assembled from harvested corpses and unholy sorcery. Appearing near Abercrombie's shack northeast of Raven Hill Cemetery, the lumbering monstrosity immediately sets out eastward along the road toward Darkshire. Imbued with immense physical strength and relentless malice, Stitches tears through any Night Watch checkpoints stationed along the thoroughfare—including the defense camp across from Vul'Gol Ogre Mound and the outpost outside the Rotting Orchard—bringing outright slaughter to unwary travelers and town defenders alike.

Strahad Farsan. Strahad Farsan is a master human warlock who dwells in a secluded stone tower overlooking Ratchet in the Barrens. Renowned across faction lines, he operates outside conventional Alliance and Horde politics, training aspiring summoners in the dangerous arts of binding higher demons. Practitioners of fel magic from Stormwind, Orgrimmar, and the Undercity alike seek his severe guidance. Perched on the bluffs above the goblin port of Ratchet, Strahad Farsan's tower stands apart from the bustling trade docks below. Ratchet's neutrality offers Strahad the freedom to conduct perilous demonic summonings away from the prying eyes of Alliance magistrates or Horde shamans. Surrounded by his acolytes, he studies the deeper mysteries of the Twisting Nether in relative seclusion, unbothered by petty territorial squabbles.

Supervisor Raelen. Supervisor Raelen oversees timber operations at the Eastvale Logging Camp on the eastern edge of Elwynn Forest. She is responsible for managing the local laborers, maintaining daily logging quotas, and ensuring that harvested lumber safely makes its way into Stormwind's supply chains. Located in the heart of Eastvale Logging Camp near Marshal Patterson and the camp's wood wagons, Supervisor Raelen directs the labor force tasked with harvesting timber for the kingdom. Operating a lumber camp on the border of the Redridge Mountains carries significant logistical challenges, from coordinating weary woodcutters to dealing with wildlife and bandit interference that threatens production quotas. Despite the hazards of the surrounding woods, Raelen focuses squarely on getting timber gathered, processed, and bundled for transport.

Suzetta Gallina. Suzetta Gallina is a member of the Gallina family, purveyors of fine vintages in Stormwind City. She can be found inside the family's wine shop tucked along the Canals, helping manage the business and spread word of their stock to thirsty patrons across the city. Situated along the scenic waterways of Stormwind's Canal District, the Gallina Winery caters to citizens seeking quality vintages imported or crafted across the kingdom. Suzetta Gallina helps oversee daily life in the establishment, maintaining the family legacy of supplying taverns, nobles, and common folk with wine. While not a public figure of high politics, her presence represents the everyday commercial heartbeat that keeps the capital thriving amidst broader troubles.

Sven Yorgen. Sven Yorgen is a grieving farmer camped on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank in western Duskwood, accompanied by his companion Lars. Having survived the brutal slaughter of his family at the Yorgen Farmstead, Sven is consumed by a relentless drive to uncover who brought ruin upon his home and exact vengeance. Sven was born before the First War, old enough to recall the days before the region became shrouded in gloom following Medivh's fall. For years he worked the soil at the Yorgen Farmstead in southern Duskwood alongside his wife and children. That quiet existence ended in sudden violence when mysterious Dark Riders raided his homestead while he was away, butchering his family and turning the farm into a graveyard.

Sylvanas Windrunner. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner is the Banshee Queen and supreme ruler of the Forsaken, holding court in the Undercity beneath the ruins of Lordaeron. Once the brave Ranger-General of Silvermoon, she was slain and raised into undeath by Arthas Menethil before breaking free from the Lich King's grip. Now allied with Thrall's Horde out of mutual survival, she is fiercely dedicated to securing a future for her free-willed undead and exacting vengeance upon the Scourge. In life, Lady Sylvanas was the celebrated Ranger-General of Silvermoon, commanding the defense of Quel'Thalas during the Third War. When Prince Arthas Menethil marched the Scourge into the high elven kingdom to reach the Sunwell, Sylvanas fought fiercely to delay his advance. Frustrated by her resistance, Arthas murdered her, but denied her a clean death. He ripped her soul from her corpse and twisted it into a vengeful banshee, forcing her to serve the Scourge and assist in the slaughter of her own people.

Syral Bladeleaf. Syral Bladeleaf is a night elf resident of Dolanaar in Teldrassil who serves as a liaison for the Council of the Forest. She guides young adventurers who arrive from Shadowglen, directing them toward local caretakers, herbalists, and elders who watch over the crown's delicate boughs. Found standing near the heart of Dolanaar, Syral Bladeleaf helps organize local affairs in the shadow of Teldrassil's canopy. Acting on behalf of the Council of the Forest, she directs newly arrived night elves to community leaders and herbalists across the village and the nearby wilderness. Through her guidance, travelers connect with the botanist Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth and replenish supplies for the village elders.

Syurna. Syurna is a night elf rogue trainer found nestled among the foliage of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. She mentors aspiring scouts, spies, and covert operatives of the Kaldorei, guiding newly trained rogues on missions that test their stealth and cunning. While Darnassus celebrates the overt martial might of the Sentinels and the spiritual wisdom of the Sisterhood of Elune, the Kaldorei have always relied on shadows and stealth. Located in the Cenarion Enclave, Syurna acts as a trainer and mentor for those who walk an unseen path. She instructs rogues in the fine arts of evasion, lockpicking, and lethal strikes, ensuring that Darnassus possesses sharp eyes and silent blades to defend Teldrassil.

Tabetha. Tabetha is a reclusive, powerful human mage dwelling deep within Dustwallow Marsh at an isolated farmstead in the Quagmire. Far from the politics of Dalaran or Theramore, she instructs aspiring spellcasters and aids those seeking mastery over potent arcane and occult relics. Hidden away in the sodden expanse of Dustwallow Marsh north of the Stonemaul Ruins, Tabetha lives in a secluded shack alongside her apprentices. Surrounding herself with alchemical vials and ancient tomes, she has deliberately chosen solitude over the academic hierarchies of the Eastern Kingdoms. Despite her remote location, her mastery of the arcane is renowned enough that spellcasters across Kalimdor brave beasts and mire alike to seek her guidance.

Tai'jin. Tai'jin is a Darkspear troll priest trainer stationed within the barracks of Razor Hill in Durotar. She guides fledgling priests of the Horde, introducing Darkspear initiates to traditional troll rites such as the Hex of Weakness. Stationed inside the sturdy barracks of Razor Hill, Tai'jin serves as a spiritual mentor for young priests stepping out into Durotar. While orcs predominantly turn to shamanism or dark warlock arts, the Darkspear trolls bring their own distinct communion with the spirits and loas to the Horde. Tai'jin offers foundational teachings in the priesthood, ensuring that new acolytes understand both the balance of light and shadow and the spiritual heritage unique to troll culture.

Taiga Wisemane. Taiga Wisemane is a tauren elder residing in Shadowprey Village along the rugged western coast of Desolace. Watchful of demonic meddling across the barren wastes, he works to thwart the Burning Blade cult entrenched in the region. He directs Horde champions to disrupt demonic rituals and seal open gateways before the Burning Legion gains ground. Though Shadowprey Village is predominantly a Darkspear troll fishing settlement tucked away against the ocean, Taiga Wisemane has taken up station there to monitor the dark sorceries stirring across Desolace. He remains acutely aware of the spiritual corruption bleeding into the soil, keeping his focus fixed eastward where shadow cults and demonic remnants fester among ancient ruins.

Takar the Seer. Takar the Seer is an elusive human hermit encamped deep within the Barrens, east of Camp Taurajo. Despite sitting entirely within Horde-dominated territory, he maintains allegiance to the Alliance and assists certain travelers with esoteric occult knowledge. Dwelling alone beneath a simple tent east of Camp Taurajo, Takar the Seer seems out of place amid the dry plains of the Barrens. Surrounding lands are watched constantly by tauren braves and orc patrols, yet Takar remains undisturbed in his remote clearing. Hostile to curious Horde interlopers but rarely eager to initiate violence, he keeps a sharp eye on the horizon and prefers solitude. His isolated existence suggests deliberate seclusion, far from the bustling politics of Stormwind.

Takata Steelblade. Takata Steelblade is an orc warrior stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. Dispatched from Orgrimmar by Keldran alongside Maurin Bonesplitter, he spearheads the Horde's local campaign against demonic corruption. His primary focus is eradicating the regional satyr population affiliated with the sinister Burning Blade. Takata Steelblade was sent from the capital to Desolace under direct orders from Keldran, an influential figure in Orgrimmar committed to uncovering and purging demonic subversion. Operating out of the isolated Tauren encampment of Ghost Walker Post, Takata coordinates military efforts against the Legion-aligned forces plaguing the barren wastes.

Tal. Tal is the primary wind rider master of Thunder Bluff, tending the city's aerial roost high above the plains of Mulgore. He provides seasoned wyverns to Horde travelers looking to traverse the vast reaches of Kalimdor. Perched upon the central mesa of Thunder Bluff, Tal manages the vital aerial thoroughfare connecting the tauren capital to the rest of the Horde. From his perch, he tends to the loyal wind riders, or wyverns, ensuring they are healthy, well-fed, and prepared for long-distance journeys across Kalimdor's rugged landscapes. Whether sending messengers down to Camp Taurajo or dispatching scouts across the Barrens to Orgrimmar, Tal maintains an indispensable lifeline that keeps the towering mesa city in constant touch with its allies.

Talen. Talen is a night elf amateur archaeologist encamped near the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale. Despite the constant danger posed by nearby naga and Horde outposts, he is dedicated to recovering ancient kaldorei relics buried along the coast. Perched at a small camp on the edge of the Zoram Strand, Talen spends his days pursuing historical curiosities rather than waging war. While the wilderness of Ashenvale is fraught with territorial skirmishes and hostile shoreline denizens, Talen remains focused on gathering long-lost treasures from the ruins submerged beneath the waves and sands. He relies heavily on passing adventurers to brave the savage Wrathtail naga and retrieve elusive artifacts—including pristine statuettes and the Ring of Zoram held by the naga leader Ruuzel.

Tallonkai Swiftroot. Tallonkai Swiftroot is a night elf resident of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Concerned with the emerging corruption tainting the great boughs, he enlists young adventurers to recover enchanted relics and stem the foul forces plaguing the woods. Dwelling in the canopy settlement of Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot keeps a watchful eye over the surrounding woods. Like many night elves living beneath the boughs of the newly grown World Tree, he is alarmed by the unnatural agitation of the wildlife and the unsettling shadows gathering at the edges of their settlements.

Tallow. Tallow is a Forsaken warrior stationed in the fortified settlement of Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills. Serving the Dark Lady and the Horde, he watches over the contested front lines, helping organize strikes against local Alliance threats. Situated in the heart of Tarren Mill, Tallow stands among the Forsaken and Horde forces holding the line in the Hillsbrad Foothills. The region is a powder keg of conflict, caught between nearby Southshore humans, wandering Syndicate outlaws, and hostile wildlife. Tallow helps direct capable adventurers into the field, testing their strength against the Boulderfist ogres of the Arathi Highlands before sending them on to aid the besieged outpost of Hammerfall.

Talvash del Kissel. Talvash del Kissel is a down-on-his-luck gnome jeweler who fled the fall of Gnomeregan and now resides in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. Plagued by debt and persistent rumors following the loss of his home, he seeks capable adventurers to help recover lost treasures and restore shattered relics. His keen eye for precious gems and ancient baubles makes him a valuable contact for those plumbing the depths of Uldaman. Once a respected jeweler in the technological heart of Gnomeregan, Talvash saw his livelihood obliterated alongside his home when the troggs overran the underground city. Escaping with the surviving refugees to the dwarven capital of Ironforge, he set up camp in the Mystic Ward. Unfortunately, relocation did not treat him kindly. Rumors of questionable dealings and unpaid obligations quickly piled up, sinking the craftsman into deep financial distress. Unable to rebuild his trade through conventional means, Talvash relies on freelance adventurers to retrieve lost assets and salvage his ruined reputation.

Tammra Windfield. Tammra Windfield is a tauren resident of Sun Rock Retreat, nestled within the heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. Deeply attuned to the balance of the land, she guides Horde travelers in honoring the natural cycle of renewal and keeping hope alive amid the peaks. Her concerns lie with both the health of the untamed wilderness and the safety of her kin. Sun Rock Retreat serves as a vital sanctuary for the Horde within the craggy peaks of Stonetalon, surrounded by hostile harpies, Venture Company loggers, and lurking predators. Tammra Windfield stands among the settlement's caretakers, keeping a watchful eye on both the mountain wilderness and travelers who cross its threshold. Her gentle demeanor belies the resolve necessary to maintain a home in such rugged terrain.

Tannok Frosthammer. Tannok Frosthammer is a dwarven resident found at Thunderbrew Distillery outside Kharanos in Dun Morogh. He serves as an anxious recipient of goods coming from Coldridge Valley, deeply troubled by how trogg attacks have cut off the roads to Anvilmar. Stationed around the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Tannok Frosthammer keeps a watchful eye on incoming deliveries and local tidings. The sudden surge of troggs swarming Coldridge Pass has severed normal transit from Coldridge Valley, leaving Tannok cut off from regular communication with the settlement at Anvilmar. Relying on couriers like the gnome tinkerer Hands Springsprocket to ferry vital supplies and news through the perilous, snowy mountain pass, Tannok represents the quiet worry shared by many Bronzebeards as subterranean threats crawl closer to their doorsteps.

Taragaman the Hungerer. Taragaman the Hungerer is a hulking felguard lurking within the molten caverns of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. While widely feared as the demonic master behind the Searing Blade cult, his presence in the fiery depths serves a darker, more deceptive purpose. The Horde seeks his destruction to eliminate the demonic taint poisoning the city's underbelly. Prowling amidst the magma pools of Ragefire Chasm, Taragaman the Hungerer represents an immediate and terrifying threat to the safety of Orgrimmar. For many scouts and young warriors sent into the dark chasm, the demonic felguard appears to be the central ringleader of the Searing Blade cultists, wielding infernal strength to bend the weak-willed and corrupt the subterranean passages beneath Thrall's fortress.

Targorr the Dread. Targorr the Dread is an infamous Blackrock orc executioner imprisoned deep within the Stormwind Stockade. Known for his brutal tortures of captured Stormwind soldiers, his execution was indefinitely delayed by bureaucratic incompetence and corruption. When the Stockade erupted into revolt under the Defias Brotherhood, Targorr broke free and allied with the rioting convicts. Before his capture, Targorr the Dread served as the supreme executioner for the Blackrock clan under Warlord Gath'Ilzogg. Operating out of the occupied ruins in Redridge, his cruelty stood out as exceptionally savage even by the violent standards of the Dark Horde. Stormwind guards and militiamen who fought to defend the borderlands were subjected to agonizing torment and slow death at his hands, making his name one of the most reviled in the kingdom.

Tarindrella. Tarindrella is a dryad found watching over the sheltered woods of Shadowglen in Teldrassil. As a daughter of Cenarius, she works closely with night elf protectors to investigate the unnatural corruption afflicting the World Tree's wildlife. Dryads are fierce caretakers of nature, born of the demigod Cenarius. While many remain deep within ancient Kalimdor forests like Ashenvale, Tarindrella dwells in the protected glade of Shadowglen atop the boughs of Teldrassil. She acts as a vital bridge between the wild spirits and young night elf defenders taking their first steps outside Aldrassil. Her primary concern is the lingering taint creeping into the forest, tasking reliable adventurers with driving back local pests and gathering clues about the root of the affliction.

Tarrel Rockweaver. Tarrel Rockweaver is an anxious dwarven husband stationed on the bridge leading into Menethil Harbor. Deeply worried for his wife Merrin, an archaeologist who ventured inland with Whelgar's excavation team, he watches the road hoping for news of her safety. While trade and military shipments flow through Menethil Harbor, Tarrel Rockweaver keeps an anxious vigil at the bridge on the edge of town. His wife, Merrin Rockweaver, joined Prospector Whelgar's prestigious archaeological expedition deeper into the Wetlands. When violent raptors overran the excavation site and cut off regular communication, Tarrel was left stranded in town, begging passing travelers to scout east toward Whelgar's Excavation Site to ensure she survived the disaster.

Tatternack Steelforge. Tatternack Steelforge is an orc smith stationed out in the harsh savanna of the Barrens, offering work to travelers who can handle raw metal and dangerous frontier fauna. Adept in the ways of iron and fire, he looks to study local ores and arm Horde forces against threats across the plains. In the arid sprawl of the Barrens, keeping Horde outposts armed is no small task. Tatternack Steelforge brings the traditional metalworking expertise of his people to the frontier, seeking both practical weapons and unusual geological specimens to bolster the Horde's foothold against wild beasts, centaur raiders, and hostile quilboar.

Tavernkeep Smitts. Tavernkeep Smitts is the barkeep of the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. Operating at the social center of Duskwood, Smitts possesses an encyclopedic knowledge of town gossip and unsolved local tragedies. His long memory and keen eye make him an invaluable contact for anyone investigating the region's dark history. Behind the bar of the Scarlet Raven Tavern, Tavernkeep Smitts offers warm hearth fires and drink to the weary travelers, local townspeople, and nervous Night Watch guards braving Duskwood's perils. As one of the longest-standing public faces in town, Smitts hears every rumor that filters through the gloom. While other townsfolk shrink behind locked shutters, Smitts maintains a pragmatic, observant eye on everyone who passes through his door, noting unusual behavior, hurried departures, and strange patrons.

Telf Joolam. Telf Joolam is a Darkspear jungle troll shaman watching over the Shrine of the Dormant Flame. He guides initiates of the Horde through the trials required to commune with and command the volatile element of fire. Perched among the crags overlooking the borderlands, Telf Joolam tends the Shrine of the Dormant Flame. Unlike the calm certainty of earth or the patient depth of water, the fiery spirits require sharp discipline and unwavering focus. Telf acts as a trialmaster, preparing young shamans to prove their worth to the wild embers before they are consumed by them.

Tenaron Stormgrip. Tenaron Stormgrip is a night elf guide high within Aldrassil, the central tree of Shadowglen. He teaches young kaldorei the recent history of their people while asking them to gather moonwell water. Perched upon the winding wooden platforms of Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip stands as an early mentor to young night elves stepping forth from the boughs of Shadowglen. From his vantage point, he monitors the health of the local woods and the vital moonwells that sustain them. His role is to instruct novices in understanding their profound spiritual connection to the World Tree.

Terenthis. Terenthis is a night elf druid stationed in the coastal settlement of Auberdine. Representing the Cenarion Circle, he is investigating the alarming corruption spreading through Darkshore and Teldrassil. He enlists capable travelers to gauge rising threats along the coast and assist local allies trapped by corrupted wildlife. Sent to Auberdine by the Cenarion Circle, Terenthis focuses on tracking the spread of Fel Moss and other corruptive forces seeping into Darkshore from Teldrassil. The night elves view this creeping blight with immense concern, fearing the wild balance of northern Kalimdor may fracture completely if left unchecked. Terenthis works to uncover the root causes of the rot and devise ways to halt its advance before it consumes the forests.

Teronis' Corpse. Teronis' Corpse lies on a secluded island within Lake Falathim in western Ashenvale. Before his untimely demise, this night elf scout was dispatched from Astranaar on a crucial mission to recover Dartol's Rod to aid in cleansing the forest. Sent forth by Raene Wolfrunner from the settlement of Astranaar, Teronis was tasked with recovering the lost rod of Dartol, an ancient night elf relic capable of purifying corrupted woodland magic. His search brought him deep into the waters of Lake Falathim, but the journey turned fatal when hostile murlocs swarmed the island. Teronis fell in battle, leaving his journal behind and the rod's radiant gemstone plundered by the lake's aggressive amphibians.

Thadius Grimshade. Thadius Grimshade is a Wildhammer dwarf diviner dwelling within the mage tower of Nethergarde Keep in the Blasted Lands. Though he parted ways with Aerie Peak long ago to study esoteric and darker magical arts, he remains loyal to his kin at heart. Unlike most Wildhammer dwarves who prefer the open skies and roaring winds of the Hinterlands, Thadius Grimshade makes his home inside Nethergarde Keep. Driven by a thirst for arcane divination and darker mystic lore, he relocated to the edge of the tainted Blasted Lands to pursue his esoteric studies. Despite his brooding discipline and separation from his clan, he retains a deep fondness for his homeland and gryphonkind, offering his rare scrying talents to those who come seeking aid on behalf of Aerie Peak.

Thalia Amberhide. Thalia Amberhide is a tauren residing at Freewind Post in the jagged canyon of Thousand Needles. A loyal friend to her kin, she waits with mounting concern for the safe return of Lakota Windsong from the clutches of the Grimtotem clan. Perched atop the towering bluffs of Freewind Post, Thalia Amberhide is a quiet presence among the bustling tauren settlement. Her heart is heavy with worry for her close companion, Lakota Windsong, who was taken captive by Arnak Grimtotem and his treacherous kin. Thalia relies on passing Horde adventurers who brave the canyon depths to find Lakota, break her bonds, and guide her safely back up the lifts to the haven of the mesa.

Tharek Blackstone. Tharek Blackstone is a hardworking toolsmith residing in Kharanos, in the snowy heart of Dun Morogh. Known for supplying heavy hardware to local craftsmen, his primary patron is Beldin Steelgrill of Steelgrill's Depot. Though constantly busy at his trade, he also serves as a reliable point of contact for travelers seeking work around the settlement. Situated amidst the cold drifts of Kharanos, Tharek Blackstone keeps busy turning out reliable dwarven tools. Between repairing gear for the locals and supplying larger operations, he rarely finds a moment to rest. His biggest headache—and most reliable customer—is Beldin Steelgrill, whose mechanostrider depot just outside town demands a steady stream of heavy wrenches, gears, and replacement implements. To keep his forge running without falling behind on deliveries, Tharek often hires wandering travelers to haul newly finished tool crates over to the depot for him.

Tharnariun Treetender. Tharnariun Treetender is a night elf naturalist stationed in the coastal settlement of Auberdine in Darkshore. Dedicated to safeguarding the delicate balance of the wild, he monitors the creeping corruption afflicting the regional flora and fauna. Travelers passing through the port often find him calling upon allies to heal diseased beasts and protect nature from further decline. Perched on the rugged coast of Darkshore, the port town of Auberdine faces threats on multiple fronts, from hostile satyrs to foul shoreline washaways. Tharnariun Treetender focuses his efforts squarely on the natural world that surrounds the village. Firmly believing that neglecting nature invites ruin, he spends his time observing the decline of the local woods and seeking ways to push back the sickness spreading across the forest floor.

The Defias Traitor. The Defias Traitor is a captured outlaw held at the base of the Sentinel Hill watchtower in Westfall. Caught red-handed by the People's Militia, he traded the secret location of the Brotherhood's headquarters to save his own neck. Not every member of the Defias Brotherhood possesses fanatical loyalty to Edwin VanCleef's cause. When this petty thief was caught attempting to rob Farmer Saldean of his wagon, Gryan Stoutmantle's militia had him dead to rights. Facing the gallows, the thief chose self-preservation over brotherhood, offering up the exact whereabouts of their hidden base of operations in exchange for his life.

Theldurin the Lost. Theldurin the Lost is a reclusive, half-mad dwarf wandering the scorched expanses of the Badlands. Formerly aligned with the insidious Twilight's Hammer cult, he fled their ranks with stolen sacred relics after realizing the horror of their designs. Perched in the barren hills of the Badlands, clutching bags of explosives in wild paranoia, Theldurin is far more than a simple mad hermit. He was once an initiate of the Twilight's Hammer cult. When the sinister cabal sought to awaken a primordial elemental power trapped beneath the earth, Theldurin recoiled in terror, rejected their mad teachings, and fled into the desert. He carried with him the Scroll of Myzrael, desperate to prevent his former masters from unleashing an ancient horror upon the world. Though the escape cost him his sanity, his defiance dealt a serious blow to the cult's plans.

Theocritus. Archmage Theocritus is an eccentric human wizard who resides at the peak of the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest. He lives independently, surrounded by servants and magical scrying devices. From his high sanctum, Theocritus directs his arcane talents toward keeping watch over the kingdom and combating his dark rival, the rogue mage Morganth. Archmage Theocritus keeps an independent stronghold in the kingdom of Stormwind. He settled in the prominent Tower of Azora, situated near the eastern road to Redridge. Theocritus is known for his eccentric habits and comfortable lifestyle, employing an extensive household staff that includes numerous gnomish attendants and his own dedicated clothier, Morley Eberlein. Though he keeps himself largely detached from the mundane concerns of local villagers, his presence serves as a critical magical bulwark in eastern Elwynn.

Therylune. Therylune is a dryad found held captive at the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore. Entrapped by the insidious Twilight's Hammer cultists who have occupied the ancient site, she relies on bold travelers to help her break free and escape their clutches. Dryads are guardians of nature and daughters of Cenarius, normally roaming the tranquil woodlands of northern Kalimdor. However, Therylune ventured too close to the ominous excavation at the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, where Twilight's Hammer cultists have gathered. Ambushed and trapped by the dark cult, she is unable to fight her way out alone through the swarms of cultists and requires an escort to flee to safety.

Therysil. Therysil is a dryad dwelling at the Shrine of Aessina in central Ashenvale. Deeply devoted to the preservation of nature, she waits anxiously for word of her sister, Therylune, who fell into the hands of sinister cultists. Therysil makes her home near the tranquil waters of the Shrine of Aessina, a sacred glade within the ancient woods of Ashenvale. Like all dryads, the daughters of Cenarius, she is bound to the defense of the wild and the spirits dwelling within it. Yet her focus has been torn from quiet stewardship to gnawing worry. Her sister, Therylune, was captured nearby by the deranged Twilight's Hammer cult, leaving Therysil desperate for any wandering ally willing to aid in her sister's rescue.

Thor. Thor is the gryphon flight master stationed at the gryphon roost at Sentinel Hill in Westfall. As the vital aerial link between the beleaguered People's Militia and the capital city of Stormwind, he oversees the dispatch of couriers, scouts, and urgent messages across kingdom skies. Stationed at Sentinel Hill's gryphon roost, Thor manages the flight roost that ties Westfall's frontier defenders to the heart of the kingdom. While the People's Militia struggles on the ground against roaming bandits, gnolls, and malfunctioning harvest golems, Thor ensures that crucial military dispatches and travelers can bypass the perilous roads altogether. Through his tamed gryphons, urgent requests for aid and reports from Gryan Stoutmantle reach the court in Stormwind far quicker than any ground messenger could manage.

Thorgas Grimson. Thorgas Grimson is the resident dwarf hunter trainer stationed inside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. A seasoned outdoorsman of Dun Morogh, he firmly believes that hands-on survival in the freezing wilds is the finest teacher any fledgling marksman can have. Perched inside the stone halls of Anvilmar, Thorgas Grimson welcomes novice mountaineers and scouts taking their very first steps into the harsh snowdrifts of Coldridge Valley. Rather than bogging young hunters down with dry lectures, Grimson espouses a practical philosophy: real skill is forged out in the freezing winds, bow or gun in hand, tracking Dun Morogh's rugged beasts firsthand.

Thorgrum Borrelson. Thorgrum Borrelson is the dwarven gryphon master stationed above Thelsamar in Loch Modan. From his roost overlooking the settlement, he tends the aerial mounts that connect the valley to Ironforge and the surrounding mountain passes. Perched on the bluff rising immediately above Thelsamar, Thorgrum Borrelson handles aerial transport for the Alliance across Loch Modan. With trogg incursions and gnoll packs threatening overland paths, his trained gryphons provide vital transit over the jagged ridges. He maintains frequent connections back through the South Gate Pass to the Great Forge in Dun Morogh, as well as routes onward toward the Wetlands and beyond.

Thork. Thork is an orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads who oversees the settlement's local defenses. Charged with securing the bustling crossroads of the Barrens, he directs Horde adventurers to push back raiders and secure vital supply lines. The Crossroads serves as the beating heart of Horde transit in Kalimdor, connecting Durotar, Mulgore, and the wilds beyond. Holding it is no easy feat. Thork shoulders the responsibility of defending the town from constant external pressures. Between quilboar raids, centaur aggression, and marauding harpies, his forces are stretched thin, forcing him to rely on capable travelers and emerging champions to handle critical security tasks.

Thorvald Deepforge. Thorvald Deepforge is a dwarven weapon merchant stationed near the border pass in the Valley of Kings. He helps arm travelers and defenders securing the critical pathway between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Positioned within the towering monument of the Valley of Kings, Thorvald Deepforge serves the Alliance as a reliable arms dealer. The mountain passes connecting Khaz Modan's interior to the outlying territories are plagued by trogg incursions and roving wildlife, making well-forged steel essential for any Mountaineer or recruit on the road. Thorvald ensures that those arriving from Dun Morogh or heading deeper into Loch Modan carry the blades and axes needed to defend dwarven lands.

Thotar. Thotar is a seasoned orc hunter trainer stationed in the settlement of Razor Hill in Durotar. He guides aspiring Horde scouts and marksmen in the ancient traditions of tracking, archery, and bonding with wild beasts. For young orcs and trolls taking their first steps outside the Valley of Trials, he provides the foundational rites needed to master Kalimdor's rugged fauna. Perched within the fortified hub of Razor Hill, Thotar serves as a veteran instructor for marksmen of the Horde. While new recruits learn the very basics in the Valley of Trials, it falls to Thotar to guide hunters as they face the harsher predatory wilderness of Durotar. Drawing upon traditions passed down through countless generations of orcs, he teaches not only marksmanship, but the deeper respect required to live alongside and direct Kalimdor's deadliest creatures.

Thrall. Thrall is the Warchief of the Horde and the ruler of Durotar, holding court from the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar. Once a human slave raised to be an arena gladiator, he broke the chains of his people, rediscovered their ancient shamanic traditions, and led them across the Great Sea to build a new homeland. Born Go'el, the son of Frostwolf chieftain Durotan and Draka, Thrall was orphaned as an infant when his parents were murdered by Gul'dan's assassins. He was discovered by human commander Aedelas Blackmoore, who named him 'Thrall'—meaning slave—and raised him at Durnholde Keep as an arena fighter with an education in human tactics. Aided by his foster sister Taretha Foxton, Thrall eventually escaped his captors. Guided by the Frostwolf exile Drek'Thar, he cast aside demonic corruption to master the elemental spirits, becoming the first of a new generation of orcish shaman.

Thran Khorman. Thran Khorman is the resident dwarven warrior trainer stationed in Anvilmar, nestled within the snowy Coldridge Valley. He oversees the basic combat drilling for newly minted warriors stepping out into Dun Morogh. Standing near the training grounds of Anvilmar, Thran Khorman is tasked with turning raw dwarven recruits and visiting gnomes into disciplined combatants. He maintains a gruff, uncompromising demeanor toward anyone who lacks the grit for front-line fighting. In his eyes, even though the Third War has concluded, peace is merely an illusion: troggs encroach upon Coldridge Pass, and the mountains remain fraught with peril. He demands relentless practice with axe, mace, and shield so that Ironforge's defenders never grow dull.

Thunderaan. Prince Thunderaan is the ancient Prince of Air, a colossal elemental struck down and betrayed during the ancient wars between fire and wind. Consumed in part by Ragnaros the Firelord, his remnant essence was sealed into shattered bindings entrusted to the Firelord's lieutenants. Adventurers who recover these relics can seek out Highlord Demitrian in Silithus to unleash him once more. Long ago, during the Elemental Sundering—a five-thousand-year clash fought between the forces of fire and air deep within Azeroth—Ragnaros sought to destroy and consume Thunderaan. The Prince was ambushed and betrayed by Ragnaros's powerful lieutenants, Baron Geddon and Garr, before being struck down by the Firelord's hammer, Sulfuras. Although defeated, Thunderaan's essence proved too mighty for Ragnaros to fully absorb.

Thyn'tel Bladeweaver. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver is a night elf sentinel stationed at the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus. She is deeply troubled by the disappearance of Priestess Velinde Starsong and dispatches trusted Alliance adventurers to track down clues regarding her whereabouts. Through her inquiries, she seeks to piece together the unraveling mystery behind the Scythe of Elune. Standing watch over Darnassus from the Warrior's Terrace, Thyn'tel Bladeweaver represents the vigilant military arm of the kaldorei. When Priestess Velinde Starsong mysteriously vanished without leaving word, Thyn'tel refused to let the trail go cold. Sensing that grave forces were involved, she takes it upon herself to commission adventurers willing to dig into the priestess's personal belongings and uncover where her journey led.

Tirion Fordring. Tirion Fordring is a legendary paladin and former lord of Mardenholde Keep, now living in quiet exile in the Eastern Plaguelands. A paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand, he was stripped of his title and lands for honoring a debt of honor to an enemy orc. From his modest cabin along the Thondroril River, he watches over the tragedy unfolding across Lordaeron and worries for his son. Before the ruin of Lordaeron, Tirion Fordring was renowned as one of the kingdom's finest knights. A paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the order Archbishop Alonsus Faol founded during the Second War, Tirion fought the Old Horde with plate, hammer, and holy devotion. He was revered as an unyielding paragon of the Holy Light.

Tiza Battleforge. Tiza Battleforge is a veteran dwarven paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand stationed within Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries. Renowned for her steadfast devotion and insight, she guides young dwarven paladins along the path of virtue, charity, and self-sacrifice. Through study of the sacred texts and trials in the field, she tests whether initiates are truly ready to wield the Light's gift of resurrection. Within the serene chambers of the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge, Tiza Battleforge stands as one of the most respected dwarven paladins of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Initiates across the Alliance—directed by tutors such as Brandur Ironhammer in Ironforge, Azar Stronghammer in Dun Morogh, and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker in Stormwind—are sent to her to advance their spiritual education. Tiza believes that the Holy Light demands more than martial skill; it requires humble service, compassion, and unwavering fortitude against the encroaching darkness of the Scourge and other threats.

Tommy Joe Stonefield. Tommy Joe Stonefield is a young farmer caught in a bitter family rivalry in the heart of Elwynn Forest. Deeply in love with Maybell Maclure, he must rely on quiet riverbanks and secret messages to keep their romance hidden from their feuding kin. Standing by the riverbank just west of the Stonefield Farm, Tommy Joe Stonefield spends his days looking across the water toward the Maclure homestead. The Stonefields and Maclures have harbored bad blood for years, clashing over land, pride, and petty farmyard squabbles. Yet despite the hostility preached by his elders, Tommy Joe has fallen head over heels for Maybell Maclure. Unable to meet openly without sparking outrage from both households, he depends on trusted intermediaries and his sympathetic grandmother, Gramma Stonefield, to exchange secret notes and tokens of affection.

Tonga Runetotem. Tonga Runetotem is a knowledgeable tauren druid stationed outside the inn at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Dispatched from Thunder Bluff, he investigates an unnatural corruption seeping into the region's sparse oases and sickening the native wildlife. His research aims to trace the spiritual disturbance back to its origin before the delicate ecosystem collapses entirely. Amid the dust and bustling commerce of the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem keeps a quiet vigil. Sent down from the high mesas of Mulgore by his elders in Thunder Bluff, Tonga possesses an intimate understanding of the arid savannah. Where others see only barren scrub and predatory beasts, he reads the subtle currents of the land's health. In recent times, those currents have soured dramatically, compelling him to recruit capable travelers to investigate the heart of the savannah's life: its isolated oases.

Tormus Deepforge. Tormus Deepforge is a dwarven smith working at the center of the Great Forge in Ironforge. A dependable craftsman, he coordinates iron deliveries and supplies armaments for Alliance defense efforts across Khaz Modan and beyond. Positioned right beside the roaring fires of the Great Forge, Tormus Deepforge oversees substantial metalworking tasks on behalf of the Bronzebeard clan. Beyond hammering steel himself, Tormus mourns his mentor, Sturgy Ironband, whose smithing compound south of Helm's Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh was overrun by Dark Iron dwarves after a load of strange umbral ore arrived there.

Torwa Pathfinder. Torwa Pathfinder is a lone tauren hunter and tracker camped at the entrance to Un'Goro Crater, just below the ramp descending from Tanaris. He observes the basin's primordial wildlife, studying the dangerous predators that rule the jungle floor. Adventurers seeking to test their mettle against the crater's legendary beasts often seek his guidance. Perched at the eastern base of the crater where the desert sands of Tanaris give way to humid jungle steam, Torwa Pathfinder serves as an informal warden for newcomers. He respects the wild forces of Un'Goro, understanding that careless wanderers quickly become fodder for the local fauna. His campsite provides a rare moment of respite before travelers dive into the sweltering depths.

Treshala Fallowbrook. Treshala Fallowbrook is a night elf residing quietly on the upper level of the Tradesmen's Terrace in Darnassus. She is the wife of Heralath Fallowbrook, whose work has taken him far from home into the thorny depths of Razorfen Kraul in the Barrens. Treshala Fallowbrook keeps a modest vigil on the second floor of a workshop in Darnassus's Tradesmen's Terrace. Her husband, Heralath, journeyed to the brambled depths of Razorfen Kraul in the Barrens, and she waits at home for word of him. The two are joined by a pendant of bonding, a keepsake of their marriage that Heralath carried with him into the quilboar's warrens.

Tsunaman. Tsunaman is a sentient water elemental stationed at Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. Acting as an agent of the Tribunal of the Tides, he watches over the elemental currents of Kalimdor and rallies Horde adventurers to confront corrupting forces. Dwelling near the path leading from Sun Rock Retreat down into the Charred Vale, Tsunaman serves the Tribunal of the Tides, high-ranking servants aligned with the Tidehunter, Neptulon. Rather than showing mindless hostility to mortal travelers, he cooperates with the Horde to monitor elemental unrest throughout Kalimdor, particularly the disturbances rippling out of the submerged caverns of Blackfathom Deeps.

Turak Runetotem. Turak Runetotem is a revered tauren druid trainer residing in the Hall of Elders atop Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise. Serving as a trusted assistant to Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem, he guides novice tauren along the sacred paths of nature and balance. Through Turak, young druids undertake foundational trials to commune with spirits and master animal aspects. Within the serene confines of the Hall of Elders, Turak Runetotem stands as one of the Horde's foremost druidic mentors. Renowned for his deep patience and balanced demeanor, he assists Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem in reviving the ancient druidic arts among the tauren people. Turak ensures that every aspiring druid honors the will of the Earthmother, teaching that physical power must always be grounded in spiritual respect and harmony with nature.

Twilight Lord Kelris. Twilight Lord Kelris is an orc warlock and high-ranking leader within the Twilight's Hammer cult operating deep inside Blackfathom Deeps. From his perch in the Moonshrine Sanctum, he leads dark rituals in worship of the primordial hydra Aku'mai, aiming to usher in a reign of cosmic chaos. Twilight Lord Kelris directs the cultists of the Twilight's Hammer who seized the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. For years, Kelris slipped through the grasp of watchful eyes in Darnassus, evading the Argent Dawn and earning a grim reputation: whenever ancient malice stirred across Kalimdor, Kelris was suspected of orchestrating it. Rather than serving warlords or clans, this orc has pledged himself entirely to the Old Gods, seeking to unmake mortal civilization and return Azeroth to a state of absolute, primordial chaos.

Tyrande Whisperwind. Tyrande Whisperwind is the High Priestess of Elune and the supreme leader of the night elves. Alongside her beloved, the Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage, she guided her people through the cataclysmic War of the Ancients and ten millennia of the Long Vigil. Now governing from the sacred boughs of Teldrassil, she commands the Sisterhood of Elune and directs the Sentinel army in defense of Kalimdor's sacred wilderness. Born in the ancient kaldorei empire, Tyrande grew up alongside the twin brothers Malfurion and Illidan Stormrage. While the brothers followed druidism and sorcery, Tyrande entered the service of Elune as a priestess. When the demonic Burning Legion first invaded Azeroth during the War of the Ancients, she stood against it at Malfurion's side. Blessed with direct favor from the Moon Goddess, Tyrande transformed the Sisterhood into a radiant fighting force, wielding both divine restoration and searing lunar wrath to deliver her people from the brink of total annihilation.

Tyrion. Tyrion is a covert gnome operative stationed inside Stormwind Keep. Operating in the shadows alongside close associates like Elling Trias, he aids adventurers in unearthing sensitive intelligence and combating treacherous plots against the kingdom. Amid the grandeur of Stormwind Keep, Tyrion keeps a low profile. While noble courtiers and royal guards bustle through the halls, this clever gnome operates under the radar, watching palace movements and liaising with outside contacts who operate far from official oversight.

Ukor. Ukor is an orc peon resting near the eastern path outside the Valley of Trials in Durotar. Eager to help his people, he carried supplies all the way from Razor Hill, only to find the training grounds already had plenty of provisions. While many orc peons spend their lives under the watchful eye of harsh taskmasters cutting lumber or hauling rocks, Ukor attempted to perform a service of his own initiative. Tasked or inspired to bring food from Razor Hill to the recruits training in the Valley of Trials, he made the dangerous trek across Durotar's red plains past prowling scorpid and boars. Upon arrival, he discovered the Valley was already well-stocked and had no need for his bundle. Exhausted and somewhat disheartened by the roadside, he relies on passing young adventurers to return the unused provisions back north to Innkeeper Grosk.

Ula'elek. Ula'elek is a Darkspear troll smith residing in Sen'jin Village along the southern coast of Durotar. Working in tandem with the veteran orc smith Thun'grim Firegaze, he crafts specialized armor for Horde warriors striving to prove their worth. His work combines traditional troll craftsmanship with exotic trophies gathered from across Kalimdor. Ula'elek plies his craft amid the huts and braziers of Sen'jin Village, serving the Darkspear tribe as a skilled armorsmith. In a coastal settlement constantly threatened by nearby hostile quilboar and sea crawlers, keeping working blades and sturdy armor ready is vital to the tribe's survival. However, Ula'elek's renown extends beyond local defense, drawing the attention of seasoned warriors across the Horde.

Umpi. Umpi is a frog residing in Tarren Mill as the unwitting laboratory assistant of Apothecary Lydon. Kept inside the Royal Apothecary Society's workshop, she serves as a recurring test subject for experimental toxins and plague concoctions. Within the dark laboratories of Tarren Mill, the Forsaken work tirelessly to brew concoctions of death and torment. For Apothecary Lydon, scientific rigor requires living flesh to test his formulas, and Umpi bears the brunt of these trials. Lydon regularly tests lethal brews—such as the Elixir of Suffering and the Elixir of Agony—directly on her. Once the poisons take their inevitable toll and kill her, the apothecary re-animates the amphibian, ensuring she is ready to endure the next lethal dose for the glory of the Royal Apothecary Society.

Undertaker Mordo. Undertaker Mordo is the caretaker of the crypt of Deathknell, serving as the very first face newly awakened Forsaken see when they open their eyes. He tells those who wake that they are the Lich King's slaves no more and sends them on toward the Forsaken cause; the bodies that never stir go to the fire. Keeping the crypt of Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades, Undertaker Mordo watches over the dead as corpses break free from the Scourge's shattered grip. For every newly liberated Forsaken who wakes in the cold of the crypt, Mordo provides their initial bearing in an unrecognizable second life. He assesses their sanity, introduces them to the reality of their condition, and immediately directs them toward duty under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner.

Ur'kyo. Ur'kyo is a revered jungle troll priest trainer located in the Valley of Spirits within Orgrimmar. Known as the spiritual leader and greatest priest among the Darkspear tribe, he guides fledgling practitioners of the spiritual arts in the capital of the Horde. Through his council, priests learn to commune with the spirits and balance the powerful forces of shadow and light. Residing in the serene waters and huts of the Valley of Spirits, Ur'kyo stands as one of the most prominent spiritual authorities in Orgrimmar. For the Darkspear trolls who fled the Echo Isles and forged a home in Durotar alongside Thrall's Horde, maintaining their sacred traditions is essential. Ur'kyo preserves these ancestral practices, serving as a pillar of spiritual discipline and guidance for tribal mystics and visiting practitioners alike.

Uzzek. Uzzek is a battle-hardened orc veteran stationed just southwest of the Far Watch Post in the Barrens. Having survived countless skirmishes across Kalimdor, he now helps evaluate and temper promising Horde warriors who journey through the arid plains. Perched southwest of Far Watch Post along the eastern border of the Barrens, Uzzek represents the enduring grit of the Horde's frontline fighters. Having endured brutal combat throughout the recent wars, he serves as an instructor and trial-giver to younger warriors seeking to master their defensive disciplines. To prove oneself to Uzzek requires testing one's mettle against the savage wildlife and raiders that plague the arid crossing.

Valstag Ironjaw. Valstag Ironjaw is an Ironforge dwarven soldier stationed within Menethil Keep in the coastal marshlands of the Wetlands. Facing the pressing dangers that plague the trade passages connecting Loch Modan and the coast, he assists in securing regional routes and keeping the harbor's garrison informed of local threats. Found inside Menethil Keep in Menethil Harbor, Valstag Ironjaw serves as part of the dwarven garrison keeping watch over the lowlands. The surrounding marsh is rife with danger, from hostile Dragonmaw orcs to ravenous wildlife, making communications and supply lines difficult to maintain. Valstag helps coordinate defense efforts along the primary thoroughfares, particularly the treacherous passage cutting through Dun Algaz toward Loch Modan.

Vanndar Stormpike. Vanndar Stormpike is a fierce dwarf mountain king who commands the Stormpike Expedition from the northern fortress of Dun Baldar. Searching the frozen peaks of Alterac Valley for ancient relics and raw resources, he leads the Alliance's unyielding war against the Frostwolf orcs. A veteran mountain king of Ironforge, Vanndar Stormpike spearheads the dwarven excavation into Alterac Valley. Following the Third War, he marched the Stormpike Guard into the northern mountains seeking hidden mineral riches and long-lost titan artifacts. Settling into the fortified redoubt of Dun Baldar, Vanndar views the valley as an ancestral right and rightful Alliance territory. He directs military outposts, defensive bunkers, and frontline pushes with grim dwarven resolve, determined that no retreat will ever be sounded under his watch.

Varimathras. Varimathras is a dreadlord of the nathrezim race who serves as the chief lieutenant and military advisor to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Forced to pledge loyalty to the Banshee Queen after suffering defeat during the civil war for Lordaeron, he now stands at her right hand in the Royal Quarter of the Undercity. Before the Third War, Kil'jaeden sent Varimathras and his fellow dreadlords to Azeroth as the Lich King's jailors, to make sure the spirit of Ner'zhul served the Legion's plans. Bound alongside his brothers Detheroc and Balnazzar, he oversaw the Scourge in Lordaeron while Archimonde invaded Kalimdor. When the Legion fell at Mount Hyjal, the triumvirate remained entrenched in the ruins of the Capital City, entirely unaware of their master's demise until Prince Arthas returned to drive them into hiding.

Varok Saurfang. High Overlord Saurfang is a legendary orc warrior and a veteran of the Old Horde's wars. Serving as Warchief Thrall's trusted military commander in Orgrimmar, he represents the proud martial spine of the modern Horde. Few living warriors possess a martial pedigree to rival Saurfang. A veteran of the Old Horde's wars, he is considered an unstoppable force on the battlefield. Today he stands in Orgrimmar as High Overlord, a bulwark of Thrall's newborn Horde.

Velarok. Velarok Windblade is a lone human swordsman camped amid the ash and cinder of Searing Gorge, flanked by the mutilated corpses of Dark Iron dwarves. He seeks vengeance against the local Dark Irons for the brutal murder of his father, recruiting passing travelers to forge a weapon of retribution. His single-minded hunger for vengeance drives everything he asks of those who help him. Found southeast of Thorium Point, Velarok Windblade presents himself as a grieving human warrior stranded in the perilous wastes of the Searing Gorge. Surrounding his camp are the bloody, battered corpses of Dark Iron dwarves who crossed his blade. According to Velarok, these clan dwarves slaughtered his father in cold blood. Consumed by hatred, he enlists travelers to gather materials to assemble the Torch of Retribution, an enchanted weapon of vengeance against the Dark Irons and the minions of Ragnaros.

Velora Nitely. Velora Nitely is an undead armorsmith residing in the Trade Quarter of the Undercity. Renowned as one of the finest smiths in Lordaeron before the kingdom fell, she now puts her cold craftsmanship to work for the Forsaken and the Horde. Despite her grim existence, she attempts dry, deadpan jokes that rarely land. Before the Third War devastated the north, Velora Nitely was celebrated across Lordaeron as an exceptional armorsmith. Though undeath stripped her of life and warmth, it left her technical skill untouched. Now stationed near the anvils of the Undercity's Trade Quarter, she collaborates across continents with Horde crafters like Thun'grim Firegaze in the Barrens. Her specialty includes reinforcing heavy battle plate, notably forging the formidable Brutal Legguards from hardened materials such as Dragonmaw shinbones.

Ventaari Brightwish. Ventaari Brightwish is a Skyborne resident of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. She greets travelers from across Azeroth and offers the quest The Gift of Skysight. Residing in Thendal Village upon the soaring cliffs of Zephras Isle, Ventaari Brightwish is one of the local Skyborne. While she shares a surname with Belathaan Brightwish, her own duties center around aiding newcomers who find their way to the village, extending hospitality to both the Alliance and the Horde as she initiates visitors into the traditions of her people through tasks like The Gift of Skysight.

Verdan the Everliving. Verdan the Everliving is a colossal bog beast lurking deep within the verdant tunnels of the Wailing Caverns. He dwells amid the nightmare spreading from the sleeping druid Naralex, alongside the corrupted Druids of the Fang, and violently attacks any who venture into his damp hollows. Verdan is a hulking bog beast, an elemental of foliage, silt, and mire that lurks in the overgrown depths of the Wailing Caverns. Nothing is known of him from before the caverns fell to corruption; he is simply the largest and most dangerous creature in their lush, flooded hollows.

Verna Furlbrow. Verna Furlbrow is an evicted farmer currently stranded beside her broken-down wagon near the northern border of Westfall. After bandits seized her family's pumpkin patch, she and her husband attempted to flee toward Elwynn Forest, only to find themselves stuck on the dangerous open road. Verna and her husband once worked their own pumpkin farm in northern Westfall, but the rising tide of lawlessness sweeping the countryside drove them out. When outlaws overran their land, the couple piled what possessions they could onto their cart and hitched up their faithful horse, Old Blanchy, intending to escape to the safety of Elwynn Forest. Disastrously, their wagon broke down just down the road from the abandoned Jansen Stead. With no means to repair the axle or move forward, Verna has been left to endure the elements, bandit raids, and scavengers while relying on traveling adventurers to keep her household fed and guarded.

Verner Osgood. Verner Osgood is the resident blacksmith of Lakeshire, stationed just outside the town smithy. Balancing local civilian trade with the crushing demands of the Stormwind military, he works tirelessly to keep horses shod and defenders armed amid relentless gnoll raids. Standing by the forge in central Lakeshire, Verner Osgood represents the strained industrial backbone of the Redridge Mountains. Tasked with crafting basic supplies like horseshoes for local mounts, Verner finds his stock constantly co-opted to manufacture weapons and armor for the Stormwind Guard. With the kingdom stretching its borders thin and local garrisons lacking supplies, independent smiths like Verner must carry the logistical burden of the realm's defense.

Veron Amberstill. Veron Amberstill is a dwarven ram breeder residing at Amberstill Ranch in eastern Dun Morogh. He tends to the rugged mountain rams that serve as the traditional mounts of Ironforge and offers them to skilled riders who have earned his trust. Tucked away in the snow-dusted hills of eastern Dun Morogh, Veron Amberstill oversees the celebrated stock of Amberstill Ranch. Mountain rams are perfectly suited for Khaz Modan's treacherous slopes, sure-footed and thick-coated against the bite of mountain blizzards. Veron breeds and trains these beasts to carry dwarven scouts, mountaineers, and traveling adventurers. While he gladly provides standard and swift mounts to fellow dwarves, outsiders must prove their unwavering loyalty to the throne of Ironforge before he will part with any of his prized herd.

Veronica Nials. Captain Veronica Nials is an officer of the Stromgarde military stationed at Refuge Pointe in the Arathi Highlands. Amid the kingdom's collapse, she coordinates defensive operations against the Syndicate and ogres that overrun the fallen capital. Following the Third War, the human kingdom of Stromgarde shattered, leaving its remnants struggling to survive against invading Boulderfist ogres and the treachery of the Syndicate. Captain Veronica Nials stands as one of the central commanders of the surviving Stromgarde defenders at Refuge Pointe. Tasked with holding the line, she directs Alliance champions against key Syndicate leadership, such as Lord Falconcrest and the warlock Marez Cowl, while striving to recover fallen soldiers' badges so their grieving families can find closure.

Vesprystus. Vesprystus is the night elf flight master stationed at the docks of Rut'theran Village at the base of Teldrassil. He oversees the roost of trained hippogryphs that carry travelers between the great World Tree and mainland Kalimdor. Perched at the southern base of Teldrassil in Rut'theran Village, Vesprystus tends the hippogryphs that bridge the isolated elven boughs to the rest of the world. While a magical portal connects Rut'theran directly to the canopy city of Darnassus above, hippogryph flights provide a swift crossing toward Darkshore and the mainland. Vesprystus works in coordination with the flight master at Auberdine across the strait, ensuring safe passage for sentinels, emissaries, and adventurers journeying into Kalimdor.

Vidra Hearthstove. Vidra Hearthstove is a dwarven cook residing in the Stoutlager Inn in Thelsamar. Known for preparing local specialties, she frequently relies on traveling adventurers to gather regional ingredients for her famous blood sausages. Within the bustling warmth of the Stoutlager Inn, Vidra Hearthstove tends the kitchen and helps feed the locals and travelers passing through Loch Modan. Sharing a surname with the innkeeper, she keeps Thelsamar well-provisioned. Her signature dish, Thelsamar blood sausages, is a hearty dwarven staple that requires fresh game meats gathered from the surrounding wilderness, including boar entrails, spider ichor, and bear meat.

Viktori Prism'Antras. Viktori Prism'Antras is an eccentric stargazer residing in a small hillside hut overlooking Darkshire. While the town around him succumbs to dread and looming horrors, Viktori focuses intently on building a telescope to view the heavens clearly. To realize his vision, he relies on adventurous travelers to acquire intricate parts based on gnomish schematics. Perched up the slope just beyond the gryphon roost, Viktori Prism'Antras spends his days peering outward from the gloom of Duskwood. Amid undead incursions, ravenous spiders, and creeping shadows, his obsession lies far beyond the suffocating canopy. He dreams of building a magnificent optical telescope capable of bringing the stars into brilliant focus, offering a quiet escape from the dread that engulfs the hamlet.

Viscous Fallout. Viscous Fallout is a toxic water elemental wandering the irradiated corridors of Gnomeregan, a living mass of the poison that fouled the city after Mekgineer Thermaplugg's devastating radiation release. When Gnomeregan was flooded with radiation on Mekgineer Thermaplugg's treacherous advice to wipe out the invading troggs, the fallout left the city's lower levels awash in toxic slime and contamination. Viscous Fallout is a water elemental of that poisoned depth, its very substance thick with the city's toxic waste. Where it came from before the fall is not known.

Vol'jin. Vol'jin is the chieftain of the Darkspear trolls and a master shadow hunter. Residing in Grommash Hold alongside Warchief Thrall, he acts as a trusted advisor to the Horde while working to secure his displaced people a permanent home in Durotar. Vol'jin took up leadership of the Darkspear tribe following the tragic death of his father, Sen'jin, on their ancestral island home. When sea witch-worshipping murlocs and human forces nearly destroyed the isolated tribe, Thrall's orcs intervened, forging a deep bond between the two peoples. After evacuating the ruins of their islands, Vol'jin pledged his trolls to the New Horde and brought them across the Great Sea to Kalimdor.

Volcor. Volcor is an injured night elf scout stranded deep within Blackwood Den in southern Darkshore. Trapped by hostile Blackwood furbolgs, he relies on his faithful companion Grimclaw and the aid of Auberdine's defenders to escape. While tracking the corrupted Blackwood tribe in their subterranean lair, Volcor was ambushed and severely wounded. Unable to fight his way past the hostile furbolgs on his own, he sent his loyal bear companion, Grimclaw, out into the wilds of Darkshore to seek help from the settlement of Auberdine.

Vorn Skyseer. Vorn Skyseer is a peaceful tauren resident of Camp Narache atop Red Cloud Mesa in Mulgore. Resting among the camp's tents, he greets young adventurers beginning their journeys and introduces them to local life. Situated in Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa, Vorn Skyseer serves as an informal welcoming presence for young tauren. As they undertake their rites of passage before venturing into the wider valleys of Mulgore, Vorn offers kind words and hospitality, helping new arrivals settle into the camp.

Warcaller Gorlach. Warcaller Gorlach is an orc herald roaming the dusty streets of Orgrimmar, calling champions of the Horde to distant battlefronts. True to his title, he rallies travelers and seasoned warriors to answer commands in perilous outposts across Kalimdor and beyond. Patrolling the thoroughfares of Orgrimmar, Warcaller Gorlach serves as a primary herald for the Horde's expansion and strategic defenses. Rather than staying confined to a garrison desk, he marches among the citizenry, issuing orders directly to volunteers ready to test their mettle. Whether dispatching hunters into the contested canopy of Ashenvale, directing scouts toward the wilderness of Camp Mojache in Feralas, or issuing desperate calls to arms for distant campaigns like the Plaguelands, Gorlach ensures that no warrior lingering in the capital remains idle while the Horde faces threats abroad.

Warden Thelwater. Warden Thelwater is the besieged overseer of the Stockade, Stormwind City's underground maximum-security prison. Caught unprepared when a violent riot erupted among the Defias prisoners, he now desperately recruits capable adventurers to quell the rebellion before word spreads to the city above. Hidden beneath the canals of Stormwind, the Stockade holds the kingdom's most dangerous miscreants, petty thieves, and political conspirators. Warden Thelwater was charged with keeping them securely locked away, but an organized revolt took the guards completely off guard. With the prisoners overwhelming security and taking control of the cells, Thelwater found himself barricaded at the threshold, struggling to contain an armed insurrection right beneath the streets of the capital.

Warlord Goretooth. Warlord Goretooth is the commanding orc officer stationed at Kargath in the dusty wastes of the Badlands. From his watchtower, he coordinates the Horde's frontier campaigns against the neighboring Dark Iron dwarves and monitors the volcanic menace of Blackrock Mountain. Though strict in military matters, he can occasionally be found relaxing around the camp's bonfire. Perched atop the watchtower of Kargath, Warlord Lunk Goretooth directs Horde operations on the hostile eastern frontier. Kargath serves as Orgrimmar's primary staging ground against the threats lurking within Blackrock Mountain and the surrounding ravines. Goretooth oversees patrols, coordinates scout forces like the Kargath Expeditionary Force, and issues direct kill orders targeting the Dark Iron clan's ranks and leadership. When he descends from his lookout, the stern commander shows a lighter side, frequently warming himself by the camp bonfire and trading quips with the camp's Forsaken casters before returning to duty.

Warmaster Laggrond. Warmaster Laggrond is a seasoned orc commander stationed outside the Horde entrance to Alterac Valley in the Alterac Mountains. He oversees recruitment and frontline recognition for warriors answering the call to aid the Frostwolf clan. Through his trials, fighters prove their mettle and earn the respect of the Horde vanguard. Standing watch in the bitter cold at the threshold of Alterac Valley, Warmaster Laggrond organizes the Horde's war effort against the Stormpike Expedition. He ensures that only capable fighters enter the valley to represent the Frostwolf clan and the wider Horde.

Warsong Outrider. Stationed along the contested road leading east from Ashenvale into Azshara, the Warsong Outrider keeps watch over the Horde's frontier. She serves as an advanced scout for the Warsong clan, monitoring travelers and relaying crucial intelligence back to their forward encampments. Although armed and vigilant against night elf incursions, she maintains a passive watch unless directly provoked. The borderlands between Ashenvale and the shattered ruins of Azshara are fraught with danger. Operating far from the fortified safety of Splintertree Post or the lumber camps, the Warsong Outrider observes troop movements and patrols the transit corridor. Armed with a bow and toxic stingers, she stands ready to defend the Horde's claim over the region, though she conserves her strength by only firing upon Alliance trespassers who actively attack her.

Watch Captain Parker. Guard Parker is a vigilant town guardsman stationed at the Three Corners outpost in the Redridge Mountains. Tasked with patrolling the roads and monitoring aggressive gnoll packs, he serves as an early line of defense for travelers heading into Lakeshire. Positioned at the vital junction known as Three Corners, Parker keeps watch over the roads connecting Elwynn Forest, Duskwood, and Redridge. With Stormwind's military resources stretched thin and little official reinforcement reaching the region, solo watchmen like Parker carry the burden of keeping the crossroads clear of bandits, prowling predators, and raiding gnolls.

Watcher Backus. Watcher Backus is a member of the Night Watch tasked with patrolling the shadowy roads of Duskwood. Stationed along the thoroughfare between Darkshire and Manor Mistmantle, he keeps a weary eye out for lurking undead and strange travelers. His post also makes him a vital contact for those investigating suspicious movements tied to Stormwind's political intrigues. Like the rest of the Night Watch, Watcher Backus faces an uphill struggle against the cursed woodland. Duskwood receives little support from the Stormwind garrison, leaving local volunteers to guard the misty paths on their own. Backus walks a solitary beat along the road leading north out of Darkshire, passing near the eerie Manor Mistmantle while keeping beast and ghoul at bay.

Watcher Dodds. Watcher Dodds is a human scout of the Night Watch stationed at the central crossroads of Duskwood. Manning a lonely roadside outpost far from Darkshire's town walls, he monitors the encroaching horrors and tasks travelers with culling the local giant spider population. Watcher Dodds serves the Night Watch under Commander Althea Ebonlocke, holding down an exposed post at the intersection connecting Darkshire to Raven Hill and Deadwind Pass. While Darkshire huddles within its palisades, forward sentries like Dodds live on the knife's edge between wolf packs, ravenous ghouls, and oversized arachnids. From his roadside camp, he keeps an eye on approaching threats and enlists wandering mercenaries to thin out the spiders crawling out from the undergrowth before they completely overrun the overgrown thoroughfares.

Wilder Thistlenettle. Wilder Thistlenettle is a dwarven miner brooding in a tavern within Stormwind's Dwarven District. The sole survivor of a tragic cave-in deep within the Deadmines, he is haunted by the gruesome fate of his mining company and his brother. Wilder Thistlenettle can be found drowning his sorrows in an alehouse near the southeastern gates of the Dwarven District. Years ago, he joined an expedition into the deep lodes of Moonbrook's Deadmines alongside his brother and their companions. A catastrophic cave-in sealed the rest of the crew in the dark while Wilder barely made it to the surface alive.

Wiley the Black. Wiley the Black is an elusive rogue currently lying low at the Lakeshire Inn in Redridge. Though shady and reticent, he owes a life-debt to Gryan Stoutmantle and serves as a vital underworld contact regarding the Defias Brotherhood. Tucked away inside the Lakeshire Inn, Wiley the Black keeps a low profile away from the open turmoil of Westfall and the gnoll-infested borders of Redridge. Despite his roguish nature and questionable past, Wiley is bound by honor to Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia. Stoutmantle once saved Wiley's life—though Stoutmantle grumbles that he should have let the scoundrel rot when he had the chance. When the People's Militia desperately needs insight into the inner workings of the Defias conspiracy, Wiley is the informant they turn to, reluctantly parting with covert intelligence to clear his debt.

Willem. Deputy Willem is a human soldier of the Stormwind Army stationed directly outside Northshire Abbey. Serving under Marshal McBride, he acts as the primary field liaison directing new recruits to handle local threats in Northshire Valley. His immediate focus is suppressing the growing encroachment of the Defias Brotherhood. Standing just steps from the gates of Northshire Abbey, Deputy Willem represents the frontline presence of the Stormwind Army in the valley. With the kingdom's military stretched thin across multiple territories, local security falls heavily on small detachments like McBride's garrison. Willem evaluates incoming volunteers, assigning them immediate tasks to assist local residents and safeguard the valley's perimeter.

William Pestle. William Pestle is a human alchemist staying inside Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn. Together with his brother Morgan, he helps run the apothecary shop in Stormwind's Trade District. He frequently employs traveling adventurers to gather odd reagents like kobold candles, murloc kelp, and herbal supplies. While his brother Morgan Pestle manages the counter at Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District of Stormwind City, William operates out of the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. Being stationed in Elwynn Forest allows him to work closely with local gatherers and secure raw materials that city shops constantly require. He maintains regular shipments back to the capital, ensuring Stormwind's citizens have steady access to restorative salves, draughts, and powders.

Williden Marshal. Williden Marshal is the ambitious human leader of Marshal's Expedition, based out of Marshal's Refuge in northern Un'Goro Crater. Driven by the lure of rare flora, mysterious crystals, and profitable scientific research, he brought his team into the crater only to watch their lower camps overrun by the basin's colossal beasts. Williden Marshal brought an entire scientific expedition deep into Un'Goro Crater seeking fortune and discovery. Intrigued by accounts of alien crystals, uncataloged plants, and untapped resources, he established multiple forward camps across the valley floor. However, the primeval wilderness quickly turned against them. The savage beasts of the crater dismantled their research posts, forcing Williden and his survivors to retreat up into the northern cliffs to establish Marshal's Refuge.

Winna Hazzard. Winna Hazzard is an eccentric Forsaken researcher stationed at Bloodvenom Post in Felwood. Accompanied by a feline companion and known for bouts of maniacal laughter, she studies the blighted ecosystem and conducts unsettling experiments with the zone's corrupted fauna. Winna Hazzard represents the Forsaken interest in Felwood's unnatural decay. Stationed in the Horde enclave of Bloodvenom Post, she spends her time observing the local wildlife and formulating experiments utilizing tainted waters and venomous samples. Her jovial, manic demeanor often masks callous motives, evident when she uses tainted liquids drawn from the land to corrupt the small kitten that stays by her side.

Winstone Wolfe. Winstone Wolfe is a human operative affiliated with the secretive Ravenholdt organization, stationed at their secluded estate nestled between Hillsbrad and the Alterac Mountains. He keeps watch over the estate's grounds and groundskeepers, serving as one of the trusted contacts within the hidden league of thieves and assassins. Tucked away in the hidden valley of Ravenholdt Manor, Winstone Wolfe operates among the ranks of Lord Jorach Ravenholdt's syndicate. Quiet, watchful, and practical, Wolfe is one of the capable hands who handles business around the manor, ensuring that only those with proper discretion and talent walk the grounds undisturbed.

Witch Doctor Jin'Zil. Witch Doctor Jin'Zil is a Darkspear troll mystic dwelling in a cave at Malaka'jin in the southern Stonetalon Mountains. A longtime comrade of Darsok Swiftdagger and the shadow hunter Rokhan, he turns dark voodoo and ritual sorcery against the Horde's local enemies. Secluded inside an eastern cavern above the camp of Malaka'jin, Jin'Zil practices ancient jungle troll arts away from the coastal home of his tribe. Surrounded by bubbling cauldrons and captive prisoners, he gathers exotic reagents from the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains to weave potent blessings and curses in defense of the Horde's mountain encampment.

Witch Doctor Uzer'i. Witch Doctor Uzer'i is a jungle troll mystic residing at Camp Mojache in the primordial forests of Feralas.
