Dedicated to advancing the magical capabilities of the Horde, he researches techniques to trap and harness the muisek—the spiritual essence of powerful natural creatures. By capturing these ancient forest spirits, Uzer'i seeks to channel the raw primal energies traditionally favored by night elves directly into enchanted weapons. Rooted in traditional troll spiritualism, Witch Doctor Uzer'i has spent considerable effort studying the natural magic inherent to the untamed wilderness of Feralas. He argues that night elves have drawn upon the spirits of forest beasts for millennia, and believes the time has come for the Horde to seize those same primal forces. Central to his study is the concept of muisek: the vibrant spiritual essence that remains within a creature. To harness it, Uzer'i crafts specialized vessels capable of rapidly shrinking fallen beings before their escaping spirit disperses, allowing the essence to be stored and studied.

Wizbang Cranktoggle. Wizbang Cranktoggle is an eccentric gnome engineer residing on the upper floor of the Auberdine inn. Despite being far from the cog-filled halls of Gnomeregan or Ironforge, he has turned his mechanical ingenuity toward setting up and maintaining automated communication devices known as buzzboxes across the wild coast of Darkshore. While the night elves of Auberdine prefer living in harmony with nature and leaning upon ancient customs, Wizbang Cranktoggle represents the curious, tinkering presence of the Alliance. Perched on the top floor of Auberdine's inn, surrounded by tools and spare components, Wizbang pays little mind to the solemn druidic traditions of Kalimdor, focusing instead on pragmatic mechanical challenges.

Wizlo Bearingshiner. Wizlo Bearingshiner is a goblin tinkerer stranded at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. The sole survivor of a centaur attack on his caravan, he recruits travelers to recover a valuable Hypercapacitor Gizmo from the wreckage. Staying alongside the tauren at Whitereach Post along the canyon road, Wizlo Bearingshiner faces an unwelcome delay. Centaur attacked his caravan, leaving him as its only survivor. His clients are waiting for their wares, and he worries that he will not deliver them in time.

Wizzle Brassbolts. Wizzle Brassbolts is a gnome engineer stationed alongside his fellow tinkerers out on the salt flats of Thousand Needles. Working with the gnomish racing team at the Mirage Raceway, he seeks durable local materials to reinforce their experimental rocket cars. Out in the shimmering heat of the Shimmering Flats, the rivalry between gnomish and goblin engineering takes the form of high-speed rocket car races. Wizzle Brassbolts works as part of the gnomish raceway crew, striving to keep their vehicles intact against blistering speeds and abrasive salt. To bolster their machines, he recruits adventurers to hunt the local wildlife—such as the sturdy turtles wandering the basin—harvesting their hard shells to build new fuel tanks strong enough to hold his brother's corrosive new rocket fuel.

Wizzlecrank's Shredder. Wizzlecrank's Shredder is a Venture Company shredder stuck in the foul depths of Sludge Fen in the northern Barrens. The goblin Pilot Wizzlecrank has climbed inside to steal it, but without its key the machine will not move, and it sits amidst hostile Venture Company operators. Helping fire up its engine is the only way the trapped pilot can make a desperate bid for freedom. Deep within the oil-slicked, heavily polluted basin of Sludge Fen sits Wizzlecrank's Shredder, immobile and surrounded by hostile Venture Company mercenaries. The goblin inside, Wizzlecrank, hopped into the Venture Co. machine to steal it, only to discover he needed a key to unlock its movement column. When another shredder operator asked if everything was all right, he panicked and blamed a mechanical problem. Now he sits sealed inside amid hostile guards and overseers, hoping someone can fetch the key before the Venture Company grows suspicious.

Wrenix the Wretched. Wrenix the Wretched is a goblin tinker stationed in the bustling port town of Ratchet. Operating beside his strange gizmotronic apparatus, he offers specialized assistance to those seeking to crack tough locks and plunder secure caches. Found lounging alongside his peculiar machinery in the goblin port of Ratchet, Wrenix the Wretched represents the opportunistic, pragmatic spirit of the Steamwheedle Cartel. Despite his downcast moniker, he possesses specialized knowledge regarding mechanisms, contraptions, and the delicate art of bypass and salvage, making him an invaluable contact for aspiring scoundrels and scouts working the coast.

Wynne Larson. Wynne Larson is a human clothier and robe merchant operating in Stormwind City's Mage Quarter. With the historic arcane textile centers of Dalaran and Quel'Thalas ruined in the Third War, she relies on local craftsmen to supply mages across the kingdom. She regularly directs adventuring spellcasters toward the rare materials required to craft powerful enchanted garments. Before the Third War, the finest woven fabrics and enchanted vestments came from the magical workshops of Dalaran and the high elven kingdom of Quel'Thalas. The destruction of both northern realms crippled traditional trade routes and devastated arcane textile production. Vendors like Wynne Larson in Stormwind's Mage Quarter have had to adapt, coordinating directly with local tailors and enchanters like Lucan Cordell to meet the city's growing demand for robes and spellwoven gear.

Xavathras. Xavathras is a vicious satyr commander residing among the tents at the Ruins of Constellas in Felwood. Leading a band of Jadefire satyrs, he oversees the corruption of an ancient moonwell in service to his master, Xavaric. Within the tainted glades of Felwood, the Ruins of Constellas have fallen into the clutches of the Jadefire satyrs. Stationed in an encampment pitched amidst the elven stonework, Xavathras directs the defilement of a nearby moonwell on behalf of another cruel satyr, Xavaric. By poisoning the pure waters with demonic energy, Xavathras deepens the corruption that grips the forest. His presence poses a direct threat to any attempts to restore the woodland, earning the ire of night elves like Eridan Bluewind who mark him for death.

Yaw Sharpmane. Yaw Sharpmane is an experienced tauren hunter trainer stationed in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. He guides young hunters venturing out from Camp Narache, helping them master the wild beasts of their ancestral plains. Positioned amidst the tents and fires of Bloodhoof Village, Yaw Sharpmane serves the Shu'halo as an instructor in the ways of marksmanship, tracking, and survival. Young hunters who have proven themselves in Red Cloud Mesa are directed to Yaw to hone their craft as they step onto the broader plains of Mulgore.

Yeh'kinya. Yeh'kinya is a jungle troll scholar residing at Steamwheedle Port on the desert coast of Tanaris. Claiming to seek ancient lore and artifacts to understand dark powers, he dispatches willing adventurers across Azeroth on missions to gather lost troll relics. Lounging among the goblins and dockworkers of Steamwheedle Port, Yeh'kinya presents himself as a quiet student of history and spirits. He recruits travelers to track down obscure magical items across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, from ancient eggs in the Hinterlands to stone prophecy tablets buried in the ruins of Zul'Farrak. While he claims these errands serve peaceful academic inquiry into ancient troll history, his specific focus on the blood god Hakkar draws suspicion from watchful onlookers.

Yvette Farthing. Yvette Farthing is a Forsaken resident of Brill in Tirisfal Glades, dwelling in the Gallows' End Tavern alongside her father, Coleman. Though she appears as hardened and detached as any of Sylvanas's people, she carries the lingering ghost of a mortal romance cut short by the Scourge. Before the Third War swept Lordaeron into ruin, Yvette was in love with Thurman Agamand, one of the heirs of the prosperous Agamand Mills. When the Scourge plague approached, Yvette and her father, Coleman, begged Thurman to abandon the estate and flee with them. Thurman refused out of devotion to his family's legacy. Both would eventually perish and rise into undeath, but while Yvette found a place among the free-willed Forsaken in Brill, Thurman's tragic final fate remained unknown to her.

Zaldimar Wefhellt. Zaldimar Wefhellt is a human mage trainer stationed on the upper floor of the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. He serves as an instructor for fledgling spellcasters passing through Elwynn Forest before sending them along to higher practitioners in Stormwind City. While Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn is best known for weary travelers, rowdy adventurers, and local gossip, its upper rooms house instructors of various trades. Tucked into one of the second-floor chambers, Zaldimar Wefhellt instructs novice mages in the foundational arts of the arcane, fire, and frost. Once an apprentice outgrows his early tutelage, he directs them north to the Mage Quarter in Stormwind to study under Jennea Cannon.

Zamja. Zamja is a Darkspear troll cooking trainer found working in the bustling corridor of the Drag in Orgrimmar. Known for her steady hand with a meat cleaver, she instructs Horde adventurers in preparing hearty meals from the beasts of Kalimdor. Stationed within the winding canyon path of the Drag, Zamja spends her days breaking down cuts of meat and teaching hungry Horde travelers how to sustain themselves. Practical cooking is a vital survival skill in the rugged terrain of Durotar and the Barrens, and Zamja ensures that anyone willing to hold a skillet learns the basics of turning raw game into wholesome rations. For cooks who have mastered basic recipes and seek further training, she directs them south toward Gadgetzan.

Zangen Stonehoof. Zangen Stonehoof is a tauren keeper situated at the High Rise bonfire in the heart of Thunder Bluff. Dutiful and revered among his peers, he faithfully tends to the central flames each evening while coordinating efforts to aid his distant kin across Kalimdor. Perched on the High Rise of Thunder Bluff, Zangen Stonehoof maintains the central communal bonfire that overlooks the city's highest bluffs. As twilight falls over Mulgore, Zangen kindles the fire, providing warmth and an enduring beacon for the tribes assembled beneath High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. Beyond keeping the flames alight, he maintains ties with allies beyond Mulgore's mesa, acting as a liaison for spiritual and ritual endeavors taking place across the continent.

Zankaja. Zankaja is a young orc woman living in Orgrimmar, residing along the path between the Valley of Strength and the Valley of Wisdom. She anxiously awaits news of her mate, Dogran, who was assigned to duty at the Crossroads in the dangerous frontier of the Barrens. Life in the fledgling Horde capital is demanding, but for Zankaja, the true ordeal is the waiting. Her mate Dogran earned a promotion that sent him south into the Barrens to bolster the outpost at the Crossroads. While an honor for a warrior, the Barrens is a brutal expanse crawling with quilboar, centaur, and aggressive beasts. When Dogran failed to send word or return home as expected, Zankaja began seeking out travelers willing to seek news of his fate.

Zardeth of the Black Claw. Zardeth of the Black Claw is a warlock dwelling in the dim subterranean chambers beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. Operating under the guise of an unassuming patron, he coordinates covert measures to protect the city's hidden warlock cabal from outside scrutiny. When inquisitive nobles begin looking too closely into their activities, Zardeth ensures those inquiries end permanently. While the Mage Quarter's towering spires study arcane discipline in the open, the underground tunnels beneath the Slaughtered Lamb house those who traffic in darker arts. Zardeth of the Black Claw operates from these crypts, functioning as a watchful guardian for the practitioners hiding right beneath the city guard's nose. Because the Alliance officially condemns fel magic, survival requires an ironclad secret and a willingness to eliminate any threat before royal investigators come knocking.

Zargh. Zargh is an orc meat merchant stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Aside from providing provisions to travelers, he frequently supplies choice cuts of local game to Innkeeper Gryshka in Orgrimmar. Amid the bustle of the Crossroads, Zargh tends his shop selling various cuts of cured meat, shank, and game taken from the surrounding plains. For adventurers pushing deep into the harsh wilderness, his stocks provide vital nourishment. Beyond basic trade, he maintains close ties with the Horde capital, regularly shipping carefully selected meats across Durotar to Gryshka, the innkeeper of the Valley of Strength.

Zarlman Two-Moons. Zarlman Two-Moons is a revered tauren mystic residing in Bloodhoof Village in central Mulgore. While Baine Bloodhoof oversees the village's daily earthly affairs, Zarlman guides its spiritual life and communions with the spirits. He plays a vital role in initiating young tauren into adulthood through the sacred Rite of Vision. Within Bloodhoof Village, leadership is divided between the physical and the mystical. Baine Bloodhoof commands the settlement's defense and temporal needs, but it is Zarlman Two-Moons who maintains the harmony of the spirit world. In a culture deeply rooted in reverence for the Earth Mother and ancestral wisdom, Zarlman serves as a conduit between the everyday struggles of the plains and the timeless voices of the past.

Zarrin. Zarrin is a night elf culinary mentor located in Dolanaar on the boughs of Teldrassil. Tending an open hearth behind the village inn, he instructs young night elves and visitors in traditional Kaldorei cooking techniques. Situated behind the Dolanaar inn away from the main thoroughfare, Zarrin tends an open fire where he shares the culinary arts of the Kaldorei. Survival in Teldrassil requires utilizing the native flora and fauna of the giant tree, and Zarrin serves as an instructor for those seeking to sustain themselves through foraging and home-cooked meals.
Zenn Foulhoof. Zenn Foulhoof is a satyr lingering just east of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. He approaches passersby with requests for forest reagents, while the local night elves keep a close eye on him.

Zevrost. Zevrost is an orc warlock trainer secluded within the subterranean Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. He mentors developing warlocks of the Horde, guiding them through the hazardous disciplines of fel magic, summoning rituals, and binding dark artifacts. Tucked away deep in the caverns of the Cleft of Shadow, Zevrost is one of the principal mentors for Horde warlocks residing in Thrall's capital. While the broader orcish society remains wary of fel energies following the demonic corruption of their past, practitioners like Zevrost are tolerated under strict watch. He instills in his pupils the harsh discipline required to command demonic forces without succumbing to their corruptive nature, asserting that the fel only ruins those lacking inner strength.

Zjolnir. Zjolnir is a Darkspear troll mount breeder stationed in Sen'jin Village along the southern coast of Durotar. He provides trained riding raptors to the Darkspear and trustworthy champions of the Horde. For troll riders, his stable of vicious, loyal beasts is a point of deep cultural pride. Situated near the pens of Sen'jin Village, Zjolnir tends to the fierce raptors favored as mounts by the Darkspear trolls. Raptors are temperamental and predatory by nature, requiring an expert hand to raise and saddle for war. Zjolnir freely provides these prized whistled mounts to fellow trolls who have learned the necessary riding arts. Outsiders belonging to the wider Horde must first earn the exalted trust of the Darkspear tribe before Zjolnir will consider trusting them with one of his pack.

Zor Lonetree. Zor Lonetree is a knowledgeable orc advisor found within Grommash Hold in Orgrimmar. Well-versed in external affairs and Alliance politics, he aids the Horde by analyzing enemy artifacts and directing travelers to troubled regions across Kalimdor. Stationed within Grommash Hold alongside the Horde's high leadership, Zor Lonetree serves as a shrewd advisor who keeps a watchful eye on developments beyond Durotar. He possesses an unusually keen understanding of human and Alliance politics, making him an invaluable counselor when foreign curiosities or political threats reach the capital. From inspecting noble jewelry recovered from human settlements to monitoring disturbances among the land's spirits in Stonetalon Mountains, Lonetree ensures the warchief's court stays informed on matters both mundane and mystical.

Zureetha Fargaze. Zureetha Fargaze is an orc mentor stationed in the Valley of Trials in Durotar alongside Foreman Thazz'ril. Vigilant against corruption, she directs young Horde recruits to investigate and root out the dark influence of the Burning Blade cult hiding within the valley. While Foreman Thazz'ril oversees the labor and discipline of young orcs and Darkspear trolls, Zureetha Fargaze keeps watch for subtler, more insidious threats. The Burning Blade cult has secretly infiltrated the Valley of Trials, corrupting lesser demons and gathering strength in the nearby cavern of Burning Blade Coven. Zureetha tasks untested adventurers with retrieving medallions from the cultists to confirm their presence and dismantle their early operations before directing seasoned recruits outward into Durotar.

Addle's Stead. Addle's Stead is an abandoned farmstead in southwestern Duskwood, lying quiet under the forest's gloom south of Raven Hill. While its original homesteaders fled long ago, the farm has become a hidden staging ground for the Defias Brotherhood. Like many of the forgotten homesteads scattered across Duskwood, Addle's Stead fell into disrepair when darkness and ruin enveloped the region. Rather than remaining empty, the farm has been repurposed by the Defias Brotherhood. Agents prowl the perimeter, lurk within the decrepit farmhouse, and stash supplies in the barn, using the shadowy cover of southwestern Duskwood to escape the notice of both the Night Watch and Stormwind authorities.

Agama'gor. Agama'gor is a major Bristleback quilboar encampment situated in the southern Barrens, nestled just north of the road leading west toward Mulgore from Camp Taurajo. It represents a constant thorn in the side of the nearby Horde outpost, teeming with hostile quilboar fiercely clinging to their rugged territory. Sprawling across the dusty plains of the southern Barrens, Agama'gor serves as a fortified settlement for the aggressive Bristleback tribe of quilboar. Located dangerously close to Camp Taurajo, the quilboar here maintain a dense network of brambles, huts, and crude totems. Their heavy presence poses an active threat to travelers moving between the Barrens and the grassy hills of Mulgore, prompting Horde scouts and hunters to wage a perpetual war of containment against them.

Agamand Family Crypt. Tucked into the hills just north of Agamand Mills, the Agamand Family Crypt is the ancient resting ground of one of Tirisfal's wealthiest farming dynasties. Now claimed by the Scourge under Captain Dargol, its tombs have been ripped open, and the slumbering ancestors raised as mindless terrors. Before the Third War, the Agamand family held expansive estates across northern Tirisfal Glades, entombing their forebears within this hillside mausoleum. When the Plague brought ruin to the kingdom, the crypt fell into the clutches of Captain Dargol, an agent of the Scourge. Rather than letting the wealthy lineage rest in peace, Dargol employed dark necromancy to awaken the entombed skeletons and vengeful apparitions, transforming a sacred burial ground into an aggressive Scourge foothold right on the edge of Forsaken territory.

Agamand Mills. Agamand Mills is a sprawling farm and windmill complex nestled in the northern heights of Tirisfal Glades. Once the proud estate of the wealthy Agamand dynasty, it has fallen into ruin and stands as the largest Scourge stronghold in the region. The wealthy Agamand family built their estate around a vast milling network across northern Tirisfal. When the Third War broke out and the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the patriarch Gregor Agamand refused to flee, fortifying the compound and convincing his retainers and laborers to make their stand. Their provisions and stone walls might have held, but their youngest son, Devlin Agamand, betrayed his blood. Devlin slaughtered the estate watchmen and let the walking dead into the sleeping quarters. Crippled from within, the remaining defenders were wiped out, and the family joined the mindless ranks of the undead.

Agmond's End. Agmond's End is an abandoned dwarven excavation site tucked into the southern hills of the Badlands. Once a hopeful exploratory dig led by the prospector Agmond, the camp turned into a slaughterhouse when burrowing troggs overran the operation and killed its leader. Like many sites in the arid Badlands, Agmond's End began as a dwarven venture to uncover ancient relics and delve into the earth's buried history. That dream ended abruptly when savage troggs surged from the surrounding crevices and overwhelmed the miners. Agmond himself was cut down during the attack, giving the site its grim name. Today, the ruined dig remains utterly infested by Stonevault troggs, with shattered crates and abandoned tools left exactly where they fell.

Aku'mai's Lair. Aku'mai's Lair is the deepest and darkest cavern within Blackfathom Deeps. Located beyond the Moonshrine Sanctum, this submerged hollow serves as the nesting ground for Aku'mai, a monstrous hydra venerated as a servant of the Old Gods. Sealed away behind the Moonshrine Sanctum, Aku'mai's Lair represents the culmination of the corruption sweeping Blackfathom Deeps. To enter the cavern, dark rituals must be engaged by igniting the four brazier fires flanking a naga statue, awakening guardians sworn to defend the threshold. Beyond these heavy double doors lies a sunless, flooded grotto. Here, both the Twilight's Hammer cultists and invading naga gather in reverence of Aku'mai, an ancient three-headed hydra considered a living servant of the Old Gods.

Aldrassil. Aldrassil is the colossal bough-tree and settlement nestled at the heart of Shadowglen in northeastern Teldrassil. Serving as the primary refuge and training ground for young kaldorei, its carved hollows shelter trainers, merchants, and local leadership. Rising high above the secluded vale of Shadowglen, Aldrassil functions as both shelter and civic hub for young night elves taking their first steps in the world. Built into and around the colossal trunk of this ancient growth, winding ramps lead past class trainers and artisans to the high roost where Tenaron Stormgrip oversees the glade's protection. While the world bough Teldrassil stretches across the horizon, Aldrassil provides a safe, grounded canopy where novices learn their arts before venturing down into the troubled wilds of Kalimdor.

Alexston Farmstead. The Alexston Farmstead is a derelict farm in Westfall, overgrown and prowled by haywire Harvest Watchers. Once the childhood home of Stormwind's city architect, Baros Alexston, it has fallen into ruin like much of the breadbasket around it. Situated amidst the dry plains of Westfall, the Alexston Farmstead stands as another grim testament to the kingdom's neglect. Like neighboring estates, the farm was abandoned by its caretakers when banditry erupted across the countryside. Today, the fields are overgrown, and the mechanical Harvest Watchers left behind to tend the crops have spun out of control, violently attacking anyone who approaches the barren farmhouse.

Algaz Station. Algaz Station is a dwarven military outpost situated in northwestern Loch Modan, directly south of the fortified pass of Dun Algaz. Manning the approach to the northern tunnels, its garrison of Mountaineers helps safeguard travelers and watch the frontier leading toward the Wetlands. Perched just east of North Gate Pass and south of Dun Algaz, Algaz Station serves as a vital strategic watchpoint for the kingdom of Ironforge. A cadre of dwarven Mountaineers maintains a permanent vigil here, keeping the vital road between Loch Modan and the northern lowlands open to trade and troop movements. Given the frequent threats in the surrounding hills, from wandering beasts to encroaching troggs, the outpost provides respite, repairs, and martial support for weary travelers before they venture through the mountain tunnels.

Altar of Storms (Burning Steppes). Perched in the jagged crags of the Burning Steppes, the Altar of Storms is a dark monument dedicated to fel rituals and demonic power. Blackrock clan warlocks occupy the sinister site, performing foul magic beneath the shadow of Blackrock Spire. Its dark aura draws ambitious practitioners of the shadow from across Azeroth. Constructed during the earlier wars to channel corrupting fel magic, the Altar of Storms stands as a grim monument to dark pacts. In the Burning Steppes, hostile warlocks of the Blackrock clan control the grounds, conducting occult rituals and drawing upon demonic forces. Nearby, the encampment of the hermit Gorzeeki Wildeyes and his master Mor'zul Bloodbringer overlooks the site, where renegade practitioners study its violent energies and concoct demanding rituals for ambitious spellcasters seeking greater dark power.

Alterac Mountains. The Alterac Mountains are a rugged, snow-capped range rising directly above the rolling pastures of Hillsbrad. Once the heart of a proud human kingdom, the slopes now harbor ruined settlements, bandit factions, and dangerous wilderness where travelers rarely walk unguarded. Long before the hills fell into chaos, these highlands formed the sovereign nation of Alterac, one of the seven kingdoms born from ancient Arathor. That legacy shattered during the Second War when King Aiden Perenolde struck a clandestine pact with the Old Horde, allowing orcish forces passage through the peaks in exchange for his kingdom's safety. The Alliance of Lordaeron uncovered the betrayal and deposed Perenolde, leaving the region fractured by martial law and territorial disputes.

Alterac Mountains (Classic). The Alterac Mountains are a rugged, overcast highland rising sharply north of Hillsbrad Foothills, crowned with permanent snow and jagged peaks. Once the home of the human kingdom of Alterac and the scholarly redoubts of Dalaran, the region now lies largely in ruins, fought over by brutal ogres, noble-born bandits, and the opposing armies of Alterac Valley. Rising high above the Hillsbrad lowlands, the Alterac Mountains are a harsh realm of rain, pine, and high-altitude snow. Once anchored by three major human powers—the mountain kingdom of Alterac, the magocracy of Dalaran, and the fortified town of Strahnbrad—the region collapsed under betrayal and war. Today, the ruined capital of Alterac is squatted by the Crushridge ogres, Strahnbrad is occupied by outlaws, and among the shattered remnants of Dalaran its surviving wizards work tirelessly to restore their ruined sanctuary.

Alther's Mill. Alther's Mill is a ruined lumber mill tucked into the rugged hills northeast of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains. Once a vital source of processed timber for local builders, the abandoned grounds have deteriorated into a haven for feral scavengers and prowling predators. For adventurers traveling east toward Stonewatch, the dilapidated structures serve as a grim landmark marking the boundary of safe frontier territory. Before the region fell prey to invading predators and orc raids, Alther's Mill bustled with timber trade that supplied the construction of Lakeshire and surrounding settlements. Its quiet clearing northeast of Lake Everstill provided ready access to mountain timber stands. As turmoil mounted across the kingdom of Stormwind and the Blackrock clan pushed down from the heights of Stonewatch, local millers abandoned the facility, leaving the dry timber buildings and wheel to decay into rot.

Ambermill. Ambermill is a fortified human settlement in southeastern Silverpine Forest, situated just southwest of Lordamere Lake. Once a quiet lumber village, it is now occupied by surviving wizards and apprentices of Dalaran. Their presence represents a dangerous outpost of human resistance on the southern borders of the Forsaken realm. Before the Third War, Ambermill was a quiet lumber town of little importance. In the chaotic aftermath of Lordaeron's fall, the surviving wizards of the Kirin Tor moved in and fortified the settlement. Dalaran spellscribes, conjurors, and apprentices now patrol its buildings and stables, using Ambermill as a forward redoubt against the undead.

Amberstill Ranch. Amberstill Ranch is a tranquil dwarven homestead nestled along the snowy roadway toward Loch Modan, directly north of Gol'Bolar Quarry. It serves as the primary breeding and training grounds for Ironforge's celebrated mountain rams. Adventurers visit the ranch to acquire hardy dwarven mounts, train in riding, or help the family defend their livestock from local predators. Tucked against the crags of Dun Morogh, Amberstill Ranch is renowned throughout Khaz Modan for raising the sturdiest mountain rams in the Eastern Kingdoms. The Amberstill family manages the stables and paddocks, training these sure-footed beasts to navigate treacherous snowy passes and steep alpine cliffs. Outside of supplying riding mounts and domestic livestock, the family often contends with the savage fauna of the hills, particularly wandering wendigos drawn by the scent of fresh flock.

Ameth'Aran. Ameth'Aran is an ancient ruin in southern Darkshore, once a thriving city where Queen Azshara's Highborne practiced arcane sorcery. When the Great Sundering shattered the ancient world, the city fell with it. Today, its broken colonnades are haunted by the vengeful ghosts of the elves who died there. Before the Great Sundering, Ameth'Aran and its sister settlement, Bashal'Aran, stood as twin centers of Highborne influence along the ancient coastline. Under the favor of Queen Azshara, its ruling nobility dedicated themselves to unrestrained arcane experimentation. Governed from afar by the sorcerer Athrikus Narassin in the Tower of Althalaxx, the city thrived until the catastrophic collapse of the Well of Eternity tore the Kaldorei Empire apart.

Andorhal. Once the thriving agricultural heart of northern Lordaeron, Andorhal became ground zero for the Kingdom's destruction during the Third War. It was here that Kel'Thuzad tainted the grain with the Plague of Undeath, unleashing horror across the region. Today, the ruined town is held firmly in the iron grip of the Scourge. Before the Third War, Andorhal was the prosperous granary of the Eastweald, gathering grain from across Lordaeron and distributing it eastward to Hearthglen and Stratholme. Because of this vast distribution network, Kel'Thuzad and the Cult of the Damned chose Andorhal as the staging ground for their horrific plot. By tainting the grain crates with the Plague of Undeath, the cult turned the breadbasket of the kingdom into an engine of necrosis, infecting countless citizens before the Crown even understood the threat.

Angerfang Encampment. The Angerfang Encampment is the primary stronghold of the Dragonmaw clan in the central Wetlands. Led by Chieftain Nek'rosh Skullcrusher, these renegade orcs use the sprawling camp as a staging ground to threaten nearby dwarven settlements and plot the destruction of Menethil Harbor. Sprawling across the muck of the central Wetlands, the Angerfang Encampment serves as the fortified heart of Dragonmaw power in the region. Unlike the scattered raiding parties found wandering the marshes, this compound boasts heavily defended barricades, watchtowers, and a formidable host of warriors, bonewarders, and dark spellcasters loyal to the old ways. From here, the Dragonmaw project military force across the marshlands, raiding travelers along the roads and menacing nearby dwarven digs like Whelgar's Excavation Site.

Anvilmar. Anvilmar is a fortified dwarven outpost nestled in the snowy depths of Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh. Centered around a massive stone forge, it serves as the primary training grounds and rallying point for young Bronzebeard dwarves and displaced gnomish refugees beginning their adventures. Tucked away in the northern crags of Coldridge Valley, Anvilmar stands as an enduring symbol of dwarven perseverance. Dominated by a roaring central forge, this sturdy masonry complex houses class mentors, supply vendors, and veteran mountain mountaineers who drill recruits before sending them out into the wider kingdom. Though sheltered behind towering drifts, the settlement remains on constant guard against the hostile Frostmane trolls and aggressive wild beasts prowling the frozen valley.

Apothecarium. The Apothecarium is the southwestern quarter of the Undercity and the headquarters of the Royal Apothecary Society. Within these noxious laboratories, Forsaken alchemists labor tirelessly under Master Apothecary Faranell to concoct virulent plagues, toxins, and engineered horrors. It stands as the grim heart of Undercity's biological research, vital to Lady Sylvanas's campaign against the living and the Scourge. Occupying the southwestern terrace of the subterranean capital, the Apothecarium is a labyrinth of bubbling vats, dissection tables, and pungent chemical fumes. Led by Master Apothecary Faranell, the Royal Apothecary Society utilizes this district to advance their understanding of mortality and rot. Here, alchemists and surgeons experiment on tissue grafts, vivisection, and the assembly of mighty abominations. Their overriding purpose, mandated by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, is the formulation of a new plague capable of eradicating both the Scourge and the lingering human presence across Lordaeron.

Ariden's Camp. Ariden's Camp is an abandoned encampment nestled just north of the path threading through Deadwind Pass. Left decaying in the shadow of Karazhan, it stands as an eerie, quiet anomaly amidst the desolate canyon winds. Travelers between Duskwood and the Swamp of Sorrows often pass it with unease, wondering who once pitched a tent here. Tucked against the crags north of the gorge road connecting Duskwood to the Swamp of Sorrows, this dilapidated campsite looks like an ordinary transient stop long forsaken by living men. Yet in the oppressive gloom of Deadwind Pass, nothing remains unmarred by dark sorcery. Whoever named the camp Ariden's and whatever fortune its owner sought in Karazhan's orbit, the pass's lingering horrors swallowed it, leaving only weathered cloth, cold ashes, and an enduring mystery.

Astranaar. Astranaar is the primary Night Elf settlement in central Ashenvale, built across a serene lake island straddling the ancient forest road. Serving as the beating heart of Alliance operations in the region, it provides vital refuge to travelers facing encroaching threats from hostile furbolgs, satyrs, and the Horde. Situated atop an island in the middle of a forest lake, Astranaar stands as the largest night elven settlement in Ashenvale. Connected to the mainland by wooden footbridges spanning the waters, the town houses sentinels, priests, and artisans who keep vigil over the woodlands. In addition to offering basic comforts such as an inn, traders, and an expert leatherworker, its elevated perches host a flight master providing hippogryph travel to distant outposts across Kalimdor.

Auberdine. Auberdine is a coastal night elven port town on the gloomy shores of Darkshore, serving as the Alliance's primary maritime gateway to northern Kalimdor. Sheltered beneath overcast skies and pine-covered bluffs, it connects the island home of Teldrassil to the Eastern Kingdoms while serving as an administrative haven against the encroaching wilderness. Resting along the shores of the Veiled Sea, Auberdine is the only major settlement to successfully endure in modern Darkshore. Unlike the secluded treetop cities of Teldrassil, Auberdine looks outward, serving as the Alliance's busiest port in the north. Regular ships sail between here and the Eastern Kingdoms, to Stormwind Harbor and, by way of Southshore, to Menethil Harbor, while local ferries run to Rut'theran Village at the boughs of the World Tree. Because of its trade role, Auberdine embraces a more cosmopolitan air than traditional elven enclaves; visitors find lamps illuminating stone-laid streets and outland merchants including dwarves and gnomes mingling among the low-slung, arched timber houses.

Azurelode Mine. Azurelode Mine is an active Alliance iron mine nestled in the southwestern hills of Hillsbrad Foothills. Guarded by Southshore's militia and worked by human laborers, its steady supply of ore fuels the local human war effort against the Forsaken of Tarren Mill. Situated southwest of the open farmland and just west of Southshore, Azurelode Mine has long tapped into the mineral-rich ridges along the coast. Today, human miners labor deep underground under the watchful eye of Foreman Bonds, extracting iron to forge arms and armor for the Alliance defenders holding the region against the Undercity.

Bael'dun Digsite. The Bael'dun Digsite is a dwarven excavation carved deep into the mountains along the western edge of Mulgore. Established by Prospector Khazgorm's team out of Bael Modan, the quarry is viewed by the local tauren as a direct desecration of their ancestral homeland and an insult to the Earth Mother. Perched on the mountain slopes of western Mulgore, the Bael'dun Digsite represents the southernmost reach of the dwarven Explorers' League expedition based out of Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. Unconcerned with territorial borders or the spiritual traditions of the newly settled tribes, dwarven prospectors arrived with picks, shovels, and blasting powder to unearth ancient Titan relics buried beneath the plains.

Bael'dun Keep. Bael'dun Keep is an imposing dwarven fortification overlooking the Bael Modan excavation in the southern Barrens. Under the command of General Twinbraid, this fortress anchors the Alliance's controversial presence in the region, bringing them into violent conflict with the surrounding Horde territories. Constructed according to designs by the dwarven architect Haggis Boatmurder, Bael'dun Keep serves as the fortified military heart of the Ironforge presence in the southern Barrens. Towering over the expansive excavation trenches of Bael Modan, the fortress protects the Prospectors and archaeologists searching for ancient titan artifacts. Heavily armed with ironworks and artillery, its garrison maintains a vigilant watch, securing dwarven supply lines and projecting Alliance martial power straight into Kalimdor's heartland.

Bael Modan. Bael Modan is a fortified dwarven outpost and archaeological dig site located in the southern Barrens. Established by dwarven excavators searching for ancient Titan relics, the heavily armed installation has ignited a bitter conflict by displacing the indigenous Stonespire tauren. Bael Modan consists of the fortified Bael'dun Keep, an array of massive siege cannons, gyrocopter landing pads, and a deep open excavation pit. Dwarven prospectors arrived in Kalimdor under the conviction that an ancient Titan facility rests buried beneath the red earth. However, their blasting operations ripped directly through sacred ground belonging to the Stonespire tauren. Rather than negotiating, the dwarven expedition drove the Stonespire off their ancestral lands with gunfire and explosives, leaving the surviving tribesmen scattered and vengeful.

Bal'lal Ruins. Bal'lal Ruins are ancient Gurubashi troll ruins set along the northwestern shore of Stranglethorn Vale, just north of Grom'gol Base Camp. Overlooking the murky waters of the Vile Reef, the crumbling stone foundations are currently occupied by hostile Bloodscalp trolls. Perched on the coastline north of Grom'gol Base Camp, Bal'lal Ruins stand as another remnant of the shattered Gurubashi Empire. Once part of the grand troll civilization that dominated southern Azeroth, the site has decayed into moss-covered stone walls and cracked masonry. The ruins sit immediately adjacent to the Vile Reef, offering an elevated vantage over the treacherous coastal shallows. Today, aggressive Bloodscalp trolls hold the grounds, fiercely defending the weathered relics of their ancestors against intruders.

Balia'mah Ruins. The Balia'mah Ruins are the moss-covered remnants of an ancient Gurubashi settlement in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Located east of Grom'gol Base Camp across the river, the crumbling stone tiers are currently claimed and guarded by warriors of the hostile Skullsplitter troll tribe. Like many of the stone edifices dotting the jungle, Balia'mah stands as a remnant of the sprawling Gurubashi Empire that once ruled much of the southern Eastern Kingdoms. Following the fall of their ancient capital, Gurubashi territory splintered into warring factions. Today, the ruins serve as a stronghold for the Skullsplitter tribe, who fiercely defend the stone terraces against wandering beasts, neighboring ogres from the Mosh'Ogg mound, and any outsiders foolish enough to cross the river.

Balnir Farmstead. The Balnir Farmstead is a derelict estate in eastern Tirisfal Glades, northeast of the Ruins of Lordaeron. Once a working farm of the Balnir family, the lands now lie ruined and infested by wandering Scourge that slip past the Bulwark. For generations, the Balnir family worked their homestead in the rolling hills of eastern Tirisfal, and their garden of snapdragons still blooms among the ruins. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron during the Third War, the farm was overrun and its people lost, leaving the buildings to rot.

Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Ban'ethil Barrow Den is a sacred subterranean sanctuary hollowed out within the roots of Teldrassil. Originally created as a resting place for the sleeping Druids of the Talon, the cavern complex has recently fallen into chaos. The corrupted furbolgs of the Gnarlpine tribe have overrun its chambers, turning a place of peaceful slumber into a perilous den of madness. Barrow dens serve as sacred resting chambers where night elf druids slumber while projecting their spirits into the Emerald Dream. Ban'ethil Barrow Den was dedicated specifically to sheltering the Druids of the Talon as they communed with nature. Divided into upper and lower subterranean chambers, the den once resonated with tranquil reverie and deep meditative magic. However, the affliction sweeping Teldrassil's wildlife did not spare the Gnarlpine furbolgs, who invaded the complex, turning its hollowed halls into a fortified warren.

Ban'ethil Hollow. Ban'ethil Hollow is a rugged ravine cutting into the woodland just south of the main road connecting Dolanaar and Darnassus. It has become a dangerous haven for corrupted, aggressive furbolgs who pose a constant threat to travelers. Tucked away in the back of the ravine lies the entrance to the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Situated off the highway between Dolanaar and Darnassus, Ban'ethil Hollow is a sharp reminder that the boughs of Teldrassil are not entirely safe. Furbolgs driven mad by the strange affliction plaguing the World Tree have taken refuge throughout the rocky descent. They frequently stalk the nearby path, waiting to ambush unwary couriers and wandering sentinels. Deep within the ravine sits the threshold of the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, where slumbering druids and ancient tunnels face encroachment from the maddened beasts outside.

Bandarion Keep. Bandarion Keep is a fortified redoubt associated with Tyr's Watch, nestled in the western reaches of Tirisfal Glades near the Whispering Forest. Named in honor of Garek Bandarion, the outpost serves as an isolated bulwark amidst lingering threats across the woodland frontier. Its defenders contend with everything from hostile coastal murlocs to roving zealots and unstable undead. Situated near the secluded Whispering Forest in western Tirisfal Glades, Bandarion Keep stands as a solitary sentinel for the Forsaken. Named after Garek Bandarion, this stronghold is closely tied to Tyr's Watch. Quartermasters like Jorin Croge work diligently to keep the garrison supplied despite its remote and challenging position far from the bustling courtyards of the Undercity.

Baradin Bay. Baradin Bay is the expansive body of water lying between the shores of Khaz Modan, the Wetlands, the Arathi Highlands, and southern Lordaeron. Once vigorously patrolled by the powerful navy of Kul Tiras during the Second War, its waters now conceal treacherous reefs, sunken warships, and hostile aquatic predators. Framed by the coasts of Dun Morogh to the south and Lordaeron to the north, Baradin Bay serves as a vital maritime passage connecting the harbors of the Eastern Kingdoms. The bay is anchored by busy ports like Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands and Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. However, navigating these waters is perilous: shallow sandbanks, jagged shoals, and dangerous fauna like murlocs, crocolisks, and deep-sea sharks pose constant threats to sailors and travelers alike.

Bashal'Aran. Bashal'Aran is an ancient Highborne ruin situated in northern Darkshore, just east of Auberdine. Once a flourishing sister city to Ameth'Aran before the Great Sundering, the site now crawls with demonic satyrs and grells feeding on lingering arcane magic, while a solitary elven ghost remains trapped by a centuries-old curse. Before the Great Sundering broke ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, Queen Azshara settled favored Highborne subjects in the twin towns of Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran. Governed by the powerful mage Athrikus Narassin, the cities boasted splendid markets and temples dedicated to Elune. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the cataclysm laid both settlements to waste. For reasons lost to time, Athrikus used his arcane mastery to bind his own second-in-command, the mage Asterion, into a moonstone seal within Bashal'Aran. Even after his physical body perished, Asterion's ghost remained shackled to the ruined shrine.

Bathran's Haunt. Bathran's Haunt is an ancient kaldorei ruin nestled in northwestern Ashenvale, east of the Zoram Strand. Recently, Forsaken herbalists and their guardians have overtaken the site to harvest local flora for their alchemical research, steadily withering the surrounding woodland. North of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran, crumbling night elf pillars stand swallowed by thick Ashenvale foliage. What was once a tranquil kaldorei relic has fallen under the shadow of the Forsaken. Skulking among the broken marble, undead herbalists and their enforcers have set up a crude open-air laboratory. Their presence alone blights the ancient soil: grass rots into a sickly brown, vibrant blossoms wilt, and an unnatural decay creeps through the grove as they methodically harvest rare woodland reagents for their experiments.

Bay of Storms. The Bay of Storms is an expansive, tempestuous gulf carving into the rugged eastern cliffs of Azshara. Its churning waters harbor ancient ruins, submerged caverns, and perilous marine beasts that make seafaring along this coast hazardous. Opening out toward the Great Sea, the Bay of Storms defines much of Azshara's dramatic coastal geography. Far from a tranquil harbor, its turbulent waters and rocky outcrops are home to dangerous wildlife and ancient aquatic threats. Within and along its waters lie landmarks like the sunken Temple of Arkkoran, the coral reefs of Hetaera's Clutch, and Scalebeard's Cave, leaving the bay largely avoided by casual sailors and claimed instead by coastal monsters.

Bear's Head. Bear's Head is a secluded mountainous stretch along the southeastern cliffs of Azshara. Named for the resident Timbermaw furbolgs whose settlements dot the rugged high ground, it serves as an outpost linked to their larger homes farther north while lying directly beneath the cliffside sanctum of Archmage Xylem. Tucked away in southeastern Azshara, Bear's Head takes its name from the encampments of uncorrupted Timbermaw furbolgs established upon its heights. These rustic settlements act as outlying camps tied to the major furbolg dens of Ursolan and Timbermaw Hold to the north. Perched atop the looming cliffs directly above the area sits Xylem's Tower, an eccentric sanctuary where Archmage Xylem and his small retinue of apprentices conduct arcane studies in quiet isolation from the rest of the troubled coastline.

Beezil's Wreck. Beezil's Wreck marks the crash site of an unfortunate goblin zeppelin deep within the quagmires of Dustwallow Marsh. Resting east of Tabetha's Farm, the shattered vessel's cargo holds scattered supplies and volatile engineering components that attract scavengers. Hidden away in the humid muck east of Tabetha's Farm lies the splintered skeleton of a goblin zeppelin known as Beezil's Wreck. The craft was hauling cargo southward across Kalimdor before suffering a disastrous plunge into the swamp. While the wreckage still smolders amid tangled reeds, its eccentric captain, Beezil, has seemingly vanished from the marsh, leaving behind scattered crates and ticking machinery to slowly rot in the brine.

Beggar's Haunt. Beggar's Haunt is an abandoned Stormwind scout tower perched on a hillside in northeastern Duskwood, near the mountain road to Deadwind Pass. While originally built to keep watch over the kingdom's eastern borders, it has become an outpost for Forsaken infiltrators deep within Alliance territory. Perched above the foggy hills east of Manor Mistmantle, Beggar's Haunt was once an active observation post manned by the Stormwind Guard to secure the eastern approaches to the realm. As the region fell into the gloom of modern Duskwood and kingdom patrols withdrew to Darkshire, the stone tower was abandoned to the elements. Today, its commanding vantage point serves a far more sinister purpose: agents of the Forsaken, including members of the Royal Apothecary Society and Deathstalkers, use the ruined stronghold to conduct research and monitor the region under the Alliance's nose.

Beren's Peril. Beren's Peril is a secluded mountain cavern tucked in the rocky hills southwest of Ambermill in Silverpine Forest. It serves as an entrenched redoubt for rogue Scourge loyalists serving the necromancer Thule Ravenclaw, plotting against the nearby Forsaken. Tucked away high in the crags southwest of Ambermill, Beren's Peril consists of a shadowed cave and winding mountain path hidden from the main roadway. Following the devastation of the Third War, rogue Scourge undead under the command of the renegade necromancer Thule Ravenclaw fortified this enclave. Rather than bowing to the Dark Lady or retreating north, Ravenclaw's thralls—regents, guardians, and drudgers—gathered here in secret to muster an assault against the Forsaken base at the Sepulcher. Their presence was uncovered by Forsaken scouts, turning the quiet cliffside into an active warzone for Horde operatives sent to eliminate the threat before an attack could materialize.

Bitter Reaches. The Bitter Reaches is a rugged, windswept wilderness in northeastern Azshara. Largely untouched by civilization, the rugged cliffs are prowled by predatory beasts and massive mountain giants. Occupying the northeastern cliffs of Azshara, the Bitter Reaches remains a stark and untamed stretch of rocky terrain overlooking the Great Sea. Flocks of feral hippogryphs and two-headed chimaeras nest amidst the heights, while acidic oozes seep through the cold ground. Along the high northern ridges, colossal mountain giants have claimed the slopes as their own, driving away lesser creatures and turning the frozen approaches into a perilous hazard for any solitary traveler.

Black Channel Marsh. Black Channel Marsh is a murky mire situated in the southwestern Wetlands, flanking the main road leading toward Menethil Harbor. Infested with aggressive raptors, the soggy terrain poses an immediate threat to unwary travelers and supply couriers traversing the coastal lowlands. Stretching across the swampy low ground southwest of the main thoroughfare, Black Channel Marsh is infamous among caravan drivers and couriers heading to Menethil Harbor. While the raised road offers the illusion of safety, the stagnant channels and thick reeds are home to territorial raptor packs. Hungry beasts frequently stray directly into traffic, ambushing fresh recruits and weary wayfarers who stray even a pace or two from the beaten path.

Blackchar Cave. Blackchar Cave is a mysterious, sealed-off cavern tucked into the southwestern crags of Searing Gorge, close to the base of Blackrock Mountain. Its entrance is choked with impassable rubble and rock. Tucked away against the scorching crags near the approaches to Blackrock Mountain, Blackchar Cave presents a solid wall of stone where a deep cavern entrance might once have been. Heavy rubble and scorched slag choke the opening, preventing anyone from exploring whatever tunnels lie deeper within the mountain roots. The desolate terrain around it is scorched by ash and magma, offering little comfort to wanderers.

Blackfathom Deeps. Blackfathom Deeps is a flooded subterranean temple ruin buried beneath the Zoram Strand along Ashenvale's northwestern coast. Once a glorious house of worship dedicated to the moon goddess Elune, its drowned halls have been overtaken by naga, satyr, and the sinister Twilight's Hammer cult. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, this complex was a temple dedicated to the goddess Elune, complete with its own moonwell. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the shrine sank beneath the ocean waves, presumed lost forever. Over millennia, receding shorelines and subterranean shifting left its remains partly flooded beneath the cliffs of Ashenvale.

Blackrock Mountain. Blackrock Mountain is a massive, active volcano that towers between the Burning Steppes and the Searing Gorge. Borne from the cataclysmic summoning of Ragnaros the Firelord, its hollowed depths house ancient dwarven masonry, warring armies, and smoldering horrors. Blackrock Mountain did not exist until the climax of the War of the Three Hammers two and a half centuries ago. Facing annihilation by the united armies of Ironforge and the Wildhammer clan, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan reached into the depths of the earth for a weapon. His reckless spell shattered the dimensional barriers and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord into Azeroth. The resulting apocalypse tore the Redridge range apart, gouging out the Searing Gorge and Burning Steppes while thrusting a colossal volcano into the sky. Thaurissan perished in the blast, and the surviving Dark Iron clan was bound into eternal servitude to the Firelord, carving their capital, Shadowforge City, deep within the mountain's roots.

Blackrock Pass. Blackrock Pass is a mountain corridor connecting the northern cliffs of Redridge Mountains to the arid wastes of the Burning Steppes. Passing beneath a heavy iron gate, it marks the sudden threshold between the tranquil human heartlands and the dangerous war grounds of the Dark Iron dwarves and the Blackrock orcs. For any weary traveler journeying north on foot, it represents a harsh and perilous frontier. Carved into the jagged spine of the mountains, Blackrock Pass serves as the overland route between Redridge Mountains and the Burning Steppes. A stout iron gate stands along the rocky boundary, demarcating the idyllic forests and lakes of the southern valleys from the volcanic ruin beyond. Crossing this line leaves behind the pastoral lands protected by Lakeshire's beleaguered militia, thrusting travelers into an open wasteland populated by fire elementals, dragonkin, and hostile orc warbands. Few make the crossing on foot unless bound for the shadow of Blackrock Mountain itself.

Blackrock Stronghold. Blackrock Stronghold is a heavily fortified encampment carved into the crags of the northern Burning Steppes, positioned right outside the entrance to Blackrock Mountain. It serves as a major field garrison for the Blackrock orcs and their allies under the Dark Horde banner. Sprawling across the scorched foothills below Blackrock Mountain, the stronghold functions as the primary ground base for the Blackrock clan in the Burning Steppes. Unlike Thrall's Horde, these orcs cling to their warlike legacy, serving Rend Blackhand and the dragonkin who lurk above in the spire.

Blackthorn Ridge. Blackthorn Ridge is a jagged, bramble-choked valley tucked away in the southern reaches of the Barrens, immediately north of Razorfen Kraul. The area crawls with aggressive Razormane quilboar guarding their thorny settlements. High on the ridge above sits the camp of the orc shaman Brine, watching over an unusually pure pool of mountain water. Nestled near the towering burls of Razorfen Kraul, Blackthorn Ridge is dominated by dense thickets of massive, sharp briars. The Razormane quilboar consider these grounds ancestral territory, using the natural barricades to ambush outsiders and stage skirmishes into the southern Barrens. Despite the constant danger, travellers seek out the ridge for the hermit orc shaman Brine, who tends a camp perched above a spring noted across Kalimdor for its remarkable clarity and spiritual purity.

Blackwolf River. Blackwolf River is a waterway flowing out of Cragpool Lake down through Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. Once a clean mountain stream, its waters have become thoroughly polluted by the Venture Company's aggressive logging and industrial operations. Descending from Cragpool Lake, the Blackwolf River cuts across the basin of Windshear Crag. What should be a pristine alpine tributary has instead borne the brunt of unchecked goblin enterprise. As the Venture Company clears the surrounding woodlands with heavy machinery and buzzsaws, sludge, oil, and logging waste leach steadily into the current. The despoiled river stands as a vivid example of the commercial plunder threatening Stonetalon's wilderness.

Blackwood Den. Blackwood Den is a corrupted furbolg encampment nestled in the southern reaches of Darkshore near the border of Ashenvale. Once a peaceful dwelling, the cave and surrounding camps have fallen into madness alongside the rest of the Blackwood tribe. A lone night elf scout named Volcor sits trapped within the cavern, awaiting aid from Auberdine. Situated near the southern border where Darkshore meets Ashenvale, Blackwood Den consists of a winding network of crude camps and a rocky cave. The Blackwood furbolgs who dwell here have succumbed to the pervasive corruption gripping the region, turning violently hostile toward outsiders. Deep inside the den's cave, the night elf Volcor remains pinned down and endangered by the aggressive tribe, desperately needing assistance from scouts and travelers dispatched from Auberdine.

Blackwood Lake. Blackwood Lake is a blighted body of water situated in the southern Eastern Plaguelands, teeming with hostile, corrupted elementals. The area is haunted by memories of tragedy and war, watched over by a small frontline camp of the Argent Dawn. Like so much of the Eastweald, Blackwood Lake has been poisoned by the rampant plague of undeath. Diseased and foul water elementals churn beneath the murky surface, attacking anyone who ventures near the shoreline.

Bladefist Bay. Bladefist Bay is the rugged stretch of coast lining eastern Durotar just outside the gates of Orgrimmar. Named in honor of Kargath Bladefist, the bay opens onto the Great Sea, shadowed by craggy bluffs and the nearby southern shores of Azshara. Stretching along the northeastern edge of Durotar, Bladefist Bay opens directly into the vast waters of the Great Sea. Flanked by rocky cliffs and treacherous surf, it lies just east of the Horde capital of Orgrimmar. Directly north, the ancient red cliffs and ruins of Azshara loom across the water, making the bay a vital maritime boundary for Durotar.

Bloodfen Burrow. Bloodfen Burrow is a cavern in southwestern Dustwallow Marsh swarming with vicious raptors. The beasts have claimed the cave and the surrounding clearing, completely overrunning the ruins of a settlement that once tried to survive the wetlands. Tucked away in the southwestern reaches of Dustwallow Marsh, Bloodfen Burrow serves as the primary den for the region's aggressive Bloodfen raptors. The cave mouth and surrounding hollow crawl with the pack, drawn to the sheltered crevice and the bountiful hunting ground the marsh provides. Just outside the entrance lie scattered debris and splintered remains of an unidentified settlement, serving as a grim reminder of who truly rules the swamp's interior. Travelers also whisper that Cortello, an adventurous buccaneer, left one of his hidden riddle clues somewhere within this deadly den.

Bloodhoof Village. Bloodhoof Village is a central tauren settlement resting along the banks of Stonebull Lake in Mulgore. Named in honor of the Bloodhoof tribe, it serves as the first major gathering hub for young hunters and braves journeying out from Camp Narache toward Thunder Bluff. Led by Baine Bloodhoof, the village coordinates local defense, trade, and traditional rites across the plains. Situated around the clear waters of Stonebull Lake, Bloodhoof Village is a bustling center of commerce, craft, and ceremony in central Mulgore. Young tauren departing their trials at Camp Narache arrive here to hone their skills before venturing onward to the great mesas of Thunder Bluff. It is also home to the patient breeders who tame wild kodo beasts for travel.

Bloodtooth Camp. Bloodtooth Camp is an encampment of hostile, corrupted furbolgs tucked into central Ashenvale, situated just west of the Falfarren River. Led by the chieftain Ran Bloodtooth, these once-peaceful creatures have succumbed to dark madness and attack anyone who approaches. The camp is a primary target for Alliance scouts working to cleanse the surrounding woodlands. Nestled southwest of the southern Moonwell and west of the Falfarren River, Bloodtooth Camp serves as a stark reminder of Ashenvale's encroaching decay. The furbolgs living here were once connected to the sacred wilderness of Kalimdor, but a lingering spiritual corruption has consumed their tribe. Under the command of Ran Bloodtooth, they guard their crude settlement with rabid hostility, turning upon travelers and night elven protectors alike.

Bloodvenom Falls. Bloodvenom Falls is a towering, foul waterfall plunging down the corrupted cliffs of northern Felwood. Its toxic flow feeds the Bloodvenom River, spreading demon-spawned rot down the mountains and into downstream lands. Pouring over the bluffs in Felwood, Bloodvenom Falls represents one of the most vivid wounds inflicted upon the ancient forests of Kalimdor. Once a pristine mountain cascade, the waters were warped into a virulent sludge during the Third War by demonic magics and the remnants of the Burning Legion. The falls feed directly into the Bloodvenom River, which weaves through the heart of Felwood. From there, the tainted torrent rushes down the mountain slopes to become the foul Wildbend River in Darkshore, carrying blight far beyond Felwood's blighted borders.

Bloodvenom Post. Bloodvenom Post is a remote Horde settlement perched on the rocky bluffs of western Felwood overlooking Darkshore. Its tauren-style structures and tauren guards provide a foothold in a region infested with demonic taint and corrupted wildlife. Tucked away along the high cliffs above Darkshore, Bloodvenom Post is reached by following the corrupted southern bank of the Bloodvenom River away from Felwood's main thoroughfare. Built with traditional tauren tents, totems, and watch posts, this encampment provides Horde wanderers with a vital base of operations amidst a dying forest. From here, scouts track the encroaching demonic forces, study the spreading corruption of the waters, and attempt to monitor the hostile wildlife mutated by the Burning Legion's lingering power.

Bloodvenom River. The Bloodvenom River is a foul waterway cutting through central Felwood, saturated with the demonic corruption that blighted the ancient forest. Its putrid waters seep downstream across the mountains into Darkshore, transforming into the tainted Wildbend River. Running through the corrupted heart of Felwood, the Bloodvenom River serves as an open conduit of the land's spiritual and physical decay. Its banks are thick with vile oozes, mutated beasts, and foul run-off left in the wake of the Burning Legion's invasion. The corruption within the channel is potent enough to taint lands far beyond Felwood itself, flowing westward down into the coastal forests of Darkshore as the Wildbend River.

Bluefen. Bluefen is a soggy marshland nestled in northern Dustwallow Marsh just east of Brackenwall Village. Crawling with aggressive wetland predators, the mire has also become a staging ground for covert Theramore Infiltrators keeping watch on local Horde movements. Situated just east of the Stonemaul ogres of Brackenwall Village, Bluefen embodies the untamed hazards of Dustwallow Marsh. The humid swampland teems with predatory beasts, including raptors, giant spiders, carrion-feeding birds, and lurking crocolisks. Beyond natural predators, travelers must contend with Theramore Infiltrators who skulk through the murky terrain to spy on the Horde and project human influence deeper into the swamp.

Bluegill Marsh. Bluegill Marsh is a sodden mire in the western Wetlands that serves as the sprawling settlement for the hostile Bluegill murloc tribe. The waterways and huts are fiercely guarded by these aquatic humanoids under the rule of the brute known as Gobbler. Travelers heading through the western fens must navigate carefully to avoid being surrounded in the shallows. Situated amidst the boggy flats of the western Wetlands, Bluegill Marsh is thick with mud, reeds, and the squawking war cries of its resident murlocs. The Bluegill tribe has erected crude primitive camps throughout the stagnant water, claiming this territory as their own. Unlike more isolated beasts of the swamp, these murlocs live and hunt in tightly knit packs. Wary wanderers and scouts from Menethil Harbor know that wading into their territory invites swift ambushes from every direction, especially with the formidable chieftain Gobbler prowling the murky shallows.

Bolgan's Hole. Bolgan's Hole is a subterranean cavern nestled in the southern cliffs of Gelkis Village in Desolace. It serves as the inner sanctum of the Gelkis centaur clan, housing their highest chieftains and sacred earth relics. Carved deep into the craggy bluffs overlooking the Gelkis encampment, Bolgan's Hole functions as the command center for the tribe. It is here that the ruling khan holds court, surrounded by veteran guards and the tribe's most influential shamans. The cavern offers natural fortification against rival clans, most notably the bloodthirsty Magram centaur to the east.

Bones of Grakkarond. The Bones of Grakkarond are the skeletal remains of a massive bronze dragon lying bleached under the sun of central Silithus. Slain during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands, this fallen wyrm serves as a grim monument held sacred by the qiraji's Anubisath sentinels. Sprawled across the windswept dunes of central Silithus lies the colossal ribcage and skull of Grakkarond, a bronze dragon who met his demise during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands. In that apocalyptic clash a millennium ago, the great dragon was struck down by Ossirian the Unscarred, an Anubisath warrior elevated by the dark powers of the city-kingdom. To the Anubisath, this battlefield trophy is a sacred testament to their might over the dragonflights, left untouched where he fell.

Booty Bay. Booty Bay is a sprawling pirate haven built into the sheer sea cliffs of southern Stranglethorn Vale, operated by the Steamwheedle Cartel's Blackwater Raiders. Entered by land through the gaping jaws of a giant shark carcass, it serves as a fiercely enforced neutral port where Alliance and Horde mingle under the watchful eyes of heavily armed goblin bruisers. Originally known as Blackwater Cove when it was a human settlement later overrun by jungle trolls, the bay was eventually captured by the goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel. Today, it is an international crossroads and a haven for scoundrels, outcasts, and merchants alike. Overseen by Baron Revilgaz alongside Fleet Master Seahorn from the balconies of the Salty Sailor Tavern, the port is ostensibly lawless yet strictly managed: anyone may drink, trade, or hire mercenaries here, provided they obey the cartel's peace and pay their harbor fees.

Bough Shadow. Bough Shadow is a secluded grove tucked away in the far northeastern corner of Ashenvale, east of Forest Song. It centers around a colossal Great Tree rooted over an ancient portal leading directly into the Emerald Dream. Bough Shadow houses one of the rare Great Trees, its roots plunging deep into the earth around a natural crossing into the Emerald Dream. Today, the tranquil yet imposing grove is heavily guarded by the Green Dragonflight. Emerald drakes such as Phantim and Dreamstalker circle above the canopy, while patrols of Emeraldon dragonspawn and oracles keep a vigilant, unyielding watch over the swirling green portal at its base, turning away any mortal who approaches unbidden.

Boulder'gor. Boulder'gor is a rugged hill in the western Arathi Highlands, situated directly north of the ruined human kingdom of Stromgarde. It serves as an active encampment for the Boulderfist ogres and their unusual allies among the Witherbark forest trolls. Rising just north of the crumbling ramparts of Stromgarde Keep, Boulder'gor is a steep bluff claimed by the Boulderfist clan. Within its shadows sits the Boulderfist Outpost mound, making it a central bastion of ogre power across the highlands. Uniquely, the ogres here share their fires and fortifications with forest trolls of the Witherbark tribe, including shadowy spellcasters who lend their dark magic to the clan's brute force. This mutual cooperation poses an ongoing danger to any travelers passing along the central roads of Arathi.

Boulder Lode Mine. Boulder Lode Mine is an aggressive excavation cut into the hills of the northeastern Barrens. Though orcish banners and watchtowers suggest the Horde first established the site, it is now firmly seized and operated by the ruthless Venture Company. The presence of weathered orcish architecture around the mouth of Boulder Lode Mine indicates that the Horde once held or founded the claim. Today, however, the area crawls with Venture Company overseers and enforcers working under the direction of Boss Copperplug. The goblin syndicate strip-mines the canyon with little regard for the local ecosystem or their workers, driven purely by the search for valuable minerals, high-yield gems, and industrial machinery.

Boulderfist Hall. Boulderfist Hall is a heavily fortified ogre mound nestled in the southern hills of the Arathi Highlands, just north of Thandol Span. It serves as the local stronghold for the Boulderfist ogres, who exert their brute influence across the neighboring trade routes and valleys under the command of Kor'gresh Coldrage. Carved into the rugged southern bluffs of the Arathi Highlands, Boulderfist Hall is the principal redoubt of the Boulderfist clan in the region. Sheltered within its earthen ramparts and deep caverns, ogre brutes and magi maintain a fortified settlement mere steps from Witherbark Village and the strategic bridge at Thandol Span. Deep within the mound lurks their regional chieftain, Kor'gresh Coldrage, alongside enforcers like Phalanax. From this stronghold, the ogres project violent control over the surrounding roads, making any peaceful transit between Arathi and the Wetlands perilous for travelers and supply caravans alike.

Boulderfist Outpost. Boulderfist Outpost is a fortified mound nestled deep within the ogre settlement of Boulder'gor in the Arathi Highlands. Serving as an interior den and holding area, it houses aggressive Boulderfist ogres alongside a few Witherbark trolls. Carved into the earth and stone of western Arathi, Boulderfist Outpost functions as the heart of Boulder'gor. While brute enforcers dominate the settlement above, the outpost's interior concentrates the clan's core strength and provides a dark subterranean shelter. A handful of Witherbark troll witch doctors occasionally mingle among the ogres here, hinting at tenuous tribal cooperation.

Boulderslide Cavern. Boulderslide Cavern is a subterranean warren tucked at the deepest end of Boulderslide Ravine in the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as the primary den and excavation site for the local Boulderslide kobolds, who obsessively tunnel in search of glowing mineral formations. The Boulderslide kobolds have burrowed deep into the crags of Stonetalon, establishing Boulderslide Cavern as their stronghold. Unlike ordinary vermin merely seeking shelter, these kobolds mine frantically for resonite, a rare glowing purple crystal embedded throughout the stone. The crystals pulse with lingering earthen magic, driving the creatures into a defensive frenzy against any intruders who approach their dig.

Boulderslide Ravine. Boulderslide Ravine is a rugged, secluded canyon tucked away in the central peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains, reached via Webwinder Path. Largely spared from the direct clashes between the Horde and Alliance, it serves as the rocky approach to Boulderslide Cavern and remains home to wild mountain beasts. Tucked away off Webwinder Path, Boulderslide Ravine is a narrow cut of rock in the Stonetalon heights. While loggers, night elves, and the Horde battle over timber and sacred glades throughout the region, this craggy pass remains relatively undisturbed by military forces. Wild mountain rams and roaming crag beasts like Cliff Stormers make up the local fauna, navigating the treacherous ledges and sheer stone walls. Prospectors also keep an eye on the ravine, as rich mineral veins frequently crop up along the rocky slopes leading deeper toward the cavern network.

Brackenwall Village. Brackenwall Village is the primary Horde outpost in Dustwallow Marsh, nestled among the bogs in the northwest corner of the zone. Founded by surviving Stonemaul ogres after dragons devastated their original settlement to the south, the village serves as a tenuous stronghold surrounded by Alliance spies, deserters, and the black dragonflight. When black dragonkin drove the Stonemaul ogres out of their ancient home at Stonemaul Village in the southern marsh, their leader, Overlord Mok'Morokk—successor to Rexxar—led the survivors north into the swamp to build Brackenwall. Formed around traditional earthen mounds, huts, and an old watchtower, the settlement gave the battered clan a defensible haven. Though aligned with the Horde, the village suffers from internal rot: Mok'Morokk sits idle, hoarding supplies and refusing to confront the draconic threat, leaving the clan's spiritual and tactical guidance to figures like the ogre mage Draz'Zilb and Horde emissaries.

Brackwell Pumpkin Patch. Brackwell Pumpkin Patch is an overrun farmstead in southeastern Elwynn Forest. Once home to the Brackwell family, the fields and cottage have been thoroughly seized by the Defias Brotherhood as an operational hideout. It serves as a meeting point for rogue conspirators and a staging ground for smuggling stolen gold. Situated southeast of the Stonefield homestead, the Brackwell farm was once a productive patch of Elwynn farmland. Today, the rightful owners have vanished without a trace, driven out or worse by the rising criminal tide. In their absence, the Defias Brotherhood claimed the farm's sturdy cottage and overgrown fields. The area functions as a safehouse and transfer post, where brigands regroup away from the watchful eyes of Goldshire's patrols. High-profile conspirators like Morgan the Collector use the isolated patch to receive shipments of illicitly gathered gold skimmed from the forest's mines.

Brambleblade Ravine. Brambleblade Ravine is a rugged canyon cutting into the northeastern edge of Red Cloud Mesa. It serves as a fortified den for the Bristleback quilboar tribe, who persistently raid the nearby tauren settlement of Camp Narache. Young tauren braves are sent here to prove their strength and protect their homeland from these fierce interlopers. Carved into the sun-scorched earth of Red Cloud Mesa, Brambleblade Ravine is choked with dense, thorny briars and quilboar encampments. The Bristleback tribe uses this natural fortress as a staging ground for raids against Camp Narache, threatening the safety of young tauren coming of age. Bristleback shamans and warriors, led by Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle, dwell deep within the ravine among trained battleboars. For the Shu'halo, striking into the heart of the canyon is a crucial rite of passage and a grim necessity to secure the plains.

Bramblescar. Bramblescar is a heavily fortified Razormane quilboar settlement situated in the southern Barrens. Thick, thorny brambles shield the encampment as its inhabitants wage a brutal war against the rival Bristleback tribe across the Gold Road. Carved into the jagged, giant briars of the southern Barrens, Bramblescar serves as a vital redoubt for the Razormane quilboar. These defensive brambles grow thick and sharp enough to deter casual wanderers, but the quilboar within are far from peaceful. Fiercely territorial and hostile to outsiders, they mount continuous skirmishes against anyone who ventures near their borders, viewing all non-quilboar as intruders upon land blessed by their ancient boar gods.

Brewnall Village. Brewnall Village is a small dwarven settlement nestled in Chill Breeze Valley near the entrance to Gnomeregan. Established by the Barleybrew family, this outpost serves as a proving ground for bold brewing experiments and regional defense against wild beasts. Despite being called a village, it functions largely as a rustic encampment in the snowy gnomish lowlands of Dun Morogh. Tucked away in the snowdrifts of Chill Breeze Valley, Brewnall Village lies squarely within the traditional gnomish reaches of western Dun Morogh. The settlement is home to the Barleybrew clan, stalwart dwarven brewers devoted to perfecting age-old recipes and crafting the ultimate stout. Though dubbed a village, the outpost consists mostly of tents and outdoor brewing equipment rather than permanent stone architecture. Between testing experimental batches of ale and defending against the ferocious local wolves and bears, the Barleybrews rely heavily on wandering mountaineers to gather rare ingredients and keep the valley secure.

Brightwater Lake. Brightwater Lake is the largest body of water in Tirisfal Glades, stretching across the mist-shrouded lowlands northeast of Brill. Once a tranquil retreat for the kingdom of Lordaeron, its waters now lie cold and dark, surrounding a central isle where an outcast necromancer conducts his forbidden research. Spanning the northern plains between the town of Brill and the Scarlet Watch Post, Brightwater Lake is a quiet and eerie landmark in the heart of Tirisfal. In the peaceful centuries under the Kingdom of Lordaeron, the lake served as a scenic country haven. Today, like the rest of the glades, its pristine character is long gone.
