The Plaguelands lie not far to the east, and the murky, chilled waters reflect only grey skies, withered trees, and the constant threat of roving murlocs and hostile undead.

Brightwood Grove. Brightwood Grove is a shadowed expanse of woodland located just west of Darkshire in Duskwood. Once part of the region's serene agrarian landscape, it is now infested with savage Nightbane worgen who make camp among ruined homesteads and attack any travelers wandering too close. Situated within sight of Darkshire's perimeter, Brightwood Grove represents the creeping peril threatening the town's borders. The homesteads and fences that once demarcated peaceful farmland now lie collapsed and rotting. In their place, crude camps have been erected by the Nightbane worgen, who prowl the overgrown clearings. The proximity of these wolf-beasts poses an ongoing threat to the town, forcing the Night Watch and passing adventurers to continually cull their numbers before the settlement is overrun.

Brill. Brill is the primary Forsaken settlement in the heart of Tirisfal Glades, situated just north of the Ruins of Lordaeron. Once a prosperous human town, it now serves as the administrative and military hub for newly awakened undead stepping beyond the confines of Deathknell. Before the Third War, Brill was a lively village under the sway of regional nobles such as the Barov and Agamand families. That prosperity ended when Kel'Thuzad chose the area for the Cult of the Damned's earliest experiments with the Plague of Undeath. The devastating blight swept through the population so quickly that local militia were driven out, leaving a sprawling mass graveyard in its wake. Now rebuilt by the Forsaken under the leadership of Magistrate Sevren, the town retains its weathered Lordaeron architecture beneath an atmosphere of grim purpose. Brill functions as the regional command center, coordinating defenses against Scarlet Crusade incursions, roaming Scourge remnants, and native beasts warped by necromantic decay.

Brill Town Hall. Brill Town Hall is the administrative heart of the settlement of Brill in central Tirisfal Glades. Standing as the most prominent structure in town, it serves as the civic headquarters from which the Forsaken govern their local holdings and coordinate the defense of the glades. While much of Lordaeron lies shattered and ruined, Brill Town Hall remains standing as a functioning civic center under undead rule. Inside, Magistrate Sevren directs town affairs from his podium, handing out vital commissions and directives to Forsaken adventurers. Aside from the Defiler's Den in the Arathi Highlands, it is one of the only recognized town halls in the known world actively run by the Forsaken, serving as a bleak parody and functional continuation of old Lordaeron's municipal bureaucracy.

Broken Hall. The Broken Hall serves as the flooded outer threshold of the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows. Shattered when the Great Dragon Aspect Ysera and her flight dragged the grand ziggurat beneath the waters, this ruin now stands deserted as the Atal'ai zealots retreat into deeper sanctums. When the green dragons brought down their wrath upon the Atal'ai priesthood and submerged their unholy ziggurat beneath the Pool of Tears, the outermost architecture bore the brunt of the cataclysm. The floor of the Broken Hall collapsed completely, allowing murky swamp waters to flood the chamber. Because of the damage and submersion, the troll cultists abandoned this entrance hall, withdrawing further into the complex. Adventurers entering the sunken temple must wade through these sodden ruins before mounting the stairs to reach the Hall of Masks.

Broken Pillar. The Broken Pillar is a weathered cluster of ancient troll ruins jutting from the dunes south of Gadgetzan. It serves as an isolated research post for the goblin prospector and scientist Marvon Rivetseeker, who studies the enigmatic artifacts buried beneath the surrounding sands. Rising out of the sands south of Gadgetzan and east of the treacherous Abyssal Sands, the Broken Pillar marks the remnants of ancient troll architecture long swallowed by Tanaris. Despite the desolate surroundings and encroaching desert beasts, the site offers rare clues to the continent's prehistoric civilisations. Marvon Rivetseeker, a goblin researcher originally based out of Ratchet, has established a lonely camp beside the shattered stonework to examine curious relics known as Gahz'ridian scattered across the waste.

Bronzebeard Encampment. Bronzebeard Encampment is a rugged dwarven outpost perched in southern Silithus, just east of the massive Scarab Wall. Staffed by hardy explorers and researchers from the Explorer's League, the camp serves as an operational base for investigating ancient silithid glyphs and the lingering mysteries buried beneath the desert sands. Positioned against the desolate southern bluffs of Silithus, Bronzebeard Encampment offers a rare refuge of dwarven grit in an otherwise hostile wasteland. Founded under the auspices of Ironforge's archaeological pursuits, the camp sits within sight of the towering Scarab Wall. Here, researchers like Rutgar Glyphshaper and Frankal Stonebridge braved scorching heat, scorpids, and encroaching silithid swarms to study the peculiar inscriptions and monuments left behind by forgotten civilizations.

Browman Mill. Browman Mill is a blighted lumber mill situated just north of Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. Once a thriving piece of Lordaeron's timber trade, it now swarms with undead minions under the iron grip of the Scourge. Its former proprietor, Stephen Browman, remains trapped in death within his ruined workshop. Before the Third War, Browman Mill served the surrounding towns and homesteads of Lordaeron, processing lumber harvested from the rich forests of the Eastweald. When the Scourge plague rolled across the kingdom, the mill fell alongside the rest of the province. Today, rotting timbers and shattered wheels sit idle while abominations, banshees, and skeletal warriors patrol the perimeter. Its close proximity to Light's Hope Chapel makes it a constant and menacing reminder of the undead horde pressing against the Argent Dawn's doorstep.

Bulwark. The Bulwark is a fortified outpost straddling the border between Tirisfal Glades and the Western Plaguelands. Maintained jointly by the Forsaken and the neutral Argent Dawn, it serves as the Horde's front line against the Scourge and the primary launching point for expeditions into the tainted east. Positioned squarely on the eastern border of Tirisfal Glades, the Bulwark is the final barrier protecting the Forsaken heartland from the blighted horrors of the Western Plaguelands. Today, rough wooden palisades and heavily armed guards defend the pass against roaming undead. It represents an uneasy but necessary collaboration, where Forsaken forces coordinate alongside the Argent Dawn to recruit seasoned champions of the Horde, turning back the minions of the Lich King before they spill into Tirisfal.

Burning Blade Coven. Tucked into the northern cliffs of the Valley of Trials, the Burning Blade Coven is an infested cave network threatening the Horde's newest recruits. Corrupted cultists and summoned demons lurk within, turning an old mineral cavern into a staging ground for dark magic right on Durotar's doorstep. The dusty red mountains rimming the Valley of Trials were once simply a testing wilderness for young orcs and Darkspear trolls taking their first steps in service to the Horde. In recent days, however, dark rituals have taken hold of the northern caves. Imps and lesser fiends spill from the cavern mouth, stirring chaos and threatening recruits. Led by the shadowy warlock Yarrog Baneshadow, the Burning Blade cult has entrenched itself deep inside, turning what was once a routine training ground into an active battleground against demonic corruption.

Caer Darrow. Caer Darrow is a fortified island situated in Darrowmere Lake in the Western Plaguelands. Formerly the aristocratic seat of the noble House Barov, the island's keep was secretly sold to Kel'Thuzad and transformed into the necromantic school of Scholomance, leaving the above-ground town plagued by wandering phantoms. Long before the Scourge, Caer Darrow was a strategic stronghold of Lordaeron that housed an ancient elven runestone. During the Second War, the Horde sacked the fortress and carved up the runestone to craft Gul'dan's Altars of Storms. When Lord Uther the Lightbringer sailed to offer relief to the survivors, his fleet was ambushed by Alterac privateers—an act of treachery that exposed Alterac's betrayal to the Alliance.

Calmbreeze Inn. Calmbreeze Inn refers to the primary establishments offering shelter and services across Zephras Isle, found in both Shen'dar Village and Valaanar. They serve as essential rest stops for travelers exploring the island, housing local trade trainers, innkeepers, and historical artifacts. The Calmbreeze Inns provide sanctuary amid the winding trails of Zephras Isle. In Shen'dar Village, the inn operates under Coriella Calmbreeze and doubles as a central hub where island tradesfolk gather, including mentors in herbalism, skinning, and enchanting. Across the way in Valaanar, another Calmbreeze Inn accommodates local wayfarers and shelters rare curios, including an audio crystal recording the history of the ancient rebellion in Eldre'Thalas.

Camp Aparaje. Camp Aparaje was once a peaceful tauren village nestled in the eastern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. Today, it lies overrun and occupied by the hostile Grimtotem tribe, who slaughtered the original settlers and took the outpost for themselves. Perched along the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, Camp Aparaje was established by peaceful tauren looking to live quietly in the highlands. That tranquility was shattered when raiders from the nearby Grimtotem Post, led by Grundig Darkcloud, launched a brutal and unprovoked assault. The villagers were butchered or driven away, and survivors such as Makaba Flathoof were left mourning the destruction of their home while dreading the fate of captive kin.

Camp E'thok. Camp E'thok is a Galak centaur settlement located in northwestern Thousand Needles. The aggressive centaur tribe uses this canyon encampment as a base to stage ambushes against passing caravans traveling through the riverbed below. Tucked into the rugged northwestern reaches of Thousand Needles, Camp E'thok serves as a key settlement for the hostile Galak centaur. Like their kin across Kalimdor, the Galak are relentlessly predatory, preying upon any travelers wandering into the canyon shadows. The camp is notorious for orchestrating raids against merchant caravans, notably ambushing the goblin Wizlo Bearingshiner and seizing his goods—though his prized gadget managed to slip beyond their grasp, guarded by his fierce pet panther.

Camp Kosh. Camp Kosh is an ogre encampment in the northern Badlands, inhabited by the aggressive Dustbelcher ogres. Perched near vital travel routes, its brutes prey on passing caravans and scavenge whatever equipment travelers leave behind in the harsh desert. Situated in the northern wastes of the Badlands, Camp Kosh serves as the northernmost settlement of the Dustbelcher ogres, who also occupy neighboring camps like Boff, Cagg, and Wurg. The ogres stationed here take advantage of their proximity to the roads, raiding vulnerable supply lines journeying toward Kargath or westward into the Searing Gorge. When dwarven prospectors led by Sigrun Ironhew were forced to flee the excavation at Uldaman, the brutes of Camp Kosh swiftly raided their abandoned wagons, hauling away precious food rations and armaments into the dusty encampment.

Camp Mojache. Camp Mojache is the primary Horde outpost in Feralas, established as a fortified tauren settlement along the waters feeding Wildwind Lake. It provides shelter, provisions, and flight connections to travelers contending with the untamed wilderness, aggressive wildlife, and ancient ruins of the deep forest. Situated in eastern Feralas along a swift-flowing stream that feeds Wildwind Lake, Camp Mojache is a tauren settlement built to secure a foothold in the wild southern forest. While the dense jungle holds perilous threats—from savage wildlife to Gordunni ogres and aggressive Woodpaw gnolls—the camp stands as an island of safety. Equipped with lodging, trade masters, and a wind rider roost, it serves as the vital logistical hub for Horde champions operating in the region.

Camp Narache. Camp Narache is a secluded village nestled upon Red Cloud Mesa in southern Mulgore. It serves as the ancestral home of the Hawkwind tribe and the proving ground where young tauren begin their training. Sheltered high above the plains, the camp maintains ancient traditions while constantly guarding against encroaching quilboar and lingering centaur threats. Situated at the northern edge of the elevated Red Cloud Mesa, Camp Narache is the primary settlement of the Hawkwind tribe. The village consists of several large hide lodges and pavilions, including a communal tent for wounded braves, an armory, a bakery tent, and a spirit lounge dedicated to meditation and ancestral communion. At the center of the camp, tribal elders and path trainers stand in a circle at the heart of the camp, where the venerable Greatmother Hawkwind still offers guidance, guiding newly initiated youth as they step into their roles as defenders of the Earth Mother.

Camp Taurajo. Camp Taurajo is a quiet tauren settlement nestled in the southern Barrens, sitting right along the mountain pass leading west into Mulgore. It serves as a vital frontier haven, offering tired wanderers an inn, supplies, profession mentors, and wind rider transit between the plains and central Kalimdor. Situated at the eastern mouth of the pass to Mulgore, Camp Taurajo is often the first glimpse of the wider Barrens seen by young tauren venturing out from Bloodhoof Village. Surrounded by dry scrubland and rugged mesas, the camp operates as both an outpost and a trading hub. It shelters hunters, leathercrafters, and field herbalists while maintaining wind rider connections to Thunder Bluff, the Crossroads, and Freewind Post deeper south.

Camp Wurg. Camp Wurg is an ogre encampment situated in the arid expanse of the Badlands. It serves as one of several outposts claimed by the territorial Dustbelcher ogres who dominate much of the Badlands. Tucked among the crags of the Badlands, Camp Wurg is one of four primary camps settled by the Dustbelcher ogres, alongside Camp Cagg, Camp Boff, and Camp Kosh. The ogres stationed here guard their rugged territory fiercely, scavenging what they can from the unforgiving desert wastes. While rank-and-file brutes and enforcers dwell around the crude fires and rough hides of Wurg, their chieftain, Boss Tho'grun, maintains no permanent seat here, instead roaming the Badlands trails to keep watch over all his encampments.

Canals (Stormwind City). The Canals are a network of stone-lined waterways weaving through Stormwind City, separating its distinct districts. They serve as quiet thoroughfares for pedestrians and anglers, while quietly harboring hidden hazards and the entrance to the city's prison. The Canals link and define the districts of Stormwind, dividing the bustling markets of the Trade District from the aged alleys of Old Town, the cathedral gardens, and the Dwarven District. Stone bridges, archways, and waterside walkways frame quiet establishments like the Gallina Winery, tailor shops, and quiet residential homes. In addition to serving local merchants and recreational fishermen, the waterways conceal the fortified entrance to the Stockade, where Stormwind's most dangerous criminals and rebels are held beneath street level.

Canals (Undercity). The Canals form a murky, circular moat winding between the distinct quarters of the Undercity. Filled with an unnatural, noxious green slime rather than fresh water, they serve as both a sewage system and a grim symbol of the Forsaken's subterranean stronghold. Carved into the subterranean depths beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, the Canals encircle the heart of the Undercity, dividing its quarters with wide channels of sluggish green sludge. While mortal cities channel flowing river water to clean their avenues, the Forsaken have filled these stone conduits with industrial refuse, chemical runoff, and alchemical waste. The liquid emits a faint, sickly glow and foul vapors, making it impossible to traverse by ordinary magical means like water walking. Despite the lethality of the slurry, desperate anglers occasionally haul bizarre, tainted curiosities from the muck.

Cape of Stranglethorn. The Cape of Stranglethorn forms the sun-baked southern tip of Stranglethorn Vale, stretching south from the Gurubashi Arena down to the ocean cliffs. Anchored by the sprawling pirate port of Booty Bay, the region is a battleground contested by goblins, Bloodsail Buccaneers, ancient jungle trolls, and encroaching wildlife. South of the ancient colosseum of Gurubashi Arena, the dense jungle gives way to the coastline known as the Cape of Stranglethorn. Dotted with crumbling troll settlements like the Ruins of Jubuwal and the Ruins of Aboraz, the cape has long since slipped from imperial Gurubashi control. Today, its beaches, coves, and jungle clearings host a chaotic mix of dangerous predators, murloc encampments, and rival pirate crews warring over trade routes and buried plunder.

Capital Gardens. The Capital Gardens form the western wing of the ancient elven ruins of Dire Maul in Feralas. Once a serene, manicured park for the Kaldorei nobility, it has withered into a blighted woodland stalked by corrupted ancients, ghosts, and remnants of the Shen'dralar. Ten millennia ago, Eldre'Thalas stood as one of the shining jewels of the Kaldorei empire. The Capital Gardens served as its outdoor district, lush with enchanted flora and grand marble terraces where Highborne sorcerers debated and relaxed. Following the Great Sundering, the enclave fell on desperate times. Deprived of the Well of Eternity, the resident Shen'dralar turned to dark magic to sustain their immortality, letting the gardens wither away. Today, gray, twisted boughs and corrupted treants fill the broken courtyards, while residual magical corruption prevents the forest from ever truly healing.

Cathedral of Light. The Cathedral of Light is the spiritual heart of Stormwind City and the primary sanctuary of the Church of the Holy Light. Standing tall over Cathedral Square, it serves as the central bastion for human priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Rebuilt after its devastation during the First War under the guidance of Archbishop Alonsus Faol and then-Bishop Benedictus, the Cathedral of Light stands as a towering beacon of resilience. With the fall of Lordaeron to the Scourge during the Third War, the seat of the Church shifted south to Stormwind. Today, Archbishop Benedictus shepherds the faithful from this grand hall, providing spiritual guidance to the entire Alliance.

Cathedral Square. Cathedral Square is the spiritual and civic heart of Stormwind City, dominated by the majestic Cathedral of Light. Beyond serving as a place of worship and devotion, the bustling plaza houses municipal institutions like City Hall, the city orphanage, and the regional headquarters of the Argent Dawn. Situated northwest of the Trade District and southeast of the Dwarven District, Cathedral Square serves as the epicenter of faith in the Kingdom of Stormwind. Dominating the skyline is the Cathedral of Light, the preeminent sanctuary for followers of the Holy Light across Azeroth. Priests, paladins, and healers gather here to study, pray, and train. Citizens, pilgrims, and local schoolchildren led by School Mistress Danna regularly mingle in the square for conversation and contemplation.

Cauldron. The Cauldron is a massive open-pit excavation site dominating the center of the Searing Gorge. Operated by the Dark Iron clan, this fiery quarry is worked day and night by broken slaves under the watch of cruel overseers and roving elementals. Carved deep into the scorched earth of the Searing Gorge, the Cauldron was fortified following the catastrophic summoning of Ragnaros by Emperor Thaurissan. Massive, smoke-belching Dark Iron excavation machinery rims the canyon walls, scraping rock and ore from the smoldering stone. Down within its burning crevices, living fire and magma elementals prowl alongside Dark Iron taskmasters, while subterranean heat rises continuously from the depths of the mountain.

Cavern of Mists. The Cavern of Mists is the expansive outer antechamber leading into the depths of the Wailing Caverns. Fed by subterranean geysers that erupt through the rock, its central pool and hanging fog harbor strange, mutated wildlife roaming just outside the portal threshold. Before descending into the true heart of the Wailing Caverns, travelers must navigate the Cavern of Mists. Thick, warm vapor hangs permanently in the air, fed by natural geysers erupting from the cavern floor into a deep central pool. Though it serves as an entryway, it is far from peaceful. Swarms of raptors, serpents, oozes, and semi-aquatic threshadons wander the ledges and waters, alongside notorious beasts like the hydra Trigore the Lasher. It provides adventurers an ominous preview of the unnatural growth festering deeper below.

Caverns of Time. Tucked into the eastern cliffs of Tanaris, the Caverns of Time serve as the mystical lair of Nozdormu and the bronze dragonflight. Within its winding depths, the dragons monitor and safeguard the fragile timeways of Azeroth against any mortal intrusion or temporal tampering. Carved deep beneath the desert cliffs, the Caverns of Time are a nexus where the currents of history converge. Charged by the titans at the dawn of the world, Nozdormu the Timeless One and his bronze dragonflight act as eternal sentinels over these corridors. Inside, time behaves erratically; glimpses of past and future slip through hidden rifts, and relics plucked from distant eras lie scattered across the sands. While the great wyrm Anachronos keeps watch near the entrance, lesser bronze drakes patrol the winding descent, fiercely protective of the one true timeline.

Cenarion Enclave. The Cenarion Enclave is the verdant northwestern district of Darnassus, serving as the central gathering place and seat of power for the Cenarion Circle in the capital. While Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage lies slumbering within the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the night elven druids from the great hollows and living boughs of this grove. Occupying a high terrace above the Temple Gardens, the Cenarion Enclave is shaped from ancient oaks and ashes marked with runic bark. Convocations of the Cenarion Circle gather within structures molded directly from living wood and stone. With Malfurion Stormrage absent in the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm oversees affairs here, pushing his ambitious vision for Teldrassil despite lingering political friction with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Beyond the druids who meditate among its streams, the enclave also hosts the capital's elven hunters and the stables where skilled riders learn to tame Darnassian nightsabers.

Cenarion Hold. Cenarion Hold is the fortified stronghold of the Cenarion Circle situated in the harsh desert of Silithus. Established to keep watch over ancient dangers buried beneath the sands, it stands as one of the largest druidic settlements on Kalimdor and a rare safe haven in an unforgiving wasteland. Perched among the desolate sands of Silithus, Cenarion Hold serves as the southern command hub for the Cenarion Circle. Reached by winding past Un'Goro Crater, the fortress was raised to monitor the dormant threats sealed beneath the desert after the historic War of the Shifting Sands. In an inhospitable expanse teeming with insectoid silithid and arid storms, the stronghold provides vital shelter, trade, and logistical support for night elf and tauren druids alike who stand sentinel over the imprisoned horrors of the past.

Chamber of Atonement. The Chamber of Atonement is the grim entrance hall to the Graveyard wing within the Scarlet Monastery. Here, beneath stone arches hung with iron chains, the Scarlet Crusade subjects captured undead and other perceived heretics to brutal interrogation and torture before casting their remains into the cloister beyond. Serving as the threshold to the Forlorn Cloister, the Chamber of Atonement is far from a sanctuary of peaceful prayer. Instead, the Scarlet Crusade has converted the grand entryway into a house of pain, outfitted with racks, shackles, and burning braziers. Zealous inquisitors use these instruments to extract confessions and torment captives, viewing excruciating pain as the only fitting penance for unholy beings. The chamber echoes constantly with the cries of the damned, presided over by cruel taskmasters who ensure that those who enter rarely walk out whole.

Champions' Hall. Tucked away in the southern reaches of Old Town, the Champions' Hall serves as the officer's barracks and supply armory for the Alliance's decorated veterans in Stormwind. Beyond its threshold, quartermasters dispense specialized weapons, plate, and regalia to proven warriors of the faction. Access is strictly guarded, reserved only for officers who have demonstrated valor on the field of war. Hidden behind a guarded threshold in Old Town, the Champions' Hall is a restricted haven for the Alliance's most distinguished combatants. Military commanders gather here over tactical maps of Azeroth to confer on ongoing campaigns, flanked by armaments and the grand insignias of rank. Only soldiers who have climbed the Alliance hierarchy to achieve officer status—specifically the rank of Knight or higher—are permitted entry. Inside, military quartermasters supply battle-hardened soldiers with elite arms, armor, and mounts crafted specifically to turn the tide against the Horde in contested zones across the world.

Charred Vale. The Charred Vale is a smoldering valley in southwestern Stonetalon Mountains, devastated by the reckless deforestation and machinery of the Venture Company. Once a thriving haven for treants and chimaeras, it is now engulfed in flames, roving elementals, and hostile harpies. Not long ago, this southwest basin was a flourishing alpine wood guarded by majestic treants and inhabited by native chimaeras and harpies. Its ruin began with the arrival of the Venture Company. The greedy goblin outfit clear-cut the forest with explosive machinery, corrupting the guardians and awakening chaotic fire elementals. Though the treants eventually forced the goblins back, the land was left broken, scarred by fire, and tainted by whatever foul devices the retreating loggers deployed.

Chill Breeze Valley. Chill Breeze Valley is a rugged, snow-covered pass in western Dun Morogh linking the dwarven settlement of Kharanos with the embattled city of Gnomeregan. While its main path is a well-traveled thoroughfare for young travelers and refugees, its secluded recesses harbor dangerous beasts and bloody dens. Chill Breeze Valley forms a T-shaped trench through the mountains of western Dun Morogh. The main east-west trail sees steady foot traffic from novice dwarves and gnomes journeying between Kharanos and the outskirts of Gnomeregan. However, straying into the valley's north-south offshoot is another matter entirely. Strewn with bloodstains and mangled carcasses, these shadowy reaches harbor ferocious predators—most notably savage wendigos that lair in deep ice caves and prey on anyone reckless enough to wander into their hunting grounds.

Chillwind Camp. Chillwind Camp sits at the southern pass leading into the Western Plaguelands from the Alterac Mountains. Manned by an Alliance contingent working alongside the Argent Dawn, it serves as the final safe staging ground before the blighted ruins of Lordaeron. From this precarious outpost, commanders direct strikes against the nearby Scourge strongholds and plague cauldrons. Tucked into the rocky pass descending from Chillwind Point, Chillwind Camp is the first line of defense and primary base of operations for Alliance forces pushing into the Western Plaguelands. Though physically separated from the worst of the corruption by the high mountain ridges, the dead chill of the north hangs heavily over the tents and palisades. Under Commander Ashlam Valorfist, a sparse garrison of soldiers, scouts, and Argent Dawn specialists attempts to contain the horrors lingering along the King's Road and gather the intelligence necessary to reclaim Lordaeron's fallen fields.

Chillwind Point. Chillwind Point is a rocky rise and ancient troll ruin sitting on the high frontier between the Alterac Mountains, Hillsbrad Foothills, and the Western Plaguelands. It gets its name from the freezing drafts howling through the mountain pass out of the blighted north. Today, it serves as a lonely vantage point inhabited primarily by a lone troll mystic. Perched on the borderlands where Hillsbrad gives way to Alterac and the plagued north, Chillwind Point looks out over the mountain ravine leading directly into the Western Plaguelands. Long before Lordaeron claimed these passes, ancient trolls built stone structures upon these heights, the remnants of which still stand weather-beaten against the elements. Today, cold winds blow south through the ravine, carrying the chill of the fallen north into the foothill valleys below.

Circle of Aquementas. The Circle of Aquementas is a mysterious ring of upright standing stones positioned along the eastern shoreline of Tanaris, just south of Lost Rigger Cove. It serves as a ritual site where travelers can call forth the elemental spirit Aquementas. Tucked away along the windswept eastern coast of Tanaris, the Circle of Aquementas sits quietly south of the pirate stronghold at Lost Rigger Cove. Composed of weathered, upright stones arranged in a circular formation, this unusual site hums with elemental energy against the desert shore. It acts as a focus for summoning Aquementas, an elemental entity tied to an ancient artifact. While the surrounding beaches crawl with Southsea brigands and roaming sea creatures, the circle itself remains a solemn pocket of ritual power amidst the dunes.

Circle of East Binding. The Circle of East Binding is a mysterious ancient ritual site situated in the eastern reaches of the Arathi Highlands, just southwest of Hammerfall. Anchored by the Stone of East Binding, the site is violently contested and guarded by roaming water elementals known as cresting exiles. Positioned amidst the rugged highlands east of Stromgarde, the Circle of East Binding is one of several ancient sites of power scattered across the Arathi basin. At its focal point stands the Stone of East Binding, an enigmatic monument radiating potent elemental magic. Swirling water elementals known as cresting exiles roam the surrounding earth and fiercely defend the stone against any mortals who dare approach.

Circle of Inner Binding. The Circle of Inner Binding is an ancient ring of ritual stones situated in the southern hills of the Arathi Highlands, just east of Stromgarde Keep. Guarded by hostile earth elementals, it holds the Stone of Inner Binding, the most potent seal used to restrain the imprisoned elemental princess Myzrael deep beneath the earth. Perched upon a plateau south of the main road, the Circle of Inner Binding anchors the strongest of the ancient wards sealing Myzrael beneath Arathi. Towering slabs surround the central Stone of Inner Binding, which thrums with dense geo-magical power. Enormous rumbling earth elementals patrol the stones relentlessly, drawn to the site's resonance or bound as guardians. Despite these potent wards, cracks in this inner seal permit the trapped entity beneath the Highlands to reach out telepathically, whispering pleas for freedom to unsuspecting wanderers who handle shards of its stone.

Circle of West Binding. The Circle of West Binding is one of several ancient ritual sites scattered across the Arathi Highlands, situated near Thoradin's Wall. Centered around the Stone of West Binding, this arcane ring is overrun by fiery elemental entities bound to the site. Tucked against the rugged slopes near Thoradin's Wall, the Circle of West Binding forms part of a wider network of ritual sites dispersed throughout the Arathi Highlands. At its heart sits the Stone of West Binding, an ancient relic tied to elemental containment. The grounds are swarming with Burning Exiles—volatile fire elementals that relentlessly guard the perimeter, making any approach to the stone a perilous endeavor for travelers traversing the western plains.

Clean Zone. The Clean Zone is a fortified, decontamination enclave nestled inside the ruined city of Gnomeregan just past the upper Hall of Gears. It serves as the sole safe haven within the irradiated facility where uncorrupted gnomish forces hold ground against surrounding troggs and leper gnomes. Here, field medics, technicians, and specialized Sparklematic machines offer respite and salvage operations amid the radioactive ruins. While most of Gnomeregan succumbed to Mekkatorque's disastrous venting of radioactive waste, the Clean Zone remains untainted. Positioned strategically between the trogg-infested Dormitory below and the contested corridors of the Hall of Gears above, it acts as a fortified forward base. Resolute gnome defenders, technicians, and field medics hold the barricades day and night, ensuring Alliance expeditions have a stable staging ground to regroup, mend wounds, and maintain machinery.

Cleft. The Cleft is a darkened hollow located northwest of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Once a tranquil corner of the boughs, it has been claimed by the corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs, who use it as a stronghold to ambush travelers moving along the main highway toward Darnassus. Situated off the highway between Dolanaar and Darnassus, the Cleft has turned into one of the most perilous dens on the world tree. Driven mad by the foul taint spreading through Teldrassil, the resident Gnarlpine furbolgs have fortified this hollow. From this redoubt, the maddened beasts terrorize the local roads, threatening to cut Dolanaar off from the capital.

Cleft of Shadow. Tucked deep within the subterranean caverns beneath Orgrimmar, the Cleft of Shadow houses the city's practitioners of stealth, sorcery, and demonology. Far from the proud warrior ethos of Thrall's upper districts, it serves as a necessary haven for rogues and warlocks operating in the shadows of the Horde. While Thrall's new Horde champions honor, shamanism, and strength of arms, practical leadership demands a place for subtler arts. Carved into the damp stone caverns below the capital, the Cleft of Shadow hosts the Shadowswift Brotherhood of rogues and the Darkfire Enclave of warlocks. Kept away from the everyday bustle of the valley districts, this dark quarter allows practitioners of poison and fel energy to ply their trades out of direct public view while remaining under the watchful eye of Orgrimmar's leadership.

Cliffspring Falls. Cliffspring Falls marks the dramatic origin of Darkshore's vital Cliffspring River, tumbling down from the eastern cliffs into the coastal forest. Long celebrated as the principal source of clean drinking water for the region, its waters have recently fallen victim to a foul, spreading taint. The subterranean cavern feeding the waterfall has become infested with hostile naga and shadowy Twilight's Hammer cultists. Pouring out from caverns perched high in the rocky bluffs along Darkshore's eastern border, Cliffspring Falls feeds the Cliffspring River, which winds westward across the woods to empty into the sea. Traditionally, this cascade provided the purest drinking water for local night elf settlements. In recent times, however, the waters have turned foul and murky, spreading sickness and ecological decay throughout the river basin. Investigating naturalists have discovered that the cave network at the falls' headwaters is overrun by vile naga and dark cultists, who plot in the shadows while demonic corruption from neighboring Felwood threatens to seep through the highland bedrock.

Clockwerk Run. The Clockwerk Run is the main entrance corridor leading into the heart of fallen Gnomeregan. Stretching between the Train Depot and the Hall of Gears, this damaged hallway is heavily contaminated by toxic fallout and overrun with irradiated troggs. Serving as the primary gateway into Gnomeregan from the outer train depot, the Clockwerk Run was once a bustling conduit of gnomish logistics and transit. When High Tinker Mekkatorque ordered the venting of radioactive waste to stem the trogg invasion, the corridor became a lethal trap. The blast and subsequent fighting caused portions of the hallway to collapse onto itself. Today, the passage is choked with toxic fumes and prowling irradiated troggs, making it the perilous frontline that any expedition must fight through to reach the upper Hall of Gears.

Cold Hearth Manor. Cold Hearth Manor is a blighted farmstead located just west of Brill along the main road of Tirisfal Glades. Once a bustling, hospitable estate known for bountiful crops, the outbreak of the Plague of Undeath wiped out its residents, leaving the surrounding fields choked with mindless Scourge. Today, the Forsaken have secured the main farmhouse as an outpost and waystation for travelers. Before the Third War, this homestead bore a reputation for warmth and hospitality, supporting rich harvests in the heart of Lordaeron. When the Plague swept through the kingdom, the entire family and their laborers succumbed, rising again as husks bound to the Scourge. While feral undead still stumble through the ruined fields, Forsaken forces managed to push the mindless dead out of the main farmhouse, reclaiming the structure to serve as a trading post and foothold along the road toward the eastern glades.

Coldridge Pass. Coldridge Pass is a rugged, snowbound tunnel cutting through the southern mountain ridge of Dun Morogh. It serves as the sole overland route connecting the secluded training grounds of Coldridge Valley to the rest of the kingdom, emerging near the bustling town of Kharanos. Because hostile troggs have overrun the passage, any traveler attempting the journey must either fight their way through or make a desperate dash for the other side. For young dwarven recruits and gnome novices taking their first steps beyond Coldridge Valley, Coldridge Pass is a harsh rite of passage. Chiseled straight through the rock, this tunnel forms the primary link sending newly trained adventurers eastward toward the frontier hub of Kharanos. What was once a secure mountain corridor has become a perilous choke point, infested with aggressive troggs that have pushed up from dark sub-terrains to menace any soul trying to travel between the sheltered valley and the wider reaches of Dun Morogh.

Coldridge Valley. Coldridge Valley is a sheltered, snow-covered vale tucked into the southwestern heights of Dun Morogh. Centered around the hamlet of Anvilmar, it serves as the training ground where young dwarves and gnome refugees first take up arms in service of Ironforge. A single tunnel, Coldridge Pass, connects this secluded hollow to the wider mountain realm. Cradled by sheer mountain cliffs, Coldridge Valley remains largely cut off from the bustling trade routes of Dun Morogh. At its heart sits Anvilmar, a sturdy stone hall and hamlet where veteran dwarven instructors and displaced gnome scholars train fresh recruits in the arts of battle, stealth, and sorcery. Outside the warmth of Anvilmar's hearths, the valley floor is carpeted in thick snow and prowled by boars and hungry winter wolves, providing novices with their first real taste of frontier survival.

Command Center. The Command Center, often referred to as the Stormwind Barracks, stands in the heart of Old Town as the operational headquarters for the city's military officers. In peacetime, it houses the standing army, but with Stormwind's forces dispatched to distant frontiers, it currently operates with a seasoned skeleton crew focused on drilling recruits and local militia. Situated within the weathered streets of Old Town, the Command Center serves as the primary garrison and martial training ground for the kingdom of Stormwind. Normally packed with regular infantry and ranking officers, the facility is uncharacteristically sparse. With much of the royal army committed to campaigns abroad, the barracks relies on a veteran cadre of instructors—including Ander Germaine and martial artist Wu Shen—to train fresh warriors to bolster the city's defenses.

Commons. The Commons serves as the vibrant commercial heart of Ironforge, connecting the city entrance directly to its vast caverns. Teeming with merchants, travelers, and bankers, it is the busiest thoroughfare in the dwarven capital and the central marketplace for the entire Alliance. Located just northeast of the Gates of Ironforge, the Commons is the first district that greets travelers entering the mountain kingdom. Carved directly out of the stone, this bustling market street houses the primary Alliance Auction House, the Stonefire Tavern, and the city's central bank within the Vault of Ironforge. Broad avenues connect it seamlessly to the Great Forge, the Mystic Ward, and the Military Ward, ensuring that nearly all foot traffic in the mountain passes through its bustling storefronts.

Corin's Crossing. Corin's Crossing is a ruined human settlement situated at a major crossroads in south-central Eastern Plaguelands. Once a thriving waystation between Stratholme, Tyr's Hand, Darrowshire, and Andorhal, the devastated town is now utterly overrun by the Scourge. Its crumbling town hall and forge harbor lingering horrors, including invisible spectral watchers. Before the Third War, Corin's Crossing served as a central junction for travel across eastern Lordaeron. Positioned between the shimmering waters of Lake Mereldar and what has now become the blighted chasm of the Infectis Scar, its thoroughfares once bore merchants, couriers, and pilgrims traveling between the great bastion of Stratholme and the southern strongholds. When the plague swept through the province, the settlement stood directly in the path of destruction, collapsing swiftly beneath the sheer weight of the undead vanguard.

Corrahn's Dagger. Corrahn's Dagger is the second ridge among the four mountainous fingers towering over northern Hillsbrad Foothills. This high ground serves as a hideout for rogue Syndicate operatives. Rising steeply in northern Hillsbrad Foothills, Corrahn's Dagger is the second of the four rocky projections known locally as the fingers of Hillsbrad. The ridge is overrun by cutthroats belonging to the Syndicate, who use the elevated perch to overlook the valley below.

Craftsmen's Terrace. The Craftsmen's Terrace is the bustling artisan district situated in the northern reaches of Darnassus. It serves as the primary trade and manufacturing hub for the night elf capital, housing workshops, profession trainers, and a lively inn. The district also hosts external representatives, including an embassy for the neutral Argent Dawn. Spanning the northern edge of the canopy city, the Craftsmen's Terrace gathers the diverse trades that keep Darnassus running. Woodworkers, leathercrafters, alchemists, and other artisans operate their shops here, integrating classic night elven methods with practical craft. The district also provides essential community amenities, including an inn, a guild master, and guild petition vendors. Bridges connect the terrace directly to the Cenarion Enclave to the west and the Warrior's Terrace to the south.

Crag of the Everliving. The Crag of the Everliving is a verdant cavern chamber nestled deep within the Wailing Caverns. Dominated by lush, corrupted flora and predatory plant creatures, it serves as the domain of the Fanglord Lord Pythas. Its towering upper reaches shelter the ancient entity after whom the crag is named. While much of the Wailing Caverns is carved of damp subterranean stone, the Crag of the Everliving bursts with unruly, twisted vegetation fueled by the Nightmare corrupting Naralex's slumber. Towering mossy platforms and winding paths are choked with Deviate Shamblers—living plant hulks prowling the undergrowth. Lord Pythas, one of Naralex's fallen disciples, watches over the crag's central reaches, having traded his noble druidic vows for the venomous rites of the Druids of the Fang.

Cragpool Lake. Cragpool Lake is a body of water tucked inside Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. Looming above its dark waters sits a massive timber structure erected by the Venture Company. Nestled within Windshear Crag, Cragpool Lake lies directly beneath the towering logging apparatus built by the Venture Company. An enormous wooden structure spans above the water, serving as the vantage point from which Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle oversees operations across the mountain valley. Venture Company workers occupy the platforms overhead.

Crossroads. The Crossroads is the beating heart of Horde travel through central Kalimdor, situated where the north-south Gold Road intersects the path from Ratchet to the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as a bustling trading outpost, military staging area, and transit hub for travelers journeying between Durotar, Mulgore, and northern frontlines. True to its name, the Crossroads sits squarely at the crossing of the Gold Road and the east-west route cutting from the goblin port of Ratchet into the Stonetalon Mountains. Despite having modest lodgings, the outpost functions as a bustling regional hub. Wind rider masters, merchants, blacksmiths, and trainers maintain permanent setups beneath its watchtowers. For young warriors traveling out from Durotar or Mulgore, the settlement is often the first place they witness the vast, multi-front logistics binding the new Horde together.

Crown Guard Tower. Crown Guard Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower in the southern Eastern Plaguelands. The Scourge destroyed it during the invasion of Lordaeron in the Third War, and its broken stones have stood amid the blight ever since. Once part of the Kingdom of Lordaeron's defenses, Crown Guard Tower was a scout tower watching over the lands of eastern Lordaeron. When the Scourge overran the kingdom, the tower was destroyed and left in ruins, one of several fallen towers scattered across what are now the Eastern Plaguelands. Its charred stones stand in a land the undead still hold.

Crusader Outpost. Crusader Outpost is a fortified watchtower perched atop the rugged hills of eastern Tirisfal Glades. Manned by zealous members of the Scarlet Crusade, it guards the approaches leading toward their stronghold at the Scarlet Monastery. From this height, Crusaders observe travel along the road and stand ready to repel any Forsaken incursion. Built into the bluffs overlooking the eastern road, the Crusader Outpost serves as a primary early-warning station for the Scarlet Crusade. From their elevated tower, sentries watch over movement between Brill and the eastern reaches of Lordaeron, ensuring that wandering undead or scouting parties are spotted long before reaching the Monastery gates. The tower also grants the garrison tactical flanking capability against any force seeking to march up the valley toward their holy bastion.

Crusader's Armory. The Crusader's Armory is a fortified interior hall within the Scarlet Monastery Armory wing. Stockpiled with munitions, gunpowder, and cannonballs, it serves as a staging ground for the zealots guarding the path toward the inner sanctum. Beyond its locked iron door lies the Hall of Champions. Situated between the Footman's Armory and the grand Hall of Champions, the Crusader's Armory displays the full military readiness of the Scarlet Crusade. Unlike the training yards outside, these narrow stone corridors are packed to the ceiling with crates of volatile gunpowder, stacked cannonballs, and heavily armed crusaders ready to repel intruders. The Crusade has turned a former monastic compound into a bristling fortress, dedicating every available hall to the tools of total war. At the far end of the armory stands a heavy locked iron door, barring entry to the inner chambers unless one holds the Scarlet Key.

Crusader's Outpost. Crusader's Outpost is a fortified scout tower manned by the Scarlet Crusade in western Tirisfal Glades. Situated adjacent to the Solliden Farmstead, it serves as the Crusade's westernmost position in all of Lordaeron. Its perilous distance from the main Scarlet bastions leaves its garrison isolated in the heart of hostile Forsaken territory. Perched inside the western Tirisfal hills just north of Deathknell, this stone tower represents the farthest reach of the Scarlet Crusade's power in Lordaeron. The garrison stationed here works in tandem with the surviving human laborers of the nearby Solliden Farmstead, attempting to hold back the encroaching undead. From the top of the tower, lookouts keep watch over the surrounding pumpkin fields and forest paths, vigilant against both roaming Scourge fiends and patrols from the Undercity.

Crypt (Badlands). Tucked away high in the dusty hills of the Badlands lies a secluded underground tomb known simply as the Crypt. Inside rests the silent remnant of an ancient warrior: an armored skeleton seated upon a stone throne, flanked by urns, chests, and a massive relic sword. Perched southeast of Hammertoe's Digsite along an unmarked earthen path rising up the hillside, the Badlands Crypt is easily missed by passersby. Down in its dark stone chambers sits an armored skeleton poised atop a throne. Resting beside the remains is the Sword of the Barbarian King, surrounded by scattered bones, urns, and forgotten chests. While miners and adventurers frequent the surrounding gullies in search of dwarven ruins and riches, the true origin and history of this seated sovereign remain a mystery lost to the arid wastes.

Crypt (Stromgarde Keep). Deep within the ruins of Stromgarde Keep lies the royal crypt, situated past the sanctum chapel in the heart of the district held by the surviving Stromgarde defenders. It holds the tomb of the fallen King Thoras Trollbane and the ancestral treasures of his dynasty. Guarded closely by Prince Galen and faithful caretakers, the vault remains a sanctuary of royal honor amid a shattered kingdom. Hidden beneath the Sanctum of Stromgarde Keep, this subterranean burial vault serves as the final resting place of King Thoras Trollbane, the warrior monarch who led Stromgarde through the Second War. Despite the devastation engulfing the city—split among Syndicate rogues and Boulderfist ogres—the remaining Stromgarde militia fiercely maintains their grip on this quarter. Prince Galen Trollbane personally watches over the crypts alongside dedicated royal caretakers, ensuring his father's body and legacy remain undisturbed by the scavengers and enemies outside.

Crystal Lake. Crystal Lake is a body of water lying just east of Goldshire in the heart of Elwynn Forest. While once a peaceful spot, its shores have been overrun by aggressive murlocs, turning it into a frequent hazard for local villagers and passing travelers. Situated within walking distance of Lion's Pride Inn, Crystal Lake should be an idyllic rural retreat, but it is plagued by dangerous wildlife. Tribes of freshwater murlocs have claimed the shoreline and shallow shoals, attacking anyone who strays too close. Local alchemist William Pestle frequently hires passing adventurers to venture to the water's edge, directing them to defeat the creatures and harvest the crystal kelp they carry for use in his experimental concoctions.

Crystal Shore. Crystal Shore is a stretch of sandy coastline along the southeastern edge of Stranglethorn Vale, washed by the waves of the South Seas. Tucked beneath steep coastal bluffs, the beach lies just south of the ancient Ruins of Aboraz and across the waters from Jaguero Isle. Running along the southeastern perimeter of Stranglethorn Vale, the Crystal Shore forms a natural boundary between the dense tropical interior and the open waters of the South Seas. The beach itself is walled off from the inland jungles by steep ridges, leaving only a couple of rugged passes for travelers attempting to move between the coast and the deeper wilderness of Mistvale Valley. To the north lie the crumbling troll structures of the Ruins of Aboraz, while the Wild Shore extends along the southern curves of the cape. Its location makes it a quiet, windswept margin far removed from the bustling docks of Booty Bay.

Crystal Vale. Tucked away in the far northwestern corner of Silithus, the Crystal Vale is a remote canyon dominated by jagged mineral spires and swirling elemental forces. Earth and air elementals roam its rocky flats, guarding rich veins of raw ore. It is also a site of potent summoning magic, deeply tied to the ancient elemental lords. The Crystal Vale stands distinct from the barren desert sands of southern Silithus. Framed by steep cliffs, the basin is filled with shimmering crystalloid formations, roaming earthen elementals, and roaring whirlwinds of living air. Rich deposits of thorium draw occasional daring prospectors, but the vale is far from quiet. The elemental beings here are inherently hostile to intruders, guarding a realm that feels steeped in the primal conflicts of primordial Azeroth.

Crystalvein Mine. Crystalvein Mine is a cavern in central Stranglethorn Vale, situated near the ancient ruins of Zul'Mamwe. The cavern is rich in valuable 'Singing Crystals', but aggressive native basilisks have completely overrun the site, turning prospective miners to solid stone. Tucked away in the jungle hills near Zul'Mamwe, Crystalvein Mine boasts rare deposits of Singing Crystals, a unique mineral that fetches a high price in southern trade ports. Enticed by the promise of immense profit, the Venture Company set its sights on extracting the veins. However, the mine's natural inhabitants have proved catastrophic for business. Local basilisks consume the strange crystals, hardening their scales and making them unnaturally lethal. Outside the cave mouth, petrified statues of trolls and humans stand as a silent testament to the Venture Company's failed expeditions.

Cut-Throat Alley. Cut-Throat Alley is a secluded, unpopulated back corner of Stormwind City hidden away behind the canal shops. Tucked behind a storefront called the Shady Lady near the Dwarven District border, it consists of a quiet courtyard and an empty residence cut off from normal city foot traffic. Cut-Throat Alley is one of Stormwind's quietest and most secretive corners. Though technically charted alongside the Dwarven District, it shares none of the district's roaring forge fires or heavy soot. The alley cannot be reached from any of the city's main avenues; the only foot path leads straight through the Shady Lady, a small shop lining the canals just south of the bridge from Cathedral Square. Beyond the shop door lies a small paved dead-end lined with stacked crates, forgotten barrels, and a single unoccupied two-story residence. Completely hidden from passing guards and ordinary citizens, it sits entirely silent amidst the bustle of the capital.

Dabyrie's Farmstead. Dabyrie's Farmstead is an Alliance-aligned rural settlement situated in northern Arathi Highlands. In a realm shattered by the Third War and overrun by Syndicate outlaws and Witherbark trolls, this estate remains a stubborn bastion of Stromgarde citizens led by Kenata Dabyrie. Perched in the northern fields of the Arathi Highlands, Dabyrie's Farmstead is one of the very few functioning human homesteads remaining in the fractured kingdom of Stromgarde. Owned by Kenata Dabyrie and worked alongside her sons, Fardel and Marcel, the grounds are fiercely defended by a local family militia. Surrounded by aggressive wildlife, opportunistic bandits, and the nearby Forsaken presence in the north, the farm stands as a symbol of human endurance in a ruined land.

Dagger Hills. The Dagger Hills form a rugged ridge rising across southern Westfall, directly behind the blighted town of Moonbrook. Long neglected by the crown, this rocky highland serves as a hostile hideout for cutthroats, bandits, and creeping terrors that threaten the surrounding plains. Rising high above the dilapidated settlement of Moonbrook, the Dagger Hills mark the jagged southern reaches of Westfall. Stripped of official royal patrols from Stormwind, this arid highland has become a natural fortification for the Defias Brotherhood. Knuckledusters, pathstalkers, and highwaymen lurk among the rocky crests and scrub, ambushing unwary travelers and keeping watch over the approaches to their strongholds below.

Dalaran. Dalaran was once the shining magocratic capital of the Kirin Tor, nestled on the southern shore of Lordamere Lake. Shattered by the Scourge and the demon lord Archimonde during the Third War, its surviving magi are rebuilding the city, having removed its protective violet shield early in the reconstruction. Founded after the ancient Troll Wars by sorcerers of the Arathorian Empire, Dalaran stood for centuries as humanity's premier sanctuary for arcane study. Under the leadership of the Council of Six, the Kirin Tor amassed vast magical archives and guarded powerful artifacts within the Violet Citadel. That age of splendor ended abruptly during the Third War. The traitor prince Arthas led the Scourge through the city gates to seize the Book of Medivh, and soon after, the demon lord Archimonde crushed Dalaran's soaring spires into rubble.

Dalson's Tears. Dalson's Tears is a blighted farmstead located in the heart of the Western Plaguelands. Once known as Dalson's Orchard, the land was overrun during the Third War and converted into a staging ground for one of the Scourge's noxious plague cauldrons. The undead remains of the former owners still haunt the fields and outbuildings. Before the Third War, this estate flourished as Dalson's Orchard, a productive farm in the breadbasket of Lordaeron. Today, the fields are choked with decay and rechristened Dalson's Tears. At the center of the ruined property stands a massive iron cauldron, constantly billowing virulent green plague vapors across the landscape. The device is overseen by Cauldron Lord Malvinious and defended by a pack of blighted zombies, rotting cadavers, and skeletal horrors serving the Lich King.

Dandred's Fold. Dandred's Fold is a secluded farmstead and manor tucked along the misty northwestern shores of Lordamere Lake in the Alterac Mountains. Now overrun by the Syndicate, it serves as a secure hideout for Lord Aliden Perenolde and his co-conspirators. Both the Horde and the Alliance keep a watchful eye on this lakefront retreat for very different reasons. Perched on the western edge of the Uplands with private access to the waters of Lordamere Lake, Dandred's Fold was once a tranquil country estate, likely owned by an Alteraci noble named Dandred. In the aftermath of the kingdom's fall, the estate transformed into a fortified enclave for the Syndicate. Syndicate assassins and enforcers now patrol its fences and docks, shielding the fallen nobility from the eyes of Southshore authorities and the Forsaken across the lake.

Dark Portal. The Dark Portal is a monumental stone gateway standing at the southern rim of the Blasted Lands. First torn open through the combined sorcery of Medivh and Gul'dan, it served as the fateful conduit that brought the Old Horde into Azeroth, initiating the First War. Before its opening, this region was part of the Black Morass, a sodden wetland that stretched across the south. That changed when Medivh, possessed by Sargeras, joined his Tirisfal magics with the fel sorcery of Gul'dan on Draenor. The ritual drained untold lives and tore the fabric of reality apart. The Old Horde raised massive stone architecture to anchor the rift, marching armies through its threshold to shatter the Kingdom of Stormwind in the First War. The portal's fel emanations fundamentally corrupted the surrounding terrain, reducing lush marshes to the red, petrified wastes seen today.

Darkcloud Pinnacle. Darkcloud Pinnacle is a fortified tauren settlement perched atop several interconnected mesas east of the Great Lift in Thousand Needles. Held by the aggressive Grimtotem clan, the aerial stronghold serves as a base of operations for regional disruption and shady dealings. Spanning three main mesas joined by rope bridges, Darkcloud Pinnacle commands the canyon basin below. The heights are accessible only by a steep natural slope leading from the canyon floor across wooden bridges, or via a high crossing near Razorfen Downs. From these windswept rocks, the Grimtotem watch the valley, safe from casual assault and isolated from the broader tauren tribes.

Darkened Bank. The Darkened Bank is the northern shoreline of Duskwood, bordering the river that separates the shadowed woods from Elwynn Forest. Stretching from the far west all the way east toward the Redridge Mountains, it marks the boundary between the relative safety of the north and the dark terrors of the forest. Running along the southern bank of the river opposite Elwynn Forest, the Darkened Bank forms the northern edge of Duskwood. It extends from the western riverbends east toward the stone span leading to the Redridge Mountains. While visually gloomy under the pervasive canopy of Duskwood's curse, this shoreline is often the first foothold for travelers venturing south from Elwynn. Near its far western tip sits a makeshift campsite where displaced refugees, including Sven Yorgen and Lars, have taken shelter just barely outside the grasp of the deep woods.

Darkmist Cavern. Darkmist Cavern is an abandoned mine tucked into northwestern Dustwallow Marsh, completely infested with predatory giant spiders. Crumbling ruins outside hint at an unfortunate former settlement swallowed up by the marsh's hazards. Locals remain divided on whether the cavern gave its name to the arachnids or the reverse. Situated in the northwest reaches of Dustwallow Marsh, Darkmist Cavern appears to have once been an active mining venture. Today, any human presence has long vanished, leaving behind rotting, ruined shacks outside the entrance and a network of tunnels choked with thick webs. The cavern is overrun by Darkmist spiders, predatory horrors whose venom and size make the tunnels deadly to unwary wanderers. Marsh dwellers still dispute whether the cavern was named after the foul brood nesting inside or if the spiders took the title from the misty cave itself.

Darkshire. Darkshire, formerly known as Grand Hamlet, is a battered settlement in eastern Duskwood. Cloaked in an enduring, unnatural gloom and neglected by Stormwind, the town survives only through the vigilance of the Night Watch and the stubborn endurance of its people. Once a peaceful woodland settlement called Grand Hamlet, the village was razed by the Old Horde during the First War and later rebuilt. Its fortune turned truly bitter following the fall of Medivh at Karazhan, whose lingering death throes cursed the surrounding woods into the shadowy wilderness of Duskwood. Despite being a nominal holding of the Kingdom of Stormwind, the town hall receives virtually no aid from the crown. Political paralysis in Stormwind City has left the garrison unstaffed and the borders unpatrolled, forcing Mayor Ello Ebonlocke and the local council to administer their own harsh, insular justice in the shadows.

Darkshire Town Hall. Darkshire Town Hall stands on the western edge of the town square as the seat of local governance in Duskwood. From inside these dimly lit halls, Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke and his council attempt to administer a settlement besieged by creeping darkness and undead monstrosities. Located directly west of the main town square, the Town Hall is where Darkshire's civic leadership gathers to govern an increasingly isolated territory. Within its weathered walls sits Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke, struggling to preserve civil order and protect the populace while Stormwind offers little in the way of military aid. Alongside the mayor, municipal officials like Clerk Daltry work to track local records and the travelers braving Duskwood's dangerous roads, though keeping ledgers current is a grim and challenging task in such perilous times.

Darkspear Strand. Darkspear Strand is the stretch of coastline in southern Durotar where the Darkspear trolls washed ashore following their exile from the Echo Isles. Located directly beside Sen'jin Village, this beach marks the bitter beginning of the tribe's mainland refuge under Vol'jin's leadership. When the witch doctor Zalazane went mad and seized control of the Echo Isles, the surviving Darkspear trolls were forced to abandon their offshore home. Desperate refugees crossed the narrow waters and landed along this sun-bleached coast. Rather than scatter into the hostile red wastes of Durotar, the survivors banded together just yards inland from the shoreline to construct Sen'jin Village. Today, the strand serves as a quiet reminder of their displacement, looking out across the surf toward the islands they still hope to reclaim.

Darkwhisper Gorge. Darkwhisper Gorge is a treacherous, demon-infested ravine carved into the southern heights of Winterspring. When Archimonde was destroyed at the climax of the Third War, remnants of the shattered Burning Legion fled down the slopes of Mount Hyjal and entrenched themselves in these jagged chasms. Today, powerful fiends stalk its heights, guarding ancient minerals and dark planar relics. Following the defeat of Archimonde atop Mount Hyjal, surviving demons of the Burning Legion scattered into the surrounding mountain ranges. A disciplined vanguard took refuge in Darkwhisper Gorge, transforming the southern border of Winterspring into a lethal stronghold. Led by Hederine demons—including lethal manastalkers, slayers, and initiates under Lady Hederine—these fiends fiercely defend their subterranean tunnels and fiery camps. Beyond the immediate threat of its elite inhabitants, an ominous, sealed archway stands at the gorge's lowest point, hinting at sealed passages leading higher up the sacred mountain.

Darnassus. High amidst the sweeping boughs of Teldrassil stands Darnassus, the capital refuge of the kaldorei. Built along tranquil waters and verdant groves, it serves as the spiritual heart of the night elves and the primary Alliance bastion on northern Kalimdor. From here, High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind and Archdruid Fandral Staghelm guide their people through the trials of newfound mortality. Constructed in the aftermath of the Third War, Darnassus was founded to honor the survival of the night elf people after the loss of the immortality granted by their sacred World Tree, Nordrassil. Unlike the dense stone metropolises of Ironforge or Stormwind, Darnassus is an open, tranquil settlement of wood-crafted lodges, glowing shrines, and arched bridges spanning crystalline lakes. Vigilant Sentinels, towering ancients of war, and tree-shaping druids keep watch over the paths, ensuring that the peaceful quiet of nature is preserved within the city's borders.

Darrow Hill. Darrow Hill is an elevated expanse of rugged grassland nestled in northern Hillsbrad Foothills directly beneath the Headland. While mountain lions and stags graze across its open slopes, feral yetis lurk inside the Foothill Caverns that pit the hillside. Rich with veins of Alterac Granite, it serves as a treacherous frontier where natural beasts and rival travelers constantly clash. Rising along the base of the northern mountains below the Headland, Darrow Hill bridges the rolling pasture of southern Hillsbrad with the jagged, colder heights of Alterac. Mountain lions and stags stalk through the tall grasses, sharing the rocky slopes with towering yetis that spill out from the Foothill Caverns. Beyond its feral wildlife, the cavern walls hide deposits of dense Alterac Granite, drawing quarry workers, miners, and adventurers straight into harm's way. Caught between contentious regional claims, its trails remain notoriously dangerous for travelers of either faction caught unawares.

Darrowmere Lake. Darrowmere Lake is an expansive freshwater lake situated in the southeastern reaches of the Western Plaguelands. At its heart lies the fortress island of Caer Darrow, whose ruined halls conceal the Cult of the Damned's dread necromantic academy, Scholomance. Darrowmere Lake is among the largest inland bodies of water in the Eastern Kingdoms, bordered by the blight-stricken forests of Lordaeron and fed by the Thondroril and Darrowmere rivers. During the Second War, these deep waters saw intense naval skirmishes between the Horde and Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet. The Horde also struck the island fortress of Caer Darrow at the lake's heart, sacking it and carrying off its ancient runestone. Once a thriving waterway and trade artery for the House of Barov, the lake is now a grim, mist-veiled basin in the heart of the Plaguelands.

Darrowshire. Darrowshire is a ruined village in the southern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands, once a peaceful hamlet of Lordaeron. During the Third War, its residents mounted a desperate, tragic stand against an overwhelming Scourge force. Today, only shattered timbers, restless spirits, and bitter memories linger amid the silence. Before the plague consumed northern Lordaeron, Darrowshire was a humble rural settlement nestled beneath the southern cliffs. When the Scourge marched south during the Third War, a force led by the death knight Marduk Blackpool and the ghoul lord Horgus the Ravager besieged the town. The villagers and local defenders fought valiantly, momentarily holding the line against impossible odds. Ultimately, the defense collapsed, and the town was slaughtered down to the last soul. Rather than finding peace in death, many of Darrowshire's fallen defenders were reanimated as ghouls to bolster the Scourge's ranks, leaving the village an eerie, empty memorial of lost valor.

Dawning Isles. The Dawning Isles are a cluster of low-lying islets situated within Lordamere Lake along the eastern edge of Silverpine Forest. Once idyllic retreats, they have succumbed to the blight of the Plague of Undeath and are overrun by aggressive murlocs. Before the Third War, the Dawning Isles were known as scenic keys resting on the calm, clear waters of Lordamere Lake. When the Plague of Undeath swept across Lordaeron, corruption seeped into the lake's shallows. The vegetation turned pallid and rotting, driving away idyllic peacefulness. Today, the Vile Fin murloc tribe dominates the muddy shores and tangled brush, aggressively defending their burgeoning colonies from anyone seeking to traverse the lake.

Dawning Wood Catacombs. Carved deep beneath Raven Hill Cemetery, the Dawning Wood Catacombs are a dark labyrinth teeming with the fiercest undead in Duskwood. Those who brave the subterranean tunnels face entrenched swarms of skeletal guardians and flesh-eating ghouls. Long before the twilight curse settled over the forest, the Dawning Wood Catacombs served as a resting place for the dead of the surrounding woods. Now buried beneath the ruined Raven Hill Cemetery, these dark stone corridors hold the most lethal undead in the region. The catacombs feature two distinct subterranean wings: the western passages are held by ranks of animated skeletons guarding ancestral tombs, while the eastern passages descend into a foul warren overrun by ravenous, disease-bearing ghouls. Lone travelers rarely survive deep within their depths.

Dead Acre. The Dead Acre is a ruined, smoldering farmstead in southeastern Westfall near the river bridge to Duskwood. Burned to ash by the Defias Brotherhood during their uprising across the countryside, the blackened fields are now abandoned by people and stalked by rogue harvest golems. Situated just north of the road linking Sentinel Hill to Duskwood, the Dead Acre was once a productive homestead among the breadbasket farms of Westfall. When the Defias Brotherhood rose in revolt and drove out the local landowners, this farm met a violent end. The homestead and its surrounding crops were put to the torch, leaving behind scorched timber, smoking earth, and wandering mechanical Harvest Watchers that still reap the barren soil.

Dead Field. The Dead Field is a blighted, abandoned farmstead situated in northern Silverpine Forest. Once quiet rural farmland, it has been seized by the Rot Hide gnolls and transformed into a forward staging ground for Scourge forces. Repeated Forsaken attempts to clear the area have faltered under the command of the banshee Nightlash. Little remains of the original farmstead in the northern reaches of Silverpine Forest, its previous living occupants long lost to the Third War. Today, the ruined plot serves as a base of operations for the Rot Hide gnolls, who act as willing servants to the Scourge. As their numbers swelled, Deathstalker scouts passing through the region noted signs of imminent military mobilization threatening Forsaken supply lines and outposts. Small Forsaken assaults against the farm have repeatedly failed, turned back by the wailing apparition Nightlash—a banshee who manifests whenever her gnoll thralls are endangered.

Deadeye Shore. Deadeye Shore is a windswept stretch of coastline along Durotar's eastern edge, directly east of Drygulch Ravine. Named in memory of the legendary Bleeding Hollow chieftain Kilrogg Deadeye, the barren sands are roamed primarily by wild raptors, scorpids, and feral boars. Stretching beneath the red bluffs of central Durotar, Deadeye Shore takes its name from Kilrogg Deadeye, the one-eyed chieftain of the Bleeding Hollow clan who fought in the First and Second Wars. From high above, the sand and rocky outcrops faintly mirror the shape of a skull with a missing eye socket. While lacking major settlements or military outposts, the shoreline is far from peaceful: aggressive wildlife dominates the sands, and shadowy cultists from the Burning Blade have been known to prowl down toward the water from their nearby hideouts in the ravines.

Deadman's Crossing. Deadman's Crossing is an ominous junction set within the bleak canyon of Deadwind Pass. Branching between Duskwood, the Swamp of Sorrows, and the haunted tower of Karazhan, it serves as a grim threshold marked by gallows and warning signs. Despite its gruesome appearance, the path remains a vital thoroughfare for travelers moving across the southern Eastern Kingdoms. Situated at the eastern crossroads of Deadwind Pass, Deadman's Crossing links the shadows of Duskwood with the murky depths of the Swamp of Sorrows, while a foreboding southern track ascends toward the haunted tower of Karazhan. The crossing takes its name from the twisted hangman's tree planted at the road's fork, where a pair of rotting corpses dangle overhead as a stark warning to all who pass. Beside the tree, battered wooden signs offer blunt advice to travelers, urging them to turn back and abandon hope. The canyon itself is thick with hostile beasts and dark sorceries, yet travelers moving steadfastly along the packed dirt road will find the crossing itself oddly unmolested, so long as they do not wander into the blighted rocks.

Deadmines. Deep beneath the dusty ghost town of Moonbrook, the Deadmines are a sprawling underground labyrinth that was once the greatest gold-production center in human lands. Abandoned during the First War and long whispered to be haunted, the forgotten shafts have become the fortified headquarters of Edwin VanCleef and his rebellious Defias Brotherhood. Before the First War, the Deadmines were the premier mining operation in human lands, rich in gold and sturdy Whitestone oak used for timber and structural supports. When the orcish Horde pushed north, the mines were abandoned in haste. Sir Anduin Lothar notably ventured into their treacherous depths to recover the sacred Tome of Divinity, surviving twenty months of captivity at the hands of subterranean ogres before being rescued. In the turmoil that followed the kingdom's fall, the shafts fell silent and gained a chilling reputation for being cursed.

Deadwood Village. Deadwood Village is a furbolg encampment nestled in southern Felwood. Once a peaceful clan attuned to nature, its residents fell victim to the demonic corruption that blighted the surrounding forest. Driven mad by fel taint, the Deadwood furbolgs now attack anyone who approaches their crude wooden settlement. Situated near the southern border of Felwood, Deadwood Village serves as the primary enclave of the Deadwood tribe. When the Burning Legion's demonic energies washed through the ancient woodlands, the furbolgs lacked the power to resist the creeping rot. Their minds warped by fel malice, they abandoned their ancient traditions and spiritual harmony. Today, the village is a squalid gathering of hostile brutes, shamans, and den watchers who violently defend their polluted grounds against intruders, earning the despair of their uncorrupted cousins, the Timbermaw.

Deathknell. Deathknell is a fortified village nestled in a secluded valley in southwestern Tirisfal Glades. It serves as the primary awakening grounds for newly freed undead breaking free from the Lich King's grasp to join the Forsaken. Besieged by mindless Scourge remnants, local zealots, and aggressive wildlife, the settlement is a harsh proving ground for those claiming a place in Sylvanas Windrunner's kingdom. Tucked away behind jagged hills just north of the Silverpine border, Deathknell is where newly awakened undead first open their eyes to their bleak reality. Unlike most settlements in Tirisfal Glades that preserved their human names from the fallen Kingdom of Lordaeron, Deathknell was explicitly renamed by the undead who claimed it. The town itself is cleaved in two: the Forsaken cling stubbornly to the southern grounds around the old church, while the northern half—including the village forge—remains overrun by mindless Scourge zombies and feral ghouls. Elite Deathguards keep the narrow gorge out of the valley securely sealed against intruders, allowing local caretakers to induct new arrivals into the Banshee Queen's service.

Decrepit Ferry. The Decrepit Ferry is a ruined dock on the eastern shore of Silverpine Forest that once provided passage across Lordamere Lake to Fenris Isle. Following the fall of Lordaeron, the ferry was destroyed, its operator murdered, and the shoreline overrun by undead and vicious Rot Hide gnolls. Before the Third War, this dock bustled with daily traffic across Lordamere Lake. Local farmers brought fresh produce down to the water, selling their crops directly to the wealthy lord of Fenris Isle and his household. For a modest fee, the ferryman carried trade goods, messengers, and visiting nobles back and forth between the mainland and the keep. That peaceful commerce ended abruptly when the Scourge swept through the kingdom. The ferryman was brutally killed, the boats were smashed, and the pier fell into decay.

Deep Elem Mine. Deep Elem Mine is an excavation site nestled in the heart of Silverpine Forest. Once an active operation, it was overrun when Archmage Arugal's dark magic swept through the region, transforming its miners into savage worgen.
