Situated central to Silverpine Forest, the Deep Elem Mine once served the living inhabitants of Lordaeron as an ordinary resource vein. When Archmage Arugal unleashed the lupine nightmare upon the forest, his feral curse spread deep into the tunnels. The laborers inside succumbed to the affliction, turning into vicious worgen who abandoned their pickaxes to claim the cavern as a predatory lair.

Deeprun Tram. The Deeprun Tram is an subterranean marvel of gnomish engineering linking the Alliance capitals of Ironforge and Stormwind City. Commissioned by King Magni Bronzebeard following the Second War, it allows citizens and soldiers to cross vast distances beneath the earth in mere minutes. The enclosed twin tracks cut beneath mountain and lake, serving as a vital artery for Alliance military support and commerce. Following the devastation of the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard grew increasingly frustrated with how slowly dwarven aid and construction supplies reached Stormwind across the mountain passes. To solve the logistical hurdle and guarantee that dwarven soldiers could rapidly reinforce the human capital in times of crisis, Magni turned to High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque. The master gnomish engineer drafted designs for an enclosed underground railway powered by cutting-edge technology. Despite excavation complications—including cutting right through a vast subterranean lake and battling relentless infestations of underground rats—the tram became a crowning achievement of the Alliance, moving thousands of travelers free of charge between Ironforge and Stormwind.

Deepwater Tavern. The Deepwater Tavern is the bustling seaside inn of Menethil Harbor, nestled in the damp marshlands of the Wetlands. It serves as the primary meeting spot, resupply point, and resting place for travelers and mariners navigating the busy port town. Between hearty drinks and harbor rumors, patrons frequently find work or run into volatile tavern brawls. Standing within the sodden streets of Menethil Harbor, the Deepwater Tavern offers travelers a welcome shelter from the perpetually drizzly, treacherous marshlands outside. Sailors, dockworkers, merchants, and weary adventurers gather beneath its timber beams to trade news, share a warm fire, and patch their wounds. Beyond the usual amenities of a harbor inn, it houses a resident first aid trainer and local merchants catering to those bound for the perils of the marsh or embarking across the Great Sea. The atmosphere is boisterous and occasionally hazardous; disputes flare up quickly over spilled ale, with notorious troublemakers like Tapoke 'Slim' Jahn known to spark the occasional tavern-wide brawl.

Defias Hideout. The Defias Hideout is an unassuming, derelict house situated on the southern edge of Moonbrook. Though it blends in with the surrounding ruined settlement, its upper floor conceals the primary overland entrance into the extensive subterranean network of the Deadmines. To the casual eye, the Defias Hideout looks like any other ransacked manor or farmhouse in Moonbrook, overrun by destitute vagrants and Defias thugs. However, its modest interior masks the nerve center of Edwin VanCleef's southern operations. Ascending to the upper floor reveals an opening that leads directly down into the sprawling labyrinth of the Deadmines. Because the Brotherhood focuses its manpower on guarding the perimeter of Moonbrook and laboring deep underground, the hideout itself is sparsely garrisoned, functioning more as a heavily monitored bottleneck than an active stronghold.

Demon Fall Canyon. Demon Fall Canyon is a scarred, fel-corrupted gorge situated in southern Ashenvale. It marks the legendary battleground where Grommash Hellscream and Thrall confronted the pit lord Mannoroth, ending the demonic blood curse that had enslaved the orcish race for a generation. Carved into the rugged southern borders of Ashenvale near Felfire Hill and Demon Fall Ridge, this canyon bears the heavy scars of the Third War. It was here that Warchief Thrall and chieftain Grommash Hellscream tracked down the pit lord Mannoroth to break his hold over the Horde. During the fierce duel, Mannoroth incapacitated Thrall, but Grom seized the opening to drive his axe, Gorehowl, straight into the demon's chest. The resulting infernal explosion shattered the pit lord and slew Grom as well, permanently liberating the orcs from their lingering demonic servitude.

Demon Fall Ridge. Demon Fall Ridge is a blighted highland in south-eastern Ashenvale, overlooking the canyon where Mannoroth fell. Swarming with lesser demons and corrupting magic, the ridge centers around a desecrated night elf barrow den claimed by the Burning Legion. Rising directly west and above Demon Fall Canyon, Demon Fall Ridge is stained with lingering fel residue from the Third War. While the canyon below marks the site of the catastrophic clash between Grommash Hellscream and the pit lord Mannoroth, this high ground serves as a staging area for surviving demonic invaders. Lesser demons patrol the rocky cliffs, defiling the ancient woodland and threatening any travelers traversing the southern border of Ashenvale.

Demont's Place. Demont's Place is a ruined homestead nestled in southwestern Westfall, just west of the forsaken town of Moonbrook. Once a working agricultural plot, the farm was driven to ruin alongside the rest of the region and claimed by the rogue agents of the Defias Brotherhood. Today, its weathered fences and empty fields stand as another casualty of the realm's fading prosperity. Situated within sight of Moonbrook, Demont's Place was once among the private family holdings feeding the Kingdom of Stormwind. Economic collapse and the sudden rise of outlaw brigands stripped the farm of its livelihood, forcing out its original caretakers. Much like its neighboring fields, the plot has degenerated into a rough hideout, overrun by outlaws using its weathered grounds as an extension of the Defias stronghold in Moonbrook.

Den of Flame. The Den of Flame is a fortified cavern in western Dustwallow Marsh, situated just west of the Stonemaul Ruins. Originally constructed by the Stonemaul ogres as their mound, it has since been overrun by the dragonkin of the black dragonflight serving Onyxia. Built by the Stonemaul ogres to serve as their main mound and sanctuary, the Den of Flame bears the unmistakable, rough-hewn stone architecture of ogre masonry. However, when the black dragonflight laid waste to the Stonemaul clan's settlement, the brood did not merely scatter the ogres—they seized the stronghold for themselves. Today, black dragonspawn patrol the burning perimeter and cavern entrance under the shadow of Onyxia's nearby lair.

Dire Maul. Dire Maul is the ruined expanse of Eldre'Thalas, an ancient Highborne city hidden deep in the wilderness of Feralas. Once built to safeguard Queen Azshara's arcane secrets, its crumbling plazas and towering coliseums are now divided between occupying Gordok ogres, invading satyrs, and the withered remnants of its original elven caretakers. Twelve thousand years ago, Eldre'Thalas served as a wondrous bastion for Queen Azshara's favored sorcerers, the Shen'dralar. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Great Sundering, Prince Tortheldrin wove a magical barrier that shielded the city from ruin. Severed from their source of magic, the surviving Highborne trapped a colossal demon named Immol'thar beneath their sanctum, siphoning its fel essence to sustain their immortality and arcane powers for millennia.

Direforge Hill. Direforge Hill is a rugged highland in the northeastern Wetlands, southeast of Dun Modr and northeast of the Green Belt. The Dark Iron dwarf warlock Balgaras the Foul commands a hostile encampment on its slopes. Direforge Hill serves as a major Dark Iron campsite in the northeastern Wetlands. Balgaras the Foul, a Dark Iron dwarf warlock, commands the hostile dwarves occupying the hill southeast of Dun Modr.

Dolanaar. Dolanaar is a tranquil night elf settlement nestled in the central-eastern boughs of Teldrassil. Situated just southwest of Shadowglen, it serves as the first true town young kal'dorei encounter after departing their sheltered training grounds. Here, rangers, druids, and craftsmen gather to guide newcomers and address the strange, encroaching afflictions disturbing the World Tree. Resting beneath the lush canopy southwest of Shadowglen, Dolanaar serves as a vital crossway for travelers traversing Teldrassil. Built in the traditional night elven manner, its homes and platforms sit seamlessly woven into the woodland. The village provides newcomers with their first comprehensive training in trades, martial arts, and nature crafts, and sits on the road to the capital city of Darnassus. Because of its central location, reports of corrupted wildlife, aggressive furbolgs, and foul mosses from the surrounding boughs inevitably find their way into Dolanaar's council.

Dor'Danil Barrow Den. Dor'Danil Barrow Den is an ancient night elven sanctuary carved into the earth of central Ashenvale, south of Splintertree Post. Once a tranquil resting place for slumbering druids commune with the Emerald Dream, it has fallen into horror following Forsaken meddling that severed the dreamers' spirits from their bodies. Barrow dens across Kalimdor are revered sanctuaries where night elven druids historically slept for centuries, roaming the Emerald Dream while their mortal frames remained protected underground. When the Horde pushed into Ashenvale, Dor'Danil fell deep behind enemy lines. The orcs largely ignored the comatose elves, but the newly allied Forsaken saw an opportunity. Forsaken operatives infiltrated the depths and began gruesome experiments designed to sever the sleeping druids from their spirits, fracturing their minds and driving them hopelessly insane. The darkened hollows now crawl with sinister Forsaken assassins and the furious, torment-maddened spirits of druids who can no longer return to their bodies.

Dormitory. The Dormitory is a residential sector within the fallen technological capital of Gnomeregan. Once providing living quarters for countless gnome citizens, it now lies choked with radioactive fallout and crawls with savage, irradiated troggs. Situated just past the decontamination chambers of the Clean Zone, the Dormitory formerly housed the inventors, laborers, and families of Gnomeregan. When High Tinker Mekkatorque initiated the emergency radiation venting to combat the invading trogg horde, this densely populated sector became a trap. Today, its communal halls and living units are completely abandoned by gnomish life, occupied instead by mutated troggs that thrive in the radioactive miasma. Travelers descending toward the lower levels of the city must fight through this tragic reminder of the catastrophe to reach the lower Hall of Gears.

Drag. The Drag is a bustling, shaded thoroughfare carved into the red rock of Orgrimmar, linking the Valley of Strength to the Valley of Honor and the Valley of Wisdom. Known throughout Durotar as the heart of the capital's commerce, its canyon walls are lined with crafters, traders, and artisans. It also conceals the cavernous descent into the notorious Cleft of Shadow. Tucked deep between the red canyon walls of Orgrimmar, the Drag serves as the commercial backbone of the Horde's capital. While the Valley of Strength focuses on military muster and administrative command, the Drag is where daily city life unfolds. Shaded under high cliffs and hides, the street is thick with the smells of tanning vats, bubbling alchemical cauldrons, and the clatter of tinkerers' gears. Craftsmen of almost every discipline gather here to practice their trades and teach aspiring adventurers, from leatherworking and tailoring to goblin-led engineering workshops like Nogg's Machine Shop.

Dragonmaw Gates. The Dragonmaw Gates are a series of imposing fortifications along the mountain road leading up from the eastern Wetlands. Built to guard the steep ascent to the mountain fortress of Grim Batol, these heavy barricades bar entry into the cursed heights of the dwarven ruins. Carved into the rugged peaks bordering the eastern Wetlands, the Dragonmaw Gates seal the winding road that climbs into the mountains toward Grim Batol. Named after the Dragonmaw clan of orcs who held the dwarven mountain city during the Second War, these defensive barriers remain deeply fortified checkpoints. Anyone attempting to ascend toward the heights must contend with the lingering perils of the pass, where powerful drakes and grim reminders of the clan's dark history still cast a long shadow.

Dragonmurk. Dragonmurk is a sprawling, hazardous tract of southern Dustwallow Marsh swarming with black dragonspawn and hatchlings. Flanked by ancient ogre ruins and scorched caverns, it serves as the hostile outer perimeter for the brood of Onyxia. Spanning the southern interior of Dustwallow Marsh, the Dragonmurk marks the threshold where damp wetlands give way to the dominion of the black dragonflight. The waterways and thick mud here crawl with black wyrmkins, dragonspawn, and ravenous whelps. The surrounding landscape has suffered deeply from their presence; adjacent territories such as the ruined village of Stonemaul and the scorched cavern known as the Den of Flame have both fallen completely under the flight's territorial grip.

Dreadmaul Post. Dreadmaul Post is an entrenched ogre settlement situated in the scorched wastes of the Blasted Lands. Established by the Dreadmaul clan, this mound serves as a fortified redoubt near the Dark Portal where ogres have lingered since their arrival from Draenor. Travelers passing through the region must contend with these fierce brutes and the treacherous terrain surrounding their encampment. When the Horde surged through the Dark Portal in decades past, clans of ogres marched alongside them into Azeroth. The Dreadmaul clan chose to dig in near the gateway itself, raising crude stone mounds and earthworks across the red wastes of the Blasted Lands. Dreadmaul Post stands as one of their primary outposts, maintaining a firm grip over the badlands and clashing with wandering beasts and any travelers foolish enough to draw near their territory.

Dreadmaul Rock. Dreadmaul Rock is a towering crag and cave complex rising out of the fiery wastes of the Burning Steppes. It serves as the primary base of operations for the Firegut ogres, who make their home within its winding, subterranean mounds. Towering above the scorched plains of the Burning Steppes, Dreadmaul Rock is a massive stone formation carved out by a labyrinthine cave system. Though its name hints at a possible connection to the Dreadmaul ogres of the Blasted Lands, the rock is held firmly by the Firegut clan. These brutish ogres use the elevated paths, crags, and interior earthen mounds as a defended encampment, dominating the surrounding wasteland and menacing anyone attempting to traverse the northern slopes toward Blackrock Spire.

Dreadmist Den. Dreadmist Den is a subterranean cavern carved beneath the crags of Dreadmist Peak in the northern Barrens. Controlled by the Burning Blade cult, the cavern is perpetually smothered in an unnerving red haze and serves as a shrine to demon worship. Dreadmist Den lies tucked within the jagged slopes of Dreadmist Peak, serving as a dark sanctuary for the Burning Blade cultists. Inside, the air hangs heavy with a thick, crimson vapor that blankets the cavern in an eerie twilight. Far from the watchful eyes of the Horde in the plains below, the cult conducts foul demonic rites within these stone tunnels, guarding their blasphemous relics and plotting to spread their corruption across Kalimdor.

Dreadmist Peak. Dreadmist Peak is a jagged, desolate mountain looming northwest of the Crossroads in the Barrens. Shrouded in an unnatural, crimson miasma, the peak serves as a secluded redoubt for the demonic cultists of the Burning Blade. Rising high above the arid savannas of the Barrens, Dreadmist Peak stands out as a site of palpable evil. As travelers wind their way up the crags, the bright sky is blotted out by a dense, reddish haze. At the mountain's crest and within its subterranean hollows, the Burning Blade cult operates in secret, harboring warlocks and toxicologists. From this vantage, the cultists spread poisons into the nearby water table and scheme against the nascent powers establishing control over central Kalimdor.

Dreadmurk Shore. Dreadmurk Shore encompasses the foggy coastline and scattered islands of Dustwallow Marsh running north toward the Barrens. Dominated by aggressive Mirefin murlocs and sea beasts, these treacherous waters have recently become the hiding ground for shipwrecked Defias Brotherhood outlaws. Stretching along the northeastern edge of Dustwallow Marsh between Theramore Isle and Northwatch Hold, Dreadmurk Shore is a dismal expanse of muddy shoals, tide pools, and misty islands. The coast is overrun by the Mirefin tribe, a territorial clan of murlocs that aggressively attacks any travelers nearing their coastal villages. Sea turtles and aquatic predators prowl the shallows, making the shoreline dangerous to navigate even without factoring in the surrounding swamplands.

Dream Bough. Dream Bough is a colossal Great Tree nestled on an island in the center of Jademir Lake in northern Feralas. The ancient tree shelters a mysterious gateway connecting Azeroth directly to the Emerald Dream. Green dragons loyally watch over the sanctuary, keeping unwanted intruders away from its verdant boughs. Rising high above the canopy of northern Feralas, the Dream Bough stands as the largest tree in the region. Situated in the tranquil waters of Jademir Lake, the towering sentinel houses a natural portal carved into its trunk, providing a direct threshold into the untamed Emerald Dream.

Dreamer's Rock. Dreamer's Rock is a secluded natural sanctuary tucked deep within the Wailing Caverns past the Screaming Gully. Here lies the sleeping night elf druid Naralex, whose noble effort to revive the Barrens has instead birthed a living nightmare. It serves as both a sacred barrow chamber and the epicenter of the corruption mutating the surrounding subterranean ecosystem. Located in the heart of the Wailing Caverns, Dreamer's Rock functions much like an improvised barrow den. Here, the night elf druid Naralex entered a deep trance to tap the underground springs and channel the Emerald Dream into the arid soil of the Barrens. Instead of bringing life, his connection was seized by dark forces. The nightmare twisting his thoughts now spills physically into this chamber, twisting the local wildlife, turning his followers into the venomous Druids of the Fang, and manifesting terrifying aberrations into the waking world.

Drowned Reef. The Drowned Reef is a treacherous stretch of coastal waters off the southern cliffs of the Arathi Highlands. Beneath the waves lie ancient sunken ruins, claimed by hostile Daggerspine naga who appear able to control the bay's tides, endangering passing vessels. Just outside the hidden entrance to Faldir's Cove, the Drowned Reef forms a watery graveyard for navigators. Shattered ships, including the Maiden's Folly and the Spirit of Silverpine, lie submerged beneath the waves. Daggerspine naga led by Prince Nazjak inhabit the reef and appear able to control the bay's tides, dooming crews seeking refuge in the cove.

Drowned Sacellum. The Drowned Sacellum is a submerged elven shrine lying just inside the entrance of Blackfathom Deeps. Submerged beneath brackish saltwater and draped in cavernous roots, its shattered masonry is now overrun by murlocs and makrura. Stepping through the threshold of Blackfathom Deeps immediately brings explorers into the Drowned Sacellum. Once a tranquil subterranean chapel dedicated to Elune, the sacellum has long collapsed into the sea-swept abyss beneath Ashenvale's coast. Saltwater pools swallow ancient marble flagstones overgrown with starfish, while massive tree roots dangle from the cavern ceiling above. Dark, flickering wisps provide the only dim light in the gloom, illuminating a ruined pathway of stones that adventurers must carefully navigate to reach the Pool of Ask'ar deeper within the temple complex.

Dry Hills. The Dry Hills form the rugged northwestern corner of the Barrens, nestled against the foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains. Contrary to their name, these uplands are noticeably greener than the arid plains below, though they are notoriously dangerous due to the aggressive Witchwing harpies roosting along their crags. Tucked away where the arid plains rise toward the Stonetalon Mountains, the Dry Hills are somewhat of a misnomer, possessing far more verdant brush and shrubbery than the sun-bleached savannas to the south. Yet this lush foothill region offers little safety for travelers. The bluffs are dominated by the Witchwing harpies, led by the matriarch Serena Bloodfeather. From these heights, their raiding parties sweep down to prey on supply caravans using the northern stretch of the Gold Road, leaving abandoned orcish fortifications and derelict siege engines rotting in the brush.

Drygulch Ravine. Drygulch Ravine is a rugged, hidden gorge tucked into the rocky bluffs of eastern Durotar. Accessible only through an obscure cave passage from Razorwind Canyon or a perilous drop from above, this craggy trench is overrun by nesting Dustwind harpies who menace nearby supply caravans. Carved deep into the crags east of Orgrimmar, Drygulch Ravine is almost entirely cut off from casual travel. Its only ground-level access is a cramped natural tunnel connected to Razorwind Canyon. Roosting Dustwind harpies have turned this sheltered depression into a lawless pocket of Durotar. The winged scavengers use the steep cliff faces to nest their broods and stockpile stolen goods taken from Horde supply trains passing along the regional trails.

Drywhisker Gorge. Drywhisker Gorge is a rugged cleft in the eastern mountains of the Arathi Highlands, situated northeast of the Horde outpost of Hammerfall. The gorge and its inner cavern are held by a hostile clan of kobolds, who fiercely guard rich mineral deposits and ancient elemental relics buried deep underground. Tucked away in the mountainous folds east of Hammerfall, Drywhisker Gorge serves as the primary redoubt of the Drywhisker clan of kobolds. While kobolds are often dismissed as simple mine pests, the Drywhiskers in Arathi are heavily entrenched. They guard their subterranean passages with fierce territorial tenacity, working veins of rare Lesser Bloodstone Ore and defending the deep recesses of the earth. Their proximity makes them a persistent nuisance to the nearby orcs of Hammerfall.

Dun Algaz. Dun Algaz is the fortified mountain pass and network of tunnels connecting Loch Modan to the Wetlands. Historically contested during the Second War, this vital trade artery has recently fallen under siege by Dragonmaw orcs, cutting off easy transit between Ironforge's territories and Menethil Harbor. Dun Algaz predates the War of the Three Hammers, originally serving as the passage the Wildhammer clan used to migrate north after being driven out of Ironforge. Carved deep into the jagged peaks separating Loch Modan and the Wetlands, the pass consists of sweeping stone tunnels, bastions, and watchposts. Its strategic value cannot be overstated: whoever holds Dun Algaz commands the only overland highway linking the dwarven heartlands to the western sea at Menethil Harbor.

Dun Garok. Dun Garok is a fortified dwarven mountain bastion situated in the southeastern heights of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Commanded by Captain Ironhill, the outpost's stalwart garrison defends regional Alliance interests and nearby operations like the Azurelode Mine against hostile encroachment. To the Forsaken of Tarren Mill, this entrenched dwarven stronghold stands as a constant military threat bordering their domain. Carved into the craggy southeastern hills of Hillsbrad Foothills, Dun Garok stands as a heavily defended redoubt of Ironforge mountaineers and riflemen. Commanded by Captain Ironhill, the dwarves here maintain a critical defensive perimeter, shielding human settlements in Hillsbrad and securing vital operations at the Azurelode Mine. Their sturdy stone architecture and deep entrenchments provide the Alliance with an anchor against nearby threats.

Dun Mandarr. Dun Mandarr is an abandoned dwarven camp situated before an icy cavern in south-eastern Winterspring. Established by the dwarf Jaron Stoneshaper, the site now sits in ruins after its occupants fled an onslaught of enraged local moonkin. Bearing the traditional dwarven prefix 'Dun', Dun Mandarr was established by the explorer Jaron Stoneshaper as a base of operations in the frozen reaches of southeastern Winterspring. Stoneshaper's curiosity proved his undoing when he uncovered a relic known as the Blue-Feathered Amulet. The artifact's disturbance provoked the fury of the native wildkin, who descended upon the encampment in an uncontrollable rage. Overwhelmed and driven out, the dwarves abandoned the camp entirely. Today, no friendly souls remain among the snowbanks; ferocious, territorial moonkin guard the cavern and prowl the broken shelters.

Dun Modr. Dun Modr is an ancient fortified dwarven town in northern Wetlands, guarding the southern approach to the Thandol Span. Once a critical fortress held and contested across multiple wars, it has recently fallen to a hostile force of Dark Iron dwarves. Situated at the northern edge of the Wetlands, Dun Modr commands the primary overland highway linking Khaz Modan with the northern human kingdoms. Because of this vital location, the stronghold has seen heavy bloodshed over the decades. During the Second War, the Orcish Horde captured and entrenched themselves within the dwarven fortress, using it as a forward staging ground to launch raids and repel Alliance armies. Stromgarde warriors launched a brutal amphibious assault from Tol Barad to reclaim it, only for the Orcs to strike back in a bloody tug-of-war. Alliance forces led by Lord Anduin Lothar ultimately drove the invaders south across the Thandol Span, restoring dwarven custody over the bastion.

Dunemaul Compound. Dunemaul Compound serves as the central settlement and ogre mound for the Dunemaul clan in Tanaris. Tucked into the rocky ridges bordering the desert wastes, it houses the clan's brute enforcers and spellcasters. Carved into the rugged desert rock of western Tanaris, the Dunemaul Compound is the primary stronghold of the Dunemaul ogres. These hulking desert dwellers have adapted to the harsh arid climate, scratching out an existence through brute force and opportunism. The compound itself centers on an ogre mound and cave network. Though primitive, the clan fields a dangerous mix of warriors, enforcers, and twisted spellcasters practicing dark warlock and mage magics. For travelers journeying across the dunes, the settlement is a treacherous den of aggressive giants who violently reject uninvited guests.

Durnholde Keep. Durnholde Keep is a shattered fortress situated east of Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Once the nerve center of the Alliance's orc internment camps and the place where Warchief Thrall was raised as a captive gladiator, it now lies in ruin, occupied by outlaws of the Syndicate. Built by the Alliance, Durnholde served as the headquarters overseeing the southern internment camps following the Second War. Commanded by the ambitious and corrupt Lieutenant General Aedelas Blackmoore, it functioned as both an administrative fortress and a gladiatorial arena. It was here that Blackmoore raised the orphaned infant Go'el, naming him Thrall and training him to fight for sport and profit. Aided by Taretha Foxton, Thrall escaped captivity and later united the dispersed orc clans under the banner of the new Horde. Returning to Durnholde, Thrall laid siege to the fortress, slew Blackmoore, and called upon the earth spirits to shatter its walls.

Dust Plains. The Dust Plains form the dry, wind-scoured southern frontier of Westfall. Marked by arid ground and scarce scrub, the region is overrun by aggressive gnoll encampments and borders an old wizard's tower along its eastern rise. Stretching across southern Westfall, the Dust Plains mark the transition from troubled farmland to desolate wilderness. Unlike the plundered farmsteads to the north, this arid reach has long been surrendered to packs of feral gnolls who ambush travelers and challenge anyone venturing toward the coast or the nearby hills. On the eastern boundary sits Klaven's Tower, an old mage tower now held by the Defias rogue Klaven Mortwake, which offers no shelter from the beasts prowling the surrounding wastes.

Dustbowl. The Dustbowl is a sprawling, arid expanse in the northwestern Badlands, lying between the Horde outpost of Kargath and the central Valley of Fangs. Swept by scouring desert winds, it is a harsh wilderness populated by scavengers, prowling beasts, and wandering elementals. It is also the site of Camp Wurg, making it a frequent crossing point for travelers braving the wasteland. Stretching across the northwest of the Badlands, the Dustbowl is characterized by dry gulches, cracked clay, and relentless winds that stir up choking plumes of grit. Despite the barren landscape, tough desert flora persists in the form of hardy cacti and scattered, gnarled trees. The open flatland presents constant danger to unguided wayfarers, who must contend with predatory coyotes, circling buzzards, and living rock elementals born of the rugged earth. Tucked within this scrubland lies Camp Wurg, providing a recognizable landmark amidst the otherwise desolate expanse.

Dustfire Valley. Dustfire Valley is a dry, windswept gulch nestled along the northern edge of the Searing Gorge. It serves as the scorched threshold leading directly to the fortified gate of Stonewrought Pass, which bars the mountain route into Loch Modan. Tucked away in northern Searing Gorge, Dustfire Valley is defined by choking ash, brittle rock, and barren canyon walls. Its most notable feature is the imposing, locked dwarven gateway sealing Stonewrought Pass. Because of these locked iron doors, direct travel north into the Valley of Kings and Loch Modan remains entirely barred to ordinary wanderers, leaving the valley an isolated cul-de-sac amidst the sulfurous wastes.

Dustwallow Bay. Dustwallow Bay is an inlet of the Great Sea tucked between the sodden coast of Dustwallow Marsh and the fortified port of Theramore Isle. Its brackish coastal shallows teem with marine life, treacherous shoals, and secluded coves just off the main maritime routes of eastern Kalimdor. Dustwallow Bay defines the coastal boundary where the stagnant, murky wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh meet the open waters of the Great Sea. Flanked to the east by Theramore Isle, the bay serves as an oceanic approach for vessels arriving at Lady Jaina Proudmoore's island haven. Despite heavy maritime traffic running to and from the docks, the surrounding coastline remains wild and hazardous, pocked with rocky outcrops, murloc encampments, and tucked-away inlets like Tidefury Cove.

Dustwind Cave. Dustwind Cave is a secluded hollow perched atop the cliffs of Razorwind Canyon, just northeast of Razor Hill. It serves as an active training ground and covert sanctuary for initiates of the nefarious Burning Blade cult operating within Durotar. Overlooking Razorwind Canyon, Dustwind Cave is one of the closest and most perilous threats to Razor Hill. While many assume demonic cultists gather only in deep subterranean depths, here the Burning Blade trains fresh recruits right under the noses of the Horde authorities. Shadowy cultists tutor initiates in forbidden dark magics and demonology, preparing them to undermine the young orcish realm from within Durotar's own borders.

Dwarven District. Tucked into the northern corner of Stormwind City, the Dwarven District is a bustling industrial enclave filled with roaring furnaces, ringing anvils, and thick smog. Home to many of the city's dwarven craftsmen, it serves as the beating mechanical heart of the city. The northern quarter of Stormwind is home to the city's dwarven artisans, smiths, and engineers and their trades. The district retains the unmistakable character of Ironforge, dominated by heavy stone masonry, sprawling smelting operations, and bustling craft shops. Shops such as Potts' Plates provide a familiar haven for craftspeople from Khaz Modan. It also houses the Stormwind portal to the Deeprun Tram, tethering the human capital directly to Ironforge.

Eastern Strand. The Eastern Strand is a stretch of southern coastline in Hillsbrad Foothills, lying to the southeast toward the border of the Arathi Highlands. Once peaceful shores, the beaches and shallows have been overrun by hostile Daggerspine naga establishing a coastal beachhead. Running along the southeastern edge of Hillsbrad Foothills, the Eastern Strand complements the Western Strand across the bay. While the region is primarily known for human farming settlements and territorial clashes between Southshore and Tarren Mill, these sandy flats and tidelines are dominated entirely by the Daggerspine naga. Creeping out of the Great Sea, the serpent folk slither across the sandbars and dwell among the rocky outcrops, watching the mainland closely.

Eastmoon Ruins. The Eastmoon Ruins are an ancient troll archaeological site situated in eastern Tanaris, perched just west of the Gaping Chasm. Once built by the desert empires of old, the crumbling stone masonry is now occupied by Dunemaul ogres using the remnants as a desert encampment. Rising out of the blistering desert floor just west of the insect-infested Gaping Chasm, the Eastmoon Ruins preserve the crumbling architecture of ancient troll civilization. Decaying pillars, weathered stone plazas, and sun-bleached monuments hint at a time long before the sands swallowed this region. Rather than scholars or troll descendants tending the shrines, the site is firmly held by the Dunemaul ogres, who rely on the broken walls for shelter and vantage over nearby trade routes.

Eastvale Logging Camp. Eastvale Logging Camp is a vital lumber settlement tucked into the eastern woodlands of Elwynn Forest, near the border with the Redridge Mountains. The camp supplies vital timber to Stormwind and surrounding settlements, but its operations are constantly hampered by hungry predators prowling the surrounding forests. Orders for timber constantly stream into Eastvale Logging Camp from buyers across the Kingdom of Stormwind, but meeting these strict deadlines is a harrowing task. The dense wilderness surrounding the camp swarms with vicious wolves and prowling bears that routinely chase lumberjacks away from their worksites, leaving valuable cut timber abandoned in the woods. Under the direction of Supervisor Raelen, the camp frequently relies on wandering adventurers to cull the encroaching beasts and retrieve fallen wood before deliveries fall fatally behind schedule.

Eastwall Gate. Eastwall Gate is a fortified side entrance set into the perimeter wall of the fallen city of Stratholme. Located in the northern reaches of the Eastern Plaguelands, it offers a direct secondary access point into Stratholme's interior ruins, bypassing the chaos of the city's main gates. While the grand main entrance of Stratholme opens directly onto King's Square, the Eastwall Gate pierces the city's eastern fortifications. Barred securely against intruders, this gateway leads straight into Elders' Square, close by the steps of Alonsus Chapel. For those venturing into the burning heart of the Scourge stronghold, bypassing the front barricades can mean the difference between a swift strike into the city's depths and a meatgrinder assault through the forward undead lines.

Eastwall Tower. Eastwall Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower situated in the Eastern Plaguelands near the eastern road. Sacked during the Third War when the Scourge swept across the kingdom, its remains overlook the Scourge-infested wilderness. Built as a border sentinel for the kingdom of Lordaeron, Eastwall Tower once watched over travelers heading toward the far reaches of the realm. When the Scourge invaded during the Third War, the outpost was crushed along with the surrounding settlements, leaving shattered stone arches and burnt timber behind. Now, with the Lich King's armies still infesting the region, the tower's elevated position makes it an indispensable forward post. Its ruined ramparts overlook roads through the Scourge-infested countryside.

Echo Isles. The Echo Isles are a cluster of tropical islands lying just off the southeastern coast of Durotar. Originally settled by the Darkspear trolls after fleeing their ancestral islands, the archipelago is currently lost to the rogue witch doctor Zalazane, who drove his people into exile with dark magic and enslaved minions. Following their flight across the Great Sea alongside Thrall, the Darkspear tribe claimed the Echo Isles as their new home. Their peace was repeatedly shattered: first by the naval forces of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore during Kul Tiras' invasion of Durotar, and later from within. Shortly after the trolls drove back Proudmoore's fleet, one of their own witch doctors, Zalazane, seized dark arts to enslave the minds of his kin. Chieftain Vol'jin and the free Darkspears were forced to abandon the islands once more, seeking temporary refuge across the narrow strait at Sen'jin Village.

Echo Ridge Mine. Echo Ridge Mine is a small excavation carved into the northwestern cliffs of Northshire Valley. Rich in stone and ore, it has recently fallen into the clutches of a destructive kobold infestation, halting Northshire's local operations. Tucked away in the hills above Northshire Abbey, Echo Ridge Mine was meant to supply the valley with useful stone and metal. Instead, opportunistic kobolds swarmed through the tunnels, driving out the local workers. Marshal McBride views the infestation as an unacceptable security risk to Northshire's safety and recruitment efforts, directing new recruits straight into the tunnels to cull their numbers and reclaim the site.

Elder Rise. Elder Rise sits directly east of Thunder Bluff's central plateau, reachable across long suspension bridges from both the High and Middle Rises. It serves as the spiritual heart of the tauren capital, hosting the Cenarion Circle, tauren druids and priests, and the governing Council of Elders. Connected to the main mesas by swaying rope bridges, Elder Rise is dedicated to quiet reflection, sacred wisdom, and civic governance. Tauren druids and priests gather here to teach acolytes the ways of nature and spiritual devotion. High atop this mesa resides Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem, the revered leader who brought druidism back to the tauren people and forged close ties with the Cenarion Circle. Alongside these wild sanctuaries stands the Hall of Elders, where tribal leaders convene to deliberate on matters facing their fledgling capital.

Eldreth Row. Eldreth Row comprises the soaring, ruined outer halls forming the western entrance to Dire Maul in Feralas. Once a grand threshold of ancient Eldre'Thalas, the area is now choked with overgrowth and fiercely patrolled by Gordunni ogres. Standing as the outermost perimeter of ancient Eldre'Thalas, Eldreth Row is an imposing avenue of high-arched elven architecture that sits just outside the deeper quarters and the Broken Commons. Centuries of neglect have cracked its stonework, allowing the creeping flora of Feralas to reclaim its colonnades. Today, the pristine majesty of the Highborne has been replaced by the crude dominance of the Gordunni ogres, who use the halls as an outer staging ground, guarding the paths leading east toward the Warpwood Quarter and west past the Dire Pool.

Emerald Sanctuary. The Emerald Sanctuary is an outpost of the Cenarion Circle situated at the southern entrance of Felwood. Here, night elven and tauren druids unite to study the pervasive demonic taint and attempt the arduous task of healing the corrupted woodland. Perched on the southern edge of Felwood near the Ashenvale border, the Emerald Sanctuary serves as the primary base of operations for the Cenarion Circle in this blighted wilderness. Unlike the bitter factional conflicts burning across Kalimdor, this sanctuary offers a neutral foothold where druids look past politics to focus entirely on ecological restoration. From here, researchers track corrupted flora and direct investigations toward Jaedenar, seeking any viable method to cleanse the poisoned soil.

Engineering Labs. The Engineering Labs are a multi-tiered research and manufacturing facility deep within Gnomeregan. Connected to the Workshop Entrance and Launch Bay, this bustling center of gnome innovation was overrun during the city's radioactive cataclysm and is now swarming with crazed leper gnomes and rogue mechanical contraptions. Built around a central mechanical structure, the Engineering Labs span two primary tiers connected by a central cargo lift. In Gnomeregan's prime, tinkerers here developed schematics and fine-tuned clockwork inventions. Today, radiation leaks have driven the remaining researchers mad, transforming them into deranged leper gnomes who mindlessly guard malfunctioning machinery alongside rogue constructs.

Ethel Rethor. Ethel Rethor is an ancient night elven ruin situated along the rugged northwestern coast of Desolace. While a solitary, sealed tower still rises above the waves, the majority of the sunken settlement now lies submerged in the sea and overrun by hostile naga. Perched on the desolate coast of western Kalimdor, Ethel Rethor stands as a haunting reminder of the ancient night elven civilization that flourished before the Great Sundering. Much of the grand architecture has collapsed into the ocean depths, leaving only shattered foundations and a lone, weathered tower protruding from the surf. A small bridge extends toward the tower's sealed portal, but the structure remains shut tight against the elements and intruders alike. The submerged chambers and surrounding shallows have become a stronghold for coastal naga, making the waters treacherous for any who wander near.

Everlook. Everlook is a snow-swept trading outpost in central Winterspring established by the Steamwheedle Cartel. Situated at the crossroads of the snowy valley's routes, it serves as a neutral haven for merchants, prospectors, and researchers braving the high-altitude cold. Everlook represents the Steamwheedle Cartel's northernmost endeavor, mirroring outposts like Gadgetzan and Booty Bay under a blanket of permafrost. The walled settlement perches at the intersection of Winterspring's snowdrifts, operating under strictly enforced neutrality. It hosts the only operational bank and shared auction house services in the region, drawing both Alliance and Horde travelers in search of warmth and shelter. Guarded by hired bruisers, the town offers refuge from ferocious frostsabers and yetis.

Faldir's Cove. Faldir's Cove is a secluded natural harbor nestled along the southern coastline of the Arathi Highlands. Steeped in human history, it is traditionally remembered as the departure point from which early settlers sailed south to found Stormwind. Today, it serves as an emergency shelter for stranded Blackwater Raiders whose fleet ran afoul of local hazards. Tucked away behind the rugged bluffs south of Stromgarde Keep, Faldir's Cove is linked to the mainland by a concealed cave tunnel. The cove honors the memory of Faldir, the ancient Arathor explorer whose expedition set sail from these very shores to cross the Great Sea and establish the southern kingdom of Stormwind. In the present day, however, its quiet waters house a very different crowd: an expedition of Blackwater Raiders from Booty Bay, led by Captains Steelgut and O'Breen, who sailed north pursuing ancient elven treasures only to end up trapped in the bay.

Falfarren River. The Falfarren River flows northeast to southwest through the heart of Ashenvale, originating on the slopes of Mount Hyjal before slipping underground beneath the Barrens' northern mountains. It forms a natural boundary between night elven domains around Astranaar to the west and the encroaching Horde outposts to the east. Travelers must tread carefully, as its shaded banks and shallows harbor hostile wildlife and mark the edge of open conflict. Feeding down from Mount Hyjal, the waters of the Falfarren cascade across waterfalls into Xavian before winding between Splintertree Post and Night Run. While it is neither exceptionally deep nor impassable under ordinary weather, it serves as the rough geopolitical dividing line in central Ashenvale. To the west lie Astranaar and the core holdings of the Kaldorei; to the east sit the camps and lumber operations of the Horde. Crossing the main road's wooden bridges brings travelers into the contested heart of the forest, where patrols clash along the banks.

Fallen Sky Lake. Fallen Sky Lake is a secluded body of water nestled deep within the forests of eastern Ashenvale. Situated between Silverwing Outpost and the encroaching Warsong Labor Camp, the serene waters hide danger in the form of hostile shadethicket bog beasts that aggressively defend the lake and its central isle. Tucked south of Silverwing Outpost and just west of the Warsong Labor Camp, Fallen Sky Lake offers a fleeting glimpse of Ashenvale's natural splendor before the Orcish axes took root nearby. The shores and the small islet rising from the middle of the lake are inhabited by shadethickets—hulking bog beasts that view any intruder as a threat. The heart of the island serves as the domain of a powerful Shadethicket Oracle, who hoards the fallen moonstones once gathered at the lake and keeps the local shadethickets bound to the waters and relentlessly vigilant against travelers passing through.

Fallow Sanctuary. The Fallow Sanctuary is a secluded village hidden deep within the bogs of the Swamp of Sorrows. It serves as home to an isolated tribe of mutated draenei known as the Lost Ones, whose severe grief and homesickness have driven them feral. Tucked away among the sunken trees of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Fallow Sanctuary was established by stranded Lost Ones seeking a place of their own. Severed from their ancestral world and deformed by dark energies, these wretched outcasts found no peace in the marshland. Over time, relentless sorrow and isolation shattered their sanity, reducing the tribe to a hostile, feral state where they fiercely attack any outsiders who trespass into their village.

Faol's Rest. Faol's Rest is a quiet, neglected gravesite situated in eastern Tirisfal Glades, just southwest of the Scarlet Monastery. It was erected as the tomb of Archbishop Alonsus Faol, the revered spiritual patriarch who founded the Knights of the Silver Hand. Today, untended beneath the blighted canopy, it serves as a release graveyard for those who perish near the monastery. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, this secluded hollow was a place of solemn pilgrimage. It holds the stone tomb of Archbishop Alonsus Faol, who led the Church of the Holy Light through the dark days of the Second War and instituted the order of paladins to protect humanity. Faol passed away peacefully prior to the arrival of the Scourge, spared the mortal agony of seeing his kingdom fall. In those brighter years, mourners regularly journeyed up the road from Capital City to leave offerings and pay respects to the beloved patriarch.

Far Watch Post. Far Watch Post is a fortified Horde outpost situated just west of the Southfury River bridge connecting Durotar to the Barrens. Serving as the front line of defense for the orcish homeland, the post guards vital trade caravans against aggressive quilboar packs and hostile Alliance incursions. Located at the western foot of the bridge out of Durotar, Far Watch Post is the first bastion of Horde authority travellers see when entering the vast, arid savannah of the Barrens. The settlement is Spartan but functional, built for tactical readiness rather than comfort. It features a sturdy orcish watchtower, a burrow, and pre-sighted siege catapults trained toward the dusty plains. Directly south of the main road, peons tend a pen of riding wolves ready to bear messengers or reinforcements. Far Watch Post exists primarily to keep the supply road to Crossroads secure, screening incoming traffic and repelling raids from roaming quilboar tribes and stealthy Alliance scouts.

Fargodeep Mine. Fargodeep Mine is an abandoned gold mine nestled in central Elwynn Forest, south of Goldshire. Once a productive source of wealth for the Kingdom of Stormwind, it has recently been overrun by a belligerent clan of kobolds. Fargodeep Mine once provided steady gold to Stormwind's treasury, but the Kingdom's dwindling military presence in Elwynn has left outlying resources vulnerable. Kobolds quickly swarmed into the dark tunnels, establishing a bustling warren beneath the hills. Marshal Dughan and the local authorities in Goldshire view the infestation with deep concern, not only because of lost ore, but because the emboldened creatures now threaten nearby farmsteads like the Stonefield and Maclure holdings.

Farstrider Lodge. Farstrider Lodge is a hunting outpost in southeastern Loch Modan. Its architecture appears to be high elven, while its residents include the high elf Vyrin Swiftwind, dwarves, and humans. Hunters and travelers come here for training, supplies, and work in the surrounding wilds. Farstrider Lodge stands apart from the sturdy stone buildings typical of Khaz Modan. Its architecture suggests high elven craftsmanship. Vyrin Swiftwind is the only known high elf still residing here, alongside dwarves and humans. The lodge's founder and date of construction are not established.

Feathermoon Stronghold. Feathermoon Stronghold is the premier night elf military base in southern Kalimdor, situated securely on Sardor Isle off the Forgotten Coast of Feralas. Commanded by General Shandris Feathermoon, this fortified outpost projects Sentinel strength across the wild forest and keeps watch over regional threats. Perched on Sardor Isle across the channel from Feralas's mainland, Feathermoon Stronghold serves as the primary strategic base for the Sentinels in southern Kalimdor. Built among ancient elven groves and supplied with a sacred moonwell, the fortress houses archers, huntresses, and support staff under the direct supervision of General Shandris Feathermoon. From this insular sanctuary, the night elves project their influence over the verdant interior of Feralas, guarding against demonic corruption, hostile wildlife, and encroaching Horde expeditions.

Feathermoon Stronghold (Classic). Feathermoon Stronghold is a fortified night elf bastion situated on Sardor Isle off the western shores of Feralas. Established by General Shandris Feathermoon, it serves as the Alliance's primary staging ground and military anchor in southern Kalimdor. Perched on Sardor Isle just off the Forgotten Coast, Feathermoon Stronghold stands as a crucial bulwark for the Night Elves and the broader Alliance. Built under the direction of General Shandris Feathermoon—Tyrande Whisperwind's trusted lieutenant for ten millennia—the fortress projects Sentinel power deep into southern Kalimdor. Its isolated island geography shields it from the beasts, ogres, and Horde interlopers prowling the primeval jungles of mainland Feralas.

Fel Rock. Fel Rock is a blighted cavern hidden within the woods just north of Dolanaar on the boughs of Teldrassil. Once a tranquil hollow, it has fallen into corruption under the influence of the satyr Lord Melenas and his horde of vicious grells. Tucked away in the forested hills north of Dolanaar, Fel Rock was once an ordinary, peaceful cavern carved into the wood and stone of Teldrassil. Today, it stands as an unsettling reminder of the creeping taint encroaching on the world tree. Twisted roots and unnatural shadows dominate the cavern interior, overrun by swarms of wild grells and grellkin.

Felfire Hill. Felfire Hill is a blighted, demon-infested rise nestled in eastern Ashenvale. Struck by falling infernals during the Third War, its corrupted soil still burns with demonic power. The Horde maintains fortified guard posts on the bridges leading into the hill to safeguard their nearby settlements. During the cataclysmic invasion of the Third War, flaming meteors fell across Kalimdor as the Burning Legion unleashed its dread infernals. Several of those fiery behemoths struck this ridge in Ashenvale, scouring away the ancient woodlands and corrupting the earth itself. Today, the scorched landscape remains saturated with fel energy and prowled by lingering demons who survived the Legion's defeat at Mount Hyjal.

Felpaw Village. Felpaw Village is a corrupted furbolg settlement nestled in the far northern reaches of Felwood, guarding the mountain path leading directly to Timbermaw Hold. Inhabited by the fallen Deadwood tribe, its huts and gathering grounds are tainted by demonic influence and hostile to all outsiders. Situated at the northern edge of Felwood, Felpaw Village serves as the primary northern redoubt for the fallen Deadwood furbolgs. Once gentle forest wardens, the tribe fell victim to the demonic blight unleashed during the Third War, driving them into a state of feral madness. Now, the village stands as a blighted enclave filled with crude huts, ritual totems, and hostile warriors who attack anyone wandering near the tunnel entrance to Timbermaw Hold.

Felstone Field. Felstone Field is a blighted farmstead located in the northwestern Western Plaguelands. Once a thriving piece of Lordaeron agricultural land, it has been claimed by the Scourge and anchored by a plague cauldron spewing toxic fumes across the ruined soil. Before the Third War, Felstone Field was a peaceful, productive family farm feeding the citizens of Lordaeron. When the plague swept through the north, the homestead fell swiftly to the Cult of the Damned and the Scourge. Today, the fields sprout dead weeds and creeping rot instead of grain. At the heart of the farmland sits an enormous plague cauldron, continuously churning foul vapors into the sky under the watch of Cauldron Lord Bilemaw and legions of skeletal flayers, sorcerers, and ravenous ghouls.

Fenris Isle. Fenris Isle is a large, mist-shrouded island in Lordamere Lake, bordering the eastern edge of Silverpine Forest. Once home to a bustling Lordaeron military stronghold, the island now lies under the iron grip of undead Rot Hide gnolls and a rogue Scourge necromancer. Before the Third War devastated northern Lordaeron, Fenris Isle served as a vital outpost for the kingdom, anchored by Fenris Keep. When the Scourge tore through the realm, the garrison was slaughtered or fled into exile, leaving the island abandoned to the dead. In the years since, the island became a stronghold for the Rot Hide gnolls—vile, plague-ridden creatures who established a crude empire across the lake's shores. The Forsaken of Silverpine Forest keep a vigilant watch on the island, viewing its entrenched inhabitants as a severe threat to their northern territories.

Fenris Keep. Fenris Keep is an isolated stone fortress situated atop Fenris Isle in the heart of Lordamere Lake. Once a strategic stronghold housing Lordaeron troops, it has fallen into the hands of the Scourge under the rogue mage Thule Ravenclaw. Before the Third War, Fenris Keep held strategic importance for the Kingdom of Lordaeron, stationing a sizable contingent of troops to safeguard Lordamere Lake. When the undead Scourge swept across the land, the island fortress was overwhelmed along with the rest of the realm. Rather than crumbling into forgotten ruin, it was seized by Thule Ravenclaw, a traitorous former wizard of the Kirin Tor. Ravenclaw allied himself with the Scourge, subjugated the resident gnolls with foul necromancy to create the ravenous Rot Hide pack, and entrenched himself deep inside the keep's stone halls.

Feral Scar Vale. Feral Scar Vale is a rocky gorge tucked within the High Wilderness of western Feralas. Overrun by territorial Feral Scar yetis, its cavernous tunnels are notoriously perilous to travelers who venture off the overgrown forest trails. Situated amid the thick foliage and sheer cliffs of the High Wilderness, Feral Scar Vale serves as the primary den for the savage Feral Scar yetis. While yetis are common in the snowy peaks of Alterac and Dun Morogh, these primal brutes have adapted completely to the wild, humid climate of Feralas. They fiercely defend the vale's cave network, hoarding bone trophies and aggressively driving off any intruders who wander into their hunting grounds.

Field of Giants. The Field of Giants is an expansive plain covering the southern Barrens between Camp Taurajo and the marshes of Dustwallow. Named for the towering kodo, thunder lizards, and massive beasts that graze its arid scrub, the region has recently grown far more perilous due to an encroaching silithid infestation. Stretching along the southern span of the Gold Road, the Field of Giants is remote, rugged, and lightly defended compared to the Barrens to the north. While the road's wooden watchtowers stand largely abandoned, the land itself thrums with life. Tremendous herds of Kalimdor's megafauna wander the vast flats, drawing hunters and naturalists alike. However, safety is elusive here: dwarven excavators from Bael Modan dig aggressively to the south, and a far more sinister menace has begun burrowing beneath the earth.

Fire Plume Ridge. Fire Plume Ridge is the active volcano rising directly from the center of Un'Goro Crater. Its searing slopes and subterranean magma channels fuel the crater's geysers and steam pools while playing host to fierce fire elementals. Towering over the primeval basin of Un'Goro, Fire Plume Ridge stands in sharp contrast to the surrounding lush jungle. Lava steadily cascades down its scorched rock faces, carving a landscape of ash and basalt. Subterranean magma arteries spiderweb outward beneath the soil from the ridge, fueling the bubbling geysers and hot springs scattered across the basin. The oppressive heat here is legendary—far exceeding ordinary volcanic temperatures according to goblin measuring devices—making it perilous for ill-prepared explorers to wander without ample water and shade.

Fire Scar Shrine. Fire Scar Shrine is a despoiled night elf shrine nestled in the southwestern forests of Ashenvale. Once a serene place of worship, it has been corrupted by demonic forces and turned into a blister of fel energy right on Astranaar's doorstep. Located southwest of Astranaar and west of the Ruins of Stardust, Fire Scar Shrine stands as a grim reminder of the Burning Legion's lingering poison in Ashenvale. The shrine has fallen under the sway of demonic corruption, nurtured by servants of the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand and the Shadow Council. Fel magic has twisted the surrounding earth into scorched rock, where roaming demons now gather in open defiance of the forest's defenders.

Firewatch Ridge. Firewatch Ridge is a high volcanic bluff in the northern reaches of Searing Gorge, serving as a primary encampment for the Dark Iron dwarves. Looming directly above the vast excavation known as the Cauldron, the ridge is heavily fortified by dwarven sentries, mechanical golems, and nesting fire spiders. To the northwest, an ominous cave system reveals an entrenched presence of the Twilight's Hammer cult. Perched above the industrial devastation of the Cauldron, Firewatch Ridge functions as a critical staging ground for the Dark Iron clan's operations in Searing Gorge. Dwarven guards, engineers, and molten golem creations patrol the crags, fiercely defending their foothold alongside venomous flame spiders native to the smoldering rocks. Its elevation provides the Dark Irons an unobstructed view of the surrounding ash plains, ensuring early warning against rival incursions from Ironforge or the Thorium Brotherhood.

Flame Crest. Flame Crest is a rugged neutral outpost perched atop a rocky ledge overlooking the volcanic wastes of the Burning Steppes. Accessed only across a crude span, this precarious encampment serves as a forward staging ground against the Dark Horde entrenched in Blackrock Mountain. It provides essential aerial connections and a haven for scouts, beast collectors, and strategists. Situated high on an isolated stone outcropping, Flame Crest commands a watchful view over the scorched ash and lava plains of the Burning Steppes. Reached only by crossing a narrow, rickety wooden bridge, the outpost is naturally defensible against the prowling beasts and roaming orc warbands of the wastes. Wind riders roost along the heights, connecting the camp back across the Redridge range to Kargath, Stonard, Thorium Point, and Rog'mar in the Riverglades.

Foothold Citadel. Foothold Citadel serves as the central military barracks and command post within Theramore Isle. Overlooking the fortified settlement, it houses the officers and guards who protect the Alliance's primary bastion on southern Kalimdor. Rising within the fortified stone walls of Theramore Isle, Foothold Citadel is the nerve center of local Alliance defense. The citadel houses the high command of the Theramore Guard, including Captain Garran Vimes and Commander Samaul, along with field medics, logistics officers, and quartermasters. Its utilitarian stone halls bustle with regular patrols and drills, keeping Lady Jaina Proudmoore's forces prepared against threats creeping out of the surrounding swamplands.

Forest's Edge. Forest's Edge is a wooded wedge of land along the southwestern frontier of Elwynn Forest, flanked by rivers leading toward Westfall. Guarded to the north by Westbrook Garrison, this untamed area has become dangerously overrun by riverpaw gnolls under the command of the notorious Hogger. Tucked southwest of Stormwind City between Mirror Lake Orchard and the rivers bordering Westfall, Forest's Edge forms a natural peninsula of woodland. Despite its proximity to Westbrook Garrison, the Stormwind army's thin ranks have left the area vulnerable to wild beasts and raiding parties. Wandering boars roam among the trees and along the riverbanks, but the true menace is the concentration of Riverpaw gnolls who have made these woods their staging ground.

Forest Song. Forest Song is an ancient night elf ruin nestled in northeastern Ashenvale, near the tainted woods of Satyrnaar and the great portal at Bough Shadow. At present, it stands largely deserted save for the vigilant druid Kayneth Stillwind, who watches over the eastern border against emergent threats. Tucked away in the dense woodlands of northeastern Ashenvale, Forest Song was once an elegant settlement of the kaldorei. Today, white stone columns and crumbling archways are overgrown with ivy and wild ferns. Located northeast of Satyrnaar and just north of the encroaching Warsong Lumber Camp, the ruins hold a quiet, strategic overlook along the eastern trails toward Azshara and Bough Shadow. While the woods around it are plagued by demonic corruption and Horde incursions, the ruin itself maintains a haunting, tranquil stillness.

Forgotten Coast. The Forgotten Coast forms the wild western shore of Feralas, where the ancient rainforest meets the Veiled Sea. Lumbering sea giants and water elementals roam this battered strand. Stretching along the western edge of Feralas, the Forgotten Coast is a windswept shoreline confronting the expanse of the Veiled Sea. Unlike the dense canopy inland, this frontier is exposed to the elements and dominated by towering sea giants and roving water elementals pacing the surf. Travelers emerging from the forest canopy must contend with these primeval coastal guardians while navigating access to the sea, where ferry connections link to the night elven bastion of Sardor Isle.

Forgotten Pool. The Forgotten Pool is a submerged cavern tucked deep beneath the flooded corridors of Blackfathom Deeps. Located beyond the Moonshrine Ruins, this quiet dead-end serves as the aquatic lair of monstrous deep-sea predators lurking in the subterranean dark. Reaching the Forgotten Pool requires diving into the sunken subterranean waterways extending past the Moonshrine Ruins. Cut off from dry ground, the pool is an isolated, stagnant cavern completely flooded by dark waters. Away from the chanting Twilight's Hammer cultists and the patrolling naga, this secluded pocket serves as the lair of the ancient aquatic terror known as Old Serra'kis, keeping the beast hidden in the flooded dark.

Forgotten Pools. The Forgotten Pools is the northernmost of the verdant oases scattered across the arid Barrens, located just northwest of the Crossroads. Fed by subterranean springs, this vibrant pocket of lush flora and waters is bitterly contested between indigenous wildlife, wandering Kolkar centaur, and the Horde. Situated off the western road leading out of the Crossroads, the Forgotten Pools offers a stark contrast to the parched savannas that surround it. Thick reeds, palm trees, and unusual flora like Laden Mushrooms cluster around its freshwater shore, drawing plainstriders, snapjaw turtles, and zhevras from miles around. However, the oasis is far from peaceful. Kolkar centaur maintain a constant encampment along the banks, jealously guarding the water supply against travelers and bringing them into direct conflict with Horde travelers from the Crossroads.

Forlorn Cavern. Tucked along the northern shores of Ironforge's subterranean lake, the Forlorn Cavern is a dimly lit, secluded district far removed from the city's bustling Great Forge. It serves as a shadowy refuge where thieves, cutpurses, and practitioners of the dark arts conduct their business away from prying dwarven guards. While the rest of Ironforge clangs with anvil strikes and radiates heat from the Great Forge, the Forlorn Cavern is cold, damp, and hushed. Wrapping along the northern edge of the mountain's underground lake, the winding pathways sit comfortably out of sight between the Mystic Ward and the Hall of Explorers. Its gloom makes it an ideal gathering place for those who prefer to keep their affairs discreet. Rogues and warlocks train here alongside vendors serving them, while weapon merchants and fishermen also work beside the lake.

Forlorn Cloister. The Forlorn Cloister is the haunted graveyard wing of the Scarlet Monastery. Here, members of the Scarlet Crusade desperately torch the bodies of fallen brothers to prevent them from rising into undeath, while restless spirits and shambling corpses roam among the tombs. Once a peaceful sanctuary where the priests and paladins of Lordaeron laid their honoured dead to rest, the Forlorn Cloister has become a grim charnel ground. Despite the Scarlet Crusade's fanatical vigilance, the taint of the plague has seeped deep into the earth. crusaders patrol the fog-shrouded cemetery with torches, frantically burning remains to stave off the rot. Even so, spectres glide between crypts and the dead pull free from their graves, ruled over by dark magic deep within the grounds.

Forlorn Ridge. Forlorn Ridge is a towering mountain ridge looming over southwestern Azshara. Its strategic elevation and commanding views over the coast have drawn the attention of both the Alliance and the Horde, who have each carved out fortifications along its slopes. Rising sharply above the autumnal forests of western Azshara, Forlorn Ridge dominates the surrounding terrain. Resembling an ancient, long-dormant volcano, its high vantage point offers a sweeping view over the coastal approaches and the ruined elven estates below. Because control over these heights dictates military dominance in the sector, both Alliance and Horde forces have established encampments and outposts along its mountain flanks, watching each other warily across the rugged bluffs.

Forlorn Rowe. The Forlorn Rowe is an ominous, shadowy hill perched on the northern boundary of the Raven Hill Cemetery in Duskwood. It is infamous as the dark abode of Morbent Fel, a necromancer whose malevolent magic animates the restless dead throughout the forest. Rising along the northern edge of the Raven Hill Cemetery, the Forlorn Rowe is perpetually cloaked in gloom. Atop this rise sits the home of Morbent Fel, the lich-like necromancer responsible for much of the walking dead haunting the surrounding wilderness. Bound by foul arcane enchantments, the master of the hill directs his skeletal servants from this vantage, rendering the entire northwestern corner of Duskwood perilous for travelers.

Fray Island. Fray Island is a windswept, rocky islet lying just off the Merchant Coast of the Barrens. Home to a rough-and-tumble training ring, it is famous as a neutral haven where warriors from across Azeroth come to test their mettle. Situated off the eastern bluffs of the Barrens, Fray Island is far removed from the watchful eyes of both Orgrimmar and Theramore. The island serves as a training place for warriors of all races and creeds. At its heart sits a fighting arena overseen by Klannoc Macleod, where seasoned fighters and raw recruits gather to compete in brutal brawls.

Frayfeather Highlands. The Frayfeather Highlands form an elevated wilderness in the dense forests of Feralas. This remote plateau is the ancestral roost and nesting ground of the wild Frayfeather hippogryphs. Intrepid scavengers and naturalists often brave its territorial flocks in search of intact hippogryph eggs. Rising above the surrounding forest floor of Feralas, the Frayfeather Highlands are dominated by steep slopes and crags where wild hippogryphs raise their broods. The local flocks are notoriously aggressive toward intruders, fiercely defending the scattered nests tucked among the rock shelves. Because these beasts are so well adapted to the rugged cliffs, their nesting grounds have drawn significant interest from outsiders—most notably goblin entrepreneurs in distant Gadgetzan who seek unhatched eggs for study and profit.

Freewind Post. Freewind Post is the primary Horde outpost in Thousand Needles, perched high atop one of the canyon's dramatic stone mesas. Accessible primarily by tauren lift and winding rope bridges, it serves as a defensive refuge against centaur warbands and a vital frontier staging ground. Built directly upon the canyon mesas, Freewind Post relies on ingenuity and height to safeguard its people. The Galak centaur dominate the arid canyon floor below, but they cannot effectively scale the towering cliffs or breach the heavy wooden elevators that haul Horde travelers up into the sky. A labyrinth of rope and plank bridges connects Freewind to neighboring spires, forming a secure aerie. Beyond keeping centaur raiding parties at bay, the outpost also helps manage the screeching harpies nesting along the bluffs and tends to the nearby wyvern grounds at Highperch, where wild eggs are culled and trained as loyal wind rider mounts for the Horde.

Frostfire Hot Springs. Frostfire Hot Springs are a curious series of steaming pools nestled amidst the western snowdrifts of Winterspring. Despite the bitter sub-zero temperatures all around them, these waters bubble constantly, attracting curious scholars, hardy fishers, and hostile furbolgs alike. Situated near the tunnel leading to Timbermaw Hold, Frostfire Hot Springs represent one of the strangest natural anomalies in northern Kalimdor. The pools remain hot amid the surrounding snow, although the source of their heat is uncertain. The local Winterfall furbolgs maintain a presence near the water, though their aggressive territorial nature makes approaching the warm banks hazardous for unwary travelers. For those able to navigate the hostile wildlife and winter chill, the unfrozen waters provide a rare haven for fish.

Frostmane Hold. Frostmane Hold is a fortified encampment and cavern complex claimed by the Frostmane ice trolls in western Dun Morogh. Tucked into the crags south of Gnomeregan, it serves as a central staging ground for troll raiders encroaching on dwarven territory. The Ironforge Guard keeps a close watch on the hold to gauge the growing troll threat. Carved into the freezing cliffs of western Dun Morogh, Frostmane Hold consists of rough outdoor structures and a winding cave system. For the Frostmane tribe, it functions as a primary stronghold, densely guarded by hideskinners and headhunters. From here, the trolls launch raids into the surrounding valleys, testing the defenses of nearby settlements like Kharanos and menacing travelers along the mountain passes.

Frostmane Hovel. Frostmane Hovel is a rugged cave den tucked into the southern crags of Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh. It serves as an entrenched shelter for aggressive Frostmane trolls pressing directly into dwarven training grounds. Carved into the southern mountains flanking Coldridge Valley, the Frostmane Hovel shelters indigenous Frostmane trolls who refuse to yield the high snows to Ironforge. Operating out of crude caverns like this, the trolls mount continuous raids against local dwarven camps and disrupt supply lines into the valley.

Frostsaber Rock. Frostsaber Rock is a towering stone promontory rising above the snowy northern reaches of Winterspring. It serves as the primary sanctuary and training grounds for the noble frostsaber cats of the region. Rising high above the frozen wastes of northern Winterspring, Frostsaber Rock commands a sweeping view of the snowbound wild. The crag is named for the fierce, majestic frostsaber predators that prowl the slopes and valleys below. At its highest apex resides Rivern Frostwind, a solitary night elf dedicated to raising and tending these beasts. For champions loyal to the Alliance willing to brave the harsh conditions and prove their devotion, Rivern offers the rare privilege of learning to raise, tame, and ride one of these legendary snowy mounts.

Frostwhisper Gorge. Frostwhisper Gorge is a frigid canyon carved into the southern highlands of Winterspring, lying directly north of the sinister Darkwhisper Gorge. Ancient night elven ruins litter its icy floor and surrounding cliffs, while towering Frostmaul giants dominate the chasm. High above the eastern rim, a solitary dwarf camp looks out over the precipice toward the ocean below. Carved into the southern mountains of Winterspring, Frostwhisper Gorge serves as a threshold just before the demon-infested depths of Darkwhisper Gorge. Its snowy floor and cliffside ridges are strewn with the forgotten stonework of ancient night elven settlements. In the present day, the gorge is claimed by immense Frostmaul giants and their preservers. Travel down into the ravine is perilous, as the giants fiercely defend the frozen crags against any wandering intruders.

Fungal Rock. Fungal Rock is a damp, cavernous hollow carved into the northeastern cliff walls of Un'Goro Crater. Dominated by aggressive primates and thick growths of Ghost Mushrooms, it is one of the crater's most dangerous ape dens. Tucked behind a small waterfall and pool along Un'Goro Crater's northeastern edge, Fungal Rock serves as the primary den for the region's massive gorillas. Inside the damp, subterranean corridors, towering Un'Goro Stompers and Thunderers patrol among clusters of rare Ghost Mushrooms. The deepest recesses house territorial behemoths, including the mighty silverback U'cha and the elusive albino gorilla Uhk'loc. Beyond its primal inhabitants, curious travelers may stumble upon artificial oddities near the cave mouth, such as A-Me 01, a damaged mechanical ape abandoned by gnome researchers.

Fungal Vale. The Fungal Vale is a deeply blighted depression located in the south-central Eastern Plaguelands, just north of the Crown Guard Tower and Marris Stead. Choked in a murky haze and blanketed with dark purple earth, the valley showcases the raw, mutating power of the Plague of Undeath. It swarms with roaming Scourge horrors and mortal acolytes serving the Cult of the Damned. Situated north of Marris Stead, the Fungal Vale represents one of the most thoroughly corrupted pockets in Lordaeron. The ground here has turned a sickly purple, swollen with alien fungal growths and drowning under a perpetual, murky haze produced by necrotic spores. Rather than simply killing the ecosystem, the Plague of Undeath has warped the soil to cultivate unholy flora, feeding monstrous carrion beasts and shambling undead. Cult of the Damned members frequent the area, tending to the blighted blooms and conducting foul rites amidst the unnatural decay.

Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm. Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm is an overrun homestead in northern Westfall, just off the main road from Elwynn Forest. Once a prosperous plot tended by Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna, the fields and farmhouse have been seized by the Defias Brotherhood and prowling harvest golems. Situated near the northern border of Westfall, Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm was once known for producing robust crops to feed the kingdom. That ended when the Defias Brotherhood swept across the countryside. Outlaws drove Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna from their land, leaving their fields overrun with mechanical harvest golems programmed to attack anyone approaching. With the farm buildings occupied by bandits and the fields prowled by renegade machinery, the rightful owners have been forced to camp along the roadside near the Jansen Stead, mourning the loss of their home and livelihood.

Gadgetzan. Gadgetzan is the walled desert hub of the Steamwheedle Cartel, standing as an island of commerce in northern Tanaris. Open to both Horde and Alliance travelers, the town operates under strictly enforced goblin neutrality, welcoming anyone with coin to spend or odd jobs to undertake. Surrounded by scorching sands, Gadgetzan serves as the regional heart for the Steamwheedle Cartel's ventures in southern Kalimdor. Built with characteristic goblin ingenuity and haphazard architecture, the town boasts an independent auction house, bank, inn, and specialized crafting facilities for engineers, blacksmiths, and alchemists. It also houses flight masters catering to both major factions, ensuring steady traffic of adventurers heading toward Tanaris, Feralas, and the untamed basin of Un'Goro. Above all, commerce rules supreme: as long as visitors keep their weapons sheathed and their purses open, they are safe within its gates.

Gahrron's Withering. Gahrron's Withering is a corrupted farmstead nestled along the eastern border of the Western Plaguelands near the path to the Eastern Plaguelands. Once a thriving piece of Lordaeron farmland, it is now occupied by the Scourge and anchored by a massive cauldron pumping virulent plague vapors into the air. Before the Third War ruined the kingdom of Lordaeron, this estate was a working farm. Its fertile fields yielded grain for the realm until the Cult of the Damned and the Scourge swept across the land. Now called Gahrron's Withering, the homestead stands broken and derelict. Haunting visions, wailing wraiths, and restless spirits wander the ruined outbuildings, overseen by Scourge overseers sworn to the Lich King.

Galardell Valley. Galardell Valley is a rugged, dangerous canyon nestled in the northeastern heights of the Redridge Mountains. The gorge is overrun by aggressive gnoll packs and sits beneath the shadow of the infamous Tower of Ilgalar. Carved into the northeastern cliffs of Redridge, Galardell Valley has fallen completely out of the control of Lakeshire's defenders.
