Fierce Redridge gnolls prowl the lowlands and camp along the canyon floor, organized under brutal pack leaders such as Lieutenant Fangore. Towering high above the ravines stands the dark spire of the Tower of Ilgalar, the stronghold of the renegade mage Morganth, making the entire valley a persistent source of dread for the surrounding settlements.

Gallery of Treasures. The Gallery of Treasures is an ornate, heavily guarded corridor inside the Scarlet Monastery's halls, connecting the Huntsman's Cloister to the Athenaeum. Lined with recovered paintings, relics, and illuminated texts, it showcases the wealth and Lordaeron heritage preserved by the Scarlet Crusade amidst their zealous war against the undead. Situated deep within the Library wing of the Scarlet Monastery, the Gallery of Treasures serves as a grand hall connecting the kennels of the Huntsman's Cloister to the sacred archives of the Athenaeum. Unlike the hound pens of the cloister, this corridor is lined with fine paintings, historical artifacts, and small chambers filled with books salvaged from across the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron. To the Scarlet Crusade, these relics represent the untainted legacy of humanity they have sworn to protect, fiercely guarded against all outsiders who dare intrude upon their sanctuary.

Gallows' End Tavern. Gallows' End Tavern is the principal inn of Brill and the heart of Forsaken hospitality in Tirisfal Glades. Beyond offering shelter and spirits to weary travelers, it serves as an essential hub for class mentors, trade instructors, and covert interrogations. Standing prominently along the road in Brill, Gallows' End Tavern serves as the primary gathering place for newly awakened Forsaken leaving Deathknell and journeying south toward the Undercity. Despite their undead condition, Forsaken still frequent its halls for fellowship, trade, and refuge. The inn houses various class instructors—guiding young warriors, priests, mages, rogues, and warlocks—as well as vendors and medical practitioners.

Gaping Chasm. The Gaping Chasm is a sprawling silithid hive carved deep into the sands of southeastern Tanaris. Infested by aggressive insectoid horrors of the Hazzali brood, it serves as a grim warning of the growing silithid menace spreading beyond the western deserts. Breaking the rolling expanses of Tanaris, the Gaping Chasm plunges down into a teeming subterranean warren of tunnels, resinous mounds, and twitching carapaces. This hive belongs to the Hazzali, an aggressive brood of silithid that have burrowed beneath the desert wastes. Between subterranean stingers, swarmers, and hulking sandreavers, any travelers or treasure-hunters foolish enough to descend into the chasm quickly find themselves hunted as prey or preserved in sticky cocoons.

Garren's Haunt. Garren's Haunt is an abandoned farmstead nestled in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a prosperous human homestead, the farm fell to ruin when the Scourge wiped out the Garren family, leaving the overgrown grounds overrun by feral Rot Hide gnolls. Before the Third War, this farmstead supported a family and produced bountiful harvests under the Kingdom of Lordaeron. When the Plague of Undeath swept across the countryside, the Scourge descended upon the farm and slaughtered Garren and his kin. Today, the fields lie gray and withered, the farmhouse and barn decaying under the perpetual gloom of Tirisfal.

Garrison Armory. The Garrison Armory is an Alliance mining operation carved into the hills southwest of Nethergarde Keep in the Blasted Lands. Miners and engineers work the underground veins to harvest valuable minerals, sustaining the lonely fortress and shipping raw wealth back to Stormwind. It forms a crucial industrial lifeline in an otherwise blasted, barren wilderness. Maintaining a permanent military garrison in the arid wastes of the Blasted Lands requires constant supply, and Nethergarde Keep cannot rely purely on long supply trains from Stormwind. The Garrison Armory serves as the keep's primary industrial excavation. Nethergarde miners, overseen by foremen and assisted by engineers, work these subterranean shafts to pull valuable minerals from the earth. The ore extracted here is utilized directly by Nethergarde's smiths and fortifications or hauled back to the capital in exchange for the foodstuffs, tools, and provisions the fortress needs to maintain its vigil over the Dark Portal.

Gates of Ironforge. The Gates of Ironforge serve as the monumental main entrance leading travelers from the snowy mountain vales of Dun Morogh into the dwarven capital. Carved directly into the sheer stone face of the mountain, they are guarded inside by a colossal statue of High King Modimus Anvilmar. Approached by climbing the winding, fortified ramp ascending from central Dun Morogh, the Gates of Ironforge present an imposing facade visible across much of the snowy lowlands. Beyond the massive portal, visitors enter the city proper, greeted immediately by an enormous stone statue honoring High King Modimus Anvilmar—the legendary ruler who united the dwarven clans before the War of the Three Hammers. Passing through these gates leads directly into the bustling commercial district of the Commons.

Gates of Orgrimmar. The Gates of Orgrimmar form the imposing southern threshold of the Horde capital, carved directly into the red rock of northern Durotar. Flanked by heavy timber and iron battlements, this grand entryway connects the arid wastes outside to the busy commons of the Valley of Strength. It stands as a physical declaration of orcish endurance and martial strength. Framed by towering wooden palisades, massive iron spikes, and fortified watchtowers, the main gate guards the primary chasm cutting into the mountains sheltering Orgrimmar. For travelers approaching from Razor Hill and the scrublands of Durotar, the entrance serves as both a welcoming monument and a stark deterrent to any who would threaten the new Horde. Heavily armed Orgrimmar Grunts patrol the approach, keeping vigilant watch over all traffic entering the city.

Gelkis Village. Gelkis Village is the primary stronghold of the earth-aligned Gelkis centaur clan in southwestern Desolace. Built around a rugged ravine connected by wooden spans and cliffside paths, the settlement guards the southern route toward Feralas. Its vantage directly overlooks the main north-south road, making it a perilous crossing for any traveler who has not earned the clan's favor. Gelkis Village sits in a deep, craggy gorge framed by precarious bluffs and rope bridges. Unlike the nomadic raiders of the Barrens, the Gelkis have fortified their ancestral grounds into a permanent settlement, complete with outposts spreading toward the border of Feralas. The heart of the clan's leadership lies within Bolgan's Hole, a cavern carved into the southern cliff face where Khan Shaka oversees his warriors. Travelers trekking south through Desolace must either cut a bloody path through the gorge or tread carefully, as the Gelkis view uninvited wanderers as fair game in their eternal war against their rival centaur brethren.

Ghost Walker Post. Ghost Walker Post is a modest tauren settlement situated in the heart of Desolace right beside the ancient Kodo Graveyard. Far more exposed to regional dangers than Shadowprey Village on the western coast, it serves as a frontline Horde staging ground against centaur clans and the Burning Blade. Perched on the dusty flats of central Desolace, Ghost Walker Post provides the Horde with an austere foothold in a hostile territory. Unlike the sheltered coastal fishing haven of Shadowprey Village, this post directly faces roaming centaur marauders and demon-worshiping cultists of the Burning Blade. Facilities are spartan, offering only the bare essentials for travelers, with no inn or flight master in sight. Despite the harsh conditions, a garrison of tauren and an orcish detachment sent by Warchief Thrall keep vigilant watch over the badlands.

Gnomeregan. Gnomeregan was the magnificent subterranean capital of the gnomish race, renowned across Azeroth for its mechanical brilliance and technological marvels. Today, it stands as a radioactive tomb, overrun by subterranean troggs, haywire defense automatons, and deranged leper gnomes after a desperate defense ended in catastrophe. Carved into the snowy crags of western Dun Morogh, Gnomeregan was built with the aid of the Ironforge dwarves centuries ago. Inside, massive steam-driven gears, intricate copper piping, and cavernous assembly halls formed the intellectual and industrial beating heart of gnomekind. It was from these subterranean halls that gnomish designs, flying machines, and complex armaments supplied the Alliance throughout the Second War, standing firm even when besieged by Orgrim Doomhammer's Horde.

Go'Shek Farm. Go'Shek Farm is an agricultural outpost in the eastern Arathi Highlands, occupied by the Horde and guarded by orcs from Hammerfall. Behind its mundane rural facade, Forsaken apothecaries conduct secretive alchemical experiments far from prying eyes. Go'Shek Farm is held by the Horde. Positioned south of Hammerfall and just north of the hostile Witherbark troll territory, the farmstead nominally serves as a vital supply and staging hub for the orcish settlement. Hammerfall Grunts patrol the fields and stables, securing food and livestock to sustain the Horde's embattled foothold in the Arathi Highlands.

Goblin Foundry. The Goblin Foundry is an industrial workshop deep within the Deadmines where goblin tinkerers manufacture heavy metalwork for the Defias Brotherhood. A massive smelting cauldron dominates the chamber, which remains occupied by goblin craftsmen and engineers under Gilnid. Carved into the subterranean depths of Moonbrook, the Goblin Foundry provides the Defias Brotherhood with heavy manufacturing power. Goblin craftsmen and engineers work among the smelters and iron ramps, producing anchors and cannonballs.

Gol'Bolar Quarry. Gol'Bolar Quarry is a dwarven excavation site carved into the snowy hills of southeastern Dun Morogh. Rich in stone and ore, the bustling mining operation has ground to a halt after being overrun by vicious troggs surging from the depths. Situated southeast of Kharanos, Gol'Bolar Quarry was established by Ironforge dwarves to extract vital stone and mineral wealth from the mountains. However, deep excavation work uncovered underground warrens, unleashing a horde of hostile troggs that quickly drove out the miners. Today, the upper camp serves as an embattled staging ground where overseers, tradesfolk, and Prospector Gehn rally dwarven and gnomish recruits to drive the beasts back and reclaim the pit.

Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine. Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine is an overrun excavation pit deep within the heart of Gol'Bolar Quarry in eastern Dun Morogh. Originally worked by dwarven miners, the tunnels breached subterranean trogg caverns, unleashing a violent infestation that claimed the entire site. Today, the deepest shafts serve as the stronghold for the trogg warband led by the brute Hammerspine. The mine was established by Ironforge dwarves seeking stone and rich ore deposits beneath the craggy peaks of Dun Morogh. Work came to an abrupt, violent halt when pickaxes fractured a wall into an ancient subterranean cavern system inhabited by troggs. Swarming out from the dark, the subterranean beasts overwhelmed the work crews and forced a hasty retreat, ultimately spilling outward to overrun the surrounding quarry pit as well.

Golakka Hot Springs. Golakka Hot Springs is a geothermal basin in western Un'Goro Crater, nestled just north of Terror Run. Its bubbling pools and erupting geysers are fueled by the intense volcanic activity of nearby Fire Plume Ridge. The mineral-rich waters attract eccentric researchers, alchemists in search of exotic reagents, and wandering water elementals known as Steaming Furies. Situated in the western reaches of Un'Goro Crater, the Golakka Hot Springs are a direct product of the subterranean heat radiating from Fire Plume Ridge. Scalding water bubbles continuously to the surface, shaping tiered mineral terraces and violently erupting geysers. The environment is heavily prowled by Steaming Furies, elemental manifestations born from the convergence of subterranean groundwater and volcanic heat. Despite the danger, the springs frequently draw explorers, herbalists, and researchers fascinated by the crater's unique geology.

Gold Coast Quarry. The Gold Coast Quarry is an open-pit mine carved into the bluffs of southwestern Westfall. Once a prized source of stone, minerals, and gold for the Kingdom of Stormwind, it has been seized by the Defias Brotherhood to fuel their growing insurrection. Before the kingdom fell into neglect, the Gold Coast Quarry supplied raw building materials and precious gold to help rebuild Stormwind. When royal troops withdrew from Westfall and left the countryside unprotected, Defias highwaymen and renegade laborers took control of the diggings. The Brotherhood now patrols the terraced stone ramps, using the site's vantage over the coast and plundering whatever minerals remain to fund their rebellion.

Gold Road. The Gold Road is the primary north-south artery cutting through the arid expanse of the Barrens. Stretching from the Mor'shan Rampart on the border of Ashenvale down past the Crossroads toward the southern reaches, it serves as the vital transit line for the young Horde. The Gold Road is a long, sun-baked dirt highway that carves its way through the center of the Barrens. To the north, it begins near the fortified Mor'shan Rampart and Mor'shan Base Camp, which guard against night elf incursions from Ashenvale. Traveling south, it connects with the eastern roadway leading to Durotar before intersecting the bustling trading settlement of the Crossroads. Continuing southward past the lush waters of the local oases and the foothills near the Wailing Caverns, the northern span of the highway reaches a dried-up riverbed, where travelers cross into the more hazardous southern portion of the savanna.

Golden Plains. The Golden Plains form a vast, sun-drenched basin stretching southeast of Thunder Bluff in central Mulgore. Cherished by the tauren, these sweeping grasslands serve as prime hunting territory and a vital grazing habitat for wandering herds of kodo. Spreading out beneath the towering mesas of Thunder Bluff, the Golden Plains represent the untamed heart of Mulgore. The shifting sea of golden and green grass offers an abundant sanctuary for local wildlife, making it one of the most treasured traditional hunting grounds of the nomadic tauren. Broad kodo herds roam across the rolling basin, while hunters share stories of legendary quarry, most notably the great kodo Arra'chea, who wanders quietly through the tall stalks.

Goldshire. Goldshire is a vital human crossroads town nestled in central Elwynn Forest, connecting Stormwind City with Westfall, Redridge, and the southern frontier. Rebuilt after its destruction in the First War, it serves as a bustling waystation anchored by the famous Lion's Pride Inn and defended by a hard-pressed contingent of the Stormwind Guard. Positioned where the king's highways meet, Goldshire has long been the civic and commercial heart of rural Elwynn. However, the town's bucolic charm masks escalating peril in Year 25 ADP. With Stormwind's military resources stretched thin and King Varian Wrynn mysteriously absent, Marshal Dughan must rely on passing adventurers rather than regular troops to contain surrounding threats. Aggressive Riverpaw gnolls push inward from the western border, while vicious murlocs claim the shores of Stone Cairn Lake and Crystal Lake, claiming the lives of royal guards and encroaching dangerously close to the town center.

Gordok Commons. The Gordok Commons comprise the fortified northern quarter of the ancient Highborne ruins of Dire Maul. Under the rule of King Gordok, this sprawling stone complex serves as the seat of power for the elite warrior caste of the Gordunni ogres. Occupying what was once an aristocratic wing of Eldre'Thalas, the Gordok Commons have been thoroughly desecrated and refitted for ogre tastes. Grand night elven pillars and arched passageways now house armories, crude barricades, and training grounds for the Gordok—the fiercest, most disciplined fighters among the Gordunni clan. At the deepest end of the wing lies Gordok's Seat, where King Gordok presides over his brutes through sheer force and intimidation.

Gordunni Outpost. Tucked into the rugged cliffs north of Lariss Pavilion, the Gordunni Outpost serves as a fortified camp for the brutish Gordunni ogres of Feralas. The clan's corrupting influence has choked the once-vibrant wilderness here, leaving the surrounding earth dry, withered, and brown. Carved into the northern mountains above the Lariss Pavilion, the Gordunni Outpost stands out as a stark scar against the lush canopy of Feralas. Wherever the Gordunni ogres settle, their reckless magical channeling and destructive habits sap the vitality of the wild, leaving the local flora dead and the hillsides barren. The outpost consists of dirt trails, a shallow entrance cave, and a larger ogre mound burrowed deep into the rear cliffs. Patrolled by heavily armed hillguards, cunning channelers, and ogre tamers, the camp also holds dangerous trophies—including a captured sasquatch named Bigfist kept in crude confinement near the deeper den.

Grand Vestibule. The Grand Vestibule is the monumental entrance hall of the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades. Lined with crimson pillars and stone effigies of fallen crusaders, it serves as the threshold where adventurers prepare to breach the monastery's inner halls. Past the heavy outer gates of the Monastery lies the Grand Vestibule, an expansive marble hall dedicated to the martial pride of the Scarlet Crusade. Statues of armored champions stand vigil beside vaulted stone pillars, and zealous sentries, disciples, and augurs patrol the flagstones to strike down anyone daring to enter without the order's crimson tabard. For trespassers, it is the first taste of the Crusade's unrelenting discipline and fanaticism.

Great Forge. The Great Forge is the fiery heart and namesake of the dwarven capital of Ironforge. Situated at the very center of the city, its massive furnaces and famed Great Anvil never rest, producing legendary armaments and serving as the bustling center of civic life. The Great Forge was the very first structure built by the early dwarves beneath Ironforge Mountain, and the grand capital grew in concentric rings around it. Molten stone and slag pour constantly from giant foundries into glowing channels, illuminating the cavern with an amber haze. At its center stands the massive Great Anvil, overseen by Master of the Forge Myolor Sunderfury. Renowned masters of metalwork gather around its rim, hammering out armor, tools, and weapons day and night.

Great Lift. The Great Lift is a massive, tauren-engineered elevator system perched on the southern edge of the Barrens. It serves as the primary route lowering travelers and supplies hundreds of feet into the sheer canyon basin of Thousand Needles. Despite its strategic value, aggressive quilboar encroaching through the southern wastes have made approaching the rim increasingly perilous. Spanning the sheer cliff edge between the southern Barrens and the canyon floor of Thousand Needles, the Great Lift stands as a marvel of practical tauren construction. Built using heavy timber, braided rope, and counterweighted pulleys, its paired platforms carry caravans, couriers, and warriors safely across a vertical precipice that would otherwise break any wagon. At the top and bottom platforms, tauren like Brave Moonhorn and Grish Longrunner maintain watch, keeping travelers informed of the road ahead and ensuring cargo passes smoothly.

Greatwood Vale. Greatwood Vale is a forested valley nestled in the eastern foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains, reached via the perilous Webwinder Path. Recently, the hostile Grimtotem tribe seized the vale, using it as a staging ground for bloody assaults on neighboring settlements. Tucked away off the Webwinder Path, Greatwood Vale has become a violent frontier. The Grimtotem tribe, under the ruthless leadership of Grundig Darkcloud, has moved into the vale in force, cutting off safe passage and bringing terror to the surrounding foothills.

Green Belt. The Green Belt is a wild stretch of marshland in the eastern Wetlands, sprawling below the ridges of Grim Batol. It is overrun by roaming bog beasts, predatory crocolisks, and toxic oozes, guarded primarily by the solitary night elf Rethiel the Greenwarden. Stretching across the eastern interior of the Wetlands, the Green Belt is one of the sodden region's untamed hollows. The local wildlife—ranging from massive crocolisks to shifting oozes and shambling bog beasts—makes travel through the mossy waters hazardous. Deep within its reaches sits a solitary watch post manned by Rethiel the Greenwarden, a lone night elf dedicated to studying the fen's ecology and keeping its hostile denizens in check.

Greenpaw Village. Greenpaw Village is a furbolg settlement nestled in central Ashenvale, situated between Raynewood Retreat and Silverwind Refuge. It serves as the primary home of the Foulweald tribe, led by Chief Murgut and the shaman Oakpaw. Gripped by demonic corruption and embattled by outside forces, the village is an active conflict point for both Alliance and Horde travelers. Situated south of Raynewood Retreat and northeast of Silverwind Refuge, Greenpaw Village was once a quiet home for the forest's ursine denizens. In the wake of the Third War, its resident furbolgs—the Foulweald tribe—succumbed to the insidious corruption tainting Ashenvale's soil and spirits. Under the dominion of Chief Murgut and their corrupted spiritual guide, Shaman Oakpaw, the Foulweald have become hostile and unstable, attacking any travelers who stray into their forest territory.

Greymane Wall. The Greymane Wall is a massive stone bulwark spanning the southern frontier of Silverpine Forest. Built by King Genn Greymane after the Second War, it seals the kingdom of Gilneas away from the outside world behind impenetrable, locked gates. Following the Second War, King Genn Greymane grew resentful of the Alliance of Lordaeron, particularly the taxes required to maintain the orc internment camps. Deciding Gilneas had given enough of its coin and blood for foreign troubles, Greymane withdrew from the Alliance and ordered a colossal barrier raised across the head of the peninsula. When the Third War brought the Plague of Undeath and countless desperate refugees to its foot, the gates remained pitilessly barred.

Grim Batol. Grim Batol is an ancient, ruined dwarven mountain fortress looming over the eastern edge of the Wetlands. Built by the Wildhammer clan, abandoned after a dark curse during the War of the Three Hammers, and later occupied by the Dragonmaw orcs as a dragon breeding lair, its sealed gates remain an ominous blight upon the highlands. Following the ancient civil war of the three clans, Thane Khardros Wildhammer carved Grim Batol out of the jagged mountains east of the marsh. During the subsequent War of the Three Hammers, the Dark Iron sorceress Modgud laid siege to the fortress. Although Khardros struck her down, Modgud cast a foul shadow across the stones before her death. The lingering taint rendered the halls uninhabitable, forcing the surviving Wildhammer dwarves to abandon their magnificent kingdom and migrate north into the Hinterlands.

Grimesilt Dig Site. Grimesilt Dig Site is an archaeological excavation in the Searing Gorge originally broken ground by Ironforge dwarves. Overrun by hostile Dark Iron dwarves, the pit is now firmly under enemy control while surviving members of the original expedition struggle to endure in hiding. Situated within the soot-choked badlands of the Searing Gorge, the Grimesilt Dig Site began as an expedition sanctioned by Ironforge scholars seeking relics beneath the crags. That venture met a violent end when the native Dark Iron dwarves drove out the excavators and claimed the equipment for themselves. Today, the trench swarms with Dark Iron sentries, leaving the wounded and scattered survivors of the original Ironforge crew trapped in and around the pit.

Grimtotem Compound. The Grimtotem Compound is a fortified tribal settlement nestled in the central wilds of Feralas, just east of the elven ruins of Dire Maul. Occupied by the aggressive and insular Grimtotem clan, the encampment serves as a base for their mysterious and destructive operations in the region. Spanning two encampments east of Dire Maul, the Grimtotem Compound establishes a firm foothold for the Grimtotem clan in Feralas. Unlike the tauren aligned with Cairne Bloodhoof in Thunder Bluff, the Grimtotem here operate independently and with hostility toward outsiders. In the southern half of the settlement, they keep captive sprite darters locked inside a large wooden cage for reasons of their own, while rogue gnolls stalk the fringes of their northern perimeter.

Grizzled Den. The Grizzled Den is a cavern nestled in the snowy hills just southwest of Kharanos. It serves as a notorious lair for the ferocious, frost-breathing wendigos indigenous to Dun Morogh. Carved deep into the crags southwest of Kharanos, the Grizzled Den is notorious among local mountaineers as the nesting ground of Dun Morogh's wendigo packs. These aggressive, ape-like beasts wield frosty breath against intruders and band together to protect their hollows. Despite the peril, daring hunters regularly brave the cavern's depths to harvest thick wendigo manes, which fetch a respectable sum among craftsmen looking to line cold chairs and carriage seats with insulated fur.

Grizzlepaw Ridge. Grizzlepaw Ridge is a rugged, craggy hillside rising south of Thelsamar in Loch Modan. It is notorious among local mountaineers for its dense population of wild bears, led by the legendary beast Ol' Sooty. Overlooking the road south of Thelsamar and bordering Stonesplinter Valley to the west, Grizzlepaw Ridge is rough country dominated by predatory wildlife. The slopes are claimed by territorial bears that pose a hazard to travelers skirting the mountains. Deep within the ridge dwells Ol' Sooty, a massive and unusually fierce bear feared by local hunters. Travelers moving between the dwarven settlements must keep a wary eye on the tree line and rocky terraces above.

Grol'dom Farm. Grol'dom Farm is a modest orcish homestead situated in the northern Barrens along the road between Durotar and the Crossroads. Inhabited by Kranal Fiss and his family, the farm raises swine in the arid plains despite constant harassment from aggressive local quilboars. Established following the settlement of Durotar, Grol'dom Farm represents the Horde's early efforts to farm the dry expanse of the Barrens. Tended by the orc Kranal Fiss and his children, the small homestead primarily raises pigs while braving the harsh wildlife and aggressive Razormane quilboar raiders that prowl the nearby ridges. It is a lonely, rugged outpost that supplies vital sustenance to the emerging orcish nation.

Grom'gol Base Camp. Grom'gol Base Camp is the Horde's primary fortified outpost in Stranglethorn Vale, situated along the western coast of northern Stranglethorn. Commanded by Commander Aggro'gosh, the settlement secures a critical foothold and supply chain in the southern Eastern Kingdoms. With direct zeppelin towers linking to Orgrimmar and the Undercity, it stands as an armed staging ground against local jungle troll tribes and hostile Alliance forces. Carved into the dense jungle of northwestern Stranglethorn Vale, Grom'gol Base Camp is a fortified military bastion commanded by Commander Aggro'gosh. Ringed by defensive palisades and heavily armed grunts, the base camp endures non-stop harassment from Bloodscalp headhunters, lurking naga, and prowling beasts. Despite these threats, its vital strategic location secures safe supply routes north toward Stonard in the Swamp of Sorrows while keeping a watchful eye on Alliance traffic descending from Duskwood or traveling up from Booty Bay.

Grommash Hold. Grommash Hold is the fortified seat of Warchief Thrall, nestled high in the red cliffs of the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar. Named in honor of Grommash Hellscream's sacrifice, the fortress serves as the command center and political heart of the new Horde. Perched within the tranquil Valley of Wisdom, Grommash Hold serves as the royal court and strategic sanctum of the Horde. Built into the towering canyon walls, its thick stone interior remains notably dim and chilly—a deliberate choice by Warchief Thrall to keep emissaries, petitioners, and warlords sharp and sober during audiences. Here, Thrall deliberates on the defense of Kalimdor, guided by veteran counselors like Eitrigg and visited by racial chieftains such as Vol'jin.

Grove of the Ancients. The Grove of the Ancients is a sacred night elven sanctuary set amidst old temple ruins in southeastern Darkshore. Nestled beside the Wildbend River, this serene haven serves as a gathering ground for nature spirits and is watched over by the venerable Ancient of Lore, Onu. Tucked away near the southeastern mountains of Darkshore, the Grove of the Ancients stands as a peaceful haven surrounded by aged temple stones. Through its heart flows the surging Wildbend River, providing a quiet refuge amidst a coastline increasingly plagued by corruption and restless wildlife. The grove serves as a meeting place for the Circle of Ancients, where nature spirits and kaldorei tend to the delicate balance of the forest.

Growless Cave. Growless Cave is a frigid cavern carved into the crags of the Alterac Mountains, overrun by ferocious mountain yetis. It is best known as the resting place of the Flame of Uzel, an unholy ceremonial pyre tied to the dark necromancy of Helcular. Tucked away in the snow-dusted heights overlooking the foothills, Growless Cave serves primarily as a den for the territorial mountain yetis that roam Alterac. Travelers navigating the treacherous slopes often steer clear of its mouth, especially when the notorious yeti Skhowl is sighted prowling outside. Beyond the primal danger of the beasts, the cave harbors a sinister past: inside lies the Flame of Uzel, an arcane brazier left behind by the ambitious human mage Helcular. Before his demise, Helcular intended to use the pyre in a dark ritual to achieve lichdom, and its foul warmth once drew the massive predator Frostmaw out from the frozen wastes.

Gryphon Roost. Perched along the ramparts just east of Stormwind's Trade District, the Gryphon Roost serves as the capital's primary transit hub for aerial travel. Managed by the human gryphon master Dungar Longdrink, it houses the majestic beasts that ferry couriers, soldiers, and adventurers across the Eastern Kingdoms. Situated atop the fortifications overlooking the Trade District canal, the Gryphon Roost connects the capital with outlying Alliance garrisons and settlements throughout the Eastern Kingdoms. The flight network is orchestrated by the seasoned master Dungar Longdrink, who coordinates routes to Ironforge, Lakeshire, Sentinel Hill, and beyond.

Gunther's Retreat. Gunther's Retreat is an isolated island sanctuary set in Brightwater Lake in central Tirisfal Glades. It serves as the refuge of Gunther Arcanus, a renegade necromancer who broke free from the Scourge through raw willpower. Distrustful of all outsiders, the recluse surrounds his campsite with loyal undead minions to keep intruders away. Situated amid the misty waters of Brightwater Lake, Gunther's Retreat is an unassuming island encampment easily mistaken for another pocket of the Scourge. Its master, Gunther Arcanus, achieved what few mortal sorcerers could: when raised in undeath, his arcane mastery allowed him to tear away his soul from the Lich King's iron grip without any outside help. Mistrusting everyone, Gunther assumed the rest of the undead wandering Lordaeron were still puppets of the Scourge. He retired to this lonely isle to practice his craft in peace, posting zombie sentinels to tear apart anyone who crosses the water.

Gurubashi Arena. Gurubashi Arena is an ancient stone colosseum standing in southern Stranglethorn Vale, originally built by the mighty Gurubashi Empire. In the present day, it serves as a chaotic free-for-all proving ground where pirates and wandering brawlers shed blood over locked chests of treasure. Long before human or orc set foot in Stranglethorn Vale, the Gurubashi Arena—known also as the Great Arena—was built as a monument to martial strength by the sprawling Gurubashi troll empire. In ancient days, champions fought to the death upon its sands until the earth was slick with troll blood.

Haldarr Encampment. The Haldarr Encampment is a corrupted satyr outpost nestled in western Azshara, situated northeast of the Shadowsong Shrine and southwest of Valormok. Densely inhabited by the vicious Haldarr satyrs, it stands as a dangerous blight among the ancient elven ruins. It is also where an injured Night Elf Sentinel, Keldara Sunblade, can be found. Perched among the broken stones of western Azshara, the Haldarr Encampment serves as a gathering ground for the Haldarr clan of satyrs. These twisted creatures, ancient remnants of the Highborne cursed by demonic corruption during the Sundering, actively hunt and harass any who traverse the autumn forests. The dense settlement poses an ongoing threat to both the Horde forces stationed at nearby Valormok and the dwindling Night Elf sentinels trying to monitor the region.

Hall of Arms. The Hall of Arms serves as the headquarters of Ironforge's military might and the chief arsenal of the dwarven kingdom. Located within the Military Ward, this fortified compound trains dwarven combatants and orchestrates the deployment of heavy armor and aerial war machines. Situated in the southeastern corner of the Military Ward, the Hall of Arms is the operational command center for the armed forces of Ironforge. Beyond housing veteran trainers for warriors and hunters, the expansive facility serves as a massive depot and staging ground for mechanized warfare. Heavy steam tanks are assembled and maintained on-site to reinforce Alliance battlefields, while gyrocopters and flying machines are brought up via industrial conveyor belts and launched directly through vertical access shafts in the cavern ceiling toward the Ironforge Airfield above.

Hall of Arms (Northshire). The Hall of Arms is the martial wing of Northshire Abbey, situated south of the Main Hall. Here, veteran instructors drill the newest recruits of the Stormwind Army in the arts of the sword, shield, and holy combat. While the clerics and scholars ponder ancient tomes across the courtyard in the Library Wing, the Hall of Arms rings with the clash of blunted steel and the heavy cadence of martial instruction. Positioned on the south side of Northshire Abbey, this chamber serves as the primary training station for raw human fighters and devout aspirants taking up arms for the Stormwind Army. Here, seasoned battle instructors and paladin mentors teach the basic postures, disciplines, and fundamentals required to defend Elwynn Forest against encroaching kobolds, Defias bandits, and gnoll raiders.

Hall of Arms (Tyr's Hand). The Hall of Arms is a heavily guarded wing within Tyr's Hand Abbey in southeastern Eastern Plaguelands. It serves as a staging ground and barracks for the martial vanguard of the Scarlet Crusade garrisoned at the stronghold. Positioned across the abbey from the library, it houses some of the crusade's most zealous and well-armored fighters. Situated to the south of the abbey's main hall, the Hall of Arms functions as an armory and quarters for the militant forces of Tyr's Hand. While the opposing wing holds archives and holy texts, this wing is dedicated purely to the discipline of war. Clad in heavy armor and sworn to eradicate the undead and anyone deemed impure, the Scarlet defenders stationed here maintain a tireless watch over their eastern bastion, keeping weapons sharpened and shields polished against the surrounding horrors of the Plaguelands.

Hall of Champions. The Hall of Champions is the inner sanctum of the Scarlet Monastery's armory wing. It serves as the seat of Herod, the Scarlet Champion, and a proving ground for the Scarlet Crusade's elite. Situated past the Footman's Armory, the Hall of Champions lies at the heart of the monastery's armory wing. Here Herod, the Scarlet Champion, holds sway over the Crusade's fiercest fighters, and Scarlet trainees harden their resolve to purge Lordaeron of all undead and outsiders.

Hall of Explorers. The Hall of Explorers is the sprawling archaeological wing of Ironforge and the bustling headquarters of the dwarven Explorers' League. Part museum, part archive, and part expedition command, it gathers relics, fossils, and ancient tomes from every corner of Azeroth to piece together the forgotten origins of the dwarven race. Occupying the northeastern cavern of Ironforge, the Hall of Explorers—sometimes referred to as the Assembly of Explorers—serves as the nerve center for all Alliance-sanctioned archaeological endeavors. Under the direction of High Explorer Muninn Magellas, scholars and field agents coordinate digs across distant lands, shipping back mysterious relics, ancient titan machinery, and prehistoric bones. The vast Library at its center functions as both a public museum and a restricted storehouse of historical lore.

Hall of Gears. The Hall of Gears is a multi-tiered industrial chamber situated inside the fallen city of Gnomeregan, just past the Clockwerk Run. Once a bustling center of mechanical movement, it has fallen into ruin, flooded with toxic sludge, roaming oozes, and irradiated troggs. Positioned just beyond the Clockwerk Run, the Hall of Gears illustrates the catastrophic collapse of the gnome capital. Divided into two main levels, the chamber's upper catwalks are held by aggressive, irradiated troggs that claw through collapsed access shafts. Below, the floor sits drenched in pools of radioactive fallout, where corrosive slimes and living poison elementals thrive in the toxic runoff.

Hall of Legends. The Hall of Legends is the elite military sanctuary and officer barracks of the Horde, nestled within Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. Behind its warded threshold, champions of the Horde gather around battle plans and arm themselves with premier weapons taken from conflicts across Azeroth and beyond. Located off the bustling avenues of the Valley of Strength, the Hall of Legends serves as the private redoubt for proven officers of the Horde. Beyond its guarded entrance, strategists and delegates from across the factions—including Chieftain Earthbind of Thunder Bluff, Blood Guard Hini'wana of the Darkspear, and Advisor Willington of the Undercity—confer over maps of contested lands and the military standing of both factions. Here, only warriors who have tested their mettle and achieved the rank of Stone Guard or higher are permitted entry to claim the spoils and armaments befitting their status.

Hall of Masks. The Hall of Masks is an ominous chamber inside the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows. Lined with giant skull masks and marred by a bone-strewn trench, it marks one of the early thresholds deeper into the Atal'ai stronghold. Located just past the staircase descending from the Broken Hall, the Hall of Masks serves as a central junction within the Sunken Temple. The chamber earns its name from the imposing, stylized skull masks mounted along its stone walls. Below them runs a deep trench choked with discarded bones, suggesting a macabre purpose whose exact nature is unknown. Beyond this eerie hall lie passages branching out to the Butchery, the Chamber of Blood, and the Den of the Caller.

Hall of Mysteries. Tucked into the Mystic Ward of Ironforge, the Hall of Mysteries serves as the city's spiritual and scholarly heart for the arcane and the divine. Within its blue-lit interior, dwarven and gnomish practitioners study ancient texts, train in the mysteries of the Holy Light, and weave arcane enchantments far from the clang of the Great Forge. Illuminated by a distinctive blue and purple luminescence, the Hall of Mysteries stands out starkly against the rest of Ironforge. While the city around it thrives on stone, iron, and heavy plate, the hall's five soaring pillars shelter scholars draped in soft, flowing robes. It bridges both arcane wizardry and holy devotion, serving as the headquarters for the dwarven priesthood and the Order of the Silver Hand within Khaz Modan. Here, young clerics and knights study holy texts like the Tome of Divinity and receive guidance before their journeys carry them onward to Stormwind's Cathedral of Light.

Hall of the Brave. The Hall of the Brave is the grand warrior barracks situated in the eastern heights of Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. It serves as the primary training compound and guild house for the Horde's front-line combatants, drillmasters, and battlemasters. Overlooking the tranquil waters and training rings of the Valley of Honor, the Hall of the Brave serves as a vital military hub for the burgeoning Horde. Inside, veteran officers and seasoned warriors instruct initiates in the brutal fundamentals of melee combat, stance mastery, and discipline. The hall is lined with training dummies and armaments, housing battlemasters who organize combatants for major military engagements across Azeroth.

Hammerfall. Hammerfall is the Horde's primary fortified outpost in the Arathi Highlands, built upon the ruins of a notorious Alliance internment camp. It honors the legendary former Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer, who fell nearby while fighting to liberate his captive people. Today, orcs and Forsaken garrison the settlement against hostile Boulderfist ogres, Witherbark trolls, and the League of Arathor. Following the Second War, the human Alliance built vast internment camps across Lordaeron to contain the defeated orcs. The compound that once stood here was among the largest. Years later, Thrall and Orgrim Doomhammer assaulted the camp to liberate the lethargic captives. During the chaos of their retreat, a charging Alliance knight drove a lance through Doomhammer's backplate, mortally wounding the legendary Warchief. Following the Third War, the new Horde reclaimed the ruined ground and established an outpost here, naming it Hammerfall in memory of their fallen leader.

Harborage. The Harborage is a quiet settlement of exiled Draenor natives situated in the northern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. While many of their afflicted kin wandering the surrounding bogs have succumbed to madness and primal hostility, the inhabitants here have managed to hold onto their sanity and wits. They live cautiously along the waterline, seeking peace amidst a harsh and unforgiving wilderness. Tucked away against the northern mountains of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Harborage stands in stark contrast to the feral tribes wandering the nearby waters. Constructed of rugged leather shelters and adorned with mysterious hanging crystals, this small encampment provides sanctuary to exiled Draenor survivors who have refused to surrender their minds. Under the guidance of elders like Magtoor, they maintain a fragile, civilized enclave while remaining watchful of the hostile wilderness, native predators, and the feral tribes of their fallen brothers lurking just beyond their perimeter.

Hearthglen. Tucked away in the northern hills of the Western Plaguelands, Hearthglen is a fortified settlement that remarkably escaped complete physical destruction during the fall of Lordaeron. Today, its sturdy stone walls, towers, and surrounding farmlands serve as the primary northern stronghold and training ground for the fanatical Scarlet Crusade. While neighboring Andorhal lies shattered in skeletal ruin, Hearthglen still resembles a living town of Lordaeron, complete with a lumber mill, scout towers, stables, and a functioning mine. Historically governed from Mardenholde Keep by Lord Tirion Fordring, Hearthglen was renowned for its prosperity and staunch defense during the Second War. When the Plague of Undeath swept Lordaeron during the Third War, Prince Arthas Menethil intercepted tainted grain here, purging the infected townsfolk and repelling a massive Scourge siege alongside Uther the Lightbringer. Through that desperate intervention, Hearthglen's formidable walls survived intact.

Helm's Bed Lake. Helm's Bed Lake is a frozen body of water nestled in the southeastern hills of Dun Morogh. A maintained hole in the thick ice provides crucial fresh water to local mountaineers and travelers. However, the surrounding shoreline has become perilous due to prowling wildlife, encroaching troggs, and hostile Dark Iron infiltrators. Helm's Bed Lake sits quietly beneath a thick sheet of winter ice in southeastern Dun Morogh. Local dwarves keep an opening chopped through the frost to draw clean, fresh water. While crossing the frozen expanse is stable enough, lingering near the banks has become increasingly risky. Wild beasts wander the edges, displaced troggs scavenge along the ridges, and a cell of hostile Dark Iron dwarves has commandeered an abandoned lodge just south of the water, aggressively ambushing any travelers who pass through.

Heroes' Vigil. Heroes' Vigil is a quiet, sacred clearing situated on the central island within Stone Cairn Lake in eastern Elwynn Forest. Centered around a monument known as the Stone of Remembrance, it was dedicated to honor those who fell during the First War. Today, however, the shrine sits largely neglected by Stormwind and is overrun by dangerous renegade wizards. Erected after the First War, Heroes' Vigil centers upon the Stone of Remembrance, an inscribed stone circle meant to honor the soldiers and citizens slaughtered during the Old Horde's sacking of Goldshire and the surrounding valleys. Though once revered as a sacred bastion of faith and sacrifice, the vigil has gradually slipped from the attention of Stormwind's current rulers, leaving its hallowed grounds overgrown and unattended by the realm's soldiers.

Hetaera's Clutch. Hetaera's Clutch is a sunken night elven temple dedicated to Elune, nestled deep beneath the churning waters of Azshara's Bay of Storms. Once a sacred site of devotion, the submerged ruins are now overrun by deadly hydras hatched by their broodmother, Hetaera. Adventurers braving the depths will find ancient stonework claimed by vicious aquatic predators. Before the Great Sundering tore ancient Kalimdor apart, this structure served as a grand temple dedicated to the moon goddess Elune. Cast into the depths of the Bay of Storms, its stone pillars and sacred halls have spent ten thousand years beneath the sea. Today, all signs of holy veneration have been swallowed by the tides, leaving behind a solemn monument to the lost Kaldorei empire.

Hidden Grove. Tucked away behind towering cliffs in northeastern Winterspring, the Hidden Grove is a secluded crater basin. Once an untroubled haven for Arctic hares, the basin has fallen under the domain of fiercely territorial wild moonkin. Walled off from the bitter howling winds of Winterspring, the Hidden Grove forms a sunken, snow-dusted forest crater that is nearly impossible to access from the outside cliffs. Travelers who discover its concealed rim must brave a sheer, dangerous drop or navigate a narrow cavern passage tucked into the southeastern ridge. Though the valley was long the undisturbed home of harmless white hares, aggressive wild moonkin have seized the glade, turning an isolated natural paradise into an ambush for unwary wanderers.

Hidden Path. The Hidden Path is a secluded mountain trail winding through the crags above the Valley of Trials in Durotar. It serves as a rite of passage for aspiring shaman seeking the sacred Spirit Rock, while offering an overlooked vantage overlooking the rugged borders of the Barrens. Carved into the red peaks bordering the Valley of Trials, the Hidden Path is intentionally difficult to spot from the canyon floor. Young shaman are directed here by their mentors to prove their awareness and discipline before communing with the spirits at Spirit Rock. Along the trail's highest reaches, travelers are treated to expansive panoramic views stretching westward toward the rolling savannas of the Barrens.

High Rise. The High Rise is the uppermost tier of Thunder Bluff's central mesa, crowning the tauren capital. It hosts a bustling amphitheater centered around a communal bonfire alongside seasoned artisans, weapon merchants, and culinary masters. Unlike the lower tiers, this summit relies entirely on suspension rope bridges and the wind rider roost for travel. The High Rise perches atop Thunder Bluff's core plateau, catching the open winds high above the rolling plains of Mulgore. A focal gathering point for the united tribes, it centers around an open-air amphitheater and fire pit where citizens listen to important tribal announcements and fateful decisions. The surrounding tents and wooden stalls house renowned merchants, armories, and culinary trainers, including Aska's Kitchen and Mountaintop Bait & Tackle. While the lower tiers connect directly to Mulgore's prairie floor via massive wooden elevators, the High Rise stays aloft, accessible primarily through the wind rider roost and sweeping rope bridges linking to the neighboring Elder Rise and Hunter Rise.

High Seat. The High Seat is the grand throne room of Ironforge, situated between the Commons and the Great Forge. From this elevated chamber, King Magni Bronzebeard presides over the dwarven realm alongside his royal advisors and historians. The room also houses the sealed passageway leading down into the ancient depths of Old Ironforge. Overlooking the vibrant bustling rings of Ironforge, the High Seat serves as the royal seat of power for the kingdom of Khaz Modan. Within this vaulted chamber, King Magni Bronzebeard hears petitioners, holds council with his advisors, and directs the defense of the Alliance's northern bastions. Flanked by royal dignitaries such as Royal Historian Archesonus and Senator Barin Redstone, the High Seat remains a symbol of unyielding Bronzebeard authority and dwarven resilience amid troubling times across Azeroth.

High Wilderness. The High Wilderness is an expansive, untamed stretch of primordial forest covering much of western Feralas. Bordered by the Verdantis River to the east and the Forgotten Coast to the west, it shelters a wide array of wildlife, wandering treants, and dangerous beasts beneath its towering emerald canopy. Stretching across the western half of Feralas, the High Wilderness represents the quintessential untamed wilderness of southern Kalimdor. Thick foliage and colossal trees block out much of the sky, creating a lush expanse teeming with wolves, bears, hippogryphs, and yetis. Ancient treants wander among the roots, while aggressive ogre clans establish footholds in the shaded clearings. Navigating this vast green expanse requires vigilance, as the dense brush hides both natural predators and lingering primeval hazards.

Highperch. Highperch is an elevated plateau in western Thousand Needles, towering high above the canyon floor. It is renowned as a primary nesting ground for wild wyverns and wind riders. The roost is home to fierce prides defending their young among the windswept crags. Rising sharply out of the canyon floor, Highperch is a rugged sanctuary for Kalimdor's native wyverns. The plateau provides natural defense against predators and an unobstructed launch point for their hunting flights across Thousand Needles. Within its reaches, wyvern prides live under the protection of watchful patriarchs and matriarchs, guarding their nests. The beasts fiercely defend their territory against any intruders who manage to climb into their high domain.

Hillsbrad Fields. The Hillsbrad Fields encompass the cultivated farmlands and rustic settlement of Hillsbrad in western Hillsbrad Foothills. As one of the few surviving human communities in former Lordaeron that refused to succumb to the Scourge or join the fanatical Scarlet Crusade, its farmers and militia now face constant assaults from the nearby Forsaken at Tarren Mill. Spanning orchards, pumpkin patches, and pastures between Darrow Hill and the Azurelode Mine, the Hillsbrad Fields supply essential provisions to Southshore and the surviving Alliance resistance. While much of Lordaeron fell to the plague of undeath, the people of Hillsbrad endured, proudly retaining the royal tabard and heraldry of their fallen kingdom. Led by Magistrate Burnside and the Council of Hillsbrad, the township operates as an independent civic body under constant siege. The local blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices keep the populace armed, ensuring every farmer and laborer is prepared to defend their land.

Hive'Ashi. Hive'Ashi is a sprawling silithid colony dominating the northern sands of Silithus. As one of three major insectoid hives in the region, its creeping tunnels and towering mounds churn with countless hostile workers, defenders, and stingers. Situated in northern Silithus, Hive'Ashi serves as a prime hive-complex for the re-emerging silithid swarms. Its chitinous spires carve out a distinct territory among the dunes, sending foraging workers and venomous defenders south and east toward the Swarming Pillar. Anyone seeking to understand the strange, coordinated intelligence stirring within the desert wastes inevitably finds their path leading directly into the dangerous, buzzing tunnels beneath these mounds.

Hive'Regal. Hive'Regal is a massive silithid hive burrowed into the southern reaches of Silithus. As one of the three primary insectoid colonies dominating the arid wastes, it teems with aggressive silithid castes that threaten to overrun the surrounding desert. Sprawling across southern Silithus, Hive'Regal represents one of the greatest concentrations of silithid activity in Kalimdor. Its towering resin spires and cavernous underground tunnels churn with dangerous insectoid broods, from venomous spitfires and burrowers to predatory slavemakers. The hive acts as a coordinated warren, aggressively defending its perimeter and harvesting organic material from any unfortunate travelers who wander too close to its borders.

Hive'Zora. Hive'Zora is one of the three major silithid colony mounds dominating the arid expanse of Silithus. Located along the western edge of the desert, this teeming subterranean hive crawls with aggressive insectoid castes serving the greater swarm. Rising out of the barren sand dunes of western Silithus, Hive'Zora serves as a bustling hub of insectoid activity. Great, porous stone spires and mounds mark the entrances into deep subterranean tunnels dug out by silithid burrowers. Waywatchers and reavers patrol the perimeter relentlessly, while tunneling castes and hive sisters brood within the depths below. For the Cenarion Circle and other scouts keeping watch over the desert, the hive represents a terrifying sign of the insectoid menace steadily reclaiming the ancient frontier.

Horizon Scout. The Horizon Scout is a sunken vessel resting on the ocean floor in the Ruined Reaches off the southern coast of Azshara. While its captain remains stranded ashore, several crew members remain trapped in the submerged hull, kept alive beneath the waves by an arcane water-breathing enchantment. Resting beneath the waves among the treacherous shoals of the Ruined Reaches, the Horizon Scout met a violent end off Azshara's jagged coast. While Captain Vanessa Beltis managed to reach land on a nearby peninsula, a portion of the crew went down with the hull. Miraculously, the survivors inside have not drowned; a gnome named Roland Geardabbler maintains a sustained magical bubble of water breathing that preserves them within the wreckage. Surrounded by hostile aquatic predators and predatory naga, the remaining sailors wait in the dark forward compartments, unable to surface on their own.

Howling Vale. Tucked away in north-central Ashenvale near the Felwood border, the Howling Vale is a darkened dell overrun by savage, alien wolf-beasts known as the Terrowulf worgen. Hidden deep within its caves lies the ancient Shrine of Mel'Thandris, an Elune-blessed ruin tied intimately to the tragic origins of the worgen curse on Kalimdor. North of the road toward Felwood, the calm majesty of Ashenvale gives way to eerie, predatory howling. The vale shelters ancient trees alongside corrupted Terrowulf packlords and aggressive wildlife. At its heart lies a cave enshrining the memory of Mel'Thandris, an ancient night elf priestess. While the shrine once stood as a place of quiet devotion, its tranquil halls have fallen into ruined disrepair, defiled by feral wolf-men whose origin puzzles the Sentinels stationed nearby.

Hunter Rise. Hunter Rise is one of the elevated mesas making up the city of Thunder Bluff, situated just south of the central bluff. It serves as the primary training and gathering ground for the tauren's warriors, hunters, trackers, and skinners. Across its windswept platforms, young braves hone their martial skills and prepare for combat. Connected to the neighboring bluffs by swaying rope bridges, Hunter Rise is dedicated to the martial traditions of the tauren. It is anchored by the Hunter's Hall, where experienced marksmen, trackers, and warriors pass down their discipline to younger generations. Surrounding the lodge are practice grounds outfitted with training dummies, weapon racks, and skinning posts, making it a bustling center for those who live by spear, bow, and hide.

Hushed Bank. The Hushed Bank is the shadowy western shoreline of Duskwood, bordering the river that divides the forest from Westfall. Stretching from the junction near the Three Corners south toward Stranglethorn Vale, it is a quiet yet hazardous woodland stalked by prowling beasts and shadowed by dark mysteries. Running along the river boundary between Duskwood and Westfall, the Hushed Bank marks the transition from open plains and sunlit farms to pervasive, unnatural twilight. The wooden covered bridge crosses the river here, offering passage to travelers heading west out of the grim wood. Thick underbrush and creeping fog dominate the riverbanks, where large spiders and hungry forest wolves stalk unwary wayfarers who stray from the beaten path.

Ice Thistle Hills. The Ice Thistle Hills are a snow-covered highland rise lying just southeast of the goblin outpost of Everlook. Dominated by a rugged cavern system, the area is claimed by ferocious Ice Thistle yetis that threaten any travelers venturing off the main road. Rising sharply out of the central drifts of Winterspring, the Ice Thistle Hills serve as the primary hunting grounds and nesting territory for the valley's aggressive Ice Thistle yetis. Centered around a prominent cave dug deep into the rockface, these hulking beasts roam both the rocky slopes and the winding tunnels within. Because of their proximity to Everlook, the yetis present a constant nuisance and danger to goblin commerce and visiting prospectors, who regularly commission intrepid hunters to cull the beasts for their valuable thick pelts and pristine horns.

Iceflow Lake. Iceflow Lake is a frigid, partially frozen body of water situated in western Dun Morogh, directly north of Brewnall Village. Despite the relentless frost, local dwarves maintain fishing holes through the sheet ice to secure fresh water and fish. The snow-covered islands in the center of the lake are prowled by aggressive winter wolves and their alpha, Timber. Spanning western Dun Morogh just outside Brewnall Village, Iceflow Lake battles the bitter Khaz Modan climate year-round. Thick ice sheets continually creep across the surface, forcing local residents like Paxton Ganter to regularly clear holes for ice fishing and drinking water. While the shore provides sustenance, the islands rising from the middle of the lake are far less welcoming. A fierce pack of wild wolves has made these icy mounds their territory, dominated by the notoriously savage gray worg known as Timber.

Infectis Scar. The Infectis Scar is a deep, unnatural chasm carved into the blighted terrain of the Eastern Plaguelands near Corin's Crossing. Unlike natural ravines, this wound in the earth was ripped open by necromantic power when a cursed runeblade shattered against a dwarven shield. The blight festering at the bottom of the fissure remains an enduring testament to the Scourge's dark sorcery. While neighboring gorges like the Pestilent Scar originated as natural terrain features poisoned by the plague, the Infectis Scar is entirely artificial. It was created during the third war's violent clashes near Corin's Crossing. When the notorious death knight Marduk Blackpool clashed with a stalwart dwarf captain, Marduk's cursed runesword shattered against the captain's shield. Discarding the broken weapon, Marduk kept the hilt, but the severed runeblade sank deep into the soil. Its foul enchantment violently tore open the crust of the earth, creating the jagged chasm that sits festering in the Plaguelands today.

Iris Lake. Iris Lake is a blighted body of water resting in north-central Ashenvale, east of Astranaar. Once pristine, its waters have turned a sickly yellowish-green from demonic corruption seeping down from Felwood, and hostile bog beasts now prowl its shores. Nestled between Astranaar and the moonwell tended by Shael'dryn, Iris Lake stands as a grim reminder of the wounds inflicted during the Third War. Fel energies drifting south from the tainted heights of Felwood have poisoned the basin, turning its once-clear waters into a foul, sickly yellow-green mire. The corruption has twisted the native plant life and water spirits, raising aggressive bog beasts that lash out at any traveler who wanders near.

Ironband's Compound. Ironband's Compound is a fortified outpost tucked into the snowy hills south of Helm's Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh. Formerly home to the prospector Sturgy Ironband, the camp has been overrun by hostile Dark Iron dwarves who attack anyone venturing too close. Originally established by Sturgy Ironband, this compound south of Helm's Bed Lake once served as a staging post in the snowy wilderness of Dun Morogh. That changed when Dark Iron infiltrators pushed deep into Bronzebeard territory and seized the site for themselves. Now bristling with hostile dwarves, the compound serves as an enemy forward base threatening travelers and nearby settlements, right under the nose of Ironforge.

Ironband's Excavation Site. Ironband's Excavation Site is an expansive dwarven dig located in southeastern Loch Modan, just south of the lake and southwest of Farstrider Lodge. Led by Prospector Ironband, the archaeological operation was abruptly halted when aggressive, volatile troggs overran the trenches. Spurred by the dwarven drive to uncover their ancient Titan origins, Prospector Ironband established this sprawling digsite along the rugged cliffs of southeastern Loch Modan. What began as a promising excavation quickly turned into a disaster when the digging disturbed an unusually fierce and large breed of subterranean troggs. The creatures surged from the earth, driving back the miners and setting up camp amidst the scattered tools, broken carts, and half-excavated relics.

Ironbeard's Tomb. Ironbeard's Tomb is a defiled dwarven burial site situated west of the road leading north toward Dun Modr in the Wetlands. Marked by an outdoor graveyard and a stone statue of its namesake, the crypt has fallen into disuse as acidic oozes swarm the grounds. Travelers rarely set foot in the hollow unless searching for lost possessions swallowed by the slime. Overlooking the marshes along the road north to Dun Modr, Ironbeard's Tomb stands as a testament to the dwarven presence in the Wetlands. A monumental stone statue, presumed to depict Ironbeard himself, watches over the surrounding burial plot. Yet solemn peace no longer keeps vigil here. The subterranean crypt has been completely overrun by oozes of various black and crimson strains, leaving the tomb contaminated. Dwarves no longer bring their dead to this ruined sanctuary, and those brave enough to disturb the vaults do so primarily to hunt through the remains digested by the lurking slimes.

Ironclad Cove. Ironclad Cove is a massive subterranean cavern hidden beneath Westfall, housing an underground shipyard and dock. It serves as the secret construction dock for the Defias Brotherhood's war juggernaught and connects directly to the sea. Buried at the deepest point of the Deadmines, Ironclad Cove is a monumental sea cavern converted into a fortified dockyard. Here, Edwin VanCleef and the Defias Brotherhood have constructed an enormous warship known as the juggernaught. The cavern features extensive wooden scaffolding, islets, and loading catwalks manned by Defias pirates, deckhands, and overseers. Its existence reveals the true scale of the Defias threat: VanCleef intends not merely to raid Westfall's farmsteads, but to assemble a private naval force capable of bombarding the shores of Stormwind itself.

Ironforge. Ironforge is the underground capital city of the dwarves, excavated deep into the stone of Ironforge Mountain within Dun Morogh. Centered around the roaring Great Forge, it serves as the political and mercantile anchor of the Kingdom of Khaz Modan and a bulwark of the Alliance. Carved into the subterranean depths of Ironforge Mountain, the city is arranged in concentric stone rings radiating out from the monumental Great Forge. Originally founded millenia ago after the dwarves awakened and migrated from Uldaman, it has weathered ages of history, including the ancient War of the Three Hammers that left the Bronzebeard clan in sole control. Powered by cascading torrents of molten magma and fortified behind massive stone gates, the cavern city is equal parts industrial powerhouse and impenetrable bastion. Beyond dwarven craftsmen and warriors, its halls also host a substantial population of exiled gnomes following the recent fall of Gnomeregan.

Ironforge Airfield. Tucked away high in the snowy peaks northeast of Ironforge, this remote dwarven airstrip serves as a proving ground and staging area for gnome flying machines and dwarven mountaineers. Unmarked by main roads, the plateau overlooks the jagged crags of Dun Morogh and the steep descent toward the Wetlands. Perched far above the beaten trails of Dun Morogh, the high-altitude airfield is a quiet marvel of Alliance cooperation. Sheltered by surrounding mountain peaks, dwarven masonry anchors the blustery ridgelines while gnomish flying machines sit parked along open landing strips. Mountaineers keep watch over the perimeter alongside engineers busy wrenching gears and inspecting steam-belching engines in the biting cold.

Ironstone Camp. Ironstone Camp is an outpost established by the Horde along the western border of the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Originally deployed to expel Alliance dwarven excavators from the nearby digsite, the encampment's forces now face a deadly threat after subterranean silithid overran the excavation. Ironstone Camp sits directly on the threshold between the high pillars of Thousand Needles and the blazing salt expanse of the Shimmering Flats. The Horde detachment stationed here was initially dispatched with a clear and singular objective: dislodge the dwarven excavators digging at the Rustmaul Digsite. However, their military confrontation was cut short when a swarm of voracious silithid burst forth from a nearby cavern, violently engulfing the dig and attacking both sides. Led by Moktar Krin, the surviving camp defenders have diverted their efforts to combating the insectoid infestation before the swarm spreads unchecked across the region.

Irontree Woods. Irontree Woods is a blighted grove situated in northern Felwood, once cherished by the night elves as a peaceful forest sanctuary. Ravaged by the demonic corruption of the Third War, its ancient protectors have been petrified into stone while twisted treants and elementals prowl among the ruins. Irontree Woods was once a tranquil woodland glade tended by the kaldorei, but the demonic taint of the Burning Legion during the Third War choked the life from its soil. The grove's guardian Ancients—Hastat, Stoma, and Vartrus—succumbed to the dark magic, petrifying into lifeless stone monuments that still stand entombed amid the corrupted brush. Now, maddened treants, vile bog beasts, and tainted water elementals wander the twisted forest floor, striking violently at any travelers who dare approach.

Isle of Dread. The Isle of Dread is a desolate, cliff-bound island situated in the Great Sea off the southwestern coast of Feralas, south of Sardor Isle. It is notorious for sheltering monstrous two-headed chimaeroks and an entrenched coven of hostile naga hidden within its subterranean sea caves. Rising out of the crashing surf of the South Seas, the Isle of Dread lives up to its ominous name. Ringed by sheer cliffs, the island's interior valley is only accessible through a narrow pathway on its southeastern coast. Within this enclosed highland roams a lethal population of chimaeroks—ravenous, two-headed beasts empowered by ambient arcane energies. These beasts are led by the monstrous Lord Lakmaeran, making the island a deadly deathtrap for unwary explorers who cross the channel from Sardor Isle.

Itharius's Cave. Itharius's Cave is a secluded hollow tucked into the far southwestern cliffs of the Swamp of Sorrows. It serves as the refuge of the enigmatic Itharius, who appears to be a high elf and tends to the brood of green dragonkin inhabiting the surrounding marsh. Tucked away in the treacherous, moss-draped crags of the southwestern Swamp of Sorrows, this damp cavern shelters the recluse Itharius. Outside its mouth, unruly green whelps wander the mire. Though he appears to be a high elf, a folk who rarely wander so far south into wild swamps alone, Itharius keeps a watchful eye on these young dragonkin as they grow, living alongside them in quiet isolation.

Ivar Patch. The Ivar Patch is a blighted pumpkin farm located in northern Silverpine Forest. Once a thriving agricultural homestead of Lordaeron, its residents were wiped out during the Third War and transformed into ravenous, mindlessly hostile ghouls. Before the Third War swept through Lordaeron, this pumpkin patch was a prosperous homestead owned by a farmer named Ivar, who employed a lively crew of farmhands and servants. When the Scourge unleashed the Plague of Undeath across the countryside, the farm was consumed completely. Rather than rising with their minds intact like the free-willed Forsaken, Ivar, his family, and his laborers were reduced to rotting, feral ghouls bound to prowl the ruined soil.

Jadefire Run. Jadefire Run is a heavily fortified satyr encampment nestled in northern Felwood. It houses some of the most powerful and cunning satyrs in the region, serving as a bastion of demonic corruption deep within the tainted forest. Situated amid the blighted woods of northern Felwood, Jadefire Run functions as a stronghold for the Jadefire satyrs. Unlike lesser outposts scattered throughout the valley, this camp features substantial demonic construction and shelters formidable spellcasters and tricksters. The satyrs here actively conspire to spread corruption further across Kalimdor, employing dark sorcery and foul trickery against anyone who dares intrude on their territory.

Jaedenar. Jaedenar is a blighted hollow in central Felwood built over ancient night elf ruins and druidic barrow dens. Named in foul homage to the demon lord Kil'jaeden, it serves as the primary base of operations for the Shadow Council in northern Kalimdor. Cultists, warlocks, and summoned demons scour the corrupt hollow, guarding the subterranean descent into the Shadow Hold. Long ago, these hollows sheltered night elf sacred grounds and slumbering druids connected to the Emerald Dream. After the devastation of the Third War, the vile remnant of the Shadow Council laid claim to the valley, christening it Jaedenar to honor the demon lord Kil'jaeden. Warlocks—predominantly renegade orcs and Forsaken—have gathered here alongside satyrs, succubi, and felguards. They occupy both the surface ruins and the deeper barrow dens, twisting what was once holy woodland into a grim center of demonic invocation.

Jagged Reef. The Jagged Reef forms the rugged northern coast of Azshara, where sandy beaches meet jagged stone spurs and churning surf. Treacherous rocks lurk beneath the shallow water, making maritime travel impossible. The desolate shore is primarily populated by prowling hydras, scavenging makrura, and territorial murloc tribes. Stretching across Azshara's northern edge, the Jagged Reef is a harsh littoral expanse where broken cliffs and jutting stone outcroppings divide the sandy shores into secluded inlets. Beneath the breaking waves lie submerged crags and shifting shallows, turning the waters into a graveyard for any vessel foolish enough to venture near. On land, the wild coastline offers little comfort; salt-crusted beasts, predatory hydras, and aggressive makrura wander the surf line alongside entrenched murlocs scouring the tides for scraps and unwary prey.

Jaggedswine Farm. Jaggedswine Farm is a modest livestock steading situated in northern Durotar, just south of the main entrance to Orgrimmar. Comprising a timber storage shed, a sprawling pen, and a muddy watering hole, it serves as a critical food source raising hardy swine for the nearby Horde capital. Carved out of Durotar's unforgiving, sunbaked earth, Jaggedswine Farm represents the harsh reality of sustaining an urban stronghold like Orgrimmar. The red soil of the region yields sparse agriculture, making robust livestock essential to feeding thousands of orcish warriors and laborers. The farm centers on a timber storehouse, a wide wooden pen, and a natural watering pond where swine are herded, bred, and butchered to keep the Horde's granaries stocked.

Jaguero Isle. Jaguero Isle is an isolated, jungle-covered island resting off the eastern coast of Stranglethorn Vale's Wild Shore. Dominated by fierce wild panthers and gorillas, it is infamous as the domain of the colossal silverback gorilla known as King Mukla. Situated off the southeastern coast of Stranglethorn Vale, Jaguero Isle stands well apart from the mainland pirate camps and troll ruins. The island is entirely overrun by untamed fauna, mainly panthers and aggressive gorillas. Looming over them all is the gargantuan ape King Mukla, whose rule over the rocky interior is absolute and territorial. Few sailors willingly approach its reefs, though occasionally washed-up bottles along the mainland beaches carry desperate pleas for rescue from those unfortunate enough to be stranded ashore.

Janeiro's Point. Janeiro's Point is a small, rocky island situated just outside the harbor of Booty Bay in southern Stranglethorn Vale. It is crowned by a colossal stone statue of an unknown goblin welcoming incoming maritime traffic with outstretched arms. The island's waters and shores are dominated by the menacing sea giant known as Mok'rash the Cleaver. Standing as the monumental gateway to Booty Bay, Janeiro's Point greets every vessel charting a course into the southern seas of Stranglethorn Vale. Atop the crag looms an immense stone effigy of a goblin, arms spread wide in a grand gesture of welcome and unbridled mercantile ambition. Though visible to sailors and corsairs for miles around, landing on the island's shores is a perilous prospect due to Mok'rash the Cleaver, a terrifying sea giant who has claimed the outcrop as his territory.

Jangolode Mine. Jangolode Mine is a rich mineral excavation located in the rolling hills of Westfall. Once a vital source of ore and raw materials for Stormwind City, the mine has been seized by the bandits of the Defias Brotherhood. Before Westfall fell into decline, the Jangolode Mine provided a steady flow of metals crucial to the reconstruction and supply of Stormwind City. As civil order deteriorated and the kingdom withdrew its garrisons, the Defias Brotherhood seized control of the site to feed their own operations. The bandits now work the rich veins for themselves, fiercely defending their subterranean prize.

Jansen Stead. Jansen Stead is the northernmost farmstead in Westfall, situated just down the road from the bridge to Elwynn Forest. Like much of the surrounding breadbasket, the homestead has fallen out of peasant hands and is swarming with rogue mechanical Harvest Watchers and roving Defias bandits. Positioned right past the Elwynn border, the Jansen Stead represents the harsh reality greeting anyone traveling westward into Westfall. Once a flourishing family farm feeding the kingdom, its rightful occupants have been driven away by the rising tide of unrest. In their place, hostile Harvest Watchers—mechanical constructs associated with the Defias Brotherhood—patrol the blighted fields alongside brigands. Its proximity to the main road makes it a prominent early hazard for couriers and travelers moving between Goldshire and Sentinel Hill.

Jasperlode Mine. Jasperlode Mine is an iron and mineral excavation in north-central Elwynn Forest that once supplied Stormwind City with vital resources. Today, the shafts are overrun by swarming kobolds and deadly giant spiders, leaving the resource-strapped kingdom unable to reclaim it. Jasperlode Mine was historically one of Stormwind's most productive mining operations, providing steady mineral wealth alongside nearby Fargodeep. With the kingdom's military stretched thin defending against external threats and unrest, local garrisons have been unable to protect the shafts. Kobolds seized the opportunity to burrow inside, driving human miners out and stockpiling stolen gold and tallow candles.

Jerod's Landing. Jerod's Landing is a modest river dock situated on the Elwynn Forest bank of the Nazferiti River. Currently seized by the Defias Brotherhood, the outpost serves as a clandestine transfer point for illicit shipments smuggled across the kingdom's waterways. Tucked away along the eastern waters of the Nazferiti River, Jerod's Landing provides river access connecting Elwynn Forest to neighboring territories. While originally an ordinary boat dock, the site has fallen firmly into the hands of the Defias Brotherhood. Under the watchful eye of a Defias dockmaster, outlaws utilize the dock as a hub to receive goods plundered from the Redridge Mountains, discreetly moving river cargo downstream toward holdings such as Klaven's Tower in Westfall.

Karazhan. Karazhan is the ominous, secluded tower standing at the southern end of Deadwind Pass. Once the sanctum of Medivh, the Last Guardian of Tirisfal, the citadel sits atop a potent convergence of ley lines that warps time, space, and reality around it. Though Medivh was slain during the First War, the abandoned fortress still hums with volatile arcane energy, restless spirits, and hidden dangers. Long before the First War, the tower of Karazhan was raised upon ground shaped like a human skull, situated at a massive nexus of mystical ley lines. It served as a secluded refuge and repository of untold magical secrets for the Guardian Medivh.
