Within its curving halls, Medivh lived alongside his loyal castellan Moroes, entertaining noble guests and housing an immense archive of arcane texts and relics that eclipsed even the libraries of the Kirin Tor. Yet the tower was also the stage for Azeroth's greatest betrayal, as Medivh fell under the demonic possession of Sargeras and secretly orchestrated the opening of the Dark Portal.

Kargath. Kargath is a fortified Horde outpost perched in the western Badlands, serving as their sole foothold in Khaz Modan. Established by the Kargath Expeditionary Force under Warchief Thrall's orders, the settlement anchors crucial transit lines across the Eastern Kingdoms while staging operations toward Blackrock Mountain and the excavation at Uldaman. Named in honor of the Shattered Hand chieftain Kargath Bladefist, the outpost of Kargath stands as the Horde's solitary settlement throughout the mountain realms of Khaz Modan. Surrounded by arid wastes, aggressive wildlife, and hostile dwarven factions, the garrison provides a vital midway sanctuary for travelers crossing the continent. Its flight master bridges the long divide between northern holdings like the Undercity and Hammerfall and southern redoubts like Stonard and Grom'gol Base Camp.

Kargathia Keep. Kargathia Keep is a fortified Horde stronghold anchoring the eastern front of the Warsong Lumber Camp in Ashenvale. Serving as headquarters for the outpost's overseers, it guards the river border and ensures rapid reinforcement lines directly back to Orgrimmar. Perched on the eastern edge of the Warsong Lumber Camp just west of the Southfury River, Kargathia Keep serves as the command center for the Horde's logging operations in Ashenvale. Upgraded with heavy spiked barricades, this fortified outpost houses Overseer Gorthak and his officers. Its strategic position against the river border allows the Warsong clan to monitor incoming incursions and receive swift reinforcements directly from the neighboring lands of Durotar and Orgrimmar whenever night elf skirmishers strike.

Kharanos. Kharanos is a bustling mountain settlement nestled in the snowy heart of Dun Morogh, just down the road from Ironforge. Serving as the primary hub for travelers leaving Coldridge Valley, the town hosts a forge, gnomish workshops, and the famous Thunderbrew Distillery. Situated along the central road of Dun Morogh, Kharanos is the first true town welcoming recruits arriving from Anvilmar. Despite the biting cold and biting winds, the settlement thrives thanks to local dwarven grit and gnomish ingenuity. It centers around a roaring public forge and the Thunderbrew Distillery, renowned across the eastern mountains for producing some of the finest ale in Khaz Modan. Between bustling crafters and weary travelers seeking warmth, the town stands as the essential staging ground for business in the lower peaks.

Kodo Graveyard. The Kodo Graveyard is a sprawling expanse in central Desolace littered with the massive, bleached remains of ancient beasts. By instinct or tradition, aging and dying kodos make a final pilgrimage to this desolate hollow to collapse among the ribs of their ancestors. Sprawling across the grey earth of Desolace, the Kodo Graveyard holds the colossal skeletons of ancient beasts, some far larger than any living kodo seen today. Dying kodos wander here to spend their final breaths among centuries of accumulated remains. This sacred peace is fragile: scavengers prowl the perimeter, and those who disturb the calcified ribs and skulls risk stirring furious kodo spirits from the dust.

Kodo Rock. Kodo Rock is a natural stone monument located in the plains of Red Cloud Mesa, between Camp Narache and Brambleblade Ravine. Standing quietly amid the grasses of Mulgore, it serves as an early pilgrimage site for young tauren shamans learning to commune with the spirits of the earth. Because of its modest silhouette against the rolling landscape, travelers must keep a keen eye out to spot it. Situated roughly halfway along the path connecting Camp Narache to the hostile quilboar territory of Brambleblade Ravine, Kodo Rock is marked by a patch of worn earth at its base. While it lacks the sheer grandeur of the towering bluffs surrounding Red Cloud Mesa, its distinct profile resembles the revered kodo beasts that wander the grasslands. For wandering tribesfolk, it acts as a quiet natural beacon in the windswept plains of Mulgore.

Kolkar Crag. Kolkar Crag is a sunbaked, jagged gorge in southern Durotar claimed by the hostile Kolkar centaur. Led by Warlord Kolkanis, this enclave serves as a staging ground for coordinated raids against nearby Horde settlements. Tucked away in the rugged canyons of southern Durotar, Kolkar Crag is a base of operations for the aggressive Kolkar clan. Despite the arid and unforgiving terrain, these centaur have fortified the natural choke points of the gorge. From this ravine, their scouts and marauders keep close watch over the surrounding flats, probing for vulnerabilities across orc and Darkspear holdings. For young warriors training in the Valley of Trials or patrolling the southern coast, Kolkar Crag represents the nearest organized front of centaur hostility.

Kormek's Hut. Kormek's Hut is a remote, ramshackle dwelling sitting amid the barren flats of north-central Desolace. Despite its desolate surroundings and mysterious namesake, it currently shelters an eccentric pair: an oddly peaceful cultist and a goblin obsessed with harvesting kodo bones. Perched out in the arid wastes of north-central Desolace, this small hovel is named after a figure whose whereabouts and identity remain completely unknown. Instead of Kormek, travelers stumbling upon the hut encounter an unusual pairing living out in the middle of nowhere: Willow and Bibbly F'utzbuckle. Inside the hut sits Willow, a member of the otherwise hostile and nihilistic Twilight's Hammer who curiously treats outsiders with calm hospitality. Outside, a pen littered with sun-bleached kodo bones serves as the personal dance floor and staging ground for Bibbly, an excitable goblin captivated by the commercial potential of bone scavenging.

Kurzen's Compound. Kurzen's Compound is a heavily fortified human settlement tucked into the hills of northern Stranglethorn Vale. Established by an expedition dispatched from Stormwind under Colonel Kurzen, the outpost has devolved into a rogue camp of cutthroats and wild beasts following their commander's descent into madness. What began as an official expedition into the untamed jungles of Stranglethorn turned into a nightmare when Colonel Kurzen lost his mind. Rather than fulfilling Stormwind's mission, the garrison broke away from the kingdom's authority, cutting ties with the crown and descending into tyranny. Today, the compound operates like a mercenary stronghold, complete with a functional lumber mill, stables for training captured Stranglethorn panthers and tigers as weapons of war, and an extensive cave complex known as the Stockpile where the rogue soldiers stash their plundered supplies.

Lake Al'Ameth. Lake Al'Ameth is one of the largest freshwater bodies nestled high in the boughs of Teldrassil, located just south of Dolanaar. Though once a tranquil haven featuring little more than a simple wooden jetty, its shores have grown perilous due to the violent agitation of the local plant life. Resting immediately south of the village of Dolanaar, Lake Al'Ameth serves as a vital natural basin in the heart of Teldrassil. Despite its serene waters and minimal settlement, peace here has evaporated. Swarms of agitated timberlings and timberling sprouts prowl the water's edge, driven mad by an unnatural sickness spreading through the world tree. Druids and researchers from Dolanaar frequently dispatch travelers to these shores to gather seeds and cull the aggressive creatures before the corruption spreads deeper into the surrounding forest.

Lake Elune'ara. Lake Elune'ara is the shimmering, sacred body of water that occupies the heart of Moonglade. Revering the Moon Goddess Elune, the lake serves as a place of spiritual reflection for the Cenarion Circle, though deep within its murky floor lies the dormant, corrupted demigod Omen. Framed by the moonlit groves of Moonglade, Lake Elune'ara provides serene waters said to be blessed by the White Lady herself. The lake lies at the spiritual center of the druidic haven, bordered by Nighthaven to the north and the shrine grounds of the Cenarion Circle. Initiates have long plumbed its tranquil depths to retrieve long-lost relics, attuning themselves to the currents of nature as they seek harmony with the land.

Lake Everstill. Lake Everstill is the expansive azure body of water dominating the heart of the Redridge Mountains, flanking the town of Lakeshire. Once celebrated for tranquil fishing and clean mountain runoff, its shores and waters have lately turned treacherous due to aggressive murloc tribes and predatory lake beasts. Spanning the central basin of Redridge, Lake Everstill provides the scenic backdrop and vital waterway for the township of Lakeshire. Its crystal-clear waters drain eastward toward the looming heights of Stonewatch. Spanned by the town's central bridge, the lake has long sustained local trade and quiet anglers, though anyone walking the shoreline today will find its peaceful reputation thoroughly shattered by encroaching wilderness threats.

Lake Falathim. Lake Falathim is a tranquil body of water nestled in the forested hills of western Ashenvale, southwest of Maestra's Post. Revered for the constant touch of Elune's moonlight upon its surface day and night, it was once a beloved retreat for night elves. In recent days, however, aggressive murlocs have overrun its shores, turning a sacred haven into a perilous hazard. Tucked away southeast of the Zoram Strand, Lake Falathim was long cherished by the Kaldorei as a peaceful sanctuary for swimming and fishing. According to local lore, the gentle radiance of Elune rests upon these waters at all hours, day or night. Despite this sacred blessing, ferocious murlocs have surged inland to seize the shores, nesting in thick numbers and driving away local travelers and scholars alike.

Lake Kel'Theril. Lake Kel'Theril is a vast, frozen lake nestled in the heart of Winterspring. Along its ice-locked shores stand ancient kaldorei ruins haunted by restless spirits who have lingered since the Great Sundering. Lake Kel'Theril is shrouded in eternal cold, its waters sealed under thick sheets of ice. Scattered across its surface and snowy banks are the shattered pillars and arches of ancient elven architecture. These are the remnants of Kel'Theril, once an outpost of the ancient Highborne civilization before the Great Sundering shattered Kalimdor. Rather than finding rest in death, the spirits of the fallen aristocracy wander the ice as tormented ghosts and specters, forever tethered to the tragic remnants of their former glory.

Lake Mennar. Lake Mennar is a tranquil body of freshwater nestled amidst the shattered ruins of Azshara. It is remarkably renowned as one of the exceedingly rare havens outside of Northrend where members of the blue dragonflight reside. While the perimeter teems with protective blue dragonspawn, the shores of the lake itself remain strangely serene. Situated in the ancient, broken landscape of Azshara, Lake Mennar serves as a secluded gathering ground for the blue dragonflight. Aside from Mazthoril to the north in Winterspring, it is virtually unheard of to encounter blue dragons in such numbers across Kalimdor. Blue dragonspawn tirelessly patrol the ridges and approaches circling the basin, fiercely guarding the waters. Yet for any wanderer daring enough to slip through this vigilant ring of sentries, the calm waters of the lake offer unexpected quietude, shielded from the arcane turmoil and roaming beast packs common to the rest of the peninsula.

Lake Mereldar. Lake Mereldar is a sprawling, contaminated body of water resting south of Corin's Crossing in the Eastern Plaguelands. Once part of the idyllic rural heartland of Lordaeron, its corrupted waters now spawn twisted elementals and rot beneath the lingering taint of the Scourge. Situated just south of the crossroads town of Corin's Crossing, Lake Mereldar was once a peaceful fixture of northern Lordaeron's countryside. Dotting its shores are the decaying ruins of an old homestead, an abandoned shack, and a dilapidated ferry that once carried local farmers and travelers across the gentle waters. With the coming of the Scourge and the plague of undeath, the lake fell into complete ruin. The surrounding soil withered, and the waters turned foul and poisonous.

Lake Nazferiti. Lake Nazferiti is a sprawling freshwater lake nestled in the dense jungle of northern Stranglethorn Vale. Fed by a vast river system stretching far north into the mountains, its waters are infested with ferocious crocolisks and snapping frenzies, while its shores host an industrial encampment operated by the goblin Venture Company. Lake Nazferiti sits along the Nazferiti River, one of the longest continuous waterways across the southern Eastern Kingdoms. The river traces its origins deep into the northern heights, tumbling down waterfalls from the Redridge Mountains and possibly originating as far inland as Deadwind Pass. Within Stranglethorn, the water widens into this murky lake, teeming with vicious predators like snapping river frenzies and ambush-hunting crocolisks that make casual swimming deadly.

Lakeridge Highway. Lakeridge Highway is an old thoroughfare running along the southern shore of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Once a vital and heavily traveled artery prior to the First War, it has fallen into ruin and disuse. Today, roving packs of gnolls and Blackrock orcs make passage along the road perilous for travelers. Before the devastation of the First War, the Lakeridge Highway served as a bustling trade corridor through Redridge, carrying goods and folk along the southern banks of Lake Everstill. In those peaceful days, travelers could journey between the valley settlements and the eastern heights under the protection of the Kingdom of Stormwind. That safety shattered when the Horde marched through the region, leaving eastern Redridge contested and desolate.

Lakeshire. Lakeshire is the primary human settlement in the Redridge Mountains, nestled along the northern shores of Lake Everstill. Led by Magistrate Solomon and guarded by Marshal Marris, the picturesque town is currently on the brink of collapse due to relentless assaults by Blackrock orcs, aggressive gnoll packs, and shoreline murlocs. Once a peaceful haven in the foothills east of Stormwind, Lakeshire has become the kingdom's most embattled frontier. The town's garrison at Stonewatch Keep was brutally overrun by Blackrock clan orcs sweeping down from the north, and dark wizardry has riled local Shadowhide gnoll packs into organized raiding parties. Blackrock saboteurs have even shattered parts of the Everstill Bridge, leaving Foreman Oslow and his crew struggling to repair the span while under constant threat of attack. With murlocs choking the lake's shores and gnolls stalking the high passes, Lakeshire's defenders are stretched to their breaking point.

Lakeshire Inn. The Lakeshire Inn is the social hub and primary refuge in the beleaguered town of Lakeshire. Situated in the heart of the Redridge Mountains, it provides warmth, ale, and safe lodging for local townsfolk and weary travelers contending with the surrounding perils. Perched on the shore of Lake Everstill, the Lakeshire Inn offers a brief respite from the gnoll bands and Blackrock orcs pressing in on the town. Despite Lakeshire's increasingly desperate military situation, the tavern maintains a cozy, bustling atmosphere. Barkeep Daniels and Innkeeper Brianna attend to the locals and travelers, serving up flagons of ale, wine, and warm meals. It is a vital meeting point where townspeople trade news, drown their sorrows, and seek hired blades to help defend the eastern border of the kingdom.

Lakeshire Town Hall. Lakeshire Town Hall serves as the administrative seat of the Redridge Mountains, standing at the heart of the lakeside settlement. Inside, Magistrate Solomon oversees local governance while wrestling with relentless threats from Blackrock orcs and gnolls. Lakeshire Town Hall is an aging stone structure that has been diligently refurbished multiple times over the years. Positioned prominently within Lakeshire, it houses Magistrate Solomon, a kind and dedicated civil leader tasked with maintaining order in the eastern reaches of the Kingdom of Stormwind. With Stormwind's military resources stretched thin and royal aid scarce, the hall has transformed from a quiet administrative office into an active command center where desperate appeals for volunteer defenders and mercenaries are processed daily.

Lakkari Tar Pits. The Lakkari Tar Pits are a series of foul-smelling, bubbling pools of thick black sludge in northern Un'Goro Crater. Situated just below the cliffs of Marshal's Refuge, they act as a natural death trap for unwary beasts and an incubator for hostile tar elementals. The Lakkari Tar Pits dominate the low ground of northern Un'Goro Crater, directly south of Marshal's Refuge. Thick, reeking pools of pitch entrap anything careless enough to step into them, quickly bogging down beasts and adventurers alike. The protruding bones of hundreds of prehistoric creatures break the black surface, bearing witness to generations of animals sucked into the mire. Opportunistic scavengers circle the margins waiting for trapped prey to exhaust itself, while living tar beasts, lurkers, and creepers rise directly from the muck to batter interlopers.

Land's End Beach. Land's End Beach is a desolate stretch of coastline at the far southern tip of Tanaris, effectively marking the southern edge of Kalimdor. Shielded by towering mountain ridges and vast ocean waters, it remains one of the most secluded and inaccessible shores on the continent. Tucked away behind the southern mountain ranges of Tanaris and the sealed titan gateway to Uldum, Land's End Beach represents the absolute southern edge of Kalimdor's mainland. Cut off from overland routes across the desert dunes, reaching this windswept coast requires swimming along the dangerous, fatigue-inducing open waters of the South Seas. The beach is a barren frontier of crashing surf, shifting sand, and quiet isolation, largely untamed by the cartels or desert explorers who dwell farther north around Gadgetzan.

Lariss Pavilion. Lariss Pavilion is an ancient elven structure tucked into the wilderness of Feralas just north of Camp Mojache. While once a peaceful retreat of classical night elf architecture, the surrounding forest has grown dangerous due to corrupted dryads, and an exiled Highborne mage now bides his time within its shade. Standing quietly on the bluffs north of Camp Mojache, Lariss Pavilion showcases the graceful stonework and towering archways of the ancient kaldorei empire. In its prime, it served the great city of Eldre'Thalas, now known as Dire Maul. Today, it offers a sheltered overlook above the dense canopy of Feralas, but the peace here is frail: the once-gentle dryads wandering the surrounding glades have fallen to madness and corruption, turning fiercely hostile to anyone who draws near.

Launch Bay. The Launch Bay is a subterranean airfield and hangar tucked within the depths of Gnomeregan, located just beyond the Hall of Gears. Once the staging ground for gnomish flying machines and bombers, it has fallen completely under the control of hostile leper gnomes and corrupted mechanical contraptions. Serving as the primary hangar for Gnomeregan's aerial fleet, the Launch Bay is split across two tiers. Its central platform, reached by ramps from the upper walkway, still houses parked gnomish flying machines and heavy bombers that never made it out before the city was evacuated. Instead of skilled pilots, the flight decks are now crawling with crazed leper gnomes who maintain and guard the idling war machines.

Lethlor Ravine. Lethlor Ravine is a jagged, rocky canyon winding through the eastern reaches of the Badlands. It serves as a perilous roost and breeding ground for the black dragonflight, swarming with aggressive whelps and mature drakes. Carved deep into the scorched plateaus of the eastern Badlands, Lethlor Ravine is one of the most hazardous stretches of the desert. The craggy canyon walls provide a natural aerie for the black dragonflight, housing nests of fierce dragon whelps guarded by larger, fire-breathing drakes. Few travelers dare approach the valley floor, as the shadows overhead constantly betray the flight of winged predators circling among the rocky spires.

Library (Ironforge). Tucked inside the eastern wing of the Hall of Explorers, the Library serves as Ironforge's foremost repository of historical knowledge, archeological relics, and ancient lore. Maintained diligently by the Explorers' League, it houses extensive historical tomes alongside rare artifacts recovered from digs across Azeroth. Occupying a massive chamber within the Hall of Explorers, the Library is where dwarven scholars sift through the relics and field reports recovered by adventurers across the world. Administered by the Explorers' League, the shelves are packed with foundational chronicles detailing the War of the Three Hammers, the ancient Troll Wars, and the origins of the dwarven race. Inquiries regarding rare books or archival locations are directed to Librarian Mae Paledust.

Library Wing (Northshire). The Library Wing is the quiet, book-lined southern wing of Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest. It serves as a sanctuary for scholars, offering early instruction to fledgling priests and mages joining the defense of Stormwind. Branching south from the Main Hall of Northshire Abbey, the Library Wing houses dusty shelves, study lecterns, and quiet alcoves dedicated to intellectual and spiritual training. While martial recruits drill in the Hall of Arms across the abbey, aspiring mages and priests gather here to grasp the fundamentals of the Arcane and the Holy Light. Currently, Priestess Anetta guides novice priests in matters of faith and healing, while Khelden Bremen teaches budding mages how to shape primal elemental energy.

Library Wing (Tyr's Hand). The Library Wing is a secluded hall inside Tyr's Hand Abbey, nestled within the Scarlet Crusade's heavily fortified redoubt in the Eastern Plaguelands. Once dedicated to holy study and contemplation, its shelves are now consumed by the zealous order's rigid dogma and propaganda. Members of the Crusade congregate here to study scripture and guard the sanctum's religious relics. Situated off the central nave of Tyr's Hand Abbey opposite the martial quarters, the Library Wing reflects the ideological core of the Scarlet Crusade. Within these quiet stone alcoves, priests and crusaders immerse themselves in theological tracts, militant doctrines, and writings twisted by years of relentless warfare against the Scourge. Rather than preserving open scholarship, the texts sheltered here fuel the Crusade's paranoia, reinforcing their conviction that all outsiders carry the taint of corruption.

Light's Hope Chapel. Light's Hope Chapel is a sacred sanctuary situated in the eastern reaches of the Plaguelands, serving as the primary redoubt and headquarters for the Argent Dawn. Once a secluded shrine of the Church of the Holy Light in the Eastweald, it now stands as an enduring bulwark against the Scourge. Originally a chapel of the Church of the Holy Light within the verdant Eastweald, Light's Hope Chapel endured the fall of Lordaeron to become a vital shelter in a blighted realm. When the zealous extremists among the survivors splintered to form the Scarlet Crusade, more temperate knights and priests banded together to establish the Argent Dawn. Choosing this secluded, hallowed site as their forward base of operations, the Dawn opened its doors to all races and factions—Alliance and Horde alike—united in the common crusade to purge the Scourge and reclaim the northern lands.

Lion's Pride Inn. The Lion's Pride Inn is the bustling tavern and community center of Goldshire in Elwynn Forest. Kept by Innkeeper Farley, it serves as the primary resting place, meeting hall, and hiring house for travelers venturing just south of Stormwind City. Standing at the crossroads of Elwynn Forest, the Lion's Pride Inn is Goldshire's lively centerpiece. Operated by Innkeeper Farley under the tavern's traditional motto—'Rest and relaxation for the tired and cold'—the inn offers warm hearths, strong drinks, and rooms for weary adventurers fresh out of Northshire. Because Goldshire lies along the vital trade routes between Stormwind, Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood, the tavern serves as an indispensable rallying point where town marshals, local crafters, and seasoned trainers gather to share news and contract passing mercenaries.

Loading Room. The Loading Room is an industrial staging chamber inside Gnomeregan's sprawling mechanical complex. In the current era, this subterranean staging area lies deep within the corrupted fallen capital, dangerously close to rogue constructs such as Techbot. Before the fall of Gnomeregan, the Loading Room functioned as a bustling transit point and cargo staging bay linked to the subterranean transit networks of the tinker capital. Today, like the rest of the ruined city, it has succumbed to chaos. Radioactive fallout, invading troggs, and malfunctioning machinery have rendered the area extremely perilous. The rogue mechanized construct Techbot guards the vicinity, posing a severe threat to any gnome survivors or daring Alliance reclaimers attempting to secure the perimeter.

Long Wash. The Long Wash is a bleak, windswept stretch of beach in Darkshore running just south of Auberdine toward the ruins of Ameth'Aran. Gloomy and scattered with marine carcasses and flotsam, the shoreline has recently grown dangerous due to an increasing presence of hostile murlocs. Despite its name, the Long Wash is actually the shortest distinct stretch of coastline in Darkshore. It sits under the region's perpetual overcast skies, an expanse of damp sand littered with flotsam, beached driftwood, and the carcasses of sea creatures washed up by the Veiled Sea. While local crabs comb through the surf, travelers southward from Auberdine must tread cautiously: murloc tribes have established camps along the water's edge, aggressively attacking anyone encroaching on their scavenged territory.

Longshore. The Longshore is the expansive sandy coastline stretching along the entire western edge of Westfall. Despite its vast and scenic expanse, the shore is notoriously hazardous due to thick populations of aggressive murlocs and scattered wrecks off the coast. Running the full western length of Westfall, the Longshore is one of the widest unbroken beaches in the Eastern Kingdoms. Yet it offers little peace to travelers. Coastal murlocs dominate the surf, led by notorious terrors like Old Murk-Eye, while the remnants of sunken vessels—including ruined elven destroyers—litter the shallows. Near the southern reaches, isolated settlers like Daphne Stilwell struggle against marauding Defias bandits, standing within sight of the Westfall Lighthouse across the water.

Lordamere Internment Camp. Lordamere Internment Camp is a former Second War detention facility perched on the heights overlooking Dalaran. Once built to confine lethargic orcs, the camp is now occupied by surviving Dalaran magi and guards alongside a treacherous band of Forsaken defectors. Following the Second War, the Alliance constructed internment camps across the northern kingdoms to contain the defeated orcish Horde. Lordamere was unique as the sole camp established within the Alterac Mountains, placed under Dalaran's jurisdiction. With the orcs long since liberated or fled, the camp today functions under Warden Belamoore as an outpost for Dalaran remnants studying dangerous magical relics.

Lordamere Lake. Lordamere Lake is one of the largest bodies of freshwater in the Eastern Kingdoms, bordered by Tirisfal Glades, Silverpine Forest, and the Alterac Mountains. Once the bustling aquatic heart of human civilization in the north, its cold waters and islands are now haunted by Scourge necromancers, feral murlocs, and the spreading shadow of the undead. In the golden age of the Alliance of Lordaeron, Lordamere Lake sat at the crossroads of human power. The Capital City of Lordaeron guarded its northern shores, the sorcerous city-state of Dalaran rose near its southern reach, and the kingdom of Alterac lined its mountainous eastern edge. Merchant vessels and fishing boats once crossed its broad, mist-covered expanse without fear. Following the devastation of the Third War, the lake was transformed from a hub of commerce into a natural barrier dividing the Forsaken-held lands of Tirisfal and Silverpine from the treacherous heights of Alterac.

Lost Fleet. The Lost Fleet consists of the shattered wooden hulks of the Kul Tiras Third Fleet, sunken off the northern coast of the Wetlands along Baradin Bay. Decimated during the Second War by Dragonmaw-enslaved red dragons, the wreckage is now haunted by restless, cursed undead sailors bound to the wreckage by a mysterious curse. During the Second War, on its last voyage, the Kul Tiras Third Fleet was ambushed from above by red dragons enslaved by the Dragonmaw clan. Sheets of dragonflame quickly engulfed the fleet, sending proud vessels like the Wave Mistress and the Intrepid crashing onto the shallows and reefs of northern Bluegill Marsh. Almost the entire contingent drowned or burned, with First Mate Fitzsimmons standing as the lone living survivor of the disaster.

Lost Point. Lost Point is a dilapidated wooden watchtower standing in western Dustwallow Marsh, originally constructed by Theramore's forces as an advance scout post. It has since fallen into disrepair and slipped from the control of Lady Jaina Proudmoore's guard, now serving as a hideout for rogue deserters. Erected by the expeditionary forces of Theramore to monitor traffic and threats emerging from the Barrens, Lost Point has long outlived its intended military function. The outpost has decayed under the relentless moisture of the marsh, its timber rotting and its defenses abandoned by regular troops. Instead of garrison sentries, the tower and its immediate surroundings are occupied by human deserters who broke away from Theramore's service, finding shelter in the isolated wilderness far from the discipline of the city's commanders.

Lost Rigger Cove. Tucked away along the eastern cliffs of Tanaris, Lost Rigger Cove serves as the primary base of operations for the Southsea Pirates in the region. Shielded by towering desert mountains on three sides, this hidden port boasts docks, fortified encampments, and an active shipyard constructing new pirate vessels. Naturally fortified by sheer rock walls on almost every side, Lost Rigger Cove provides the Southsea Freebooters an ideal maritime stronghold on Kalimdor's southeastern edge. Here, pirate cutthroats, dockworkers, and brigands haul salvage and assemble fresh hulls right under the noses of Gadgetzan's authorities. The cove allows the Southseas to project power across the Great Sea while raiding trade routes between Ratchet, Booty Bay, and coastal settlements.

Lower Wilds. The Lower Wilds form the eastern threshold of Feralas, where the humid forests meet the arid canyons of Thousand Needles. The main road cutting through these woods connects Thalanaar at the border to the settlements further west, flanked by ancient greenery and unpredictable woodland creatures. Spanning the eastern reaches of Feralas, the Lower Wilds serve as the natural transition between the sun-baked ravines of Thousand Needles and the deep, primordial jungle to the west. Travelers entering the zone must traverse this stretch of forest along the main highway, past the elven outpost of Thalanaar guarding the mountain pass. The dense canopies here house ancient treants, alongside indigenous wildlife that makes straying from the beaten path perilous.

Lushwater Oasis. Lushwater Oasis is one of the three life-giving watering holes nestled in the arid Barrens, located just south of the Crossroads. Despite its verdant appearance, the oasis is fraught with danger, infested by aggressive Kolkar centaur and harboring the entrance to the Wailing Caverns. Its tainted waters are well-known to anglers seeking the peculiar Deviate Fish. Situated a short march south of the Crossroads, Lushwater Oasis offers a deceptive respite amid the sun-bleached expanse of the Barrens. While its palm canopies and fresh springs draw thirsty beasts from across the savanna, Kolkar centaur claim the banks, lying in wait to butcher both game and unwary travelers. The oasis is also the gateway to the Wailing Caverns, whose sprawling underground networks seep corruptive energies into the pools above, breeding unnatural wildlife and bizarre mutations.

Maclure Vineyards. Maclure Vineyards is a sprawling agricultural estate in southern Elwynn Forest owned by the Maclure family. While known for producing grapes and wine for the kingdom of Stormwind, the farmstead is equally infamous for an ongoing, bitter feud with the neighboring Stonefield family. Nestled in the lush hills of southern Elwynn Forest, the Maclure Vineyards should be a peaceful haven of winecraft and farming. Instead, everyday labor is overshadowed by a vicious, long-standing rivalry with the Stonefields just down the road. Accusations of theft and bad blood run deep between the households, keeping tempers flaring even as common troubles—like hungry prowling boars and encroaching kobolds—threaten both homesteads.

Maestra's Post. Maestra's Post is a small Alliance settlement in western Ashenvale, perched along the road northwest of Astranaar and south of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran. Guarded by night elven Sentinels and hosting a rare human presence in Kalimdor's ancient forest, it serves as a forward watch against encroaching threats. Positioned under the canopy of western Ashenvale, Maestra's Post consists of a slender night elven tower and an open lodge. It sits as an essential waypoint for travelers marching between the coast of Darkshore and the larger hub of Astranaar. Despite its tranquil elven architecture, the outpost stands perpetually on edge. The local Sentinels keep a wary eye on the surrounding wilderness, where corrupted furbolg stir and nearby Horde movements constantly threaten the Alliance's supply lines.

Mage Quarter. The Mage Quarter forms the arcane heart of Stormwind City, resting across the canals in the capital's southwestern corner. Towering over its cobblestone streets and esoteric specialty shops stands the Wizard's Sanctum, where the kingdom's conjurers hone their craft. Beneath the district's scholarly surface also lie shadowy recesses, harboring practitioners of far darker arts. Reachable by bridges crossing the canals from Cathedral Square or the Trade District, the Mage Quarter caters entirely to the mystical needs of the Alliance. Centered around the spire of the Wizard's Sanctum, human and allied spellcasters gather to study the weave of arcane magic and train apprentices. The surrounding streets are crowded with purveyors of tailoring cloth, reagents, alchemical supplies, and enchanted staves, creating an insular district dedicated to research and the defense of the kingdom.

Magic Quarter. The Magic Quarter is the northeastern district of the Undercity, serving as the center for Forsaken arcane study and dark spellcraft. Dominated by an ominous Temple of the Damned, the quarter houses practitioners of both the arcane and fel arts. Occupying the northeastern quadrant of the subterranean city, the Magic Quarter is where the Forsaken preserve their arcane heritage and delve into darker methodologies. The centerpiece of the district is a looming Temple of the Damned, an architectural relic of Scourge design that has been repurposed by the free-willed undead. Beneath its vaulted, shadowy ceilings, mages practice subtle manipulations of magical energies alongside warlocks communing with demonic entities, making the quarter the nexus of intellectual power and occult research in Lordaeron.

Magram Village. Magram Village is the settlement of the Magram centaur clan, situated among foul yellow pools in southeastern Desolace. It serves as the primary base for the Magram as they wage relentless war against their hated rivals, the Gelkis. Sprawled across islands and shores around stagnant, sulfurous pools in southeast Desolace, Magram Village is a rugged settlement cobbled together with crude wooden bridges and hide tents. The Magram centaur dwell here in constant vigilance against neighboring clans. Known for their sheer brutality and deep-seated animosity toward the southern Gelkis clan, the Magram are willing to tolerate outsiders only if those travelers prove their worth by slaughtering their Gelkis enemies.

Main Hall (Northshire). The Main Hall is the central entrance chamber of Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest. It serves as the primary crossroads connecting the abbey's grounds to its upper tower, the Hall of Arms, and the Library Wing. Here, newly recruited human adventurers report to receive their initial assignments in service of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Stepping through the grand archways of Northshire Abbey brings visitors directly into the Main Hall. As the building's central hub, it channels arriving trainees and clerical staff between the abbey's distinct wings: the martial Hall of Arms on one side, the scholastic Library Wing on the other, and the stairs rising into the abbey tower. The quiet sanctuary of the hall is tempered by the ongoing strife in the valley, as officers rally able-bodied newcomers to defend the kingdom's borders.

Maker's Terrace. The Maker's Terrace is a sprawling outdoor excavation site situated in the northern Badlands, directly fronting the entrance to the ancient titan vault of Uldaman. Travelers venturing south from Loch Modan must navigate its rugged perimeter, which is aggressively occupied by Dark Iron dwarves. The dig represents a contested threshold between the surface wastes and the titan mysteries entombed below. Sprawling across the northern bluffs of the Badlands, the Maker's Terrace serves as the exterior staging ground for the subterranean halls of Uldaman. Long before travelers delve into the subterranean ruins, they must contend with the sun-scorched earthworks, scaffolding, and stone trenches of this grand excavation. It sits right along the pass coming down from Loch Modan, making it the first landmark greeting any traveler daring to venture into the arid wastes. The Terrace buzzes with violent industry as rival factions seek a way into the ancient secrets buried beneath the rock.

Malaka'jin. Malaka'jin is a small Horde encampment nestled in the lower hills of the Stonetalon Mountains, just south of the Grimtotem Post. Inhabited primarily by Darkspear troll hunters, the settlement serves as a rustic waystation and hunting outpost for travelers ascending into the rugged peaks from the Barrens. Tucked away near the main path into the Stonetalon Mountains, Malaka'jin provides a welcome sanctuary for Horde wanderers venturing into contested heights. The village is home to a band of rugged troll hunters who eke out a living off the crags and scrublands. While living modestly, these hunters offer supplies, trade their fresh game to weary adventurers, and keep a wary eye on the hostile mountain wildlife and the belligerent Grimtotem tauren lurking further up the trails.

Malden's Orchard. Malden's Orchard is a ruined farmstead in northern Silverpine Forest, named after the human owner who fled during the Scourge invasion of Lordaeron. Long abandoned, its dark evergreen trees sit overgrown while vicious black worgs stalk the grounds. The orchard's crumbling cottage served as a temporary refuge for a stranded Forsaken scout cut off from his unit. Before the Third War, this homestead supplied fresh fruit to the towns of Lordaeron, tended by a farmer named Malden. When the Scourge tore through the kingdom, Malden abandoned his land to flee the plague. In the years since, the orchard has choked under the dark, encroaching mists of Silverpine Forest. The evergreen trees remain unpruned and their fruit rots ungathered on blighted boughs, leaving the plot entirely reclaimed by wild predators.

Mannoroc Coven. Mannoroc Coven is a demon-infested ruin in southern Desolace, named after the pit lord Mannoroth. Settled among ancient night elf architecture, it stands as the largest stronghold of the Burning Legion in central Kalimdor. Cultists of the Burning Blade maintain active summoning portals here, filling the ash-choked land with felhounds, succubi, and infernals. Situated south of Ghost Walker Post and east of Shadowprey Village, Mannoroc Coven blankets the ancient night elf ruins in an oppressive, fel-tainted pall. The coven is commanded on the ground by Lord Azrethoc, alongside the Burning Blade warlock Jugkar Grim'rod. Together, they harness active summoning portals to pull demonic reinforcements straight into Kalimdor, including doomguards, infernals, and felhounds. Even as Horde-aligned travelers attempt to sever these links using relics like the Hand of Iruxos, new rifts continue to tear open through the scarred earth.

Manor Mistmantle. Manor Mistmantle is a decaying estate nestled in the shadowed hills of northeastern Duskwood, north of Darkshire. Once a proper family homestead, it has fallen into ruin and horror, crawling with undead ghouls bound to its infamous master. Located west of Beggar's Haunt, Manor Mistmantle stands as a grim monument to murder and madness. The grounds are choked with decay and prowled by vicious ghouls who defend the ruined structure. Amidst the rot and withered vegetation, the only sign of living beauty on the entire property is a solitary, sorrowful blossom growing in the untended garden: the flower known as the Tear of Tilloa.

Mardenholde Keep. Mardenholde Keep is the imposing stone citadel overlooking Hearthglen in the northern reaches of the Western Plaguelands. Once the ancestral seat of Lord Tirion Fordring, it now serves as the regional command center for the fanatical Scarlet Crusade under the rule of his son, Highlord Taelan Fordring. Built as the administrative heart of the Hearthglen principality, Mardenholde Keep was long celebrated by the people of Lordaeron for having never breached during the Second War. From its council chambers, Lord Tirion Fordring governed the surrounding vales alongside his trusted advisors, maintaining peace until his controversial trial and exile for defending the orc Eitrigg. Following Tirion's fall, governance fell to his ambitious apprentice Barthilas and eventually passed to Tirion's son, Taelan, who inherited his father's domain on the eve of Lordaeron's destruction.

Marris Stead. Perched on a ridge in the southwestern Eastern Plaguelands, the Marris Stead was once a peaceful Lordaeron homestead. Following the devastation of the Third War, it now serves as the lonely, heavily defended redoubt of Nathanos Blightcaller, Champion of the Forsaken.

Marshal's Refuge. Marshal's Refuge is a precarious, neutral haven tucked into the northern cliffs of Un'Goro Crater. Established by Williden Marshal and his expedition party, it serves as an emergency redoubt after the basin's primeval beasts routed their lower camps. When Williden and Hol'anyee Marshal led their expedition into Un'Goro Crater, they drastically underestimated the ferocity of its prehistoric denizens. After their initial base camps were repeatedly overrun by rampaging beasts, the battered survivors scrambled up into the cavernous northern cliffside to escape slaughter. Re-established as Marshal's Refuge, the camp clings high above the jungle floor, offering the only stable resting ground, basic supplies, and flight masters for weary explorers in the northern crater.

Marshlands. The Marshlands is a sprawling, sodden marsh occupying the southeastern reach of Un'Goro Crater. Sitting directly at the base of the winding ramp down from Tanaris, it is often the first wilderness newcomers witness upon entering the primeval basin. Descending the steep trail from the arid expanse of Tanaris brings travelers directly into the humid mire of the Marshlands. Navigating anywhere else along the sheer crater rim invites a lethal fall, making this treacherous swath of wetlands the primary threshold into Un'Goro. Dense canopies, standing water, and mud conceal abundant packs of fierce raptors, including venomous varieties that stalk the reeds. Amid the damp clearings, explorers can find Blue Power Crystals scattered across the earth, unique to this quarter of the crater.

Mast Room. The Mast Room is a cavernous subterranean lumber mill nestled deep within the Deadmines. Overseen by the goblin taskmaster Sneed and his woodcarvers, this chamber processes timber stripped from Westfall to construct Edwin VanCleef's secret juggernaut.

Master's Cellar. The Master's Cellar is a sprawling subterranean complex situated beneath the ruined settlement south of Karazhan in Deadwind Pass. Once serving Medivh's estate as wine cellars and storage vaults, it has descended into a haunted ruin teeming with the restless spectres of former servants and caretakers. Just south of the imposing tower of Karazhan lie the ruined remnants of a hamlet that once housed the servants, groundskeepers, and attendants who maintained Medivh's estate. Beneath these crumbled homes sits the Master's Cellar. Accessible through two separate entrances in the surface ruins, the complex expands far underground. One doorway opens into an extensive vaulted wine cellar, while the other descends through collapsed stonework into deep natural caverns. Whatever dark demise befell Karazhan and its master swallowed this basement as well, leaving the unliving remnants of caretakers, wailing spectres, and damned souls trapped in endless servitude.

Master's Glaive. The Master's Glaive is an ancient, unsettling landmark tucked into southwestern Darkshore where a colossal adamantine weapon stands impaled in a massive petrified skull. Long revered by local night elves as a sacred mystery, the site now swarms with Twilight's Hammer cultists drawn to the lingering malevolence of an ancient entity. Rising out of the Darkshore earth, the Master's Glaive is a massive adamantine blade buried deep in a colossal petrified skull. No record names the creature that died here or the hand that drove the blade home. Onu, the Ancient of Lore, says only that an old, old lord of the earth fell on this spot, and the night elves long believed that only the titans could have wielded so gigantic a weapon. Today, the impaled monolith stands as a stark, petrified monument to that forgotten struggle.

Maul (subzone). The Maul is a sunken fighting arena situated in the Broken Commons outside the ruins of Dire Maul in Feralas. Formerly a grand venue of ancient elven Eldre'Thalas, the pit is now an uncontrolled bloodsport ring where wanderers fight for glory or survival against fierce beasts and rival champions. Carved deep into the stone of the Broken Commons, the Maul once served the Highborne of Eldre'Thalas as a theater or ceremonial arena. Following the Sundering and the subsequent occupation by the Gordok ogres, the pit devolved into a raw colosseum. Like the notorious Gurubashi Arena in distant Stranglethorn Vale, entering the sands of the Maul suspends all allegiances, casting combatants into a lawless free-for-all where faction lines dissolve and survival depends purely on martial strength.

Mazthoril. Mazthoril is a massive, frostbitten cavern in central Winterspring that serves as the primary redoubt for the blue dragonflight in northern Kalimdor. Heavily guarded by dragonkin, spell-wielding wyrms, and arcane sentries, its winding ice tunnels conceal powerful magic and lead to the aerie of the reclusive blue matriarch Haleh. Carved into the frozen mountains just south of Everlook, Mazthoril houses an extensive brood answering to the Spell-Weaver, Malygos. The cavern and its surrounding crags are patrolled by vigilant dragonkin including Spellmaw, Azurous, and General Colbatann, while elite guardians watch the inner caverns. Intruders who wander into Mazthoril face dragonspawn thoroughly attuned to raw arcane energy, making any venture inside perilous without serious preparation.

Menethil Bay. Menethil Bay is the sheltered body of water along the western coast of the Wetlands, nestled between Menethil Harbor and the steep northern cliffs of Dun Morogh. Opening outward into the wider Baradin Bay, these waters are home to aggressive crocolisks and the remains of sunken vessels. It serves as the primary maritime approach for Alliance traffic journeying between the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. Part of the larger Baradin Bay along the Great Sea, Menethil Bay forms a natural inlet bordered by Menethil Harbor to the north, Black Channel Marsh to the east, and the towering coastal bluffs of Dun Morogh to the south. Its shallow margins and marshy shores crawl with crocolisks of various ages and sizes, making the shallows treacherous for unguided travelers even though the bay serves as the lifeblood of Alliance maritime travel. Near the mouth of the bay lies the ruined wreckage of the Flying Osprey, a silent reminder of the dangers lurking beneath the surface.

Menethil Harbor. Menethil Harbor is a heavily fortified dwarven port town perched on an island off the western shore of the Wetlands. Named after King Terenas Menethil II, it acts as the primary maritime lifeline connecting the Eastern Kingdoms to the distant shores of Kalimdor. Sheltered behind massive stone battlements and the sturdy towers of Menethil Keep, it is a bustling hub for merchants, off-duty soldiers, and salty adventurers. Named in tribute to King Terenas Menethil II of Lordaeron, Menethil Harbor stands as a premier Alliance haven on the Wetlands coast. Despite its remote marshland setting, it remains a heavily defended bastion, reinforced by massive walls, a single bridged causeway, and the four stone watchtowers of Menethil Keep.

Menethil Keep. Menethil Keep is the stone stronghold dominating the skyline of Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Marked by four sturdy watchtowers, it serves as the administrative heart and defensive bastion of the Alliance port, housing the local militia commander, Captain Stoutfist. Rising above the wooden docks and soggy marshes of the Wetlands, Menethil Keep is the central military strongpoint of Menethil Harbor. With four stone watchtowers gazing out over the town and the bay, the fortress offers a commanding view against seaward raiders, renegades, and the encroaching swamp beasts. Inside, Captain Stoutfist oversees the defense of the port, directing the town militia and organizing patrols to safeguard Alliance interests throughout the region.

Merchant Coast. The Merchant Coast is the stretch of eastern shoreline in the Barrens bordering the Great Sea. Dominated by the bustling goblin port of Ratchet, the coast derives its name from lucrative sea trade, though it remains constantly contested by pirates. Running along the eastern edge of the Barrens, the Merchant Coast serves as a vital maritime artery connecting central Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms and Theramore. Its name honors the industrious goblin traders of the Steamwheedle Cartel, whose neutral port of Ratchet handles cargo for anyone with coin. However, the open sea lanes attract more than merchant vessels: Southsea Freebooters prowl the sands and nearby waters, preying on merchant ships and setting up illicit operations along the beaches.

Military Ward. The Military Ward serves as the martial heart of Ironforge, housing the city's command infrastructure, weapons masters, and barracks. Marked by bold red banners, it is where dwarven soldiers, hunters, and siege engineers train alongside mechanized siege engines and flying machines. Situated within the northern perimeter of the mountain fortress, the Military Ward concentrates Ironforge's defensive forces into a bustling staging ground. The central complex, the Hall of Arms, accommodates warrior and hunter trainers, battlemasters, and hangars housing dwarven flying machines and steam tanks. Surrounding the drill squares and training dummies are supply outlets such as Craghelm's Plate and Chain, Goldfury's Hunting Supplies, and Timberline Arms, making the ward the primary staging point for mountaineers and city defenders.

Mirage Flats. Mirage Flats is a barren, sun-scorched expanse nestled in the central wastes of the Badlands. Lying east of Dustbelch Grotto, this dry plateau is notorious for shimmering heat hazes and hungry predators. Situated east of Dustbelch Grotto, the Mirage Flats present travelers with an unforgiving stretch of cracked red dirt and shimmering heat waves that give the plain its name. Few civilized souls linger here; instead, the open flats are dominated by opportunistic scavengers and lethal beasts. Flocks of giant buzzards circle lazily on hot thermals above, watching for the leavings of ferocious ridge stalkers and pack-hunting crag coyotes that scour the brush for easy prey.

Mirage Raceway. The Mirage Raceway is an impromptu engineering proving ground situated in the shimmering salt flats of Thousand Needles. Founded on the heated rivalry between goblin tinkerer Pozzik and gnome engineer Fizzle Brassbolts, it pits high-speed rocket cars against one another across the baked earth. The track serves as a neutral gathering place where members of both the Alliance and Horde come to wager, tinker, and cheer on their favored machines. Sprawled across the vast white desert floor of the Shimmering Flats, the Mirage Raceway was born out of an unrelenting grudge match between two master tinkerers: the goblin Pozzik and the gnome Fizzle Brassbolts. Determined to settle once and for all whose race possesses superior technical ingenuity, the two constructed custom rocket-powered drag cars and recruited rival crews to pit them against each other in daily high-velocity showdowns. The relentless competition has turned the barren flats into a bustling hub of invention, sabotage, and testing as each crew desperately looks for any mechanical advantage.

Mirkfallon Lake. Mirkfallon Lake sits in a central highland basin in the Stonetalon Mountains, nestled beneath the sheer cliffs of Windshear Crag. Its waters and surrounding banks teem with native wildlife, including aggressive slimes, roaming thunder lizards, and descending wyverns. Positioned at the geographic center of the Stonetalon range, Mirkfallon Lake rests between the mountain passes leading south toward the Webwinder Path and north toward Stonetalon Peak. Fed by highland runoff, the lake offers a fertile oasis amidst the craggy peaks, drawing thunder lizards down to drink and wyverns from their roosts high above. The waters are also inhabited by strange, bubbling slimes, turning an otherwise serene mountain tarn into a hazardous crossing for lone travelers.

Mirror Lake. Mirror Lake is a picturesque body of water tucked into northwestern Elwynn Forest near an orchard. Fed by a gentle waterfall beneath the cliffs of Stormwind, its tranquil surface belies the dangers lurking on its shores, from prowling Defias bandits to strange disruptions in the local ley lines. Situated beneath the towering ramparts of Stormwind City, Mirror Lake ought to be a peaceful retreat for fishermen and weary travelers. Instead, brigands of the Defias Brotherhood stalk the surrounding orchards, making any prolonged stay perilous for passing locals. Worse still, mystical disturbances across Azeroth have begun warping the natural channels of arcane energy throughout the forest. The mages of the Wizard's Sanctum keep a cautious eye on the lake, sending practitioners to sample its currents and ensure that downstream communities are not poisoned by chaotic arcane runoff.

Mirror Lake Orchard. Mirror Lake Orchard is a quiet grove and cottage nestled on the southern banks of Mirror Lake in western Elwynn Forest. Once a peaceful homestead near Thunder Falls, it has fallen into the hands of Defias bandits who exploit the countryside while Stormwind's guards look elsewhere. Tucked away near the cascading waters of Thunder Falls, Mirror Lake Orchard was once a productive farmstead benefiting from the clean waters of Mirror Lake. Today, the peaceful cottage sits overrun, claimed by opportunistic thieves and brigands flying the colors of the Defias Brotherhood. With the kingdom's military stretched thin and King Varian Wrynn missing, rural properties like this orchard have become easy pickings for outlaws looking to secure hideouts across the Elwynn countryside.

Mist's Edge. Mist's Edge is the long, windswept coastline stretching north from Auberdine along western Darkshore. Shrouded in damp ocean fog, these gray beaches are littered with shipwrecks, colossal sea creature remains, and roving packs of crabs and murlocs. Running along the western edge of Darkshore, Mist's Edge is defined by damp sands, rocky tidepools, and perpetual coastal fog. The beach is a graveyard of the sea, littered with decaying sea behemoths, drift timber, and the shattered ribs of wrecked vessels. While seemingly barren, the coastline teems with shoreline scavengers, notably aggressive crabs and territorial murloc tribes that nest in the surf.

Misty Pine Refuge. Misty Pine Refuge is a small outpost building of the Argent Dawn tucked amidst the frigid snows of central Dun Morogh. Situated amid the windswept hills of Dun Morogh, Misty Pine Refuge is an unassuming outpost of the Argent Dawn in the dwarven realm. While the surrounding crags are patrolled by Ironforge mountaineers, the refuge is home to Father Gavin, the order's lone agent here, who offers a quiet hearth amid the bitter elements and the perils that threaten the mountain roads.

Misty Reed Post. Misty Reed Post is a rugged Horde encampment situated between Stagalbog and the Misty Reed Strand in the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Established as a frontline watch under the authority of Stonard, it serves to monitor the dangerous wetlands and the treacherous coastline. Tucked away in the humid gloom between the Stagalbog and the eastern shore, Misty Reed Post is little more than a spartan camp under Stonard's banner. It is manned by a handful of Stonard hunters, a shaman, Katar, and Tok'Kar, who oversees the watch. Conditions are rough, offering no fortified shelter from the marsh's hostile wildlife and lingering damp. Tok'Kar harbors quiet ambitions that the Horde command in Stonard will one day reinforce the position with a sturdy orcish burrow or watchtower, though for now, the scouts must hold the marsh with tents, campfire smoke, and sharpened steel.

Misty Reed Strand. The Misty Reed Strand is the fog-shrouded, desolate eastern coastline of the Swamp of Sorrows. Lined with jagged rocks, washed-up wreckage, and creeping swamp mist, it is home to aggressive crabs, crocolisks, and coastal murloc tribes. Travelers venturing down to the surf often find themselves contending with the local wildlife for whatever resources wash ashore. Stretching along the entire eastern border of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Misty Reed Strand forms a damp barrier between the deep mire and the Great Sea. Heavy mists constantly roll in off the water, obscuring vision and muffling the cries of native wildlife. The beaches are littered with sea debris, driftwood, and decaying vegetation washed out from the bog inland. Because of its remote position and harsh climate, no formal permanent settlements hold the shoreline, leaving the sands to aggressive crustaceans, stalking crocolisks, and territorial murlocs who violently defend their foraging grounds.

Misty Shore. Misty Shore is the quiet lakeshore of the Alterac Mountains, skirting the eastern shore of Lordamere Lake. Stretching between Dandred's Fold and the perimeter of Dalaran, it offers wide, foggy views of the Dawning Isles and the sinister silhouette of Fenris Keep. Running along Lordamere Lake, the Misty Shore stretches between Dandred's Fold and Dalaran. Thick, damp air regularly drifts off the lake, obscuring snapping turtles and the occasional zealous fanatic who wanders down from regional strongholds.

Misty Valley. Tucked away in the northwestern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Misty Valley is a shadowed, fog-drenched hollow north of the pass into Deadwind. The secluded basin is overrun by primordial swamp beasts, wandering swampwalkers, and tangled horrors. Deep in its rearmost cave dwells the colossal and terrifying Mire Lord. Nestled beneath the high cliffs separating the Swamp of Sorrows from Deadwind Pass, the Misty Valley is perpetually choked with thick marsh vapor. Unlike the open wetlands to the east, this isolated pocket is dense with colossal marsh elementals, including looming swampwalkers, ancient swampwalker elders, and creeping tangled horrors. At the far end of the misty gorge lies a cavern that serves as the lair of the Mire Lord, one of the most formidable natural threats haunting the bog.

Mizjah Ruins. The Mizjah Ruins are ancient stone remains nestled in northern Stranglethorn Vale, situated just southeast of Grom'gol Base Camp. Long abandoned by their original troll architects, the crumbling structures have been seized by the brute-strength Mosh'Ogg ogres. From this vantage, the ogres launch disruptive ambushes against passing supply caravans traveling toward the Swamp of Sorrows. Like many of the ancient stone ruins scattered throughout Stranglethorn Vale, the Mizjah Ruins were built by the Gurubashi Empire long before modern empires rose. Today, the moss-choked arches and cracked flagstones are occupied by the Mosh'Ogg clan, primarily brute warriors and crude witch doctors. Far from keeping to their stolen perimeter, these ogres routinely raid nearby supply convoys bound for the Horde settlement of Stonard, transforming ancient history into a persistent, bloody thorn in the side of Grom'gol's commanders.

Mo'grosh Stronghold. Mo'grosh Stronghold is a fortified den of ogres dug into the northeastern hills of Loch Modan. Nestled among ancient, weathered ruins, these brutal giants pose a constant threat to the dwarven settlements below. Tucked away in the crags of northeastern Loch Modan, Mo'grosh Stronghold serves as the primary base for the Mo'grosh clan of ogres in the region. The brute forces lurking within the caves and outer camps raid traveling dwarven supply caravans and present an enduring danger to the peace of Thelsamar. The rugged stonework scattered around the camp suggests the site once belonged to an older settlement, before the lumbering ogres claimed the territory and raised their distinctive mounds.

Molsen Farm. Molsen Farm is an abandoned homestead located in the breadbasket region of Westfall. Once a fertile piece of farmland feeding Stormwind, it has fallen into ruin following the rise of the Defias Brotherhood and the prowling mechanical harvest golems left in their wake. Like many homesteads across Westfall, Molsen Farm stands as a casualty of the kingdom's neglect and criminal uprising. When the Defias Brotherhood took control of the countryside, the resident farmers were driven out or worse, abandoning their crops and buildings. Now, instead of laborers gathering grain, hostile mechanical Harvest Watchers and wandering outlaws scour the untended fields, making the farm a hazard to anyone traveling through the province.

Moon Horror Den. Moon Horror Den is a secluded, frost-rimed cave located just northeast of the goblin trading post of Everlook in Winterspring. Tucked against the jagged mountainside, the cavern serves as a nesting hollow for ferocious raging owlbeasts. Travelers must take care when venturing near its icy mouth, as these territorial wildkin fiercely defend their shelter. Situated only a short trek northeast from Everlook's guarded gates, the Moon Horror Den cuts deep into the mountain rock. The cave is home to powerful raging owlbeasts—formidable wildkin known for their brute strength and feral disposition in the harsh snows of Winterspring. Although geographically close to the furbolg settlement of Winterfall Village to the south, the sheer mountain face creates an impassable natural barrier, ensuring the den remains an isolated refuge for the wildkin rather than a corridor of travel.

Moonbrook. Once a bustling agricultural hub and mining town in southwestern Westfall, Moonbrook now stands as a lawless ghost town. The town has been completely overrun by the Defias Brotherhood, who use it as a fortified screen to hide their subterranean headquarters in the Deadmines. Before the First War, Moonbrook was a vital community at the center of Westfall's breadbasket, supporting local farming families and the lucrative gold shafts of the Deadmines. Though it was razed by the Old Horde and painstakingly rebuilt after the Second War, its peace did not last. Neglected by the House of Nobles in Stormwind and stripped of military protection, the settlement could not resist the vengeful Stonemasons Guild when they fled into the wilderness. Bandits drove out the honest homesteaders, forcing citizens and teachers alike to flee toward Sentinel Hill and Elwynn Forest.

Moonbrook Schoolhouse. Standing in the northwestern corner of Moonbrook, the Schoolhouse is a prominent building resembling a town hall with a small graveyard behind it. Originally erected to educate local children under headmaster Stalvan Mistmantle, it now stands derelict amidst the Defias occupation of Westfall. Before Moonbrook fell to ruin and bandits, the community invested in the education of its youth by raising this grand schoolhouse. After Stalvan Mistmantle began tutoring local children, the mayor commissioned him to run a school. In those brighter days, the hall bustled with students rather than thieves, standing as proof of Moonbrook's former prosperity. Now, the schoolhouse lies abandoned to the elements and infested with outlaws, while the weathered headstones of its rear cemetery silently oversee Westfall's steady decay.

Moonshrine Ruins. The Moonshrine Ruins are a flooded expanse of ancient night elven architecture deep within Blackfathom Deeps. Once dedicated to the worship of Elune, these crumbling halls have been desecrated and seized by the Twilight's Hammer cult. Past the cavernous Pool of Ask'ar lies the Moonshrine Ruins, a somber testament to the night elves' ancient past along the Ashenvale coast. These partially submerged halls once rang with chants honoring the Moon Goddess Elune, but the Great Sundering shattered the temple and drowned its lower levels in sea water. Today, the murky waters churn with feral aquatic beasts, from aggressive crabs to serpentine threshadons, while the Twilight's Hammer cult maintains an active presence throughout the stones, bent on dark rituals that mock the shrine's sacred origin.

Moonshrine Sanctum. Moonshrine Sanctum is an ancient elven shrine deep within Blackfathom Deeps, now serving as the inner redoubt for the Twilight's Hammer cult. Presided over by Twilight Lord Kelris, the chamber houses a pristine monument to Queen Azshara and directly guards the sealed entrance to Aku'mai's lair. Situated just beyond the flooded Moonshrine Ruins, the Moonshrine Sanctum represents the central hub of cultist activity inside Blackfathom Deeps. Though originally built millennia ago by night elves to honor the moon and their rulers, the hall is now defiled by the Twilight's Hammer. Interestingly, the cultists have carefully maintained the towering effigy of Queen Azshara, seemingly untroubled by its subject. Under the watchful gaze of Twilight Lord Kelris, dark rituals are chanted day and night beneath the cavernous stone ceiling.

Moonspray. The Moonspray is an Alliance transport vessel belonging to the Kaldorei Fleet. It provides essential maritime passage across the waters separating mainland Kalimdor from the great World Tree, Teldrassil. The Moonspray serves as an indispensable lifeline between the docks of Auberdine on Darkshore's coast and Rut'theran Village at the root of Teldrassil. Traversing the Veiled Sea, the transport carries adventurers, couriers, and vital provisions between the isolated night elf sanctuary in the crown of the World Tree and the ancient mainland of Kalimdor.

Moonwell (Ashenvale). This secluded shrine, known to the night elves as the Moonwell of Purity, rests in central Ashenvale east of Iris Lake and west of Raynewood Retreat. Its blessed waters channel the grace of Elune to nourish the ancient forest and cleanse creeping foulness from the land. Alliance travelers following Raene Wolfrunner's research often seek out Shael'dryn, who keeps watch beside its tranquil basin. Tucked away beneath the canopy of central Ashenvale, this moonwell serves as a spiritual anchor for the kaldorei. Its luminescent waters tap into nature's latent magic and the light of the Moon Goddess. As the surrounding forest suffers from satyr corruption, fel taint, and logging incursions, pure shrines like this one become vital lifelines for those trying to heal the woods.

Mor'shan Rampart. The Mor'shan Rampart is a heavily fortified Horde barricade positioned at the northern border of the Barrens, guarding the entrance to Ashenvale. Constructed primarily by the Warsong clan, it shields Horde territory from night elf counterattacks while serving as a staging ground for incursions deeper into the forest. Standing at the northern terminus of the Gold Road, the Mor'shan Rampart marks the transition between the arid plains of the Barrens and the ancient canopies of Ashenvale. Built from heavy timber, defensive palisades, and fortified watchtowers, this bulwark was raised to stem the retaliatory strikes of night elven forces outraged by the Horde's logging operations. It acts both as a shield securing the northern gate to Kalimdor's interior and as a forward staging post for raiding parties pushing north toward Astranaar.

Morgan's Plot. Morgan's Plot is a desolate burial ground and crumbling chapel tucked away just behind the tower of Karazhan in Deadwind Pass. Dominated by restless undead and brooding silence, it holds the forgotten crypts and final resting places of those once tied to Medivh's domain. Nestled against the sheer rocky slopes directly behind Karazhan, Morgan's Plot is a sorrowful, overgrown cemetery centered on a ruined chapel and underground crypts. Long before the land decayed into Deadwind Pass, the estate served the burial needs of the tower's inhabitants and nearby grounds. Following the downfall of the Last Guardian, Medivh, dark energies seeped into the earth, driving away all normalcy. Today, restless unliving wander the chapel grounds, haunting the headstones of servants and historic figures alike.

Morgan's Vigil. Morgan's Vigil is a ruined Alliance redoubt nestled in the southeastern heights of the Burning Steppes. Once a small village, its charred homes and shattered wizard's tower now serve as an austere forward camp for scouts watching the passes to Blackrock Mountain. It remains the sole Alliance foothold in an ash-choked land dominated by Dark Iron dwarves and Blackrock orcs. Perched upon high stone overlooking the fiery wastes, Morgan's Vigil was once a modest settlement before the horrors of the Burning Steppes overran it. Today, charred timbers and the cracked shell of a ruined mage tower stand as grim reminders of the onslaught. The remaining defenders make do beneath rough canvas tents pitched amid the soot. Despite the ruin, the camp retains a gryphon roost, offering an unbroken aerial link back across the mountains to Stormwind City. It serves as a desperately needed haven where scouts, marshals, and passing adventurers catch their breath away from the marauding warbands below.

Morlos'Aran. Morlos'Aran is an ancient night elf ruin nestled in the southern reaches of Felwood. Once a proud and thriving settlement before the Great Sundering, it now stands as a grim monument to a lost golden age, drowned under the demonic blight that plagues the surrounding forest. Ten thousand years ago, prior to the Sundering, Morlos'Aran was a grand urban center of the ancient kaldorei civilization. Much like sister settlements such as Ameth'Aran, Bashal'Aran, and Ordil'Aran across northern Kalimdor, its marble arches and moonlit plazas bustled with elven life and arcana. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the city broke, leaving only shattered colonnades behind as monuments to their civilization's zenith.

Klaven's Tower. Klaven's Tower, also called the Defias Tower, is a fortified watchtower standing near the river in southeastern Westfall. Commanded by the rogue Klaven Mortwake, it serves as a critical waypoint for smuggling stolen goods across kingdom borders. Perched on the borderlands north of the Dagger Hills, Klaven's Tower is a vital hub for Defias Brotherhood operations in southern Westfall. Together with Jerod's Landing across the river in Elwynn Forest, the site acts as a receiving post and staging ground for contraband plundered from the Redridge Mountains. Its commanding vantage over the waterways allows the Brotherhood to slip supplies past Kingdom patrols, shielding their logistical network from the crown's eyes.

Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound. The Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound is a fortified cavern complex in northern Stranglethorn Vale, situated just south of the ruins of Zul'Gurub. It serves as the primary stronghold for the brute Mosh'Ogg tribe in the jungle, dominated by their ruthless ogre mage chieftain, Mai'Zoth. Carved into the rugged jungle ridges south of Zul'Gurub, the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound swarms with brutish Mosh'Ogg maulers, shamans, and warmongers. The ogres seized the cavernous network as an ideal redoubt against hostile jungle trolls and prowling beasts.

Mosshide Fen. Mosshide Fen is a swampy, treacherous tract in the eastern Wetlands overrun by the Mosshide gnoll tribe. Dotted with primitive encampments, it is one of the most perilous regions for travelers venturing off the main trade roads. Sprawling across the murky eastern reaches of the Wetlands, Mosshide Fen serves as the primary domain of the aggressive Mosshide gnolls. The swamp here is dense and tangled, dotted with rough lean-tos and bone-strewn camps. Under the vicious command of pack leaders like Gnawbone, the gnolls fiercely guard their muddy claims, readily ambushing and devouring any travelers, scouts, or prospectors foolish enough to wander into their hunting grounds.

Mystic Ward. The Mystic Ward is the northwestern district of Ironforge, serving as the dwarven capital's quiet sanctuary for spiritual devotion and arcane study. Distinguishable by its cool, pale blue banners and quiet halls, it stands in stark contrast to the clanging anvils of the nearby Great Forge. Its grandest structure, the Hall of Mysteries, gathers priests, paladins, and mages beneath cavernous stone arches. While dwarves are famed across Azeroth for their prowess at the forge and on the battlefield, the Mystic Ward represents the kingdom's quieter intellectual and spiritual pursuits. Marked by pale blue heraldry, this cavernous quarter connects the bustling Commons to the Forlorn Cavern and the Great Forge. Within its reaches, merchants supply scholars and spellweavers with regalia, scrolls, and alchemical reagents from shops like The Fighting Wizard and Maeva's Mystical Apparel. Dominating the district is the majestic Hall of Mysteries, where the holy disciplines of the Holy Light intersect with the practiced arts of arcane magic, offering guidance to those who wield unseen powers in defense of the Alliance.

Mystral Lake. Mystral Lake is the largest body of water in Ashenvale, resting in the south-central forest just below Silverwind Refuge. Its deep waters draw travelers from both the Alliance and the Horde. Spanning a vast expanse south of Silverwind Refuge and east of Talondeep Vale, Mystral Lake is the largest lake in Ashenvale. The night elves keep watch over it from their outpost at Silverwind Refuge on its northern shore, and travelers from both the Horde and the Alliance frequently find their journeys pulling them to its banks.

Nat's Landing. Nat's Landing is a modest fishing outpost nestled along the shores of Dustwallow Bay in Dustwallow Marsh. It serves as the personal camp and retreat of Nat Pagle, widely regarded as the most famous angler on Azeroth. Adventurers from across the world seek out this humble dock to hone their mastery of the fishing craft. Tucked away southwest of Theramore Isle along the murky waters of Dustwallow Bay, Nat's Landing is little more than a weathered campsite. It consists of a simple canvas tent, drying racks heavy with the day's catch, extra tackle hung from trees, and a rickety wooden pier jutting into the bay. Despite the mists and hazards of the swamp, this quiet patch of shoreline provides the legendary angler Nat Pagle with a solitary place to cast his line and enjoy a quiet drink away from civilization's clamor.

Nek'mani Wellspring. Perched high in the cliffs above the Southern Savage Coast, the Nek'mani Wellspring holds a fountain of remarkably pure holy water. It is renowned as the only pristine source of fresh water found south of Duskwood. However, this sacred site has recently been overrun by hostile naga explorers who jealously guard its flow. The Nek'mani Wellspring sits tucked away in the jagged coastal heights of western Stranglethorn Vale. Dispensing the only untainted freshwater south of Duskwood, the spring is hailed by various scholars and pilgrims as holy. Because differing cultures and traditions each claim its divine waters were blessed uniquely for their own kind, it remains a subject of intense theological fascination. Despite its spiritual renown, peaceful contemplation here is impossible: a vicious contingent of naga has recently seized the basin and guards the waters against all intruders.

Nesingwary's Expedition. Nesingwary's Expedition is a rustic hunting encampment situated in northern Stranglethorn Vale, just north of Lake Nazferiti. Established by the famed dwarven marksman Hemet Nesingwary, the outpost serves as a staging ground for hunters seeking to test their mettle against the jungle's fiercest predators. Tucked alongside the river north of Lake Nazferiti, this remote encampment is a bustling haven for big game hunters, trackers, and marksmen. Hemet Nesingwary established the camp to stalk the legendary beasts of Stranglethorn Vale, surrounded by seasoned peers like Sir S. J. Erlgadin, Ajeck Rouack, and Barnil Stonepot. Guarded by hired marksmen and supplied by neutral vendors, the camp welcomes anyone capable of handling a rifle or bow, regardless of their allegiances, uniting them under the singular pursuit of tracking down the deadliest predators the jungle has to offer.

Nethander Stead. Nethander Stead is an abandoned farmstead lying along the road just east of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Once a working human farm, it has fallen into ruin and is completely overrun by the Mudsnout gnoll pack. The fields are overgrown with giant white mushrooms known as Mudsnout Blossoms, attracting the interest of Forsaken alchemists.
