Situated within sight of Southshore's eastern borders, Nethander Stead was once an active piece of the region's agricultural belt. Like much of the eastern foothills, the farm was abandoned as regional security eroded and wild packs moved in. Today, it serves as the sole enclave of the Mudsnout gnolls in the foothills. The brutes dwell among the ruined fences and outbuildings, aggressively driving off any travelers who wander too close to their claimed territory.

Nethergarde Keep. Nethergarde Keep is a fortified Alliance stronghold perched high upon the bluffs along the road entering the Blasted Lands. Raised by the Alliance after the Second War, it stands as a vigilant sentinel over the dormant Dark Portal and the chaotic energies bleeding across the red wastes. Today, mages and garrisons supported by Stormwind continue their lonely vigil against demons and lingering corruption. Following the destruction of the Dark Portal at the end of the Second War, Archmage Khadgar and the leaders of the Alliance of Lordaeron recognized that Azeroth could never again leave the rift unguarded. Builders labored to raise towering bastions, barracks, and mage spires along the canyon pass into the Blasted Lands. Staffed by Kirin Tor sorcerers, its dual purpose was to keep constant watch on the shattered gateway and weave wards preventing the demonic blight of the scorched landscape from creeping northward into the human kingdoms.

Night Run. Night Run is a small, secluded satyr outpost perched atop a cliff-ringed bluff in east-central Ashenvale. Inhabited by the demonic Felmusk satyr, it serves as a corrupted encampment harboring dark soul magic within ancient elven ruins. Night Run is the smallest and most isolated of Ashenvale's three major satyr strongholds, alongside Xavian and Satyrnaar. Sheltered among crumbling elven stonework and broken pillars, the settlement juts outward on a high ridge bounded by steep, impassable cliffs. Reaching it requires a circuitous trek along the Falfarren River near the waters of Xavian or navigating a precarious northern ledge above Raynewood Retreat. Despite its modest size, the enclave poses a severe danger: the Felmusk satyr who dwell here work in concert with the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand, anchoring twisted soulgems to pool demonic essence within the forest.

Night Web's Hollow. Night Web's Hollow is a sunken vale and abandoned gold mine located just northwest of Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. Heavily overrun with arachnids, it serves as a testing ground for freshly awakened Forsaken sent to cull the vermin and prove their combat readiness. Tucked away in the northern hills of Deathknell, Night Web's Hollow was once an ordinary human gold mine before the plague swept through Lordaeron. In the aftermath of the kingdom's fall, the shafts were entirely abandoned to nature. Today, thick strands of webbing shroud the rock walls and suffocating shadows conceal a thriving colony of aggressive night web spiders. Freshly raised Forsaken are routinely dispatched into the hollow and its subterranean tunnels to cull the young and adult spiders so the Forsaken can regain access to the mine's gold.

Nighthaven. Nighthaven is a secluded settlement resting on the northern shores of Lake Elune'ara in Moonglade. Serving as the heart of the Cenarion Circle, it is a haven where night elf and tauren druids study together in peace beyond the factional wars of Azeroth. Built with traditional night elf architecture along the calm shores of Lake Elune'ara, Nighthaven is a tranquil retreat largely secluded from the outside world. Here, moonwells cast a gentle glow over groves and halls dedicated to preserving the natural balance. As the primary enclave of the Cenarion Circle, it provides trainers, herbalists, and specialized suppliers for druidic initiates. The settlement maintains a strict neutrality, welcoming practitioners regardless of whether their home loyalties lie with the Alliance or the Horde.

Nightmare Vale. Nightmare Vale is a shadowed hollow nestled in southwestern Tirisfal Glades, just west of the Crusader's Outpost. Once a lush forest haven, its trees have withered under the blight, and vicious predators now roam among the twisted trunks. Before the Third War, this valley was a verdant part of the Tirisfal countryside, filled with songbirds and standard woodland game. In the wake of the Scourge's plague, the vegetation has blackened and rotted away. Ravenous darkhounds and massive vampire bats have devoured the native wildlife, turning the hollow into a grim haven for scavengers and beasts of prey.

Nightsong Woods. Nightsong Woods forms the embattled eastern expanse of Ashenvale, reaching from Raynewood Retreat toward the borders of Azshara. It serves as the primary battleground between the night elves defending their sacred forest and the Warsong clan harvesting lumber for the Horde. Across its shadowed glades, ancient groves clash with fortified encampments amidst persistent demonic corruption. Stretching eastward across Ashenvale to Azshara, Nightsong Woods is defined by escalating violence. The Falfarren River bisects the western reaches, creating a volatile boundary between Alliance settlements and Horde encroachments. Further east, the forest fractures into heavily disputed territories where Splintertree Post coordinates Horde campaigns against the Silverwing Sentinels. Orcish axes continuously clear southern groves to fuel the Horde's expansion, leaving clear-cut swaths that infuriate the Kaldorei. Adding to the peril, satyr strongholds like Satyrnaar and Xavian, alongside demonic remnants in Demon Fall Canyon and Felfire Hill, taint the eastern canopies.

Nijel's Point. Nijel's Point is a fortified Alliance and Cenarion Circle redoubt perched high on the northern bluffs of Desolace. Tucked safely away from the blighted valleys below, it serves as the sole safe haven for Alliance travelers, researchers, and soldiers navigating the harsh wasteland. Carved into the sheer cliffs bordering the Stonetalon Mountains, Nijel's Point stands well above the gray dust and marauding centaur packs of Desolace. The settlement is held by a detachment of the Stormwind Army under Captain Pentigast, charged with monitoring the violent clan wars that threaten Alliance interests across southern Kalimdor. Its high elevation and narrow access trails make it readily defensible, providing a secure staging ground for couriers, scouts, and griffin riders travelling between Stonetalon Peak, Theramore, and Feathermoon Stronghold.

North Coast. The North Coast is a bleak, fog-shrouded stretch of shoreline marking the northern edge of Tirisfal Glades along the Great Sea. Tainted by the fall of Lordaeron, the cold beaches are littered with rotting marine life and aggressively defended by tribes of hostile murlocs. Before the Third War, these northern waters and stony beaches were part of the peaceful northern boundary of Lordaeron. When the Plague of Undeath swept across the continent, its corrupting blight seeped down the bluffs and poisoned the coast. The waters turned chill and murky, washing up the carcasses of giant sea creatures that now rot upon the sand amid the perennial coastal fog.

North Gate Outpost. North Gate Outpost is a fortified dwarven camp situated high in the North Gate Pass of Dun Morogh. Manning the rugged route between Ironforge's snowy heartland and Loch Modan, its mountaineers guard travelers against the hostile wildlife that infests the crags. Positioned in the middle of North Gate Pass, this small settlement serves as the northeastern threshold of Dun Morogh. Dwarven mountaineers stationed here keep the main roadway cleared of prowling beasts and monitor traffic heading through the mountain tunnels into Loch Modan. The harsh climate and steep ravines make patrol duty treacherous, and the garrison frequently calls upon travelers to scout the surrounding ridges for missing patrols and dangerous predators.

North Gate Pass. North Gate Pass is a vital mountain thoroughfare connecting the snowy crags of Dun Morogh with the rolling basin of Loch Modan. It forms the northern corridor through the Khaz Modan peaks, watched over by a fortified dwarven outpost. Travelers heading toward the northern lowlands of the Wetlands frequently traverse this high road. Carved into the sheer stone of Khaz Modan, North Gate Pass serves as the northern arterial link between the high, frozen valleys of Dun Morogh and the temperate waters of Loch Modan. Descending through steep mountain tunnels, travelers emerging from the west are greeted by the broad expanse of the loch valley. Because it sits within easy striking distance of the paths heading down into the Wetlands, the pass carries heavy traffic of dwarven messengers, merchants, and roaming adventurers. Its strategic value is anchored by the North Gate Outpost, where mountaineers keep vigilant watch against troggs and mountain predators.

North Tide's Hollow. North Tide's Hollow is a rugged wilderness pocket in Silverpine Forest located just north of the Sepulcher. Haunted by feral Moonrage worgen loyal to the rogue Archmage Arugal, the clearing serves as a base of operations for the beasts stalking the coastal woods. Tucked away in the dense timber north of the Forsaken settlement of the Sepulcher, North Tide's Hollow is dominated by the savage Moonrage pack. These feral worgen, brought into Lordaeron through the reckless sorcery of Archmage Arugal, have established crude encampments throughout the hollow. Built with only the barest necessities required by the hardy beasts, these rough shelters provide a forward staging ground dangerously close to Forsaken travel routes.

North Tide's Run. North Tide's Run is the windswept northwestern shoreline of Silverpine Forest, skirting the edge of the Great Sea. Marked by a half-sunken shipwreck, this stretch of sand is known as a secluded trial ground for traveling druids seeking harmony with the waters. Stretching along the northwest edge of Silverpine Forest, North Tide's Run consists of cold sand, pounding surf, and a strip of the Great Sea. Its most unmistakable landmark is a partially submerged shipwreck tilted precariously in the shallows near the beach.

Northdale. Northdale is a ruined settlement nestled north of Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands, near the border of Quel'Thalas. Once a thriving northern township, it now lies broken and overrun by banshees, shadowy watchers, and corrupted elementals. It is most famous as the bitter crossroads where Taelan Fordring abandoned the Order of the Silver Hand to embrace the fanaticism of the Scarlet Crusade. Situated along the hills north of Light's Hope Chapel, Northdale was once a peaceful community along the northern highway leading toward Quel'Thalas. The Third War left it in shattered ruins, its hearths cold and its population slain or driven out. Today, wailing banshees drift through the crumbling masonry, while invisible Eyeless Watchers lurk in the dark to survey the cursed roads. Even the nearby lake has succumbed to the plague, its waters bubbling with twisted, corrupted water elementals.

Northfold Manor. Northfold Manor is a dilapidated agricultural estate situated on the northwestern fringes of the Arathi Highlands. Once a prosperous human homestead before the collapse of Stromgarde, the grounds are now occupied by criminal operatives of the Syndicate engaging in unsettling, dark practices. Perched on the rolling highlands near the Thoradin's Wall passage, Northfold Manor once supported the kingdom of Stromgarde. In the chaos following the realm's fracturing, displaced Alteraci nobility and outlaws of the Syndicate claimed the manor house, barn, and fields as an operational base. Instead of tending crops, Syndicate mercenaries, highwaymen, and pathstalkers use the farmstead to stage ambushes along the roads and coordinate their presence across Arathi.

Northpass Tower. Northpass Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower situated in the northern reaches of the Eastern Plaguelands along the road to Quel'Thalas. Shattered during the Third War, it still overlooks the northern road toward the elven lands. Built by the Kingdom of Lordaeron to guard the vital thoroughfare leading north into Quel'Thalas, Northpass Tower was reduced to a broken shell during the Scourge invasion. Despite its shattered stonework, the tower's elevated position retains immense tactical value, overlooking the blight-choked frontier between Stratholme's blighted outskirts and the distant elven lands.

Northridge Lumber Camp. Northridge Lumber Camp is an active lumber mill nestled in the northern hills of the Western Plaguelands near Hearthglen. Currently held and fortified by the Scarlet Crusade, it provides timber vital to sustaining their nearby strongholds. Both the Alliance and the Horde view the facility as a prime target to cripple the zealots' regional infrastructure. Situated just down the road from Hearthglen, the Northridge Lumber Camp serves as a vital logistics node for the Scarlet Crusade. Despite the lingering plague choking the surrounding forests, the camp fells and processes regional timber to construct fortifications, repair watchtowers, and furnish the crusade's war effort in Lordaeron. Heavily garrisoned by fanatical laborers and guards, the mill is fiercely protected against both the Scourge and outside trespassers.

Northshire Abbey. Northshire Abbey is a historic monastery nestled in Northshire Valley within the northern foothills of Elwynn Forest. Rebuilt after its destruction in the First War, it serves as the spiritual heart of the Brotherhood of Northshire and a premier training center for new defenders answering the kingdom of Stormwind's call. Centuries ago, clerics from Lordaeron traveled south into the kingdom of Stormwind to spread the worship of the Holy Light, establishing the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics and their abbey. The monastery quickly became an anchor of kingdom life, caring for the sick and even tending to the young Guardian Medivh during his years in a coma. During the First War, the abbey suffered repeated assaults by brigands and the Orcish Horde, culminating in its utter destruction. When the Alliance of Lordaeron liberated the region in the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol helped rebuild the sanctuary, refounding its protectors as the Brotherhood of Northshire.

Northshire Valley. Tucked away in the northern mountains of Elwynn Forest, Northshire Valley serves as the peaceful cradle and training ground for the kingdom of Stormwind's newest defenders. Surrounded by natural barriers, it hosts the historic Northshire Abbey, fertile vineyards, and the rich Echo Ridge Mine. Despite its tranquil appearance, the valley faces mounting unrest from rogue bandits, infesting kobolds, and displaced predators. Northshire Valley is framed by nearly impassable mountain ridges, with its only road heading south through a fortified gatehouse toward Goldshire and the rest of Elwynn Forest. A clear river winds through its pastures before feeding south into Crystal Lake. At the valley's heart stands Northshire Abbey, an ancient sanctuary where the Holy Light is taught and where recruits are trained by the Knights of the Silver Hand and seasoned veterans. Beyond the abbey walls lie the bountiful Northshire Vineyards and Echo Ridge Mine, forming a self-sustaining pocket of Stormwind territory that feels far removed from the wider world's wars.

Northshire Vineyards. The Northshire Vineyards are cultivated grape fields lying just east of Northshire Abbey in the valley's sheltered basin. Though once a peaceful source of wine for the clerics, the fields have fallen under the control of the Defias Brotherhood and their local brigands. Located east across the stream from Northshire Abbey, the Northshire Vineyards represent the valley's quiet agrarian life. The fields are tended by local workers like Milly Osworth, but rising civil unrest has left them unprotected. Bandits aligned with the Defias Brotherhood, led on the ground by a cutthroat named Garrick Padfoot, have seized the acreage. Rather than mere vandalism, the thieves occupy the fields to plunder the harvest and strip the local farmers of their livelihood, providing new recruits to the Brotherhood an easy foothold right under the abbey's nose.

Noxious Glade. Tucked away in the hills just north of Light's Hope Chapel, the Noxious Glade is a secluded basin steeped in concentrated plague. Choked with toxic green air and darkened soil, it functions as a nearby redoubt for Scourge operations right under the Argent Dawn's nose. While the Argent Dawn maintains its vigil at Light's Hope Chapel, an encampment of the Scourge lurks directly in the hills above them to the north. The Noxious Glade suffers from an infection far more severe than much of the surrounding terrain: the air hangs thick with a sickly green mist, and the soil has rotted into deep bruised purples. Within the hollow, the undead have erected ziggurats, a slaughterhouse for cobbling together abominations, and a plague cauldron that continuously spews pestilence into the atmosphere.

Noxious Lair. The Noxious Lair is a sunken silithid hive situated in the southwestern deserts of Tanaris, bordering Un'Goro Crater. Once a verdant basin with flowing water, the territory has been infested and drained of its vital resources by the burrowing Centipaar swarm. Now, it stands as an acidic breeding ground filled with swarming insectoids and rich mineral veins. Resting against the western ridges overlooking Un'Goro Crater, the Noxious Lair occupies a depression in the sand that once held a lake or shallow river. When the Centipaar silithid invaded, they consumed the desert's remaining underground moisture and transformed the basin into an encroaching colony. Vast pincers and twitching limbs rise directly from the sand dunes, surrounding subterranean tunnels slick with corrosive insect secretions and clusters of incubating eggs.

Old Ironforge. Old Ironforge, also called the Assembly of Thanes, is an ancient subterranean chamber lying directly beneath the High Seat of Ironforge. Carved deep into the mountain's roots above glowing magma veins, it represents the ancestral heart of the dwarven capital. In the present day, its heavy access gates in the royal throne room remain sealed and vigilantly guarded. Beneath King Magni Bronzebeard's throne in the High Seat rests the cavernous hall known as Old Ironforge or the Assembly of Thanes. Deep inside these fiery subterranean foundations, winding stone bridges cross pools of subterranean lava. Long before the bustling halls of the Great Forge and the Commons echoed with modern dwarven commerce, early thanes gathered in these cavernous depths to deliberate and govern the mountain kingdom.

Old Port Authority. The Old Port Authority is a bustling, multi-vendor warehouse nestled along the boardwalks of Booty Bay. Beneath its roof, travelers browse everything from exotic pets and firearms to hearty rations and finely crafted weapons. Perched inside the pirate haven of Booty Bay, the Old Port Authority serves as an indoor marketplace divided into distinct stalls, and its interior buzzes with brisk commerce. Merchants hawk general adventuring supplies, firearms, bows, food, and weapons to scoundrels and privateers alike. It also houses exotic imports, offering colorful birds and nautical oddities straight off the docks to anyone with coin.

Old Town. Old Town is the oldest and grittiest quarter of Stormwind City, having largely survived the destruction of the First War intact. Rather than gleaming stone plazas, its narrow alleys feature weathered brick, working-class tenements, and bustling military facilities. It serves as home to the kingdom's military Command Center as well as the clandestine headquarters of SI:7. While the rest of Stormwind was painstakingly rebuilt from the ground up by the Stonemasons following the First War, Old Town escaped total ruin. Because it did not require wholesale reconstruction, it never received the pristine marble facades and grand canals seen in the Trade District or Cathedral Square. Instead, it remains a rustic, crowded quarter where working folk, laborers, and the city's poorest residents reside. Its cobbled streets are narrower, dirtier, and far more chaotic than the rest of the capital, yet they preserve the authentic atmosphere of pre-war Stormwind.

Olsen's Farthing. Olsen's Farthing was once a flourishing farmstead situated along the primary trade road running through Silverpine Forest. In the wake of the Third War, the fields fell into ruin and became overrun by reanimated thralls bound to the renegade necromancer Thule Ravenclaw. Before the plague consumed Lordaeron, Olsen's Farthing was a busy agricultural homestead with direct access to Silverpine's main overland trading route. Today, its tilled fields are choked with weeds, its structures lie broken, and any memory of honest farming has been erased by Scourge necromancy. Undead thralls, bound as slaves and raiders under the command of Thule Ravenclaw, wander the barren grounds to slaughter any travelers who stray too close.

Oneiros. Oneiros is a sprawling expanse of ancient night elven ruins located south of Jademir Lake in northern Feralas. Tied intimately to the nearby portals leading toward the realm of Ysera, its moss-covered stones are guarded by elite green dragonkin. Stretching across the dense forest floor of northern Feralas, the crumbling stone arches and column fragments of Oneiros hint at an ancient Kaldorei settlement abandoned millennia ago. In the present day, nature has reclaimed the structures, entwining them with massive roots and verdant overgrowth. Elite guardians of the Green Dragonflight relentlessly patrol the shaded paths and broken plazas, warding mortals away from ancient secrets.

Onyxia's Lair. Onyxia's Lair is a subterranean cavern located deep within the Wyrmbog of Dustwallow Marsh. It serves as the nesting sanctuary and stronghold for Onyxia, broodmother of the black dragonflight. Inside its sweltering, magma-filled chambers, the great dragon watches over clutches of black dragon eggs. Carved into the treacherous mud and petrified wood of the Wyrmbog, the cavern entrance resembles the yawning maw of a dragon. Within, the cool rot of the marsh gives way to intense volcanic heat. Magma seeps from cracks in the obsidian stone, while subterranean tremors routinely shake the ceilings. The central chamber opens into a vast incubator where hundreds of black dragon eggs lie nested amid ash and embers, overseen by flightkin, dragonspawn guards, and Onyxia herself.

Oracle Glade. Nestled in northwestern Teldrassil, the Oracle Glade is a sacred woodland sanctuary home to the wondrous Oracle Tree and the World Tree's premier moonwell. Despite its serene purpose as a center of communion and vigilance, the glade faces constant harassment from encroaching Bloodfeather harpies. The Oracle Glade rests quietly between Darnassus and Wellspring Lake, serving as a vital nexus of night elven communion with nature. At its center stands the Oracle Tree, an ancient specimen whose massive boughs evoke the silhouette of an eagle perched atop a bear. Nearby shimmers the first and most potent of Teldrassil's sacred moonwells, an oasis of lunar magic bathed in Elune's grace. Alongside the Circle of the Ancients, the Oracle Tree watches over the island boughs, shedding inscribed bark that acts as vital communiques to Archdruid Fandral Staghelm regarding the World Tree's health.

Orgrimmar. Orgrimmar is the formidable warrior capital of the New Horde, carved into the winding red canyons of northern Durotar. Founded by Warchief Thrall and named in memory of Orgrim Doomhammer, it serves as the beating heart of orcish renewal and intertribal survival on Kalimdor. Following the Third War and the victory at Mount Hyjal, Warchief Thrall brought his surviving people south to establish a permanent homeland in Durotar. Nestled into a natural barrier of sheer mountain crags, Orgrimmar was engineered to withstand siege, boasting spiked timber palisades, stone watchtowers, and deep mountain-carved caverns. Built in cooperation with the Darkspear trolls, tauren stonemasons, and goblin engineers, the fortress turned a desolate wilderness into an unassailable bastion of strength.

Ortell's Hideout. Ortell's Hideout is a modest, secluded cave nestled against the mountains in southeastern Silithus. It serves as the refuge of Hermit Ortell, one of the few solitary souls hardy or foolish enough to dwell alone in this barren wasteland. Tucked away in the jagged cliffs of southeastern Silithus, Ortell's Hideout offers sparse sanctuary from the raging sandstorms and prowling silithid swarms that dominate the wastes. The cave is occupied solely by Hermit Ortell, an eccentric recluse who ekes out an existence far from civilization and the fortified garrisons of the Cenarion Hold. Travelers who brave the dangerous journey to this remote corner often seek his peculiar knowledge of the desert and its hazards.

Owl Wing Thicket. Owl Wing Thicket is a rugged cluster of caves and stone roosts in southern Winterspring. It is heavily populated by berserk, moontouched, and crazed owlbeasts that prowl the snowy crags. Deep within, ancient night elf altars preserve sacred knowledge about the origin of these creatures and their connection to the moon goddess Elune. Carved into the snowy highlands south of Everlook, Owl Wing Thicket serves as one of the densest nesting grounds for Winterspring's wild owlbeasts. Long ago, night elf caretakers revered these creatures as sacred guardians blessed by Elune. Ancient shrines and moonstone altars are still tucked among the cavern overhangs, watched over by the lingering spirits of the Guardians of Elune. Today, however, many of the beasts have succumbed to madness, lashing out at travelers who trespass upon their holy hollows.

Palemane Rock. Palemane Rock is a cavern and campsite nestled into the western mountains of Mulgore. It serves as a primary stronghold for the aggressive Palemane gnoll tribe, posing a continual nuisance and threat to the nearby tauren of Bloodhoof Village. Situated along the western rim of the grassy plains of Mulgore, Palemane Rock consists of a sprawling open-air encampment fronting a deep, shadowed cavern carved into the mountainside. The Palemane gnolls have claimed both the cave interior and the immediate foothills outside as their territory. Hostile and territorial, these gnolls aggressively defend their den, attacking hunters, travelers, and scouts who wander too close to their rocky haven.

Park. Tucked along the western edge of Stormwind City between Cathedral Square and the Mage Quarter, the Park is a lush sanctuary of greenery and quiet reflection. Devoted to nature and leisure amidst the bustling stone capital, it serves as the primary haven for visiting night elves and houses the only druid trainers in the Eastern Kingdoms. While the rest of Stormwind is dominated by cobbled walkways, towering limestone ramparts, and crowded market stalls, the Park offers a tranquil breath of wilderness. Originally established as a quiet place of recreation for the city's populace, it naturally transformed into an enclave for night elf emissaries and travelers arriving from across the Great Sea. Sheltered beneath shaded canopies and surrounding a central Moonwell, the district brings a sliver of Kalimdor's sacred glades into the heart of the human kingdom.

Pestilent Scar. The Pestilent Scar is a deep, blighted gorge carved into the blighted terrain of the Eastern Plaguelands. Unlike the jagged rents torn open by catastrophic Scourge blight, this chasm appears to be a natural canyon or dried lakebed that was subsequently corrupted and overrun by ravenous oozes. Winding through the eastern reaches of the Eastern Plaguelands, the Pestilent Scar forms a gloomy rift in the corrupted landscape. While nearby rifts like the Infectis Scar were ripped into the earth by sudden catastrophic eruptions of the Plague of Undeath, scholars note that the Pestilent Scar seems to have originated as a natural geological formation. It was likely a deep river canyon or natural lake that dried up when the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, leaving a barren trench that gradually pooled with noxious runoff and foul slime.

Petitioner's Chamber. The Petitioner's Chamber, also known as the Hall of Petitioners, is an antechamber situated just off the main entrance ramp of Stormwind Keep. It serves as an official waiting room for nobility, church dignitaries, and visiting subjects seeking an audience with the crown. Those lingering here often pass the hours mingling, drinking, or waiting upon the regent's pleasure. Found immediately to the right upon ascending into Stormwind Keep, the Petitioner's Chamber is where matters of state meet everyday bureaucracy. Nobles such as Count Remington Ridgewell and high-ranking clergy like Bishop DeLavey pass their time in these halls while waiting for an audience with the boy-king Anduin Wrynn and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. Behind the polished veneer of courtly etiquette, it is an ideal corner of the castle for gossip, quiet lobbying, and discerning who truly holds influence within the realm.

Pig and Whistle Tavern. The Pig and Whistle Tavern is a bustling tavern nestled within Stormwind City's rugged Old Town district. It serves as a favored gathering spot for Alliance travelers, local laborers, and weathered veterans recalling the kingdom's past conflicts. Situated amidst the gritty, winding alleys of Old Town, the Pig and Whistle Tavern offers warmth, ale, and lodging to those who walk the capital's rougher quarter. While the nobles of the city congregate in cathedral squares and marble plazas, this establishment caters to common citizens, working folk, and travelers fresh from the road. Inside, patrons can find merchants like the renowned recipe vendor Kendor Kabonka, alongside grizzled veterans who nurse their tankards while trading memories of the First and Second Wars.

Plaguemist Ravine. Plaguemist Ravine is a narrow mountain passage connecting the verdant wilderness of the Hinterlands to the haunted shores of Darrowmere Lake in the Western Plaguelands. Named for the sickly fog that rolls down from the north, it provides a quiet and desolate route across the mountain range. Tucked away in the mountains northwest of Quel'Danil Lodge, Plaguemist Ravine acts as a geographic threshold between two radically different realms. To the south lies the lush, untamed highland forest of the Hinterlands, while to the north the pass opens directly upon Caer Darrow and the blighted expanse of the Western Plaguelands. The ravine earned its name from the foul, unnatural vapors that creep southward out of the Plaguelands, creating a jarring contrast with the crisp mountain air of the neighboring wilderness.

Plaguewood. Once a peaceful woodland known as Greenwood, the Plaguewood is now a blighted, fungus-choked expanse stretching south of Stratholme. Crawling with Scourge infrastructure and patrolling Scarlet Crusaders, it stands as one of the most corrupt corners of the Eastern Plaguelands. Before the Third War, this region was Greenwood, a vibrant forest that mirrored the lush woods of Elwynn. A modest village sat near its entrance, and its roads were traveled by farmers and soldiers alike. All of that collapsed when tainted grain arrived from Andorhal. Today, spongy, corrupted soil has taken the place of rich earth, and titanic mushrooms dwarf the dead trees, constantly spewing noxious brown vapors across the woodland floor.

Plaguewood Tower. Plaguewood Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower situated in the northern reaches of the Plaguewood near Terrordale. Shattered during the Scourge invasion, it now stands as a broken ruin amid the blighted forest. Standing on the edge of the blight-choked Plaguewood and the blighted town of Terrordale, Plaguewood Tower once served the Kingdom of Lordaeron as a vital northern watchpost. When the Scourge swept across the land, the fortification was battered into crumbling masonry and left in ruins amid corrupted fungal canopies. Today the fractured stones still overlook the northern trails, a silent reminder of the watch Lordaeron once kept over this land.

Pool of Ask'ar. The Pool of Ask'ar is a sprawling, submerged cavern lake located deep within Blackfathom Deeps. Teeming with aquatic beasts and foul naga invaders, its waters conceal ancient night elven architecture alongside hidden passageways that wind deeper into the corrupted sanctuary. Situated just beyond the Drowned Sacellum, the Pool of Ask'ar fills a massive subterranean vault with murky, cold water. The natural caverns and ancient stonework have become a nesting ground for oversized snapping turtles and deep-sea crabs, overseen by the enormous ancient chelonian known as Ghamoo-ra. The naga who have taken over the temple utilize this submerged threshold as a defensive staging ground, guarding the waterlogged approaches that lead deeper into the complex toward Lady Sarevess and the Moonshrine Ruins.

Pool of Tears. The Pool of Tears is a large, murky lake dominating the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Deep beneath its surface lies the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar, brought low by the Green Dragonflight to contain the horrors within. Today, vicious frenzies patrol the turbid waters, and ancient troll ruins litter its drowned banks. Long ago, fanatical Atal'ai trolls raised a monumental ziggurat to their bloodthirsty god, Hakkar the Soulflayer. Horrified by the blasphemies taking place within, the Dragon Aspect Ysera shattered the ground beneath the structure, submerging the massive temple into the depths of the marsh. The existing lake flooded over the temple ruins. While the dragons sought to bury the evil forever, the ziggurat still stands beneath the silt and waves, and green drakes remain vigilant in the area to keep its corruption sealed.

Pools of Arlithrien. The Pools of Arlithrien are a cluster of secluded springs resting in western Teldrassil, just south of the gates to Darnassus. Once a tranquil retreat centered around a sacred moonwell, the area has fallen into neglect and danger as local wildlife and nearby hostile Gnarlpine furbolgs encroached upon it. Tucked along the shaded boughs south of Darnassus, the Pools of Arlithrien were originally meant to be a quiet place of natural harmony. At their heart lies a stone moonwell, a vessel for the waters imbued with the grace of Elune. Yet despite its proximity to the night elven capital, the sanctuary has become perilous. Agitated beasts roam the shallows, and the persistent hostility of the displaced Gnarlpine furbolgs forced the night elves to abandon routine upkeep of the site, leaving a peaceful wonder shadowed by the island's growing malaise.

Pools of Vision. The Pools of Vision are a subterranean cavern nestled beneath Spirit Rise in Thunder Bluff. Marked by still waters and dim caverns, this secluded subterranean space serves as the primary enclave for the Forsaken within the tauren capital. While the sunlit peaks of Thunder Bluff belong to the wind, earth, and sky, the Pools of Vision plunge directly beneath Spirit Rise into shadowy seclusion. Accessible from a discreet cave path off the bridge leading to the rise, this subterranean grotto offers subterranean respite quite unlike the open-air lodges above. Here, misty waters pool in the dark, creating an isolated atmosphere where Horde spellcasters gather far from the bustling central mesas.

Purgation Isle. Purgation Isle is a spiraling, rocky island lying off the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Crowned with a cemetery and a ruined scout tower, the desolate rock is cursed and swarming with the restless, condemned spirits of fallen humans and dwarves. Rising abruptly from the sea south of Hillsbrad, Purgation Isle is a grim sight marked by winding paths that lead past tombstones to an abandoned watchtower. No living nation claims it today. Instead, the isle is plagued by condemned souls—former paladins, priests, mages, and judges who wander among the graves, unable to find peace in death.

Pyrewood Village. Pyrewood Village is an isolated human settlement nestled in southern Silverpine Forest beneath Shadowfang Keep. Originally part of Gilneas before being stranded outside the Greymane Wall, its living residents harbor a horrific secret brought upon them by the mad archmage Arugal. Pyrewood was once a prosperous Gilnean settlement. When King Genn Greymane chose to isolate his kingdom behind the massive Greymane Wall following the Second War, Pyrewood was left on the northern side. Cut off from their homeland, the townsfolk were left entirely defenseless during the Third War as the Scourge marched across Lordaeron. Though they managed to survive the initial wave of the undead, their true nightmare began when the mage Arugal took refuge in the fortress above.

Quagmire. The Quagmire comprises the sprawling, treacherous heart of central Dustwallow Marsh. Bound by Brackenwall Village to the north and the Dragonmurk to the south, its waterlogged flats are notoriously difficult to navigate. Hostile beasts and ravenous oozes make any journey through this central fen perilous. Occupying the wide expanse between Lost Point in the west and Dustwallow Bay in the east, the Quagmire represents the wild core of the marsh. Footing is unreliable at best, with solid earth constantly giving way to murky water and clinging mud. Travelers must contend with predatory crocolisks lurking beneath the scum, aggressive spiders nesting in the dead brush, and strange oozes that seep through the muck.

Quel'Lithien Lodge. Quel'Lithien Lodge is an isolated high elven hunting lodge nestled in the forested northern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands near the entrance to Quel'Thalas. Its Farstrider rangers hold out among the blighted woods, surrounded by the Scourge and hunted by Forsaken agents, while guarding old elven archives. Before the Third War, Quel'Lithien was a Farstrider camp on the road toward Quel'Thalas, and it housed elven records of the ranger order. The lodge fell on hard times after the Scourge swept through Lordaeron and into the elven kingdom. Today its rangers keep their vigil in the corrupted forest, one of only two major concentrations of high elves left in Lordaeron.

Rage Scar Hold. Rage Scar Hold is a cavern carved into the wilderness of Feralas, situated on the mainland not far from Feathermoon Stronghold. It is notorious for housing some of the most vicious yetis in the region. Strangely, scattered books, symbols, and traces of night elven architecture deeper within suggest the den once served a far more civil purpose before the beasts claimed it. Carved into the rugged wilds of Feralas, Rage Scar Hold is dominated by savage yetis that attack anyone venturing near their lair. The creatures make the surrounding forest trails hazardous for both Alliance sentinels and passing travelers. While yetis are common to the untamed reaches of Kalimdor, the denizens of Rage Scar Hold stand out for their raw aggression and territorial ferocity.

Ragefire Chasm. Ragefire Chasm is a network of volcanic caverns situated directly beneath the Horde capital of Orgrimmar. Accessible through the Cleft of Shadow, its magma-lit tunnels harbor feral troggs and a hidden sect of the Shadow Council bent on unraveling the young orcish nation from within. While Thrall works to secure Durotar above, subterranean dangers fester directly beneath Orgrimmar's foundation. Ragefire Chasm is an unstable network of volcanic vents and magma rivers that has become infested with savage Ragefire troggs. Rising from unknown depths below the tunnels, these hostile creatures violently rebuffed diplomatic overtures made by Magatha Grimtotem. Left unchecked, their sheer numbers threaten to undermine and overrun the capital.

Ragefire Chasm (Classic). Ragefire Chasm is a sprawling network of volcanic tunnels carved directly beneath Orgrimmar, accessible through the shadowy depths of the Cleft of Shadow. Despite being situated under the Horde's sovereign capital, these fiery caverns crawl with hostile troggs and a subversive coven of cultists loyal to the Shadow Council. Beneath the stone streets and fortified towers of Orgrimmar lies Ragefire Chasm, a treacherous network of magma-filled subterranean caverns. The tunnels recently became overrun by the savage Ragefire troggs, who pushed upward from deep subterranean fissures. Magatha Grimtotem of the tauren attempted peaceful diplomacy with the creatures, but her overtures were violently rejected. Left unchecked, the troggs threaten to tunnel further into the foundations of the city itself.

Raptor Grounds. Tucked into the dusty hills of the southern Barrens, the Raptor Grounds is a secluded valley claimed by the Sunscale raptors. Unlike ordinary wild beasts, the pack here exhibits an eerie, tool-using cunning and a compulsive urge to steal bright trinkets from nearby settlements. Located west of Northwatch Hold, the Raptor Grounds serves as the primary nesting territory for the Sunscale raptors. Travelers quickly discover that these creatures are far from mindless predators: they display an unnatural intelligence, fashioning crude shelters, assembling primitive tools, and coordinating their hunts. Driven by a relentless fascination with shiny and unusual items, the pack regularly raids passing caravans and Horde encampments, dragging coins, trinkets, and supplies back into their canyon dens.

Raptor Ridge. Raptor Ridge is an elevated, rugged expanse in the eastern Wetlands, sitting northwest of the fortified Dragonmaw Gates. It serves as the primary hunting and nesting grounds for packs of ferocious Razormaw raptors, overseen by a particularly vicious matriarch deep within its caverns. Rising above the sodden marshes of the eastern Wetlands, Raptor Ridge is among the most perilous wilderness areas in the region. Vicious Razormaw raptors prowl its crags and rocky trails in large packs, making travel near the foothills of Khaz Modan hazardous for wanderers. At the heart of the ridge lies a brooding cavern dominated by the Razormaw Matriarch, whose aggressive brood aggressively defends their nests against any encroaching predators or foolish travelers wandering too close to the Dragonmaw Gates.

Ratchet. Ratchet is a bustling neutral port town run by the Steamwheedle Cartel on the eastern coast of the Barrens. Founded by chief engineer Gazlowe after he helped construct Orgrimmar, it serves as the primary maritime trade hub linking central Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms. Perched on the arid coastline between Durotar and Dustwallow Marsh, Ratchet offers safe harbor to anyone carrying coin. Founded by the entrepreneurial engineer Gazlowe following the Third War, the port arose from smugglers, exiles, and daring traders looking to exploit Kalimdor's frontier. It operates beneath the banner of the Steamwheedle Cartel, maintaining strict neutrality between the Horde and the Alliance. Ships like The Maiden's Fancy regularly ply the waters across the Great Sea to Booty Bay, transporting goods, mercenaries, and raw materials between continents. Local bruisers keep a watchful eye on the docks, ruthlessly thrashing anyone foolish enough to start a brawl and disrupt commerce.

Ravaged Caravan. The Ravaged Caravan is a smoldering wreck located on the northeastern shore of Stonebull Lake in Mulgore. Once a supply convoy bound for Supervisor Fizsprocket's mining operations, it was ambushed and destroyed by local tauren determined to halt goblin exploitation of their homeland. Perched on a rise above Stonebull Lake, the Ravaged Caravan marks an early clash between the tauren of Bloodhoof Village and the encroaching Venture Company. Sent to deliver mining supplies, blueprints, and equipment to Supervisor Fizsprocket's dig site, the caravan was cut off and wrecked by tauren defenders before it could reach its destination. Despite the devastation, stubborn Venture Co. survivors still cling to the ruined wagons and smoldering crates, jealously guarding what little cargo remains.

Ravaged Twilight Camp. Tucked away in the secluded Crystal Vale of northwestern Silithus, the Ravaged Twilight Camp sits ruined among towering mineral formations. It serves as an isolated redoubt for the eccentric hermit Highlord Demitrian, a devotee of the Windseeker. While the Twilight's Hammer maintains numerous active outposts across the sands of Silithus, this broken encampment in the Crystal Vale tells a different story. Nestled far from the primary cult fortresses, the camp lies largely ruined and deserted, save for Highlord Demitrian. A servant of Thunderaan, Demitrian lingers amidst the stones, seemingly abandoned by or detached from the wider Twilight hierarchy while brooding over elemental bindings and the lost power of the Windseeker.

Raven Hill. Raven Hill is a desolate, ruined village in western Duskwood sitting in the long shadow of the vast Raven Hill Cemetery. Once a lively human settlement, it lies abandoned by all but a handful of frightened squatters and invisible spirits. Situated along the western thoroughfare of Duskwood just north of Addle's Stead, Raven Hill is a tragic shell of its former self. When dark magic and undead horrors swept through the Grand Hamlet region, the living evacuated eastward toward Darkshire or fled the territory entirely. Today, ruined timber homes rot beneath perpetual gloom, avoided by travelers who fear both the restless dead wandering down from the neighboring cemetery and the invisible Unseen lurking between the crumbling walls.

Raven Hill Cemetery. Raven Hill Cemetery is a vast, cursed graveyard stretching across the western reaches of Duskwood. Once a peaceful burial ground for local hamlets, the cemetery has been overrun by hordes of walking dead, scavenger spiders, and ruthless grave robbers. Before the darkness engulfed the Dawning Wood, Raven Hill Cemetery served as the primary resting place for the surrounding settlements. As dark sorceries fell upon the region, the dead failed to remain in their plots. Skeletons, ghouls, and shambling horrors clawed their way out of the soil, swelling the graveyard's grim boundaries. Today, it stands as one of the most perilous blights in Duskwood. The cemetery is prowled not only by rotting abominations and giant spiders, but also by desperate grave robbers eager to plunder ancestral crypts unhindered by local authorities.

Ravencrest Monument. Perched upon the windswept cliffs of southern Azshara, the Ravencrest Monument marks the shattered remnant of an ancient night elven colossus. Once a towering tribute overlooking the Great Sea, the statue has long since broken apart, leaving only towering legs and scattered stone ruins now stalked by hostile Spitelash naga. Standing high above the ocean southeast of the Ruins of Eldarath, the Ravencrest Monument was once an awe-inspiring marvel of Kaldorei stonework. Today, little remains of the majestic colossus beyond its pair of gigantic broken legs rooted to the stone plinth, with the shattered fragments of its torso and head either buried in the cliffside dirt or lost beneath the waves below. Reaching this remote coastal promontory requires trekking across the mainland bridges of Azshara, as sheer, rocky drops prevent any approach from the sea.

Ravenholdt Manor. Tucked away high in the mountains above Hillsbrad Foothills, Ravenholdt Manor serves as the secluded headquarters for the guild of thieves and assassins known as Ravenholdt. Overseen by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the estate provides a discreet haven where practitioners of stealth hone their craft far from the eyes of authorities. Hidden behind a narrow mountain pass and a winding cave northwest of Durnholde Keep, Ravenholdt Manor sits isolated on the borderlands of the Alterac Mountains. The property belongs to Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, a nobleman who maintains a disciplined enclave of rogues, assassins, and intelligence operatives. The grounds feature a tranquil garden and an outdoor training arena overseen by martial experts like Master Kang, providing a disciplined space to practice lockpicking, poison-crafting, and close-quarters combat. While the manor welcomes those with a talent for skullduggery, clumsy outsiders and unwanted visitors are treated with cold suspicion by the manor's watchful sentries.

Raynewood Retreat. Raynewood Retreat is an ancient night elf outpost perched around a massive great tree in north-central Ashenvale. Guarded by dryads and Cenarion protectors, it serves as a watchful sanctuary monitoring the northern passes toward corrupted Felwood. It is also the sanctuary of Keeper Ordanus, an elder son of Cenarius targeted by sinister outside forces. Nestled between Shael'dryn's moonwell and the satyr-infested ruins of Night Run, the outpost is fiercely guarded by Cenarion Protectors, faerie dragons, and Laughing Sisters. Their collective vigilance keeps a wary eye on the encroaching taint descending from Felwood just to the north.

Razor Hill. Razor Hill is the principal Horde settlement in central Durotar, nestled at the strategic crossroads between the Valley of Trials, the Barrens, and Orgrimmar. Centered around a prominent fortified barracks, it serves as the staging ground and training center for young orc and troll warriors testing their mettle in the harsh wilderness. Built at a vital geographical junction, Razor Hill connects northern Durotar with the coastal settlements to the south and the sprawling plains of the Barrens across the Southfury River. Dominated by its stone-and-timber barracks and classic orcish burrows, the settlement was established early in the founding of Durotar. Shortly after the Third War, human forces from Kul Tiras lured the Horde into an ambush here under the guise of an emissary summit, an assault thwarted when Rexxar went in Thrall's stead. Today, the outpost stands fully fortified against further coastal incursions.

Razor Hill Watchtower. Perched on the red stone bluffs overlooking Razor Hill, this sturdy outpost serves as an early warning post for the heart of Durotar. Furl Scornbrow keeps a vigilant eye across the dusty plains and toward the coast, safeguarding the settlement below from encroaching threats. Constructed from thick timber and iron framing, the Razor Hill Watchtower guards the settlement of Razor Hill and the surrounding canyons. Durotar faces relentless threats from Kul Tiras marines along the eastern shore, quilboar raiders prowling the scrublands, and Burning Blade cultists lurking in nearby crags. From this elevated vantage point atop the ridgeline, the lookout can spot approaching warbands, smoke signals, and incursions long before they reach the settlement gates.

Razorfen Downs. Razorfen Downs is the ancestral capital and sacred burial labyrinth of the quilboar, carved deep into the colossal brambles bordering the southern Barrens and Thousand Needles. Once their holiest sanctuary, it has fallen under the sway of the undead Scourge, transforming into a festering bastion of necromancy. Long revered as the ancestral capital city and burial grounds of the quilboar race, Razorfen Downs rests within the colossal petrified briars sprung from the fallen demigod Agamaggan. Legend holds that its arched entryway was carved directly from the Great Boar's very maw. For centuries, the high priests of the Death's Head tribe tended these deep, winding burrows and honored their revered dead. Yet despite its sacred standing among the boar-folk, the maze of bone and bramble has recently suffered a catastrophe far darker than any squabble over Barrens water.

Razorfen Downs (Classic). Razorfen Downs is the ancestral burial ground and traditional capital city of the quilboar, nestled deep within giant thorny brambles in the southern Barrens. Recently, agents of the undead Scourge led by the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer seized control of the labyrinth, reanimating the quilboar dead and threatening to expand their dominion across central Kalimdor. Grown from the same towering, petrified vines as nearby Razorfen Kraul, Razorfen Downs rests where the ancient boar demigod Agamaggan fell during the War of the Ancients. For generations, the labyrinth of thorns served as the sacred necropolis and seat of power for the quilboar, guarded closely by the mystics of the Death's Head tribe. To the quilboar, the dense briars are holy ground, soaked in the blood of their divine progenitor.

Razorfen Kraul (Classic). Razorfen Kraul is the ancestral heartland of the quilboar, carved deep into the colossal thorns that sprang from the blood of the fallen boar demigod Agamaggan. Ruled by the ruthless crone Charlga Razorflank, this fortified labyrinth serves as a staging ground for bloody raids across the southern Barrens. Ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients, the colossal boar demigod Agamaggan perished battling the Burning Legion to save Azeroth. Wherever his sacred blood seeped into the soil of southern Kalimdor, massive, impenetrable thorn vines erupted from the earth. The quilboar, believing themselves the mortal progeny of the Great Boar, gathered within these dense briars to dwell and venerate his sacrifice. The dense mass known as Razorfen Kraul stands as their most revered redoubt, thick with quilboar warriors, beast trainers, and earth-shaping shamans.

Razormane Grounds. The Razormane Grounds form the forward encampment of the Razormane quilboar pushing eastward from the Barrens into central Durotar. Choked with sharp briars and the stripped carcasses of wild game, this bristling outpost serves as the frontline in the quilboars' unending clash with the orcs of Orgrimmar. Sprawling beneath the red cliffs of central Durotar, the Razormane Grounds mark the furthest eastern reach of quilboar expansion out of the Barrens. Entangled within thick brambles and surrounded by bleached bones, the encampment poses a constant danger to travelers along the Southfury River. The camp is led by figures such as Captain Flat Tusk of the Battleguard and Geolord Mottle, who orchestrate raids against neighboring orc settlements and passing supply lines. Despite regular patrols dispatched from Razor Hill and nearby outposts, the Razormane replenish their ranks tirelessly, sprouting from the briars faster than the Horde can clear them.

Razorwind Canyon. Razorwind Canyon is a winding, rocky gulch split across the main road between Razor Hill and Orgrimmar. Infested by the aggressive Dustwind harpies, the canyon poses a persistent danger to travelers moving north toward the Horde's capital. Razorwind Canyon flanks the central artery linking Razor Hill to Orgrimmar, carving paths into both the eastern bluffs and the western scrublands toward Tor'kren Farm. The canyon is the nesting ground of the Dustwind harpies, territorial creatures that strike without hesitation at travelers who stray too close to their roosts. Their presence so near the capital's trade routes makes clearing out these gullies an ongoing necessity for the defenders of Durotar.

Rebel Camp. Tucked just off the road in northern Stranglethorn Vale, the Rebel Camp serves as a fortified refuge for Alliance soldiers who broke away from Colonel Kurzen. Led by Lieutenant Doren, these troops refused to surrender to the madness gripping their commander's expedition and now fight to survive and undo his descent into tyranny. When Colonel Kurzen's expedition pushed deep into the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale on behalf of Stormwind, things rapidly fell apart. Afflicted by the dark jungle magic and the curse of the ogre mage Mai'Zoth, the Colonel and his core loyalists succumbed to madness, turning rogue and terrorizing the wilds. A handful of sound-minded soldiers led by Lieutenant Doren refused to participate in the atrocities. Breaking away from Kurzen's Compound, they established this hidden camp in the north to stage a desperate guerrilla campaign against their former comrades.

Red Rocks. Red Rocks is a towering sandstone bluff in northeastern Mulgore that serves as a sacred ancestral burial ground for the tauren. Here, the most valiant fallen champions are laid to rest, and young braves travel to its quiet heights to seek the wisdom of their forebears. Rising high above the plains of northeastern Mulgore, the crimson formations of Red Rocks mark a sacred threshold between the living world and the next. Tauren tradition reserves this solemn ground for their most valiant heroes—chieftains, defenders, and champions who gave their lives founding and protecting Thunder Bluff. They are laid to rest here in honor, among the graves of their forebears. It is equally a place of spiritual beginning, where young tauren complete their rites of passage by honoring the ancestral graves and communing with the wind.

Refuge Pointe. Refuge Pointe is the primary redoubt for the Alliance and the surviving remnants of Stromgarde within the Arathi Highlands. Perched centrally along the highlands' trade road, it serves as a staging ground to reclaim the shattered capital of Stromgarde Keep and hold back rival forces across the region. Following the devastation of the Third War and the catastrophic fall of Stromgarde Keep, the bulk of Stromgarde's surviving populace fled south toward friendlier lands. Those who remained formed a resolute vanguard, digging in at Refuge Pointe under Captain Nials. Composed of battle-hardened Stromgarde soldiers, League of Arathor forces, and supporting Alliance specialists, the encampment represents the kingdom's last organized stand in its ancestral homeland.

Remtravel's Excavation. Remtravel's Excavation is an archaeological dig site located in the southern reaches of Darkshore. Established by the dwarven Prospector Remtravel, the expedition recently struck ancient subterranean ruins, inadvertently unearthing hostile troggs and stone golems that quickly overran the quarry. Prospector Remtravel came to Darkshore in search of relics of the distant past, establishing an ambitious dig far from the safety of Auberdine. While excavating ancient strata, his team unearthed a swarm of subterranean Gravelflint troggs alongside hulking stone golems buried beneath the earth. The site was instantly transformed from a scholarly quarry into a hazard zone, scattering the miners and leaving Remtravel scrambling to retrieve his most promising findings.

Render's Rock. Render's Rock is a cavern stronghold tucked into the northwestern crags of the Redridge Mountains, sitting near the high pass leading toward the Burning Steppes. Controlled by the fierce Blackrock orcs, it serves as a forward redoubt and an active staging ground for their raids on the valleys below. Carved into the rugged heights north of Lakeshire, Render's Rock serves as a fortified cave system for the invading Blackrock clan. From this defensible redoubt near the mountain pass to the Burning Steppes, veteran Blackrock orcs orchestrate attacks against the local defenders of Redridge. Its shadowed depths are strictly guarded, making any foray inside a perilous undertaking for those seeking to disrupt the orcish supply lines or recover captives lost in the ongoing conflict.

Render's Valley. Render's Valley is a tucked-away encampment held by Blackrock orcs in the southeastern Redridge Mountains. Far less entrenched than the massive fortresses of Stonewatch, it nonetheless poses a persistent threat to nearby travelers and hosts captives taken from surrounding lands. Tucked among the rocky ridges southeast of Lake Everstill, Render's Valley serves as an auxiliary camp for the Blackrock orcs operating in Redridge. Unlike the heavily fortified keeps and stone towers of the northern cliffs, the valley consists of a modest cluster of war tents, banners, and sentry outposts. Despite being smaller and less armed than the clan's core forces, the warriors here raid local roads, harass travelers, and keep captured prisoners in crude cages under guard.

Rethban Caverns. Rethban Caverns is an extensive cave system tucked into the northwestern cliffs of the Redridge Mountains. Infested with aggressive Redridge gnolls, it is best known as the sole source of uncommon Rethban ore. Carved deep into the northwestern mountains overlooking Lake Everstill, Rethban Caverns serves as a fortified redoubt for the local gnolls. Under the cunning leadership of Ardo Dirtpaw, the pack fiercely guards the twisting passages and subterranean chambers, attacking any wanderers who stray too close to their hillside entrance.

Ridgepoint Tower. Ridgepoint Tower is a fortified guard post watching the eastern frontier of Elwynn Forest. Manned by the Stormwind Guard, it serves as an early warning bulwark against hostile incursions threatening the heart of the kingdom. Its guards keep vigil over the perilous corridors leading to neighboring wilderness. Standing sentinel on the high ground of eastern Elwynn Forest, Ridgepoint Tower marks the final bastion of direct Stormwind authority before the untamed wilds take over. The garrison stationed here keeps a constant watch over the surrounding valleys and roads. With tensions mounting across the continent, this stone watchtower ensures that encroaching threats are spotted and checked before they can endanger the farms and settlements closer to Northshire and Goldshire.

Rocktusk Farm. Rocktusk Farm is a small swine ranch situated in northern Durotar just down the road outside the gates of Orgrimmar. Tucked near the fortified approaches of the capital, the stead supplies vital meat and provisions to the city's inhabitants. Carved out of the arid soil of Durotar, Rocktusk Farm is dedicated to raising hardy swine suited to the rough desert climate. Due to Durotar's notoriously dry and stony ground, raising crops is difficult, making domestic swine farms an essential lifeline for feeding Orgrimmar's burgeoning population. Nestled close to the capital's fortified perimeter, the homestead enjoys a degree of safety rarely found in the harsh wilds of the red canyonlands.

Roguefeather Den. Roguefeather Den is a cavern nestled in the south-central reaches of Thousand Needles. Infested with ferocious screeching harpies, the cave serves as a fortified roost where the flock hoards scavenged provisions deep within its shadowed recesses. Carved into the sheer sandstone bluffs of southern Thousand Needles, Roguefeather Den is the foul nesting ground of local harpies. Known for their feral screeching and aggressive territorialism, the harpies treat the cavern as both a secure haven and a storehouse, vigilantly guarding the gathered food and stolen supplies they pile in the dark recesses at the back of the cave.

Rogues' Quarter. The Rogues' Quarter is a dimly lit district in the southeastern wing of the Undercity. It serves as the staging ground for the Forsaken's scouts, assassins, and underworld operatives, along with the craftsmen who support them. Tucked away in the southeastern quadrant of the subterranean city, the Rogues' Quarter gathers the Forsaken's most cunning and lethal survivors. In life, many were thieves, cutpurses, or silent blades for the Kingdom of Lordaeron; in death, their expertise in stealth, poisons, and misdirection has been repurposed to protect the fledgling nation from the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. The district hums with quiet activity, offering a covert haven where operatives sharpen their daggers, brew deadly toxins, and hone clandestine skills.

Roland's Doom. Roland's Doom is an abandoned, shadow-drenched mine tucked into the southeastern hills of Duskwood, just east of the Rotting Orchard. Once an ordinary delve, it has become infamous as a dangerous den overrun by savage worgen. Cut into the ridges east of the Rotting Orchard, Roland's Doom long ago ceased to be a functioning mine. Instead, it serves as a violent staging ground for the Nightbane worgen pack, led by beasts such as Gutspill and Nefaru. The dark tunnels echo with guttural snarls and the reek of damp earth and blood, making it one of the most perilous corners in all of Duskwood for unwary travelers.

Rolling Plains. The Rolling Plains span the southern expanse of Mulgore, stretching between Bloodhoof Village and the border of the Barrens. These windswept grasslands are home to thriving herds of wildlife, but they are also a point of perpetual vigilance due to prowling centaur raiders and aggressive harpies. Spanning south from Bloodhoof Village toward the natural earthen gates leading into the Barrens, the Rolling Plains embody the vast open ranges of the tauren homeland. The area teems with wild game essential to the tribes, including prairie wolves, kodo herds, flatland cougars, and swift tallstriders. For young hunters proving their worth to the elders, these sweeping savannahs serve as an indispensable proving ground where tracking, patience, and reverence for nature are put to the test.

Rotting Orchard. The Rotting Orchard is a blighted, abandoned fruit grove situated in southern Duskwood. Once a source of harvest for the nearby settlement of Darkshire, it has fallen into ruin and is now overrun by ravenous lupine predators known as the Nightbane pack. Located east of the ruined Yorgen Farmstead and west of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, the Rotting Orchard stands as a grim testament to Duskwood's decline. The trees hang heavy with withered, spoiled fruit, while dilapidated barns and outbuildings have been converted into rough encampments by the Nightbane worgen. Nightbane Stalkers prowl the twisted brush, while dark casters known as Shadow Weavers weave their sinister magic amid the decaying timber. The pack answers to the fierce worgen Gutspill and Nefaru, who lair in the nearby mine of Roland's Doom.

Royal Gallery. Tucked away inside Stormwind Keep past the courtyard garden, the Royal Gallery serves as a quiet hall of remembrance. It displays magnificent statues and fine works of art honoring prominent figures from the kingdom's history and the Grand Alliance. The Royal Gallery sits adjacent to the Royal Library, just beyond the verdant interior garden of Stormwind Keep. The hall houses statues of towering figures who shaped the realm: King Llane Wrynn, the fallen ruler of Stormwind; Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras; and Lady Mara Fordragon, patron of the refugees who fled to Lordaeron after the First War. It serves as both a private museum of noble heritage and a quiet retreat for courtly visitors like Lady Dena Kennedy.

Royal Library. Tucked deep within the stone wing of Stormwind Keep, the Royal Library preserves the collective memory, chronicle scrolls, and treatises of the kingdom. Under the watchful eye of Head Librarian Milton Sheaf, its shelves hold crucial records of ancient wars, lost legends, and the realms beyond the sea. While Stormwind Keep bristles with armored guards and courtly intrigue, its Royal Library offers an island of scholarly quiet. Overseen by Milton Sheaf, the hall serves as the premier archive of southern human history, preserving surviving texts from before the First War alongside recent military chronicles and recovered tomes. Alliance scholars, priests, and travelers are free to browse its open treatises, which cover everything from the formation of the original Alliance of Lordaeron to the recent emergence of Thrall's Horde in Kalimdor.

Royal Quarter. The Royal Quarter is the secluded seat of power within the Undercity, serving as the throne room for Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Here, the Banshee Queen directs the Forsaken alongside her dreadlord enforcer, Varimathras, guarded by an elite cohort of Royal Dreadguards. Tucked away behind towering archways and shadowed corridors, the Royal Quarter—also known as the Hall of the Dark Lady—is the political and military nerve center of the Forsaken. Sylvanas Windrunner holds court in this cavernous subterranean chamber, plotting the survival of her free-willed undead and the destruction of the Scourge. Heavily armored Royal Dreadguards stand vigil along the dais, ensuring that uninvited guests and would-be assassins never reach their queen.

Ruined Reaches. The Ruined Reaches comprise the treacherous southern coastline of Azshara near the border with Durotar. Marked by crumbling ancient ruins, shattered shipwrecks, and jagged shallows, these beaches are overrun by aggressive shoreline predators. Amid the desolation, a small gnomish outpost perches high on a cliffside above the surf. Stretching along the southern borders of Azshara just north of Durotar, the Ruined Reaches are a maze of rocky inlets, cliff faces, and debris-strewn sand. Like the Jagged Reef further north, hidden shallows make maritime travel extremely hazardous, leaving numerous ruined vessels broken along the shore. The waters and beaches teem with hostile wildlife, including territorial murlocs, vicious hydras, and armored makrura, making overland transit just as dangerous as navigating the surf.

Ruins of Aboraz. The Ruins of Aboraz are ancient Gurubashi stone ruins nestled along the southeastern cliffs of Stranglethorn Vale. Once part of the sprawling jungle troll empire, the crumbling terraces now serve as the secluded redoubt for the renegade witch doctor Zanzil the Outcast and his mind-addled thralls. Perched on the bluffs southeast of the Ruins of Jubuwal and south of the Crystalvein Mine, the weathered masonry of Aboraz has been transformed into an alchemical testing ground. Zanzil the Outcast was banished by the local tribes and the mainlanders alike, retreating here to brew potent mind-altering concoctions and toxic elixirs. Within the stone courtyards, Zanzil exerts total control over an unsettling menagerie of servitors, including shambling undead ghouls, corrupted troll thralls, and even co-opted coastal naga.

Ruins of Alterac. The snow-covered Ruins of Alterac are all that remain of Alterac City, once the proud mountain capital of the Kingdom of Alterac. Cast out of the Alliance and put under martial law after King Aiden Perenolde's treason during the Second War, the shattered stronghold is now overrun by the brutish Crushridge ogres. Alterac was once an independent human realm carved out of the old Arathor empire, perched high on the trade routes through the mountains. During the Second War, fearing destruction at the hands of the invading Old Horde, King Aiden Perenolde secretly struck a pact with the orcs. When the betrayal was uncovered following the fighting at Caer Darrow, the Alliance of Lordaeron retaliated swiftly. King Terenas Menethil II put the city under martial law and deposed Perenolde. The grand fortifications, church, and palace fell into disrepair as the populace fled or turned to outlawry.

Ruins of Andorhal. Once the agricultural hub and grain distribution center of northern Lordaeron, the Ruins of Andorhal now lie at the heart of the Western Plaguelands as a devastated Necropolis stronghold. Under the dominion of the lich Araj the Summoner, the shattered township crawls with legions of undead abominations, ghouls, and wraiths. Andorhal was the initial staging ground for the plague of undeath in Lordaeron, where grain tainted by the Cult of the Damned was packed and distributed across the human kingdom. Today, the ruined city serves as a sprawling bastion of the Scourge in the Western Plaguelands. Araj the Summoner presides over the center of the ruins, flanked by ghouls, skeletal horrors, and towering flesh golems. Scouting parties of the Scarlet Crusade periodically probe the city's outskirts, but the Scourge maintains iron control over the shattered streets.

Ruins of Constellas. The Ruins of Constellas are the shattered remnants of an ancient night elf settlement in Felwood, nestled near the roots of Mount Hyjal. Today, the once-sacred grounds are overrun by the Jadefire satyrs, who have violently profaned the settlement's moonwell with demonic fel magic. The classical stone arches and crumbling plazas of Constellas reveal that this was once an idyllic night elven community. During the Third War, the Burning Legion's march through Felwood shattered the haven, leaving it exposed to lingering demonic corruption. Now, the foul Jadefire satyrs hold dominion over the stones. Led by Xavathras, they actively tend to a defiled moonwell, transforming pure waters into a font of noxious fel power on behalf of their master, Lord Xavaric.

Ruins of Eldarath. The Ruins of Eldarath are the shattered remains of a pre-Sundering Highborne city perched along the rocky bluffs of Azshara. Once a bastion of Kaldorei arcane scholarship, its fallen plazas and crumbling temples are now overrun by hostile naga. Scholars and adventurers brave the dangerous coastal ruins searching for inscribed tablets and forgotten relics of the ancient past. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, Eldarath was a flourishing night elven city. Renowned Highborne mages gathered here, carving their deepest arcane insights and fundamental magical rules into grand stone tablets left in public squares for their peers to study. The Sundering dropped much of Eldarath into the Bay of Storms. The portions that survived along the eastern cliffs have sat shunned by modern night elves for millennia, slowly claimed by creeping salt spray and ivy.

Ruins of Isildien. The Ruins of Isildien are the sprawling remains of an ancient night elven city in southwestern Feralas, destroyed ten millennia ago during the Great Sundering. Today, the overgrown stonework and cracked temple courtyards are occupied by brutish Gordunni ogres. Ten thousand years ago, before the world shattered, Isildien was a grand night elven settlement nestled in the primordial forests of ancient Kalimdor. Its graceful marble arches and grand terraces stood as monuments to kaldorei civilization and devotion. When the Well of Eternity imploded and tore the continents apart, Isildien fell into ruined desolation, smothered under millennia of untamed jungle growth. Dominating the upper terrace is a colossal domed structure remarkably reminiscent of Darnassus's Temple of the Moon, suggesting the city was once a significant sanctuary dedicated to Elune.

Ruins of Jubuwal. The Ruins of Jubuwal are the crumbling remnants of an ancient Gurubashi settlement located just east of the Gurubashi Arena in Stranglethorn Vale. Once a place of empire and ritual, the ruins have fallen under the sway of the rogue witch doctor Zanzil the Outcast and his bizarre retinue of minions. Situated off the primary thoroughfare cutting through Stranglethorn Vale, Jubuwal was once part of the grand Gurubashi civilization. Today, stone carvings and ivy-draped masonry have been overtaken by Zanzil the Outcast, an eccentric witch doctor known for his potent concoctions and foul voodoo. Zanzil has filled the ruins with an unnatural menagerie of followers, including enthralled ghouls, subjugated naga, and renegade trolls. Desperate fugitives also lurk among the stone arches, such as Jon-Jon the Crow and Maury 'Club Foot' Wilkins, both hiding from the ruthless debt collector 'Sea Wolf' MacKinley back in Booty Bay.

Ruins of Kel'Theril. The Ruins of Kel'Theril are the shattered remnants of an ancient night elven city bordering the frozen expanse of Lake Kel'Theril in central Winterspring. Destroyed ten thousand years ago during the Great Sundering, its frostbitten stone pillars and temples remain haunted by the tormented spirits of Highborne who perished in the cataclysm. Long before Winterspring became a frozen highland, Kel'Theril stood as a grand settlement of the ancient night elven empire. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Great Sundering, the city was blasted into ruin and buried beneath ice and snow. The disaster caught the residing Highborne unaware, binding their souls to the snowbound stones. Today, the spirits of these former spellcasters linger among the frostbitten arches, endlessly reliving their final, catastrophic moments.

Ruins of Lordaeron. The Ruins of Lordaeron are the hollowed-out surface remnants of Capital City, the once-glorious heart of humanity's northern empire. Destroyed when Prince Arthas murdered his father and unleashed the Scourge, the blasted courtyards and throne room now serve as the fortified gateway to the Undercity below. Capital City was once the radiant summit of human civilization, uniting the northern realms under King Terenas Menethil II. When Prince Arthas returned from Northrend carrying the cursed runeblade Frostmourne, the celebrations turned into a slaughterhouse. Arthas slew his father on the throne, leaving the metropolis to rot under Scourge rule. Following the civil war that tore the Scourge apart, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner claimed the devastated palace, securing the surface while expanding the crypts and dungeons beneath into the Undercity.

Ruins of Mathystra. The Ruins of Mathystra are the crumbled remnants of an ancient night elven city sitting along the northern coast of Darkshore. Shattered during the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago, the coastal ruins are now overrun by hostile Stormscale naga and prowled by elusive Ghost Sabers. Ten millennia ago, Mathystra stood as a bustling night elven settlement, home to high-ranking Highborne nobility. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Great Sundering, cataclysmic waves shattered the coastal city, toppling its grand marble arches and washing much of its stonework into the sea. The surviving night elves abandoned the ruined city in favor of smaller woodland villages further south, leaving Mathystra's sunken courtyards and cracked foundations to the relentless coastal elements.

Ruins of Ordil'Aran. The Ruins of Ordil'Aran are the crumbling remnants of an ancient night elf settlement in northwestern Ashenvale, situated between Maestra's Post and Bathran's Haunt. Once a hidden redoubt for shadow cultists, the fallen stones have recently been overrun by the corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs. Little remains of the original Kaldorei architecture at Ordil'Aran save for weathered pillars, cracked arches, and moss-draped stonework. For a time, the isolated ruins served as a lair for the Cult of the Dark Strand, who lurked among the debris to ambush travelers along the northwestern paths of Ashenvale. Recently, however, violent furbolgs of the Thistlefur tribe drove out the cultists in a bloody takeover. The bodies of fallen Dark Strand practitioners still litter the ground while aggressive furbolgs patrol the perimeter, fiercely guarding the site and the ancient Heartswood tree growing within.

Ruins of Ravenwind. The Ruins of Ravenwind are the shattered remnants of an ancient Highborne city nestled in northern Feralas. Today, the crumbling marble structures are heavily infested by the vicious Northspring harpies and guarded by brooding dragonkin. Much like the great city of Dire Maul to the east, the Ruins of Ravenwind stand as a solemn monument to the height and hubris of ancient Highborne civilization before the Great Sundering. Long abandoned by its original kaldorei architects, the site has succumbed to creeping wild foliage, forgotten arcane altars, and the foul roosts of Northspring harpies who prey on anything wandering beneath the shattered arches.

Ruins of Stardust. The Ruins of Stardust are an ancient, fallen night elven holy sanctuary nestled on a lake island in southwestern Ashenvale. Once a serene place of worship, the island's waters and native bog beasts have suffered corruption from demonic rot washing down from Felwood.
