Despite this pervasive blight, luminous stardust shrubs still thrive amidst the crumbling stones, retaining potent restorative power. Resting on a solitary island south of Astranaar, the Ruins of Stardust were once a venerated night elf holy site. Today, an eerie, sickly yellowish-green hue hangs over the water—a consequence of foul demonic rot draining south from Felwood, much like at nearby Iris Lake. The local plant life has twisted into hostile bog beasts that prowl the fallen masonry, their temperaments warped by the tainted lake.

Ruins of Thaurissan. The Ruins of Thaurissan are the scorched remnants of the Dark Iron clan's original surface capital in the Burning Steppes. Once a proud city nestled in the lush northern reaches of the Redridge Mountains, it was blasted to cinders during the War of the Three Hammers when Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan inadvertently summoned the Firelord, Ragnaros. Roughly two centuries ago, following their exile from Ironforge after the death of High King Modimus Anvilmar, the Dark Iron clan journeyed south and established Thaurissan City. At the climax of the War of the Three Hammers, facing total defeat by the combined forces of the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan sought an ultimate weapon to turn the tide. He and seven trusted sorcerers channeled ancient magic deep beneath the earth. Instead of an obedient servant, their ritual ripped open a conduit to the Elemental Plane and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord. The cataclysmic eruption shattered the surrounding mountains, burned the verdant landscape into the ashen Burning Steppes, raised the volcano of Blackrock Mountain, and incinerated the city.

Ruins of Uldum. Tucked into the jagged cliffs of the Valley of the Watchers in southern Tanaris, the Ruins of Uldum consist of an ancient stone hall guarding a sealed Titan facility. Massive stone doors protect its secrets from grave robbers and curious explorers alike. Carved deep into the bedrock of southern Tanaris, the Ruins of Uldum appear to be an antechamber or grand threshold to a far larger, sealed subterranean complex. Its colossal stone gates stand shut against the outside world, and no mechanism or key known to modern scholars has managed to open them.

Ruins of Zul'Mamwe. Tucked away in a mountainous pocket south of the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound, the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe serve as a heavily fortified stronghold for the Skullsplitter troll tribe. Enclosed by steep cliffs on almost all sides, the ancient stone platforms now teem with fierce jungle trolls under the rule of their ruthless chieftain, Ana'thek the Cruel. The Ruins of Zul'Mamwe represent one of the primary seats of power for the Skullsplitter tribe in central Stranglethorn Vale. Cradled within a natural mountain amphitheater, the site has only a single open approach from the north, making it an exceptional defensive redoubt. From atop its weathered ziggurats and stone terraces, Chief Ana'thek the Cruel directs his warriors and witch doctors, defending their territory fiercely against both intruding adventurers and rival jungle troll tribes.

Rustmaul Dig Site. The Rustmaul Dig Site is a ruined excavation in the southern reaches of the Shimmering Flats. Originally established by the dwarven Explorers' League to unearth ancient ruins, the camp fell into tragedy when a Horde war party slaughtered the miners, after which a subterranean silithid swarm emerged. Now abandoned by mortals, the site crawls with hostile insectoids emerging from the caverns below. Prospectors from the Ironforge Explorers' League set up the Rustmaul Dig Site hoping to uncover forgotten artifacts buried beneath the salt flats. Their efforts were brutally cut short when an aggressive Horde war party, led by Moktar Krin, fell upon the camp and wiped out the dwarven excavators. However, the conquerors enjoyed no triumph. The violent clash apparently disturbed a dormant cave network beneath the site, releasing an endless horde of silithid insects that quickly overwhelmed and drove off the battered survivors.

Rut'theran Village. Rut'theran Village is a coastal haven nestled at the southern base of Teldrassil. Serving as the primary maritime harbor for Darnassus, it connects the secluded World Tree to the mainland of Kalimdor via ferry and hippogryph routes. Perched at the water's edge below the towering heights of Teldrassil, Rut'theran Village acts as the threshold between the night elven capital and the wider world. While Darnassus rests within the boughs high above, Rut'theran provides the logistical foundation required to sustain it. A mystical portal arches beneath the trees, whisking travelers between the shore and Darnassus in an instant. For journeys across the sea, ferry service runs from the village docks directly to Auberdine on the mainland of Darkshore, accompanied by flight masters tending dedicated roosts of trained hippogryphs.

Saldean's Farm. Saldean's Farm is the only homestead in Westfall that has not been completely overrun and abandoned to the Defias Brotherhood. Held by the stubborn Farmer Saldean and his wife Salma, the farmhouse remains a rare safe haven amid the region's turmoil. While neighboring lands fell to banditry and mechanical sabotage, the Saldean family refused to abandon their soil. Farmer Saldean and his wife Salma have stayed on their homestead, offering hot food and a kind word to passing travelers. Despite their resilience, the fields remain plagued by rogue harvest golems deployed across the plains, forcing the family to stay close to the farmhouse walls.

Saltspray Glen. Saltspray Glen is a windswept expanse in the northwestern Wetlands hugging the shores of Baradin Bay. Strong coastal gales regularly fling briny seawater across the mossy lowland, which is overrun by aggressive wild raptors. It forms a treacherous natural corridor between neighboring murloc-infested marshes and ancient dwarven ruins. Tucked away in the far northwestern reach of the Wetlands, Saltspray Glen takes its name from the sea spray driven inland off Baradin Bay whenever coastal gales kick up. Bordered by the murloc-haunted waters of Bluegill Marsh to the south and the quiet bluffs of Ironbeard's Tomb to the east, the glen offers little comfort to passing travelers. Packs of cunning wild raptors nest throughout the marshy grass, hunting along the brackish flats alongside their kin from nearby Raptor Ridge and Black Channel Marsh.

Salty Sailor Tavern. The Salty Sailor Tavern is the beating heart of Booty Bay's social life, serving as the port's primary inn and watering hole. Run by the goblin Innkeeper Skindle, it welcomes scoundrels, mercenaries, and travelers from both factions seeking respite from the perils of the jungle. Perched amidst the wooden tiers of Booty Bay, the Salty Sailor Tavern offers warm beds and strong drinks under the watchful eye of the Blackwater Raiders. Behind the bar stands Innkeeper Skindle, keeping glasses filled while a menagerie of buccaneers, traders, and adventurers mingle on neutral ground. Outside the establishment hangs a massive, curious curio—a Zul'Gurub Protector Stone—serving as a strange trophy in this bustling den of commerce.

Sanctum (Stromgarde Keep). The Sanctum is a sacred redoubt tucked behind the chapel within Stromgarde Keep. Sheltered within the crumbling fortress, it guards the entrance to the ancestral Trollbane family crypt and stands as one of the few remaining bastions of the Holy Light amidst Arathi's ruin. While much of Stromgarde Keep has fallen to Syndicate infiltrators and the Boulderfist ogres, the Sanctum and its adjacent chapel have remained under the fierce protection of the surviving Stromgarde defenders. Located behind the house of worship, the Sanctum borders the citadel's graveyard and marks the threshold to the royal crypt where the kings of Stromgarde rest. For the battered loyalists rallying around Prince Galen Trollbane, holding this hallowed ground represents more than a tactical foothold; it is a desperate fight to keep their kingdom's ancestral heritage and faith from being trampled by invaders.

Sandsorrow Watch. Sandsorrow Watch is a sprawling desert outpost located just west of Gadgetzan in Tanaris. The surrounding dunes and ruins are overrun by hostile Sandfury trolls and their reanimated dead, who also hold the eastern watch tower overlooking the waste. Situated directly west of the bustling goblin trading hub of Gadgetzan, Sandsorrow Watch is a grim borderland in the Tanaris desert. The broad expanse is dominated by the Sandfury tribe, who aggressively defend the arid territory alongside legions of shambling troll zombies. An elevated watch tower at the eastern edge anchors the position, providing a fortified vantage point amidst the encroaching desert wilderness and the hostile indigenous tribes.

Sar'theris Strand. Sar'theris Strand forms the western coastline of Desolace, fronting the Veiled Sea. In stark contrast to the barren, grey inland wastes, the shore is sunny and grassy, though it remains perilous due to prowling naga, sea giants, and makrura. Running the length of western Desolace, Sar'theris Strand offers a bizarre respite from the ash and dust of the inland plains. Here, the clifftops and beaches are bright and green. Yet the strand is far from welcoming: serpentine naga patrol the surf alongside towering sea giants and territorial makrura. Shipwrecks litter the shoals, including the ruined Karnitol vessel to the north and small shattered skiffs beneath the towers of Ethel Rethor, proving the sea is as treacherous as the shore.

Sardor Isle. Sardor Isle is a lush island situated off the western coast of Feralas, north of the perilous Isle of Dread. It serves as the home to Feathermoon Stronghold, the primary night elven military bastion in southern Kalimdor. Despite the heavy sentinel presence, parts of the island remain prowled by wild beasts and hostile naga creeping up from the shallows. Resting across the water from mainland Feralas, Sardor Isle is anchored by Feathermoon Stronghold, an impressive elven garrison commanded by General Shandris Feathermoon. While the fortress itself is heavily fortified and linked to the mainland via regular ferry crossings, the broader island is far from tame. Roaming wolf packs claim the timbered slopes, while encroaching naga lurk along the rocky western and northern beaches, constantly testing the resolve of the night elven sentinels.

Sargeron. Sargeron is the crumbled ruin of an ancient night elf city located in northern Desolace. Shattered during the Great Sundering, its former temples of Elune have been defiled and claimed by the Hatefury satyrs, who renamed the grounds in tribute to their master, Sargeras. Before the War of the Ancients broke the continent, this settlement was a flourishing center of worship dedicated to Elune, housing sacred grounds such as Elune's Temple, Sanctuary, and Cathedral. Its true name is lost to antiquity. When the world shattered, the city collapsed into rubble, leaving behind sanctified relics like the Cup of Elune, Elune's Brazier, and Elune's Handmaiden. In the millennia since, corrupted Hatefury satyrs overran the stones, repurposing the sacred Kaldorei architecture into a stronghold honoring the titan Sargeras.

Satyrnaar. Satyrnaar is an ancient, ruined night elf settlement in northeastern Ashenvale that has fallen entirely into the hands of the Bleakheart satyrs. Perched just off the main road between Splintertree Post and Azshara, it is the most intact and easily accessible of the satyr strongholds in the forest. Located northeast of Splintertree Post and southwest of Forest Song, Satyrnaar stands as one of Ashenvale's three primary satyr settlements alongside Xavian and Night Run. Unlike the deeper wilderness ruins, Satyrnaar is relatively well-preserved, featuring pitched tents nestled among crumbled elven architecture. It serves as a bustling camp for the Bleakheart satyrs, making the nearby trade route fraught with peril for travelers moving east toward Azshara. Furthermore, dark ties fester here: the satyrs have forged an alliance with the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand, harboring one of their insidious soulgems amidst the corrupted stones.

Savage Coast. The Savage Coast is the rugged western shoreline of northern Stranglethorn Vale, stretching from the southern border of Westfall down toward Grom'gol Base Camp. Prowled by river crocolisks, shore basilisks, and hostile troll tribes, the strand earns its brutal name with every tide. Running from the cliffs bordering Westfall south toward Grom'gol Base Camp, the Savage Coast marks the perilous western edge of northern Stranglethorn Vale. The sandy banks offer little hospitality: snapjaws, crocolisks, and stonestalkers roam freely among the tide pools and drift logs. Just inland lie territorial jungle troll encampments, making any casual walk along the beach a fight for survival. Offshore, the waters dip toward the submerged dangers of the Vile Reef, ensuring that danger lurks both on the sand and under the waves.

Scarab Dais. The Scarab Dais is an ancient raised platform situated northwest of the Scarab Wall in southern Silithus. It holds the legendary Scarab Gong, the ritual instrument tied directly to the magical wards sealing the qiraji empire within Ahn'Qiraj. Overlooking the shifting sands before the colossal barrier of the Scarab Wall, the Scarab Dais serves as the focal point for the seal placed upon Ahn'Qiraj a millennium ago. Upon this stone dais rests the Scarab Gong, a relic forged during the War of the Shifting Sands. According to ancient night elven history and the bronze dragonflight, striking this gong with the reconstructed Scepter of the Shifting Sands is the only means to shatter the magical barrier and breach the gates. Until that fateful moment arrives, the platform remains an ominous vigil over the sealed insectoid horrors slumbering beyond the wall.

Scarab Wall. The Scarab Wall is a colossal barricade at the southern border of Silithus, before the insectoid empire of Ahn'Qiraj. Conjured at the end of the War of the Shifting Sands, the barrier combined stone and bronze dragonflight sorcery to contain the ancient swarms. It stands as an imposing reminder of the terrible cost of that war. Spanning the desert from east to west, the Scarab Wall was raised a thousand years ago at the conclusion of the catastrophic War of the Shifting Sands. Pushed to the brink of annihilation by the qiraji, the night elf armies and their dragon allies forced the swarms back into their ancient kingdom. To contain them permanently, an immense rampart of desert stone was raised, crowned by a colossal magical barrier woven by the bronze dragonflight. The wall successfully severed the insectoid armies from Kalimdor, though the dread presence locked behind its stone remains palpable.

Scarlet Base Camp. Scarlet Base Camp is a fortified outpost on the eastern shore of Lake Mereldar in the Eastern Plaguelands, just west of Tyr's Hand. Its barricades mark an outer defensive position of the Scarlet Crusade. Perched on the eastern bank of Lake Mereldar, Scarlet Base Camp is a barricaded fortification just west of Tyr's Hand. It marks an outer position of the Scarlet Crusade in the blighted countryside.

Scarlet Basilica. The Scarlet Basilica is a grand cathedral standing at the heart of Tyr's Hand in the Eastern Plaguelands. It serves as the high seat of spiritual and military authority for the Scarlet Crusade in the east. Overseen by Crusader Lord Valdelmar, its halls represent the zealots' unyielding bastion against the Scourge. Rising prominently over the fortified enclave of Tyr's Hand, the Scarlet Basilica acts as the central cathedral and command hub for the Scarlet Crusade's operations in the Eastern Plaguelands. While the Scarlet Monastery far to the west in Tirisfal Glades serves as the order's spiritual heart, this basilica anchors their surviving territorial stronghold against the blighted horrors of Lordaeron. Guarded fiercely by elite crusaders, the cathedral houses Crusader Lord Valdelmar, who directs the local defense and zealously purges any outsiders who dare approach.

Scarlet Monastery. Perched in the northeastern hills of Tirisfal Glades, the Scarlet Monastery was once a peaceful center of scholarship and worship for the Church of the Holy Light. In the wake of Lordaeron's fall, it has become a heavily fortified redoubt for the fanatical Scarlet Crusade. Anyone approaching without red colors is treated as an infected carrier of the plague and executed on sight. Before the Third War, this complex was a proud bastion of Lordaeron's priesthood, serving as a vital center for theological study, sacred archives, and paladin training. When the Kingdom of Lordaeron fell to the Scourge, surviving defenders held the site against the undead. As they devolved into the zealous Scarlet Crusade, they fortified the cloister, turning its peaceful libraries, gardens, and cathedral into an armed citadel.

Scarlet Monastery Armory. The Armory is the fortified martial wing of the Scarlet Monastery, dedicated to manufacturing weapons and training recruits for the Scarlet Crusade. Behind locked iron gates, ranks of zealous footmen and crusaders drill under the fierce command of Herod, the Scarlet Champion. Once part of a peaceful retreat for Lordaeron's priesthood, the monastery was completely overhauled following the Third War. The Armory now serves as the Crusade's primary forge, weapons depot, and combat proving ground. From the open training grounds to the deep weapon halls, ranks of Scarlet footmen, conjurers, and crusaders prepare relentlessly to purge the Scourge and anyone else they deem tainted. The wing remains locked away from the Grand Vestibule, accessible only to those carrying the Scarlet Key found in the neighboring Library.

Scarlet Monastery Cathedral. The Cathedral is the spiritual and military heart of the Scarlet Monastery, housing the Crusade's inner sanctum. Once a serene hall of worship for Lordaeron's priesthood, it now serves as the command seat for High Inquisitor Whitemane and Scarlet Commander Mograine, guarded by the Crusade's most devoted zealots. Once a peaceful center of enlightenment and prayer for the priesthood of Lordaeron, the Cathedral fell into madness in the wake of the Third War. Following the fall of the kingdom to the Scourge, surviving zealots transformed the complex into a fortress of unyielding hatred. Beyond the manicured cloister of the Chapel Gardens lies the grand Crusader's Chapel, where priests and warriors gather in devotion to their crusade. They view all outsiders—regardless of race or faction—as carriers of the undead plague who must be cleansed by blade and holy fire.

Scarlet Monastery Graveyard. The Scarlet Monastery Graveyard is the burial wing of the grand religious complex in northeastern Tirisfal Glades. Once a serene resting place for Lordaeron's clergy and nobility, it has fallen into chilling neglect, overrun by lingering undead and the corrupted magic of the skeletal Bloodmage Thalnos. Before the Third War, this cloistered cemetery served as the peaceful burial ground for the priesthood of Lordaeron. When the Scarlet Crusade fortified the monastery against the undead, their fanatical vigilance failed to cleanse their own crypts. Today, the Graveyard is neglected and deeply haunted. Lingering spirits, restless corpses, and shambling horrors wander the Chamber of Atonement and the mist-covered Forlorn Cloister. Rather than hallowed rest, the dead have found endless torment beneath the crusade's uncaring gaze.

Scarlet Monastery Library. The Library is the eastern wing of the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades, once dedicated to holy scholarship and Lordaeron's priesthood. Now guarded by battle hounds and zealots, it houses ancient archives and rare tomes fiercely coveted by scholars and mages from both factions. Before the Third War, the monastery served as a center for learning and enlightenment for Lordaeron's priesthood. The eastern cloisters housed vast archives of religious thought, historical records, and arcane treatises. When the Scarlet Crusade fortified the monastery against the Scourge, they retained these repositories, turning the quiet halls into an armed redoubt. Today, beastmasters run tracking hounds through the courtyards while battle-mages patrol the shelves, guarding historic volumes like the Compendium of the Fallen and ancient research on the Titans against outsiders.

Scarlet Raven Tavern. The Scarlet Raven Tavern is the social center and primary inn of Darkshire, offering hearthside shelter in the gloom of Duskwood. Presided over by Tavernkeep Smitts, it serves as a gathering spot for beleaguered locals, passing adventurers, and terrified travelers trying to escape the horrors lurking beyond the town's perimeter. Standing near the heart of Darkshire, the Scarlet Raven Tavern keeps its hearth ablaze while eternal dusk chokes the surrounding forest. Years ago, it was a bustling stop where Marshal Haggard and the Stormwind Guard would share pints after patrols. Today, business has withered alongside the town's security. Tavernkeep Smitts tends bar for a somber, anxious clientele huddled against the cold and fear. Even so, the tavern remains an indispensable crossroads for rumors, serving as the starting point for travelers seeking answers to the dark phenomena consuming the region.

Scarlet Watch Post. The Scarlet Watch Post is an isolated watchtower stationed in the rocky hills of northeastern Tirisfal Glades, just north of the Scarlet Monastery. Maintained by a vigilant garrison of Crusaders, its sole purpose is to safeguard the monastery's vulnerable northern flank against flanking assaults. Perched in the rugged heights behind the Scarlet Monastery, the Scarlet Watch Post serves as a critical early-warning bastion for the zealots below. While the southern road up to the monastery gate receives heavy traffic and fortifications, the rugged cliffs along Tirisfal's northern coastline provide a tempting back route for infiltrators. To eliminate this blind spot, the Scarlet Crusade maintains this fortified stone tower—one of several Crusader outposts scattered across Tirisfal Glades. Under the stern command of Captain Melrache, a mixed force of Neophytes, Vanguards, and devout Friars keeps ceaseless vigil over the cliffs, ensuring neither the Scourge nor the Forsaken can surprise the order from behind.

Scholomance. Hidden deep within the crypts beneath Caer Darrow, Scholomance is the Scourge's premier academy of dark arts and necromancy. Here, mortals and undead alike study the Plague of Undeath and fleshcrafting under the sadistic guidance of Darkmaster Gandling and the watchful gaze of the lich Ras Frostwhisper. Before the Third War, Caer Darrow was the proud seat of House Barov, a wealthy aristocratic dynasty holding vast lands across Lordaeron, including Brill, Tarren Mill, and Southshore. Fearing the loss of their wealth and mortality, the Barovs succumbed to Kel'Thuzad's seductive promises of eternal life. They deeded their fortress and ancestral catacombs to the Cult of the Damned, who promptly repaid the nobles by butchering them and turning the sprawling crypts into a hidden necromantic training ground.

Scholomance (Classic). Scholomance is a subterranean academy of necromancy hidden in the crypts beneath Caer Darrow in the Western Plaguelands. Founded by Kel'Thuzad and the Cult of the Damned, it serves as the Scourge's premier training ground for mortal spellcasters seeking to master death. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, the rogue archmage Kel'Thuzad sought recruits for his Cult of the Damned. He found willing benefactors in the wealthy Barov family, lords of Caer Darrow, who traded their lands and crypts in exchange for promised immortality. Instead, the cult slaughtered them and raised them as monstrous undead. Beneath the ruined fortress, the Cult renovated the ancient Arathorian catacombs into an academy for the dark arts. Here, mortal acolytes study plaguecraft, soul binding, and flesh shaping away from watchful eyes, honing the foul magics that shattered Lordaeron.

Screaming Gully. Screaming Gully is the first sprawling subterranean cavern encountered just beyond the entrance of the Wailing Caverns. Bathed in unnatural fungal glow and shallow waters, it serves as the outer redoubt for the corrupted Druids of the Fang and their mutated beasts. Stepping through the threshold of the Wailing Caverns leads directly into Screaming Gully, an echoing chasm where the wind groans through subterranean fissures. Far from the arid Barrens above, the gully is choked with damp overgrowth, humid mist, and aggressive wildlife twisted by the Emerald Nightmare. The Fanglord Lady Anacondra oversees the chamber, surrounded by acolytes of the Druids of the Fang and vicious deviate raptors, while ancient snapping turtles like Kresh patrol the shallow waterways below.

Scuttle Coast. The Scuttle Coast is the wave-battered eastern shoreline of Durotar, situated between Razor Hill and Tiragarde Keep. The rocky beach is strewn with sunken wreckage from Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's Kul Tiras fleet, making it an active scavenging ground for the Horde and a lingering reminder of recent naval warfare. Running along Durotar's eastern edge out to the Great Sea, the Scuttle Coast earned its grim character during the invasion led by Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore. When the Kul Tiras fleet assaulted the fledgling nation of Durotar, fierce battles with the Horde drove many human warships against the jagged shoals, smashing them into splintered hulks. Today, the shoreline is choked with barnacle-encrusted timber, broken rigging, and salvaged cargo barrels. For the nearby encampments of Razor Hill, the coast remains a lingering reminder of how close the Kul Tiran threat still lies.

Sea of Cinders. The Sea of Cinders is an expanse of scorched, windblown terrain lying across the southern stretch of the Searing Gorge, directly north of Blackrock Mountain. Ravaged by elemental heat and relentless gusts, the flat ground constantly vents ash and embers, creating a choking wasteland where very little can endure. Stretching between the rocky cliffs of the Searing Gorge and the imposing bulk of Blackrock Mountain, the Sea of Cinders earns its name from the suffocating haze of particulate and burning grit that constantly sweeps its plains. When the Firelord Ragnaros was summoned into the mortal world centuries ago, the violent upheaval fractured the Redridge Mountains and transformed the surrounding landscape into an arid slag heap. The Sea of Cinders is among the most barren remnants of that cataclysm, an uninhabitable plain where the earth itself refuses to cool.

Sen'jin Village. Sen'jin Village is a coastal settlement on the southern shores of Durotar, serving as a sanctuary for the Darkspear trolls. Established by Chieftain Vol'jin after his people were driven from their ancestral home on the Echo Isles, the hamlet honors his fallen father, the witch doctor Sen'jin. Today, it stands as a fragile haven focused on survival, herbalism, and reclaiming what was stolen. When the dark witch doctor Zalazane betrayed the Darkspear and seized control of the Echo Isles, Chieftain Vol'jin was forced to lead the survivors across the strait to the mainland of Durotar. There, nestled beneath coastal cliffs and looking out over the water, they raised crude huts and established Sen'jin Village. The settlement carries the name of Vol'jin's father, the venerable elder who was captured and sacrificed by murlocs during the Third War. Despite their close alliance with Thrall's Horde, the trolls here live under the shadow of exile, staring daily across the shallows at the home they lost.

Sentinel Hill. Sentinel Hill is the primary bastion of the Alliance in Westfall, serving as the command center for the People's Militia. Surrounded by overgrown fields, scavenging gnolls, and hostile outlaws, this fortified rise is the only secure foothold for lawful citizens in the region. Perched on high ground in central Westfall, Sentinel Hill stands as a vital sanctuary in an otherwise lawless territory. It features a barracks-style inn, a gryphon roost connecting travelers to Stormwind and beyond, a forge, and a lumber mill, all anchored by the imposing Sentinel Tower. While the surrounding lands have fallen to banditry and ravenous beasts, the encampment maintains a fragile perimeter where travelers, beleaguered farmers, and recruits can regroup under the watchful eyes of veteran defenders.

Sentinel Tower. Sentinel Tower crowns the apex of Sentinel Hill, standing as the primary vantage point and headquarters for defenders in Westfall. From its heights, Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia organize their desperate defense against bandits, gnolls, and the growing shadow of the Defias Brotherhood. Erected upon the crest of Sentinel Hill, Sentinel Tower is the military heart of unsettled Westfall. With Stormwind's official army largely absent and withholding aid, local volunteers and veterans banded together to create a central redoubt. The stone tower grants lookouts an unbroken view across the dusty plains, from the abandoned pumpkin patches to the misty shores, giving early warning when rogue highwaymen or gnoll raiding parties begin to prowl.

Sentry Point. Sentry Point is a human watchtower stationed on the mainland edge of Dustwallow Marsh, guarding the causeway bridge that leads directly to Theramore Isle. Maintained by Theramore's forces, it monitors traffic entering and exiting Lady Jaina Proudmoore's island citadel. Positioned at the western end of the long bridge linking Theramore Isle to the treacherous wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh, Sentry Point serves as the stronghold's first line of defense on the mainland. The stone scout tower keeps watch over the swamp road, ensuring that hostile marsh beasts or Horde raiders cannot approach the island city unnoticed.

Sepulcher. The Sepulcher is the primary Forsaken settlement and stronghold in Silverpine Forest. Once an ordinary Lordaeron graveyard and burial crypt overlooking the western coast, it now serves as a fortified sanctuary for the Horde against surrounding regional threats. Perched in the hills above the Lordaeron coastline, the Sepulcher was originally a quiet cemetery and crypt alongside the western road. In the wake of the Third War, the newly emancipated Forsaken repurposed the ancient stone vault and its grounds into an essential outpost. Surrounded by hostile forces on all sides—the feral worgen to the south, wandering Scourge remnants to the east, and Kirin Tor wizards watching from Ambermill—the Sepulcher provides a rare haven of safety, supplies, and command for travelers marching through Silverpine.

Serpent's Coil. Serpent's Coil is a winding network of caves and burnt-out encampments nestled in the eastern ridges of the Blasted Lands. Littered with scorched orcish architecture left behind from the older wars, it serves as a secluded redoubt for dark cultists. Carved into the jagged eastern cliffs of the Blasted Lands, the winding path and caverns of Serpent's Coil wind past ruined orcish huts that date back to the First and Second Wars. Rather than simple beasts, the tunnels harbor cabals of Shadowsworn cultists and practitioners of dark arts drawn to the residual demonic energies permeating the red wastes. Deep within its twisting hollows, they work far from the watchful eyes of Nethergarde Keep.

Sewers. The Sewers are a sprawling subterranean drainage network that provides a secondary entrance directly into the Undercity. Cutting beneath the hills west of the ruined palace of Lordaeron, this conduit allows bat handlers and stealthy travelers to bypass the precarious elevators leading down from the throne room. Before the plague wiped out Lordaeron, these stone culverts served as the mundane sewer lines draining the royal capital. In the hands of Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken, however, the runoff tunnels have been integrated into the Undercity's outer defenses. Emerging west of the surface ruins near a contested Scarlet Watchtower in Tirisfal Glades, the passage provides a level, direct slope inside. Forsaken bat handlers use this cavernous conduit to fly riders swiftly into the subterranean rings, avoiding the sluggish cage lifts entirely. Because it circumvents the heavily fortified surface courtyards, it remains a dangerous vulnerability that hostile infiltrators constantly seek to exploit.

Shadow Grave. Shadow Grave is a stone crypt perched atop the sloping burial grounds above Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. It serves as the physical awakening point where newly liberated Forsaken shake off the stupor of death and the Lich King's faded control. Tucked into the rocky foothills at the top of the graveyard slope above Deathknell, the Shadow Grave is a simple stone mausoleum with an extraordinary purpose. Inside its damp vaults, corpses raised into the mindless servitude of the Scourge gradually awaken to free will. Under the watchful eye of caretakers like Undertaker Mordo, these freshly liberated undead stand up from their stone slabs and take their first shuddering steps into a world that despises them, setting out down the footpath toward Deathknell to pledge themselves to the Banshee Queen.

Shadow Hold. Shadow Hold is a sprawling subterranean complex hidden within the blighted canyon of Jaedenar in western Felwood. Once a sacred night elf barrow den, it has been seized and desecrated by the Shadow Council to serve as their primary bastion on Kalimdor. Beneath the corrupted red earth of Jaedenar lies Shadow Hold, a vast underground labyrinth carved out of what was once an ancient night elf barrow den. Where sleeping druids once rested to tend the Emerald Dream, dark warlocks and demonic servitors now stalk twisted corridors illuminated by fel fire. At its deepest tiers, the cult commands a formidable force under the dreadlord Lord Banehollow, Prince Xavalis, and Shadow Lord Fel'dan, making it the supreme seat of demonic influence in the region.

Shadowbreak Ravine. Shadowbreak Ravine is a secluded mountain hollow tucked away in southeastern Desolace. Cloaked among jagged crags near Magram Village, this eerie ravine serves as a hidden redoubt for the demonic forces and mortal zealots of the Burning Blade. Tucked deep into the barren mountain ridges southeast of Magram Village, Shadowbreak Ravine provides the Burning Blade with a secluded staging ground away from the eyes of wandering centaur tribes. Amid strange, oversized mushrooms and grim ritual encampments, cultists labor alongside summoned demons. Here, dark practitioners invoke fel energies and tend heavy ritual chains, using the natural isolation of the ravine to marshal reinforcements and maintain a firm demonic foothold within the badlands of Desolace.

Shadowfang Keep. Perched on a rugged bluff overlooking Pyrewood Village in southern Silverpine Forest, Shadowfang Keep is the dark lair of the mad Archmage Arugal and his feral worgen. Formerly known as Silverlaine Keep, the fortress fell to ravenous wolf-beasts summoned during the Third War, leaving its ancient halls haunted by the slain nobility and crawling with lupine horrors. Before the Third War, this towering fortress was called Silverlaine Keep, the ancestral seat of Baron Silverlaine and the center of authority for nearby Pyrewood Village. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, desperate wizards sought forbidden means to stem the undead tide. Relying on the dimensional research of the Dalaran mage Ur, the Archmage Arugal summoned the extra-dimensional worgen into Azeroth. The savage beasts tore through the Scourge, but quickly spiraled out of control. Rampaging across southern Silverpine, the pack besieged the stronghold, slaughtering Baron Silverlaine, his family, and Commander Springvale's defenders. Guilt and grief shattered Arugal's sanity; rather than flee, he claimed the fortress, renaming it Shadowfang Keep and adopting the monstrous predators as his 'children.'

Shadowglen. Shadowglen is a secluded, twilit vale nestled within the northeastern boughs of Teldrassil. Dominated by the great barrow-tree Aldrassil, it serves as the safe haven where young night elves take their first steps into service before journeying out into the wider world. Tucked away in the northeastern canopy of Teldrassil, Shadowglen is ringed by high ridges that shelter it from the rest of the world. Bathed in eternal dusk, the vale centers on Aldrassil, a massive barrow-tree whose hollowed trunk houses elders, priestesses, and mentors for young night elves beginning their training. The only route out of the valley leads south through a narrow mountain pass toward Starbreeze Village and Dolanaar, making Shadowglen one of the most naturally fortified and peaceful sanctuaries on the World Tree.

Shadowprey Village. Shadowprey Village is a remote Horde fishing settlement built along the rocky southern coast of Sar'theris Strand in Desolace. Populated largely by Darkspear troll fishermen and supported by tauren service keepers, it acts as a critical coastal outpost and trade lifeline amidst a barren wasteland. Tucked against the cliffs of southern Desolace, Shadowprey Village offers safe harbor in a region notorious for centaur clans and desolate wastes. The settlement is primarily an encampment of troll fishermen whose hauls sustain not only their own village but also inland outposts like Ghost Walker Post. Despite the rough shoreline, towering wooden piers reach out into the ocean, allowing local anglers to brave deep waters and dive for shellfish among the submerged wreckage dotting Sar'theris Strand.

Shadowsong Shrine. Shadowsong Shrine is a ruined hillside sanctuary situated in western Azshara, not far from the Ashenvale border. Haunted by the restless spirits of ancient Highborne, the site bears the illustrious name of the Shadowsong bloodline, though its true historical connection to them remains shrouded in mystery. Perched upon a high hill overlooking the shattered lands of Azshara, the Shadowsong Shrine lies in ancient, overgrown ruin. Like much of the surrounding coast, it is plagued by the lingering apparitions of Highborne ghosts who wander among the fallen stonework, seeking to extinguish any mortal life that trespasses upon their domain. The shrine shares its name with Maiev Shadowsong, the unrelenting warden of Illidan Stormrage. Whether this sanctuary honors her family or dates back to before the Sundering is a secret lost to the ages.

Shadowthread Cave. Shadowthread Cave is a damp cavern carved into the northwest cliffs of Shadowglen on Teldrassil. Traditionally inhabited by indigenous Webwood spiders, the cave has recently turned dangerously aggressive under the dominion of their broodmother, Githyiss the Vile. Tucked away in the shaded perimeter of Shadowglen, Shadowthread Cave has long served as a natural lair for Teldrassil's giant spiders. In earlier years, these arachnids coexisted quietly alongside the nascent boughs of the World Tree. Recently, however, their temperament has turned fiercely territorial. Thick layers of webwood silk now choke the stone corridors, and the aggressive nature of the brood poses an immediate hazard to young kaldorei taking their first steps beyond Aldrassil.

Shady Rest Inn. The Shady Rest Inn was once a welcoming human-built waystation sitting just off the road between the Barrens and Theramore Isle. Today, only charred timbers and smoldering ashes remain following a sudden and violent arson attack. The tragedy left the innkeeper shattered and sparked tension across the marsh as investigators sift through the wreckage for clues. Built to serve travelers navigating the treacherous crossing between Dustwallow Marsh and the Barrens, the Shady Rest Inn stood as an outpost of civilized comfort in a harsh wilderness. That ended when the inn was abruptly razed to the ground in a devastating fire. Innkeeper James Hyal managed to survive the inferno, but the blaze claimed the lives of his wife and child. Traumatized and grief-stricken, Hyal was left with nothing as the ruins became an active crime scene, drawing scrutiny from Theramore authorities desperate to identify who ignited the flames.

Shalzaru's Lair. Shalzaru's Lair is a sprawling, submerged cavern located at the northern tip of the Isle of Dread in Feralas. It serves as a major stronghold for the Hatecrest naga and shelters their formidable master, Shalzaru. From within these damp tunnels, the serpentine invaders coordinate their aggressive presence just south of Feathermoon Stronghold. Carved into the rugged bluffs at the northern end of the Isle of Dread, Shalzaru's Lair is divided into a massive main cavern and a smaller auxiliary chamber, linked together by submerged subterranean waterways. The interior teems with Hatecrest serpent guards and spell-weaving sorceresses on high alert. Deep within the recesses dwells Lord Shalzaru, the serpentine overlord directing the Hatecrest brood across the island. Its proximity to Sardor Isle poses a direct, constant threat to the night elf Sentinels garrisoned at Feathermoon Stronghold just across the channel.

Shaper's Terrace. Perched high on the northern bluffs above Marshal's Refuge, the Shaper's Terrace is a mysterious overlook marked by ancient titan architecture. It is named in honor of Khaz'goroth the Shaper and bears quiet witness to the primordial experiments that shaped Un'Goro Crater. Overlooking the lush, prehistoric basin of Un'Goro Crater, the Shaper's Terrace holds monumental stone edifices left behind by the titans. Believed to be dedicated to Khaz'goroth the Shaper, this high plateau stands as a testament to the celestial architects who cultivated the crater as a living laboratory for early life on Azeroth. From these elevated stones, ancient entities once observed and directed the flora and fauna below. Its cold stone arches and massive metallic plinths stand in stark, enigmatic contrast to the untamed wilderness thriving directly beneath them.

Shatter Scar Vale. Shatter Scar Vale is a scorched basin in central Felwood, located just north of Bloodvenom Falls. It marks the ground zero where demonic infernals crashed into northern Kalimdor during the Third War. Today, the craters still burn with fel fire and host lingering remnants of the Burning Legion. During the Third War, the Burning Legion rained living siege engines down upon northern Kalimdor. Shatter Scar Vale bore the brunt of this celestial assault. Demonic infernals plummeted from the skies, tearing through the ancient canopy and smashing deep craters into the earth. The violent impact shattered the terrain, leaving blackened hollows that smolder with unholy fire to this day. Though the Legion was shattered at Mount Hyjal, the infernals and lingering lesser demons never truly dispersed, maintaining an entrenched foothold in the scarred earth.

Shattered Strand. The Shattered Strand is a wild, rugged coastline flanking the northern rim of the Bay of Storms in Azshara. Dominated by crashing surf and crumbling ancient ruins, the beach crawls with hazardous marine beasts and tribal aquatic creatures. Stretching along the northern edge of the Bay of Storms, the Shattered Strand is far from a peaceful shoreline. The rocky beaches and tidal shallows are heavily inhabited by aggressive wildlife, including towering sea giants, multi-headed hydras, and snapping makrura, alongside encampments of coastal murlocs. Crumbling elven architecture overlooks the waves, anchored by landmarks such as the ancient Temple of Arkkoran and the solitary Tower of Eldara. For travelers navigating Azshara's treacherous cliffs, descending to this isolated strip of coast means confronting some of the region's deadliest amphibious threats.

Shifting Mire. The Shifting Mire forms the vast, muddy heart of the Swamp of Sorrows, lying just west of the Pool of Tears. Its name comes from the strange, restless silt beneath the murky water, which seems to drift and gather under the influence of an unseen force. Spanning the central reaches of the marshland, the Shifting Mire is an unsettling expanse where solid footing is hard to come by. The silt along the swamp floor shifts and collects as though moved by a living will, driven by a strange, ambient energy permeating the peat. Amidst the drifting mud prowl predatory swamp jaguars, massive sorrow spinners, and hungry sawtooth crocolisks, while bands of broken draenei known as the Lost Ones stalk the sunken paths.

Shimmer Ridge. Shimmer Ridge is a rugged highland nestled in northern Dun Morogh, directly west of the Gates of Ironforge. Occupied by hostile Frostmane trolls, the rocky heights consist of two camps joined by a rickety bridge and are renowned as the sole harvesting ground for potent shimmerweed. Perched along the craggy slopes just west of Ironforge's mighty entryway, Shimmer Ridge serves as an active redoubt for the Frostmane troll tribe. Divided into twin camps straddling a chasm and linked by a wooden span, the enclave is heavily guarded by troll scavengers and their tamed mountain boars. Their proximity to the main roadway and the dwarven capital poses a continuous nuisance to travelers and mountain patrols, who must constantly remain on guard against opportunistic raids from the high ground.

Shimmering Flats. The Shimmering Flats is an expansive salt flat lying at the southeastern tip of Thousand Needles, bordering the desert of Tanaris. Once the bed of an ancient lake, this sun-baked expanse is now famous for the high-speed mechanical rivalries of the Mirage Raceway and a harsh population of desert beasts. Stretching out under the blinding southern sun, the Shimmering Flats is a vast dried lakebed devoid of vegetation, dotted with the sun-bleached bones of turtles and even the wooden wreck of an ancient sailing vessel. Its sheer, unbroken level surface makes it the premier testing ground on Kalimdor for experimental vehicles. At the center of the flats lies the Mirage Raceway, where gnome and goblin tinkerers constantly clash to see whose rocket cars, gyrocopters, and engines can achieve the highest speeds—often resulting in fiery crashes and smoking craters across the white crust.

Shining Strand. The Shining Strand is the strip of shoreline hugging Lordamere Lake along eastern Silverpine Forest, stretching south from the Ruins of Lordaeron toward the rugged foothills of Alterac. Its shallows are home to settlements of aggressive Vile Fin murlocs, making the lakeshore dangerous ground for unseasoned travelers. Running along the eastern edge of Silverpine Forest, the Shining Strand borders the misty waters of Lordamere Lake. The Vile Fin tribe of murlocs has established several aggressive settlements along these shallows, posing a deadly hazard to anyone attempting to travel the lake road, while feral worgen roam the deep woods of Silverpine behind the shore.

Shrine of Aessina. The Shrine of Aessina is a sacred elven landmark nestled in the forests of southwestern Ashenvale, dedicated to the ancient forest spirit of nature and wild creatures. Located between Maestra's Post and Astranaar, it stands as a serene sanctuary amidst the growing border friction in the region. Tucked away west of Astranaar, the Shrine of Aessina honors the mysterious Wild God who embodies the heart and spirit of the deep forests. For generations, night elves and their woodland kin have revered this quiet place, communing with nature away from the bustling main roads. However, with the Horde pushing into Ashenvale to gather timber and establish footholds, sacred grounds throughout the territory face an uncertain peace.

Shrine of the Dormant Flame. Perched atop the highest peak northwest of the Valley of Trials, the Shrine of the Dormant Flame is a secluded sanctuary revered by Horde shaman. Guided by its solitary keeper, Telf Joolam, initiates make the treacherous climb to commune with the element of fire and prove their spiritual mastery. Reaching the Shrine of the Dormant Flame requires braving a narrow, winding trail that begins along the Southfury River at the southwestern edge of the Southfury Watershed. High above the red cliffs of Durotar, the mountain summit offers a commanding view of the surrounding lands, though a single misstep along the precipice means certain death. In this quiet refuge wanders Telf Joolam, a solitary hermit tasked with overseeing sacred rites. For aspiring orc and troll shaman undertaking the ritual Call of Fire, the shrine's brazier serves as the crucible where they must ignite slumbering coals using the ember of a vanquished elemental, proving their power to commune with and respect the destructive spirits of flame.

Shrine of the Fallen Warrior. Perched upon a secluded ridge west of the Crossroads lies the Shrine of the Fallen Warrior, a quiet memorial overlooking the sweeping red savannahs of the Barrens. Marked by a stone plinth bearing the initials 'MK' and the body of a fallen orc warrior, it is watched over by the gentle presence of a Spirit Healer named Koiter. Tucked away high upon the hills northwest of the Crossroads, the Shrine of the Fallen Warrior stands as an unusually solemn haven amidst the dust and peril of the Barrens. To find it, travelers must scale a winding ridge pathway southwest of the summit until they reach a gentle mound. Upon the summit rests a carved stone monument, its plinth carved with the initials 'MK'. Before it lies the armored form of an orc warrior at rest, watched over day and night by a named Spirit Healer known as Koiter. There are no battle horns here, only quiet contemplation honoring a champion who walked Kalimdor's lands.

SI:7 (Stormwind City). Tucked away in the eastern corner of Old Town, this unassuming stone manor houses the headquarters of SI:7, the kingdom of Stormwind's elite intelligence and espionage service. Behind its heavy doors, spymaster Master Mathias Shaw and his senior operatives quietly monitor threats to the realm, coordinating undercover agents across the kingdom. To the casual passerby in Old Town, this fortified stone structure looks little different from a standard manor or military barracks. In truth, it serves as the nerve center for Stormwind Intelligence, Section 7. Directed by Master Mathias Shaw, SI:7 gathers intelligence, conducts surveillance, and executes covert operations to protect the kingdom from subversion. While the city guard patrols the open cobblestones and the Royal Guard defends Stormwind Keep, SI:7 works in the margins, training handlers and dispatching stealthy operatives against foreign enemies, saboteurs, and domestic unrest alike.

Silver Stream Mine. Silver Stream Mine is a depleted dwarf mine located in northern Loch Modan, nestled between Algaz Station and the Stonewrought Dam. Once a rich silver vein for the kingdom of Ironforge, the excavated hollow was repurposed as a Miners' League supply depot before being overrun by vermin. Today, Tunnel Rat kobolds squat inside the tunnels, hoarding stolen equipment and rare mineral curiosities. Silver Stream Mine once flowed with precious ore, contributing heavily to the silver reserves of Ironforge. In time, the dwarf pickaxes dug deep enough to exhaust the primary veins, turning the sprawling chambers into an empty subterranean complex. Rather than abandon the hard-won earthworks, the Miners' League transformed the shafts into a secure storage depot for tools, mining crates, and regional equipment. It also serves as the only known source of rare Charged Rift Gems, which draw inquisitive arcanists searching for delicate tailoring reagents.

Silverwind Refuge. Silverwind Refuge is a serene night elven settlement nestled in south-central Ashenvale, situated just north of Mystral Lake. Protected by Sentinels, it offers a welcoming haven for travelers along the forest's wooded trails. Resting between the placid waters of Mystral Lake and Iris Lake to the north, Silverwind Refuge stands as one of the major night elven waystations in central Ashenvale alongside Astranaar. It boasts craftsmen and wilderness trainers who instruct travelers in herbalism, alchemy, skinning, and hunting. Guarded by stalwart Sentinels, the retreat serves as a peaceful rest stop for allies moving through the shaded ancient woods.

Silverwing Grove. Tucked away in south-central Ashenvale near Fallen Sky Lake, Silverwing Grove serves as the staging grounds for the Silverwing Sentinels. From this fortified hollow, night elf warriors muster Alliance forces to push back the Warsong Clan loggers tearing through the forest. Hidden beneath the emerald canopy southwest of Silverwing Outpost, Silverwing Grove is a crucial military staging post for the Silverwing Sentinels. Rather than a tranquil woodland retreat, it functions as the operational heartbeat for the night elves' bitter territorial contest against the Horde's lumber operations in Warsong Gulch. High-ranking Alliance officers, provisions, and scouts gather here, organizing skirmishes and marshaling champions to defend ancient Ashenvale against orcish expansion.

Silverwing Outpost. Silverwing Outpost is a fortified night elf garrison positioned in south-central Ashenvale, east of the Falfarren River. Commanded by Duriel Moonfire, it stands as the easternmost bastion of the Alliance against the Horde in the contested woodland. Situated southwest of Splintertree Post and just north of the border with the Barrens, Silverwing Outpost holds an inherently perilous strategic position. By sitting on the eastern side of the Falfarren River—territory heavily contested and patrolled by the Horde—the outpost serves as a direct shield for night elf holdings deeper in the forest. Duriel Moonfire and her Silverwing Sentinels remain under constant siege from nearby orcs determined to purge night elf forces from the area entirely.

Sishir Canyon. Sishir Canyon is a rugged gorge in the Stonetalon Mountains, carving an eastward path through the craggy heights. Thickly swarmed by monstrous Deepmoss spiders and choked in webbing, it serves as the dangerous approach to the Ruins of Eldre'thar. Travelers who brave its tangled depths must contend with venomous arachnids and their brooding matriarch. Branching off the mountain roads of the Stonetalon range, Sishir Canyon is a treacherous natural corridor cutting toward the ancient Ruins of Eldre'thar. Rather than a quiet mountain trail, the gorge has been thoroughly overrun by Deepmoss spiders. Their sticky silken sheets and clusters of egg sacs smother the stony ground and rock walls, transforming the ravine into a living nest. Travelers and sentinels seeking the night elven ruins beyond must cut their way through swarms of aggressive webspinners.

Skittering Dark. The Skittering Dark is an abandoned mine and shadowy woodland hollow in western Silverpine Forest. Infested by aggressive giant spiders, the cavern and its surrounding woods are thick with webbing and danger for unwary beasts and travelers. Tucked into the hills just east of the western coast of North Tide's Run, the Skittering Dark was once a working mine. Today, the shafts are completely choked with cobwebs, serving as the sprawling nest of giant spiders. With the shadowy weaver Krethis haunting the exterior, the spiders hunt anything that strays too close.

Skull Rock. Skull Rock is a cavern tucked into the eastern coastal cliffs of Durotar, just east of Orgrimmar. It serves as a fortified coven for the demonic Burning Blade cult right under the capital's nose. Hidden beneath the crags of northeastern Durotar, Skull Rock is one of the most perilous strongholds of the Burning Blade cult in the region. Dark cultists, fel-worshipping orcs, and summoners gather deep within the winding tunnels to practice demonic arts and weave conspiracies against the nascent Horde. The cell is led by the dangerous warlock Gazz'uz, whose operations pose an imminent threat to the nearby gates of Orgrimmar and travelers traversing the eastern shoreline.

Slag Pit. The Slag Pit is an extensive subterranean mining excavation nestled inside the Cauldron of Searing Gorge. Overseen by ruthless Dark Iron taskmasters and slavers, these fiery tunnels are driven by forced labor under the shadow of Blackrock Mountain. Trespassers must contend not only with hostile dwarf overseers, but also ravenous incendosaurs prowling the lower levels. Carved into the depths of the Cauldron, the Slag Pit represents the grinding industrial engine of the Dark Iron dwarves in Searing Gorge. Day and night, enslaved workers are driven to extract rich ores and minerals under the lash of brutal overseers and taskmasters. The environment is harsh and suffocating, dominated by scorching heat, choking dust, and the clatter of iron picks. The Dark Irons maintain ruthless discipline over their excavation, violently repelling any outside interference with their supply lines to Blackrock Depths.

Slaughter Hollow. Slaughter Hollow is a secluded ogre mound tucked away in the snowy heights of the Alterac Mountains. Controlled by the brutish Crushridge clan, it stands as a rough camp rather than a bustling settlement. Travelers rarely have reason to trespass unless hunting ogres or exploring the frozen mountain passes. Hidden high in the peaks bordering Hillsbrad and Alterac, Slaughter Hollow serves as an encampment for the local Crushridge ogres. Like many ogre mounds scattered across the highlands, it is littered with makeshift bonfires, discarded bones, and crude shelters. While other ogre dens in the mountains see frequent conflicts over territory or stolen supplies, Slaughter Hollow remains largely quiet and bypassed by major military campaigns.

Slaughtered Lamb. Tucked away in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, the Slaughtered Lamb appears to be nothing more than a quiet, seedy tavern. Beneath its floorboards, however, sprawling catacombs hide the sanctum and training grounds of the Alliance's illicit warlocks. On the surface, the Slaughtered Lamb offers little more than dark corners and sparse patronage, attended by barkeep Jarel Moor, who warns casual visitors to stay away from the shadows. That warning is literal. Descending through the back passages reveals a subterranean complex of crypts and summoning circles, where human warlocks and transfer practitioners from Khaz Modan openly study fel arcana sheltered from the disapproving eyes of the Church of the Holy Light and the Kirin Tor.

Slither Rock. Slither Rock is a secluded cave tucked into the far northeastern cliffs of the Burning Steppes, past the perilous Terror Wing Path. It serves as the solitary refuge of Cyrus Therepentous, a sharp-tongued black dragonspawn with his own hidden agenda. Tucked away in the scorched crags beyond the Terror Wing Path, Slither Rock is easy to overlook amid the fiery wastes of the Burning Steppes. Far from the roaring forges and marching orc warbands of Blackrock Spire, this remote hollow houses the solitary black dragonspawn Cyrus Therepentous. While dragonspawn are typically fiercely loyal soldiers of the Black Dragonflight, Cyrus maintains a strange, cantankerous independence here, willing to converse with mortal travelers rather than slaughtering them on sight—though never without a steady stream of insults.

Slithering Scar. The Slithering Scar is a sprawling silithid hive dominating the southern cliffs of Un'Goro Crater. Home to the aggressive Gorishi swarm, its excavated tunnels and organic spires represent a dangerous insectoid encroachment into the primeval basin. Gouged into the red earth and rock of southern Un'Goro, the Slithering Scar stands as an alien intrusion against the lush prehistoric landscape. The hive is controlled by the Gorishi silithid, an organized strain of insectoids that have honeycombed the cliffs with damp burrows and egg chambers. Within these subterranean warrens, workers and tunnelers nurture vast clutches of eggs and grubs alongside towering wasp broods. More alarmingly, the colony cultivates fledgling silithid colossi, monstrous behemoths intended to carve an uncontested path through the crater's ecology. Strange crystalline formations nestled within the hive pulse with unnatural resonance, acting as focal points for the colony's dark, coordinated will.

Sludge Fen. Sludge Fen is a toxic industrial oil field operated by the Venture Company in the northeastern Barrens. Once a pristine, crystal-blue pool, the wetland was transformed into an oily quagmire after the goblins erected drilling platforms and machinery. The operation is overseen by Supervisor Lugwizzle and attracts constant industrial espionage and sabotage from rivals in Ratchet. Before the arrival of the Venture Company, Sludge Fen was an untainted pool of crystal-clear water fed by natural springs in the arid Barrens. Driven by the relentless pursuit of profit, the Venture Company constructed an extensive oil-drilling operation over the basin, despoiling the wetland into a sludge-filled reservoir coated in heavy industrial waste. Overseen by Supervisor Lugwizzle, goblin drillers, engineers, and overseers pump crude oil around the clock, heedless of the environmental ruin. The waters are now thick with runoff and toxic byproducts, leaving the native aquatic life choked beneath the grease.

Solliden Farmstead. Solliden Farmstead is an active human pumpkin farm nestled in western Tirisfal Glades, just north of Deathknell. It represents a rare anomaly in northern Lordaeron: living native farmers who survived the Plague of Undeath and cling fiercely to their soil under the shadow of the Scarlet Crusade. While most of Lordaeron fell to ruin and rot, the fields of Solliden Farmstead still produce healthy crops. Today, these surviving human farmers live under the watchful shield of the Scarlet Crusade patrolling from a nearby tower. Traumatized and insular, they defend their homestead with unyielding hostility, striking at any outsiders who draw near—Horde and Alliance alike.

Sorrow Hill. Sorrow Hill is an expansive graveyard resting south of Andorhal in the Western Plaguelands. Once the final resting place for commoners, soldiers, and nobility alike, it has been corrupted by nearby plague cauldrons into a sprawling haven of restless undead. Before the Third War, Sorrow Hill served as the primary burial ground for the city of Andorhal and its surrounding townships. When the Scourge unleashed the Plague of Undeath, the gravediggers could not keep pace with the dead. Neatly kept crypts were soon surrounded by shallow, poorly marked earthen pits. Eventually, terrified survivors ceased traditional burials entirely, instead resorting to burning the corpses of their loved ones in a mass pyre to the south out of fear they would rise. Before the town fell completely, the remnants of the populace entombed Lord Uther the Lightbringer atop the cemetery's high ground, bestowing upon the hill its tragic name.

Sorrowmurk. The Sorrowmurk is the treacherous wetland expanse lying directly east of the Pool of Tears in the Swamp of Sorrows. Long dominated by patrolling green dragonkin guarding the approach to the Sunken Temple, it remains one of the most perilous regions in the eastern marshes. Stretching out along the eastern edge of the Pool of Tears, the Sorrowmurk is a dense and murky mire that borders the Forbidding Sea. For years, the waters and tangled boughs have crawled with ferocious green dragonspawn and towering drakes, remnants of the brood sent to watch over the submerged temple of Atal'Hakkar. Their presence ensures that only seasoned travelers dare wander through its sodden reaches.

South Gate Outpost. South Gate Outpost is a fortified dwarven mountain post situated along the South Gate Pass between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Manning the snowy southern road, its mountaineers guard the steady flow of travelers walking between Ironforge's frigid heights and the temperate valley of the Loch. Perched midway through the high mountain cut of South Gate Pass, South Gate Outpost marks the frontier between the snowy slopes of Dun Morogh and the verdant basin of Loch Modan. Stationed here are Ironforge mountaineers tasked with patrolling the rocky switchbacks and keeping dangerous wildlife off the main highway. Compared to their hard-pressed kin up at North Gate Outpost, the defenders here have largely secured their stretch of road, allowing travelers, pilgrims, and trade wagons headed toward Thelsamar to journey in relative safety.

South Gate Pass. South Gate Pass is the primary mountain thoroughfare linking the snowy heights of Dun Morogh with the valley basin of Loch Modan. Flanked by dwarven tunnels and watch posts, it serves as the most direct route between Ironforge and the settlement of Thelsamar. Carved straight through the Khaz Modan range, South Gate Pass connects Dun Morogh's high mountains to the rolling valley of Loch Modan to the east. Travelers leaving the cold slopes behind emerge through stone archways into the warmer dwarven heartlands. Because the path leads straight toward Thelsamar, it carries a steady flow of mountaineers, couriers, and newly trained adventurers setting out from the capital.

South Seas. The South Seas encompass the vast, sun-drenched waters separating the southern regions of Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Lapping at the shores of Tanaris and Stranglethorn Vale, these tropical expanses are famed for lucrative trade routes, perilous reefs, and brazen pirate crews. Spanning southward beneath the Great Sea and the Maelstrom, the South Seas wash against the deserts of Tanaris and the lush jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Since the Great Sundering shattered the primeval continent ten thousand years ago, this ocean has nurtured remote tropical islands, unique oceanic beasts, and independent merchant networks. Goblin shipping cartels, operating out of havens like Steamwheedle Port and Booty Bay, maintain tenuous shipping lanes across the waves. However, the waters remain notoriously lawless, crawling with corsairs, Bloodsail buccaneers, and predatory sea life that prey on any vessel daring to venture far from shore.

South Tide's Run. South Tide's Run is the lonely southwestern coastline of Silverpine Forest, stretching along the cold waters of the Great Sea. Flanking the forested interior, these damp sands and surf serve as the southern complement to North Tide's Run. Stretching along the southwestern edge of Silverpine Forest, South Tide's Run forms a desolate boundary between the woods and the Great Sea. Unlike the protected eastern roads that lead down toward the Greymane Wall, this open shore takes the brunt of the western tides, serving as a bleak coastal wilderness largely untouched by the settlements inland.

Southern Gold Road. The Southern Gold Road is the vital desert thoroughfare stretching through the southern half of the Barrens, linking the central plains to the Great Lift. It serves as an indispensable artery for regional trade, carrying caravans, supplies, and wayfarers traveling between distant reaches of Kalimdor. Officially beginning at the stone bridge dividing the northern and southern halves of the Barrens, the Southern Gold Road runs directly south until it meets the Great Lift leading down into the Thousand Needles. Like the northern portion simply named the Gold Road, this dusty highway derives its moniker from the endless stream of lucrative merchant caravans that trek along its length. Despite constant harassment from local quilboar tribes and predators prowling the savannah, it remains one of the busiest long-distance paths on the continent, ferrying goods between remote outposts and bustling ports.

Southern Savage Coast. The Southern Savage Coast encompasses the long strand of beaches and tidal waters hugging southwestern Stranglethorn Vale. Flanked by the treacherous depths of the South Seas, these shores are home to prowling wildlife, hostile naga, and the ever-present threat of coastal raiders. Stretching down the western edge of the southern jungle, the Southern Savage Coast marks where the mainland gives way to the warm currents of the South Seas. Divided from the northern Savage Coast by the submerged ruins and perils of the Vile Reef, this coastline skirts inlets near the Gurubashi Arena and Nek'mani Wellspring before tapering off past Booty Bay and Janeiro's Point. While the beaches offer open ground compared to the suffocating interior jungle, travelers must contend with aggressive reptilian predators, predatory naga hunting the shallows, and passing corsairs scanning the strand for easy prey.

Southfury River. The Southfury River is one of the most prominent waterways on central Kalimdor, carving a swift and wide path southward from the heights of Mount Hyjal. It forms the natural border separating Azshara from Ashenvale, as well as Durotar from the Barrens, before plunging into the Great Sea near Ratchet. Beginning high in Mount Hyjal, the Southfury drops over dramatic cascades before coursing through central Kalimdor. Its roaring waters serve as a clear geographic divide, separating the sacred forests of Ashenvale from ancient Azshara, and dividing the arid hills of Durotar from the savanna of the Barrens. Only a few strategic bridges dare cross its swift currents—most notably the heavy span guarding the rear gates of Orgrimmar and the crossing connecting Durotar to the Barrens. The river eventually empties into the Great Sea via a cascading waterfall just northeast of the neutral port of Ratchet.

Southmoon Ruins. The Southmoon Ruins are ancient stone remains situated in southern Tanaris, just north of the Valley of the Watchers. Long claimed by the brutish Dunemaul ogres, the crumbling stonework preserves remnants of the ancient troll civilization that dominated the desert before the sands swallowed it. Rising out of the blistering wastes of southern Tanaris, the Southmoon Ruins stand as a weathered testament to the ancient troll empires that once ruled Kalimdor's southern reaches. Like nearby Eastmoon and Noonshade, its stone pillars and altars have weathered thousands of years of wind and abrasive grit. The site has often served as a squalid camp for the Dunemaul ogres, who show little reverence for the craftsmanship of the past, using the ancient structures purely for shelter and territory.

Southpoint Tower. Southpoint Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower situated at the western border of Hillsbrad Foothills, overlooking the road to Silverpine Forest. Once a human sentry post, the shattered structure is now utilized by Forsaken scouts keeping watch over Alliance movements in the region. Standing just south of the highway linking Silverpine Forest and Hillsbrad Foothills, Southpoint Tower was originally built by the Kingdom of Lordaeron to guard traffic moving between the eastern farmlands and the western woods. Following the Third War and the Scourge's destruction of the kingdom, the stonework fell into ruin. Today, it stands roofless and crumbling, an isolated relic of human dominion in a fractured territory.

Southridge Beach. Southridge Beach stretches along the southern shores of the Bay of Storms in central Azshara. Once a grand district of the ancient kaldorei city of Eldarath, its shattered ruins are now overrun by hostile naga, murlocs, and towering sea giants. Southridge Beach forms the southern boundary of the turbulent Bay of Storms. Thousands of years ago, this coast was part of the magnificent Highborne city of Eldarath, but the Great Sundering broke the land and plunged most of its palaces beneath the tides. Today, crumbling marble pillars and weathered stone pavilions dot the sand. Rather than scholars and noble courtiers, the strand is contested by aggressive Spitelash naga, prowling makrura, vicious hydras, and scavenging murloc tribes. Even massive sea giants occasionally wander ashore from the deeps.

Southshore. Southshore is a coastal human port in the Hillsbrad Foothills and one of the Alliance's few surviving strongholds in fallen Lordaeron. Once a sleepy fishing village, it now stands as an embattled bastion facing constant hostility from the Forsaken garrison at Tarren Mill, rogue Syndicate bandits, and shoreline monsters. Southshore first rose to prominence during the First War when refugee boats carrying survivors from the fallen kingdom of Stormwind landed upon its beaches. Though contested and overrun during the Second War, it was rebuilt and later endured the horrors of the Third War. Today, while the rest of Lordaeron lies in ruins or under the rule of the Forsaken, Southshore remains fiercely loyal to the Grand Alliance. It offers shelter to displaced human survivors, veteran paladins of the Silver Hand, and scholars of the Kirin Tor.

Southshore Town Hall. Southshore Town Hall serves as the administrative seat of the southern coast of Hillsbrad Foothills, standing as one of the last functioning centers of Lordaeron's civil authority. From inside, Magistrate Henry Maleb coordinates local defenses and governs the town's surviving populace. The hall is a vital hub for the Alliance as they struggle to maintain a foothold in the plagued north. While much of Lordaeron lies shattered under Scourge corruption and Forsaken expansion, Southshore's town hall maintains the semblance of an intact human government. Magistrate Henry Maleb oversees daily governance from his office here, working alongside officials like Kundric Zanden to secure resources and preserve civic order. In a region surrounded by aggressive undead, Syndicate rogues, and Hillsbrad's fierce border skirmishes, the hall is the nerve center directing the town's survival against constant threats.

Southwind Village. Southwind Village is the haunted ruin of a night elf outpost located in the sands of Silithus. Wiped out by the qiraji during the War of the Shifting Sands, its streets are now bound by the restless spirits of fallen defenders and prowling silithid. Southwind Village once served as a primary night elf stronghold during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands a thousand years ago. When the qiraji legions breached the defensive perimeter, Valstann Staghelm—son of Archdruid Fandral Staghelm—led a detachment to hold the village. The defense ended in utter disaster: the night elven defenders were overwhelmed and slaughtered, and Valstann himself was dragged away into captivity by General Rajaxx. The village was completely ruined, leaving its former buildings fractured under the sun.

Spirit Rise. Spirit Rise is the northwest mesa of Thunder Bluff, serving as the tauren capital's premier sanctum for spiritual and shamanic study. Overseen by spiritual guides such as the Skychaser tribe, it features sacred training halls above and descends into the cavernous Pools of Vision below. Perched high upon the bluffs overlooking the plains of Mulgore, Spirit Rise is devoted to communion with the elements and ancestor spirits. Connected to the central mesa by rope bridges, it houses the Hall of Spirits and the Spiritual Healing pavilion, where young and veteran shaman gather to deepen their connection with the earth, air, fire, and water. The Skychaser tribe maintains a strong presence across the rise, guiding seekers through ancient traditions.

Spirit Rock. Spirit Rock is a sacred crag perched in the rugged bluffs above the Valley of Trials in Durotar. Reached by a winding trail known as the Hidden Path, it serves as a secluded holy site where initiates commune directly with the elemental forces of the land. Overlooking the red canyon where young Horde warriors and scouts begin their training, Spirit Rock stands as an altar of communion. Isolated from the clatter of the Valley of Trials, it is approached only via the Hidden Path winding up the rocky ridgeline. Aspiring shaman make pilgrimages to this desolate outcrop to drink the traditional sapta, piercing the veil of the physical world to hear the rumblings and whisperings of the earth itself.

Splinterspear Junction. Splinterspear Junction is a strategic fork in the main road winding through the heart of the Swamp of Sorrows. Dominated by a rugged orc watchtower and regularly patrolled by Horde sentries, it divides the path between northern retreats and southern outposts. Standing near the center of the Swamp of Sorrows, Splinterspear Junction divides travelers between two paths: the northern trail leading toward the Lost One refuge of the Harborage and the Fallow Sanctuary, and the southern road running directly past the fortress of Stonard toward the Blasted Lands. An ancient orcish watchtower oversees the split, garrisoned and patrolled by active Horde troops. For members of the Horde, it serves as a secure landmark in a treacherous marsh; for Alliance travelers, it represents a deadly ambush point along an already unforgiving trail.

Splintertree Post. Splintertree Post is the primary Horde fortress in eastern Ashenvale, situated northwest of Felfire Hill. Established by Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan during the Third War, it serves as a heavily fortified bulwark against the night elves and a staging ground for territorial expansion. Carved straight out of the ancient woodlands, Splintertree Post serves as the Horde's main military and logistical hub across eastern Ashenvale. Originally established by Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan when orcs first pressed into the forest during the Third War, it remains a heavily armed enclave defended primarily by orcish and tauren scouts and warriors. Armed with a flight master, an inn, and steady supply lines to Orgrimmar, it anchors the Horde's contested presence beneath the canopy.

Splithoof Crag. Splithoof Crag is a fortified settlement of the Galak centaur, tucked along the northern cliffs of Thousand Needles. It serves as one of the tribe's major enclaves alongside the high mesas, guarding the entrance to Splithoof Hold. Travelers traversing the canyon floor must contend with aggressive Galak patrols roaming near the bluffs. Nestled against the sheer northern rock face of Thousand Needles, Splithoof Crag sits just east of the towering Darkcloud Pinnacle. It is an established enclave of the Galak centaur, complete with crude tent encampments and dirt pathways cutting through the crags. At the heart of the village against the cliffside lies Splithoof Hold, a subterranean cavern holding the Cloven Hoof, an ancient relic of the centaur safeguarded by a sacred brazier.

Splithoof Hold. Splithoof Hold is a deep cavern stronghold carved into the stone of Splithoof Crag in Thousand Needles. Held by the Galak centaur tribe, the cavern serves as a fortified den and houses the Ancient Brazier, a site holding an eternally burning sacred flame. Tucked away inside Splithoof Crag, Splithoof Hold serves as a fortified redoubt for the Galak centaur. Unlike the windswept canyon floor, this enclosed cave offers them shelter, defensible chokepoints, and a secure sanctuary from rival tribes and travelers passing through the Needles.

Stagalbog. The Stagalbog is a dense, waterlogged marsh stretch across the southern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Bordering the southern mountain range just below the Pool of Tears, it remains an untamed wilderness. Stretching beneath the shadow of the southern crags, the Stagalbog is typical of the Swamp of Sorrows: stagnant water, drooping reeds, and tangled vegetation. It sits immediately south of the sunken ruins of the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, caught between the tainted lake and the rocky boundary of the region. Apart from rough wildlife, civilization has established no foothold here.
