Stagalbog Cave. Stagalbog Cave is a damp subterranean cavern situated in the Stagalbog within the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. It serves as a fortified den for the Marsh murlocs and their sinister spiritual leader, the Swamp Talker. Tucked away in the murky eastern wetlands of the Swamp of Sorrows, Stagalbog Cave provides shelter from the relentless swamp rains for the local murlocs. Known as the Marsh tribe, these amphibious creatures aggressively guard the winding cavern chambers alongside their chief mystic, the Swamp Talker. Travelers venturing near the sunken mire of the Stagalbog often hear their gurgling calls echoing out across the mossy banks, warning trespassers away from their nesting grounds.

Staghelm Point. Staghelm Point is an ancient night elven watchtower perched atop a craggy peak in northeastern Silithus. Overlooking the encroaching dunes and the nearby caverns of Twilight's Run, the tower stands as a vigil against the ancient threats haunting the desert. Rising high above the arid flats of northeastern Silithus, Staghelm Point is crowned by a solitary night elf tower. The outpost serves as a lonely sentinel, keeping watch over the wasteland and the shadowed cultists lurking in nearby caves like Twilight's Run. Watched over by Ralo'shan the Eternal Watcher and accompanied by a bronze drake circling overhead, the tower bears the proud and tragic name of the Staghelm lineage—a reminder of the immense sacrifices made by the Kaldorei during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands.

Stagnant Oasis. The Stagnant Oasis is one of the precious bodies of water nestled in the arid heart of the Barrens, positioned between the Gold Road and the Merchant Coast. Ringed by lush palms and contested by Kolkar centaur, its murky waters and surrounding shores sustain unique local wildlife, including snapping turtles and wandering kodos. Tucked away east of the Gold Road and inland from the Merchant Coast, the Stagnant Oasis provides a vital pocket of greenery amid the dusty scrubland of the Barrens. Like its neighboring waters, the pool supports dense foliage and aggressive snapjaw turtles, while weakened Barrens kodos often stray here away from the massive herds of the Field of Giants. However, travelers must tread carefully: Kolkar centaur maintain encampments along its banks, fiercely guarding the water rights against any who wander into their territory.

Starbreeze Village. Starbreeze Village is an abandoned night elf settlement situated east of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Once a tranquil woodland hamlet, it has recently fallen to the maddened furbolgs of the Gnarlpine tribe. The ruined settlement now stands as a glaring symbol of the growing corruption seeping into the roots of the World Tree. Located southeast of Shadowglen and just down the road from Dolanaar, Starbreeze Village was once home to peaceful night elf families living beneath the boughs of Teldrassil. Today, the village lies in shambles, its wooden structures overrun by aggressive Gnarlpine furbolgs. Driven wild by a sinister corruption afflicting the boughs of the World Tree, the beast-men drove the elven residents out and now defend the ruined grounds ferociously.

Starfall Village. Starfall Village is a tranquil night elven sanctuary nestled along the snowy road of Winterspring. As the sole Alliance outpost in the frozen valley, it offers shelter and supplies to travelers braving the bitter northern chill. It also stands watch over the nearby barrow den. Situated northwest of the goblin trading post of Everlook and south of Frostsaber Rock, Starfall Village represents the lone bastion of Alliance civilization in Winterspring. Composed of traditional night elven timber lodges, the settlement serves as a haven for wayfarers, providing critical supplies and a warm hearth amid the harsh mountain elements. Despite its peaceful appearance, the village remains ever vigilant, positioned adjacent to a quiet, unoccupied barrow den.

Steamwheedle Port. Steamwheedle Port is a bustling coastal outpost on the eastern shore of Tanaris, directly connected to Gadgetzan. Operated by the neutral Steamwheedle Cartel, it serves as an essential sea link across the South Seas while constantly warding off encroaching Southsea Pirates. Tucked against the dunes along the South Seas, Steamwheedle Port offers the inland desert city of Gadgetzan a direct lifeline to maritime trade. Run by the Steamwheedle Cartel, the settlement bustles with dockhands, traders, and sea captains braving the treacherous waters. Supply vessels regularly ply the routes between here and distant goblin trading posts, bringing valuable mechanical components, luxuries, and raw materials into southern Kalimdor.

Steelgrill's Depot. Steelgrill's Depot is a bustling engineering workshop and repair station situated directly east of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Overseen by Beldin Steelgrill and a crew of craftsmen, it serves as a frontline hub for vehicle maintenance, tinker supply runs, and salvage efforts. Nestled just off the snowy road east of Kharanos, Steelgrill's Depot buzzes with the clamor of clanking metal, hissing steam vents, and the hum of experimental engines. Dwarven miners and eccentric gnome engineers gather here amid heavy machinery, mechanized walking frames, and stockpiles of raw ores hauled out from nearby quarries. With Dun Morogh facing relentless trogg disruptions and mechanical supply shortages, Beldin Steelgrill and his crew keep Alliance machinery in working order, serving as an indispensable stop for travelers seeking spare parts or technical guidance in the bitter cold.

Stendel's Pond. Stendel's Pond is a small, possibly tainted body of water located southwest of Sentinel Hill in Westfall. Surrounded by prowling gnolls and marked by nearby graves, it remains one of the few fresh fishing spots in the parched countryside despite its sinister hazards. Tucked away southwest of Sentinel Hill, Stendel's Pond offers a quiet break from Westfall's dusty plains, though danger is never far. Gnolls roam the muddy banks, while scattered skeletons and a pair of lone graves suggest that either the waters or the beasts around it are fatal to careless travelers. Anglers still risk the trek for schools of sagefish.

Stillwater Pond. Stillwater Pond is a quiet, stagnant body of water resting just west of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Once a beloved picnic and swimming spot for the living children of Lordaeron, it has decayed into a murky pool inhabited by skeletal fish and prowled by dangerous scavengers. Before the Third War and the ravages of the Plague of Undeath, Stillwater Pond served as a tranquil retreat for the folk of Tirisfal Glades. Families from nearby hamlets gathered on its grassy banks for afternoon picnics, and children too young to brave the treacherous depths of Brightwater Lake learned to swim in its shallows. Today, the idyllic waters have turned lifeless and gray. The living have long vanished, leaving only skeletal fish darting beneath the surface and wandering undead drifting through the surrounding woods.

Stonard. Stonard is a fortified Horde outpost situated in the southern marshes of the Swamp of Sorrows. Originally built during the First War, it serves the modern Horde as an essential foothold in the southern Eastern Kingdoms and an observation post watching the Blasted Lands. Stonard stands as one of the oldest orcish settlements on Azeroth. First established when the Old Horde spilled through the Dark Portal into what was once the Black Morass, Stonard and its sister post, Rockard, anchored the invaders' lines. Though abandoned and damaged during the fallout of the Second War, Thrall's New Horde moved to reconstruct and garrison Stonard. Anchored by a traditional orcish Great Hall and fortified burrows, the outpost is now a vital island of Horde authority in an untamed, perilous mire.

Stone Cairn Lake. Stone Cairn Lake is a ring-shaped body of water resting in northeastern Elwynn Forest. At its center lies an island crowned with Heroes' Vigil, a memorial to the fallen of the First War. Once a tranquil site for reflection, the lake is now troubled by hostile murlocs along its shores and renegade wizards occupying the isle. Stone Cairn Lake earns its name from the prominent stone memorial erected on the large island in its center. Known as Heroes' Vigil, this monument was raised to honor the heavy loss of human life suffered during the First War against the Orcish Horde. Families and pilgrims once traveled safely to the island to pay respects to the fallen, gazing across the calm waters at the solemn stonework. Today, however, dangerous renegade wizards have established a camp directly beside the memorial, turning a place of sacred remembrance into a hostile redoubt.

Stonebull Lake. Stonebull Lake is a serene, horseshoe-shaped body of water wrapping around Bloodhoof Village in central Mulgore. Fed by the pristine natural runoff of the plains, it provides vital fresh water, abundant fish, and peaceful shores for the young tauren coming of age under Cairne Bloodhoof's guidance. Curving around Bloodhoof Village on three sides, Stonebull Lake defines the geography of central Mulgore. A wooden bridge crosses the lake's narrowest stretch, carrying the main dirt road between the settlement and the great mesa of Thunder Bluff to the north. Its calm waters are filled with native fish, making its banks a favored spot for resting hunters, weary travelers, and apprentice fishers learning their trade under the sweeping open sky.

Stonefield Farm. Stonefield Farm is a working homestead situated in southern Elwynn Forest. It is home to the Stonefield family, who have long been locked in a bitter feud with their neighbors, the Maclures. Nestled in the rolling greenery south of Goldshire, Stonefield Farm produces crops for the realm while maintaining a fierce, decades-long grudge against the nearby Maclure Vineyards. The bad blood between the households leads to petty squabbles, mutual accusations of theft, and constant tension. Yet beneath the hostile bickering, young Tommy Joe Stonefield has fallen secretly in love with Maybell Maclure, creating a quiet romance that could either bridge the divide between the families or ignite further outrage.

Stonefire Tavern. The Stonefire Tavern is the primary inn serving travelers inside the mountain city of Ironforge. Situated in the bustling Commons district just north of the city gates, it provides a warm hearth, strong dwarven ale, and a resting place for adventurers arriving from across Khaz Modan. Located immediately north of the fortress gates in the Commons, the Stonefire Tavern serves as the premier public house in Ironforge. Run by Innkeeper Firebrew alongside his daughter Gwenna, the inn offers weary wayfarers hearty meals, local brews, and lodging beneath the mountain. Whether seeking respite from the harsh mountain snows of Dun Morogh or looking to trade tales and supplies before venturing deep into the city, travelers from all corners of the Alliance routinely gather around its roaring hearth.

Stonemaul Ruins. The Stonemaul Ruins are the shattered remnants of Stonemaul Village, once the proud Kalimdor settlement of the Stonemaul ogres. After being driven out by the black dragonflight, the clan fled north, leaving their former home overrun by Firemane dragonspawn. Following their migration to Kalimdor, the Stonemaul ogres founded their settlement amid the murky swamps of Dustwallow Marsh. The village became famous when the beastmaster Rexxar braved the clan's lethal trials, slew their brutal chieftain Kor'gall, and rallied the ogres to defend the nascent Horde against Admiral Proudmoore's forces. After the war, Rexxar left the ogre Mok'Morokk in command. Under Mok'Morokk's selfish rule, the village fell into decline and was ultimately ambushed and shattered by the black dragonflight. The surviving ogres fled north to establish Brackenwall Village, while Onyxia's brood took complete possession of the ruins.

Stonesplinter Valley. Stonesplinter Valley is a rugged mountain vale in southwestern Loch Modan overrun by hostile troggs. Once a pristine alpine hollow, it has transformed into a fortified encampment under the brute command of the trogg chieftain Grawmug. Tucked away among the craggy slopes of southwestern Loch Modan, Stonesplinter Valley was once a quiet alpine hollow. That serenity ended when waves of subterranean troggs clawed their way to the surface across Khaz Modan. Claiming the valley for their own, the Stonesplinter tribe rapidly turned the rocky defiles into crude fortifications, digging dens, erecting barricades, and hunting anything that strays too close. Their numbers make the valley an open wound on roads through southern Loch Modan, forcing Mountaineers out of Thelsamar to hire adventurous mercenaries willing to cull their ranks and eliminate their towering warlord, Grawmug.

Stonetalon Peak. Stonetalon Peak is an ancient night elven sanctuary tucked into a verdant alpine valley at the northwestern edge of the Stonetalon Mountains. Sacred to the kaldorei and cared for by local druids, it serves as the primary bastion of the Alliance in these craggy heights. Perched high above the arid dust of the lower ranges, Stonetalon Peak opens into a lush, mist-shrouded sanctuary. Long considered sacred and steeped in ancient magic, the valley holds ruins dating back millennia to when the region housed temples honoring Queen Azshara before the Great Sundering. In the modern era, kaldorei Sentinels and druids have restored a measure of peaceful stewardship here, maintaining a tranquil refuge complete with a barrow den and a vital Alliance flight roost.

Stonewatch. Stonewatch is a fortified stronghold in central Redridge Mountains, built to defend the surrounding human lands from northern invasions. Formerly manned by Stormwind soldiers, the fortress has fallen under the brutal control of the Blackrock orcs, posing an immediate threat to nearby Lakeshire. Positioned over the cliffs near Stonewatch Falls, Stonewatch comprises a heavily built tower and keep designed to guard the approaches from the Burning Steppes. Originally held by Lakeshire's defenders, the fortification fell when the rogue warlock Morganth forged an alliance with the Blackrock clan. Infused with dark magic, the invading orcs overwhelmed the local human garrison—the 12th Sabre Regiment—and claimed the fortress. Although Morganth eventually turned on his allies and withdrew to the nearby Tower of Ilgalar with an army of Shadowhide gnolls, the Blackrock orcs retained a stranglehold over the keep under the command of Warlord Gath'Ilzogg and Lieutenant Tharil'zun.

Stonewatch Falls. Stonewatch Falls is a scenic waterfall and deep mountain pool situated in the eastern reaches of the Redridge Mountains, fed by the outflow of Lake Everstill. Cascading down the hillside beneath the looming heights of Stonewatch, its isolated waters are claimed by a hostile tribe of murlocs. Pouring from the eastern river of Lake Everstill, Stonewatch Falls cascades down the rugged terrain beneath the Blackrock orc stronghold of Stonewatch. The plunging water carves out a deep pool tucked against the mountainside. Despite its natural beauty, travelers rarely linger to admire the view; a vicious band of murlocs infests the pool, building crude reed hovels and preying upon any foolish enough to trespass along the water's edge.

Stonewatch Keep. Stonewatch Keep is a fortified stone stronghold looming in eastern Redridge Mountains, once built and manned by the Kingdom of Stormwind. It has fallen to an invading host of Blackrock orcs, serving as the forward operational base from which their warlords terrorize Lakeshire. Stonewatch Keep originally defended the eastern ridges and guarded the settlers of Lakeshire against hostile incursions. That peace shattered when the renegade warlock Morganth struck an alliance with the Blackrock clan. Bolstered by dark magic, the orcs stormed the fortress with vicious ferocity, overwhelming the human defenders and taking the keep for themselves. Although Morganth later abandoned his allies to raise the nearby Tower of Ilgalar and subjugate local gnolls, the Blackrock invaders successfully consolidated their grip over Stonewatch, transforming a former bastion of the Alliance into a fortified staging ground for their assault on the valley.

Stonewatch Tower. Stonewatch Tower is a stone guard tower standing within the overrun stronghold of Stonewatch in northeastern Redridge. Once maintained by the defenders of Lakeshire, the outpost was captured by the Blackrock clan to monitor the surrounding ridges and secure their mountain bastion. Built by the Kingdom of Stormwind to guard the high mountain passes above Lake Everstill, Stonewatch Tower served as the forward scouting sibling to Stonewatch Keep. From its elevated vantage point, sentries could easily watch the eastern ridges and alert Lakeshire to any threats advancing from the Burning Steppes. That early warning network collapsed when Warlord Gath'Ilzogg's Blackrock orcs swept down from the heights, overrunning the human defenders and claiming the stronghold for their own war effort. Today, the tower bristles with Blackrock sentinels, ensuring no Alliance scouts approach the fortress undetected.

Stonewrought Dam. The Stonewrought Dam is a colossal dwarven engineering marvel standing along the northern rim of Loch Modan. It holds back the waters of the Loch, creating the massive highland lake while draining the Wetlands below into habitable marshes. Stretching across the canyon east of Dun Algaz, the Stonewrought Dam is widely regarded as one of the great structural triumphs of dwarven civilization. Designed by the master Dark Iron architect Franclorn Forgewright, the barrier was built using his pioneering stonewrought technique. By trapping the waters of the mountain basin, the dam doubled the surface area of the Loch while steadily lowering water levels to the north, allowing the marshy basin of the Wetlands to emerge from a once completely flooded valley.

Stonewrought Pass. Stonewrought Pass is an underground tunnel cut directly through the southern mountains of Loch Modan into the blighted expanse of the Searing Gorge. Masterfully engineered by the famed architect Franclorn Forgewright, this passage connects the Valley of Kings directly to Dustfire Valley. Heavy iron gates secure both ends to protect peaceful dwarven lands from the volcanic terrors to the south. Carved out of the bedrock by the legendary master architect Franclorn Forgewright—famed also for the massive Stonewrought Dam—the Stonewrought Pass serves as a direct corridor between the pastoral beauty of Loch Modan and the scorched wastes of Searing Gorge. Emerging in Loch Modan near the colossal Valley of Kings, it cuts straight through the mountain ridge down into Dustfire Valley. Because Searing Gorge is infested with Dark Iron dwarves and fiery beasts, the Ironforge mountaineers keep the passage locked tight behind heavy gates to prevent danger from spilling into the north.

Stormrage Barrow Dens. The Stormrage Barrow Dens are an ancient subterranean sanctuary carved beneath the sacred valley of Moonglade. Named for Malfurion Stormrage, these quiet earth-hewn chambers serve as a dedicated resting place where druids enter long, restorative slumbers to wander the Emerald Dream. Barrow dens serve as sacred havens throughout night elven lands, providing druids a safe subterranean refuge where their physical bodies can lie undisturbed during lengthy immersions in the Emerald Dream. The Stormrage Barrow Dens are particularly esteemed within the sacred realm of Moonglade. Named in honor of Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage, these winding earthen halls hold both ancient reverence and quiet vigil. While some druids like Clintar Dreamwalker still slumber safely within its alcoves, the absence of the great Archdruid himself casts a somber shadow over the hollowed roots and peaceful glowing lanterns.

Stormwind City. Stormwind City is the majestic capital of the Kingdom of Stormwind and the military and political heart of the Alliance. Rebuilt from ashes following its destruction in the First War, it stands as the greatest remaining bastion of human power in Azeroth following the fall of the northern kingdoms. Founded over a millennium ago by Arathi descendants migrating south, Stormwind flourished as a vibrant coastal capital ringed by stone ramparts and powered by swift rivermills. That grandeur ended in the First War when the Orcish Horde besieged the city, breached its defenses, and burned it to the ground, forcing Sir Anduin Lothar to lead surviving refugees across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. Following the victory of the Alliance in the Second War, the Stonemasons' Guild undertook the monumental task of rebuilding the capital into the gleaming fortress of white stone, canal networks, and towering spires that stands north of Elwynn Forest today.

Stormwind Gate. The Stormwind Gate is the monumental fortified entryway connecting Elwynn Forest to Stormwind City. Guarded constantly by royal sentries, this threshold stands as the primary boundary between the tranquil woodlands and the grand Valley of Heroes. Towering over the southern road of Elwynn Forest, the Stormwind Gate serves as both a defensive bulwark and a ceremonial threshold for the capital. Sentinels of the Stormwind City Guard maintain a constant watch across the stone portal, guarding the approaches from the forest while regular patrols march between the outer arch and the Valley of Heroes. Despite lingering unrest throughout Elwynn, the massive iron-and-stone gates remain wide open to welcome travelers, merchants, and returning defenders into the heart of the Alliance.

Stormwind Keep. Stormwind Keep stands high above the capital as the stone fortress and seat of power for the Kingdom of Stormwind. Rebuilt after its ruin in the First War, it currently houses the royal court of the young boy-king Anduin Wrynn and his regent, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. Perched upon a plateau overlooking the entire city, Stormwind Keep serves as both a palace and a military bastion. The original stronghold was burned to the ground by the Old Horde when King Llane was assassinated near the end of the First War. Raised anew upon the old foundations after the Alliance reclaimed the kingdom, the reconstructed keep houses not only the grand throne room and the War Room, but peaceful garden courtyards and the expansive Royal Library.

Stormwind Stockade. Tucked away beneath the canals along the northern edge of the Mage Quarter, the Stockade serves as Stormwind's high-security penitentiary. Intended to lock away murderers, political dissidents, and foreign enemies, the subterranean fortress has recently collapsed into total chaos following a coordinated inmate rebellion. Ordinarily overseen by Warden Thelwater, the Stockade is where the kingdom deposits its most volatile prisoners, ranging from cutthroats and Defias operatives to captured Blackrock orcs and Dark Iron dwarves. However, a violent uprising orchestrated by the cunning Defias conspirator Bazil Thredd has entirely displaced the prison guards. The inmates now roam freely in the lower cells, turning the fortress into a fortress of riots. Thelwater, having barely secured the entry thresholds, relies on independent adventurers to plunge into the subterranean corridors and suppress the revolt before it spills out into the canals.

Stormwind Stockade (Classic). The Stormwind Stockade is a fortified underground prison beneath the canal district of Stormwind City. Originally built to contain petty criminals, violent mercenaries, and political subversives, it has recently plunged into chaos following a violent inmate revolt. Tucked away off the canals between Old Town and the Mage Quarter, the Stockade serves as the primary penal facility of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Presided over by Warden Thelwater, the subterranean complex houses an assortment of the realm's most dangerous malefactors: cutthroats of the Defias Brotherhood, a marauding Blackrock orc, an ogre, and even an infiltrating Dark Iron dwarf. Recently, a coordinated prison riot orchestrated by the cunning felon Bazil Thredd overwhelmed the garrison, driving out surviving guards and leaving the convicts in full control of the interior halls.

Stoutlager Inn. The Stoutlager Inn is the lively heart of Thelsamar and a primary haven for travelers in Loch Modan. Tucked beneath the rolling hills of the loch, it offers warm hearths, strong dwarven ale, and a bustling gathering place for adventurers and locals alike. Situated squarely in the settlement of Thelsamar, the Stoutlager Inn serves as the center of community life for western Loch Modan. Miners, mountaineers, and wayfarers passing between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands stop here to trade rumors, secure lodging, and share hearty drafts of dwarven brew. While the wilderness beyond Thelsamar grows increasingly hostile with trogg and kobold activity, the thick stone walls and roaring fires of the Stoutlager provide a dependable sanctuary.

Strahnbrad. Strahnbrad is a ruined human settlement nestled in the northeastern heights of the Alterac Mountains, near the border of the Western Plaguelands. Once famous as the site of Prince Arthas Menethil's early defense against Blackrock orc raiders, the town has since fallen into decay and serves as a fortified stronghold for the criminal Syndicate. Originally a holding of the Kingdom of Alterac before being absorbed into Lordaeron following the Second War, Strahnbrad's misfortune began on the eve of the Third War. Blackrock clan orcs raided the settlement to take human sacrifices for the Burning Legion, leading Prince Arthas Menethil and the Knights of the Silver Hand to ride to its defense. Though Arthas drove the raiders away and slew their slave master, the town was heavily bloodied. When Lordaeron crumbled beneath the Scourge shortly thereafter, Strahnbrad was abandoned to the elements.

Stratholme. Stratholme was once the jewel of the Eastweald and the second greatest city in the Kingdom of Lordaeron. During the Third War, it became the site of Prince Arthas Menethil's infamous culling after its citizens consumed grain tainted by the Plague of Undeath. Today, the ruined metropolis still burns, serving as the Scourge's primary stronghold in northern Lordaeron. Long before its downfall, Stratholme stood as a cornerstone of northern civilization. Emerging centuries ago from the Arathi expansion into the Eastweald, it flourished into Lordaeron's second-largest settlement, renowned for holy shrines and sacred water capable of resisting dark sorcery. Prior to the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol gathered at the city's chapel to establish the Order of the Knights of the Silver Hand, ordaining legends like Uther the Lightbringer. Throughout that war, Stratholme served as a vital port, supply hub, and northern oil refinery for the Alliance of Lordaeron, enduring an assault by the Old Horde before rebuilding in victory.

Stratholme (Classic). Stratholme, once northern Lordaeron's proudest jewel and the birthplace of the Silver Hand, is now a burning ruin serving as the Scourge's regional capital. Divided between the fanatical Scarlet Crusade and Baron Rivendare's undead legions, the cursed city remains locked in endless, violent war. Before the Third War, Stratholme was the northern powerhouse of Lordaeron and the sacred birthplace of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Its fate was sealed when Prince Arthas purged the city, slaughtering his own subjects after infected grain brought the plague within its walls. Left smoldering and ruined, Stratholme was claimed by the Scourge. Today, under the overarching authority of the lich Kel'Thuzad and the field command of Baron Rivendare, the city serves as the primary base for undead power in the Plaguelands.

Stratholme Main Gate. The Stratholme Main Gate stands as the grand, burning entrance to Lordaeron's northern metropolis in the northwestern Eastern Plaguelands. It provides direct access through the city's ruined avenues toward King's Square and the crusader fortifications within. Stratholme was once the pride of northern Lordaeron, famed as the birthplace of the Order of the Silver Hand. Today, its colossal arched main gates mark the threshold of an ongoing nightmare. It was here during the Third War that Prince Arthas turned on his mentor, Uther the Lightbringer, and purged his own citizens before the Plague of Undeath could claim them. The city has burned relentlessly ever since, transformed into the primary Scourge stronghold in the region.

Stratholme Service Entrance. The Stratholme Service Entrance is a fortified rear gateway located at Eastwall Gate in the northern Eastern Plaguelands. It provides direct, covert access into the Scourge-controlled eastern quarter of the burning city, bypassing the grand front gates. While the monumental Main Gate of Stratholme opens into King's Square and provides a route toward the Scarlet Bastion, the Service Entrance breaches the city's eastern fortification at Eastwall Gate. Today, it leads directly into the corrupted heart of the metropolis: Elders' Square and the blighted pathways leading toward Baron Rivendare's slaughterhouses.

Stromgarde Keep. Stromgarde Keep is the battered, divided capital of the fallen human kingdom of Stromgarde in the Arathi Highlands. Once the proud cradle of human civilization known as Strom, the fortress is now partitioned between hostile Syndicate rogues, invading Boulderfist ogres, and a desperate remnant of royal defenders under Prince Galen Trollbane. Long before it bore its current name, this fortress was founded nearly three millennia ago as Strom, the first capital of the unified human empire of Arathor under King Thoradin. It served as the staging ground for humanity's victory against the forest trolls and was the birthplace of human wizardry, where high elven magi tutored the first hundred human spellcasters. Over centuries, as younger sister kingdoms like Dalaran, Lordaeron, and Stormwind rose and prospered, Strom's influence waned. Renamed Stromgarde by the stubborn Trollbane dynasty who stayed behind, it remained a proud warrior bastion throughout the Second War, anchoring the Alliance of Lordaeron against the Orcish Horde.

Sun Rock Retreat. Sun Rock Retreat is a hidden Horde sanctuary nestled high within the central peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains, just south of Mirkfallon Lake. Dominated by tauren and orcish forces, it serves as the Horde's primary staging ground and supply post in the region. Beyond its strategic utility, the settlement rests upon sacred ground long revered by the tauren for its deep spiritual resonance. Tucked away in a mountain basin south of Mirkfallon Lake, Sun Rock Retreat has long held spiritual importance for the tauren. According to ancient tradition, An'she, the Sun, kissed the very mountain peak where the village stands. For generations before the Horde's arrival, tauren shamans and pilgrims journeyed here to perform rituals bridging the mortal veil, drawing strength from the land's strong bond to the spirit world.

Sundown Marsh. Sundown Marsh marks the deepest, westernmost reaches of the Wetlands where stagnant waters meet treacherous wildlife. Despite the prowling raptors, oozes, and gnolls, an eccentric pair maintains a solitary homestead along its muddy borders. Sundown Marsh sits tucked into the northwest of the Wetlands, characterized by deep water, thick mud, and a dense population of predators. Giant crocolisks, shifting oozes, roaming raptors, and territorial Mosshide gnolls roam freely through the mist. The hazardous terrain keeps most passing travelers strictly to the main cobblestone road connecting Menethil Harbor to Ironforge, leaving this deep corner largely untamed.

Sunnyglade. Sunnyglade was once a wealthy, prosperous human settlement belonging to the kingdom of Stormwind during the First War. Devastated and eventually abandoned as the front lines collapsed, the ruined settlement now languishes under the dark influence of the Twilight's Hammer cult. Before the First War tore southern Azeroth apart, Sunnyglade was celebrated for its wealth and comfortable prosperity. That peace was violently shattered when the Old Horde invaded. Orc raiding parties attacked the town and enslaved its surviving residents, leaving only a lone wizard's tower intact to study the arcane arts of human conjurers. Though Stormwind forces mounted an effort to rescue the captive peasants and rebuild the settlement, the surrounding Riverglades were steadily swallowed by the advancing Horde. Deeming the outer province lost, Stormwind's commanders eventually withdrew their resources to defend the homeland, leaving Sunnyglade to ruin.

Swamplight Manor. Swamplight Manor is an ironically named, ramshackle wooden shack nestled deep within Witch Hill in Dustwallow Marsh. It serves as the eccentric home and kitchen of 'Swamp Eye' Jarl, an isolated recluse known across the mire for his strange culinary appetites. Despite its humble, eerie isolation, the surrounding garden conceals intrigue that catches the attention of both Theramore and Brackenwall Village. Despite what its grandiose title suggests, Swamplight Manor is far from a lordly estate. It is merely a crooked, weather-beaten shack tucked into the haunted wetlands of Witch Hill. Its lone resident, the odd recluse known as 'Swamp Eye' Jarl, lives a solitary existence surrounded by fog, muck, and restless marsh ghosts. Jarl spends his days concocting unusual regional delicacies out of local wildlife, frequently recruiting wandering adventurers to hunt down bizarre ingredients like marsh frog legs and creature eyes to satisfy his strange craft.

Swarming Pillar. The Swarming Pillar is a towering rock formation in the heart of Silithus, thoroughly infested and reshaped by the silithid. Situated just south of Cenarion Hold, the spire takes its name from the relentless clouds of winged insectoids buzzing around its peaks and subterranean entrances. Rising abruptly from the shifting dunes of central Silithus, the Swarming Pillar serves as a grim monument to the unchecked expansion of the silithid. What began as a natural rock formation has been carved and encrusted with the resinous secretions and burrows of the insectoid swarm. Just south of Cenarion Hold, it constantly churns out broods of winged workers and soldiers, whose dark clouds fill the dry desert air and warn travelers to keep their distance.

Tabetha's Farm. Deep in the murkiest reaches of the Quagmire lies Tabetha's Farm, an isolated homestead centered around a small wooden hut, a modest garden, and a private dock. Despite the treacherous marsh surroundings, this sanctuary serves as a hidden redoubt for the hermit mage Tabetha. Tucked away in the western wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh, Tabetha's Farm defies its unforgiving environment. Consisting of a weather-worn hut, small vegetable plots, and a dock for navigating the swamp's murky waterways, the homestead offers a quiet refuge far from the political rivalries of Theramore and Brackenwall Village. Here, the reclusive human sorceress Tabetha lives in near-total seclusion, pursuing esoteric studies of arcane and fel power without interference from Dalaran or local authorities.

Tahonda Ruins. The Tahonda Ruins are the sun-bleached remnants of an ancient tauren settlement swallowed by the salt and sand of the Shimmering Flats. Little is remembered of the villagers who once lived here, and dangerous Saltstone basilisks now stalk among the decaying tent poles and shredded leather. Situated in the southern reaches of the Shimmering Flats near the pass into Tanaris, the Tahonda Ruins stand as a somber monument to an abandoned tauren past. The village fell long ago, its weathered structures gradually engulfed by shifting white salt crusts. While some suspect the local Saltstone basilisks drove the inhabitants away, odd clues linger on the surviving structures. Two distinct sets of three parallel tears cut through the leather of a ruined lodge, suggesting the village met a violent end at the claws of powerful predators or hostile invaders before the desert claimed what remained.

Tainted Scar. The Tainted Scar is a demon-infested canyon carved into the southwestern Blasted Lands, saturated with foul fel magic from the nearby Dark Portal. It currently serves as the primary redoubt for the remnants of the Burning Legion on Azeroth, commanded by the doomguard Lord Kazzak. Once lush wetlands belonging to the ancient Black Morass, this desolate trench was utterly drained of life and turned the color of dried blood by chaotic fel energies leaking from the Dark Portal. Following Archimonde's defeat at Mount Hyjal during the Third War, surviving forces of the Burning Legion rallied in the south. The colossal ered'ruin Lord Kazzak claimed the Tainted Scar as his stronghold, stationing elite demons across its blackened rises and dispatching dreadful lieutenants like Razelikh the Defiler to hold dominion over the wasted red soils.

Talonbranch Glade. Talonbranch Glade is a quiet night elf redoubt nestled in the blighted hills of northern Felwood. Located just south of Timbermaw Hold, it provides a rare haven of pristine moonlight, sanctuary, and hippogryph transit in an otherwise corrupted wilderness. Perched on high ground near the tunnel to Timbermaw Hold, Talonbranch Glade serves as the northernmost bastion of the Alliance in Felwood. Centered around a sheltered night elf lodge and a functioning moonwell, the outpost offers a crucial refuge from the demonic corruption that has swallowed the surrounding forest. Alliance scouts, Sentinels, and passing adventurers use the glade to rest, recover, and plan their excursions deeper into the tainted woods or onward toward Winterspring and Moonglade.

Talondeep Path. Talondeep Path is a winding underground tunnel boring through the mountain ridge between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains. Devoid of hostile creatures or travelers, it serves as a tranquil, natural subterranean passage connecting Mystral Lake to Windshear Crag. Hidden beneath the rugged ridgeline separating Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains lies Talondeep Path, a quiet subterranean route. The passage links the forests just west of Mystral Lake directly to the northwestern reaches of Windshear Crag. Unlike the dangerous surface trails haunted by predators and warring factions, the tunnel interior remains eerily calm, free of hostile beasts or encampments, though riddled with twisting side pockets, crevices, and natural alcoves in the rock. Above ground, faint remnants of an ancient surface road still linger, hinting that travelers once scaled the high peaks before this sheltered cave became the preferred route through the stone.

Talondeep Vale. Talondeep Vale is a quiet, forested hollow nestled in south-central Ashenvale. Bordering Silverwind Refuge, the Ruins of Stardust, and the gateway to the Stonetalon Mountains, it acts as a peaceful canopy through which travelers navigate southern Kalimdor. Tucked away beneath the dense canopy of south-central Ashenvale, Talondeep Vale serves as a crossroads between several landmark sites. It is framed by Silverwind Refuge to the east, the haunting Ruins of Stardust nearby, and the rugged rise leading up into the Stonetalon Mountains. Shaded by ancient trees, the valley remains an untamed tract of woodland through which night elf wardens, sentinels, and passing wanderers traverse as they move between the heart of the forest and the high crags beyond.

Tarren Mill. Tarren Mill is a beleaguered Forsaken outpost nestled in the northern reaches of the Hillsbrad Foothills beneath the Alterac Mountains. Once a peaceful human farming village, it now serves as the primary bastion of the Horde in Hillsbrad, locked in constant conflict with the Alliance town of Southshore to the south. Before the Third War, Tarren Mill was a thriving agricultural township loyal to the Kingdom of Lordaeron. During the Second War, it earned renown when Alliance forces rescued captured high elven archers from nearby orc encampments, securing Quel'Thalas's full commitment to the Alliance of Lordaeron. Today, however, the town's original living inhabitants are gone, replaced by the Forsaken. The town's architecture stands weathered and decayed, its fields barren, and its old mill silent as the new undead occupants fortify the settlement against constant threats from mountain beasts, Syndicate outlaws, and Alliance skirmishers.

Temple Gardens. The Temple Gardens form the tranquil, water-filled heart of Darnassus, surrounding small islets just north of the Temple of the Moon. Decorated with bridges and pristine flora, the district hosts the city bank and the mystical tree portal leading to the base of Teldrassil. Spanning the waters at the center of Darnassus, the Temple Gardens serve as the crossroads of the night elven capital. Wooden bridges connect its landscaped islets to the Cenarion Enclave in the north, the bustling terraces to the east, and the grand sanctuary of the Temple of the Moon to the south. The night elves carefully shape the district's flowing waters and lush foliage, creating a serene atmosphere that offers rest to travelers and priestesses alike.

Temple of Arkkoran. The Temple of Arkkoran is an ancient night elven ruin resting on the northeastern cliffs of Azshara above the Shattered Strand. Originally built in honor of Elune, the crumbling structure has since been claimed by the towering sea giant Arkkoroc and his aquatic thralls. Like many of the grand ruins dotting Azshara's coast, the Temple of Arkkoran was once a sanctum dedicated to the moon goddess Elune before the Sundering shattered the ancient night elf empire. Today, its weathered marble steps and broken colonnades are overrun by tidal monstrosities. The sea giant Arkkoroc presides over the temple's highest level, surrounded by loyal makrura and vicious murlocs who violently defend the surrounding coastline from any land-dwelling intruders.

Temple of Atal'Hakkar. The Temple of Atal'Hakkar, widely known as the Sunken Temple, is a submerged fortress built by exiled troll priests dedicated to the blood god Hakkar. Sunk beneath the marshes by the green dragonflight centuries ago, its drowned halls remain a staging ground for forbidden rituals and dark corruption. Over a millennium ago, a catastrophic civil war shattered the Gurubashi Empire when the Atal'ai priesthood attempted to summon Hakkar the Soulflayer. Exiled to the north, the surviving zealots raised a massive stone temple in the Swamp of Sorrows to finish their dark work. Learning of their scheme, the Dragon Aspect Ysera smashed the ziggurat deep into the mire, inundating its chambers beneath the Pool of Tears. Green dragon wardens were left behind to guard the drowned ruins and ensure Hakkar's return was thwarted forever.

Temple of the Moon. The Temple of the Moon stands in Darnassus as the spiritual heart of the night elven people and the seat of government on Teldrassil. Presided over by High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, the sanctuary serves as the headquarters for the Sisterhood of Elune. Its towering marble tiers house a sacred moonwell whose blessed waters bring healing and communion with the Moon Goddess. Erected shortly after the Third War when the night elves settled Teldrassil, the Temple of the Moon is among the largest stone structures constructed by modern kaldorei hands. Much of its marble was quarried from the Kalimdor mainland and transported across the sea through magical means. At the center of its interior lies an expansive moonwell overseen by the statue of Haidene, where consecrated waters radiate quiet power. Beyond serving as a place of worship and quiet reflection for pilgrims, the temple functions as the political apex of Darnassus, housing High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind as she guides her people through the dawn of a uncertain new age.

Temple of Zin-Malor. The Temple of Zin-Malor is an ancient night elven sanctuary located within the Ruins of Eldarath in Azshara. Originally dedicated to the moon goddess Elune, the crumbling structure is now held by the Spitelash naga under the direct command of Warlord Krellian. Before the Great Sundering, the Temple of Zin-Malor stood as a grand house of worship dedicated to Elune. Its architecture closely mirrors both the nearby Temple of Arkkoran and the modern Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, bearing the graceful, sweeping stonework characteristic of pre-Sundering night elven civilization. Today, however, its moonlit marble is weathered and broken, overtaken by the serpent-bodied Spitelash naga. These invaders have claimed the holy grounds for themselves, turning a place of quiet reflection into a militarized redoubt.

Terrace of Repose. The Terrace of Repose is a pristine courtyard garden located just outside the entrance to the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades. Maintained by the Scarlet Crusade, it stands as one of the few places in northern Lordaeron completely untouched by the Plague of Undeath, complete with green hedges and clean water. Situated just north of the grand entrance into the Scarlet Monastery, the Terrace of Repose offers a surreal contrast to the rotting forests of Tirisfal Glades. While the rest of Lordaeron chokes under grey mist, corrupt soil, and stagnant bogs, this terrace boasts verdant, neatly pruned hedges and a functioning fountain fed by fresh, uncontaminated water. For the zealots of the Scarlet Crusade, the garden serves as physical proof of their divine righteousness and purity, a sacred bastion demonstrating that holy devotion can ward off the Scourge's corruption.

Terror Run. Terror Run is a perilous swath of land situated in the southwestern reaches of Un'Goro Crater, directly west of the insectoid hives of the Slithering Scar. True to its fearsome name, the territory is stalked by predatory beasts, ranging from massive devilsaurs to ravenous diemetradons and swooping pterrordax. Stretching across the southwestern shelf of Un'Goro Crater, Terror Run lives up to its ominous reputation. Fierce pterrordax wheel through the humid air above while massive diemetradons, stegodons, and apex devilsaurs roam the low brush below. The territory sits directly in the shadow of the mountainous rim, wedged uncomfortably close to the chittering alien mounds of the Slithering Scar. Along the eastern edge of the flats lie the ruined remnants of a camp left behind by Williden Marshal's expedition, a sobering reminder of researchers who were caught unprepared when the crater's primeval predators closed in.

Terror Wing Path. Terror Wing Path is a rocky canyon winding through the eastern reaches of the Burning Steppes. Infested by whelps and dragonkin of the black dragonflight, it serves as a perilous approach into the remote northeastern corner of the Steppes. Carved into the craggy, ash-covered foothills of the eastern Burning Steppes, Terror Wing Path earns its name from the aerial predators and wyrmkin that claim it. Broods of the black dragonflight prowl these defiles, fiercely guarding clutches and hunting anything foolish enough to wander into their shadow. Ash and soot blanket the stone trails, making any trek beneath the canyon walls a treacherous venture.

Terrordale. Terrordale is a ruined, ghost-haunted settlement nestled in the northwestern edge of the Eastern Plaguelands. Bordered by the blighted Plaguewood and the arachnid-infested Terrorweb Tunnel, the ruined town swarms with the Scourge and the restless dead. Once a quiet settlement in northern Lordaeron, Terrordale fell along with the rest of the kingdom to the Scourge. Today, the village stands in grim ruin near the mouth of the Terrorweb Tunnel. Its streets are choked with restless shades and wandering undead, while the surrounding trees of the Plaguewood encroach on its rotten timber. Amidst the desolation, only a handful of eccentric residents dare remain—such as the peculiar merchant Augustus the Touched and the ghost hunter Egan, who attempts to free the tortured spirits caught between worlds.

Terrorweb Tunnel. Terrorweb Tunnel is a subterranean passage carving through the mountains between Terrordale and the Thondroril River. Infested with the Scourge's undead nerubian crypt fiends, it forms a hazardous subterranean shortcut across the western border of the Eastern Plaguelands. Bored straight through the mountains flanking the Thondroril River, the Terrorweb Tunnel links the contaminated village of Terrordale with the riverbanks to the south. Rather than typical ghouls or skeletal sentries, this dark subterranean bypass is claimed entirely by crypt fiends—mummified nerubian arachnids raised into servitude by the Lich King. Traveling the length of the passage cuts out long circuits around the mountain slopes, but requires navigating thick webs and avoiding towering nerubian overseers that patrol the dark.

Thalanaar. Thalanaar is a secluded night elf outpost nestled directly on the border between the verdant wilds of Feralas and the arid canyons of Thousand Needles. Serving as the primary eastern gateway into Feralas for the Alliance, it offers tired travelers a vital hippogryph roost and shelter beneath the canopy. Though modest in size, it acts as a critical link between mainland Kalimdor and the remote stronghold of Feathermoon. Perched at the natural choke point where the baked sandstone of Thousand Needles gives way to the dense, misty canopy of Feralas, Thalanaar is the first sign of night elven presence awaiting travelers from the east. It is little more than a fortified grove with a few sturdy pavilions and sentinels on watch, yet its position is vital. The outpost shelters Alliance scouts, couriers, and craftsmen venturing into the untamed forest, providing a secure staging ground against the beasts, ogres, and Horde forces roaming Southern Kalimdor.

Thalassian Base Camp. Tucked onto a high ridge in northern Azshara, the Thalassian Base Camp serves as the staging ground for an expedition of blood elves unearthing ancient arcane relics. Though initially funded under an agreement with the Horde, the camp's leadership quickly broke faith once digging commenced. Now, amidst their red pavilions and pulverized magical artifacts, darker summoning practices hint at their true objectives. The blood elf expedition nestled east of Ursolan was not supposed to be hostile to travelers from Orgrimmar. Their leader, Magus Rimtori, negotiated a formal pact with the Horde: in exchange for supply lines, funding, and armed escort through Azshara's treacherous wildlands, her researchers would share whatever magical riches they uncovered. Instead, as soon as the base camp was fortified and the first relics were pried from the elven ruins, Rimtori reneged entirely, driving away Horde emissaries. While Rimtori searches deeper reaches with an armed retinue, Magister Hawkhelm keeps watch over the ridge, guarding the encampment against retribution.

Thandol Span. The Thandol Span is a pair of colossal dwarven stone bridges connecting the Wetlands of Khaz Modan with the Arathi Highlands of southern Lordaeron. Long celebrated as a marvel of engineering and the vital artery between the northern and southern kingdoms, it is currently in a state of disaster following a sabotage attack by Dark Iron infiltrators. Constructed following the War of the Three Hammers to bridge Ironforge with the Wildhammer clan of the Aerie Peak, the Thandol Span stands among the grandest stonecraft feats of dwarven history. Capable of supporting entire marching armies, it served as the critical land corridor between Lordaeron and Khaz Modan throughout the Second War, notably carrying Sir Anduin Lothar's counter-offensive southward. Today, the crossing is grievously wounded. Dark Iron saboteurs led by Balgaras the Foul and Kam Deepfury mounted a devastating assault from nearby Dun Modr, shattering one span entirely with explosives and threatening to sever overland travel between the allied realms completely.

The Den. The Den is the sheltered cave at the heart of the Valley of Trials in southwestern Durotar. Serving as the primary base of operations for young orc and troll adventurers, it provides martial and magical training before they set out into the wider world. Tucked into the red canyon walls of the Valley of Trials, the Den serves as an austere proving ground. Within its carved, shadowy interior, novice fighters, spellcasters, and hunters report to veterans like Gornek and Zureetha Fargaze. It is here that fledglings receive their foundational combat instruction, supplies, and initial rites of passage, hardening them for the harsh realities of Durotar and the greater struggles facing the new Horde.

The Loch. The Loch is the vast freshwater lake that dominates the valley of Loch Modan. Held back by the monumental Stonewrought Dam, it is the largest body of water on Khaz Modan and the lifeblood of the surrounding dwarven settlements. Spanning the center of Loch Modan, The Loch is among the largest inland lakes in the known world, rivaled only by Lordamere Lake and Darrowmere Lake in the north. Its waters support local fishermen and provide a peaceful backdrop for the town of Thelsamar and nearby hunting lodges. Beneath its calm surface, however, prowl aggressive threshadons and freshwater beasts that make swimming across a perilous venture.

Thelgen Rock. Thelgen Rock is an extensive cavern system cut into the southern mountain wall of the Wetlands. Infested with venomous spiders, it is notorious for harboring rare veins of volatile Incendicite Ore. Nestled against the southern mountains separating the Wetlands from Loch Modan, Thelgen Rock is a deep subterranean cave network overrun by aggressive arachnids. The passages are thick with webs and crawling with poisonous spiders that make entering the caverns extremely hazardous for travelers. Despite the infestation, miners and adventurers brave its depths for the valuable deposits of Incendicite Ore found embedded in the rocky tunnels.

Thelsamar. Thelsamar is the primary dwarven settlement in Loch Modan, nestled on the western bluffs overlooking the great lake. Positioned along the main road between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands, it serves as a bustling hub of commerce, hospitality, and civic defense against surrounding trogg and ogre incursions. Thelsamar serves as the central bastion of dwarven civilian life in the valley. Built with traditional Khaz Modan stone and timber architecture, it features the lively Stoutlager Inn, a dedicated gryphon roost, crafting stations, and various supply merchants. Sitting directly on the thoroughfare connecting the South Gate Pass into Dun Morogh with the Algaz Pass toward the Wetlands, almost all travelers through the region pass beneath its warm hearths and stout roofs.

Theramore Isle. Theramore Isle is a heavily fortified human port citadel off the eastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh. Founded by Lady Jaina Proudmoore for refugees escaping the fall of Lordaeron, it stands as the Alliance's primary bastion in southern Kalimdor. Following the devastation of Dalaran and Lordaeron by the Scourge during the Third War, Lady Jaina Proudmoore guided a fleet of survivors across the Great Sea to the shores of Kalimdor. After fighting alongside orcs and night elves to defeat the Burning Legion atop Mount Hyjal, her coalition of humans, dwarves, and high elves retreated to the misty fringes of Dustwallow Marsh. On a jagged island just off the coast, they built Theramore Isle—a thriving harbor city anchored by towering stone ramparts and Jaina's personal citadel, created to safeguard what remained of the northern kingdoms.

Thistlefur Hold. Thistlefur Hold is a cavernous den carved into northern Thistlefur Village in west-central Ashenvale. Once peaceful bears of the forest, the Thistlefur furbolgs residing here have succumbed to corruption and turn violent toward any outsider who draws near. Tucked into the northern reaches of Thistlefur Village, Thistlefur Hold serves as the heart of the Thistlefur tribe's territory. The furbolgs here have been driven mad by corruption, falling into a state of feral hostility that makes them dangerous to travelers and neighbors alike. Deep within the winding caverns, the tribe hordes scavenged relics—including troll charms of interest to the Darkspear—and keeps captives bound in wooden cages, such as the imprisoned tauren brave Ruul Snowhoof.

Thistlefur Village. Thistlefur Village is a sprawling settlement tucked into the forest north of Astranaar in west-central Ashenvale. It serves as the primary home of the Thistlefur furbolg tribe, who have fallen prey to dark corruption and violently assault any outsiders venturing near their dens. Situated just north of the night elf haven of Astranaar, Thistlefur Village was once part of the peaceful woodland communities native to Ashenvale. However, the malignant corruption that has seeped into the ancient forests has entirely claimed the Thistlefur tribe. Now thoroughly maddened and intensely hostile, the furbolgs fiercely guard the paths winding through their settlement. The clan answers to two exceptionally ferocious chieftains, Dal Bloodclaw and Rorgish Jowl, whose unyielding aggression poses a constant threat to travelers and nearby settlements.

Thistlefuzz Arcanery. Thistlefuzz Arcanery is a prominent workshop and academy of the magical arts located east of the Great Forge in Ironforge. Run primarily by gnome practitioners, it serves as the capital's premier haven for enchanters and scholars seeking to weave magic into metal and parchment. Its busy chambers hum with arcane energy right alongside the roaring fires of dwarven industry. Tucked directly east of the thundering Great Forge, Thistlefuzz Arcanery offers a stark contrast to the clanging anvils of dwarven smiths. Within its two levels, scholars, practitioners, and apprentices gather to master the subtle disciplines of enchanting and magical study. While the Ironforge dwarves prefer to reshape steel through muscle and fire, the gnomes of the Arcanery demonstrate how raw arcane energy can be bound directly into weaponry, armor, and curious tools. It stands as an essential sanctuary for spellcasters navigating the mountain stronghold.

Thistleshrub Valley. Tucked away in the southwestern reaches of Tanaris, Thistleshrub Valley is a bizarre oasis of prickly plant life amidst endless dunes. The canyon is known for its strange grove of giant cacti and hostile animated thistleshrubs that attack anything stepping through their thorn-choked territory. While most of Tanaris is an arid wasteland stripped bare of vegetation, Thistleshrub Valley is curiously choked with life. Giant blooming cacti tower over the canyon floor, providing a sharp contrast to the surrounding sea of sand. However, this is no peaceful sanctuary. The valley takes its name from the hostile, living plant creatures that lurk among the brush. These thistleshrubs lash out with razor-sharp spines at any traveler who wanders near, making navigation hazardous for those trying to push past the cliffs toward the mysterious southern gates.

Thondroril River. The Thondroril River is a vital natural boundary separating the Western and Eastern Plaguelands. Originating in the mountains of Northern Lordaeron near the Terrorweb Tunnel, its blighted waters flow southward into Darrowmere Lake. Once a vibrant trade and travel waterway of the fallen kingdom, it is now flanked by monstrous Scourge beasts and the humble refuge of a legendary hermit. Before the fall of Lordaeron, the Thondroril served as an important waterway connecting northern holdings toward Stratholme and south to Darrowmere Lake. Today, the river marks the hazardous divide between the Western and Eastern Plaguelands. The waters carry the taint of the plague, and its banks are infested with giant maggots, plaguebats, diseased bears, and predatory snapjaws, turning what was once a scenic riverbed into a deadly crossing for travelers.

Thoradin's Wall. Thoradin's Wall is a monumental, crumbling stone rampart dividing the Arathi Highlands from the Hillsbrad Foothills. Commissioned millennia ago by King Thoradin during the dawn of the Empire of Arathor, it was built to shield early humanity from the fierce incursions of the Amani trolls. Erected nearly three thousand years ago, Thoradin's Wall marks the western frontier of ancient Strom, the heart of the first unified human empire. King Thoradin recognized that humanity's fledgeling settlements were acutely vulnerable to the predatory raids of the Amani forest trolls. By raising this vast stone barrier across the valley corridor, Arathor secured its heartland and forged a defensible bastion from which humanity could survive and eventually contest troll supremacy in the north.

Thorium Point. Perched upon the northern bluffs of the Searing Gorge, Thorium Point serves as the primary staging camp for the Thorium Brotherhood. From this neutral outpost, these rogue Dark Iron dwarves recruit passing adventurers and strike back against their tyrannical kin deeper within the volcanic wastes. Overlooking the scorched slag heaps of the Searing Gorge, Thorium Point is a modest mountain encampment built out of necessity. It is held by the Thorium Brotherhood, a renegade faction of Dark Iron dwarves who have severed ties with their enslaved brethren in Shadowforge City. Unwilling to bow to the Firelord or Emperor Dagran Thaurissan, these outcasts maintain an open-air forge, a busy flight master, and a well-guarded perimeter northeast of Firewatch Ridge. Because of their desperate struggle for survival and master-level smithing aspirations, the Brotherhood keeps the camp open to both the Alliance and the Horde, welcoming anyone willing to dig ores out of the ash or bash Dark Iron skulls.

Thorn Hill. Thorn Hill is a fortified Razormane quilboar enclave nestled on the high ridges east of the Crossroads in the Barrens. The settlement serves as a forward base for quilboar warbands raiding Horde supply lines traveling between Durotar and the interior savanna. Perched on the north face of the rugged hills between Durotar and the Crossroads, Thorn Hill commands a watchful vantage over the primary trade corridors of the Barrens. The settlement is home to a dangerous gathering of the Razormane tribe, including hunters, trained wolves, and earth-shaping geomancers. Guided by mystics like Elder Mystic Razorsnout, the quilboar here have escalated their attacks against passing Horde supply caravans. Because this mountain camp sits so close to vital transit routes, the guards at the Crossroads consider Thorn Hill one of the most immediate military hazards in the central savanna.

Three Corners. Three Corners is a vital crossroads nestled just inside the western border of the Redridge Mountains. Branching toward the three neighboring towns of Goldshire, Lakeshire, and Darkshire, it marks the boundary between the heart of the kingdom and Redridge's perilous wilderness. A Stormwind Guard watchtower stands over the intersection, holding the line against encroaching gnoll packs. Situated at the western edge of the Redridge Mountains, Three Corners connects three key Alliance settlements: Goldshire in Elwynn Forest to the west, Lakeshire to the northeast, and Darkshire in Duskwood to the south. Because of this strategic junction, Stormwind erected Tower Watch at the center of the crossroads. Manning the post, local guards and scouts attempt to keep the thoroughfares clear of Redridge's aggressive gnolls, who constantly threaten travelers and supply wagons passing between the regions.

Thunder Axe Fortress. Thunder Axe Fortress is a fortified compound in northwestern Desolace serving as a stronghold for the demonic Burning Blade cult. Within its stone barracks, watchtowers, and darkened caves, cultists perform dark rituals to summon demonic entities and store stolen artifacts of power. The cult remains an active threat to anyone traversing the desolate wastes. Perched in northwestern Desolace, Thunder Axe Fortress serves as a heavily guarded redoubt for the Burning Blade. Composed of stone barracks, defensive watchtowers, and deep caverns, it allows the cult to maintain a fortified foothold far from the gaze of Kalimdor's major cities. Here, the cultists gather fel energies, summon lesser demons, and concoct schemes to bring far more dangerous entities into the world.

Thunder Bluff. Thunder Bluff is the high-perched capital city of the tauren, rising hundreds of feet above the rolling plains of Mulgore. Founded by Cairne Bloodhoof following the Third War, it serves as the united sanctuary and cultural heart for a people who roamed as nomads for generations. For countless generations, the tauren lived as nomadic wanderers across central Kalimdor, constantly beset by brutal centaur raiding parties. That era of flight ended during the Third War, when Cairne Bloodhoof forged a bond of honor with Warchief Thrall and the New Horde. Together, they drove back the centaur menace and claimed the fertile grasslands of Mulgore. Cairne gathered the scattered tribes and established Thunder Bluff atop a series of sweeping, natural stone mesas. Today, the city is connected by dizzying rope bridges and accessed by ingenious wooden elevators, offering both absolute defense and a bustling center of trade and spiritual assembly.

Thunder Falls. Thunder Falls is a secluded mountain ravine tucked away in the northwestern heights of Elwynn Forest. Cradled between sheer cliffs and fed by roaring cascades, it features a quiet riverside cottage that has fallen into the hands of local bandits. Tucked away in the jagged ridges above Mirror Lake, Thunder Falls is an unusual geographical cleft. The ravine is carved by a swift mountain stream that enters via an inaccessible northern cascade, only to drop away on both sides in dramatic waterfalls. One side plunges down into Mirror Lake, while the downstream course flows west toward the rugged borders of Westfall. Despite the roaring waters, a small cottage, a dock, and an outdoor forge sit along the shore, though outlaws now claim the peaceful clearing for themselves.

Thunder Ridge. Thunder Ridge is a rugged canyon in western Durotar, situated just southwest of Orgrimmar along the banks of the Southfury River. Once a lush grove of ancient trees inhabited by herds of thunder lizards, the canyon has suffered severe deforestation from human lumber operations and dark sorcery. Today, the agitated beasts and lingering cultists pose an ongoing threat to nearby settlements. Not long ago, Thunder Ridge was a rare green haven in arid Durotar, sustained by ancient trees. Its tranquil balance shattered shortly after the Third War when human interlopers from Kul Tiras began felling its timber, driving the native thunder lizards into a frenzy. Later, fel sorcery wielded by the Burning Blade finished the destruction, stripping the canopy and leaving behind a barren, exposed gorge where angry lightning-spewing beasts now roam unrestrained.

Thunderbrew Distillery. Thunderbrew Distillery serves as the bustling tavern and central gathering place of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Renowned far and wide for its potent ales, it functions as both an active brewhouse and an essential rest stop for travelers passing through the snowy mountain passes. Inside, patrons find warm hearths, cold pints, and a wide array of class mentors and local tradesfolk. Perched in the center of Kharanos, the Thunderbrew Distillery is the heart of civic life in southern Dun Morogh. Founded by the Thunderbrew clan—established by Arkilus Thunderbrew and maintained by his kin—the brewhouse is famous across Khaz Modan for producing robust, warming ales built to ward off the biting mountain chill. It operates as the local inn, managed on the floor by Innkeeper Belm, offering weary mountaineers a roaring fire, hearty fare, and beds to escape the blizzards outside.

Thunderhorn Water Well. Thunderhorn Water Well is a vital water source situated in the rolling plains of central Mulgore along the path between Bloodhoof Village and Thunder Bluff. Like all the wells across the valley, it provides essential nourishment to the tribes and the herds roaming the grasslands. Keeping this water clean and defended is crucial to maintaining life in the tauren homeland. Situated amid the sprawling grasslands of central Mulgore, the Thunderhorn Water Well taps directly into the pure aquifers feeding the valley. For the nomadic tauren and their newly settled villages, these communal wells represent life, sustenance, and the Earth Mother's bounty. Because water is precious across the sun-drenched plains, controlling the wells means controlling the land itself. Intruders such as the Venture Company have repeatedly eyed these sources, attempting to harness them for industrial exploitation and disrupt the fragile balance the tribes fight to preserve.

Tidefury Cove. Tidefury Cove is a treacherous stretch of water and rocky shallows along the southeastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh, south of Theramore Isle. Renowned for its hazardous reefs and wrecked vessels, it serves as a secluded haven for roaming makrura and solitary anglers. Tucked away at the far end of Dustwallow Bay between Theramore Isle and the Wyrmbog, Tidefury Cove presents a notorious navigational hazard to passing sailors. Jagged reefs and shifting shoals have claimed multiple vessels over the years, leaving rotting wooden hulks half-submerged in the tideline. Today, the ruined ships are crawled over by opportunistic makrura, turning the cove into a dangerous, isolated stretch of coastline visited mostly by hardy scavengers or quiet hermits seeking distance from Theramore's busy docks.

Tidus Stair. Tidus Stair is a natural rock formation of broad, stepped stone terraces perched over the Merchant Coast southeast of Ratchet. Sheltered beside the Great Sea, it serves as a quiet retreat for two tauren shamans communing with the tides and water spirits. Descending toward the surf southeast of Ratchet, the Tidus Stair resembles a monumental set of weathered stone steps cut directly into the coastal bluffs. While the surrounding Barrens are arid, dusty, and prone to skirmishes, this quiet stretch overlooking the Merchant Coast is dominated by the sound of crashing waves. Perched on the terraces is a modest hut where the tauren Islen Waterseer and Mahren Skyseer reside. Far from the bustling trade docks of the goblins, the two spend their days fishing, watching the horizon, and seeking insight from the coastal water spirits.

Timbermaw Hold. Timbermaw Hold is a fortified subterranean network of tunnels that links Felwood, Moonglade, and Winterspring. It serves as the stronghold for the Timbermaw furbolgs, one of the last tribes to resist the demonic corruption plaguing northern Kalimdor. Carved deep into the mountain roots between Felwood, Moonglade, and Winterspring, Timbermaw Hold stands as a desperately guarded bastion. While neighboring furbolg tribes fell to the foul taint of the Burning Legion during the Third War, the Timbermaw clan weathered the nightmare within these stone corridors. Though safe beneath the earth, they were forced to watch their beloved forests warp into corrupted mockeries. Extremely protective and deeply suspicious of outsiders, the furbolgs guard every tunnel entrance fiercely, expecting violence from anyone wandering in from the infected woods.

Timbermaw Post. Timbermaw Post is a small furbolg camp situated in the snowy expanse of Winterspring, nestled between Frostfire Hot Springs and Lake Kel'Theril. Despite bearing the name of the uncorrupted Timbermaw tribe, the encampment has fallen under the aggressive grip of the corrupted Winterfall furbolgs. Positioned just southeast across the road from Frostfire Hot Springs and west of the frozen Lake Kel'Theril, Timbermaw Post stands as a bitter reminder of the furbolgs' internal strife in Winterspring. Despite its Timbermaw name, travelers approaching the camp will find no friendly welcomes. The outpost is controlled by the hostile Winterfall tribe, driven mad and violent by demonic corruption. Now crowded with savage Winterfall furbolgs, the camp serves as an aggressive staging ground encroaching upon the central road.

Tinker Town. Tinker Town is the bustling gnomish quarter nestled within the subterranean dwarven city of Ironforge. Established to shelter refugees following the tragic fall of Gnomeregan, the district serves as the seat of High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque's government-in-exile and the primary terminus for the Deeprun Tram. When subterranean troggs overran the high-tech city of Gnomeregan, the dwarven hosts of Ironforge opened their gates to the survivors. To accommodate the sudden influx of refugees, a cavernous district—previously home to dwarven residents and the entrance to the Deeprun Tram—was set aside for them. Under the watchful eye of High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his council, Tinker Town quickly became an energetic hub of whirring gears, experimental alchemy, and gadgetry. Despite being cramped guests in a stone city, the gnomes have rebuilt a semblance of their civilization around a massive spherical contraption, determined to reclaim their subterranean homeland.

Tinkers' Court. Tinkers' Court is the grand council chamber at the heart of Gnomeregan. Once the bustling seat of the High Tinker and his ruling council, it is now the grim stronghold of the traitor Mekgineer Thermaplugg. Before the disaster that ruined Gnomeregan, the Tinkers' Court served as the civic and political heart of the nation. It was here that High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque gathered with advisors and master inventors, including Tinkmaster Overspark, to debate technological advancements, govern civic matters, and guide gnomish society. The court represented the pinnacle of gnomish ingenuity and governance, situated just beyond the industrial works of the Engineering Labs and the Launch Bay.

Tiragarde Keep. Tiragarde Keep is a fortified human stronghold situated along Durotar's Scuttle Coast, south of Razor Hill. Originally built during Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's invasion, the ruined citadel remains garrisoned by hostile Kul Tiran marines under Lieutenant Benedict. It serves as a defiant, permanent thorn in the Horde's side right on their home territory. Erected during Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's campaign to eradicate Thrall's newly founded realm, Tiragarde Keep provided the Kul Tiran fleet an entrenched beachhead on the red shores of Durotar. Although the Horde eventually broke the siege and killed Proudmoore at Theramore Isle, the keep was never fully abandoned. Resupply forces under Lieutenant Benedict reclaimed the shattered stone walls, following the late Admiral's standing orders to wage an unyielding war against the orcs, entirely refusing the peace forged by Lady Jaina Proudmoore.

Tkashi Ruins. The Tkashi Ruins are ancient stone remnants situated southwest of Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Overrun by hostile Bloodscalp trolls, the site remains a stronghold of the tribe. Perched southwest of Hemet Nesingwary's hunting camp, the crumbling stone masonry of the Tkashi Ruins marks the ancient domain of Stranglethorn's jungle trolls. Today, the encampment is heavily occupied by the Bloodscalp tribe, who aggressively defend the territory and practice their shamanistic rituals among the vines and decayed stone. While Hemet Nesingwary noted passing through the ruins without trouble in his hunting memoirs, modern travelers find the trolls far less accommodating, guarding valuable tribal relics buried among the rubble.

Tor'kren Farm. Tor'kren Farm is a quiet, struggling swine farm in northwestern Durotar, near Thunder Ridge and the Southfury River. Misha Tor'kren tends the homestead while anxiously awaiting news of her son Kron, who has not returned from a hunting trip. Carving out a living from the dry, unforgiving red dirt of Durotar is never simple, but Tor'kren Farm has had a harder time than most. Situated southeast of Thunder Ridge, the homestead focuses on raising pigs in a rugged climate where feed and water are scarce. Unlike the bustling trade posts or heavily defended barracks of the Horde, the farm stands isolated and quiet, producing meager yields in the shadow of nearby bluffs.

Tower of Althalaxx. The Tower of Althalaxx is an ancient Highborne spire standing in northern Darkshore near the coast. Once an isolated retreat for the sorcerer Athrikus Narassin before the Great Sundering, it has become infested by demonic cultists and warlocks practicing dark arts. Ten thousand years ago, Queen Azshara settled favored Highborne servants in the coastal towns of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, placing the powerful sorcerer Athrikus Narassin in authority over them. Growing distant from civic governance, Athrikus chose to isolate himself within the nearby Tower of Althalaxx. When the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, the tower endured along the desolate coastline of Darkshore, standing as a quiet ruin of forgotten elven magics.

Tower of Arathor. The Tower of Arathor is a ruined wizard's tower situated in the former mage district in the southwestern reaches of Stromgarde Keep. Once the workshop of Archmage Trelane, it was overrun during the fall of the city and is currently occupied by Boulderfist ogres. Erected in the heart of Stromgarde Keep's mage district and named after the ancient Empire of Arathor, this spire long served the realm's sorcerers. Its most notable resident, Archmage Trelane, devised a magical defensive grid keyed to enchanted gemstones to protect the sanctum. However, when the Syndicate and the Boulderfist ogre clan assaulted Stromgarde following the Third War, the kingdom fractured. Despite Trelane's desperate attempts to hold the tower using his arcane wards, the sheer brutish force of the ogres overwhelmed him. Forced to flee the city for his life, the archmage left behind his most prized arcane artifacts, leaving the spire in the hands of the Boulderfist brute Ruul Onestone and his followers.

Tower of Azora. The Tower of Azora is a slender wizard's spire rising out of eastern Elwynn Forest, north of the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch. Presided over by the human Archmage Theocritus, the enclave serves as a scholarly outpost locked in a silent magical feud with a hostile tower in neighboring Redridge Mountains. Standing along the eastern road toward the Redridge Mountains, the Tower of Azora is an arcane sanctuary staffed almost entirely by gnome spellcasters. Under the stewardship of Archmage Theocritus, these scholars study strange curiosities and provide magical instruction to wandering spellweavers. The wild magical aura surrounding the spire occasionally warps the nearby wildlife, leaving the gnome servants to contend with enchanted household items and mutated insects creeping past the doorway.

Tower of Eldara. The Tower of Eldara is an ancient, sealed night elven spire situated on the far northeastern promontory overlooking the Bay of Storms in Azshara. Though long abandoned, its sturdy stone architecture has survived the Sundering, standing silent above coasts roamed by aggressive coastal beasts. Perched on a remote cliff edge northeast of the Bay of Storms, the Tower of Eldara stands as a lonely testament to the vast kaldorei empire that once dominated this coastline. Like much of Azshara's ruined architecture, it fell into disuse following the Great Sundering thousands of years ago.
