Today, Stormwind stands as the preeminent seat of human leadership, carrying the banners of honor and faith into a fractured world.

Alliance of Lordaeron. The Alliance of Lordaeron was the historic grand coalition of the seven human kingdoms, Khaz Modan dwarves, Wildhammer gryphon riders, gnomes, and high elves formed to resist the Old Horde in the Second War. Led militarily by Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar and diplomatically by King Terenas Menethil II, it shattered the invading orcish forces and secured the Eastern Kingdoms. Though political fractures and the devastation of the Scourge tore it apart during the Third War, its legacy laid the foundation for the current Alliance. Following the horrific sack of Stormwind in the First War, Regent Lord Anduin Lothar brought the battered southern refugees across the Great Sea to Capital City. Pleading their cause before King Terenas Menethil II, Lothar convinced him to gather the rulers of the human nations in council. Old rivalries and border tensions ran deep, but the threat of the Horde outweighed them. Choosing Lothar as their Supreme Commander, the seven human nations bound themselves together in a desperate pact.

Alterac (kingdom). Alterac was one of the seven historic human kingdoms, nestled high in the rugged Alterac Mountains. During the Second War, its ruler, King Aiden Perenolde, made a treacherous pact with the Old Horde to spare his realm, leading to the kingdom's military downfall and total collapse. Today, its ruined capital lies abandoned in the snow, while dispossessed nobles and outlaws wage a guerrilla war under the banner of the Syndicate. Alterac arose thousands of years ago as an Arathorian city-state following the Troll Wars. Settlers capitalized on strategic mountain passes and trading outposts, eventually establishing an independent realm when the empire fractured. Though rugged and mountainous, Alterac bordered the prosperous lands of Lordaeron and Stromgarde. Historically, it fielded tough mountain fighters, but enduring border friction with Thoras Trollbane's Stromgarde left the kingdom politically isolated from its neighbors long before the Dark Portal ever opened.

Anduin Lothar. Sir Anduin Lothar, known as the Lion of Stormwind, was the last descendant of the ancient Arathi bloodline and the Supreme Commander of the Alliance of Lordaeron. A childhood companion of King Llane Wrynn and the Guardian Medivh, Lothar led humanity through the horrors of the First War and rallied the northern nations during the Second War before falling at Blackrock Mountain. Carrying the ancient bloodline of the Arathi kings, Lothar grew up within Stormwind's royal court alongside Prince Llane Wrynn and Medivh. The trio embarked on reckless excursions into the wilderness, skirmishing with Gurubashi trolls in Stranglethorn Vale. Lothar rose rapidly through Stormwind's martial ranks, joining the King's Honor Guard and earning renown as an Armsman of the Brotherhood of the Horse.

Argent Dawn. The Argent Dawn is a neutral, knightly order dedicated to stamping out malevolent threats across Azeroth, most notably the Scourge and the Burning Legion. Formed by survivors of the Knights of the Silver Hand who rejected the fanatical zealotry of the Scarlet Crusade, they welcome champions of any race or faction who honor the cause of the Light. From their fortified sanctuary at Light's Hope Chapel to far-flung outposts across Kalimdor, they stand on the front lines against darkness. When Highlord Alexandros Mograine fell and Lordaeron collapsed into ruin, the shattered remnants of the Knights of the Silver Hand broke into bitter disagreement. Many survivors surrendered to grief and paranoia, morphing into the xenophobic Scarlet Crusade. Yet veterans like Lord Maxwell Tyrosus recognized that their former comrades had abandoned the true tenets of the Holy Light. Refusing to succumb to madness or abandon the dead kingdom, they split away to form the Argent Dawn—an order committed to defending Azeroth alongside anyone willing to fight, whether Alliance or Horde.

Arthas Menethil. Once the golden prince of Lordaeron and a celebrated paladin of the Silver Hand, Arthas Menethil fell from grace during the Third War while pursuing the demonic orchestrators of the plague. After claiming the cursed runeblade Frostmourne in the frozen north, he surrendered his soul, murdered his father King Terenas, and spearheaded the destruction of his own homeland as the Scourge's dark champion. Born to King Terenas Menethil II, Arthas was raised to embody the ideals of the Alliance of Lordaeron. Trained in combat by Muradin Bronzebeard and inducted into the Order of the Silver Hand under the tutelage of Uther the Lightbringer, he was revered by high and low alike as the future of humanity. Bold, skilled, and fiercely protective of his people, he fought tenaciously against Blackrock clan orc incursions and forest troll warbands. Yet beneath his radiant exterior lay an uncompromising pride and an obsessive dread of failure.

Black dragonflight. Once the stalwart Earth-Warders charged by the titans to safeguard Azeroth's deep subterranean realms, the black dragonflight fell to madness and treachery. Corrupted by the insidious whispers of the imprisoned Old Gods, their leader Neltharion became Deathwing, turning his brood into one of the most destructive and hated forces on the planet. Today, their surviving scions weave plots from the shadows and wage covert wars against mortal kingdoms. Long ago, the Titan Khaz'goroth bestowed his blessing upon Neltharion, creating the black dragonflight to watch over the earth, raise mountains, and guard Azeroth's deep caverns. For ages, they stood alongside the other flights as patient, unyielding guardians. Yet their intimate bond with the world's subterranean foundations proved their undoing. Dwelling within the deepest hollows, they lay dangerously close to the sunken prisons of the Old Gods. Over centuries, dark whispers eroded the noble Earth-Warder's mind, driving him to madness and twisting his entire brood into vicious instruments of ruin.

Blackrock clan. The Blackrock clan is a martial orcish clan renowned for its strict military discipline, unmatched blacksmithing, and central role in the First and Second Wars. Today, the clan is deeply fractured: while some veterans follow Thrall in the New Horde, a vicious and renegade splinter group known as the Dark Horde occupies the upper peaks of Blackrock Mountain under Rend Blackhand. Hailing from Draenor, the Blackrock clan made its name through rigid hierarchy, heavy armor, and mastery over the forge. Under Chieftain Blackhand, they served as the brutal core of the Old Horde during the invasion of Azeroth, laying siege to Stormwind. When Orgrim Doomhammer slew Blackhand to cleanse the Horde of Gul'dan's direct puppet mastery, leadership of both the clan and the Horde remained firmly in Blackrock hands through the grueling campaigns of the Second War.

Bronzebeard clan. The Bronzebeard clan is the ruling dwarven royal line and dominant population of Ironforge. Following their victory in the ancient War of the Three Hammers, they forged strong ties with humanity and the gnomes, standing today under King Magni Bronzebeard as a cornerstone of the Alliance. Long ago, dwarven society in Ironforge flourished under High King Modimus Anvilmar. When the king died of old age roughly 230 years ago, simmering rivalries erupted into civil war. Thane Madoran Bronzebeard commanded the traditional garrison and largest standing army within Ironforge, successfully driving both the Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans from under the mountain. When Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan mounted an assault to reconquer Khaz Modan, Madoran Bronzebeard led his clan in a decisive campaign that shattered the Dark Iron host, solidifying Bronzebeard supremacy over Ironforge.

Brotherhood of Northshire. The Brotherhood of Northshire is a holy human clerical order dedicated to the Church of the Holy Light, based out of Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest. Originally known as the Clerics of Northshire, the order suffered catastrophic losses during the First War before being reformed under Archbishop Alonsus Faol. Today, the Brotherhood serves as both a spiritual sanctuary and the primary training ground for fledgling Alliance defenders. Centuries ago, pious missionaries traveled south from Lordaeron into the kingdom of Stormwind, establishing Northshire Abbey to minister to the people and soothe the realm through the Holy Light. Originally known as the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics, their compassion was legendary—they even tended to injured gnolls and jungle trolls during past border wars. When the Orcish Horde crossed through the Dark Portal, the clerics marched bravely to the front lines without armor or weapons to heal fallen soldiers. Because their healing sustained the Stormwind Army, the orcs ruthlessly targeted them. The order was decimated, the abbey was ransacked and burned, and the surviving clerics were forced to flee north across the sea to Southshore with Sir Anduin Lothar.

Burning Blade clan. Once an ancient orcish clan renowned for its deadly blademasters and consumed by chaotic frenzy during the early wars, the Burning Blade now largely persists as a sinister demon-worshiping cult. Its acolytes infiltrate Durotar and the Barrens under the direction of the Shadow Council. Meanwhile, a handful of honorable blademasters have forsaken its demonic corruption to serve Warchief Thrall in the New Horde. Originating in the lands of Draenor alongside clans like the Warsong, the Burning Blade were long respected for the lethal tradition of their blademasters. When they drank the blood of Mannoroth and marched through the Dark Portal into Azeroth during the First War, however, the clan fractured mentally. By the Second War, they were scarcely an organized society, behaving instead like a berserk force of nature. Nomadic and demented, they threw themselves into battle with total disregard for survival, requiring ogres to hold them in check until unleashed. Ultimately, their numbers were battered and routed near the Dark Portal by the Alliance.

Burning Legion. The Burning Legion is an infinite, apocalyptic host of demons led by the fallen titan Sargeras, dedicated to scouring all life from creation. Having already shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, the demons remain Azeroth's most relentless nemesis, orchestrating the corruption of the orcs and the horrors of the Third War. Long ago, Sargeras stood as the champion of the titans, tasked with hunting down and imprisoning the demons that plagued the cosmos. Over countless ages of battling their evil, he grew disillusioned and concluded that creation itself was fatally flawed and must be unmade in flame. To enact his crusade, he freed the demons he had imprisoned, bending them to his will through fel magic. He augmented their chaos with the intellect of the corrupted eredar—elevating Archimonde and Kil'jaeden as his chief lieutenants—and forged an unstoppable engine of cosmic annihilation.

Cenarion Circle. The Cenarion Circle is an ancient, independent order of druids founded by Malfurion Stormrage under the guidance of the demigod Cenarius. Operating from their sacred haven in Moonglade, they strive to maintain the balance of nature, safeguard the Emerald Dream, and mend Azeroth's blighted lands. Though historically composed of night elves, they have recently welcomed the tauren into their ranks, transcending factional divides to defend the living world. The roots of the Cenarion Circle go back thousands of years to the teachings of Cenarius, the Patron of Druids, who mentored the first mortal druid, Malfurion Stormrage. Following the Great Sundering, Malfurion bound together those who wished to study nature's ways. The order made its home in the sacred vale of Moonglade, and ever since, the Circle has held sacred vigil over Azeroth's wild places.

Cenarius. Cenarius, the Lord of the Forest, is the ancient demigod son of Elune and Malorne who taught the night elves the secrets of druidism. For thousands of years he served as the great patron of mortal druids and guardian of the wilderness before falling in battle during the Third War. Cenarius was born to Elune, the goddess of the moon, and the great white stag demigod Malorne. Because Cenarius was bound to the mortal world, Elune placed him in the care of Malorne, while Ysera the Dreamer embraced him as a foster mother and guided him through the infinite paths of the Emerald Dream. Blessed with powers over living wood and earth, Cenarius fathered the Keepers of the Grove and the dryads, forever tying his bloodline to the wild places of Kalimdor.

Centaur. Centaur are a violent, horse-bodied humanoid race whose nomadic clans dominate the arid plains of central Kalimdor. Born from the tragic union between the demigod Zaetar and the earth princess Theradras, they spent centuries driving the tauren toward extinction before the newly arrived orcish Horde intervened. Centaur legend traces the race to the caverns of Maraudon beneath Desolace. There, Zaetar, one of the immortal sons of the demigod Cenarius, and Princess Theradras, daughter of the elemental lord Therazane, sired the first centaur. Upon their emergence, the barbaric offspring turned on their father and killed him. Grief-stricken, Theradras trapped Zaetar's spirit within the winding caverns of Maraudon, yet she shielded her vicious children, who swiftly multiplied across Kalimdor.

Church of the Holy Light. The Church of the Holy Light is the dominant religious institution of humanity, guiding mortal souls through the virtues of compassion, justice, and devotion. Originally centered in the lost northern kingdom of Lordaeron, its leadership now resides within the grand Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City following the devastation wrought by the Scourge. The Church's origins reach back over a millennium to the faith in the Holy Light that took root among the humans of Arathor, teaching them to channel sacred power to cure injuries and purge affliction. Driven by tenets of charity, righteousness, and the fundamental belief that the Light resides within all thinking beings, these teachings eventually coalesced into an organized faith. The kingdom of Lordaeron became the religious heartland of this doctrine, establishing revered sanctuaries throughout the north, including Stratholme, Andorhal, Tyr's Hand, and Light's Hope Chapel.

Cult of the Damned. The Cult of the Damned is a secretive cabal of mortal zealots, necromancers, and aristocrats devoted to the Lich King. Formed in northern Lordaeron prior to the Third War, its members poisoned the grain supplies that spawned the Scourge and engineered the downfall of humanity's greatest kingdom. Today, the surviving cultists manage the plague cauldrons and necromantic academies across the Plaguelands while actively infiltrating the cities of the living. The Cult of the Damned was forged by the exiled Archmage Kel'Thuzad after he answered the telepathic whispers of the Lich King emanating from the Frozen Throne. Returning to Lordaeron with vast wealth and forbidden dark arts, Kel'Thuzad offered two false gospels: to the desperate, impoverished lower classes, he promised social equality and liberation from misery; to the wealthy landowners, such as the noble House of Barov, he promised eternal life and an unshakeable grip upon their domains. In truth, both the destitute and the affluent were cattle intended for slaughter, bound into a death cult designed to betray their homeland from the inside.

Dark Iron clan. The Dark Iron clan is an ancient, ash-skinned dwarven faction ruling from the volcanic depths of Blackrock Mountain. Cast out of Ironforge during the War of the Three Hammers, they accidentally summoned Ragnaros the Firelord, who enslaved their empire. Today, under Emperor Dagran Thaurissan, they wage shadow wars against both the Alliance and the Horde while serving their fiery elemental master. Long ago, three dwarven factions lived together in Ironforge under High King Modimus Anvilmar. When the king died, civil war erupted. The Bronzebeards defeated both rival factions, casting out the Wildhammers and Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan's Dark Irons. Vowing vengeance, Thaurissan established a settlement in the Redridge Mountains while his sorceress wife, Modgud, led an army against Grim Batol. When both assaults failed and the united Bronzebeard and Wildhammer armies marched on his stronghold, Thaurissan attempted to unleash an apocalyptic subterranean entity to save himself. His ritual breached the core of the world and freed Ragnaros the Firelord.

Dark Iron dwarf. Dark Iron dwarves are a distinct dwarven sub-race distinguished by their ashen skin, blazing red eyes, and innate affinity for fire. Banished from Ironforge following the civil War of the Three Hammers, they dwell deep within Blackrock Mountain where their society has fallen under the tyrannical rule of the Firelord, Ragnaros. Unlike their Bronzebeard and Wildhammer cousins, Dark Iron dwarves possess dark gray or soot-black skin and eyes that burn like glowing embers. Their history fractured during the War of the Three Hammers, when their Sorcerer-thane Thaurissan sought to conquer Ironforge. Defeated and driven south into the Redridge Mountains, Thaurissan attempted to summon dark powers to avenge his losses, inadvertently releasing Ragnaros the Firelord from the Elemental Plane. The catastrophic summoning shattered the surrounding peaks into the volcanic waste of Blackrock Mountain and bound the Dark Iron race into fiery servitude.

Dark Riders. The Dark Riders are a band of mysterious, hooded horsemen who terrorize Duskwood. Merciless hunters of magical relics, they strike from hiding and leave only slaughter in their wake. Little is known of the Dark Riders' origins. Witnesses describe hooded horsemen who speak in voices both harsh and shrill, and one was seen using a small gem to take orders from a master it called only its 'Lord'. They hunt objects of magical power across the kingdom, cutting down anyone who stands between them and their prize.

Darkspear tribe. The Darkspear are a tribe of jungle trolls who joined Thrall's Horde after being driven from their ancestral home in Stranglethorn Vale and rescued from a sea witch in the Great Sea. Led by Shadow Hunter Vol'jin from their temporary refuge at Sen'jin Village, they now serve as core members of the Horde across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Despite their alliance, they currently struggle to reclaim their new home, the Echo Isles, from the traitorous witch doctor Zalazane. Originally a smaller, less ruthless tribe within the broken Gurubashi Empire of Stranglethorn Vale, the Darkspear endured centuries of warfare and famine against brutal neighbors like the Bloodscalp and Skullsplitter tribes. Driven out to sea, they settled on remote islands, only to face aquatic murlocs, Kul Tiran sailors, and a naga sea witch. Their elder chieftain, Sen'jin, was captured and slain in dark sacrificial rites beneath the sea, but before dying he foretold that the orc Warchief Thrall would lead the Darkspear to a new destiny. Rescued by Thrall's passing fleet, the survivors pledged their undying loyalty to the new Horde and sailed westward to Kalimdor.

Defias Brotherhood. The Defias Brotherhood is a widespread criminal network of bandits, brigands, and assassins waging an underground insurgency against the Kingdom of Stormwind. Originally formed by the artisans of the Stonemasons Guild who were cheated of their pay for rebuilding the capital, they have devolved into violent outlaws terrorizing the southern farmlands. From their hidden redoubt deep beneath Westfall, they aim to overthrow the corrupt House of Nobles and lay waste to the kingdom. Following the Second War, the Stonemasons Guild was hired to rebuild Stormwind from smoldering ruins into a grand stone capital. When their masterwork was finished, the House of Nobles refused to deliver the promised payment, citing crushing wartime debt. Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef spoke out on behalf of his workers, demanding fair restitution, but the nobles responded by ordering the Stonemasons Guild disbanded. The ensuing riots in the city streets ended with the laborers driven out of Stormwind into exile. Stripped of their livelihood and outlawed, VanCleef and the desperate workers banded together, binding their faces in red silk to represent the blood of the wronged, and turned to highway robbery to claim what they believed they were owed.

Dragonmaw clan. The Dragonmaw clan is an infamous orcish faction notorious for subduing and riding red dragons during the Second War. Guided by dark artifacts and foul magic, they imprisoned the Dragonqueen Alexstrasza beneath the cursed halls of Grim Batol until her liberation shattered their dominion. Today, their scattered remnants lurk in the wetlands and mountains of Khaz Modan, remaining hostile to both the Alliance and Thrall's New Horde. The Dragonmaw clan hailed from Draenor and crossed the Dark Portal with the Old Horde. On Azeroth, they turned their talents to subjugating its winged terrors.

Druid. Druids are guardians of the natural world who draw power directly from the wild spirits, the celestial bodies, and the Emerald Dream. Master shapeshifters, they adopt the forms of primal beasts to protect the land or mend grievous wounds. Practiced primarily by the night elves, newly revived among the tauren and kept alive by the Skyborne, druids place the preservation of nature above all mortal allegiance. Druidism is far more than a martial art; it is an ancient way of life rooted in deep communion with nature and the demigod Cenarius. Druids wield raw natural energies, commanding roots to entangle their foes, directing the celestial brilliance of the moon and stars, and invoking restorative flora to knit bone and flesh. Their duty is to preserve the cosmic balance and protect the unfettered wild from exploitation and corruption.

Druids of the Fang. The Druids of the Fang are a splinter sect of night elf druids who succumbed to corruption deep within the Wailing Caverns. Originally disciples of the visionary Naralex, they abandoned the Cenarion Circle after their master's connection to the Emerald Dream turned into a foul nightmare. Under the self-proclaimed Lord Serpentis, they now wield serpent-like forms and seek to remake the Barrens into their own twisted paradise. The Barrens was not always an arid wasteland, and Naralex sought to return it to the lush, verdant sanctuary it once was. Naralex led a dedicated order of young druids into the subterranean depths of the Wailing Caverns, tapping into the natural underground fissures and subterranean springs. By entering an induced slumber, Naralex hoped to channel the living energies of the Emerald Dream into the waterways, nursing the scorched savannah above back to vibrant life.

Dwarf. Dwarves are a stout, resilient race carved from the living stone of ancient titan-forged earthen, now inhabiting the snow-capped mountain kingdoms of Khaz Modan and beyond. Known for their mastery of stonework, metallurgy, and devastating frontline combat, they stand as one of the Alliance's fiercest and most dependable pillars. Under the reign of King Magni Bronzebeard, their sprawling subterranean capital of Ironforge serves as the beating heart of dwarven society. Long ago, the subterranean titan-forged known as earthen awoke from an eons-long slumber within the vaults of Uldaman, transformed by the Curse of Flesh into beings of blood and bone. Taking the name dwarves, they reclaimed the high crags of Khaz Modan—named in honor of the titan Khaz'goroth—and carved the majestic subterranean stronghold of Ironforge beneath the peaks of Dun Morogh. Endowed with incredible natural fortitude, a sharp eye for stone and ore, and a penchant for roaring hearths and heady ale, dwarves approach craftsmanship and warfare with identical tenacity.

Earth Mother. The Earth Mother is the supreme, benevolent creator deity worshipped by the tauren, revered as the living embodiment and architect of Azeroth's land and elements. In tauren myth, she shaped the mountains, plains, and seasons and set the sun and moon in the sky as her watchful eyes. Her presence permeates everyday tauren culture, guiding their reverence for nature, duty to the elements, and hopes for the afterlife. Tauren creation myths tell that before day and night existed, the Earth Mother set about shaping Azeroth as a haven for her coming children. Scraping her nails across newly raised mountains sparked the world's first fires, while her hands carved rivers and ocean beds. Her laughter gave breath to the wind, and by lifting the primordial fogs into the sky, she brought the first rains, which coaxed grass, forests, and grain from the soil.

Elemental Plane. The Elemental Plane is an interconnected pocket dimension forged by the titans to imprison Azeroth's chaotic elementals. Divided into four distinct realms—Skywall, Deepholm, the Abyssal Maw, and the Firelands—it confines the primordial spirits away from the mortal world. Though sealed long ago, cracks in its barriers allow violent elemental incursions and catastrophic summonings into Azeroth. In the ancient days, the elementals served as lieutenants of the Old Gods. When the titans triumphed, they banished the elemental lords and their myriad servants into an isolated realm known as the Elemental Plane, divided into four domains tailored to each primal force: Skywall for air, Deepholm for earth, the Abyssal Maw for water, and the Firelands for fire. With the elementals' departure, nature calmed, and Azeroth's surface finally knew peace.

Elune. Elune is the revered moon goddess of Azeroth, worshipped primarily by the night elves as their benevolent protector and mother of the forest demigod Cenarius. Associated with the larger moon, the White Lady, she governs peace, healing, and lunar fury across the world. In tauren myth, she is honored as Mu'sha, the gentle left eye of the Earth Mother. Elune is one of the few true deities acknowledged across Azeroth, bound inseparably to the night sky and the larger of the world's two moons, the White Lady. While never appearing in a physical form on the world, night elven artisans portray her as a kaldorei of transcendent grace, bathed in luminescence with alabaster skin, silver hair, and eyes of pure moonlight. Ancient legends among the kaldorei claim she once rested in the depths of the Well of Eternity during the daylight hours, whispering wisdom to the early night elves.

Emerald Dream. The Emerald Dream is a vast, ever-shifting spirit realm representing Azeroth in its primordial state, completely untouched by civilization. Watched over by the Dragon Aspect Ysera and her green flight, it serves as the spiritual blueprint of nature and the sacred domain where druids commune with the cycle of life. Existing outside the physical plane yet tethered to its heartbeat, the Emerald Dream reflects what Azeroth would look like had intelligent beings never cleared its forests or built cities upon its stone. Sculpted during the ancient ordering of the world, it is an ever-shifting wilderness of pristine forests, boundless plains, and primordial rivers. Time and distance hold little meaning within the Dream; days in the physical world can feel like decades in the spirit, and landmarks change shape like mist before mortal eyes.

Explorers' League. The Explorers' League is a renowned dwarven archaeological guild headquartered in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers. Founded under King Magni Bronzebeard and led by his wandering brother Brann, the League seeks to uncover the forgotten origins of the dwarven race. Their expansive digs span across Azeroth, uncovering ancient titan ruins while frequently igniting regional conflicts. For centuries, the dwarves of Khaz Modan focused their formidable energies on mining, stonework, and engineering. That focus changed drastically when ancient ruins were unearthed, hinting at a forgotten legacy connecting dwarves to mythical titan creators. Eager to solve the mystery of his people's beginnings, King Magni Bronzebeard decreed that dwarven industry pivot heavily toward archaeology. Magni, alongside his brother Brann, established the Explorers' Guild—now widely known as the Explorers' League—to scour the world for relics, forgotten cities, and traces of their ancient ancestry.

First War. The First War was the devastating five-year conflict in which the Orcish Horde emerged through the Dark Portal and completely destroyed the human Kingdom of Stormwind. Orchestrated behind the scenes by the demon-possessed Guardian Medivh and the warlock Gul'dan, it concluded with the assassination of King Llane Wrynn I and the flight of human survivors north to Lordaeron. Before the war, the Kingdom of Stormwind enjoyed long years of peace following the Gnoll War, guarded by its Knights and the Clerics of Northshire Abbey. That stability shattered when the Guardian Medivh, secretly possessed by the demon lord Sargeras, contacted the orc warlock Gul'dan on Draenor. Together, they forged the Dark Portal in the swampy Black Morass. Driven by demon blood and the slow death of their homeworld, the Orcish Horde crossed into Azeroth in force. Early rumors dismissed the invaders as vengeful spirits or strange offshoots of trolls, but Sir Anduin Lothar's scouting patrols quickly confirmed the arrival of a disciplined, bloodthirsty army.

Forsaken. The Forsaken are a free-willed faction of intelligent undead who broke away from the Scourge following the Third War. Led by the Banshee Queen Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, they dwell within the subterranean Undercity carved beneath the ruins of Lordaeron's capital. Though deeply distrusted across Azeroth, they maintain a tenuous alliance of convenience with the Horde. When the Lich King's grip over his northern armies slipped after the Third War, thousands of undead in the blighted ruins of Lordaeron suddenly regained their sapience and memories. Horrified by the butchery they had been forced to carry out while enslaved to his will, these former citizens found themselves reviled and hunted by the living. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the fallen ranger-general of Quel'Thalas who had been transformed into an unholy banshee, rallied these adrift spirits, claimed the catacombs beneath Capital City, and dubbed her new nation the Forsaken.

Frostmane tribe. The Frostmane tribe consists of fierce ice trolls indigenous to the frigid peaks of Dun Morogh. Driven into caves and remote ridges by the dwarves of Ironforge centuries ago, they wage an unrelenting guerrilla war to reclaim their ancestral home. Long before the Bronzebeard clan united under Ironforge, the Frostmane trolls held dominion across the snowbound expanses of Dun Morogh. The rise and expansion of the dwarven kingdom crushed their realm, pushing the surviving ice trolls into retreat along the frozen ridges and crags. This humiliating defeat sparked a bitter generational hatred that endures to this day. The Frostmane treat every mountaineer, traveler, and homestead as an invading enemy to be driven out or slaughtered.

Furbolg. Furbolgs are a hulking, reclusive race of bear-men native to northern Kalimdor who lived in harmony with nature and the night elves for millennia. In the wake of the Third War, demonic corruption and lingering fel magic have driven nearly every tribe into a frenzied madness. Today, former friends have become vicious territorial predators, with only a tiny handful of tribes clinging to their sanity. Furbolgs are an ancient people of Kalimdor who have long revered the wild god Ursoc. During the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago, tribal packs united under chieftain Unng Ak to fight alongside night elves and tauren against the first demonic invasion. Following the Great Sundering, they chose seclusion deep in the northern woodlands, maintaining peaceful ties with night elf druids and forest wardens while living in simple harmony with the wild.

Gnoll. Gnolls are a savage, hyena-like race of humanoid scavengers and raiders found scattered across both the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. Renowned for their vicious infighting, brutal strength, and animal cunning, they survive by pillaging settlements, butchering wildlife, and ambushing unwary travelers. Left unchecked, their sprawling packs and warlords pose a constant threat to frontier hamlets and trade roads alike. Standing slightly shorter than the average human but possessing explosive physical power, gnolls are bipedal hyena-kin known for their spiky teeth, thick pelts, and distinct barking laugh. While fully capable of walking upright, they often drop to all fours to lope swiftly through brush or track prey by scent. Gnoll culture values raw physical dominance above all else. They organize into fractious packs led by the strongest, cruelest alpha, only yielding when battered into submission by a superior force.

Gnome. Gnomes are a diminutive, eccentric, and astonishingly intelligent race renowned across Azeroth for their inventive engineering and mastery of the arcane. Despite their cheerful demeanor, they recently suffered a catastrophic tragedy when a subterranean trogg invasion and a disastrous defense plan irradiated their capital of Gnomeregan. Now living as refugees in Ironforge's Tinker Town, the gnomes remain staunch Alliance allies as they fight to reclaim their lost home. Small in stature but towering in intellect, gnomes approach the world with boundless curiosity and scientific ambition. While other races focus on recording histories and preserving traditions, gnomes look relentlessly forward, dedicating their lives to mechanical engineering, arcane studies, and technological innovation. Their inventions—ranging from clockwork devices and flying machines to complex subterranean trains—have shaped the modern world. Even after devastating hardships, gnomefolk maintain an irrepressible cheerfulness and an unshakable drive to rebuild and solve the impossible.

Goblin. Goblins are diminutive, cunning humanoids originating from the Isle of Kezan, renowned across Azeroth for their relentless pursuit of profit, explosive engineering, and aggressive trade cartels. While most maintain a stance of strict neutrality to maximize commerce between the Alliance and Horde, mercenary and cutthroat outfits like the Venture Company and Steamwheedle Cartel leave an indelible mark on every corner of the world. Goblins hail from the Isle of Kezan in the South Seas, where their society long ago divided into competing economic syndicates known as cartels. Rather than building kingdoms or armies of their own, goblin leaders channeled their ambitions into cutthroat mercantilism, volatile engineering, and industrial ventures that now reach every corner of the world.

Grimtotem tribe. The Grimtotem tribe is an aggressive, fiercely traditionalist tauren clan that refuses to formally swear allegiance to Thrall's Horde. Distinguishable by their dark hides and fierce warpaint, they seek to purge foreign races from Kalimdor and retake ancestral lands by any means necessary. Even as their matriarch, the Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem, resides atop Thunder Bluff playing regional politics, her kin actively raid settlements across Kalimdor. Unlike their peaceful cousins who honor the Earth Mother through reverence, the Grimtotem believe Kalimdor belongs exclusively to the tauren. From youth, they are trained not in the patient harmony of the Great Hunt, but in ruthlessness, stealth, and lethal combat. They harbor immense disdain for the other races that have settled upon their ancient soils. Though Cairne Bloodhoof has welcomed them into Thunder Bluff in an effort to unite all tauren people, the Grimtotem clan stands alone as the only major tribe that has never formally joined Thrall's Horde, maintaining their own insular and violent agenda.

Grommash Hellscream. Grommash Hellscream was the legendary chieftain of the Warsong clan, a close brother-in-arms to Warchief Thrall, and the first orc to drink the blood of Mannoroth. Though his thirst for battle once bound his people to the Burning Legion, he redeemed the orcish race by slaying the demon lord in Ashenvale at the cost of his own life. Before the Dark Portal ever bridged worlds, Grom Hellscream led the Warsong clan with unyielding ferocity, distinguished by his pitch-black tattooed jaw and the deadly sweep of his two-handed axe, Gorehowl. When Gul'dan and the Shadow Council offered the chalice of demonic strength on Draenor, Grom was the first chieftain to drink the blood of the pit lord Mannoroth. That fateful draught doomed the orcish race to demonic subservience and a burning bloodlust. Yet unlike many chieftains who perished or succumbed entirely, Grom possessed an iron will that kept his fierce spirit intact, surviving the horrors of the old Horde while harboring an unspoken ache for what his people had surrendered.

Harpy. Harpies are predatory, avian humanoids resembling winged night elves who dwell in foul-smelling roosts across Kalimdor and the high mountain passes of Alterac. Infamous for their shrill shrieks and tempestuous elemental magic, they raid unwary travelers and blight the environments they inhabit. Night elf folklore links them to cursed betrayers of Queen Azshara, though their true origins remain uncertain. Harpies bear the upper torsos and heads of night elf women, joined to broad feathered wings and wicked talons. Despite their delicate, elven visage—which ironically grows more striking as they age—their nature is thoroughly savage. Originally roosting among the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, they have aggressively migrated across Kalimdor, terrorizing the arid canyons of Durotar, the sacred boughs of Teldrassil, and the heights of Mulgore. Unlike the wild creatures they hunt, harpies do not live in harmony with nature; they despoil surrounding flora and fauna, turning their nesting grounds into foul, fetid middens littered with the picked-clean bones of their prey.

Highborne. The Highborne, or quel'dorei, were the aristocratic sorcerer caste of the ancient Kaldorei Empire who served Queen Azshara. Their reckless manipulation of the Well of Eternity brought the Burning Legion to Azeroth, leading to the devastating War of the Ancients and the Great Sundering. Before the Sundering, the Highborne arose as the favored upper class surrounding Queen Azshara. Claiming superiority over common kaldorei through selective bloodlines, intelligence, and opulent privilege, they strictly controlled access to the Well of Eternity. They discovered how to tap and shape its primal arcane energies, erecting magnificent cities across ancient Kalimdor. Their endless thirst for greater sorcery led them to draw deeper from the Well, turning its calm waters turbulent and dark.

Horde. The Horde is a coalition of outcast nations united under Warchief Thrall to secure their mutual survival and freedom. Anchored by the shamanic bond of the orcs, Darkspear trolls, and tauren across Kalimdor, the faction also maintains an uneasy alliance of convenience with the Forsaken in Lordaeron. Beset by historical grievances and hostile neighbors, the Horde values strength, action, and honor over political maneuverings. The modern Horde bears little resemblance to the demonic army that marched through the Dark Portal in the First and Second Wars. After shattering the Burning Legion's grasp upon his people, Warchief Thrall led the orcs across the Great Sea to Kalimdor to build a spiritual homeland founded on ancestral traditions and honor. Along the way, Thrall forged lasting ties with Vol'jin's displaced Darkspear trolls and Cairne Bloodhoof's tauren tribes, fighting side by side to drive off centaur and demonic incursions during the Third War.

House of Nobles. The House of Nobles is the hereditary aristocratic council that helps administer the kingdom of Stormwind from Stormwind Keep. Holding immense leverage over regional land, taxation, and trade, their refusal to pay the rebuilt city's laborers ignited the bloody riots that gave birth to the Defias Brotherhood. Composed of Stormwind's most powerful patrician bloodlines, the House of Nobles serves as the primary advisory body to the Crown. Because the aristocracy owns the majority of the arable land throughout Elwynn, Westfall, and Duskwood, they wield outsized authority over commerce, regional magistrates, and royal decrees. While the boy-king Anduin Wrynn and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon officially rule the kingdom, the council routinely ties the throne's hands in red tape, asserting the power to stall trials, block executions, and meddle in provincial administration.

Human. Humans are an adaptable and resilient mortal race who have shaped much of the Eastern Kingdoms' history. Once unified under the ancient Empire of Arathor, their civilization fractured into the Seven Kingdoms, with Stormwind now standing as humanity's primary surviving bastion within the Alliance. Millennia ago, early humans lived as scattered, nomadic tribes constantly threatened by the Amani forest trolls. Recognizing that disunity would mean extinction, Warlord Thoradin of the Arathi tribe united the disparate clans through diplomacy and conquest, establishing the Empire of Arathor with its fortress capital at Strom. During the Troll Wars, the beleaguered high elves of Quel'Thalas allied with Arathor, teaching one hundred humans the arts of arcane magic. Together, they broke the troll armies, securing humanity's dominion over the central continents and laying the foundation for future mortal alliances.

Hunter. Masters of wilderness survival and deadly marksmanship, hunters roam the untamed reaches of Azeroth alongside fierce beast companions. Armed with bows, rifles, or crossbows, they excel at harassing enemies from a distance while relying on clever traps and primal aspects to control the flow of battle. Whether tracking elusive quarry across snowcapped peaks or stalking prey through dense forests, they live by their wits and connection to nature. At the heart of every hunter lies an instinctual empathy for the primal world. Unlike those who exploit nature or isolate themselves within stone bastions, hunters immerse themselves entirely in untamed lands. They study the habits, movements, and strengths of predatory beasts, earning their respect rather than breaking their spirits. Through patient bonding, a hunter tames dangerous creatures—such as fierce prowling cats, stubborn mountain bears, and sharp-eyed raptors—turning wild animals into steadfast allies that defend them to the death.

Juggernaught. A Juggernaught is an enormous, heavily armored battleship bristling with heavy naval cannons. Built with ogre help to serve as the iron core of the Old Horde's fleet during the Second War, these floating fortresses were built to pulverize coastal strongholds and trade routes. Reports of a great vessel beneath Westfall draw attention to the hidden workings of the Defias Brotherhood. Orcs were not traditionally a seafaring culture, so when the Horde required a fleet capable of crossing the Great Sea and contesting the Alliance's naval superiority during the Second War, they relied heavily on ogre ingenuity. The resulting craft—the ogre juggernaught—became the backbone of the Horde armada. Though vastly slower and less nimble than swift troll destroyers, these behemoths carried immense plating and devastating broadside batteries that could shatter Alliance hulls and smash shore fortifications to rubble.

Knights of the Silver Hand. The Knights of the Silver Hand are the legendary order of holy paladins founded after the First War to combine martial combat with the healing and smiting power of the Holy Light. Though their original northern chapter was broken during the fall of Lordaeron, surviving knights carry on their sacred vows in Stormwind and Ironforge, while scattered remnants battle the undead in the northern Plaguelands. Following the destruction of Stormwind during the First War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol recognized a dire flaw in the Alliance's defenses: the clerics of Northshire were devoted and skilled healers, but they lacked martial training and fell easily on the front lines. To ensure holy warriors could endure the brutal combat of the Second War, Faol and his premier student, Uther the Lightbringer, founded the Order of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Faol recruited both battle-hardened knights willing to learn devotion to the Light and devout clerics willing to bear plate armor and warhammers.

Kobold. Kobolds are diminutive, rat-like subterranean humanoids found scuttling through mines and caverns across Azeroth. Notorious for their obsessive devotion to the tallow candles strapped to their heads, they are individually cowardly but dangerous in swarms, fiercely defending their dig sites against any who threaten their light. Standing barely four feet tall, kobolds are filthy, subterranean scavengers who spend their lives delving into the earth. Though they possess low-light vision, the deepest shafts are pitch-black, compelling every kobold to affix a crude candle to their head. While cowardly when cornered alone, kobolds breed in massive numbers and work with relentless energy. When agitated, their rat-like tails whip violently, and they overwhelm intruders in frantic mobs, beating foes to death with heavy iron mining picks.

Kolkar clan. The Kolkar are an aggressive clan of centaur native to central Kalimdor, claiming descent from the legendary first Khan, Kolk. They maintain strongholds in Desolace and across the Barrens, frequently raiding Horde settlements and fighting anyone who crosses their path. The Kolkar take their name from Khan Kolk, the legendary first centaur khan born from the union of Zaetar and Theradras. Driven by a deep hatred for other races and their fellow centaur clans alike, the Kolkar distinguish themselves by their red markings and an absolute refusal to form alliances. Historically based out of their ancient village in eastern Desolace, the restless spirit of Khan Kolk still wanders the subterranean depths of their ancestral lands.

Kul Tiras. Kul Tiras is an insular maritime human kingdom situated on an island archipelago in the Great Sea, west of Dun Morogh and Baradin Bay. Renowned for possessing the mightiest navy in Azeroth, it served as a cornerstone of the Alliance of Lordaeron during the Second War under Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore. Following the fracturing of the old Alliance and tragic losses in Kalimdor, the island realm has largely receded into isolated waters. Kul Tiras blossomed into an unmatched seafaring power, sustained by an industrious merchant marine, rich fishing grounds, and a naval armada without peer in human history.

Leper gnome. Leper gnomes are the tragic, mutated survivors of Gnomeregan's catastrophic irradiation during the Third War. Maddened by toxic fallout and lingering fumes, most have sworn fealty to the usurper Mekgineer Thermaplugg, fiercely defending their ruined city against all outsiders. When trogg invaders breached Gnomeregan during the Third War, Mekgineer Thermaplugg advised High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque to flood the city with radioactive toxins. Thermaplugg claimed the poison would exterminate the troggs while sparing the gnomish population. Instead, the catastrophe wiped out eighty percent of the city's inhabitants. Those who survived within the sealed lower levels were warped in mind and flesh by toxic fallout, mutating into pale, pustulant wretches dubbed leper gnomes.

Lich King. The Lich King is the lord and psychic master of the undead Scourge, ruling from the Frozen Throne far to the north in Icecrown. Originally forged by the demon Kil'jaeden from the spirit of the orc shaman Ner'zhul, the entity eventually lured Prince Arthas Menethil into corruption, culminating in their fateful union atop Northrend's icy peaks. When the orc shaman Ner'zhul attempted to flee the dying world of Draenor, he fell directly into the clutches of Kil'jaeden the Deceiver. The demon lord tore Ner'zhul's body to shreds but bound his tormented soul into a block of diamond-hard ice cast out of the Twisting Nether. Flung into Azeroth, the glacial monolith struck the northern wastes of Northrend, forming the Frozen Throne. Kil'jaeden intended the Lich King to forge an unstoppable undead vanguard that would dismantle the mortal kingdoms without succumbing to the infighting that ruined the Orcish Horde. Instead, armed with immense telepathic power, Ner'zhul immediately began plotting his own bid for freedom.

Light. The Light is a boundless primal cosmic force whose energy connects and suffuses all living things across creation. Manifested in the mortal realm as Holy magic, it responds to willpower, meditation, and unyielding faith to mend flesh, shield allies, and purge darkness. The Light is an omnipresent force of living energy. When brought into Azeroth, it manifests as Holy magic. Its power flows through living souls as a connective tissue, binding mortal hearts together. While mortals often personify it as a conscious protector, the Light fundamentally answers the absolute conviction of the soul calling upon it.

Llane Wrynn I. King Llane Wrynn I was the ruler of Stormwind during the catastrophic First War, whose reign ended with the fall of the kingdom and his own tragic murder. A beloved and proud monarch, his steadfast refusal to believe his friend Medivh had betrayed humanity ultimately doomed his defense of the capital. Born to King Barathen Wrynn, young Prince Llane grew up alongside Anduin Lothar and Medivh. In their youth, the three companions ventured into the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale and clashed with the Gurubashi trolls there. In time, Llane ascended to the throne as Stormwind's king.

Lordaeron. Lordaeron is the great northern subcontinent of the Eastern Kingdoms, once the glorious heart of human civilization and the Alliance. Following the devastation of the Third War, its former kingdoms lie in ruins, contested by the undead Scourge, Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken, and desperate remnants of the living. Lordaeron shares its name with the human city-state of Lordaeron, which rose in the north after the ancient Empire of Arathor and grew into the most powerful of the human kingdoms. Stretching from the rugged Arathi Highlands in the south across scenic forests and waterways up toward Quel'Thalas, the region nurtured thriving kingdoms like Lordaeron, Dalaran, Gilneas, and Alterac. It was historically celebrated for fertile farmlands in Tirisfal and Hillsbrad, mountain strongholds, and the sacred cradle of the Holy Light.

Mage. Mages are scholarly spellcasters who bend the fabric of reality through arcane study, hurling destructive fire, controlling frost, and raw arcane energy. While physically fragile and cloaked only in cloth, their mastery over teleportation, conjuration, and battlefield crowd control makes them formidable allies and terrifying foes. Their discipline requires immense mental dedication, balancing immense destructive potential against the perilous history of arcane misuse. The path of the mage demands intellect, focus, and years of rigorous study. Rather than communing with spirits or relying on divine faith, magi treat magic as a precise cosmic science. By drawing upon arcane energies, a practitioner can weave raw destructive power, summon searing bursts of flame, or chill the surrounding air into solid ice and howling blizzards. Because heavy armor disrupts the delicate somatic gestures and mental focus required for incantations, mages wear light cloth, relying instead on wards, mana barriers, and evasive spells to protect themselves.

Medivh. Medivh was the last Guardian of Tirisfal, an ancient order tasked with defending Azeroth from demonic corruption. Bound from before his birth by the spirit of the Dark Titan Sargeras, he opened the Dark Portal and brought the orcish Horde into the world, setting off decades of catastrophic warfare. Medivh was born to the powerful Guardian Aegwynn and the court conjurer Nielas Aran. Centuries earlier, Aegwynn had fought the fallen Titan Sargeras in Northrend, unaware that his dark essence slipped into her body to await an heir. When Medivh reached his fourteenth birthday, the vast magical inheritance bestowed by his mother manifested in a terrifying explosion of power, plunging the boy into a decade-long coma under the watch of the clerics at Northshire Abbey.

Mor'Ladim. Mor'Ladim is a dangerous, vengeful skeletal warrior wandering the grounds of Raven Hill Cemetery in Duskwood. Formerly the noble knight Morgan Ladimore, he succumbed to profound grief and madness upon discovering the loss of his family, rising in undeath to slaughter anyone crossing his path. Before he became the terror of Raven Hill, Mor'Ladim lived as Morgan Ladimore, a devoted knight and defender of the helpless from Grand Hamlet—the town now known as Darkshire. Married at eighteen to his wife Lys, he raised three children in peace until war summoned him north. Morgan marched alongside Uther the Lightbringer to Lordaeron during the Third War, witnessing the downfall of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the spread of Kel'Thuzad's plague, and the tragic death of Uther himself.

Muradin Bronzebeard. Muradin Bronzebeard was the brother of King Magni Bronzebeard and Brann Bronzebeard, as well as a renowned warrior, diplomat, and co-founder of the Explorers' League. Revered across Khaz Modan and Lordaeron alike, he is believed to have died in the frozen wastes of Northrend when Prince Arthas Menethil claimed the cursed runeblade Frostmourne. Muradin fought with distinction during the Second War, acting as the vital liaison between the mountain halls of Khaz Modan and the Alliance of Lordaeron. He helped hold Ironforge during the Horde's siege and marched alongside Alliance forces all the way through Blackrock Spire to the Dark Portal. In the peaceful years that followed, Muradin settled into Capital City as Ironforge’s official ambassador. Jovial yet formidable, he became a fixture in the palace, growing close to King Terenas Menethil and taking it upon himself to tutor young Prince Arthas in the arts of swordplay and combat.

Murloc. Murlocs are amphibious, bipedal humanoids famous for their gurgling battle cries, territorial coastal villages, and sudden swarming tactics. Though historically dwelling in the deep ocean, they have steadily migrated inland along the shores, lakes, and rivers of Azeroth, acting with far greater coordination and cunning than their primitive appearance suggests. Murlocs dwell in densely populated settlements along coastlines, riverbanks, and freshwater lakes. Averaging roughly four feet in height, they possess bulbous, slime-coated bodies, wide mouths filled with sharp fangs, and keen vision capable of piercing pitch-black water. While individuals are rarely seen wandering far from their kin, encountering one murloc invariably means a dozen more lurk just beneath the surface. They rely on overwhelming numbers and sharp crude weaponry.

Naga. The naga are a monstrous, serpentine race dwelling beneath the ocean's depths, ruled by their ancient empress, Queen Azshara. Once the Highborne elite of the Kaldorei Empire, they were warped into amphibious horrors during the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago. Recently emerging from the dark waters, they have seized shorelines across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to reclaim their forgotten surface empire. Ten millennia ago, the Highborne nobility of the Kaldorei Empire ruled supreme from their grand capital of Zin-Azshari. Consumed by an obsession with arcane power, Queen Azshara and her inner court tapped the Well of Eternity to draw the gaze of the Dark Titan Sargeras, inviting the catastrophic invasion known as the War of the Ancients. When the Well of Eternity collapsed into ruin, triggering the Great Sundering, the palace slipped into the crushing abyss. Facing utter annihilation, Azshara bargained with the malevolent Old Gods deep below. In exchange for survival, she and her followers were transformed into cold, scaly, serpentine beings bound to the deeps.

New Horde. The New Horde is the modern coalition forged under Warchief Thrall, departing from the bloodthirsty, demon-corrupted Old Horde of the First and Second Wars. Founded upon shamanic tradition, honor, and mutual survival, it unites the liberated orcs, the Darkspear trolls, the tauren tribes of Kalimdor, and a tenuous pact with the Forsaken in Lordaeron. The original Horde was a weapon crafted by the Burning Legion and the Shadow Council, fueling the orcs with demonic bloodlust and driving them across the Dark Portal. After the Second War ended in devastation, surviving orcs were rounded up into Alliance internment camps, sinking into a soul-draining lethargy. Through the efforts of Orgrim Doomhammer, Grommash Hellscream, and the young shaman Thrall, the orcs cast off their demonic shackles, rediscovered their ancestral shamanism, and fought their way to freedom.

Night elf. The night elves, or kaldorei, are an ancient and reclusive race native to the forests of northern Kalimdor. Once the masters of a sprawling magical empire, they abandoned arcane magic following the catastrophic War of the Ancients and turned to the worship of Elune and the path of druidism. In the wake of the Third War, having sacrificed their immortality to stop the Burning Legion, they joined the Alliance to defend their ancestral lands from Horde encroachment. Millennia ago, an inquisitive nocturnal tribe gathered around the shores of the Well of Eternity, a vast font of raw arcane energy. Over generations, the Well's cosmic magic transformed them into tall, violet-skinned, long-lived beings who called themselves the kaldorei—'children of the stars.' Guiding their early society were the moon goddess Elune and the forest demigod Cenarius, who nurtured their deep connection to the living wilds of Kalimdor.

Night Watch. The Night Watch is the beleaguered town militia responsible for defending Darkshire and the shadowy roads of Duskwood. Abandoned by the House of Nobles in Stormwind, these local volunteers stand alone against roaming undead, feral worgen, and lurking necromancy. Led by Commander Althea Ebonlocke, they rely heavily on visiting adventurers to keep darkness from overtaking their home. When foul magic overtook the once-vibrant Grand Hamlet and turned the forest into Duskwood, the kingdom of Stormwind turned its back. Following King Varian Wrynn's disappearance, the royal garrison was pulled back to the capital. Stripped of official royal troops and supplies, the townsfolk formed their own volunteer militia—the Night Watch—swearing to hold the borders of Darkshire against the creeping horrors of the woods.

Nordrassil. Nordrassil, the 'Crown of the Heavens,' is the original World Tree planted atop Mount Hyjal to shield the second Well of Eternity. Blessed by the Great Dragon Aspects, it granted the night elves ageless immortality and a deep connection to the Emerald Dream for ten thousand years. Its sacrifice during the climax of the Third War broke Archimonde's assault, leaving the tree wounded and the night elves mortal. Ten thousand years ago, in the ashes of the Great Sundering, Illidan Stormrage cast vials of the original Well of Eternity into a mountaintop lake atop Mount Hyjal, birthing a new font of arcane power. To prevent this raw magic from corrupting the world or drawing the Burning Legion anew, the Dragon Aspect Alexstrasza planted an acorn from the Mother Tree, G'Hanir, directly over the waters. From it grew Nordrassil. The roots spread deep beneath Azeroth, sealing the Well's volatile energies and distributing gentle, life-giving vigor across the continents.

Old God. The Old Gods are colossal, malevolent horrors of flesh and madness who ruled Azeroth in its primordial dawn. Though vanquished and bound deep beneath the crust by the Titans, their ancient whispers still corrode mortal minds, twist nature, and drive doomsday cults to unearth their prisons. Long before mortal records began, Azeroth was dominated by the Old Gods, colossal entities of chaotic flesh such as C'Thun. They embedded themselves into the planet's crust, commanding elemental armies and insectoid swarms. When the Titans arrived, their armies fought an apocalyptic war against them. Rather than destroying them, the Titans bound the Old Gods in vast, subterranean prisons to keep them dormant forever.

Old Horde. The Old Horde was the blood-crazed coalition of orcish clans manipulated by demonic power into conquering Draenor and invading Azeroth. Led first by Blackhand and later by Orgrim Doomhammer, its path of destruction shaped the First and Second Wars until its decisive defeat by the Alliance of Lordaeron. Today, Thrall's New Horde seeks to overcome that dark legacy, while isolated remnants like the Dark Horde still cling to its bloody past. Before it crossed into Azeroth, the Horde was forged on Draenor through demonic manipulation. The demon lord Kil'jaeden used the warlock Gul'dan and the elder shaman Ner'zhul to corrupt the proud, spiritual orc clans. As elemental spirits abandoned the warring orcs, shamanistic traditions were cast aside for warlock magic. Sealed by the consumption of the blood of Mannoroth, the clans surrendered to bloodlust, slaughtering the draenei and draining their homeland of life.

Orc. Originally a shamanistic clan people hailing from the alien world of Draenor, the orcs were deceived and corrupted into a bloodthirsty conquering force by the demonic Burning Legion. After invading Azeroth and suffering eventual defeat and internment, they were rallied by Warchief Thrall to reclaim their spiritual heritage. In this new era, the orcs lead the Horde from their newly carved nation of Durotar, striving for honor while grappling with the lingering shadow of their demonic past. Before their fall, orcs lived as nomadic hunter-gatherers and spiritual clans across the rugged landscapes of Draenor. Their culture was grounded in ancestral reverence and deep communion with elemental spirits, guided primarily by revered shamans. Among the disparate clans were the Frostwolves, Warsongs, and Shadowmoon. Though physically formidable and deeply proud, traditional orcish society was defined by survival, honor, and harmony with the natural elements rather than mindless conquest.

Paladin. Paladins are holy warriors who blend martial prowess with the power of the Holy Light. Clad in heavy plate, they protect the innocent, heal the wounded and strike down wicked foes. Humans and dwarves carry the Silver Hand's legacy for the Alliance, and among the Horde, Forsaken who served the Light in life still answer its call, though it burns them. The paladins were originally established during the Second War by Archbishop Alonsus Faol. Having witnessed the devastation wrought upon the pious Clerics of Northshire during the First War, Faol recognized that healers alone could not survive the brutality of orcish warfare. He gathered virtuous knights of Lordaeron and trained surviving clerics in the ways of martial combat and divine magic. Baptized as the Knights of the Silver Hand and led by Uther the Lightbringer, these champions provided both physical defense and spiritual renewal to the kingdoms of humanity.

Pirate. Pirates and buccaneers are lawless seafaring plunderers operating across the Great Sea and coastal waters of Azeroth. Preying on Alliance, Horde, and neutral merchant vessels alike, they band together under loose flags to seize wealth, capture cargo, and control coastal coves. Their violent presence drives constant naval skirmishes from the waters of Kalimdor to the shores of the Eastern Kingdoms. Pirates—often called buccaneers, corsairs, or freebooters—are maritime raiders of nearly every race who make their living seizing ships and raiding coastal settlements. Their operations stretch far beyond simple robbery; crews regularly engage in smuggling, kidnappings, and mercenary contracts for whoever has coin. With the chaos left behind by the Third War and the collapse of northern kingdoms, naval enforcement has fractured, giving pirate factions the freedom to carve out fortified footholds on neglected islands and coastal coves.

Plague of Undeath. The Plague of Undeath is a supernatural contagion concocted by the Lich King under the direction of the Burning Legion to scourge northern Eastern Kingdoms. Transmitted through infected grain, airborne cauldrons, and tainted waterways, the sickness rapidly kills living mortals and raises them as mind-bound thralls of the Scourge. The plague was devised by the fallen shaman Ner'zhul after he was transformed into the Lich King by Kil'jaeden. From his icy seat atop the Frozen Throne in Northrend, Ner'zhul perfected the sickness as an unholy vanguard for the Burning Legion's invasion. Testing his power on isolated human villages across Northrend, he discovered that he could snuff out life and psychically command the corpses that arose shortly after. Ner'zhul's telepathic summon reached across the Great Sea to the Kirin Tor mage Kel'Thuzad, who abandoned Dalaran to serve the entity. Kel'Thuzad organized the secretive Cult of the Damned, whose mortal infiltrators laid the groundwork to poison Lordaeron from within.

Priest. Priests are spiritual guides and conduits of immense unseen power who shape belief, mend flesh, and guard souls. Channeling the radiant energies of faith or plumbing the terrifying depths of the Void, they serve as the vital heart of any war party. Across Azeroth, their traditions range from the Church of the Holy Light to the Moon Goddess's Sisterhood and shadowy Forsaken cults. Priests guide the spiritual destiny of their communities. While physical combatants test their mettle with steel, priests draw power directly from conviction. Through divine connection, they soothe grievous wounds, raise fallen companions from death's threshold, and weave mystic barriers to repel incoming harm. Their presence on the field often marks the difference between survival and annihilation.

Quilboar. Quilboar are aggressive, boar-like humanoids native to central Kalimdor, renowned for their sharp spinal quills and relentless territorial savagery. Claiming descent from the fallen demigod Agamaggan, they dwell within dense mazes of razor-sharp brambles across Durotar, Mulgore, and the Barrens. Their fierce struggle over water, soil, and sacred ground makes them a constant threat to travelers and Horde settlements. Quilboar revere Agamaggan, the colossal boar Ancient who perished battling the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. According to their sacred traditions, the quilboar are his mortal offspring. Where Agamaggan bled and died across central Kalimdor, enormous thorny vines erupted from the scorched earth, forming sprawling root-mazes that the quilboar treat as holy ground. His crystallized blood endures across the Barrens as crimson Blood Shards, which their geomancers dig up and revere as powerful talismans.

Ravenholdt. Ravenholdt, also known as the Assassin's League, is an elite guild of rogues, thieves, and killers based out of a secluded mountain manor above the Hillsbrad Foothills. Led by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the league maintains strict neutrality from faction politics while waging an unending shadow war against their bitter rivals, the Syndicate. They test and recruit only the most cunning operatives across Azeroth, valuing peerless discipline, stealth, and lethal efficiency above all else. Tucked away in the craggy mountains connecting Hillsbrad to Alterac, Ravenholdt Manor serves as the nerve center for Azeroth's premier brotherhood of assassins. Led by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the organization operates far beyond the jurisdiction of kings and warchiefs. Within its walls, master specialists hone every lethal art: Master Kang instructs disciples in close combat and assassination, the Thunderwood brothers brew rare and deadly poisons, and gnome craftsmen engineer intricate locks to test fledglings. To non-rogues, entering the estate is an overt flirtation with death, where an unwary step easily ends with a poisoned dagger in the ribs.

Razorfen. Razorfen is the collective name associated with the predominant quilboar tribe of southern Kalimdor and their sprawling thorn-choked settlements. Carved into massive briars along the southern border of the Barrens and the edge of Thousand Needles, Razorfen encompasses the strongholds of Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs. It serves as both the spiritual heart and the central bastion of quilboar power. According to legend, the colossal thorned brambles that make up the Razorfen sprouted ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients. When the giant boar Ancient, Agamaggan, fell in battle against the Burning Legion, his blood seeped into the earth wherever he bled and died. From that divine sacrifice grew massive vines of petrified bramble and iron-hard thorns, creating a natural fortress where his descendants, the quilboar, have dwelled ever since.

Refugee. Throughout the violent history of Azeroth, constant warfare has repeatedly driven civilian populations from their homes. From the exodus of Stormwind during the First War to the tragic flight from Lordaeron in the Third War, refugees remain living testaments to the devastating costs of invasion, plague, and betrayal. When the Orcish Horde swept through the kingdom of Stormwind during the First War, settlements like Goldshire, Moonbrook, and Grand Hamlet burned. Following the assassination of King Llane Wrynn, Sir Anduin Lothar took command of the kingdom's remnants. He gathered surviving soldiers and desperate civilians, escorting them to the harbor as the city burned. Lothar led a massive fleet across the Great Sea to the northern shores of Lordaeron. Arriving near Southshore, the exiled survivors—including the young Prince Varian Wrynn—were granted sanctuary by King Terenas Menethil II.

Riverpaw pack. The Riverpaw pack is a savage clan of gnolls inhabiting the borderlands of Elwynn Forest and Westfall. Known for their brutal raids and ruthless dominance over local kobolds, they have grown increasingly organized and brazen following the Third War. With Stormwind's military stretched thin, their presence threatens vital roads and settlements throughout the heartland. For decades, the Riverpaw clan prowled the fringes of human civilization, but their boldness has surged in recent years. In Elwynn Forest, packs led by the infamous brute Hogger prowl the southern woods around Forest's Edge and roam the shores of Stone Cairn Lake. In Westfall, they roam across the Dust Plains and along the coasts, ambushing solitary travelers and raiding homesteads. Deputy Rainer at Westbrook Garrison and Captain Danuvin at Sentinel Hill rely heavily on mercenary blades to cull their numbers, issuing standing bounties for painted armbands and severed paws.

Rogue. Rogues are masters of stealth, espionage, and sudden, lethal combat who dictate the terms of engagement from the shadows. Relying on light leather armor, dual-wielded blades, and brewed toxins, they strike unawares before vanishing back into the dark. Across Azeroth, they serve as scouts, assassins, pickpockets, and agents for factions and hidden syndicates alike. Rogues eschew the heavy plate and open confrontation of traditional frontline warriors. Clad in lightweight leather to remain completely silent and mobile, they stalk their quarry unseen. When they engage, they seize the opening moments through precision and surprise, aiming for vital organs or exposed joints. Utilizing an ever-flowing pool of energy and rapid weapon combinations, a rogue softens up an enemy with carefully chained strikes before unleashing a catastrophic finishing blow.

Royal Apothecary Society. The Royal Apothecary Society is an alchemical guild established under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and based in the Apothecarium beneath the Undercity. Composed of Forsaken researchers, its primary mission is compounding a lethal New Plague capable of eradicating the Scourge while claiming vengeance against the living. While Horde allies believe the society seeks a cure for undeath, its researchers actively harvest venoms, slimes, and toxic reagents across Azeroth to perfect weapons of mass destruction. Founded in the wake of the Forsaken's liberation, the Royal Apothecary Society serves as the scientific and alchemical arm of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's kingdom. From their vats and subterranean laboratories in the Apothecarium, researchers seek to weaponize the very force that damned them. Their preeminent endeavor is the creation of a 'New Plague'—a concoction intended to eradicate the Scourge and destroy the Lich King. Unlike traditional human alchemy, which prioritizes elixirs of healing or transmutation, the Society experiments ruthlessly with foul pathogens, caustic acids, and necromantic blends, raising fallen warhorses as skeletal steeds and brewing deadlier strains of toxic blight.

Gilneas. Gilneas is a secluded human kingdom occupying a rugged, storm-lashed peninsula south of Silverpine Forest. Following the Second War, King Genn Greymane severed ties with the outside world and locked his nation behind the colossal Greymane Wall, leaving neighboring territories abandoned and the kingdom shrouded in total isolation. Gilneas was once an assertive maritime powerhouse among the human realms, claiming lineage from the ancient empire of Arathor. King Genn Greymane participated reluctantly in the Second War, believing his kingdom could defend itself without foreign entanglements. Bitter over the loss of Gilnean lives and unwilling to help finance the internment camps for captured orcs, Greymane severed relations with the Alliance of Lordaeron. To permanently shield his realm from outside calamity, he ordered the construction of a massive stone barricade along the kingdom's northern frontier.

Sargeras. Sargeras is the fallen titan and supreme creator of the Burning Legion, bent on scouring all life from the cosmos. Once the noble champion and defender of the Pantheon, his descent into madness led to the Sundering of ancient Azeroth and nearly every demonic catastrophe since. Before his fall, Sargeras was the greatest and noblest warrior among the titans. Entrusted by the Pantheon of Order to safeguard their grand creations across the Great Dark Beyond, he waged war against the chaotic demons spawned from the Twisting Nether. Incapable of conceiving pure evil, Sargeras trapped countless fiends away within a great prison. Yet eons of relentless warfare against cosmic horrors gradually wore down his altruistic spirit.

Satyr. Satyrs are twisted, caprine demons born from the curse of the Highborne sorcerer Xavius during the ancient War of the Ancients. Once night elves, they were warped by Sargeras into horned, hooved beasts dedicated to spreading fel corruption, tormenting their former kin, and furthering the Burning Legion's will. Across the wilds of Kalimdor, scattered satyr sects corrupt pristine woodlands, desecrate moonwells, and subvert vulnerable mortal cults. Ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients, the Highborne councilor Xavius failed to keep the Burning Legion's initial gateway stable against Malfurion Stormrage. Enraged by this blunder, Sargeras dismantled Xavius's spirit and rebuilt him as a punishment and tool: his torso retained elven features, but he gained wicked horns, taloned claws, a leonine tail, and the cloven lower body of a goat. Sent back into Zin-Azshari, Xavius gleefully passed his fel affliction to other power-hungry Highborne. Though Xavius was struck down, his demonic progeny survived, continually seeking to reproduce their kind by corrupting others.

Scarlet Crusade. Born from the shattered remnants of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the Scarlet Crusade is a fanatical holy order obsessed with purging the undead from Lordaeron. Blighted by paranoia and radical zealotry, they view anyone outside their ranks as carriers of the plague and shoot outsiders on sight. From strongholds across Tirisfal Glades and the Plaguelands, their crimson banners wage a ruthless war against Scourge and living alike. When Prince Arthas betrayed Lordaeron and murdered King Terenas Menethil II, the Order of the Silver Hand was broken. Surviving paladins and priests rallied under leaders like Alexandros Mograine, Saidan Dathrohan, and General Abbendis to reclaim their ruined homeland. Reorganizing their forces at Hearthglen and Tyr's Hand, they swore to cleanse the undead scourge with holy fire. Yet as the war dragged on, tragedy and suspicion festered within their ranks. What began as a desperate resistance soon devolved into an unyielding, xenophobic crusade.

Scourge. The Scourge is an apocalyptic army of undead monsters, necromancers, and enslaved spirits bound to the will of the Lich King. Originally created by the Burning Legion to destabilize Azeroth ahead of the Third War, the legion of walking corpses broke free from demonic control and shattered the kingdoms of Lordaeron and Quel'Thalas. Today, they wage unending war from their arctic stronghold in Northrend and their corrupt dominion over the Plaguelands. The Scourge was born as an instrument of destruction forged by the Burning Legion. The demon lords bound the spirit of the fallen orc shaman Ner'zhul to the Frozen Throne in distant Northrend, fashioning him into the Lich King. With terrifying telepathic power, he was commanded to prepare Azeroth for conquest. The Lich King unleashed the Plague of Undeath southward into the unsuspecting human realm of Lordaeron, relying on the mortal traitors of the Cult of the Damned to poison grain supplies. Those who perished arose not as restful dead, but as twisted thralls entirely subservient to the Lich King's iron mind.

Second War. The Second War was the continent-spanning clash across the Eastern Kingdoms between the Orcish Horde and the newly forged Alliance of Lordaeron. Sparked after the sack of Stormwind, the war devastated Khaz Modan and northern human realms before turning at the gates of Capital City. It ended in the destruction of the Dark Portal and the dispersal of the old Horde. Following the fall of Stormwind during the First War, Regent Anduin Lothar led human refugees north across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. King Terenas Menethil II convened the Council of Seven Nations, forging the Alliance of Lordaeron alongside the high elves of Quel'Thalas, the Bronzebeard dwarves of Ironforge, and the gnomes of Gnomeregan. Meanwhile, Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer consolidated the Horde, forging alliances with forest troll tribes and the Steamwheedle Cartel while subjugating red dragons through the Dragonmaw clan to invade the northern continents.

Sentinels. The Sentinels are the elite, predominantly female military force of the night elves, formed ten thousand years ago after the War of the Ancients. Guided by the Sisterhood of Elune and commanded by General Shandris Feathermoon, they guard kaldorei settlements and defend sacred lands from Ashenvale to Feralas. Today, they wage a bitter war against Horde deforestation while watching over their new home on Teldrassil. Before the Great Sundering, the military of the ancient Kaldorei Empire had devolved into a decadent hierarchy where rank was decided by noble lineage rather than martial skill.
